UBERON:0012249.def: The part of the cervix uteri that protrudes into the vagina and is lined with stratified squamous epithelium.

UBERON:0012250.name: cervix glandular epithelium
UBERON:0012250.def: A glandular epithelium that is part of a uterine cervix.

UBERON:0012251.name: ectocervical epithelium
UBERON:0012251.def: An epithelium that is part of a ectocervix.

UBERON:0012252.name: endocervical epithelium
UBERON:0012252.def: The glandular epithelium that lines the endocervix.

UBERON:0012253.name: cervical squamo-columnar junction
UBERON:0012253.def: Region of cervical epithelium where columnar epithelium of endocervic and the stratified non-keratinising squamous epithelium of the ectocervic meet.

UBERON:0012254.name: abdominal aorta artery
UBERON:0012254.def: An artery that originates from the abdominal aorta.

UBERON:0012255.name: inferior phrenic artery
UBERON:0012255.def: The inferior phrenic arteries are two small vessels, which supply the diaphragm but present much variety in their origin. They may arise separately from the front of the aorta, immediately above the celiac artery, or by a common trunk, which may spring either from the aorta or from the celiac artery. Sometimes one is derived from the aorta, and the other from one of the renal arteries; they rarely arise as separate vessels from the aorta. They diverge from one another across the crura of the diaphragm, and then run obliquely upward and lateralward upon its under surface. The left phrenic passes behind the esophagus, and runs forward on the left side of the esophageal hiatus. The right phrenic passes behind the inferior vena cava, and along the right side of the foramen which transmits that vein. Near the back part of the central tendon each vessel divides into a medial and a lateral branch. The medial branch curves forward, and anastomoses with its fellow of the opposite side, and with the musculophrenic and pericardiacophrenic arteries. The lateral branch passes toward the side of the thorax, and anastomoses with the lower intercostal arteries, and with the musculophrenic. The lateral branch of the right phrenic gives off a few vessels to the inferior vena cava; and the left one, some branches to the esophagus. Each vessel gives off superior suprarenal branches to the suprarenal gland of its own side. The spleen and the liver also receive a few twigs from the left and right vessels respectively.

UBERON:0012260.name: alular digit
UBERON:0012260.def: A manual digit found in Aves that is the most preaxial position and is morphologically similar to digit 1 in the standard tetrapod configuration and develops from embryonic digit 2, with contributions from embryonic digit 1.

UBERON:0012261.name: manual major digit (Aves)
UBERON:0012261.def: A manual digit found in Aves that is morphologically similar to digit 2 in the standard tetrapod configuration and develops from embryonic digit 3.

UBERON:0012262.name: manual minor digit (Aves)
UBERON:0012262.def: A manual digit found in Aves that is morphologically similar to digit 3 in the standard tetrapod configuration and develops from embryonic digit 4.

UBERON:0012267.name: equine splint bone
UBERON:0012267.def: The splint bones sit either side of the equine cannon bone. Homologous to metapodium bones 2 or 4.

UBERON:0012268.name: equine forelimb splint bone
UBERON:0012268.def: A splint bone in the metacarpal region.

UBERON:0012269.name: equine hindlimb splint bone
UBERON:0012269.def: A splint bone in the metatarsal region.

UBERON:0012270.name: forestomach-glandular stomach junction
UBERON:0012270.def: The distinct low fold of tissue that separates the non-glandular area of the stomach (forestomach) from the glandular stomach; the limiting ridge extends circumferentially from the large curvature of the stomach to the small curvature, just below the esophagus; at the esophagus, the course of the limiting ridge bends into a U-shape and almost surrounds the esophageal opening.
synonym: squamo-columnar junction between forestomach and glandular stomach
squamocolumnar junction with the glandular stomach

UBERON:0012271.name: major duodenal papilla
UBERON:0012271.def: The common bile duct and the pancreatic duct together perforate the medial side of the second portion of the duodenum obliquely, some 7 to 10 cm below the pylorus, forming a structure called the major duodenal papilla. The accessory pancreatic duct sometimes pierces it about 2 cm above and slightly in front of these.

UBERON:0012272.name: minor duodenal papilla
UBERON:0012272.def: The minor duodenal papilla is the opening of the accessory pancreatic duct into the duodenum. It is sometimes absent, and often nonfunctional.

UBERON:0012274.name: columnar epithelium
UBERON:0012274.def: An epithelium that consists of columnar epithelial cells. Columnar epithelia are epithelial cells whose heights are at least four times their width. Columnar epithelia are divided into simple (or unilayered), and the rarer stratified (or multi-layered).[WP, modified].

UBERON:0012275.name: meso-epithelium
UBERON:0012275.def: Epithelium that derives from the mesoderm. [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0012278.name: gland of nasal mucosa
UBERON:0012278.def: The nasal glands are the seromucous glands in the respiratory region of the nasal mucous membrane. The three major types of nasal glands are anterior serous glands, seromucous glands, and Bowman glands.

UBERON:0012279.name: chromaffin paraganglion
UBERON:0012279.def: Small bodies containing chromaffin cells occurring outside of the adrenal medulla, most commonly near the sympathetic ganglia and in organs such as the kidney, liver, heart and gonads.

UBERON:0012281.name: perianal sebaceous gland
UBERON:0012281.def: A holocrine gland that is part of the pilosebaceous unit of a hair located in the area around the anus.

UBERON:0012282.name: mammary fat pad
UBERON:0012282.def: Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the mammary gland.

UBERON:0012283.name: femoral fat pad
UBERON:0012283.def: Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the femur.

UBERON:0012286.name: hemisphere of embryo
UBERON:0012286.def: One of two hemispheres of the embryo at the zygote or blastula stage[WP,modified].

UBERON:0012287.name: Rathkes pouch epithelium
UBERON:0012287.def: An epithelial sac that is part of a Rathke's pouch.

UBERON:0012288.name: centroquartal bone
UBERON:0012288.def: A tarsal bone that is formed from the fusion of the central and 4th tarsal bones.

UBERON:0012289.name: fused tarsal bones 2 and 3
UBERON:0012289.def: A tarsal bone that is formed from the fusion of the 2nd and 3rd tarsal bones.

UBERON:0012290.name: fused carpal bones 2 and 3
UBERON:0012290.def: A carpal bone that is formed from the fusion of the 2nd and 3rd distal carpal bones.

UBERON:0012291.name: lateral malleolus of fibula
UBERON:0012291.def: Malleolus is the name for the bony prominence on each side of the ankle.

UBERON:0012292.name: embryonic cloacal fold
UBERON:0012292.def: One of the pair of mesenchymal swellings (folds) located on either side of the cloacal membrane during the indifferent stage of embryonic development; cranial to the cloacal membrane the folds unite to form the genital tubercle; caudally the folds are subdivided into urogenital folds anteriorly and anal folds posteriorly.

UBERON:0012293.name: anal fold
UBERON:0012293.def: A slight elevation flanking the cloacal membrane and derived from a cloacal fold; anal folds form the border of the anus.

UBERON:0012294.name: navicular fossa of spongiose part of urethra
UBERON:0012294.def: The dilated terminal portion of the male spongy urethra located in the glans penis right before the external urethral orifice, also referred to as the most distal pendulous urethra; it is lined by stratified squamous, non-keratinizing epithelium; during development, the glans of the penis is initially solid but cannulates to give rise to the navicular fossa.
synonym: fossa navicularis urethrae (pars spongiosa, urethra masculina)

UBERON:0012295.name: Guérin's valve
UBERON:0012295.def: An inconstant fold or valve of mucous membrane sometimes found in the root or upper wall of the navicular fossa of the urethra.
synonym: valve of fossa navicularis of urethra

UBERON:0012296.name: urethral crest
UBERON:0012296.def: A longitudinal mucosal fold in the dorsal wall of the urethra[MP].

UBERON:0012297.name: male urethral crest
UBERON:0012297.def: Narrow longitudinal fold of mucosa on the posterior wall of the male urethra, extending from the uvula of the bladder through the prostatic urethra; when distended, it may serve to prevent the passage of the semen backward into the bladder; on either side of the male urethral crest is a slightly depressed fossa, the prostatic sinus, the floor of which is perforated by the orifices of the prostatic ducts from the lateral lobes of the prostate; the ducts of the middle lobe open behind the crest; at the forepart of the crest, below its summit, is a median elevation, the colliculus seminalis, upon or within the margins of which are the orifices of the prostatic utricle and the slit-like openings of the ejaculatory ducts[MP].

UBERON:0012298.name: female urethral crest
UBERON:0012298.def: The conspicuous longitudinal fold of mucosa on the posterior wall of the female urethra[MP].

UBERON:0012299.name: mucosa of urethra
UBERON:0012299.def: A mucosa that is part of a urethra.

UBERON:0012300.name: limb paddle
UBERON:0012300.def: A transient developing limb structure that develops from the limb bud; it is a dorsoventral flattening of the limb bud structure and develops into the foot plate.

UBERON:0012301.name: female membranous urethra
UBERON:0012301.def: A membranous urethra of male or female that is part of a female urethra.

UBERON:0012302.name: male membranous urethra
UBERON:0012302.def: The shortest, least dilatable, and, with the exception of the external orifice, the narrowest part of the male urethral canal located in the deep perineal pouch and lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium; it extends downward and forward, with a slight anterior concavity, between the apex of the prostate and the bulb of the urethra, perforating the urogenital diaphragm below and behind the pubic symphysis; the membranous portion of the urethra is completely surrounded by the fibers of the sphincter urethrae membranaceae; on either side near its termination are the bulbourethral glands.

UBERON:0012303.name: ureteral orifice
UBERON:0012303.def: The slit-like opening of either ureter into the bladder; normally, the two ureteral orifices are placed at the posterolateral angles of the urinary bladder trigone while the internal urethral orifice is placed at its anteroinferior angle (apex); wide gaping usually indicates vesicoureteral reflux.

UBERON:0012304.name: nasal diverticulum
UBERON:0012304.def: Caudally blind-ending cutaneous pouch lined with skin that occupies the nasoincisive notch. It's ventral and medial walls is formed by the alar fold. It's lateral wall is formed by the external nares and it's dorsal wall is formed by the straight fold. Lined by pigmented predominantly hairless skin. It has an external opening located on the dorsolateral aspect of the "true nostril". When the horse is exercising, obliteration of the nasal diverticulum greatly widens the nostrils increasing air intake[MURDOCH].

UBERON:0012305.name: marginal cutaneous pouch of ear
UBERON:0012305.def: A fold of skin at the caudal border of the auricle.

UBERON:0012306.name: lateral cervical lymph node
UBERON:0012306.def: A cervical lymph nodes are found in proximity to an internal or external jugular vein.

UBERON:0012307.name: anterior cervical lymph node
UBERON:0012307.def: The anterior cervical lymph nodes are a group of nodes found on the anterior part of the neck.

UBERON:0012308.name: superficial lateral cervical lymph node
UBERON:0012308.def: The superficial lateral cervical lymph nodes are found in proximity to the external jugular vein.

UBERON:0012309.name: superficial anterior cervical lymph node
UBERON:0012309.def: The superficial anterior cervical lymph nodes are found in proximity to the anterior jugular vein.

UBERON:0012310.name: deep lateral cervical lymph node
UBERON:0012310.def: The deep lateral cervical lymph nodes are found near the upper part of the internal jugular vein in the neck, lateral or posterior to the carotid sheath.

UBERON:0012311.name: deep anterior cervical lymph node
UBERON:0012311.def: The deep anterior cervical lymph nodes are found near the middle cricothyroid ligament and the trachea.

UBERON:0012314.name: embryonic facial prominence
UBERON:0012314.def: One of five swellings formed during the development of the face.

UBERON:0012315.name: incisive foramen
UBERON:0012315.def: The point where the primary palate and both palatine shelves fuse.

UBERON:0012316.name: primitive palate
UBERON:0012316.def: Roof of the buccal cavity, formed from the fusion of vomer, pterygoid, parasphenoid, palatine, ectopterygoid.

UBERON:0012317.name: vagina orifice
UBERON:0012317.def: The median slit located inferior and posterior to the external urethral orifice in the female; the exit for menstrual flow and birth and the entrance for the penis during sexual intercourse; the size and appearance of the vaginal orifice varies inversely with that of the hymen (G. membrane), a thin fold of mucous membrane that surrounds the vaginal orifice.

UBERON:0012318.name: anterior ethmoidal artery
UBERON:0012318.def: The anterior ethmoidal artery, also anterior ethmoid artery is an artery of the head. Once branching from the ophthalmic artery, it accompanies the nasociliary nerve through the anterior ethmoidal canal to supply the anterior and middle ethmoidal cells, frontal sinus, and anterosuperior aspect of the lateral nasal wall[WP].

UBERON:0012319.name: posterior ethmoidal artery
UBERON:0012319.def: The posterior ethmoidal artery is an artery of the head. It is smaller than the anterior ethmoidal artery, branches off from the ophthalmic artery when it reaches the medial wall of the orbit.

UBERON:0012321.name: deep cervical artery
UBERON:0012321.def: The deep cervical artery (Profunda cervicalis) is an artery of the neck.

UBERON:0012322.name: ascending cervical artery
UBERON:0012322.def: The ascending cervical artery is a small branch which arises from the inferior thyroid artery as that vessel is passing behind the carotid sheath; it runs up on the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrC& in the interval between the Scalenus anterior and Longus capitis. To the muscles of the neck it gives twigs which anastomose with branches of the vertebral, and it sends one or two spinal branches into the vertebral canal through the intervertebral foramina to be distributed to the medulla spinalis and its membranes, and to the bodies of the vertebrC&, in the same manner as the spinal branches from the vertebral. It anastomoses with the ascending pharyngeal and occipital arteries.

UBERON:0012324.name: transverse cervical artery
UBERON:0012324.def: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck, transversa colli artery) is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk, running at a higher level than the suprascapular artery.
synonym: descending branch of the transverse cervical

UBERON:0012325.name: retrocerebral complex
UBERON:0012325.def: Corpora allata with Corpora cardiaca form the retrocerebral complex, a neurosecretory organ.

UBERON:0012326.name: gubernacular bulb
UBERON:0012326.def: The caudal, swollen portion of the gubernaculum.

UBERON:0012327.name: pearly penile papule
UBERON:0012327.def: Small saliences on the ridge of the glans of the male genital organs.

UBERON:0012328.name: penile spine
UBERON:0012328.def: Keratinized structures along the glans and/or shaft of their penis that may be involved in sexual selection.

UBERON:0012329.name: keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
UBERON:0012329.def: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium is a stratified squamous epithelium, the cells of which synthesize and accumulate keratin.

UBERON:0012330.name: nasal-associated lymphoid tissue
UBERON:0012330.def: The lymphocytic cell population present in the mucosa of the nasopharyngeal duct of some animals.

UBERON:0012331.name: mesosalpinx
UBERON:0012331.def: A serous layer that is part of the peritoneal lining of the abdominal cavity in higher vertebrates, specifically the portion of the broad ligament that stretches from the uterine (fallopian) tube to the ovary. It is made up of epithelial cells of mesothelium and a mesh of serous membrane lining.

UBERON:0012332.name: broad ligament of uterus
UBERON:0012332.def: A broad fold of peritoneum that extends from the side of the uterus to the wall of the pelvis.

UBERON:0012333.name: ovarian bursa
UBERON:0012333.def: A pouch formed by the mesosalpinx and the mesovarium that encloses the infundibulum of the uterine tube and the ovary.

UBERON:0012334.name: navicular bursa
UBERON:0012334.def: A fluid-filled sac that lies between the navicular bone and the deep digital flexor muscle.

UBERON:0012335.name: navicular bursa of manus
UBERON:0012335.def: A navicular bursa that is part of a manus.

UBERON:0012336.name: perianal skin
UBERON:0012336.def: A zone of skin that is part of the area surrounding the anus.

UBERON:0012337.name: cauda equina
UBERON:0012337.def: The cauda equina is a structure within the lower end of the spinal column of most vertebrates, that consists of nerve roots and rootlets from above. The space in which the cerebrospinal fluid is present is actually an extension of the subarachnoid space.

UBERON:0012343.name: navicular bursa of pes
UBERON:0012343.def: A navicular bursa that is part of a pes.

UBERON:0012344.name: holocrine gland
UBERON:0012344.def: Any exocrine gland whose secretion consists of its own disintegrated secretory cells along with its secretory product; holocrine secretions are produced in the cytoplasm of the cell and released by the rupture of the plasma membrane, which destroys the cell and results in the secretion of the product into the lumen.

UBERON:0012348.name: autopod pad
UBERON:0012348.def: Pigmented, keratinised, hairless epidermis covering subcutaneous, collagenous, and adipose tissue.

UBERON:0012349.name: digital pad
UBERON:0012349.def: A thick spongy structure at the base of the autopod, centred over the flexor surfaces of the distal interphalangeal joints.

UBERON:0012350.name: carpal pad
UBERON:0012350.def: An autopod pad found in the carpal region of a manus. Used for additional traction when stopping or descending a slope in digitigrade species.

UBERON:0012351.name: urachal lumen
UBERON:0012351.def: An anatomical space that is enclosed by a urachus.

UBERON:0012352.name: mesangial matrix
UBERON:0012352.def: Extracellular matrix secreted by intraglomerular mesangial cells.

UBERON:0012353.name: fin skeleton
UBERON:0012353.def: Skeletal subdivision consisting of all the skeletal elements in a single fin.

UBERON:0012354.name: acropodium region
UBERON:0012354.def: The segment of the autopod that is distal to the metapodial region and consists of the digits.

UBERON:0012355.name: manual acropodium region
UBERON:0012355.def: The segment of the manus that is distal to the metacarpal region and consists of the manual digits (fingers).

UBERON:0012356.name: pedal acropodium region
UBERON:0012356.def: The segment of the pes that is distal to the metatarsal region and consists of the pedal digits (toes).

UBERON:0012357.name: digitopodium bone
UBERON:0012357.def: A bone that is part of a the digitopodium skeleton - i.e. the acropodial skeleton or the metapodial skeleton.

UBERON:0012358.name: manual digitopodium bone
UBERON:0012358.def: A bone that is part of a the manual digitopodium skeleton - i.e. the fingers or the metacarpal skeleton.

UBERON:0012359.name: pedal digitopodium bone
UBERON:0012359.def: A bone that is part of a the pedal digitopodium skeleton - i.e. the toes or the metatarsal skeleton.

UBERON:0012360.name: bone of jaw
UBERON:0012360.def: A bone element that is part of a jaw region.

UBERON:0012363.name: thyroid follicle epithelium
UBERON:0012363.def: An epithelium that is part of a thyroid follicle.

UBERON:0012364.name: colloid of thyroid follicle
UBERON:0012364.def: Portion of substance contained within the thyroid follicle lumen. Contains prohormone thyroglobulin.

UBERON:0012367.name: muscle layer of intestine
UBERON:0012367.def: A muscle layer that is part of an intestine.

UBERON:0012368.name: circular muscle layer of muscular coat
UBERON:0012368.def: The inner layer of the muscular coat.

UBERON:0012369.name: longitudinal muscle layer of muscular coat
UBERON:0012369.def: The outer layer of the muscular coat.

UBERON:0012373.name: sympathetic nerve plexus
UBERON:0012373.def: A nerve plexus that is part of a sympathetic nervous system.

UBERON:0012374.name: subserosal plexus
UBERON:0012374.def: The subserous part of the enteric plexus of autonomic nerves.

UBERON:0012375.name: subserosa
UBERON:0012375.def: A layer of tissue between the muscularis and serosa.

UBERON:0012376.name: retromolar triangle
UBERON:0012376.def: The small area behind the wisdom teeth.

UBERON:0012377.name: muscle layer of jejunum
UBERON:0012377.def: A muscular coat that is part of a jejunum.

UBERON:0012378.name: muscle layer of urinary bladder
UBERON:0012378.def: A muscular coat that is part of a urinary bladder.

UBERON:0012398.name: large intestine smooth muscle circular layer
UBERON:0012398.def: A circular muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a large intestine smooth muscle.
UBERON:0012398.synonym: circular muscle layer of segment of large intestine

UBERON:0012399.name: large intestine smooth muscle longitudinal layer
UBERON:0012399.def: A longitudinal muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a large intestine smooth muscle.
UBERON:0012399.synonym: longitudinal muscle layer of zone of large intestine

UBERON:0012401.name: small intestine smooth muscle circular layer
UBERON:0012401.def: A circular muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a small intestine smooth muscle.
synonym: circular layer of small intestine muscularis propria
circular muscle coat of small intestine
circular muscle layer of small intestine
short pitch helicoidal muscle layer of small intestine
stratum circulare tunicae muscularis intestini tenuis
stratum helicoidale brevis gradus tunicae muscularis intestini tenuis

UBERON:0012402.name: small intestine smooth muscle longitudinal layer
UBERON:0012402.def: A longitudinal muscle layer of muscular coat that is part of a small intestine smooth muscle.
synonym: long pitch helicoidal muscle layer of small intestine
longitudinal layer of small intestine muscularis propria
longitudinal muscle coat of small intestine
longitudinal muscle layer of small intestine
stratum helicoidale longi gradus tunicae muscularis intestini tenuis
stratum longitudinale tunicae muscularis intestini tenuis

UBERON:0012418.name: respiratory system venous smooth muscle
UBERON:0012418.def: A smooth muscle tissue that is part of a respiratory system venous blood vessel.

UBERON:0012419.name: taenia coli
UBERON:0012419.def: The taeniae coli (also teniae coli) are three separate longitudinal ribbons of smooth muscle on the outside of the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colons. They are visible, and can be seen just below the serosa or fibrosa. They are the Mesocolic, Free and Omental Coli. The teniae coli contracts length wise to produce the haustra, the bulges in the colon. The bands converge at the root of the vermiform appendix and the rectum. These bands correspond to the outer layer of the muscularis externa, in other portions of the digestive tract.
synonym: longitudinal band of large intestine muscularis

UBERON:0012420.name: coprodeum
UBERON:0012420.def: Most proximal cloacal compartment, into which the large intestine empties[Kardong].

UBERON:0012421.name: urodeum
UBERON:0012421.def: Cloacal compartment into which the urogenital system empties[Kardong].

UBERON:0012422.name: secretion of crop
UBERON:0012422.def: Nutritional fluid secreted by the crop in some species[Kardong].

UBERON:0012423.name: layer of microvilli
UBERON:0012423.def: A layer of microvilli, Thin cylindrical membrane-covered projections on the surface of an animal cell containing a core bundle of actin filaments[GO,modified].

UBERON:0012424.name: brush border layer
UBERON:0012424.def: The microvilli-covered surface of simple cuboidal epithelium and simple columnar epithelium cells found in certain locations of the body; mainly in the small an large intestines and kidneys.

UBERON:0012425.name: striated border microvillus layer
UBERON:0012425.def: A microvillus layer that is striated and found in the intestine.

UBERON:0012426.name: short microvillus layer
UBERON:0012426.def: A layer of microvilli covering lymphocytes.

UBERON:0012427.name: intestinal brush border layer
UBERON:0012427.def: A brush border layer that is part of a intestine.
synonym: brush border microvillus layer of intestine

UBERON:0012428.name: proximal convoluted tubule brush border
UBERON:0012428.def: A brush border layer that is part of a proximal tubule in the kidney.

UBERON:0012429.name: hematopoietic tissue
UBERON:0012429.def: Blood-forming tissue, consisting of reticular fibers and cells.

UBERON:0012430.name: tunica fibrosa of eyeball
UBERON:0012430.def: The sclera and cornea form the fibrous tunic of the bulb of the eye; the sclera is opaque, and constitutes the posterior five-sixths of the tunic; the cornea is transparent, and forms the anterior sixth.

UBERON:0012437.name: epithelial-mesenchymal boundary
UBERON:0012437.def: An anatomical line that adjacent_to a epithelium and adjacent_to a mesenchyme.

UBERON:0012438.name: blastema of regenerating fin/limb
UBERON:0012438.def: A blastema that is part of a regenerating fin/limb.

UBERON:0012439.name: blastema of regenerating digit tip
UBERON:0012439.def: A blastema that is part of a distal segment of digit.

UBERON:0012441.name: endothelium of peritubular capillary
UBERON:0012441.def: An endothelium that is part of a peritubular capillary.

UBERON:0012442.name: epiploic foramen
UBERON:0012442.def: The passage of communication, or foramen, between the general cavity (of the abdomen), and the omental bursa.

UBERON:0012444.name: gastropege
UBERON:0012444.def: A single row of large ventral scales in snakes that aid locomotion.

UBERON:0012446.name: obsolete cloacal spur
UBERON:0012446.def: Retained pelvic vestiges found in birds. They are generally used in courtship and are more pronounced in males than females.

UBERON:0012447.name: podotheca
UBERON:0012447.def: A horny sheath covering the lower leg of some birds.

UBERON:0012448.name: Herbst's corpuscle
UBERON:0012448.def: The Corpuscles of Herbst or Herbst corpuscles are a nerve-ending similar to the Pacinian corpuscle, in the mucous membrane of the tongue, in pits on the beak and in other parts of the bodies of birds. It differs from the Pacinian corpuscle in being smaller, in its capsules being more closely approximated, and in that the axis-cylinder in the central clear space is coated with a continuous row of nuclei. In many wading birds, a large number of Herbst corpuscles are found embedded in pits on the mandibles that are believed to enable birds to sense prey under wet sand or soil.

UBERON:0012449.name: mechanoreceptor
UBERON:0012449.def: A sensory receptor that responds to mechanical pressure or distortion.

UBERON:0012450.name: Meissner's corpuscle
UBERON:0012450.def: A type of nerve ending in the skin that is responsible for sensitivity to light touch. In particular, they have highest sensitivity (lowest threshold) when sensing vibrations lower than 50 Hertz. They are rapidly adaptive receptors.
synonym: tactile corpuscles of Wagner and Meissner

UBERON:0012451.name: sensory receptor
UBERON:0012451.def: A sensory nerve ending that responds to a stimulus in the internal or external environment of an organism. In response to stimuli the sensory receptor initiates sensory transduction by creating graded potentials or action potentials in the same cell or in an adjacent one.

UBERON:0012453.name: nerve ending
UBERON:0012453.def: Specialized terminations of peripheral neurons. Nerve endings include NEUROEFFECTOR JUNCTION(s) by which neurons activate target organs and sensory receptors (see RECEPTORS, SENSORY) which transduce information from the various sensory modalities and send it centrally in the nervous system. Presynaptic nerve endings are PRESYNAPTIC TERMINALS.

UBERON:0012456.name: Merkel nerve ending
UBERON:0012456.def: Mechanoreceptors found in the skin and mucosa of vertebrates that provide touch information to the brain. The information they provide are those regarding pressure and texture. Each ending consists of a Merkel cell in close apposition with an enlarged nerve terminal.

UBERON:0012457.name: Ruffini nerve ending
UBERON:0012457.def: An encapsulated nerve receptor present in subpapillary dermis and deep dermis of hairy and glabrous skin.

UBERON:0012458.name: antler velvet
UBERON:0012458.def: Highly vascular skin called velvet that covers the antler whilst it grows, supplying oxygen and nutrients to the growing bone.

UBERON:0012459.name: antler pedicle
UBERON:0012459.def: Attachment point for antler on skull.

UBERON:0012462.name: proctodeum portion of cloaca
UBERON:0012462.def: Most distal cloacal compartment; function is copulation and in some species develops a penis[Kardong].

UBERON:0012463.name: cloacal lumen
UBERON:0012463.def: An anatomical space that is enclosed by a cloaca.

UBERON:0012464.name: cloacal vent
UBERON:0012464.def: The opening of the cloacal chamber to the outside of the organism. Birds maintain a single cloacal opening throughout their lives.

UBERON:0012465.name: lumen of terminal part of digestive tract
UBERON:0012465.def: An anatomical space that is enclosed by a terminal part of digestive tract.

UBERON:0012467.name: enclosed anatomical space
UBERON:0012467.def: An anatomical space with no opening to another space or to the exterior.

UBERON:0012468.name: anal tooth
UBERON:0012468.def: Triangular calcified papillae (often five) placed radially around the anus of some Holothuriidae.

UBERON:0012471.name: hepatogastric ligament
UBERON:0012471.def: Ligament extending between the liver and stomach.

UBERON:0012472.name: hepatoduodenal ligament
UBERON:0012472.def: The hepatoduodenal ligament is the portion of the lesser omentum extending between the porta hepatis of the liver and the superior part of the duodenum.

UBERON:0012473.name: oral cirrus
UBERON:0012473.def: Small tentacle-like structure surrounding the mouth; they act as sensory devices and as a filter for the water passing into the body.

UBERON:0012474.name: hepatic cecum
UBERON:0012474.def: A ventral evagination extending anteriorly in the mid-portion of the intestine in Amphioxi.

UBERON:0012475.name: skeleton of pectoral complex
UBERON:0012475.def: The collection of all skeletal elements in a pectoral complex - i.e. the combination of free limb or fin plus pectoral girdle.
synonym: set of bones of upper limb
skeleton of anterior limb/fin and girdle

UBERON:0012476.name: skeleton of pelvic complex
UBERON:0012476.def: The collection of all skeletal elements in a pelvic complex - i.e. the combination of free limb or fin plus pelvic girdle.
synonym: set of bones of lower limb
skeleton of posterior limb/fin and girdle

UBERON:0012477.name: dorsal part of neck
UBERON:0012477.def: The posterior region of the neck, including the suboccipital region.

UBERON:0012478.name: cloacal gland
UBERON:0012478.def: A gland that is part of a cloaca.

UBERON:0012479.name: urodeal gland
UBERON:0012479.def: A gland that is part of a urodeum.

UBERON:0012480.name: cloacal mucosa
UBERON:0012480.def: A mucosa that is part of a cloaca [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0012481.name: cloacal epithelium
UBERON:0012481.def: An epithelium that is part of a cloaca.

UBERON:0012482.name: submucosa of cloaca
UBERON:0012482.def: A submucosa that is part of a cloaca [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0012483.name: serosa of cloaca
UBERON:0012483.def: A serous membrane that is part of a cloaca [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0012486.name: muscle layer of cloaca
UBERON:0012486.def: A muscular coat that is part of a cloaca.

UBERON:0012487.name: vaginal sphincter
UBERON:0012487.def: A sphincter muscle that is part of a vagina.

UBERON:0012488.name: muscle layer of duodenum
UBERON:0012488.def: A muscular coat that is part of a duodenum.

UBERON:0012489.name: muscle layer of colon
UBERON:0012489.def: A muscular coat that is part of a colon.

UBERON:0012490.name: muscle layer of anal canal
UBERON:0012490.def: A muscular coat that is part of a anal canal.

UBERON:0012494.name: muscularis mucosae of duodenum
UBERON:0012494.def: A muscularis mucosa that is part of a duodenum.
synonym: lamina muscularis of duodenal mucous membrane

UBERON:0012497.name: muscularis mucosae of rectum
UBERON:0012497.def: A muscularis mucosa that is part of a rectum.
synonym: lamina muscularis of rectal mucous membrane

UBERON:0012498.name: serosa of appendix
UBERON:0012498.def: A serous membrane that is part of a vermiform appendix.

UBERON:0012499.name: serosa of fallopian tube
UBERON:0012499.def: A serous membrane that is part of a fallopian tube.

UBERON:0012503.name: serosa of fundus of stomach
UBERON:0012503.def: A serous membrane that is part of a fundus of stomach.
UBERON:0012503.synonym: visceral peritoneum of fundus of stomach

UBERON:0012504.name: adventitia of esophagus
UBERON:0012504.def: An adventitia that is part of a esophagus.

UBERON:0012520.name: forelimb epitrochlearis muscle
UBERON:0012520.def: The superficial-most muscle of the anterior surface of the arm is the epitrochlearis. It has no homolog in humans.

UBERON:0012615.name: umbilical smooth muscle
UBERON:0012615.def: A smooth muscle tissue that is part of a umbilical cord.

UBERON:0012621.name: muscle of Aristotle's lantern
UBERON:0012621.def: Any muscle organ that is part of a Aristotle's lantern.

UBERON:0012642.name: vestimentum muscle
UBERON:0012642.def: The vestimentum is a muscle that the tubeworm uses to anchro itself in the tube. Generates new tube material.

UBERON:0012643.name: plume
UBERON:0012643.def: Vascularized tip of their free end of a tubeworm which is an organ for exchanging compounds with the environment.

UBERON:0012644.name: trophosome
UBERON:0012644.def: An organ of dark green-brown spongy tissue in a tubeworm which is a host to symbiotic microbes.

UBERON:0012645.name: opisthosome
UBERON:0012645.def: Organ at the distal end of a tubeworm. Helps anchor the tubeworm.

UBERON:0012648.name: ampulla of fallopian tube
UBERON:0012648.def: The ampulla is the second portion of the uterine tube. It is an intermediate dilated portion, which curves over the ovary. It is the most common site of human fertilization. The word ampulla is from the Latin for flask.

UBERON:0012649.name: anococcygeus muscle
UBERON:0012649.def: One of a pair of thin sheets of smooth muscle inserting on the rectum, having a tendinous origin largely on sacral vertebrae.

UBERON:0012650.name: gastroduodenal junction
UBERON:0012650.def: An anatomical junction that connects a stomach and connects a duodenum.

UBERON:0012651.name: mucosa of gastroduodenal junction
UBERON:0012651.def: A mucosa that is part of a gastroduodenal junction.

UBERON:0012652.name: colorectum
UBERON:0012652.def: The subdivision of the digestive tract that consists of the colon and the rectum.

UBERON:0013067.name: colorectal mucosa
UBERON:0013067.def: A mucosa that is part of a colorectum.

UBERON:0013068.name: palatine torus
UBERON:0013068.def: A bony protuberance sometimes found on the hard palate at the junction of the intermaxillary suture and the transverse palatine suture.

UBERON:0013069.name: popliteal area
UBERON:0013069.def: A depression on the ventral side of the femur, at the knee joint, between the condyles.

UBERON:0013070.name: prepatagium
UBERON:0013070.def: A roughly triangular flap of skin on the wing of a bird or pterosaur which fills the space bounded by the humerus and ulna.

UBERON:0013074.name: cornual diverticulum
UBERON:0013074.def: An extension of the frontal sinus into the horn.

UBERON:0013075.name: venom gland duct
UBERON:0013075.def: A duct that is part of a venom gland.

UBERON:0013076.name: snake venom
UBERON:0013076.def: Solutions or mixtures of toxic and nontoxic substances elaborated by snake (Ophidia) salivary glands for the purpose of killing prey or disabling predators and delivered by grooved or hollow fangs. They usually contain enzymes, toxins, and other factors.

UBERON:0013078.name: venom-injecting tooth
UBERON:0013078.def: A fang that is used to inject venom into prey, through either a tube or a groove.

UBERON:0013106.name: elapid venom
UBERON:0013106.def: Venoms from snakes of the family Elapidae, including cobras, kraits, mambas, coral, tiger, and Australian snakes. The venoms contain polypeptide toxins of various kinds, cytolytic, hemolytic, and neurotoxic factors, but fewer enzymes than viper or crotalid venoms. Many of the toxins have been characterized.

UBERON:0013110.name: hydrophid venom
UBERON:0013110.def: Venoms of sea snakes, Hydrophiinae, found around Pacific islands. The venoms contain fewer enzymes and more neuro- or myotoxins than land snakes. The neurotoxic proteins are similar to elapid small, short, or type I neurotoxins, some of which have been characterized.

UBERON:0013112.name: viper venom
UBERON:0013112.def: Venoms from snakes of the viperid family. They tend to be less toxic than elapid or hydrophid venoms and act mainly on the vascular system, interfering with coagulation and capillary membrane integrity and are highly cytotoxic. They contain large amounts of several enzymes, other factors, and some toxins.

UBERON:0013113.name: angular/surangular bone
UBERON:0013113.def: Bone formed from the fusion of angular and surangular bones. Found in snakes.

UBERON:0013114.name: compressor glandulae muscle
UBERON:0013114.def: A prominent compressor muscle found in poisonous snakes that originates in the lower jaw, sweeps around the venom gland, and inserted on the gland's surface. The muscles acts to squeeze the gland and release venom.

UBERON:0013118.name: sulcus of brain
UBERON:0013118.def: A depression or fissure in the surface of the brain. It surrounds the gyri, creating the characteristic appearance of the brain in humans and other large mammals.

UBERON:0013119.name: haemal node
UBERON:0013119.def: A lymphoid organ found in various mammals and some birds.

UBERON:0013121.name: proximal epiphysis of phalanx of pes
synonym: basal epiphysis of phalanx of foot
proximal epiphysis of phalanx of toe

UBERON:0013122.name: distal epiphysis of phalanx of pes
synonym: distal end of phalanx of foot
distal epiphysis of phalanx of toe
ungual tuberosity of distal phalanx of toe

UBERON:0013124.name: left posterior cardinal vein
UBERON:0013124.def: A posterior cardinal vein that is in_the_left_side_of a multicellular organism.

UBERON:0013125.name: left subcardinal vein
UBERON:0013125.def: A subcardinal vein that is in_the_left_side_of a multicellular organism.

UBERON:0013126.name: vein of abdomen
UBERON:0013126.def: A vein that is part of a abdomen.

UBERON:0013127.name: pulmonary venous system
UBERON:0013127.def: The part of the venous system that drains the lungs[Kardong].

UBERON:0013128.name: bulb of penis
UBERON:0013128.def: Just before each crus of the penis meets its fellow it presents a slight enlargement, named by Kobelt the bulb of the corpus spongiosum penis. It is homologous to the vestibular bulbs in females.
synonym: bulb of the corpus cavernosum penis
bulb of the corpus spongiousum penis

UBERON:0013129.name: bulb of vestibule
UBERON:0013129.def: Aggregations of erectile tissue that are an internal part of the clitoris. They can also be found throughout the vestibule: next to the clitoral body, clitoral crura, urethra, urethral sponge, and vagina.

UBERON:0013132.name: penicillar arteriole
UBERON:0013132.def: One of the small straight arteries of the red pulp of the spleen; a branch of the spleen central artery that supplies the red pulp[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013133.name: superior phrenic artery
UBERON:0013133.def: A phrenic artery that arises from the lower part of the thoracic aorta and is distributed to the posterior part of the upper surface of the diaphragm, and anastomoses with the musculophrenic and pericardiacophrenic arteries.

UBERON:0013135.name: interdental plate
UBERON:0013135.def: The interdental plate refers to the bone-filled mesial-distal region between the teeth.

UBERON:0013136.name: vein of lip
UBERON:0013136.def: A vein that drains a lip.

UBERON:0013137.name: external pudendal artery
UBERON:0013137.def: Either the superficial or deep external pudendal arteries.

UBERON:0013138.name: coronary ligament of liver
UBERON:0013138.def: The coronary ligament of the liver refers to parts of the peritoneal reflections that hold the liver to the inferior surface of the diaphragm.

UBERON:0013139.name: ligament of liver
UBERON:0013139.def: A nonskeletal ligament that is part of a liver.

UBERON:0013140.name: systemic vein
UBERON:0013140.def: Any vein within the general circulation that transports blood back to the right atrium of the heart.

UBERON:0013141.name: capillary bed
UBERON:0013141.def: A localized group of blood capillaries.

UBERON:0013142.name: soleal vein
UBERON:0013142.def: A vein that drains the soleus.

UBERON:0013143.name: gastrocnemius vein
UBERON:0013143.def: A vein that drains the gastrocnemius.

UBERON:0013146.name: venous system of brain
UBERON:0013146.def: Missing definition for term UBERON:0013146. Please replace it using linked reference.

UBERON:0013151.name: choroidal artery
UBERON:0013151.def: One of two arteries (anterior and posterior choroidal artery) that supply blood to the choroid plexus, optic tract, hippocampus, globus pallidus, and other various brain regions.

UBERON:0013152.name: interventricular foramen of heart
UBERON:0013152.def: A temporary opening between the developing ventricles of the heart. The ventricles arise as a single cavity is divided by the developing interventricular septum. Before the septum closes completely, the remaining opening between the two ventricles is termed the interventricular foramen.

UBERON:0013153.name: arachnoid villus
UBERON:0013153.def: Small protrusions of the arachnoid mater into vascular sinuses, acting as one-way pressure-sensitive valves.

UBERON:0013158.name: foregut-midgut junction gland
UBERON:0013158.def: A gland that is part of a foregut-midgut junction.

UBERON:0013161.name: left lateral ventricle
UBERON:0013161.def: A telencephalic ventricle that is in_the_left_side_of a telencephalon.

UBERON:0013162.name: right lateral ventricle
UBERON:0013162.def: A telencephalic ventricle that is in_the_right_side_of a telencephalon.

UBERON:0013165.name: epiglottic vallecula
UBERON:0013165.def: A depression in front of the epiglottis, in which food is temporarily gathered as the animal chews.

UBERON:0013166.name: vallecula of cerebellum
UBERON:0013166.def: On the upper surface of the cerebellum the vermis is elevated above the level of the hemispheres, but on the under surface it is sunk almost out of sight in the bottom of a deep depression between them; this depression is called the vallecula of the cerebellum, and lodges the posterior part of the medulla oblongata.

UBERON:0013167.name: cricopharyngeal ligament
UBERON:0013167.def: Laryngeal ligament that connects the cricoid cartilage to the pharynx[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013168.name: thyroepiglottic ligament
UBERON:0013168.def: Laryngeal ligament that connects the epiglottis to the thyroid cartilage[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013169.name: vestibular ligament
UBERON:0013169.def: The vestibular fold is a fibroelastic band which passes from the ventral margin of the cuneiform cartilage to the cranial dorsal surface of the thyroid cartilage. It forms the support for the free edge of the vestibular fold.

UBERON:0013170.name: cricoarytenoid ligament
UBERON:0013170.def: Laryngeal ligament that connects the cricoid and arytenoid cartilages[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013171.name: cricothyroid ligament
UBERON:0013171.def: This attaches the caudal border of the thyroid cartilage to the ventral arch of the cricoid cartilage. Its sheetlike ventral portion is sometimes referred to as the cricothyroid membrane. Being elastic, it 'balances' movement at the hinge-like cricothyroid joint and determines the resting position of the larynx when the muscles are relaxed[MURDOCH]. The cricothyroid ligament is the larger part of the laryngeal membrane, continuing inferiorly as a median or anterior part and twin lateral ligaments. The median cricothyroid ligament is a flat band of white tissue joining the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, while the lateral cricothyroid ligament is also known as the cricothyroid membrane (also called conus elasticus).

UBERON:0013172.name: cricotracheal ligament
UBERON:0013172.def: The cricotracheal ligament connects the cricoid cartilage with the first ring of the trachea[WP]. The caudal border of the cricoid cartilage is joined to the first ring of the trachea by this ligament. It is an extrinsic laryngeal ligament. It resembles the fibrous membrane which connects the cartilaginous rings of the trachea to each other.

UBERON:0013173.name: anterior part of tympanic bone
UBERON:0013173.def: The anterior aspect of the tympanum.

UBERON:0013174.name: sigmoid process of tympanic bone
UBERON:0013174.def: A wavy crest externally on the tympanic bone of cetaceans.

UBERON:0013175.name: nasal air sac
UBERON:0013175.def: An air sac opening into the passage of the blowhole that is hypothesized to be involved in echolocation.

UBERON:0013182.name: core of melon organ
UBERON:0013182.def: The core component of the ovoid-shaped, fatty organ found in the forehead of all toothed whales.

UBERON:0013188.name: monkey lips dorsal bursa complex
UBERON:0013188.def: A structure consisting of a pair of anterior and posterior dorsal bursae in which a pair of phonic lips are embedded, along with the bursal cartilage and a blowhole ligament.

UBERON:0013190.name: entotympanic bone
UBERON:0013190.def: Entotympanics are independent elements present in the auditory bullae of various eutherians.

UBERON:0013191.name: ovarian cortex
UBERON:0013191.def: The layer of the ovarian stroma lying immediately beneath the tunica albuginea, composed of connective tissue cells and fibers, among which are scattered primary and secondary (antral) follicles in various stages of development; the cortex varies in thickness according to the age of the individual, becoming thinner with advancing years; included in the follicles are the cumulus oophorus, membrana granulosa (and the granulosa cells inside it), corona radiata, zona pellucida, and primary oocyte; the zona pellucida, theca of follicle, antrum and liquor folliculi are also contained in the follicle; also in the cortex is the corpus luteum derived from the follicles.

UBERON:0013192.name: ovarian medulla
UBERON:0013192.def: Highly vascular stroma found in the center of the ovary that forms from embryonic mesenchyme and contains blood vessels, lymphatic vessels, and nerves; this stroma forms the tissue of the hilum by which the ovarian ligament is attached, and through which the blood vessels enter; it does not contain any ovarian follicles.

UBERON:0013193.name: parakeratinized epithelium
UBERON:0013193.def: An epithelium that is characterized by incomplete keratinization of the cells in the stratum corneum. The cells are flattened and composed primarily of packed tonofilaments. However, the cells may retain remnants of nuclei and other organelles.

UBERON:0013194.name: orthokeratinized epithelium
UBERON:0013194.def: A keratinized epithelium in which the cells of the stratum corneum become very flat, loose their nuclei and cytoplasmic organelles and are now composed of densely packed tonofilaments cemented by filaggrin.

UBERON:0013195.name: parakeratinized epithelium of gingiva
UBERON:0013195.def: A parakeratinized epithelium that is part of a gingiva.

UBERON:0013196.name: strand of wool
UBERON:0013196.def: A strand of pelage hair that is crimped and grows in clusters.

UBERON:0013198.name: cocoon
UBERON:0013198.def: A casing spun of silk by many moth caterpillars, and numerous other holometabolous insect larvae as a protective covering for the pupa[WP].

UBERON:0013201.name: olfactory pathway
UBERON:0013201.def: Set of nerve fibers conducting impulses from olfactory receptors to the cerebral cortex. It includes the olfactory nerve; olfactory bulb; olfactory tract, olfactory tubercle, anterior perforated substance, and olfactory cortex. The term rhinencephalon is restricted to structures in the CNS receiving fibers from the olfactory bulb.

UBERON:0013203.name: hypogastrium
UBERON:0013203.def: The hypogastrium (or hypogastric region, or pubic region) is an area of the human abdomen located below the navel.

UBERON:0013204.name: epipubic bone
UBERON:0013204.def: One of a pair of bones running antero-laterally from the centre of the pubis in marsupials and some other mammals.

UBERON:0013206.name: nasal tentacle
UBERON:0013206.def: A fleshy appendage ringing the snout of a Star-nosed mole.

UBERON:0013207.name: entepicondylar foramen
UBERON:0013207.def: A canal through the medial epicondyle at the distal end of the vertebrate humerus, usually traversed by the median nerve and brachial artery.

UBERON:0013208.name: Grueneberg ganglion
UBERON:0013208.def: An olfactory ganglion at the entrance of the nose of mammals that is involved in the detection of alarm pheromones and cold temperatures.

UBERON:0013211.name: cerumen gland
UBERON:0013211.def: A specialized sudoriferous gland (sweat glands) located subcutaneously in the external auditory canal.

UBERON:0013212.name: anal sac gland secretion
UBERON:0013212.def: A bodily secretion that is produced by a gland of anal sac.

UBERON:0013213.name: ossicone
UBERON:0013213.def: Ossicones are horn-like protuberances on the heads of giraffes, male okapis, and their extinct relatives, such as Sivatherium, and the climacoceratids, such as Climacoceras. Only giraffids have true ossicones (as opposed to horns or antlers). The base that a deer's antlers grow from is very similar to ossicones. Ossicones are similar to the horns of antelopes and cattle, save that they are derived from ossified cartilage, and that the ossicones remain covered in skin and fur, rather than horn. Antlers (such as on deer) are derived from bone tissue: when mature, the skin and fur covering of the antlers, termed 'velvet,' is sloughed and scraped off to expose the bone of the antlers.

UBERON:0013216.name: udder
UBERON:0013216.def: A large pendulous organ consisting of two or more mammary glands enclosed in a common envelope and each provided with a single nipple.

UBERON:0013217.name: zygomatic plate
UBERON:0013217.def: In rodent anatomy, the zygomatic plate is a bony plate derived from the flattened front part of the zygomatic arch (cheekbone). At the back, it connects to the front (maxillary) root of the zygomatic arch, and at the top it is connected to the rest of the skull via the antorbital bridge. It is part of the maxillary bone, or upper jaw, which also contains the upper cheekteeth. Primitively, rodents have a nearly horizontal zygomatic plate. In association with specializations in zygomasseteric system, several distinct morphologies have developed across the order. The term is also used for an analogous structure in some South American typotheres, including Pseudotypotherium and Medistylus.

UBERON:0013218.name: rete mirabile
UBERON:0013218.def: A rete mirabile (Latin for 'wonderful net'; plural retia mirabilia) is a complex of arteries and veins lying very close to each other, found in some vertebrates. The rete mirabile utilizes countercurrent blood flow within the net (blood flowing in opposite directions. ) It exchanges heat, ions, or gases between vessel walls so that the two bloodstreams within the rete maintain a gradient with respect to temperature, or concentration of gases or solutes.

UBERON:0013219.name: parotoid gland
UBERON:0013219.def: The parotoid gland (alternatively, paratoid gland) is an external skin gland on the back, neck, and shoulder of toads and some frogs and salamanders. It secretes a milky alkaloid substance to deter predators. The substance produced acts as a neurotoxin. Parotoid glands are sometimes said to be wart-like in appearance, though warts are abnormal growths caused by viral infections while parotoid glands are normal, healthy parts of the animals that bear them. The vague similarity in appearance, however, is the reason behind the mistaken belief that touching a toad causes warts.

UBERON:0013220.name: foramen of Panizza
UBERON:0013220.def: A hole with that connects the left and right aorta in animals of the order Crocodilia.

UBERON:0013221.name: caudofemoralis
UBERON:0013221.def: The caudofemoralis (from the latin cauda, tail and femur, thighbone) is a muscle found in the pelvic limb of mostly all animals possessing a tail, since it is a synapomorphy appeared on the Archosauria clade. It is thus found in felids (cats) and Mustela ('Weasels'), but also on crocodiles and birds.

UBERON:0013222.name: otic notch
UBERON:0013222.def: Otic notches are invagination in the posterior margin of the skull roof, one behind each orbit. Such notches are found in labyrinthodonts and some of their immediate ancestors, but not their reptilian descendants. The presence or absence of the otic notches is one of the traits used to separate the amniotes from the amphibian grade tetrapods.

UBERON:0013223.name: alveolar gland
UBERON:0013223.def: In contrast to tubular glands, in the second main variety of gland, the secretory portion is enlarged and the lumen variously increased in size. These are termed alveolar glands (or saccular glands, or acinar glands, or acinous glands). Some sources draw a clear distinction between acinar and alveolar glands, based upon the shape of the lumen. A further complication in the case of the alveolar glands may occur in the form of still smaller saccular diverticuli growing out from the main sacculi. These are termed alveoli. The term 'tubulo-alveolar' (or 'tubulo-acinar', or 'compound tubulo-acinar', or 'compound tubulo-alveolar') is used to describe glands that start out as branched tubular, and branch further to terminate in alveoli. This type of gland is found in the salivary glands, esophagus, and mammary glands. The term 'racemose gland' is used to describe a 'compound alveolar gland' or 'compound acinar gland'.

UBERON:0013224.name: Ciaccio's gland
UBERON:0013224.def: Ciaccio's glands are small tubular accessory lacrimal glands (glandulae lacrimales accessoriae) found in the lacrimal caruncle of the eyelid. They are located in the upper border of the tarsus, approximately in the middle between the extremities of the tarsal glands. Sometimes they are situated slightly above the tarsus. There are usually 2 to 5 of these glands in the upper eyelid, and their function is to produce tears which are secreted onto the surface of the conjunctiva. They are named after Italian anatomist Giuseppe Vincenzo Ciaccio (1824b1901), who described these glands in 1874. They are sometimes called Wolfring's glands after Polish ophthalmologist Emilj von Wolfring (1832-1906), who described them during the same time period as did Ciaccio. Another type of accessory lacrimal gland are Krause's glands, which are smaller, more numerous than Ciaccio's glands and are found along the superior and inferior fornices of the conjunctival sac.

UBERON:0013226.name: accessory lacrimal gland
UBERON:0013226.def: Serous gland with distended lumen. It includes the gland of Krause in the lacrimal sac and the gland of Wolfring on the inner surface of the upper eyelid. (NCI).

UBERON:0013227.name: crypt of Henle
UBERON:0013227.def: Crypts of Henle are microscopic pockets found in scattered sections of the conjunctiva around the eyeball. They are responsible for secreting mucin, a proteinous substance that makes up the inner layer of tears. It coats the cornea to provide a hydrophilic layer that allows for even distribution of the tear film. The layer of mucin allows tears to glide evenly across the eye's surface[WP].

UBERON:0013228.name: sweat gland of eyelid
UBERON:0013228.def: Glands of Moll, also known as ciliary glands, are modified apocrine sweat glands that are found on the margin of the eyelid. They are next to the base of the eyelashes, and anterior to the Meibomian glands within the distal eyelid margin. These glands are relatively large and tubular-shaped. The glands of Moll are named after Dutch oculist Jacob Anton Moll (1832-1914). Glands of Moll empty into the adjacent lashes. Glands of Moll and Zeis secrete lipid that adds to the superficial layer of the tear film, retarding evaporation. The glands of Moll are prone to infection and blockage of its duct with sebum and cell debris. Blockage of the gland's duct causes swelling which can manifest itself as a stye.

UBERON:0013229.name: eyelid gland
UBERON:0013229.def: Any gland that is part of an eyelid. This includes sebaceous glands (Zeis gland, tarsal gland) and sweat glands (Moll's gland).

UBERON:0013230.name: nictitans gland
UBERON:0013230.def: A gland producing tears in a third eyelid in the corner of each eye.
synonym: superficial gland of the nictitating membrane
superficial gland of the third eyelid

UBERON:0013231.name: sebaceous gland of eyelid
UBERON:0013231.def: Any of the sebaceous glands that are in the eyelid. Examples: gland of Zeis (services eyelashes), gland of Meibom (tarsal gland - unconnected to eyelids).

UBERON:0013232.name: serous acinus
UBERON:0013232.def: The secretory unit of a serous gland. The acinar portion is composed of serous secreting cells.

UBERON:0013233.name: supraorbital gland
UBERON:0013233.def: A lateral nasal gland that removes sodium chloride from the bloodstream.

UBERON:0013234.name: violet gland
UBERON:0013234.def: The violet gland or supracaudal gland is an important gland located on the upper surface of the tail of certain mammals, including European badgers and canids such as foxes, wolves the domestic dog, as well as the domestic cat. It is used for intra species signalling, scent marking, and contributes to the strong odor of foxes in particular.

UBERON:0013235.name: ventrum
UBERON:0013235.def: A major organism subdivisionthat is the entire part of an anatomical structure ventral to a horizontal plane and bounded on one side by the same horizontal plane.

UBERON:0013236.name: ventral trunk
UBERON:0013236.def: The subdivision of the trunk that overlaps with the ventrum.

UBERON:0013237.name: genital papilla of vulva
UBERON:0013237.def: The genital papilla is a part of female external genitalia not present in humans, which appears as a small, fleshy flab of tissue. The papilla covers the opening of the vagina.

UBERON:0013239.name: future glans penis
UBERON:0013239.def: A future glans that is part of a male genital tubercle.

UBERON:0013240.name: future glans clitoris
UBERON:0013240.def: A future glans that is part of a female genital tubercle.

UBERON:0013244.name: vaginal plate
UBERON:0013244.def: The vaginal plate is a precursor to the inferior portion of the vagina. They form from sinovaginal bulbs.

UBERON:0013245.name: sinovaginal bulb
UBERON:0013245.def: Solid evaginations of the UG sinus that develops into a vaginal plate that which will will eventually canalize to form the inferior portion of the vagina.

UBERON:0013247.name: male paramesonephric duct
UBERON:0013247.def: An epithelial tube that develops from a Mullerian duct in a male. Later degenerates.
UBERON:0013247.synonym: degenerating mesonephric portion of male paramesonephric duct

UBERON:0013248.name: paradidymis
UBERON:0013248.def: A small collection of convoluted tubules, situated in front of the lower part of the cord above the head of the epididymis. These tubes are lined with columnar ciliated epithelium, and probably represent the remains of a part of the Wolffian body but are functionless and vestigial. The Wolffian body operates as a kidney (metanephros) in fishes and amphibians, but the corresponding tissue is co-opted to form parts of the male reproductive system in other classes of vertebrate. The paradidymis represents a remnant of an unused, atrophied part of the Wolffian body[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013249.name: paroophoron
UBERON:0013249.def: A collection of a few scattered rudimentary tubules child, situated in the broad ligament between the epoophoron and the uterus.

UBERON:0013250.name: vesicular appendage of epoophoron
UBERON:0013250.def: In connection with the fimbriae of the uterine tube, or with the broad ligament close to them, there are frequently one or more small pedunculated vesicles. These are termed the vesicular appendages of the epoophoron.

UBERON:0013262.name: remnnant of ductus deferens
UBERON:0013262.def: Remnant in a female of the portion of the embryonic mesonephric duct that develops into the ductus deferens in males.

UBERON:0013277.name: remnant of processus vaginalis
UBERON:0013277.def: Incompletely obliterated remnants of the vaginal process of the peritoneum remaining in the spermatic cord.

UBERON:0013278.name: canal of Nuck
UBERON:0013278.def: A patent pouch of peritoneum extending into the labia majora of women. It is analogous to the processus vaginalis in males. The pouch accompanies the gubernaculum during development of the urinary and reproductive organs, more specifically during the descent of the ovaries, and normally obliterates.

UBERON:0013279.name: diaphysis of fibula
UBERON:0013279.def: A diaphysis that is part of a fibula[Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0013280.name: diaphysis of tibia
UBERON:0013280.def: A diaphysis that is part of a tibia.

UBERON:0013397.name: stratum argenteum of choroid
UBERON:0013397.def: A silver reflective layer in the outer choroid, adjacent to the sclera, frequently present in fish larvae but not as frequent in adults.

UBERON:0013398.name: choroidal gland
UBERON:0013398.def: A gland that is part of a optic choroid.

UBERON:0013403.name: asterion of skull
UBERON:0013403.def: The asterion is the point on the skull corresponding to the posterior end of the parietomastoid suture.

UBERON:0013406.name: bregma
UBERON:0013406.def: The bregma is the anatomical point on the skull at which the coronal suture is intersected perpendicularly by the sagittal suture.

UBERON:0013411.name: cranial cavity
UBERON:0013411.def: Anatomical cavity that is the lumen of the skull and contains the brain.

UBERON:0013412.name: crotaphion
UBERON:0013412.def: The crotaphion refers to two points on the skull at the tips of the greater wing of sphenoid bone. It is near the pterion.

UBERON:0013417.name: epicranium
UBERON:0013417.def: The Epicranium is the medical term for the collection of structures covering the cranium. It consists of the muscles, aponeurosis, and skin.

UBERON:0013420.name: groove for sigmoid sinus
UBERON:0013420.def: Groove for Sigmoid Sinus is a groove in the posterior cranial fossa.

UBERON:0013422.name: infratemporal fossa
UBERON:0013422.def: The infratemporal fossa is an irregularly shaped cavity, situated below and medial to the zygomatic arch. Boundaries defined by: anteriorly, by the infratemporal surface of the maxilla and the ridge which descends from its zygomatic process posteriorly, by the articular tubercle of the temporal and the spinal angularis of the sphenoid superiorly, by the greater wing of the sphenoid below the infratemporal crest, and by the under surface of the temporal squama, containing the foramen ovale, which transmits the mandibular branch of the trigeminal nerve, and the foramen spinosum, which transmits the middle meningeal artery inferiorly, by the medial pterygoid muscle attaching to the mandible medially, by the lateral pterygoid plate laterally, by the ramus of mandible, which contains the mandibular foramen, leading to the mandibular canal through which the inferior alveolar nerve passes. This also contains the lingula, a triangular piece of bone that overlies the mandibular foramen antero-medially. Finally, the mylohyoid groove descends obliquely transmitting the mylohyoid nerve the only motor branch of the anterior division of the trigeminal nerve.

UBERON:0013423.name: jugal point
UBERON:0013423.def: The jugal point is the point at the anterior end of the upper border of the zygomatic arch where the masseteric and maxillary edges meet at an angle.

UBERON:0013424.name: anatomical point connecting sagittal and lambdoidal sutures
UBERON:0013424.def: The occipital angle is rounded and corresponds with the point of meeting of the sagittal and lambdoidal sutures-a point which is termed the lambda (after the Greek letter of the same name); in the fetus this part of the skull is membranous, and is called the posterior fontanelle.

UBERON:0013426.name: obelion
UBERON:0013426.def: The point of the sagittal suture which is on a level with the parietal foramina.

UBERON:0013427.name: occipital bun
UBERON:0013427.def: A prominent bulge, or projection, of the occipital bone at the back of the skull[WP].

UBERON:0013428.name: ophryon
UBERON:0013428.def: The ophryon is the point in the forehead just above the optic foramen, or eyesocket, and glabella.

UBERON:0013436.name: porion
UBERON:0013436.def: The porion is the point on the human skull located at the upper margin of each ear canal (external auditory meatus, external acoustic meatus). It underlies the tragus. The anatomical landmark has significance in biological anthropology and craniometry.

UBERON:0013442.name: postorbital process
UBERON:0013442.def: The Postorbital Process marks the rear, upper edge of the eye socket and is a projection from the frontal bone.

UBERON:0013445.name: pterygomaxillary fissure
UBERON:0013445.def: The pterygomaxillary fissure is a fissure of the human skull. It is vertical, and descends at right angles from the medial end of the inferior orbital fissure; it is a triangular interval, formed by the divergence of the maxilla from the pterygoid process of the sphenoid. It connects the infratemporal with the pterygopalatine fossa, and transmits the terminal part of the maxillary artery. Alveolar branches of the maxillary nerve go from the pterygopalatine fossa to the infratemporal region via this fissure. In older texts, the pterygomaxillary fissure is sometimes called the pterygopalatine fissure.

UBERON:0013447.name: sagittal crest of skull
UBERON:0013447.def: A ridge of bone running lengthwise along the midline of the top of the skull of many mammalian and reptilian skulls and serves as an attachment site for the temporailis muscle[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013448.name: sagittal keel
UBERON:0013448.def: The Sagittal keel (torus) is a thickening of bone on part or all of the midline of the frontal bone, or parietal bones where they meet along the sagittal suture, or on both bones..

UBERON:0013450.name: simian shelf
UBERON:0013450.def: A bony buttress on the inner surface of the foremost part of the ape mandible, functioning to reinforce the mandible.

UBERON:0013454.name: spheno-maxillary fossa
UBERON:0013454.def: The speno-maxillary fossa is a small triangular space situated at the angle of the junction of the spheno-maxillary and pterygo-maxillary fissures, and placed beneath the apex of the orbit. It is formed above by the under surface of the body of the sphenoid and by the orbital process of the palate bone.

UBERON:0013455.name: spheno-petrosal fissure
UBERON:0013455.def: The sphenopetrosal fissure (or sphenopetrosal suture) is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the petrous portion of the temporal bone. It is in the middle cranial fossa.

UBERON:0013459.name: stephanion
UBERON:0013459.def: The point where the upper temporal line cuts the coronal suture is named the stephanion.

UBERON:0013460.name: suprainiac fossa
UBERON:0013460.def: The suprainiac fossa is an elliptic depression on the occiput above the superior nuchal line, or inion.

UBERON:0013462.name: sylvian point
UBERON:0013462.def: The Sylvian point is the point on the human skull nearest the Sylvian fissure and is located about 30 millimeters behind the Zygomatic process of frontal bone.

UBERON:0013463.name: temporal fossa
UBERON:0013463.def: The temporal fossa is a shallow depression on the side of the skull bounded by the temporal lines and terminating below the level of the zygomatic arch.

UBERON:0013466.name: obsolete zygomasseteric system
UBERON:0013466.def: The zygomasseteric system (or zygomasseteric structure) in rodents is the anatomical arrangement of the masseter muscle of the jaw and the zygomatic arch of the skull. The anteroposterior or propalinal (front-to-back) motion of the rodent jaw is enabled by an extension of the zygomatic arch and the division of the masseter into three distinct parts. The main types are described as protrogomorphous, sciuromorphous, hystricomorphous, and myomorphous.

UBERON:0013468.name: zygomatic fossa
UBERON:0013468.def: The Zygomatic Fossa is an irregularly shaped cavity, situated below and on the inner side of the zygoma; bounded, in front, by the zygomatic surface of the superior maxillary bone and the ridge which descends from its malar process; behind, by the posterior border of the external pterygoid plate and the eminentia articularis; above, by the pterygoid ridge on the outer surface of the great wing of the sphenoid and the under part of the squamous portion of the temporal; below by the alveolar border of the superior maxilla; internally, by the external pterygoid plate; and externally, by the zygomatic arch ramus of the lower jaw. It contains the lower part of the temporal, the External and Internal pterygoid muscles, the internal maxillary artery and vein, and inferior maxillary nerve and their branches. At its upper and inner part may be observed two fissures, the spheno-maxillary and pterygo-maxillary.

UBERON:0013469.name: external occipital protuberance
UBERON:0013469.def: Near the middle of the occipital squama is the external occipital protuberance, and extending lateralward from it on either side is the superior nuchal line, and above this the faintly marked highest nuchal line. It is less pronounced in females. The inion is the highest point of the external occipital protuberance. a projection on the external surface of the squamous part of the occipital bone in the midline.

UBERON:0013471.name: retromolar space
UBERON:0013471.def: The retromolar space or retromolar gap is a space at the rear of a mandible, between the back of the last molar and the anterior edge of the ascending ramus where it crosses the alveolar margin.[WP].

UBERON:0013472.name: upper esophagus
UBERON:0013472.def: The upper one third of esophagus in which the muscle layer is composed of muscle cells of the striated type.

UBERON:0013473.name: lower esophagus
UBERON:0013473.def: The lower one third of the esophagus in which the muscle layer is composed of muscle cells predominantly of the smooth type.

UBERON:0013474.name: middle part of esophagus
UBERON:0013474.def: The middle one third of the esophagus in which the muscle layer is composed of muscle cells of the striated and smooth types.

UBERON:0013475.name: gustatory gland
UBERON:0013475.def: A serous salivary gland which resides adjacent to the moats surrounding the circumvallate papillae in the posterior one-third of the tongue, anterior to the terminal sulcus.

UBERON:0013476.name: dermal layer of tongue
UBERON:0013476.def: Missing definition for term UBERON:0013476. Please replace it using linked reference.

UBERON:0013477.name: blowhole
UBERON:0013477.def: A hole at the top of a cetacean's head through which the animal breathes air.

UBERON:0013478.name: cecal tonsil
UBERON:0013478.def: A thickened round patch of lymphoid tissue located at the ileocecal junction adjacent to the sacculus rotundus.

UBERON:0013479.name: lung endothelium
UBERON:0013479.def: A blood vessel endothelium that is part of a lung [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0013481.name: crypt of Lieberkuhn of ileum
UBERON:0013481.def: An intestinal crypt that is located in the ileum.

UBERON:0013482.name: crypt of Lieberkuhn of duodenum
UBERON:0013482.def: An intestinal crypt that is located in the duodenum.

UBERON:0013483.name: crypt of Lieberkuhn of jejunum
UBERON:0013483.def: An intestinal crypt that is located in the jejunum.

UBERON:0013485.name: crypt of Lieberkuhn of colon
UBERON:0013485.def: An intestinal crypt that is located in the colon. The colonic crypts of Lieberkühn are straight and unbranched and lined largely with goblet cells.

UBERON:0013486.name: crypt of Lieberkuhn of appendix
UBERON:0013486.def: An intestinal crypt that is located in the appendix.

UBERON:0013487.name: epidermal ridge of digit
UBERON:0013487.def: The grooves in the outermost layer of skin on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet where sweat glands open.

UBERON:0013488.name: panniculus adiposus
UBERON:0013488.def: The panniculus adiposus is the fatty layer of the subcutaneous tissues, superficial to a deeper vestigial layer of muscle, the panniculus carnosus. An example is the Fascia of Camper. Another example is the superficial cervical fascia[WP].

UBERON:0013489.name: superficial cervical fascia
UBERON:0013489.def: Superficial cervical fascia is a thin layer of subcutaneous connective tissue that lies between the dermis of the skin and the deep cervical fascia. It contains the platysma, cutaneous nerves, blood, and lymphatic vessels. It also contains a varying amount of fat, which is its distinguishing characteristic.
synonym: superficial layer of deep cervical fascia

UBERON:0013490.name: deep cervical fascia
UBERON:0013490.def: The deep cervical fascia (or fascia colli in older texts) lies under cover of the Platysma, and invests the neck; it also forms sheaths for the carotid vessels, and for the structures situated in front of the vertebral column. Its attachment to the hyoid bone prevents the formation of a dewlap. The investing portion of the fascia is attached behind to the ligamentum nucha and to the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra. The 'alar fascia' is a portion of deep cervical fascia.

UBERON:0013491.name: cervical fascia
UBERON:0013491.def: Any fascia tissue that is part of the neck region.

UBERON:0013492.name: prevertebral cervical fascia
UBERON:0013492.def: The prevertebral fascia (or prevertebral layer of cervical fascia) is a fascia in the neck.
synonym: prevertebral layer of deep cervical fascia

UBERON:0013493.name: abdominal fascia
UBERON:0013493.def: A fascia that is part of a abdomen.

UBERON:0013494.name: keratin-coated spine
UBERON:0013494.def: A modified strand of hair covered in a keratin coat, as found in porcupines and hedgehogs.

UBERON:0013495.name: barbed keratin-coated spine
UBERON:0013495.def: A keratin-coated spine that is tipped with a barb.

UBERON:0013496.name: unbarbed keratin-coated spine
UBERON:0013496.def: A keratin-coated spine that is lacks a barbed end.

UBERON:0013497.name: muscularis orbicularis
UBERON:0013497.def: A fringe of muscle running along the periphery of the panniculus.

UBERON:0013501.name: cloacal sphincter
UBERON:0013501.def: A sphincter muscle that is part of a cloaca.

UBERON:0013502.name: 5th arch mesenchyme
UBERON:0013502.def: A mesenchyme that is part of a pharyngeal arch 5.

UBERON:0013503.name: caudal vertebra cartilage element
UBERON:0013503.def: A caudal vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of cartilage tissue.

UBERON:0013504.name: caudal vertebra pre-cartilage condensation
UBERON:0013504.def: A caudal vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of a pre-cartilage condensation.

UBERON:0013505.name: cervical vertebra cartilage element
UBERON:0013505.def: A cervical vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of cartilage tissue.

UBERON:0013506.name: cervical vertebra pre-cartilage condensation
UBERON:0013506.def: A cervical vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of a pre-cartilage condensation.

UBERON:0013507.name: thoracic vertebra cartilage element
UBERON:0013507.def: A thoracic vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of cartilage tissue.

UBERON:0013508.name: thoracic vertebra pre-cartilage condensation
UBERON:0013508.def: A thoracic vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of a pre-cartilage condensation.

UBERON:0013509.name: lumbar vertebra cartilage element
UBERON:0013509.def: A lumbar vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of cartilage tissue.

UBERON:0013510.name: lumbar vertebra pre-cartilage condensation
UBERON:0013510.def: A lumbar vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of a pre-cartilage condensation.

UBERON:0013511.name: ambiens muscle
UBERON:0013511.def: A long muscle found in reptiles that originates on the ilium and crosses the acetabulum and the knee joint before being inserted on the tibia.

UBERON:0013513.name: anal pterya
UBERON:0013513.def: One of two rows of feathers encircling the cloaca.

UBERON:0013514.name: space surrounding organism
UBERON:0013514.def: The space that surrounds an organism.

UBERON:0013515.name: subdivision of oviduct
UBERON:0013515.def: A section through the tube or network of tubes that connects the ovaries to the outside of the body.

UBERON:0013516.name: uterine tube magnum
UBERON:0013516.def: The second segment of the oviduct. This is where most of the egg white is added to the egg as it moves down the duct.

UBERON:0013519.name: avian uterine tube isthmus
UBERON:0013519.def: The third segment of the oviduct. At this point in the egg's journey down the oviduct, the membranes form and calcification starts.

UBERON:0013523.name: lateral vaginal canal
UBERON:0013523.def: One of two lateral tracts connecting a uterus to a common median tract separated from the median vagina via ureters which prevent their fusion. Found in marsupials.

UBERON:0013524.name: median vaginal canal
UBERON:0013524.def: A median canal in the reproductive system of marsupials that connects the uteri to a common tract, joining with the two lateral vaginas. Connects the uterine openings directly with the urogenital sinus.

UBERON:0013525.name: stomach lumen
UBERON:0013525.def: The anatomical space that is enclosed by a stomach.

UBERON:0013526.name: otocyst lumen
UBERON:0013526.def: An anatomical cavity that is part of a ear vesicle.

UBERON:0013527.name: pectoral flipper tubercle
UBERON:0013527.def: A bump or swelling adorining the head and leading edge of a pectoral flipper, associated with the multiple joints and terminal phalanges as found in the multiple phalanges of the humpback whale.

UBERON:0013528.name: Brodmann (1909) area 11
UBERON:0013528.def: Brodmann area 11 is one of Brodmann's cytologically defined regions of the brain. It is involved in planning, reasoning, and decision making.

UBERON:0013529.name: Brodmann area
UBERON:0013529.def: A segmentation of the cerebral cortex on the basis of cytoarchitecture as described in Brodmann-1905, Brodmann-1909 and Brodmann-10. Maps for several species were presented. NeuroNames includes only areas in the human and in Old World monkeys.
