Of the latter, Brodmann studied representatives of several species including guenons (one Cercopithecus mona, one Cercocebus torquatus, and one Cercopithecus otherwise unspecified), which are all closely related African species, and one macaque (Macaca mulatta) an Asian species (Brodmann-1905). The legend to the summary map in Brodmann-1909 ascribes the areas simply to Cercopithecus. Brodmann referenced the areas by name and number. The same area number in humans and monkeys did not necessarily refer to topologically or cytoarchitecturally homologous structures. In NeuroNames the standard term for human areas consists of the English translation of Brodmann's Latin name followed by the number he assigned, e.g., agranular frontal area 6; the standard terms for monkey areas are in the format: area 6 of Brodmann-1909. He mapped a portion of areas limited to the banks of sulci, e.g., area 3 of Brodmann-1909 (Brodmann-1909) onto the adjacent, visible surface. This accounts for the fact that some areas appear larger on his surface map than on maps of other authors, e.g., area 3 of Vogts-1919. (Adapted from NeuroNames).

UBERON:0013531.name: retrosplenial region
UBERON:0013531.def: The retrosplenial region is a brain area and part of the cingulate cortex. It is defined by Brodmann area 26, Brodmann area 29 and the Brodmann area 30.

UBERON:0013535.name: Brodmann (1909) area 4
UBERON:0013535.def: The term area 4 of Brodmann-1909 refers to a cytoarchitecturally defined portion of the frontal lobe of the guenon. It is located predominantly in the precentral gyrus. Brodmann-1909 regarded it as topographically and cytoarchitecturally homologous to the human gigantopyramidal area 4 and noted that it occupies a much greater fraction of the frontal lobe in the monkey than in the human. Distinctive features (Brodmann-1905): the cortex is unusually thick; the layers are not distinct; the cells are relatively sparsely distributed; giant pyramidal (Betz) cells are present in the internal pyramidal layer (V); lack of an internal granular layer (IV) such that the boundary between the external pyramidal layer (III) and the internal pyramidal layer (V) is indistinct; lack of a distinct external granular layer (II); a gradual transition from the multiform layer (VI) to the subcortical white matter.

UBERON:0013538.name: Brodmann (1909) area 7
UBERON:0013538.def: Brodmann area 7 is one of Brodmann's cytologically defined regions of the brain. It is involved in locating objects in space. It serves as a point of convergence between vision and proprioception to determine where objects are in relation to parts of the body.

UBERON:0013539.name: Brodmann (1909) area 8
UBERON:0013539.def: Brodmann area 8 is one of Brodmann's cytologically defined regions of the brain. It is involved in planning complex movements.

UBERON:0013541.name: Brodmann (1909) area 10
UBERON:0013541.def: Brodmann area 10, or BA10, is part of the frontal cortex in the human brain. BA10 encompasses the most anterior part of the frontal cortex, known as the frontopolar region. This area is believed to play a part in strategic processes involved in memory retrieval and executive function. This area is also called frontopolar area 10, and it refers to a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined frontal region of cerebral cortex. It occupies the most rostral portions of the superior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus. In humans, on the medial aspect of the hemisphere it is bounded ventrally by the superior rostral sulcus (H). It does not extend as far as the cingulate sulcus. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded dorsally by the granular frontal area 9, caudally by the middle frontal area 46, and ventrally by the orbital area 47 and by the rostral area 12 or, in an early version of Brodmann's cortical map (Brodmann-1909), the prefrontal Brodmann area 11-1909.

UBERON:0013543.name: Brodmann (1909) area 12
UBERON:0013543.def: Brodmann area 12 is a subdivision of the cerebral cortex of the guenon defined on the basis of cytoarchitecture. It occupies the most rostral portion of the frontal lobe. Brodmann-1909 did not regard it as homologous, either topographically or cytoarchitecturally, to rostral area 12 of the human. Distinctive features (Brodmann-1905): a quite distinct internal granular layer (IV) separates slender pyramidal cells of the external pyramidal layer (III) and the internal pyramidal layer (V); the multiform layer (VI) is expanded, contains widely dispersed spindle cells and merges gradually with the underlying cortical white matter; all cells, including the pyramidal cells of the external and internal pyramidal layers are inordinately small; the internal pyramidal layer (V) also contains spindle cells in groups of two to five located close to its border with the internal granular layer (IV).

UBERON:0013544.name: Brodmann (1909) area 13
UBERON:0013544.def: Brodmann area 13 is a subdivision of the cerebral cortex as defined on the guenon monkey and on the basis of cytoarchitecture. Brodmann area 13 is found in humans, however it seems to act as a bridge between the lateral and medial layers of the brain. Thus it is sometimes misidentified as not being a Brodmann area.

UBERON:0013545.name: Brodmann (1909) area 14
UBERON:0013545.def: Brodmann Area 14 is one of Brodmann's subdivisions of the cerebral cortex in the brain. It was defined by Brodmann in the guenon monkey. No equivalent structure exists in humans.

UBERON:0013546.name: Brodmann (1909) area 15
UBERON:0013546.def: Brodmann Area 15 is one of Brodmann's subdivisions of the cerebral cortex in the brain. Area 15 was defined by Brodmann in the guenon monkey, but he found no equivalent structure in humans. However, functional imaging experiments have found structures that may be homologous.

UBERON:0013547.name: Brodmann (1909) area 16
UBERON:0013547.def: Brodmann area 16 is a subdivision of the cerebral cortex of the guenon defined on the basis of cytoarchitecture. It is a relatively undifferentiated cortical area that Brodmann regarded as part of the insula because of the relation of its innermost multiform layer (VI) with the claustrum (VICl). The laminar organization of cortex is almost totally lacking. The molecular layer (I) is wide as in area 15 of Brodmann-1905. The space between layer I and layer VI is composed of a mixture of pyramidal cells and spindle cells with no significant number of granule cells. Pyramidal cells clump in the outer part to form glomeruli similar to those seen in some of the primary olfactory areas (Brodmann-1905). This term also refers to an area known as peripaleocortical claustral - a cytoarchitecturally defined (agranular) portion of the insula at its rostral extreme where it approaches most closely the claustrum and the prepyriform area (Stephan-76).

UBERON:0013550.name: Brodmann (1909) area 19
UBERON:0013550.def: Brodmann area 19, or BA19, is part of the occipital lobe cortex in the human brain. Along with area 18, it comprises the extrastriate (or peristriate) cortex. In normally-sighted humans, extrastriate cortex is a visual association area, with feature-extracting, shape recognition, attentional, and multimodal integrating functions. This area is also known as peristriate area 19, and it refers to a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined occipital region of cerebral cortex. In the human it is located in parts of the lingual gyrus, the cuneus, the lateral occipital gyrus (H) and the superior occipital gyrus (H) of the occipital lobe where it is bounded approximately by the parieto-occipital sulcus. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded on one side by the parastriate area 18 which it surrounds. Rostrally it is bounded by the angular area 39 (H) and the occipitotemporal area 37 (H) (Brodmann-1909).

UBERON:0013551.name: Brodmann (1909) area 20
UBERON:0013551.def: Brodmann area 20, or BA20, is part of the temporal cortex in the human brain. The region encompasses most of the ventral temporal cortex, a region believed to play a part in high-level visual processing and recognition memory. This area is also known as inferior temporal area 20, and it refers to a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined temporal region of cerebral cortex. In the human it corresponds approximately to the inferior temporal gyrus. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded medially by the ectorhinal area 36 (H), laterally by the middle temporal area 21, rostrally by the temporopolar area 38 (H) and caudally by the occipitotemporal area 37 (H) (Brodmann-1909).

UBERON:0013552.name: Brodmann (1909) area 21
UBERON:0013552.def: Brodmann area 21, or BA21, is part of the temporal cortex in the human brain. The region encompasses most of the lateral temporal cortex, a region believed to play a part in auditory processing and language. Language function is left lateralized in most individuals. BA21 is superior to BA20 and inferior to BA40 and BA41. This area is also known as middle temporal area 21. It is a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined temporal region of cerebral cortex. In the human it corresponds approximately to the middle temporal gyrus. It is bounded rostrally by the temporopolar area 38 (H), ventrally by the inferior temporal area 20, caudally by the occipitotemporal area 37 (H), and dorsally by the superior temporal area 22 (Brodmann-1909). [WP,unvetted].

UBERON:0013553.name: Brodmann (1909) area 22
UBERON:0013553.def: Brodmann area 22 is one of Brodmann's cytologically defined regions of the brain. It is involved in auditory processing.

UBERON:0013554.name: Brodmann (1909) area 23
UBERON:0013554.def: The term area 23 of Brodmann-1909 refers to a subdivision of the cerebral cortex of the guenon defined on the basis of cytoarchitecture. Brodmann regarded it as topographically and cytoarchitecturally homologous to the combined ventral posterior cingulate area 23 and dorsal posterior cingulate area 31 of the human (Brodmann-1909). Distinctive Features (Brodmann-1905): the cortex is relatively thin; smaller cells predominate; the cell density of the multiform layer (VI) is great, producing a distinct boundary with the subcortical white matter; the internal granular layer (IV) is rather well developed; the internal pyramidal layer (V) contains a dense population of round, medium-sized ganglion cells concentrated at the border with layer IV; layers V and VI are narrow with a distinct mutual boundary.nn* Definition Source NeuroNames.

UBERON:0013556.name: Brodmann (1909) area 25
UBERON:0013556.def: Brodmann area 25 (BA25) is an area in the cerebral cortex of the brain and delineated based on its cytoarchitectonic characteristics. It is also called the subgenual area or area subgenualis. It is the 25th 'Brodmann area' defined by Korbinian Brodmann (thus its name). BA25 is located in the cingulate region as a narrow band in the caudal portion of the subcallosal area adjacent to the paraterminal gyrus. The posterior parolfactory sulcus separates the paraterminal gyrus from BA25. Rostrally it is bound by the prefrontal area 11 of Brodmann.

UBERON:0013558.name: Brodmann (1909) area 27
UBERON:0013558.def: Area 27 of Brodmann-1909 is a cytoarchitecturally defined cortical area that is a rostral part of the parahippocampal gyrus of the guenon (Brodmann-1909). It is commonly regarded as a synonym of presubiculum (Crosby-62). [WP,unvetted].

UBERON:0013560.name: Brodmann (1909) area 32
UBERON:0013560.def: The Brodmann area 32, also known in the human brain as the dorsal anterior cingulate area 32, refers to a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined cingulate region of cerebral cortex. In the human it forms an outer arc around the anterior cingulate gyrus. The cingulate sulcus defines approximately its inner boundary and the superior rostral sulcus (H) its ventral boundary; rostrally it extends almost to the margin of the frontal lobe. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded internally by the ventral anterior cingulate area 24, externally by medial margins of the agranular frontal area 6, intermediate frontal area 8, granular frontal area 9, frontopolar area 10, and prefrontal area 11-1909. (Brodmann19-09). Dorsal region of anterior cingulate gyrus is associated with rational thought processes, most notably active during the Stroop task.

UBERON:0013561.name: Brodmann (1909) area 43
UBERON:0013561.def: Brodmann area 43 is a subdivision of the cerebral cortex of the guenon defined on the basis of cytoarchitecture. It was described (but not labeled) on the map of cortical areas in Brodmann-1909, and it was regarded as cytoarchitecturally homologous to area 30 of Mauss in 1908 in the guenon and subcentral area 43 of the human (Brodmann-1909). The Vogts found no distinctive architectonic area of the corresponding location in the guenon (Vogts-1919).

UBERON:0013573.name: Brodmann (1909) area 40
UBERON:0013573.def: Brodmann area 40, or BA40, is part of the parietal cortex in the human brain. The inferior part of BA40 is in the area of the supramarginal gyrus, which lies at the posterior end of the lateral fissure, in the inferior lateral part of the parietal lobe. It is bounded approximately by the intraparietal sulcus, the inferior postcentral sulcus, the posterior subcentral sulcus and the lateral sulcus. Cytoarchitecturally it is bounded caudally by the angular area 39 (H), rostrally and dorsally by the caudal postcentral area 2, and ventrally by the subcentral area 43 and the superior temporal area 22 (Brodmann-1909). Cytoarchitectonically defined subregions of rostral BA40/the supramarginal gyrus are PF, PFcm, PFm, PFop, and PFt. Area PF is the homologue to macaque area PF, part of the mirror neuron system, and active in humans during imitation. The supramarginal gyrus part of Brodmann area 40 is the region in the inferior parietal lobe that is involved in reading both in regards to meaning and phonology. [WP,unvetted].

UBERON:0013581.name: metapodium bone 1
UBERON:0013581.def: A metapodium bone that is part of a digit 1 plus metapodial segment.

UBERON:0013582.name: metapodium bone 2
UBERON:0013582.def: A metapodium bone that is part of a digit 2 plus metapodial segment.

UBERON:0013583.name: metapodium bone 3
UBERON:0013583.def: A metapodial bone that is associated with digit III.

UBERON:0013584.name: metapodium bone 4
UBERON:0013584.def: A metapodium bone that is part of a digit 4 plus metapodial segment.

UBERON:0013585.name: metapodium bone 5
UBERON:0013585.def: A metapodium bone that is part of a digit 5 plus metapodial segment.

UBERON:0013586.name: fused metapodial bones 3 and 4
UBERON:0013586.def: An element formed from the fusion of metapodium 3 and metapodium 4 (i.e. either metatarsals 3 and 4 or metacarpals 3 and 4).

UBERON:0013587.name: fused metacarpal bones 3 and 4
UBERON:0013587.def: An element formed from the fusion of metacarpal 3 and metacarpal 4.

UBERON:0013588.name: fused metatarsal bones 3 and 4
UBERON:0013588.def: An element formed from the fusion of metatarsal 3 and metatarsal 4.

UBERON:0013589.name: koniocortex
UBERON:0013589.def: Regions of the cerebal cortex characterized by a particularly well-developed inner granular layer (layer 4); this type of cerebral cortex is represented by the primary sensory Brodmann area 17 of the visual cortex, Brodmann areas 1-3 of the somatic sensory cortex, and Brodmann area 41 of the auditory cortex.

UBERON:0013590.name: cruciate sulcus
UBERON:0013590.def: A deep groove which runs transversely across the rostro-dorsal surface of the cerebrum and which is one of the landmarks on the cerebral cortex.

UBERON:0013598.name: accessory nucleus of optic tract
UBERON:0013598.def: One of a set of small groups of neuron cell bodies located along the trajectory of optic fibers in the mesencephalon. These consist of the posterior nucleus [TA] (nucleus posterior [TA]), medial nucleus [TA] (nucleus medialis [TA]), and lateral nucleus [TA] (nucleus lateralis [TA]), which are also called the posterior, medial, and lateral terminal nuclei. The connections of these nuclei, along with the nucleus of the optic tract, make up the accessory optic system that appears to be concerned with retinal slip in specific directions.
synonym: terminal nucleus of accessory optic tract

UBERON:0013599.name: dorsal accessory nucleus of optic tract
synonym: dorsal terminal nucleus of accessory optic tract
dorsal terminal nucleus of the accessory optic tract
posterior accessory nucleus of optic tract
posterior terminal nucleus of accessory optic tract

UBERON:0013600.name: lateral accessory nucleus of optic tract
synonym: lateral terminal nucleus of the accessory optic tract

UBERON:0013601.name: medial accessory nucleus of optic tract
synonym: medial terminal nucleus of the accessory optic tract

UBERON:0013606.name: magnocellular layer of dorsal nucleus of lateral geniculate body
synonym: magnocellular layer of lateral geniculate nucleus
strata magnocellularia nuclei dorsalis corporis geniculati lateralis

UBERON:0013607.name: parvocellular layer of dorsal nucleus of lateral geniculate body
synonym: parvocellular layer of lateral geniculate nucleus
strata parvocellularia nuclei dorsalis corporis geniculati lateralis

UBERON:0013608.name: inferior olive dorsal accessory nucleus
UBERON:0013608.synonym: dorsal accessory nucleus of inferior olivary complex

UBERON:0013609.name: inferior olive medial accessory nucleus
UBERON:0013609.synonym: medial accessory nucleus of inferior olivary complex

UBERON:0013610.name: inferior olive ventral accessory nucleus
UBERON:0013610.synonym: ventral accessory nucleus of inferior olivary complex

UBERON:0013614.name: fasciculus aberans
UBERON:0013614.def: The fasciulus aberrans is a distinct bundle of fibers at the dorsal aspect of the anterior commisure. These fibers travel in the internal capsule between the putamen and caudate nuclei, and cross the midline to connect the dorsal neocortex of the two hemispheres. When the fasciculus aberrans is absent, the fibers connecting the neocortex of the two hemispheres takes a diffderent route through the external capsule[Johnson et al., (1982a, 1982b, 1994)].

UBERON:0013615.name: koniocellular layer of dorsal nucleus of lateral geniculate body
synonym: konioocellular layer of lateral geniculate nucleus
stratum koniocellulare nuclei dorsalis corporis geniculati lateralis

UBERON:0013617.name: upper primary molar tooth
UBERON:0013617.def: A primary molar tooth that is part of a upper jaw region.

UBERON:0013619.name: upper secondary molar tooth
UBERON:0013619.def: A secondary molar tooth that is part of a upper jaw region.

UBERON:0013620.name: lower primary molar tooth
UBERON:0013620.def: A primary molar tooth that is part of a lower jaw region.

UBERON:0013621.name: lower secondary molar tooth
UBERON:0013621.def: A secondary molar tooth that is part of a lower jaw region.

UBERON:0013622.name: manual autopod pad
UBERON:0013622.def: An autopod pad that is part of a manus.

UBERON:0013623.name: pedal autopod pad
UBERON:0013623.def: An autopod pad that is part of a pes.

UBERON:0013630.name: short bone
UBERON:0013630.def: Short bones are designated as those bones that are as wide as they are long. Their primary function is to provide support and stability with little to no movement. They are one of five types of bones: long, short, flat, irregular and sesamoid. Examples of these bones include the tarsals in the foot and the carpals in the hand.

UBERON:0013631.name: sesamoid element
UBERON:0013631.def: Ossicle that develops within bands of dense, regular connective tissue (e.g., tendons and ligaments). Sesamoids are generally located proximate to a bony prominence, over which the dense regular connective tissue wraps, and/or a joint or articulation.

UBERON:0013632.name: sesamoid cartilage
UBERON:0013632.def: A sesamoid element that is composed primarily of cartilage tissue.

UBERON:0013633.name: intertrochanteric crest
UBERON:0013633.def: The intertrochanteric crest is a bony ridge located on the posterior side of the head of the femur, stretching obliquely downward and medially from the summit of the greater trochanter to the lesser trochanter.

UBERON:0013634.name: intertrochanteric line
UBERON:0013634.def: The intertrochanteric line (or spiral line of the femur) is a line located on the anterior side of the proximal end of the femur that stretches between the lesser trochanter and the greater trochanter forming the base of the neck of the femur, roughly following the direction of the shaft of the femur.

UBERON:0013636.name: epithelium of intestinal villus
UBERON:0013636.def: An epithelium that is part of a intestinal villus.

UBERON:0013637.name: prostate gland lateral lobe
UBERON:0013637.def: The prostate gland lobe that is located on the lateral side of the organ.
synonym: lateral ventral lobe of prostate gland

UBERON:0013643.name: lophophore
UBERON:0013643.def: A ring of ciliated tentacles surrounding the mouth.

UBERON:0013644.name: duodenal ampulla
UBERON:0013644.def: The very first part of the duodenum which is slightly dilated.

UBERON:0013645.name: gular gland
UBERON:0013645.def: A gland that is part of the gular region (throat).

UBERON:0013646.name: buccal nerve
UBERON:0013646.def: The buccal nerve (also called the long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face. It is a branch of the mandibular nerve (which is itself a branch of the trigeminal nerve) and transmits sensory information from skin over the buccal membrane (in general, the cheek) and from the second and third molar teeth.

UBERON:0013647.name: lateral pterygoid nerve
UBERON:0013647.def: A nerve that innervates the lateral pterygoid muscle.
synonym: branch of buccal nerve to lateral pterygoid

UBERON:0013648.name: masseteric artery
UBERON:0013648.def: The masseteric artery is small and passes laterally through the mandibular notch to the deep surface of the masseter muscle, which it supplies. It anastomoses with the masseteric branches of the external maxillary artery and with the transverse facial artery.

UBERON:0013649.name: fused tarsal bones 1 and 2
UBERON:0013649.def: A tarsal bone that is formed from the fusion of the 1st and 2nd tarsal bones.

UBERON:0013653.name: velar skeleton
UBERON:0013653.def: Subdivision of skeleton that is part of the velum and consists of a complex arrangement of thin cartilage rods and arches.

UBERON:0013656.name: dulla
UBERON:0013656.def: A diverticulum on the lingual aspect of the soft palate of male dromedaries which may be inflated with air and be extruded from the oral cavity during rut.

UBERON:0013657.name: hump
UBERON:0013657.def: A fatty deposit found on the back of camels.

UBERON:0013658.name: corpus cavernosum maxillaris
UBERON:0013658.def: A bulbous ridge of highly vascularized tissue that runs along the center of the hard palate, expanding cranially to form two large lobes that terminate under the tip of the rostral palate, with another enlarged node at the caudal terminus.

UBERON:0013659.name: spongiose tissue of corpus cavernosum maxillaris
UBERON:0013659.def: An erectile tissue that is part of a corpus cavernosum maxillaris.

UBERON:0013671.name: nerve ending of of corpus cavernosum maxillaris

UBERON:0013672.name: priapium
UBERON:0013672.def: A complex muscular and bony clasping and copulatory organ derived mainly from the pelvic fins, found under the head of male Phallostethoidea with the anus opening on one side and the genital pore on the other. The structure varies among family members. Hook-like ctenactia articulate basally with the aproctal axial which is movably articulated with the proctal axial bone itself, suspended anteriorly by the outer (and sometimes inner) pulvinular bone from the cleithrum and perhaps the urohyal. Other elements are the priapal ribs, the anteplural cartilage (supporting elements along with the cleithrum and the pulvinar), the toxactinium, the infrasulcar and the uncus (forming the claspers along with the ctenactinium), the penial, basipenial, papillary, prepapillary and cristate bones (forming the papillary unit).

UBERON:0013674.name: ctenactinium
UBERON:0013674.def: A curved rod-like clasper on the posterior side of the priapium in Phallostethidae.

UBERON:0013675.name: toxactinium
UBERON:0013675.def: A long curved projection from the anterior end of the priapium in some Phallostethidae.

UBERON:0013676.name: aproctal bone of priapium
UBERON:0013676.def: The ventral element in the priapium of the Phallostethidae on which articulate the ctenactinia (q.v.). Also called aproctal or pelvic bone.

UBERON:0013678.name: anatomical line between inner canthi
UBERON:0013678.def: An anatomical line of the face that connects the two inner (medial) canthi of the eye. The length of this line is known as the inter canthal distance.

UBERON:0013679.name: inner canthus of right eye
UBERON:0013679.def: An inner canthus that is part of a right eye.

UBERON:0013680.name: inner canthus of left eye
UBERON:0013680.def: An inner canthus that is part of a left eye.

UBERON:0013682.name: peripheral region of retina
UBERON:0013682.def: Region of retina that extends from central retina to ora serrata. Peripheral retina is dominated by rods and also has less ganglion cells and is not as thick as central retina. It is responsible for peripheral and night vision.

UBERON:0013683.name: left dorsal thalamus
UBERON:0013683.def: A dorsal thalamus that is in_the_left_side_of a diencephalon.

UBERON:0013684.name: right dorsal thalamus
UBERON:0013684.def: A dorsal thalamus that is in_the_right_side_of a diencephalon.

UBERON:0013685.name: foramen of skull
UBERON:0013685.def: Anatomical space that is an opening in a bone of the skull.

UBERON:0013686.name: anatomical conduit space
UBERON:0013686.def: An anatomical space which is the lumen of some anatomical conduit and connects two or more spaces together[FMA,modified].

UBERON:0013687.name: pericranium
UBERON:0013687.def: Periosteum that is part of a skull.

UBERON:0013688.name: tonsil germinal center
UBERON:0013688.def: A germinal center that is part of a tonsil.

UBERON:0013689.name: appendix lymphoid tissue
UBERON:0013689.def: Lymphoid tissue located in the appendix.

UBERON:0013691.name: buttock
UBERON:0013691.def: A zone of soft tissue located on the posterior of the lateral side of the pelvic region corresponding to the gluteal muscles.

UBERON:0013692.name: inframammary fold
UBERON:0013692.def: Inframammary fold, inframammary crease or inframammary line is the feature of human anatomy which is a natural boundary of a breast from below, the place where the breast and the chest meet. The choice of the term depends on the prominence of the feature.

UBERON:0013693.name: cerebral cortex neuropil
UBERON:0013693.def: A neuropil that is part of a cerebral cortex [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0013694.name: brain endothelium
UBERON:0013694.def: Vascular endothelium found in blood vessels of the blood-brain-barrier.

UBERON:0013695.name: colon endothelium
UBERON:0013695.def: Vascular endothelium found in colon blood vessels.

UBERON:0013696.name: tonsil epithelium
UBERON:0013696.def: The epithelium that forms the surface of the tonsil dips into the underlying connective tissue in numerous places, forming crypts kown as tonsillar crypts. Stratified squamous epithelium, that may be heavily infiltrated by lymphocytes. Epithelial cells are present in the germinal as well as in the periphery of the nodule.

UBERON:0013698.name: strand of pubic hair
UBERON:0013698.def: A hair in the frontal genital area of adolescent and adult humans, located on and around the sex organs, the crotch, and sometimes at the top of the inside of the thighs, in the pubic region around the pubis bone.

UBERON:0013699.name: strand of axillary hair
UBERON:0013699.def: A strand of hair that is part of a axilla.

UBERON:0013700.name: axial musculature
UBERON:0013700.def: Musculature of the head and neck, spine, and ribs.

UBERON:0013701.name: main body axis
UBERON:0013701.def: A principle subdivision of an organism that includes all structures along the primary axis, typically the anterior-posterior axis, from head to tail, including structures of the body proper where present (for example, ribs), but excluding appendages.

UBERON:0013702.name: body proper
UBERON:0013702.def: The region of the organism associated with the visceral organs.

UBERON:0013703.name: integumentary projection
UBERON:0013703.def: Anatomical projection that is part of the integumentl system.

UBERON:0013704.name: notochordal canal
UBERON:0013704.def: A tubular passage that extends from the primitive pit into the head process during the early stages of embryonic development in mammals. It perforates the splanchnopleure layer so that the yolk sac and the amnion are connected temporarily.

UBERON:0013705.name: fascia of Scarpa
UBERON:0013705.def: The deep layer (fascia of Scarpa) is a layer of the anterior abdominal wall.
synonym: deep layer of superficial fascia of abdomen
membranous layer of subcutaneous tissue of abdomen
membranous layer of superficial fascia of abdomen

UBERON:0013707.name: iliac spine
UBERON:0013707.def: A bone spine that is part of a ilium.

UBERON:0013708.name: anterior superior iliac spine
UBERON:0013708.def: The anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) is an important landmark of surface anatomy. It refers to the anterior extremity of the iliac crest of the pelvis, which provides attachment for the inguinal ligament, the sartorius muscle, and the tensor fasciae latae. ASIS provides a clue in identifying some other clinical landmarks, including: McBurney's point Gardner's line Roser-NC)laton line A - Anterior (front, like the face) S - Superior (towards the head, opposite to feet) I - Iliac S - Spine.

UBERON:0013709.name: anterior inferior iliac spine
UBERON:0013709.def: The anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS) is a bony eminence on the anterior border of the hip bone, or, more precisely, the wing of the ilium (i.e. the upper lateral parts of the pelvis).

UBERON:0013710.name: posterior superior iliac spine
UBERON:0013710.def: The posterior border of the ala, shorter than the anterior, also presents two projections separated by a notch, the posterior superior iliac spine and the posterior inferior iliac spine. The posterior superior iliac spine serves for the attachment of the oblique portion of the posterior sacroiliac ligaments and the Multifidus.
synonym: posterior superior spine of the ilium

UBERON:0013711.name: posterior inferior iliac spine
UBERON:0013711.def: The posterior border of the ala, shorter than the anterior, also presents two projections separated by a notch, the posterior superior iliac spine and the posterior inferior iliac spine. The posterior inferior iliac spine corresponds with the posterior extremity of the auricular surface.
synonym: posterior inferior spine of the ilium

UBERON:0013715.name: ilio-marsupialis muscle
UBERON:0013715.def: A muscle that originates on the anterior iliac spine that passes through the inguinal canal before dividing into four branches, each attaching to a pouch nipple.

UBERON:0013716.name: branch of ilio-marsupialis muscle
UBERON:0013716.def: One of the branches of the ilio-marsupialis that attaches to a pouch nipple.

UBERON:0013717.name: superficial inguinal ring
UBERON:0013717.def: The exit of the inguinal canal.

UBERON:0013718.name: dartos muscle
UBERON:0013718.def: The dartos fascia is a fat-free layer of smooth muscular fiber outside the external spermatic fascia but below the skin. It is a continuation of Scarpa's Fascia which is a membranous layer of the subcutaneous tissue in the abdominal wall.

UBERON:0013719.name: dartos muscle of scrotum
UBERON:0013719.def: A dartos muscle that is part of a male reproductive system.

UBERON:0013720.name: dartos muscle of labia majora
UBERON:0013720.def: A dartos muscle that is part of a female reproductive system.

UBERON:0013721.name: deep inguinal ring
UBERON:0013721.def: The entrance to the inguinal canal.

UBERON:0013725.name: anterior talofibular ligament
UBERON:0013725.def: The anterior talofibular ligament is a ligament in the ankle. It passes from the anterior margin of the fibular malleolus, anteriorly and medially, to the talus bone, in front of its lateral articular facet. It is one of the lateral ligaments of the ankle and prevents the foot from sliding forward in relation to the shin.

UBERON:0013726.name: posterior talofibular ligament
UBERON:0013726.def: The posterior talofibular ligament, runs almost horizontally from the depression at the medial and back part of the fibular malleolus (lateral malleolus) to a prominent tubercle on the posterior surface of the talus immediately lateral to the groove for the tendon of the flexor hallucis longus.

UBERON:0013727.name: notochordal fluid
UBERON:0013727.def: Fluid contained within the notochordal canal.

UBERON:0013730.name: mycetome
UBERON:0013730.def: A specialized organ that is linked to the gut in beetles and host to a symbiotic yeast. The yeast cells assist in the digestion of less nutritious foods, supply needed B-vitamins and sterols, and provide resistance to certain toxins.

UBERON:0013731.name: basilar papilla
UBERON:0013731.def: The auditory sensory organ of lizards, amphibians, and birds, which is homologous to the Corti in mammals.

UBERON:0013732.name: vestibule of nasal cavity
UBERON:0013732.def: A tube leading from the external naris to the nasal cavity.

UBERON:0013734.name: rostral linear nucleus
UBERON:0013734.def: Nucleus of the medial ventral tegmental area, originally identified in the rat but also in cat, monkey and human, comprising an average of 7% volume of the VTA across the different species, with the largest being present in the cat.
synonym: rostral linear nucleus of the raphe

UBERON:0013738.name: parabrachial pigmental nucleus
UBERON:0013738.def: Nucleus identified in the medial ventral tegmental area that borders the red nucleus and superior cerebellar peduncle dorsally, the medial lemniscus laterally, the subtantia nigra pars compacta and paranigral nucleus ventrally and the rostral linear nucleus and interfascicular nucleus medially. Generally, the largest nucleus in the ventral tegmental area, occupying an average of 50% of the total volume as measured in rat, cat, monkey and human.

UBERON:0013739.name: base of crypt of Lieberkuhn
UBERON:0013739.def: The basal portion (further from lumen) of an intestinal crypt. Contains multipotent stem cells. Stem cells in the crypts divide to form daughter cells. One daughter cell from each stem cell division is retained as a stem cell. The other becomes committed to differentiate along one of four pathways to become an enterocyte, enteroendocrine cell, goblet cell or Paneth cell.
synonym: base part of epithelium of intestinal gland

UBERON:0013740.name: wall of crypt of Lieberkuhn
UBERON:0013740.def: The lateral parts of an intestinal crypt, continuous distally with the base and proximally with the intestinal villus epithelium.
synonym: wall part of epithelium of intestinal gland

UBERON:0013741.name: base of crypt of Lieberkuhn of large intestine
UBERON:0013741.def: A base of crypt of Lieberkuhn that is part of a large intestine.

UBERON:0013742.name: wall of crypt of Lieberkuhn of large intestine
UBERON:0013742.def: A wall of crypt of Lieberkuhn that is part of a large intestine.

UBERON:0013743.name: base of crypt of Lieberkuhn of small intestine
UBERON:0013743.def: The basal portion (further from lumen) of a intestinal crypt that is located in the small intestine.

UBERON:0013744.name: wall of crypt of Lieberkuhn of small intestine
UBERON:0013744.def: The lateral parts of an intestinal crypt that is located in the small intestine, continuous distally with the base and proximally with the intestinal villus epithelium.

UBERON:0013745.name: zona intermedia of adrenal gland
UBERON:0013745.def: A zone of the adrenal cortex located between the zona glomerulosa and the zona fasciculata.

UBERON:0013746.name: basibranchial element
UBERON:0013746.def: Endochondral element that is ventral, median, and associated with a single pharyngeal arch in the pharyngeal arch 3-7 skeleton.

UBERON:0013747.name: basibranchial cartilage
UBERON:0013747.def: A basibranchial element that is cartilage. Basibranchial elements are ventral, median, and associated with a single pharyngeal arch in the pharyngeal arch 3-7 skeleton.

UBERON:0013748.name: ulnar metaphysis
UBERON:0013748.def: A metaphysis that is part of a ulna.

UBERON:0013749.name: metaphysis of humerus
UBERON:0013749.def: A metaphysis that is part of a metaphysis.

UBERON:0013750.name: metaphysis of tibia
UBERON:0013750.def: A metaphysis that is part of a tibia.

UBERON:0013751.name: metaphysis of radius
UBERON:0013751.def: A metaphysis that is part of a radius bone.

UBERON:0013752.name: diaphysis of metacarpal bone
UBERON:0013752.def: A diaphysis that is part of a metacarpal bone.

UBERON:0013753.name: distal epiphysis of metacarpal bone
UBERON:0013753.def: A distal epiphysis that is part of a metacarpal bone.

UBERON:0013754.name: integumentary system layer
UBERON:0013754.def: An organ component layer that is part of a integumental system.

UBERON:0013755.name: arterial blood
UBERON:0013755.def: A blood that is part of a artery.

UBERON:0013756.name: venous blood
UBERON:0013756.def: A blood that is part of a vein.

UBERON:0013757.name: capillary blood
UBERON:0013757.def: A blood that is part of a capillary.

UBERON:0013758.name: cervical os
UBERON:0013758.def: One of two openings in the uterine cervix.

UBERON:0013759.name: internal cervical os
UBERON:0013759.def: Opening of uterine cervix into the body of the uterus.

UBERON:0013760.name: external cervical os
UBERON:0013760.def: Opening of uterine cervix into the vagina.

UBERON:0013761.name: cervical cavity
UBERON:0013761.def: The cavity formed by the walls of the cervix.

UBERON:0013763.name: obsolete sensory epithelium of spiral organ

UBERON:0013764.name: common crus of semicircular duct
UBERON:0013764.def: A nonampullary end of the superior or posterior semicircular ducts.
synonym: common membranous limb of membranous semicircular ducts
common membranous limb of semicircular ducts

UBERON:0013765.name: digestive system element
UBERON:0013765.def: Any of the organs or elements that are part of the digestive system. Examples: tongue, esophagus, spleen, crop, lunge feeding organ, tooth elements.

UBERON:0013766.name: epicanthal fold
UBERON:0013766.def: A fold of skin of the upper eyelid that partially covers the inner corner of the eye.

UBERON:0013767.name: frontal process of maxilla
UBERON:0013767.def: A plate of bone from the maxilla that that projects upward, medialward, and backward, by the side of the nose, forming part of its lateral boundary[WP,modified].

UBERON:0013768.name: great vessel of heart
UBERON:0013768.def: Great vessels is a term used to refer collectively to the large vessels that bring blood to and from the heart.

UBERON:0013769.name: uterine lumen
UBERON:0013769.def: An organ cavity that is part of a uterus.

UBERON:0013771.name: line connecting laterally paired nipples
UBERON:0013771.def: Line across midline connecting a left and right nipples.

UBERON:0013772.name: left nipple
UBERON:0013772.def: A nipple that is in_the_left_side_of a body proper.

UBERON:0013773.name: right nipple
UBERON:0013773.def: A nipple that is in_the_right_side_of a body proper.

UBERON:0013774.name: diaphysis of metatarsal bone
UBERON:0013774.def: A diaphysis that is part of a metatarsal bone.

UBERON:0013776.name: skin of palmar/plantar part of autopod
UBERON:0013776.def: A zone of skin that is part of a palmar/plantar part of autopod.

UBERON:0013777.name: skin of palm of manus
UBERON:0013777.def: A zone of skin that is part of a palmar part of manus.
synonym: skin of palmar area of hand

UBERON:0013778.name: skin of sole of pes
UBERON:0013778.def: A zone of skin that is part of a skin of pes.
synonym: skin of plantar part of foot

UBERON:0014169.name: nigrostriatal tract
UBERON:0014169.def: The term nigrostriatal fibers refers to a dopaminergic fiber pathway connecting the substantia nigra with the striatum. It is not readily distinguished in myelin-stained cross-sections (Carpenter-83).

UBERON:0014277.name: piriform cortex layer 1
UBERON:0014277.def: Most superficial of 3 cytoarchitecturally defined layers of the piriform cortex, characterized by few neuronal cell bodies. It has been divided into a superficial part and a deep part.

UBERON:0014280.name: piriform cortex layer 2
UBERON:0014280.def: Middle of three cytoarchitecturally defined layers of the piriform cortex characterized by a compact layer of cell bodies. It can be divided into a superficial part and a more densely packed deep part.

UBERON:0014283.name: piriform cortex layer 3
UBERON:0014283.def: Deepest of 3 cytoarchitecturally defined layers of the piriform cortex characterized by a moderately high density of pyramidal cells and large numbers of basal dendrites descending from pyramidal cells in layer 2.

UBERON:0014284.name: endopiriform nucleus
UBERON:0014284.def: An elongated nucleus consisting largely of multipolar spiny cells lying deep to the piriform cortex.  According to Price (1990; pp. 979-998 in The Human Nervous System, G. Paxinos, (Ed.), Academic Press, San Diego), it is part of the claustrum.

UBERON:0014287.name: medial accessory olive
UBERON:0014287.def: Regional part of the inferior olivary complex.

UBERON:0014370.name: extrastriate cortex
UBERON:0014370.def: A group of cortical areas related by direct or indirect connectivity to the striate area 17 and functionally involved primarily in vision. They include the parastriate area 18, the peristriate area 19 and adjacent areas in the parietal lobe and temporal lobe (Adapted from BrainInfo and Zilles-1990).

UBERON:0014371.name: future telencephalon
UBERON:0014371.def: Embryonic structure that gives rise to the telencephalon.

UBERON:0014372.name: fibroelastic membrane of larynx
UBERON:0014372.def: A layer of fibrous and elastic fibers, taking the place of the submucosa in the larynx. It is divided by the laryngeal ventricle into two parts: the quadrangular membrane superiorly and the conus elasticus inferiorly.

UBERON:0014374.name: embryoid body
UBERON:0014374.def: Embryoid bodies (EBs) are three-dimensional aggregates of pluripotent stem cells.

UBERON:0014375.name: intrinsic muscle of manus
UBERON:0014375.def: Any of the intrinsic muscles of the manus (hand).

UBERON:0014376.name: thenar muscle
UBERON:0014376.def: Any of the muscles of the thenar eminence, a raised fleshy area on the palm of the hand near the base of the thumb.

UBERON:0014377.name: hypothenar muscle
UBERON:0014377.def: Any of three muscles of the palm that control the motion of the little finger.

UBERON:0014378.name: intrinsic muscle of pes
UBERON:0014378.def: Any of the intrinsic muscles of the pes (foot).

UBERON:0014379.name: adductor hallucis muscle
UBERON:0014379.def: The Adductor hallucis (Adductor obliquus hallucis) arises by two headsboblique and transverse and is responsible for adducting the big toe. It is innervated by the lateral plantar nerve. It evolved from the contrahens I muscle as Man's ancestors' thumbs and big toes became opposable.

UBERON:0014380.name: flexor digitorum brevis muscle
UBERON:0014380.def: The flexor digitorum brevis lies in the middle of the sole of the foot, immediately above the central part of the plantar aponeurosis, with which it is firmly united. Its deep surface is separated from the lateral plantar vessels and nerves by a thin layer of fascia.

UBERON:0014381.name: whorl of hair
UBERON:0014381.def: A patch of hair growing in the opposite direction of the rest of the hair.

UBERON:0014382.name: collection of hairs on head or neck
UBERON:0014382.def: A collection of hairs that is part of a craniocervical region.

UBERON:0014385.name: aryepiglottic fold
UBERON:0014385.def: The entrance of the larynx is a triangular opening, narrow in front, wide behind, and sloping obliquely downward and backward. It is bounded, in front, by the epiglottis; behind, by the apices of the arytenoid cartilages, the corniculate cartilages, and the interarytenoid notch; and on either side, by a fold of mucous membrane, enclosing ligamentous and muscular fibers, stretched between the side of the epiglottis and the apex of the arytenoid cartilage; this is the aryepiglottic fold, on the posterior part of the margin of which the cuneiform cartilage forms a more or less distinct whitish prominence, the cuneiform tubercle. These folds form the upper borders of the quadrangular membrane.

UBERON:0014386.name: vertebral endplate
UBERON:0014386.def: Either of the the top and bottom portions of the vertebral bodies that interface with the vertebral discs. It is composed of a layer of thickened cancellous bone.

UBERON:0014387.name: mesenchyme derived from neural crest
UBERON:0014387.def: Mesenchyme that develops_from the neural crest[Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014388.name: kidney collecting duct epithelium
UBERON:0014388.def: The simple cuboidal epithelium lining the lumen of kidney collecting ducts.
synonym: collecting duct of renal tubule epithelium
epithelium of collecting duct of renal tubule

UBERON:0014389.name: gustatory papilla of tongue
UBERON:0014389.def: A papilla that contain taste buds, including the fungiform, foliate, and circumvallate papillae.

UBERON:0014390.name: muscle layer of ileum
UBERON:0014390.def: A muscular coat that is part of a ileum.

UBERON:0014391.name: palmar/plantar sweat gland
UBERON:0014391.def: A sweat gland that is part of the skin of the palmar part of the manus or plantar part of the pes.
synonym: sweat gland of palmar part of manus
sweat gland of palmar/plant part of autopod

UBERON:0014392.name: sweat of palm
UBERON:0014392.def: Sweat that is produced by the glands on the palmar and plantar surfaces.

UBERON:0014393.name: sweat of axilla
UBERON:0014393.def: Sweat that is produced by the glands of the axilla.

UBERON:0014394.name: uterine fat pad
UBERON:0014394.def: Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the uterus.

UBERON:0014395.name: proximal mesopodial bone
UBERON:0014395.def: A proximal mesopodial endochondral element that is composed primarily of a bone tissue.

UBERON:0014396.name: interscapular fat pad
UBERON:0014396.def: Encapsulated adipose tissue located between the scapulae.

UBERON:0014397.name: lateral process of malleus
UBERON:0014397.def: A short projection from the base of the manubrium of the malleus, attached firmly to the drum membrane.

UBERON:0014398.name: respiratory muscle
UBERON:0014398.def: Muscle that is part of the respiratory system.

UBERON:0014399.name: sinusoidal space
UBERON:0014399.def: An anatomical space that is enclosed by a sinusoid.

UBERON:0014400.name: hepatic sinusoidal space
UBERON:0014400.def: A sinusoidal space that is part of a hepatic sinusoid.

UBERON:0014401.name: renal venous blood vessel
UBERON:0014401.def: Any member of the network of tubes that return blood from the renal tissues to the systemic circulation.

UBERON:0014402.name: sex-specific anatomical structure
UBERON:0014402.def: A part of the body present only in a specific gender.

UBERON:0014403.name: male anatomical structure
UBERON:0014403.def: A part of the body present only in males.

UBERON:0014404.name: female anatomical structure
UBERON:0014404.def: A part of the body present only in females.

UBERON:0014405.name: nymph stage
UBERON:0014405.def: A larval stage of that is the immature stage of some invertebrates that undergoe gradual metamorphosis (hemimetabolism) before reaching its adult stage.

UBERON:0014406.name: nauplius stage
UBERON:0014406.def: The free-swimming first stage of the larva of certain crustaceans, having an unsegmented body with three pairs of appendages and a single median eye. The eye is known for that reason as the 'naupliar eye', and is often absent in later developmental stages, although it is retained into the adult form in some groups, such as the Notostraca.

UBERON:0014409.name: metacromion
UBERON:0014409.def: A process projecting backward and downward from the acromion of the scapula of some mammals.

UBERON:0014411.name: greater sciatic notch
UBERON:0014411.def: On the dorsal border of the wing of the ilium , at it's junction with the shaft is a cut away. This forms the Greater sciatic notch. The sciatic nerve runs over the notch in passage to the hindlimb.

UBERON:0014430.name: sciatic notch
UBERON:0014430.def: Either of two notches on the dorsal border of the hip bone on each side that when closed off by ligaments form the corresponding sciatic foramina.

UBERON:0014436.name: lesser sciatic notch
UBERON:0014436.def: Below the ischial spine is a smaller notch, the lesser sciatic notch; it is smooth, coated in the recent state with cartilage, the surface of which presents two or three ridges corresponding to the subdivisions of the tendon of the Obturator internus, which winds over it. It is converted into a foramen, the lesser sciatic foramen, by the sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, and transmits the tendon of the Obturator internus, the nerve which supplies that muscle, and the internal pudendal vessels and nerve.

UBERON:0014437.name: iliac crest
UBERON:0014437.def: Is part of the pelvis on the edge of the wing of the ilium. Round in shape, dorsal to the pubis and ischium. Acts as structrure that muscles can attach too.

UBERON:0014438.name: superior pubic ramus
UBERON:0014438.def: The superior pubic ramus is a part of the pubic bone which forms a portion of the obturator foramen. It extends from the body to the median plane where it articulates with its fellow of the opposite side. It is conveniently described in two portions, viz. , a medial flattened part and a narrow lateral prismoid portion.

UBERON:0014439.name: inferior pubic ramus
UBERON:0014439.def: The inferior pubic ramus is thin and flattened. It passes lateralward and downward from the medial end of the superior ramus; it becomes narrower as it descends and joins with the inferior ramus of the ischium below the obturator foramen.

UBERON:0014440.name: ischiopubic ramus
UBERON:0014440.def: The ischiopubic ramus is a compound structure consisting of the following two structures: from the pubis, the inferior pubic ramus from the ischium, the inferior ramus of the ischium It serves as part of the origin for the Obturator internus muscle. It also marks a vertex of the anal triangle and the urogenital triangle. The fascia of Colles is attached to its margin.
synonym: rami of the pubis and ischium

UBERON:0014442.name: superior ischial ramus
UBERON:0014442.def: The superior ramus of the ischium (descending ramus) projects downward and backward from the body and presents for examination three surfaces: external, internal, and posterior. The external surface is quadrilateral in shape. It is bounded above by a groove which lodges the tendon of the Obturator externus; below, it is continuous with the inferior ramus; in front it is limited by the posterior margin of the obturator foramen; behind, a prominent margin separates it from the posterior surface. In front of this margin the surface gives origin to the Quadratus femoris, and anterior to this to some of the fibers of origin of the Obturator externus; the lower part of the surface gives origin to part of the Adductor magnus. The internal surface forms part of the bony wall of the lesser pelvis. In front it is limited by the posterior margin of the obturator foramen. Below, it is bounded by a sharp ridge which gives attachment to a falciform prolongation of the sacrotuberous ligament, and, more anteriorly, gives origin to the Transversus perinC&i and Ischiocavernosus. Posteriorly the ramus forms a large swelling, the tuberosity of the ischium.

UBERON:0014443.name: inferior ischial ramus
UBERON:0014443.def: The Inferior Ramus of the ischium (ascending ramus) is the thin, flattened part of the ischium, which ascends from the superior ramus, and joins the inferior ramus of the pubisbthe junction being indicated in the adult by a raised line. The outer surface is uneven for the origin of the obturator externus and some of the fibers of the adductor magnus; its inner surface forms part of the anterior wall of the pelvis. Its medial border is thick, rough, slightly everted, forms part of the outlet of the pelvis, and presents two ridges and an intervening space. The ridges are continuous with similar ones on the inferior ramus of the pubis: to the outer is attached the deep layer of the superficial perineal fascia (fascia of Colles), and to the inner the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. If these two ridges be traced downward, they will be found to join with each other just behind the point of origin of the transversus perinC&i; here the two layers of fascia are continuous behind the posterior border of the muscle. To the intervening space, just in front of the point of junction of the ridges, the transversus perinC&i is attached, and in front of this a portion of the crus penis vel clitoridis and the ischiocavernosus. Its lateral border is thin and sharp, and forms part of the medial margin of the obturator foramen.

UBERON:0014445.name: acetabular fossa
UBERON:0014445.def: The acetabular fossa is the roughened depression in the centre of the acetabulum, surrounded by the lunate acetabular surface and the acetabular notch. The acetabular fossa provides an insertion point for the teres ligaments that secure the femoral head.

UBERON:0014446.name: acetabular notch
UBERON:0014446.def: The acetabulum presents below a deep notch, the acetabular notch, which is continuous with a circular non-articular depression, the acetabular fossa, at the bottom of the cavity: this depression is perforated by numerous apertures, and lodges a mass of fat. The notch is converted into a foramen by the transverse ligament; through the foramen nutrient vessels and nerves enter the joint; the margins of the notch serve for the attachment of the ligament of the head of the femur.

UBERON:0014447.name: feathered facial disc
UBERON:0014447.def: A collection of feathers arranged in a concave pattern surrounding the eyes in some birds, particularly owls.

UBERON:0014448.name: feathered ear tuft
UBERON:0014448.def: A collection of feathers found on the heads of some owls.

UBERON:0014450.name: pretectal nucleus
UBERON:0014450.def: A neural nucleus of the pretectal area (between dorsal thalamus and optic tectum) that receives afferents primarily from the retina and the optic tectum and are involved in modulating motor behavior in response to visual input.

UBERON:0014451.name: tongue taste bud
UBERON:0014451.def: A taste bud that is located on the tongue, situated on a gustatory papilla.

UBERON:0014452.name: gustatory epithelium of tongue
UBERON:0014452.def: A gustatory epithelium that is part of a tongue.

UBERON:0014453.name: gustatory epithelium of palate
UBERON:0014453.def: A gustatory epithelium that is part of a roof of mouth.

UBERON:0014454.name: visceral abdominal adipose tissue
UBERON:0014454.def: Subcutaneous adipose tissue that is located in the peritoneal cavity.

UBERON:0014455.name: subcutaneous abdominal adipose tissue
UBERON:0014455.def: Subcutaneous adipose tissue that is located in the abdominal region.

UBERON:0014456.name: extraperitoneal space
UBERON:0014456.def: The extraperitoneal space is the portion of the abdomen and pelvis which does not lie within peritoneum. It includes: Retroperitoneal space Retropubic space The space in the pelvis is divided into the following components: prevesical space perivesical space perirectal space.

UBERON:0014457.name: obsolete adult eye primordium
UBERON:0014457.def: Missing definition for term UBERON:0014457. Please replace it using linked reference.

UBERON:0014458.name: female bulbospongiosus muscle
UBERON:0014458.def: A bulbospongiosus muscle that is part of a female reproductive system.

UBERON:0014459.name: temporal fenestra
UBERON:0014459.def: One of two bilaterally symmetrical holes (fenestrae) in the temporal bone.

UBERON:0014460.name: supratemporal fenestra
UBERON:0014460.def: A temporal fenestra in the upper part of the temporal bone.

UBERON:0014461.name: infratemporal fenestra
UBERON:0014461.def: An infratemporal fenestra, also called the lateral temporal fenestra is an opening in the skull behind the orbit in some animals.

UBERON:0014462.name: obsolete ptychocyst
UBERON:0014462.def: A cnida that is glutinous and is capable of sticking to prey. Found on burrowing (tube) anemones, which help create the tube in which the animal lives.

UBERON:0014463.name: cardiac ganglion
UBERON:0014463.def: Any of the parasympathetic ganglia of the cardiac plexus between the arch of the aorta and the bifurcation of the pulmonary artery.

UBERON:0014464.name: renal fat pad
UBERON:0014464.def: Encapsulated adipose tissue associated with the kidney.

UBERON:0014465.name: antorbital fenestra
UBERON:0014465.def: An antorbital fenestra is an opening in the skull, in front of the eye sockets. This skull formation first appeared in archosaurs during the Triassic Period. Living birds today possess antorbital fenestrae, but the feature has been lost in modern crocodilians. In some archosaur species, the opening has closed but its location is still marked by a depression, or fossa, on the surface of the skull. This is called an antorbital fossa.

UBERON:0014468.name: ansoparamedian fissure of cerebellum
UBERON:0014468.def: Fissure between cerebellar hemispheric lobules VIIBi and VIIBii.

UBERON:0014471.name: primary fissure of cerebellum
UBERON:0014471.def: The monticulus of the cerebellum is divided by the primary fissure (or preclival fissure) into an anterior, raised part, the culmen or summit, and a posterior sloped part, the clivus; the quadrangular lobule is similarly divided.

UBERON:0014473.name: precentral fissure of cerebellum
UBERON:0014473.def: Fissure between cerebellar lobules I and II.

UBERON:0014475.name: endostylar duct
UBERON:0014475.def: A duct in ammocetes (larval lamprey) that is reputed to connect the endostylar lumen to the pharyngeal lumen. Resembles the thyroglossal duct.

UBERON:0014477.name: thoracic skeleton
UBERON:0014477.def: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all skeletal elements in the thoracic region of the trunk. In most vertebrates this is the rib cage and sternum.

UBERON:0014478.name: rib skeletal system
UBERON:0014478.def: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all ribs and rib joints in an organism. In many vertebrates this consists of the combination of the rib cage and all rib joints, but some vertebrates have ribs outside the thoracic rib cage.

UBERON:0014479.name: elephant trunk
UBERON:0014479.def: An appendage formed by the fusion of the nose and upper lip.

UBERON:0014481.name: sex skin
UBERON:0014481.def: An area of skin adjacent to the female external genitals of various lower primates that undergo marked alteration in turgidity and often in color during estrus.

UBERON:0014482.name: ischial callosity
UBERON:0014482.def: An area of hardened, leathery skin on either side of the base of the tail on the rump.

UBERON:0014483.name: distal phalanx of digit 1
UBERON:0014483.def: A distal phalanx that is part of a digit 1 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014484.name: distal phalanx of digit 2
UBERON:0014484.def: A distal phalanx that is part of a digit 2 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014485.name: distal phalanx of digit 3
UBERON:0014485.def: A distal phalanx that is part of a digit 3. In odd-toes ungulates (Perissodactyla e.g. horses) this is called the coffin bone. In even-toed ungulates (Artiodactyla e.g cattle) this is associated with the medial claw.

UBERON:0014486.name: distal phalanx of digit 4
UBERON:0014486.def: A distal phalanx that is part of a digit 4 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014487.name: distal phalanx of digit 5
UBERON:0014487.def: A distal phalanx that is part of a digit 5 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014488.name: middle phalanx of digit 2
UBERON:0014488.def: A middle phalanx that is part of a digit 2 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014489.name: middle phalanx of digit 3
UBERON:0014489.def: A middle phalanx that is part of a digit 3 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014490.name: middle phalanx of digit 4
UBERON:0014490.def: A middle phalanx that is part of a digit 4 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014491.name: middle phalanx of digit 5
UBERON:0014491.def: A middle phalanx that is part of a digit 5 [Automatically generated definition].

UBERON:0014501.name: proximal phalanx of digit 1
UBERON:0014501.def: A proximal phalanx that is part of a autopod digit 1 [Automatically generated definition].
synonym: proximal phalanx of first digit of autopod

UBERON:0014502.name: proximal phalanx of digit 2
UBERON:0014502.def: A proximal phalanx that is part of a autopod digit 2 [Automatically generated definition].
synonym: proximal phalanx of 2nd digit of autopod
proximal phalanx of second digit of autopod

UBERON:0014503.name: proximal phalanx of digit 3
UBERON:0014503.def: A proximal phalanx that is part of a autopod digit 3 [Automatically generated definition].
synonym: proximal phalanx of 3rd digit of autopod
proximal phalanx of third digit of autopod

UBERON:0014504.name: proximal phalanx of digit 4
UBERON:0014504.def: A proximal phalanx that is part of a autopod digit 4 [Automatically generated definition].
synonym: proximal phalanx of 4th digit of autopod
proximal phalanx of fourth digit of autopod

UBERON:0014505.name: proximal phalanx of digit 5
UBERON:0014505.def: A proximal phalanx that is part of a autopod digit 5 [Automatically generated definition].
synonym: proximal phalanx of 5th digit of autopod
proximal phalanx of fifth digit of autopod

UBERON:0014506.name: distal interphalangeal joint of digit 3
UBERON:0014506.def: A distal inter-phalangeal joint that is part of the 3rd digit.
synonym: distal interphalangeal joint of digit III
equine second interphalangeal joint of limb digit III

UBERON:0014507.name: distal interphalangeal joint of pedal digit 3
UBERON:0014507.def: A distal inter-phalangeal joint that is part of the 3rd pedal digit.
synonym: distal interphalangeal joint of pedal digit III
distal interphalangeal joint of third digit of foot
distal interphalangeal joint of third toe
equine distal interphalangeal joint of hindlimb

UBERON:0014508.name: distal interphalangeal joint of manual digit 3
UBERON:0014508.def: A distal inter-phalangeal joint that is part of the 3rd manual digit.
synonym: distal interphalangeal joint of manual digit III
distal interphalangeal joint of middle finger
equine distal interphalangeal joint of forelimb
equine second interphalangeal joint of forelimb digit III

UBERON:0014509.name: distal sesamoid impar ligament
UBERON:0014509.def: A short wide fibrous structure that attaches proximally to the navicular (distal sesamoid) and distally to the palmar margin of the flexor surface of the distal phalanx.
synonym: impar ligament of distal equine limb

UBERON:0014510.name: lamina of omasum
UBERON:0014510.def: A muscular sheet of the omasum wall consisting of two lateral layers and an intermediate layer of smooth muscle covered with non-glandular stratified squamous epithelium.

UBERON:0014521.name: anterodorsal nucleus of medial geniculate body
synonym: anterodorsal nucleus of medial geniculate complex
anterodorsal nucleus of the medial geniculate body
nucleus corporis geniculati medialis, pars anterodorsalis

UBERON:0014522.name: dorsolateral oculomotor nucleus
synonym: dorsolateral nucleus of oculomotor nuclear complex

UBERON:0014523.name: oculomotor division of oculomotor nuclear complex
UBERON:0014523.def: A division of oculomotor nuclear complex that exists in organisms with electric organs which is responsible for eye movements.

UBERON:0014524.name: electromotor division of oculomotor nuclear complex
UBERON:0014524.def: A division of oculomotor nuclear complex that exists in organisms with electric organs which has axons terminating in the electric organs.

UBERON:0014525.name: limb of internal capsule of telencephalon

UBERON:0014526.name: anterior limb of internal capsule
UBERON:0014526.def: Portion of internal capsule lying between the lenticular nucleus and the head of the caudate nucleus.

UBERON:0014527.name: posterior limb of internal capsule
UBERON:0014527.def: Portion of internal capsule lying between the globus pallidus and the thalamus (Nolte, The Human Brain, 6th ed., 2009, pg 409, modified by MM).
synonym: posterior limb of the internal capsule

UBERON:0014528.name: extreme capsule
UBERON:0014528.def: Thin band of fibers separating the claustrum from the insular cortex.

UBERON:0014529.name: lenticular fasciculus
UBERON:0014529.def: The lenticular fasciculus is a tract connecting the globus pallidus to the Thalamic fasciculus. The thalamic fasciculus (composed of the lenticular fasciculus and ansa lenticularis) runs into the Thalamus. It connects the globus pallidus to the thalamus.

UBERON:0014532.name: white matter lamina of cerebral hemisphere

UBERON:0014533.name: medullary lamina of thalamus
UBERON:0014533.def: Medullary laminae of thalamus are layers of myelinated fibres that appear on cross sections of the thalamus. They also are commonly referred to as laminae medullares thalami or medullary layers of thalamus. The specific layers are: Lamina medullaris lateralis (external medullary lamina) - separates ventral and lateral thalamus from the subthalamus and thalamic reticular nucleus; Lamina medullaris medialis (internal medullary lamina) - positioned between the dorsomedial and ventral nuclei of thalamus, encloses the intralaminar nuclei (centromedian nucleus, paracentral, and central lateral).

UBERON:0014534.name: external medullary lamina of thalamus
UBERON:0014534.def: A medullary lamina that separates ventral and lateral thalamus from the subthalamus and thalamic reticular nucleus.
synonym: external medullary lamina of the thalamus

UBERON:0014537.name: periamygdaloid cortex
UBERON:0014537.def: Is located ventral to the basal nucleus and has three subdivisions: the periamygdaloid cortex, the medial division, and the sulcal division.

UBERON:0014538.name: subdivision of spinal cord central canal
UBERON:0014538.def: A subdivision of the central canal of the spinal cord along its anterior-posterior axis. This is typically subdivided into cervical, thoracic, lumbar and sacral segments.
UBERON:0014538.synonym: regional part of spinal cord central canal

UBERON:0014539.name: precommissural fornix of forebrain
UBERON:0014539.def: Part of fornix extending from the body that curves ventrally rostral to the crossing of the anterior commissure ending in the septal nuclei.

UBERON:0014540.name: white matter lamina of cerebellum
UBERON:0014540.def: The white laminae of cerebellum is subdivision of the cerebellar cortex comprised of myelinated axons lying deep to the granule cell layer of the cerebellar cortex.

UBERON:0014541.name: thoracic division of spinal cord central canal
UBERON:0014541.def: Part of spinal cord central canal contained in the thoracic spinal cord. It is continuous rostrally with the cervical spinal cord central canal and caudally with the lumbar spinal cord central canal.

UBERON:0014542.name: cervical division of cord spinal central canal
UBERON:0014542.def: Part of central canal contained within the cervical spinal cord. It is continuous caudally with the thoracic spinal cord central canal and rostrally with the fourth ventricle of the brain via the obex.

UBERON:0014543.name: lumbar division of spinal cord central canal
UBERON:0014543.def: Part of central canal lying within the lumbar spinal cord. It is continuous rostrally with the central canal of the thoracic spinal cord and caudally with the central canal of the sacral spinal cord.

UBERON:0014544.name: frontomarginal sulcus
UBERON:0014544.def: A superficial feature of the human frontal lobe; it is located at the rostral margin of the orbital surface of the lobe (Ono-90). (NN).

UBERON:0014547.name: sacral division of spinal cord central canal
UBERON:0014547.def: Part of spinal cord central canal contained in the sacral spinal cord. It is continuous rostrally with the spinal cord central canal of the lumbar cord.

UBERON:0014548.name: pyramidal layer of CA1
UBERON:0014548.def: CA1 part of stratum pyramidale hippocampi.
synonym: CA1 part of stratum pyramidale hippocampi
stratum pyramidale of the CA1 field

UBERON:0014549.name: pyramidal layer of CA2
UBERON:0014549.def: Part of pyramidal cell layer in area CA2, lying superficial to the CA2 stratum oriens, and deep to the stratum radiatum of CA2, continuous with the pyramidal cell layers of CA1 and CA3.
synonym: CA2 part of stratum pyramidale hippocampi
stratum pyramidale of the CA2 field

UBERON:0014550.name: pyramidal layer of CA3
UBERON:0014550.def: A layer of hippocampal field that is part of a hippocampus pyramidal layer and is part of a CA3 field of hippocampus.
synonym: CA3 part of stratum pyramidale hippocampi
stratum pyramidale of the CA3 field

UBERON:0014551.name: CA2 stratum oriens
UBERON:0014551.def: Part of stratum oriens lying in area CA2 deep to the CA2 pyramidal cell layer and continuous with stratum oriens of area CA2 and bounded by the dentate gyrus hilus[Modified from NIFSTD by CJM].
synonym: stratum oriens of the CA2 field

UBERON:0014552.name: CA1 stratum oriens
UBERON:0014552.def: Part of stratum oriens lying in area CA1, superficial to the alveus of CA1 and deep to the pyramidal cell layer of CA1. It is continuous with the stratum oriens of CA2 and bounded by the subiculum.
synonym: stratum oriens of the CA1 field

UBERON:0014553.name: CA3 stratum oriens
UBERON:0014553.def: Part of stratum oriens lying in area CA3 deep to the CA3 pyramidal cell layer and continuous with stratum oriens of area CA2 and bounded by the dentate gyrus hilus.
synonym: stratum oriens of the CA3 field

UBERON:0014554.name: CA1 stratum radiatum
UBERON:0014554.def: Part of stratum radiatum lying in area CA1, superficial to the CA1 pyramidal cell layer and deep to the CA1 stratum lucidum-moleculare, continuous with the stratum radiatum of CA2 and bounded by the subiculum. It contains the Schaffer collateral projection from CA3.
synonym: stratum radiatum of the CA1 field

UBERON:0014555.name: CA2 stratum radiatum

UBERON:0014558.name: CA2 stratum lacunosum moleculare

stratum lacunosum moleculare of the CA2 field

UBERON:0014559.name: CA3 stratum lacunosum moleculare

stratum lacunosum moleculare of the CA3 field

UBERON:0014560.name: CA3 stratum lucidum

UBERON:0014567.name: layer of hippocampal field

UBERON:0014641.def: A nerve root that extends_fibers_into a terminal nerve.

UBERON:0014642.name: vestibulocerebellum
UBERON:0014642.def: A phylogenetic subdivision of the cerebellum, the oldest part, which regulates balance and eye movements. It receives vestibular input from both the semicircular canals and from the vestibular nuclei, and sends fibres back to the medial and lateral vestibular nuclei. It also receives visual input from the superior colliculi and from the visual cortex (the latter via the pontine nuclei, forming a cortico-ponto-cerebellar pathway). Lesions of the vestibulocerebellum cause disturbances of balance and gait.

UBERON:0014643.name: spinocerebellum
UBERON:0014643.def: A phylogenetic subdivision of the cerebellum, the intermediate part, which regulates body and limb movements. It receives proprioception input from the dorsal columns of the spinal cord (including the spinocerebellar tract) and the trigeminal nerve, as well as from visual and auditory systems. It sends fibres to deep cerebellar nuclei which in turn project to both the cerebral cortex and the brain stem, thus providing modulation of descending motor systems.

UBERON:0014644.name: cerebrocerebellum
UBERON:0014644.def: The part of the cerebellar cortex that receives input from the cerebral cortex via axons from the pontine relay nuclei.

UBERON:0014645.name: nucleus H of ventral tegmentum
UBERON:0014645.def: A nucleus present in the ventral tegmentum of squalomorph sharks.

UBERON:0014646.name: nucleus K of ventral tegmentum
UBERON:0014646.def: A nucleus present in the ventral tegmentum of skates.

UBERON:0014647.name: hemisphere part of cerebellar anterior lobe
UBERON:0014647.def: A multi-tissue structure that is part of a anterior lobe of cerebellum and is part of a cerebellar hemisphere.
synonym: hemisphere of anterior lobe of cerebellum

UBERON:0014648.name: hemisphere part of cerebellar posterior lobe
UBERON:0014648.def: A multi-tissue structure that is part of a cerebellar hemisphere and is part of a posterior lobe of cerebellum.

UBERON:0014649.name: white matter of medulla oblongata
UBERON:0014649.def: A white matter that is part of a medulla oblongata.

UBERON:0014650.name: dorsal hypothalamic nucleus
UBERON:0014650.def: A nerve cell nucleus situated in the dorsal portion of the intermediate hypothalamic region.

UBERON:0014665.name: nucleus preopticus
UBERON:0014665.def: The nucleus preopticus (NPO) of the hypothalamus of common carp, is a homolog of the paraventricular nucleus of mammals.

UBERON:0014667.name: periventricular nucleus of hypothalamus
UBERON:0014667.def: A small nucleus at the base of the hypothalamus, adjacent to the arcuate nucleus.
