UBERON:8600026.def: A tree-like structure formed by chorionic villi that sprouts from the chorionic plate in the placental disc. The arborous shape of the chorionic villous tree provides maximal contact area with maternal blood in the intervillous space.

UBERON:8600027.name: chorionic stem villus
UBERON:8600027.def: A chorionic villus that provides structural support to the villous tree. A chorionic stem villus is characterized by a condensed fibrous stroma in which fetal arteries, veins, arterioles, and venules are embedded. It represents a distributing framework for fetal chorionic circulation, supplying the floating villi. It can exhibit a diameter ranging from approximately 3000 μm (trunci near the chorionic plate) to 80 μm (smallest ramuli chorii).

UBERON:8600028.name: chorionic mesenchymal villus
UBERON:8600028.def: The first generation of a tertiary villus that is derived from a syncytial sprout by the invasion of the mesenchyme, in which blood vessels differentiate through vasculogenesis, and gradually transforms into a new immature intermediate villus. A chorionic mesenchymal villus has a thick trophoblastic covering, and cytotrophoblast cells are interposed between syncytium and the trophoblastic basal lamina over 50–100% of the surface. The stroma is characterized by loosely arranged collagen fibers that enmesh mesenchymal and some villous macrophages. The fetal capillaries are poorly developed.

UBERON:8600029.name: chorionic immature intermediate villus
UBERON:8600029.def: A bulbous, immature chorionic villus that is formed of loose connective tissue with few fetal vessels. A chorionic immature intermediate villus develops from a chorionic mesenchymal villus, and is the forerunner of a chorionic stem villus.

UBERON:8600030.name: chorionic terminal villus
UBERON:8600030.def: The most distal part of a chorionic villus. A chorionic terminal villus is a grape-like structure characterized by a high degree of capillarization and highly dilated sinusoids. A terminal villus has less stroma and a discontinuous cytotrophoblast layer, and contains 4–6 fetal capillaries per cross section. It exhibits a diameter ranging from 40 to about 80 μm.

UBERON:8600031.name: chorionic mature intermediate villus
UBERON:8600031.def: A slender branch of a chorionic stem villus. A chorionic mature intermediate villus lacks fetal arterioles and venules in the stroma, which is composed of slender fetal capillaries embedded into a loose connective tissue that is rich in cells but poor in fibers. It exhibits a diameter ranging from 60 to about 100 μm.

UBERON:8600032.name: chorionic floating villus
UBERON:8600032.def: A chorionic villus that is not attached to the placental basal plate and it is immersed in maternal blood.

UBERON:8600033.name: chorionic anchoring villus
UBERON:8600033.def: A distal smaller chorionic stem villus that is connected to the maternal side of the placenta (in early gestational stages to the decidua, and later to the developing basal plate) via a cytotrophoblast cell column. A chorionic anchoring villus stabilizes the position of the villous tree in the maternal intervillous bloodstream.

UBERON:8600034.name: jejunum lamina propria
UBERON:8600034.def: A lamina propria that is part of a jejunum.

UBERON:8600035.name: ileum lamina propria
UBERON:8600035.def: A lamina propria that is part of an ileum.

UBERON:8600036.name: kidney loop of Henle long descending thin limb outer medulla
UBERON:8600036.def: A section of the long descending thin limb of the loop of Henle that is part of the outer medulla of the kidney.
synonym: long descending limb of the loop of Henle in the outer medulla

UBERON:8600037.name: kidney loop of Henle long descending thin limb inner medulla
UBERON:8600037.def: A section of the long descending thin limb of the loop of Henle that is part of the inner medulla of the kidney.
synonym: long descending limb of the loop of Henle in the inner medulla

UBERON:8600038.name: placental disc
UBERON:8600038.def: A disc-shaped structure that is part of the placenta. A placental disc supports fetal development through the exchange of nutrients between maternal and fetal bloodstreams. The placental disc is structured to keep the blood streams separate, while maximizing surface area for the transport of nutrients between them, to maintain an immunological barrier.

UBERON:8600039.name: chorionic villous mesenchyme
UBERON:8600039.def: A mesenchyme that is part of a chorionic villus.

UBERON:8600040.name: chorionic stem villous blood vessel
UBERON:8600040.def: A blood vessel that is part of a chorionic stem villus.

UBERON:8600041.name: chorionic terminal villous capillary
UBERON:8600041.def: A capillary that is part of a chorionic terminal villus. This capillary is generally narrow, but displays sinusoidal dilations along its length, often at the points of acute bends. These dilations bring the capillary endothelium into close contact with the overlying syncytiotrophoblast to form a vasculosyncytial membrane.

UBERON:8600042.name: endometrial lymphatic vessel
UBERON:8600042.def: A lymphatic vessel that is part of an endometrium.

UBERON:8600043.name: lateral wall of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600043.def: A wall of the urinary bladder that is situated on the sides or flanks.

UBERON:8600044.name: left lateral wall of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600044.def: A lateral wall of the urinary bladder that is located on the left side.

UBERON:8600045.name: right lateral wall of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600045.def: A lateral wall of the urinary bladder that is located on the right side.

UBERON:8600046.name: anterior wall of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600046.def: The most anterior wall of the urinary bladder.

UBERON:8600047.name: posterior wall of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600047.def: The most posterior wall of the urinary bladder.

UBERON:8600048.name: apex of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600048.def: The anterior angle of the superior surface of the urinary bladder. The apex of urinary bladder is connected to the umbilicus by the urachus in embryos, and by the median umbilical ligament, a remnant of urachus, in adults.

UBERON:8600049.name: dome of urinary bladder
UBERON:8600049.def: The anterosuperior surface of the urinary bladder, with boundaries at the apex and fundus of the urinary bladder.

UBERON:8600050.name: trophoblast island
UBERON:8600050.def: An accumulation of extravillous trophoblast cells at the tip of a floating villus or occasionally attached to the chorionic plate embedded in fibrin.

UBERON:8600051.name: segmental pulmonary vein
UBERON:8600051.def: A vein that is tributary of the main pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a segment of the lung.

UBERON:8600052.name: subsegmental pulmonary vein
UBERON:8600052.def: A vein that is tributary of the segmental pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a subsegment of the lung.

UBERON:8600053.name: esophageal vein
UBERON:8600053.def: A vein that is tributary of the azygos vein and drains blood from the esophagus.

UBERON:8600054.name: supreme intercostal vein
UBERON:8600054.def: A vein that is tributary of the superior intercostal vein and drains the first intercostal space.

UBERON:8600055.name: atrioventricular nodal artery
UBERON:8600055.def: An artery that branches from the right coronary artery and supplies the atrioventricular node.
UBERON:8600055.synonym: atrioventricular node branch of right coronary artery

UBERON:8600056.name: lateral sacral vein
UBERON:8600056.def: A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the anterior surface of the sacrum.

UBERON:8600057.name: middle hemorrhoidal vein
UBERON:8600057.def: A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein.

UBERON:8600058.name: uterine vein
UBERON:8600058.def: A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the uterus.

UBERON:8600059.name: deep cervical vein
UBERON:8600059.def: A vein that is tributary of a vertebral vein and drains the suboccipital region, adjacent vertebral column, and deep muscles of the neck.

UBERON:8600060.name: subsegmental pulmonary artery
UBERON:8600060.def: An artery that is a branch of the segmental pulmonary artery and supplies deoxyge blood to a smaller subsegment of the lung.

UBERON:8600061.name: intra-acinar venule
UBERON:8600061.def: A venule that receives drainage from the capillary beds after blood has perfused the pulmonary alveoli, and is tributary of the pulmonary venules.

UBERON:8600062.name: thyrocervical trunk
UBERON:8600062.def: An artery that branches from the subclavian artery and supplies the thyroid gland, neck, and upper back regions.

UBERON:8600063.name: septal perforating artery
UBERON:8600063.def: An artery that branches from the left anterior descending artery and supplies the interventricular septum of the heart.

UBERON:8600064.name: posterolateral artery
UBERON:8600064.def: An artery that branches from the right coronary artery or the circumflex artery and supplies the posterior and lateral walls of the left ventricle.

UBERON:8600065.name: lateral femoral circumflex vein
UBERON:8600065.def: A vein that is tributary of the femoral vein and drains blood from the front and middle areas of the thigh.
UBERON:8600065.synonym: set of lateral circumflex femoral veins

UBERON:8600066.name: basivertebral vein
UBERON:8600066.def: A vein that is tributary of the anterior internal vertebral venous plexus and drains blood from the vertebral bodies.

UBERON:8600067.name: bronchial venule
UBERON:8600067.def: A venule that is tributary of the bronchial veins and drains blood from the bronchi and bronchioles of the lungs.

UBERON:8600068.name: mental vein
UBERON:8600068.def: A vein that is tributary of the facial vein and drains blood from the chin and lower lip.

UBERON:8600069.name: deep lingual vein
UBERON:8600069.def: A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the tongue.

UBERON:8600070.name: dorsal lingual vein
UBERON:8600070.def: A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the dorsum of the tongue, and the sides of the tongue.

UBERON:8600071.name: sublingual vein
UBERON:8600071.def: A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the ventral (inferior) surface of the tongue and the sublingual glands.

UBERON:8600072.name: glandular venous plexus
UBERON:8600072.def: A venous plexus tha connects the middle and superior thyroid veins.

UBERON:8600073.name: circumflex humeral vein
UBERON:8600073.def: A vein that is tributary of the axillary vein and drains blood from the region around the neck of the humerus.

UBERON:8600074.name: thoracoacromial vein
UBERON:8600074.def: A vein that is tributary of the axillary vein and drains blood from the thoracoacromial region, including the pectoral, shoulder, and clavicular regions.

UBERON:8600075.name: transverse cervical vein
UBERON:8600075.def: A vein that is tributary of the external jugular vein and drains blood from the superficial muscles of the back, mainly the trapezius muscle.

UBERON:8600076.name: suboccipital venous plexus
UBERON:8600076.def: A venous plexus that is tributary of the deep cervical veins and drains blood from the suboccipital region.

UBERON:8600077.name: pulmonary arteriole
UBERON:8600077.def: An arteriole that branches from the pulmonary arteries and supplies deoxygenated blood to the pulmonary capillaries and alveolar capillaries of the lungs.

UBERON:8600078.name: ascending pharyngeal artery
UBERON:8600078.def: An artery of the neck that branches from the external carotid artery and supplies the pharynx.

UBERON:8600079.name: dural artery
UBERON:8600079.def: An artery that branches from the internal carotid artery and supplies the anterior clinoid process of the dura mater.

UBERON:8600080.name: pericardial artery
UBERON:8600080.def: An artery that branches from the descending thoracic aorta and supplies the dorsal portion of the pericardium.

UBERON:8600081.name: percardiacophrenic artery
UBERON:8600081.def: An artery that branches from the internal thoracic artery and supplies the pericardium and the diaphragm.

UBERON:8600082.name: superficial iliac circumflex vein
UBERON:8600082.def: A vein that is tributary of the great saphenous vein and drains blood from the inguinal region and the anterior abdominal wall.

UBERON:8600083.name: fibular vein
UBERON:8600083.def: A vein that is tributary of the posterior tibial vein and drains blood from the lateral compartment of the leg.

UBERON:8600084.name: prostatic venule
UBERON:8600084.def: A venule that is tributary of the prostatic venous plexus and drains blood from the prostate gland.

UBERON:8600085.name: hepatic portal venule
UBERON:8600085.def: A venule that branches from the hepatic portal vein to transport nutrient-rich blood from the gastrointestinal tract and spleen to supply the liver. The hepatic portal venule is tributary of the hepatic sinusoids.

UBERON:8600086.name: incisor artery
UBERON:8600086.def: An artery that branches from the inferior alveolar artery and supplies the roots and pulp of the teeth of the lower jaw. It forms anastomoses with its contralateral partner.

UBERON:8600087.name: external nasal vein
UBERON:8600087.def: A vein that is tributary of the angular vein and drains blood from the superficial tissues and skin of the dorsum (bridge) and ala (wings) of the nose.

UBERON:8600088.name: supratrochlear vein
UBERON:8600088.def: A vein that is tributary of the angular vein and drains blood from the muscles and skin of the forehead.

UBERON:8600089.name: transverse nasal root vein
UBERON:8600089.def: A vein that is tributary of the angular veins and drains blood from the bridge of the nose.

UBERON:8600090.name: hypophyseal vein
UBERON:8600090.def: A vein that is tributary of the cavernous sinus and drains blood from the pituitary gland.

UBERON:8600091.name: inferior anastomotic vein
UBERON:8600091.def: A vein that is tributary of the transverse sinus and drains blood from the adjacent cortical regions of the temporal lobe. The inferior anastomotic vein forms an anastomosis (connection) between the superficial middle cerebral vein anteriorly and the transverse sinus posteriorly.

UBERON:8600092.name: radial vein
UBERON:8600092.def: A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the lateral structures of the forearm, carpal and metacarpal bones, joints of the hand, and lateral forearm muscles.

UBERON:8600093.name: ulnar vein
UBERON:8600093.def: A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the hand and medial and posterior aspect of forearm.

UBERON:8600094.name: intra-acinar arteriole
UBERON:8600094.def: An arteriole that branches from the pulmonary arteriole and supplies deoxygenated blood to the pulmonary capillaries in the alveoli of the lungs.

UBERON:8600095.name: ascending palatine artery
UBERON:8600095.def: An artery that branches from the facial artery, and branches to supply the soft palate and the palatine tonsil.

UBERON:8600096.name: submental artery
UBERON:8600096.def: An artery that branches from the facial artery that runs forward under the mouth, then turns upward upon reaching the chin.

UBERON:8600097.name: deep lingual artery
UBERON:8600097.def: An artery that branches from the lingual artery and supplies blood to the tongue itself, particularly the body and tip of the tongue. The deep lingual artery travels superiorly in a tortuous course along the under (ventral) surface of the tongue, below the longitudinalis inferior, and above the mucous membrane.

UBERON:8600098.name: dorsal lingual artery
UBERON:8600098.def: An artery that branches from the lingual artery and supplies the soft palate, tonsils, epiglottis, palatoglossal arch, and adjacent mucous membrane. The dorsal lingual artery runs along the upper border of the hyoid bone and anastomises with its fellow of the opposite side.

UBERON:8600099.name: accessory meningeal artery
UBERON:8600099.def: An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies the meninges. The accessory meningeal artery ascends through the foramen ovale to enter the cranial cavity and supply the dura mater of the floor of the middle cranial fossa and of the trigeminal cave, and to the trigeminal ganglion.

UBERON:8600100.name: artery of pterygoid canal
UBERON:8600100.def: An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies blood to structures in the auditory tube, tympanic cavity, and upper pharynx. The artery of the pterygoid canal courses through the pterygoid canal, a small bony canal located in the sphenoid bone of the skull.

UBERON:8600101.name: descending palatine artery
UBERON:8600101.def: An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies the hard and soft palate.

UBERON:8600102.name: left anterior descending artery
UBERON:8600102.def: An artery that branches from the left coronary artery and supplies the anterior wall of the left ventricle, the interventricular septum, and the apex of the heart.
UBERON:8600102.synonym: anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery

UBERON:8600103.name: anterior internal vertebral venous plexus
UBERON:8600103.def: A venous plexus that is tributary of the basivertebral veins and internal vertebral veins, draining blood from the vertebrae and spinal cord. The anterior internal vertebral venous plexus is located within the vertebral canal.

UBERON:8600104.name: intervertebral vein
UBERON:8600104.def: A vein that drains blood from the vertebral column and intervertebral discs. In the neck, it is tributary of into the vertebral veins. In the thorax, it is tributary of the posterior intercostal veins. In the lumbar and sacral regions, it is tributary of the lumbar and lateral sacral veins

UBERON:8600105.name: lumbar vein
UBERON:8600105.def: A vein that is tributary of the inferior vena cava and drains blood from the posterior abdominal wall and lumbar region.

UBERON:8600106.name: anterior humeral circumflex artery
UBERON:8600106.def: An artery that branches from the axilliary artery and supplies the deltoid, biceps brachii, and coracobrachialis muscles, the glenohumeral joint, the proximal humeral head, and the skin overlying the anterior aspect of the proximal humerus. This artery courses laterally across the anterior surface of the humerus and anastomoses with the posterior humeral circumflex artery.

UBERON:8600107.name: posterior humeral circumflex artery
UBERON:8600107.def: An artery that branches from the axilliary artery and supplies the deltoid, teres major, teres minor, and long and lateral heads of the triceps brachii muscles, glenohumeral joint, and the cutaneous supply to the area posterolateral to the proximal humerus. This artery courses posteriorly with the axillary nerve, through the quadrangular space, to the posterior aspect of the humerus and anastomoses with the anterior humeral circumflex artery.

UBERON:8600108.name: proximal ureter
UBERON:8600108.def: A segment of the ureter that extends from the renal pelvis to the common iliac artery bifurcation (to form the internal and external iliac arteries).

UBERON:8600109.name: distal ureter
UBERON:8600109.def: A segment of the ureter that extends from the common iliac artery bifurcation to the bladder. From there, the ureter curves back and follows the lateral pelvic wall inferiorly to connect with the posterolateral bladder wall.

UBERON:8600110.name: intramural ureter
UBERON:8600110.def: The terminal segment of the ureter that is continuous with the distal ureter, lies where the ureter enters the bladder and extends within the bladder wall. The intramural ureter is aperistaltic, serving as a reflux-preventing mechanism, preventing the backflow of urine from the bladder into the ureters.

UBERON:8600111.name: right distal ureter
UBERON:8600111.def: A distal ureter that is part of the right ureter.

UBERON:8600112.name: left distal ureter
UBERON:8600112.def: A distal ureter that is part of the left ureter.

UBERON:8600113.name: right proximal ureter
UBERON:8600113.def: A proximal ureter that is part of the right ureter.

UBERON:8600114.name: left proximal ureter
UBERON:8600114.def: A proximal ureter that is part of the left ureter.

UBERON:8600115.name: right intramural ureter
UBERON:8600115.def: An intramural ureter that is part of the right ureter.

UBERON:8600116.name: left intramural ureter
UBERON:8600116.def: An intramural ureter that is part of the left ureter.

UBERON:8600117.name: antimesosalpinx
UBERON:8600117.def: A posterior free border of a mesosalpinx.

UBERON:8600118.name: myenteric ganglion
UBERON:8600118.def: A ganglion that is part of a myenteric plexus. The myoenteric ganglion serves as a control center for local gut functions, such as motility.

UBERON:8600119.name: myenteric ganglion of small intestine
UBERON:8600119.def: A myenteric ganglion located in the myenteric plexus of the small intestine.

UBERON:8600120.name: atrial intrinsic cardiac ganglion
UBERON:8600120.def: A ganglion that is part of the atrial region of the heart. The activation of efferent neurons in this ganglion results in the modulation of heart rate, atrio-ventricular node conduction, and inotropism of atria and ventricles.

UBERON:8600121.name: lumbar ganglion
UBERON:8600121.def: A ganglion that is part of the lumbar portion of the sympathetic trunk. The neurons in a lumbar ganglion are postganglionic sympathetic neurons that synapse with axons from preganglionic sympathetic neurons.

UBERON:8600122.name: sacral ganglion
UBERON:8600122.def: A ganglion that is part of the sacral portion of the sympathetic trunk. A sacral ganglion consists of postganglionic sympathetic neurons that receive presynaptic input from preganglionic sympathetic axons descending through the sympathetic trunk from thoracolumbar levels.

UBERON:8600123.name: lower airway ganglion
UBERON:8600123.def: A parasympathetic ganglion that is located within the airway walls of the lower respiratory tract. This ganglion is responsible for controlling the constriction of the airway by stimulating smooth muscle contraction in the lower respiratory tract to regulate airflow.

UBERON:8600124.name: fallopian tube epithelium
UBERON:8600124.def: A simple columnar epithelium that is part of the fallopian tube.

UBERON:8600125.name: superior fallopian tube epithelium
UBERON:8600125.def: The superior region of the fallopian tube epithelium.

UBERON:8600126.name: inferior fallopian tube epithelium
UBERON:8600126.def: The inferior region of the fallopian tube epithelium.

UBERON:8600127.name: mesosalpinx-proximal fallopian tube epithelium
UBERON:8600127.def: The most proximal region to the mesosalpinx of the fallopian tube epithelium.

UBERON:8600128.name: antimesosalpinx-proximal fallopian tube epithelium
UBERON:8600128.def: The most proximal region to the antimesosalpinx of the fallopian tube epithelium.

UBERON:8600130.name: superior muscular layer of fallopian tube
UBERON:8600130.def: The most superior region of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.

UBERON:8600131.name: inferior muscular layer of fallopian tube
UBERON:8600131.def: The most inferior region of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.

UBERON:8600132.name: mesosalpinx-proximal muscular layer of fallopian tube
UBERON:8600132.def: The most proximal region to the mesosalpinx of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.

UBERON:8600133.name: antimesosalpinx-proximal muscular layer of fallopian tube
UBERON:8600133.def: The most proximal region to the antimesosalpinx of the muscularis layer of the fallopian tube.

UBERON:8700000.name: aorta-gonad-mesonephros
UBERON:8700000.def: A transient organ in the developing embryo composed of the dorsal aorta, developing gonads, and embryonic kidney. This structure is located in the embryonic mesoderm and serves as the primary site for the generation of definitive hematopoietic stem cells.

UBERON:8700001.name: follicle associated epithelium
UBERON:8700001.def: A specialized epithelial layer overlying the luminal surface of lymphoid follicles in gut-associated lymphoid tissue. It is found in Peyer's patches of the small intestine and appendix in humans and in the intestine and caecal patches in mice. This layer contains specialised M cells and has fewer goblet cells compared to surrounding tissue. This layer plays a crucial role in mucosal immune surveillance.

UBERON:8700002.name: stratum spinosum of esophageal epithelium
UBERON:8700002.def: The second deepest layer of the stratified squamous epithelium lining the esophagus, positioned directly above the stratum basale. It consists of multiple layers of keratinocytes connected by strong intercellular junctions called desmosomes, giving the cells a characteristic \

UBERON:8850000.name: lumen of pulmonary alveolus
UBERON:8850000.def: An anatomical cavity that is part of the alveolus of the lung

UBERON:8900000.name: sensory corpuscle
UBERON:8900000.def: A mechanosensory complex in the terminal end of some nerves that forms a corpuscle. It consists of one or more neuronal terminations and associated non-neuronal cells.

UBERON:8910000.name: stomatogastric nervous system
UBERON:8910000.def: The part of the nervous system that controls the stomach, such as in crabs, lobsters, and flies

UBERON:8910001.name: stomatogastric ganglion
UBERON:8910001.def: The stomatogastric ganglion (STG) consists of about 30 neurons that form two central pattern generator circuits in crustaceans. STG neurons have large soma (~50-100 um) and have complex branches. The STG contains the motor neurons that innervate the striated muscles that move the gastric mill and pyloric regions of the stomach.

UBERON:8910010.name: stomatogastric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910010.def: The stomatogastric nerve (SGN) is made up of four separate nerves that emerge from the paired commissural ganglia, the superior and inferior esophageal nerves (SONs and IONs).

UBERON:8910011.name: dorsal gastric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910011.def: Nerve carrying dorsal gastric (DG) neurons which control the medial tooth movements in crustaceans.

UBERON:8910012.name: gastropyloric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910012.def: Consists of gastropyloric receptor (GPR) neurons, which are stretch receptors that innervate stomach muscles in crustaceans.

UBERON:8910013.name: lateral gastric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910013.def: Consists of lateral gastric (LG) neurons. The alternation between the lateral gastric neurons/medial gastric neurons and the lateral posterior gastric neurons control the movements of the lateral teeth in crustaceans.

UBERON:8910014.name: lateral ventricular nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910014.def: The motor axons that project into the dorsal ventricular nerve bifurcate and then project into both lateral ventricular nerves.

UBERON:8910015.name: pyloric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910015.def: Innervates pyloric region of the stomach.

UBERON:8910016.name: pyloric dilator nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910016.def: Innervates muscles that dilate valves of the pylorus motor neurons involved in filtering in crustaceans. Anterior burster neurons are intrinsic oscillators that are electrically coupled with pyloric dilator neurons, causing them to fire bursts of action potentials. Together these neurons inhibit lateral pyloric and pyloric neurons, forcing them to fire in alternation with the pyloric dilator neurons.

UBERON:8910017.name: inferior esophageal nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910017.def: The inferior esophageal nerve (ION) is one of the four nerves that make up the stomatogastric nerve (SGN).

UBERON:8910018.name: superior esophageal nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910018.def: The superior esophageal nerve (SON) is one of the four nerves that make up the stomatogastric nerve (SGN).

UBERON:8910020.name: esophageal ganglion (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910020.def: Neurons with cell bodies in the esophageal ganglion turn on the gastric mill rhythm and strongly affects the pyloric rhythm.

UBERON:8910021.name: commissural ganglion (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910021.def: Contains motor fibers that innervate the esophagus. Stimulating the pyloric suppressor neuron alters both pyloric and gastric rhythms but also elicits activity in a third oscillatory circuit located in the commissural ganglia called the esophageal rhythm.

UBERON:8910022.name: junction of superior esophageal nerve and stomatogastric nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910022.def: The junction between the stomatogastric nerve (STN) and the superior esophageal nerve (SON) shows synaptic structures. Octopamine may be released at this site by projection neurons; its application at this junction induces action potentials in the axons of the modulatory commissural neuron 5 (MCN5) that project from the commissural ganglia to the stomatogastric ganglion (STG).

UBERON:8910023.name: median ventricular nerve (sensu Cancer borealis)
UBERON:8910023.def: Most of the efferent fibers leaving the stomatogastric ganglion and leading to the gastric mill or pyloric stomach muscles run posteriorly in the dorsal median ventricular nerve. This nerve branches bilaterally into the right and left lateral ventricular nerves (LVN) which go to their respective sides of the stomach.

UBERON:8920000.name: anterior ciliary artery
UBERON:8920000.def: An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the anterior segment of the eyeball and ciliary body.

UBERON:8920001.name: short posterior ciliary artery
UBERON:8920001.def: An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the choroid and ciliary processes.
synonym: Set of short posterior ciliary arteries

UBERON:8920002.name: long posterior ciliary artery
UBERON:8920002.def: An artery that branches from the ophthalmic artery and supplies the choroid, ciliary body and iris.
synonym: Set of long posterior ciliary arteries

UBERON:8920003.name: right marginal artery
UBERON:8920003.def: An artery that is a branch of the right coronary artery. It follows the acute margin of the heart supplying blood to the right ventricle.
UBERON:8920003.synonym: Marginal branch of right coronary artery

UBERON:8920004.name: segmental renal artery
UBERON:8920004.def: An artery that branches from the renal artery. The anterior division of the renal artery typically divides into four segmental arteries, whereas the posterior division of the renal artery supplies one segmental artery.

UBERON:8920005.name: superior segmental renal artery
UBERON:8920005.def: A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, superiorly and laterally. It supplies the superior (apical) lobe of the kidney.

UBERON:8920006.name: anterior superior segmental renal artery
UBERON:8920006.def: A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, superiorly and laterally towards the superior pole of the kidney. It does not ascend as steeply as the superior segmental artery and does not extend into the superior pole. It supplies the anterosuperior lobe of the kidney, which includes the central anterosuperior region, extending to the lateral aspect and slightly onto the posterior surface of the kidney.

UBERON:8920007.name: anterior inferior segmental renal artery
UBERON:8920007.def: A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, laterally and angled slightly inferiorly. It supplies the anteroinferior lobe of the kidney, which includes the central anteroinferior region, extending to the lateral aspect and slightly onto the posterior surface of the kidney.

UBERON:8920008.name: inferior segmental renal artery
UBERON:8920008.def: A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, inferiorly and laterally towards the inferior pole of the kidney. It supplies the inferior lobe of the kidney, which encompasses the whole of the inferior pole of the kidney, including the anterior and posterior surfaces.

UBERON:8920009.name: posterior segmental renal artery
UBERON:8920009.def: A segmental renal artery that passes posterior to the renal pelvis and travels laterally, more or less horizontally. It supplies the posterior lobe of the kidney, which includes all of the central-posterior surface of the kidney. This excludes the superior and inferior poles and a small posterolateral portion.

CL:0000000.name: cell
CL:0000000.def: A material entity of anatomical origin (part of or deriving from an organism) that has as its parts a maximally connected cell compartment surrounded by a plasma membrane.

CL:0000001.name: primary cultured cell
CL:0000001.def: A cultured cell that is freshly isolated from a organismal source, or derives in culture from such a cell prior to the culture being passaged.

CL:0000002.name: obsolete immortal cell line cell
CL:0000002.def: OBSOLETE: A cell line cell that is expected to be capable of an unlimited number of divisions, and is thus able to support indefinite growth/propagation in vitro as part of a immortal cell line.

CL:0000003.name: obsolete native cell
CL:0000003.def: OBSOLETE. A cell that is found in a natural setting, which includes multicellular organism cells 'in vivo' (i.e. part of an organism), and unicellular organisms 'in environment' (i.e. part of a natural environment).

CL:0000004.name: obsolete cell by organism
CL:0000004.def: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by the organisms within which they are contained.

CL:0000005.name: neural crest derived fibroblast
CL:0000005.def: Any fibroblast that is derived from the neural crest.

CL:0000006.name: neuronal receptor cell
CL:0000006.def: Any sensory receptor cell that is a(n) neuron and is capable of some detection of stimulus involved in sensory perception.

CL:0000007.name: early embryonic cell (metazoa)
CL:0000007.def: A cell found in the embryo before the formation of all the gem layers is complete.

CL:0000008.name: migratory cranial neural crest cell
CL:0000008.def: Cell that is part of the migratory cranial neural crest population. Migratory cranial neural crest cells develop from premigratory cranial neural crest cells and have undergone epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination.

CL:0000009.name: obsolete fusiform initial
CL:0000009.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000079 from Plant Ontology instead. An elongated cell with approximately wedge-shaped ends, found in the vascular cambium, which gives rise to the elements of the axial system in the secondary vascular tissues.

CL:0000010.name: cultured cell
CL:0000010.def: A cell in vitro that is or has been maintained or propagated as part of a cell culture.

CL:0000011.name: migratory trunk neural crest cell
CL:0000011.def: Cell that is part of the migratory trunk neural crest population. Migratory trunk neural crest cells develop from premigratory trunk neural crest cells and have undergone epithelial to mesenchymal transition and delamination.

CL:0000014.name: germ line stem cell
CL:0000014.def: A stem cell that is the precursor of gametes.

CL:0000015.name: male germ cell
CL:0000015.def: A germ cell that supports male gamete production. In some species, non-germ cells known as Sertoli cells also play a role in spermatogenesis.

CL:0000016.name: male germ line stem cell
CL:0000016.def: A stem cell that is the precursor of male gametes.

CL:0000017.name: spermatocyte
CL:0000017.def: A male germ cell that develops from spermatogonia. The euploid primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis and give rise to the haploid secondary spermatocytes which in turn give rise to spermatids.

CL:0000018.name: spermatid
CL:0000018.def: A male germ cell that develops from the haploid secondary spermatocytes. Without further division, spermatids undergo structural changes and give rise to spermatozoa.

CL:0000019.name: sperm
CL:0000019.def: A mature male germ cell that develops from a spermatid.

CL:0000020.name: spermatogonium
CL:0000020.def: An euploid male germ cell of an early stage of spermatogenesis.

CL:0000021.name: female germ cell
CL:0000021.def: Female germ cell is a germ cell that supports female gamete production.

CL:0000022.name: female germ line stem cell
CL:0000022.def: A stem cell that is the precursor of female gametes.

CL:0000023.name: oocyte
CL:0000023.def: A female germ cell that has entered meiosis.

CL:0000024.name: oogonial cell
CL:0000024.def: An undifferentiated germ cell that proliferates rapidly and gives rise to oocytes.

CL:0000025.name: egg cell
CL:0000025.def: A female gamete where meiosis has progressed to metaphase II and is able to participate in fertilization.

CL:0000026.name: invertebrate nurse cell
CL:0000026.def: A germline cell that contributes to the development of the oocyte by transferring cytoplasm directly to oocyte.

CL:0000027.name: smooth muscle cell neural crest derived
CL:0000027.def: A smooth muscle cell derived from the neural crest.

CL:0000029.name: neural crest derived neuron
CL:0000029.def: Any neuron that develops from some migratory neural crest cell.

CL:0000030.name: glioblast
CL:0000030.def: A non-terminally differentiated cell that develops form the neuroectoderm. Glioblast has the potential to differentiate into various types of glial cells, including astrocytes and oligodendrocytes.

CL:0000031.name: neuroblast (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000031.def: A cell that will develop into a neuron often after a migration phase.

CL:0000032.name: neuroplacodal cell
CL:0000032.def: A cell of a platelike structure, especially a thickened plate of ectoderm in the early embryo, from which a sense organ develops.

CL:0000033.name: apocrine cell
CL:0000033.def: An exocrine cell characterized by loss of part of the cytoplasm during the process of secretion. The secreted substance is accumulated at the apical end and is either budded off through the plasma membrane producing secreted vesicles or dissolved in the cytoplasm that is lost during secretion.

CL:0000034.name: stem cell
CL:0000034.def: A relatively undifferentiated cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

CL:0000035.name: single fate stem cell
CL:0000035.def: A stem cell that self-renews as well as give rise to a single mature cell type.

CL:0000037.name: hematopoietic stem cell
CL:0000037.def: A stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop, including blood cells and cells of the immune system. Hematopoietic stem cells lack cell markers of effector cells (lin-negative). Lin-negative is defined by lacking one or more of the following cell surface markers: CD2, CD3 epsilon, CD4, CD5 ,CD8 alpha chain, CD11b, CD14, CD19, CD20, CD56, ly6G, ter119.

CL:0000038.name: erythroid progenitor cell
CL:0000038.def: A progenitor cell committed to the erythroid lineage.

CL:0000039.name: germ line cell
CL:0000039.def: A cell that is within the developmental lineage of gametes and is able to pass along its genetic material to offspring.

CL:0000040.name: monoblast
CL:0000040.def: A myeloid progenitor cell committed to the monocyte lineage. This cell is CD11b-positive, has basophilic cytoplasm, euchromatin, and the presence of a nucleolus.

CL:0000041.name: mature eosinophil
CL:0000041.def: A fully differentiated eosinophil, a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and which can be stained by the dye eosin. Cells are also differentiated from other granulocytes by a small nuclear-to-cytoplasm ratio (1:3). This cell type is CD49d-positive.

CL:0000042.name: neutrophilic myeloblast
CL:0000042.def: A myeloblast committed to the neutrophil lineage. This cell type is GATA-1 positive, C/EBPa-positive, AML-1-positive, c-myb-positive and has low expression of PU.1 transcription factor.

CL:0000043.name: mature basophil
CL:0000043.def: A fully differentiated basophil, a granular leukocyte with an irregularly shaped, pale-staining nucleus that is partially constricted into two lobes, and with cytoplasm that contains coarse granules of variable size. Basophils contain vasoactive amines such as histamine and serotonin, which are released on appropriate stimulation.

CL:0000045.name: obsolete thymus processed stem cell
CL:0000045.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000046.name: obsolete bursa processed stem cell
CL:0000046.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000047.name: neural stem cell
CL:0000047.def: An undifferentiated neural cell that originates from the neuroectoderm and has the capacity both to perpetually self-renew without differentiating and to generate multiple central nervous system neuronal and glial cell types.

CL:0000048.name: multi fate stem cell
CL:0000048.def: A stem cell that can give rise to multiple lineages of cells.

CL:0000049.name: common myeloid progenitor
CL:0000049.def: A progenitor cell committed to myeloid lineage, including the megakaryocyte and erythroid lineages.
synonym: colony forming unit granulocyte, erythrocyte, macrophage, and megakaryocyte

CL:0000050.name: megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor cell
CL:0000050.def: A progenitor cell committed to the megakaryocyte and erythroid lineages.

CL:0000051.name: common lymphoid progenitor
CL:0000051.def: A oligopotent progenitor cell committed to the lymphoid lineage.

CL:0000052.name: totipotent stem cell
CL:0000052.def: A stem cell from which all cells of the body can form.

CL:0000055.name: non-terminally differentiated cell
CL:0000055.def: A precursor cell with a limited number of potential fates.

CL:0000056.name: myoblast
CL:0000056.def: A cell that is commited to differentiating into a muscle cell.  Embryonic myoblasts develop from the mesoderm. They undergo proliferation, migrate to their various sites, and then differentiate into the appropriate form of myocytes.  Myoblasts also occur as transient populations of cells in muscles undergoing repair.

CL:0000057.name: fibroblast
CL:0000057.def: A connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules. Flattened and irregular in outline with branching processes; appear fusiform or spindle-shaped.

CL:0000058.name: chondroblast
CL:0000058.def: Skeletogenic cell that is typically non-terminally differentiated, secretes an avascular, GAG rich matrix; is not buried in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, located adjacent to cartilage tissue (including within the perichondrium), and develops from prechondroblast (and thus prechondrogenic) cell.

CL:0000059.name: ameloblast
CL:0000059.def: Skeletogenic cell that produces enamel, overlies the odontogenic papilla, and arises from the differentiation of a preameloblast cell.

CL:0000060.name: odontoblast
CL:0000060.def: Skeletogenic cell that secretes dentine matrix, is derived from the odontogenic papilla, and develops from a preodontoblast cell.

CL:0000061.name: cementoblast
CL:0000061.def: Skeletogenic cell that produces cementum (a bony substance that covers the root of a tooth), is part of the odontogenic papilla, and develops from a precementoblast cell.

CL:0000062.name: osteoblast
CL:0000062.def: Skeletogenic cell that secretes osteoid, is capable of producing mineralized (hydroxyapatite) matrix, is located adjacent to or within osteoid tissue, and arises from the transformation of a preosteoblast cell.

CL:0000063.name: obsolete cell by histology
CL:0000063.def: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by their microscopic appearance.

CL:0000064.name: ciliated cell
CL:0000064.def: A cell that has a filiform extrusion of the cell surface.

CL:0000065.name: ependymal cell
CL:0000065.def: A neuroepithelial glial cell, derived from a radial glial cell originating from the neuroectoderm, lines the ventricles of the brain and the central canal of the spinal cord. This cell is characterized by the presence of cilia on its apical surface, which can be motile or non-motile.

CL:0000066.name: epithelial cell
CL:0000066.def: A cell that is usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface. The cell has a cytoskeleton that allows for tight cell to cell contact and for cell polarity where apical part is directed towards the lumen and the basal part to the basal lamina.

CL:0000067.name: ciliated epithelial cell
CL:0000067.def: An epithelial cell that has a cilia.

CL:0000068.name: duct epithelial cell
CL:0000068.def: An epithelial cell that is part of a duct.

CL:0000071.name: blood vessel endothelial cell
CL:0000071.def: An endothelial cell that lines the vasculature.

CL:0000074.name: obsolete epithem cell
CL:0000074.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000066 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell that constitutes the mesophyll of a hydathode and is located between the xylem endings and the epidermis. Proposed to be involved in the retrieval of solutes from the xylem sap.

CL:0000075.name: columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell
CL:0000075.def: A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface. Columnar/cuboidal epithelial cells take on the shape of a column or cube.

CL:0000077.name: mesothelial cell
CL:0000077.def: A flat, squamous-like epithelial cell of mesodermal origin. It forms the mesothelium, which lines the body's serous cavities including the pleural, peritoneal, and pericardial spaces. This cell plays a crucial role in synthesizing and secreting lubricants, such as glycosaminoglycans and surfactants, which minimize friction between adjacent tissues during movement.

CL:0000078.name: peridermal cell
CL:0000078.def: Any squamous epithelial cell that is part of some periderm.

CL:0000079.name: stratified epithelial cell
CL:0000079.def: An epithelial cell, organized into multiple layers, with only the basal layer being in contact with the basement membrane.

CL:0000080.name: circulating cell
CL:0000080.def: A cell which moves among different tissues of the body, via blood, lymph, or other medium.

CL:0000081.name: blood cell
CL:0000081.def: A cell found predominately in the blood.

CL:0000082.name: epithelial cell of lung
CL:0000082.def: An epithelial cell of the lung.

CL:0000083.name: epithelial cell of pancreas
CL:0000083.def: An epithelial cell of the pancreas.

CL:0000084.name: T cell
CL:0000084.def: A type of lymphocyte whose defining characteristic is the expression of a T cell receptor complex.

CL:0000085.name: obsolete germ line stem cell (sensu Vertebrata)

CL:0000086.name: obsolete germ line stem cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)

CL:0000087.name: obsolete male germ line stem cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)

CL:0000088.name: obsolete female germ line stem cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)

CL:0000089.name: obsolete male germ line stem cell (sensu Vertebrata)

CL:0000090.name: obsolete female germ line stem cell (sensu Vertebrata)

CL:0000091.name: Kupffer cell
CL:0000091.def: A tissue-resident macrophage of the reticuloendothelial system found on the luminal surface of the hepatic sinusoids involved in erythrocyte clearance. Markers include F4/80+, CD11b-low, CD68-positive, sialoadhesin-positive, CD163/SRCR-positive. Irregular, with long processes including lamellipodia extending into the sinusoid lumen, have flattened nucleus with cytoplasm containing characteristic invaginations of the plasma membrane (vermiform bodies); lie within the sinusoid lumen attached to the endothelial surface; derived from the bone marrow, form a major part of the body's mononuclear phagocyte system.

CL:0000092.name: osteoclast
CL:0000092.def: A specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue, which typically differentiates from monocytes. This cell has the following markers: tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase type 5-positive, PU.1-positive, c-fos-positive, nuclear factor NF-kappa-B p100 subunit-positive, tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 11A-positive and macrophage colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor-positive.

CL:0000093.name: obsolete osteochondroclast
CL:0000093.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000094.name: granulocyte
CL:0000094.def: A leukocyte with abundant granules in the cytoplasm.

CL:0000096.name: mature neutrophil
CL:0000096.def: A fully differentiated neutrophil, a granular leukocyte having a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes. They are produced in bone marrow at a rate of 5e10-10e10/day and have a half-life of 6-8 hours. Neutrophils are CD15-positive, CD16-positive, CD32-positive, CD43-positive, CD181-positive, and CD182-positive.

CL:0000097.name: mast cell
CL:0000097.def: A cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation. Progenitors leave bone marrow and mature in connective and mucosal tissue. Mature mast cells are found in all tissues, except the bloodstream. Their phenotype is CD117-high, CD123-negative, CD193-positive, CD200R3-positive, and FceRI-high. Stem-cell factor (KIT-ligand; SCF) is the main controlling signal of their survival and development.

CL:0000098.name: sensory epithelial cell
CL:0000098.def: A specialized epithelial cell involved in sensory perception. Restricted to special sense organs of the olfactory, gustatory, and vestibulocochlear receptor systems; contain sensory cells surrounded by supportive, non-receptive cells.

CL:0000099.name: interneuron
CL:0000099.def: Most generally any neuron which is not motor or sensory. Interneurons may also refer to neurons whose axons remain within a particular brain region as contrasted with projection neurons which have axons projecting to other brain regions.

CL:0000100.name: motor neuron
CL:0000100.def: An efferent neuron that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes or inhibits movement.

CL:0000101.name: sensory neuron
CL:0000101.def: Any neuron having a sensory function; an afferent neuron conveying sensory impulses.

CL:0000102.name: polymodal neuron
CL:0000102.def: A neuron type that respond to multiple stimuli such as mechanical, thermal and chemical. This neuron type is responsible for integrating different types of sensory inputs, allowing organisms to respond appropriately to diverse environmental challenges.

CL:0000103.name: bipolar neuron
CL:0000103.def: A type of interneuron that has two neurites, usually an axon and a dendrite, extending from opposite poles of an ovoid cell body.

CL:0000104.name: multipolar neuron
CL:0000104.def: A neuron with three or more neurites, usually an axon and multiple dendrites.

CL:0000105.name: pseudounipolar neuron
CL:0000105.def: Neuron with two neurites that are fused grossly when they protrude from the soma and bifurcate a short distance from the soma.

CL:0000106.name: unipolar neuron
CL:0000106.def: Neuron with one neurite that extends from the cell body.

CL:0000107.name: autonomic neuron
CL:0000107.def: A neuron whose cell body is within an autonomic ganglion.

CL:0000108.name: cholinergic neuron
CL:0000108.def: A neuron that uses acetylcholine as a vesicular neurotransmitter.

CL:0000110.name: peptidergic neuron
CL:0000110.def: A neuron that uses neuropeptides as transmitters.

CL:0000112.name: columnar neuron
CL:0000112.def: A neuron of the invertebrate central nervous system. This neuron innervates the central complex (CX) of an invertebrate brain and it forms columnar patterns with its dendrites. It is involved in navigation and spatial processing.

CL:0000113.name: mononuclear phagocyte
CL:0000113.def: A vertebrate phagocyte with a single nucleus.

CL:0000114.name: surface ectodermal cell
CL:0000114.def: An ectodermal cell that is part of the external ectoderm, forming the outermost layer of the developing embryo. It is characterized by its polarized nature, with distinct apical and basal surfaces (Ferrante Jr., Reinke, & Stanley, 1995). Surface ectodermal cell gives rise to the epidermis, hair follicles, nails, sensory organs, and specialized structures like the apical ectodermal ridge crucial for limb development (Skoufa et al., 2024).

CL:0000115.name: endothelial cell
CL:0000115.def: An endothelial cell comprises the outermost layer or lining of anatomical structures and can be squamous or cuboidal. In mammals, endothelial cell has vimentin filaments and is derived from the mesoderm.

CL:0000116.name: pioneer neuron
CL:0000116.def: Pioneer neurons establish a pathway in the developing central nervous system and then undergo programmed cell death once the adult axons, which follow them, have made connections with the target site. Thus, they are a transient cell type involved in axon guidance.

CL:0000118.name: basket cell
CL:0000118.def: Basket cells are inhibitory GABAergic interneurons of the brain. In general, dendrites of basket cells are free branching and contain smooth spines. Axons are highly branched. The branched axonal arborizations give rise to basket-like structures that surround the soma of the target cell. Basket cells form axo-somatic synapses, meaning their synapses target somas of other cells.

CL:0000119.name: cerebellar Golgi cell
CL:0000119.def: Large intrinsic neuron located in the granule layer of the cerebellar cortex that extends its dendrites into the molecular layer where they receive contact from parallel fibers. The axon of the Golgi cell ramifies densely in the granule layer and enters into a complex arrangement with mossy fiber terminals and granule cell dendrites to form the cerebellar glomerulus. Llinas, Walton and Lang. In The Synaptic Organization of the Brain. 5th ed. 2004.

CL:0000120.name: granule cell
CL:0000120.def: A neuron of the vertebrate central nervous system that is small in size. This general class includes small neurons in the granular layer of the cerebellar cortex, cerebral cortex neurons that are not pyramidal cells and small neurons without axons found in the olfactory bulb.

CL:0000121.name: Purkinje cell
CL:0000121.def: An inhibitory neuron and the sole output neuron of the cerebellar cortex, the Purkinje cell's soma is located between the granular and molecular layers of the cerebellum. It is one of the largest neural cells in the mammalian brain, ranging from 50 to 80 micrometres in diameter. Purkinje cells have planar, fan-shaped dendrites that branch extensively with little overlap. This cell type receives synaptic input from parallel fibres, which modulate high-frequency spike activity known as simple spikes and climbing fibres, which modulate infrequent calcium spike activity known as complex spikes. Purkinje cells are involved in motor coordination, particularly in correcting movements in progress.

CL:0000122.name: stellate neuron
CL:0000122.def: A neuron that has dendritic processes radiating from the cell body forming a star-like shape.

CL:0000124.name: obsolete glial cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)

CL:0000125.name: glial cell
CL:0000125.def: A non-neuronal cell of the nervous system. They not only provide physical support, but also respond to injury, regulate the ionic and chemical composition of the extracellular milieu. Guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons.

CL:0000126.name: macroglial cell
CL:0000126.def: A neuroglial cell of ectodermal origin, i.e., the astrocytes and oligodendrocytes considered together.

CL:0000127.name: astrocyte
CL:0000127.def: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes (from 'star' cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with 'end feet' which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the blood-brain barrier. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and 'reactive astrocytes' (along with microglia) respond to injury.

CL:0000128.name: oligodendrocyte
CL:0000128.def: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system. Form the insulating myelin sheath of axons in the central nervous system.

CL:0000129.name: microglial cell
CL:0000129.def: A transcriptomically distinct central nervous system macrophage found in the parenchyma of the central nervous system. Marker include CD11b-positive, F4/80-positive, and CD68-positive.

CL:0000130.name: neuron associated cell (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)

CL:0000131.name: gut endothelial cell
CL:0000131.def: An endothelial cell that lines the blood and lymphatic vessels of the digestive tract. This cell forms the gut–vascular barrier (GVB) through tight junctions and crosstalk with pericytes and enteric glial cells, regulating the passage of nutrients and immune cells while restricting microbial translocation into the bloodstream.

CL:0000132.name: corneal endothelial cell
CL:0000132.def: An hexagonal, flattened, mitochondria-rich endothelial cell that forms a monolayer on the posterior surface of the cornea (the corneal endothelium). Corneal endothelial cells are derived from the neural crest and are responsible for keeping the cornea transparent by maintaining the tissue in a semi-dry state through the action of their ionic pumps and tight junction barrier.

CL:0000133.name: neurectodermal cell
CL:0000133.def: Ectoderm destined to be nervous tissue.

CL:0000134.name: mesenchymal stem cell
CL:0000134.def: A connective tissue cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses. In humans, this cell type is CD73-positive, CD90-positive, CD105-positive, CD45-negative, CD34-negative, and MHCII-negative. They may further differentiate into osteoblasts, adipocytes, myocytes, neurons, or chondroblasts in vitro. Originally described as residing in the bone marrow, this cell type is now known to reside in many, if not all, adult organs.

CL:0000135.name: fibrocyte
CL:0000135.def: An inactive fibroblast; cytoplasm is sparse, endoplasmic reticulum is scanty with flattened nucleus. Term used by some histologists; when fibroblasts become relatively inactive in fiber formation. However, this cell has the potential for fibrogenesis in quiescent connective tissue of the adult, as well as during development, other histologists prefer to use the term fibroblast in all circumstances. These cells represent ~0.5% of peripheral blood leukocytes.

CL:0000136.name: adipocyte
CL:0000136.def: A fat-storing cell found mostly in the abdominal cavity and subcutaneous tissue of mammals. Fat is usually stored in the form of triglycerides.

CL:0000137.name: osteocyte
CL:0000137.def: A mature osteoblast that has become embedded in the bone matrix. They occupy a small cavity, called lacuna, in the matrix and are connected to adjacent osteocytes via protoplasmic projections called canaliculi.

CL:0000138.name: chondrocyte
CL:0000138.def: Skeletogenic cell that is terminally differentiated, secretes an avascular, GAG-rich matrix, is embedded in cartilage tissue matrix, retains the ability to divide, and develops from a chondroblast cell.

CL:0000140.name: odontocyte
CL:0000140.def: Skeletogenic cell that secretes dentine matrix, is derived from odontogenic papilla. Embedded in dentine tissue, and is the transformation of a non-terminally differentiated odontoblast cell.

CL:0000141.name: cementocyte
CL:0000141.def: An osteocytelike cell with numerous processes, trapped in a lacuna in the cement of the tooth.

CL:0000142.name: hyalocyte
CL:0000142.def: A cell occurring in the peripheral part of the vitreous body of the eye that may be responsible for production of hyaluronic acid and collagen.

CL:0000144.name: obsolete cell by function
CL:0000144.def: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by their primary end goal or behavior.

CL:0000145.name: professional antigen presenting cell
CL:0000145.def: A cell capable of processing and presenting lipid and protein antigens to T cells in order to initiate an immune response.

CL:0000147.name: pigment cell
CL:0000147.def: A pigment cell is a cell that contains pigment granules.

CL:0000148.name: melanocyte
CL:0000148.def: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which gives a brown to black appearance.

CL:0000150.name: glandular secretory epithelial cell
CL:0000150.def: An epithelial cell, located in a gland, that is specialised for the synthesis and secretion of specific biomolecules, such as hormones, or mucous.

CL:0000151.name: secretory cell
CL:0000151.def: A cell that specializes in controlled release of one or more substances.

CL:0000152.name: exocrine cell
CL:0000152.def: A cell of an exocrine gland; i.e. a gland that discharges its secretion via a duct.

CL:0000154.name: protein secreting cell
CL:0000154.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some protein secretion.

CL:0000155.name: peptic cell
CL:0000155.def: An epithelial cell of the stomach that is part of the fundic gastric gland. This cell is characterized by a basally located nucleus, abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum, and large apical secretory granules. It produces and secretes pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of the digestive enzyme pepsin.

CL:0000156.name: obsolete antibody secreting cell
CL:0000156.def: OBSOLETE: A cell of the lymphoid series that can react with antigen to produce specific cell products called antibodies. Various cell subpopulations, often B cells, can be defined, based on the different classes of immunoglobulins that they synthesize.

CL:0000157.name: surfactant secreting cell
CL:0000157.def: A cell that specializes in secretion of surfactant in the alveoli of the lung.

CL:0000158.name: club cell
CL:0000158.def: A non-mucous, epithelial secretory cell that is part of the tracheobronchial tree. A club cell has short microvilli but no cilia. A club cell is able to multiply and differentiate into ciliated cells to regenerate the bronchiolar epithelium and it also protects the tracheobronchial epithelium.

CL:0000160.name: goblet cell
CL:0000160.def: A specialized, columnar, mucus secreting epithelial cell shaped like a flask or goblet. A narrow basal end contains the nucleus while the apical end is swollen by the accumulation of mucus laden secretory granules.  Short microvilli project from the apical plasma membrane.

CL:0000162.name: parietal cell
CL:0000162.def: An epithelial cell of the stomach that is part of the fundic gastric gland. This cell is characterized by its pyramidal shape, abundant mitochondria, and a complex network of secretory canaliculi lined with microvilli. It secretes hydrochloric acid into the stomach lumen and produces intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption.

CL:0000163.name: endocrine cell
CL:0000163.def: A cell of an endocrine gland, ductless glands that secrete substances which are released directly into the circulation and which influence metabolism and other body functions.

CL:0000164.name: enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000164.def: An endocrine cell that is located in the epithelium of the gastrointestinal tract or in the pancreas.

CL:0000165.name: neuroendocrine cell
CL:0000165.def: A neuron that is capable of some hormone secretion in response to neuronal signals.

CL:0000166.name: chromaffin cell
CL:0000166.def: A cell that stores epinephrine secretory vesicles. During times of stress, the nervous system signals the vesicles to secrete their hormonal content. Their name derives from their ability to stain a brownish color with chromic salts. Characteristically, they are located in the adrenal medulla and paraganglia of the sympathetic nervous system.

CL:0000167.name: peptide hormone secreting cell
CL:0000167.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some peptide hormone secretion.

CL:0000168.name: insulin secreting cell
CL:0000168.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some insulin secretion.

CL:0000169.name: type B pancreatic cell
CL:0000169.def: A cell that secretes insulin and is located towards the center of the islets of Langerhans.

CL:0000171.name: pancreatic A cell
CL:0000171.def: A type A enteroendocrine cell found in the periphery of the islets of Langerhans that secretes glucagon.
synonym: alpha cell of islet of Langerhans

CL:0000172.name: somatostatin secreting cell
CL:0000172.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some somatostatin secretion.

CL:0000173.name: pancreatic D cell
CL:0000173.def: A D cell located in the pancreas. Peripherally placed within the islets like type A cells; contains somatostatin.

CL:0000174.name: steroid hormone secreting cell
CL:0000174.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some steroid hormone secretion.

CL:0000175.name: luteal cell
CL:0000175.def: A progesterone secreting cell in the corpus luteum. The large luteal cells develop from the granulosa cells. The small luteal cells develop from the theca cells.

CL:0000176.name: ecdysteroid secreting cell
CL:0000176.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some ecdysteroid secretion.

CL:0000177.name: testosterone secreting cell
CL:0000177.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some testosterone secretion.

CL:0000178.name: Leydig cell
CL:0000178.def: A Leydig cell is a testosterone-secreting cell in the interstitial area, between the seminiferous tubules, in the testis.

CL:0000179.name: progesterone secreting cell
CL:0000179.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some progesterone secretion.

CL:0000180.name: estradiol secreting cell
CL:0000180.def: A steroid hormone secreting cell that secretes estradiol.

CL:0000181.name: obsolete metabolising cell
CL:0000181.def: A cell whose primary function is intermediary metabolism.

CL:0000182.name: hepatocyte
CL:0000182.def: The main structural component of the liver. They are specialized epithelial cells that are organized into interconnected plates called lobules. Majority of cell population of liver, polygonal in shape, arranged in plates or trabeculae between sinusoids; may have single nucleus or binucleated.

CL:0000183.name: contractile cell
CL:0000183.def: A cell whose primary function is to shorten.

CL:0000185.name: myoepithelial cell
CL:0000185.def: Contractile cells resembling smooth muscle cells that are present in glands, notably the mammary gland, and aid in secretion. This cell has long weaving dendritic processes containing myofilament.

CL:0000186.name: myofibroblast cell
CL:0000186.def: An animal cell that has characteristics of both a fibroblast cell and a smooth muscle cell.

CL:0000187.name: muscle cell
CL:0000187.def: A mature contractile cell, commonly known as a myocyte. This cell has as part of its cytoplasm myofibrils organized in various patterns.

CL:0000188.name: cell of skeletal muscle
CL:0000188.def: A somatic cell located in skeletal muscle.

CL:0000189.name: slow muscle cell
CL:0000189.def: A muscle cell that develops tension more slowly than a fast-twitch fiber.

CL:0000190.name: fast muscle cell
CL:0000190.def: A muscle cell that can develop high tension rapidly. It is usually innervated by a single alpha neuron.

CL:0000192.name: smooth muscle cell
CL:0000192.def: A non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. They develop from specialized myoblasts (smooth muscle myoblast).

CL:0000193.name: cardiac muscle cell (sensu Arthopoda)
CL:0000193.def: A striated muscle cell of an arthropod heart that participates in heart contraction.

CL:0000196.name: insect flight muscle cell
CL:0000196.def: A muscle cell that is involved in the mechanism of insect flight. This encompasses both, cells that power flight and cells that control flight.

CL:0000197.name: sensory receptor cell
CL:0000197.def: A cell that is capable of detection of a stimulus involved in sensory perception.

CL:0000198.name: pain receptor cell
CL:0000198.def: The peripheral receptor for pain. Includes receptors which are sensitive to painful mechanical stimuli, extreme heat or cold, and chemical stimuli. All mammalian nociceptors are free nerve endings.

CL:0000199.name: mechanoreceptor cell
CL:0000199.def: A cell specialized to transduce mechanical stimuli and relay that information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000200.name: touch receptor cell
CL:0000200.def: Any neuron that is capable of some detection of mechanical stimulus involved in sensory perception of touch.

CL:0000202.name: auditory hair cell
CL:0000202.def: A mechanoreceptor cell of the auditory or vestibular system that is sensitive to auditory stimuli. The accessory sensory structures are arranged so that appropriate stimuli cause movement of the hair-like projections (stereocilia and kinocilia) which relay the information centrally in the nervous system.

CL:0000203.name: gravity sensitive cell
CL:0000203.def: Any neuronal receptor cell that is capable of some detection of mechanical stimulus involved in sensory perception of gravity.

CL:0000205.name: thermoreceptor cell
CL:0000205.def: A cellular receptor which mediates the sense of temperature. Thermoreceptor cells in vertebrates are mostly located under the skin. In mammals there are separate types of thermoreceptors for cold and for warmth and pain receptor cells which detect cold or heat extreme enough to cause pain.

CL:0000206.name: chemoreceptor cell
CL:0000206.def: A cell specialized to detect chemical substances and relay that information centrally in the nervous system. Chemoreceptors may monitor external stimuli, as in taste and olfaction, or internal stimuli, such as the concentrations of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the blood.

CL:0000207.name: olfactory receptor cell
CL:0000207.def: Any neuron that is capable of some detection of chemical stimulus involved in sensory perception of smell.

CL:0000209.name: taste receptor cell
CL:0000209.def: A specialized cell involved in gustatory sensory perception.

CL:0000210.name: photoreceptor cell
CL:0000210.def: A cell specialized in detecting light stimuli that are involved in visual perception.

CL:0000211.name: electrically active cell
CL:0000211.def: A cell whose function is determined by the generation or the reception of an electric signal.

CL:0000212.name: obsolete absorptive cell
CL:0000212.def: OBSOLETE. A cell that takes up and metabolizes substances.

CL:0000213.name: obsolete lining cell
CL:0000213.def: OBSOLETE. A cell within an epithelial cell sheet whose main function is to act as an internal or external covering for a tissue or an organism.

CL:0000214.name: synovial cell
CL:0000214.def: A cell located in the synovial joint.

CL:0000215.name: obsolete barrier cell
CL:0000215.def: OBSOLETE. A cell whose primary function is to prevent the transport of stuff across compartments.

CL:0000216.name: Sertoli cell
CL:0000216.def: A supporting cell projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules. They surround and nourish the developing male germ cells and secrete androgen binding protein. Their tight junctions with the spermatogonia and spermatocytes provide a blood-testis barrier.

CL:0000218.name: myelinating Schwann cell
CL:0000218.def: A neuroglial cell of the peripheral nervous system which forms the insulating myelin sheaths of peripheral axons.

CL:0000219.name: motile cell
CL:0000219.def: A cell that moves by its own activities.

CL:0000221.name: ectodermal cell
CL:0000221.def: A cell of the outer of the three germ layers of the embryo.

CL:0000222.name: mesodermal cell
CL:0000222.def: A cell of the middle germ layer of the embryo.

CL:0000223.name: endodermal cell
CL:0000223.def: A cell of the inner of the three germ layers of the embryo.

CL:0000224.name: obsolete cell by nuclear number
CL:0000224.def: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by the number of their nuclei.

CL:0000225.name: anucleate cell
CL:0000225.def: A cell that lacks a nucleus.

CL:0000226.name: single nucleate cell
CL:0000226.def: A cell with a single nucleus.

CL:0000227.name: binucleate cell
CL:0000227.def: Any cell that has characteristic some binucleate.

CL:0000228.name: multinucleate cell
CL:0000228.def: A cell with more than one nucleus.

CL:0000229.name: obsolete lymphoblast
CL:0000229.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000230.name: obsolete T lymphoblast
CL:0000230.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000231.name: obsolete B lymphoblast
CL:0000231.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000232.name: erythrocyte
CL:0000232.def: A red blood cell. In mammals, mature erythrocytes are biconcave disks containing hemoglobin whose function is to transport oxygen.

CL:0000233.name: platelet
CL:0000233.def: A non-nucleated disk-shaped cell formed by extrusion from megakaryocytes, found in the blood of all mammals, and mainly involved in blood coagulation.

CL:0000234.name: phagocyte
CL:0000234.def: Any cell capable of ingesting particulate matter via phagocytosis.

CL:0000235.name: macrophage
CL:0000235.def: A mononuclear phagocyte present in variety of tissues, typically differentiated from monocytes, capable of phagocytosing a variety of extracellular particulate material, including immune complexes, microorganisms, and dead cells.

CL:0000236.name: B cell
CL:0000236.def: A lymphocyte of B lineage that is capable of B cell mediated immunity.

CL:0000239.name: brush border epithelial cell
CL:0000239.def: An epithelial cell characterized by the presence of a brush border on its apical surface, which increases the surface area for absorption.

CL:0000240.name: stratified squamous epithelial cell
CL:0000240.def: A stratified epithelial cell that is part of squamous epithelium, characterized by multiple layers of cells. The basal layer is directly attached to the basement membrane and the apical layer consists of flattened squamous cells. This provides a protective barrier, commonly found in areas subject to abrasion, such as the skin, oral cavity, and esophagus.

CL:0000241.name: stratified cuboidal epithelial cell
CL:0000241.def: A stratified epithelial cell that is part of cuboidal epithelium, characterized by multiple layers of cuboidal cells forming the apical layer. This provides a protective lining for ducts in large glands, such as sweat glands.

CL:0000242.name: Merkel cell
CL:0000242.def: A modified epidermal cell located in the stratum basale. They are found mostly in areas where sensory perception is acute. Merkel cells are closely associated with an expanded terminal bulb of an afferent myelinated nerve fiber.

CL:0000243.name: obsolete glial cell (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000243.def: A non-neuronal cell of the nervous system. They not only provide physical support, but also respond to injury, regulate the ionic and chemical composition of the extracellular milieu. Form the myelin insulation of nervous pathways, guide neuronal migration during development, and exchange metabolites with neurons. Neuroglia have high-affinity transmitter uptake systems, voltage-dependent and transmitter-gated ion channels, and can release transmitters, but their role in signaling (as in many other functions) is unclear.

CL:0000244.name: transitional epithelial cell
CL:0000244.def: A cell characteristically found lining hollow organs that are subject to great mechanical change due to contraction and distention; originally thought to represent a transition between stratified squamous and columnar epithelium.

CL:0000245.name: obsolete passage cell
CL:0000245.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000353 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell in exodermis or endodermis that remains thin walled when the associated cells develop thick secondary walls. Has casparian strip in endodermis.

CL:0000247.name: Rohon-Beard neuron
CL:0000247.def: Type of neuron that is a primary mechanosensory cell, with peripheral neurites innervating the skin with free nerve endings.

CL:0000248.name: obsolete microsporocyte
CL:0000248.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020047 from Plant Ontology instead. A diploid (2n) cell that undergoes meiosis and forms four haploid (1n) microspores; also called microspore mother cell and, in seed plants, pollen mother cell.

CL:0000250.name: obsolete megaspore
CL:0000250.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020019 from Plant Ontology instead. A haploid (1n) spore developing into a female gametophyte in heterosporous plants.

CL:0000252.name: obsolete microspore
CL:0000252.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020048 from Plant Ontology instead. A haploid (1n) spore developing into a male gametophyte in heterosporous plants; the uninucleate pollen grain in seed plants.

CL:0000254.name: obsolete egg cell
CL:0000254.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020094 from Plant Ontology instead. The female gamete of plants.

CL:0000255.name: eukaryotic cell
CL:0000255.def: Any cell that in taxon some Eukaryota.

CL:0000257.name: Eumycetozoan cell
CL:0000257.def: Any cell that in taxon some Eumycetozoa.

CL:0000258.name: obsolete fiber tracheid
CL:0000258.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000355 from Plant Ontology instead. A fiber like tracheid in the secondary xylem; commonly thick walled, with pointed ends and bordered pits that have lenticular to slit like apertures.

CL:0000260.name: obsolete mucilage cell
CL:0000260.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000373 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell containing mucilages or gums or similar carbohydrate material characterized by the property of swelling in water.

CL:0000262.name: obsolete guard mother cell
CL:0000262.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000351 from Plant Ontology instead. An epidermal cell that divides to produce the guard cells.

CL:0000264.name: obsolete phloem initial
CL:0000264.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000400 from Plant Ontology instead. A cambial cell on the phloem side of the cambial zone that is the source of one or more cells arising by periclinal divisions and differentiating into phloem elements with or without additional divisions in various planes.

CL:0000266.name: obsolete meristemoid
CL:0000266.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0004011 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell constituting an active locus of meristematic activity in a tissue composed of somewhat older, differentiating cells.

CL:0000268.name: obsolete sieve element
CL:0000268.def: Obsolete. Consult Plant Ontology instead. The cell in the phloem tissue concerned with mainly longitudinal conduction of food materials. Classified into sieve cell and sieve tube member.

CL:0000270.name: obsolete subsidiary cell
CL:0000270.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000284 from Plant Ontology instead. An epidermal cell associated with a stoma and at least morphologically distinguishable from the epidermal cells composing the groundmass of the tissue.

CL:0000272.name: obsolete cambial initial
CL:0000272.def: OBSOLETE, use term from Plant Ontology. A cell localized in the vascular cambium or phellogen. Its periclinal division can contribute cells either to the outside or to the inside of the axis; in vascular cambium, classified into fusiform initials (source of axial cells of xylem and phloem) and ray initials (source of the ray cells).

CL:0000276.name: obsolete sclerenchyma cell
CL:0000276.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000077 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell variable in form and size, being more or less thick, often lignified, secondary walls. Belongs to the category of subcells and may or may not be devoid of protoplast at maturity.

CL:0000277.name: obsolete prestalk I cell
CL:0000277.def: OBSOLETE: Initial population of prestalk cells that activate the ecmA promoter at the mound stage and that presumably further differentiate into pstA and pstO cells.

CL:0000278.name: obsolete central cell
CL:0000278.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020090 from Plant Ontology instead. OBSOLETED, use term from Plant Ontology. A cell containing the two polar nuclei which, after double fertilization, will develop into the endosperm.

CL:0000280.name: obsolete generative cell
