CL:0000280.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020097 from Plant Ontology instead. The cell that will give rise to the generative nuclei which will participate in fertilization.

CL:0000282.name: obsolete trichome
CL:0000282.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000282 from Plant Ontology instead. An outgrowth from the epidermis. Trichomes vary in size and complexity and include hairs, scales, and other structures and may be glandular. In Arabidopsis, patterning of trichome development is not random but does not appear to be lineage-based like stomata.

CL:0000284.name: obsolete companion cell
CL:0000284.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000071 from Plant Ontology instead. A specialized parenchyma cell associated with a sieve-tube member in angiosperm phloem and arising from the same mother cell as the sieve-tube member.

CL:0000286.name: hyphal cell
CL:0000286.def: A cell of a filament of a fungal mycelium.

CL:0000287.name: eye photoreceptor cell
CL:0000287.def: Any photoreceptor cell that is part of some eye.

CL:0000288.name: obsolete synergid
CL:0000288.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000191 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell in the micropylar end of the embryo sac associated with the egg in the egg apparatus of angiosperms. Plays a vital role in fertilization.

CL:0000290.name: obsolete xylem fiber cell
CL:0000290.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000274 from Plant Ontology instead. A fiber of the xylem tissue, Two types are recognized in the secondary xylem: fiber tracheids and libriform fibers.

CL:0000292.name: obsolete guard cell
CL:0000292.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000293 from Plant Ontology instead. One of a pair of cells flanking the stomatal pore and causing the opening and closing of the pore by changes in turgor.

CL:0000293.name: structural cell
CL:0000293.def: A cell whose primary function is to provide structural support, to provide strength and physical integrity to the organism.

CL:0000294.name: obsolete sieve cell
CL:0000294.def: Obsolete. Consult Plant Ontology instead. A type of sieve element that has relatively undifferentiated sieve areas (with narrow pores), rather uniform in structure on all walls; that is, there are no sieve plates. Typical of gymnosperms and lower vascular plants.

CL:0000295.name: somatotropin secreting cell
CL:0000295.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that produces growth hormone, somatotropin.

CL:0000296.name: obsolete vegetative cell
CL:0000296.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020099 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell type formed after the first mitotic division of the microgametophye, The nucleus of this cell migrates to the tip of the pollen tube after germination and disintegrates when the pollen tube penetrates the nucellus.

CL:0000297.name: obsolete socket cell
CL:0000297.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000115 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell that surrounds a trichome and provides support for the trichome.

CL:0000298.name: obsolete xylem element
CL:0000298.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000273 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell composing the xylem.

CL:0000299.name: obsolete trichoblast
CL:0000299.def: OBSOLETED. Commonly used for a cell in root epidermis that gives rise to a root hair. The daughter cell produced by the asymmetric division of a root epidermal cell that gives rise to a root hair.

CL:0000300.name: gamete
CL:0000300.def: A mature sexual reproductive cell having a single set of unpaired chromosomes.

CL:0000301.name: pole cell
CL:0000301.def: A primordial germ cell of insects. Such cells form at the posterior pole of the early embryo.

CL:0000302.name: obsolete IgM B cell
CL:0000302.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000303.name: obsolete IgG B cell
CL:0000303.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000304.name: obsolete IgA B cell
CL:0000304.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000305.name: obsolete IgE B cell
CL:0000305.def: OBSOLETE (was not defined before being made obsolete).

CL:0000307.name: tracheal epithelial cell
CL:0000307.def: An epithelial cell found in the trachea.

CL:0000312.name: keratinocyte
CL:0000312.def: An epidermal cell which synthesizes keratin and undergoes a characteristic change as it moves upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin. Successive stages of differentiation of the keratinocytes forming the epidermal layers are basal cell, spinous or prickle cell, and the granular cell.

CL:0000313.name: serous secreting cell
CL:0000313.def: Columnar glandular cell with irregular nucleus, copious granular endoplasmic reticulum and supranuclear granules. Secretes a watery fluid containing proteins known as serous fluid.

CL:0000315.name: tear secreting cell
CL:0000315.def: A cell secreting tears, the fluid secreted by the lacrimal glands. This fluid moistens the conjunctiva and cornea.

CL:0000316.name: obsolete ray initial
CL:0000316.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000082 from Plant Ontology instead. A meristemic ray cell in the vascular cambium that gives rise to ray cells of the secondary xylem and secondary phloem.

CL:0000317.name: sebocyte
CL:0000317.def: An epithelial cell that is part of a sebaceous gland. This cell produces and secretes sebum, an oily, lipid-rich substance, through holocrine secretion where the entire cell ruptures to release its contents.

CL:0000318.name: sweat secreting cell
CL:0000318.def: A cell secreting sweat, the fluid excreted by the sweat glands of mammals. It consists of water containing sodium chloride, phosphate, urea, ammonia, and other waste products.

CL:0000319.name: mucus secreting cell
CL:0000319.def: Any cell that is capable of some mucus secretion.

CL:0000320.name: obsolete megasporocyte
CL:0000320.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000431 from Plant Ontology instead. A diploid (2n) cell that undergoes meiosis and produces four haploid (1n) megaspores; also called megaspore mother cell.

CL:0000322.name: pulmonary alveolar epithelial cell
CL:0000322.def: An epithelial cell that lines the peripheral gas exchange region of the lungs of air-breathing vertebrates.
synonym: epithelial cell of alveolus of lung

CL:0000325.name: stuff accumulating cell
CL:0000325.def: A cell that is specialised to accumulate a particular substance(s).

CL:0000329.name: oxygen accumulating cell
CL:0000329.def: Any cell that is capable of some oxygen transport.

CL:0000330.name: obsolete collenchymal cell
CL:0000330.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000075 from Plant Ontology instead. An elongated living cell with unevenly thickened nonlignified primary walls.

CL:0000331.name: obsolete tracheid
CL:0000331.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000301 from Plant Ontology instead. A tracheary element of the xylem that has no perforations, as contrasted with a vessel member. May occur in primary and in secondary xylem. May have any kind of secondary wall thickening found in tracheary elements.

CL:0000332.name: obsolete atrichoblast
CL:0000332.def: OBSOLETE, use term from Plant Ontology. A cell formed after asymmetric division of root epidermal cell that does not give rise to a root hair.

CL:0000333.name: migratory neural crest cell
CL:0000333.def: A cell derived from the specialized ectoderm flanking each side of the embryonic neural plate, which after the closure of the neural tube, forms masses of cells that migrate out from the dorsal aspect of the neural tube to spread throughout the body.

CL:0000335.name: mesenchyme condensation cell
CL:0000335.def: A mesenchymal cell in embryonic development found in a contracting mass and that gives rise to osteoprogenitors.

CL:0000336.name: adrenal medulla chromaffin cell
CL:0000336.def: A cell found within the adrenal medulla that secrete biogenic amine hormones upon stimulation.
CL:0000336.synonym: medullary chromaffin cell of adrenal gland

CL:0000338.name: neuroblast (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
CL:0000338.def: A neural precursor of the central nervous system.

CL:0000339.name: glioblast (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000339.def: An early neural cell developing from the early ependymal cell of the neural tube.

CL:0000340.name: glioblast (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
CL:0000340.def: A precursor of the central nervous system that gives rise to glial cells only.

CL:0000342.name: pigment cell (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000342.def: Any animal cell containing pigment granules.

CL:0000343.name: visual pigment cell (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000343.def: A pigment cell that is capable of detecting light stimulus that is involved in visual perception.

CL:0000345.name: dental papilla cell
CL:0000345.def: A mesenchymal cell that is part of a small mass of condensed mesenchyme in the enamel organ; it differentiates into the dentin and dental pulp.

CL:0000346.name: hair follicle dermal papilla cell
CL:0000346.def: A specialized mesenchymal cell that resides in the dermal papilla located at the bottom of hair follicles. This cell plays a pivotal roles in hair formation, growth, and cycling.

CL:0000347.name: scleral cell
CL:0000347.def: A cell of the sclera of the eye.

CL:0000348.name: choroidal cell of the eye
CL:0000348.def: A structural cell that is part of optic choroid.

CL:0000349.name: extraembryonic cell
CL:0000349.def: Any cell that is part of some extraembryonic structure.

CL:0000350.name: amnioserosal cell
CL:0000350.def: Any extraembryonic cell that is part of some amnioserosa.

CL:0000351.name: trophoblast cell
CL:0000351.def: An extraembryonic cell that develops from a trophectodermal cell. This cell is found in the outer layer of the blastocyst and can invade other structures in the uterus once the blastocyst implants into the uterine wall. A trophoblast cell is involved in the implantation of the embryo into the uterine wall, placental formation, remodelling of maternal vasculature in the uterus, nutrient and gas exchange, hormone production, and immune modulation to support fetal development.

CL:0000352.name: epiblast cell
CL:0000352.def: A cell of the outer layer of a blastula that gives rise to the ectoderm after gastrulation.

CL:0000353.name: blastoderm cell
CL:0000353.def: An undifferentiated cell produced by early cleavages of the fertilized egg (zygote).

CL:0000355.name: multi-potent skeletal muscle stem cell
CL:0000355.def: A multifate stem cell found in skeletal muscle than can differentiate into many different cell types, including muscle. Distinct cell type from satellite cell.

CL:0000358.name: sphincter associated smooth muscle cell
CL:0000358.def: A smooth muscle cell that is part of a sphincter. A sphincter is a typically circular muscle that normally maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice and which relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning.

CL:0000359.name: vascular associated smooth muscle cell
CL:0000359.def: A smooth muscle cell associated with the vasculature.

CL:0000360.name: morula cell
CL:0000360.def: A cell of the early embryo at the developmental stage in which the blastomeres, resulting from repeated mitotic divisions of the fertilized ovum (zygote), form a compact cell mass.

CL:0000361.name: gastrula cell
CL:0000361.def: A cell of the embryo in the early stage following the blastula, characterized by morphogenetic cell movements, cell differentiation, and the formation of the three germ layers.

CL:0000362.name: epidermal cell
CL:0000362.def: An epithelial cell of the integument (the outer layer of an organism).

CL:0000363.name: obsolete axial cell
CL:0000363.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000081 from Plant Ontology instead. OBSOLETE, use term from the Plant Ontology. A secondary vascular cell that develops from the fusiform cambial initials and oriented with their longest diameter parallel with the main axis of stem or root. These cells make up the axial system, also known as vertical or longitudinal system.

CL:0000364.name: obsolete ray cell
CL:0000364.def: Obsolete. Consult Plant Ontology. A cell that develops from the ray initial and composes all rays (panels of tissue variable in height and width, formed by the ray initials in the vascular cambium and extending radially in the secondary xylem and secondary phloem) in the secondary vascular tissues.

CL:0000365.name: animal zygote
CL:0000365.def: Diploid cell produced by the fusion of sperm cell nucleus and egg cell.

CL:0000366.name: obsolete sperm cell (sensu Viridiplantae)
CL:0000366.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000084 from Plant Ontology instead. Male gamete, part of male germ unit.

CL:0000368.name: obsolete myrosin cell
CL:0000368.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000352 from Plant Ontology instead. Cell containing glucosinolates ('mustard oil glucosides') and myrosinases, enzymes hydrolyzing the glucosinolates. Occurs in eleven dicotyledon families, the two largest of which are the Brassicaceae and Euphorbiaceae.

CL:0000370.name: obsolete transfer cell
CL:0000370.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000078 from Plant Ontology instead. Parenchyma cell with the wall ingrowth (or invaginations) that increase the surface of the plasmalemma. Appears to be specialized for short-distance transfer of solutes.

CL:0000371.name: protoplast
CL:0000371.def: The cell protoplasm after removal of the cell wall.

CL:0000372.name: tormogen cell
CL:0000372.def: An epidermal cell that is part of a cell cluster organ of the insect integument (such as a sensillum) and that secretes a cuticular specialization that forms a socket around the base of a cuticular specialization produced by a trichogen cell.

CL:0000373.name: histoblast
CL:0000373.def: A progenitor cell found in the larval epidermis of insects and that gives rise to the adult abdominal epidermis.

CL:0000374.name: trichogen cell
CL:0000374.def: An epidermal cell that is part of a cell cluster organ of the insect integument (such as a sensillum) and that secretes a cuticular specialization, often in the form of a hair, bristle, peg or scale. The base of this specialization is often surrounded by a socket produced by a closely associated tormogen cell.

CL:0000380.name: thecogen cell
CL:0000380.def: The support cell that makes the thecogen dendritic cap - a cuticle-like matrix around the tip of the eo-dendrite and which encloses the soma of the eo-neuron.

CL:0000382.name: scolopale cell
CL:0000382.def: A cell that is part of a scolopidium and surrounds the dendrite of a scolopidial neuron.

CL:0000387.name: hemocyte (sensu Arthropoda)
CL:0000387.def: A blood cell of the circulatory system of arthropods.

CL:0000388.name: tendon cell
CL:0000388.def: An elongated fibrocyte that is part of a tendon. The cytoplasm is stretched between the collagen fibres of the tendon. They have a central cell nucleus with a prominent nucleolus. Tendon cells have a well-developed rough endoplasmic reticulum and they are responsible for synthesis and turnover of tendon fibres and ground substance.

CL:0000392.name: crystal cell
CL:0000392.def: A hemocyte that synthesizes and secretes melanins as part of the antimicrobial immune response. It is characterized morphologically by crystal inclusions of phenoloxidases in its cytoplasm, hence its name.

CL:0000393.name: electrically responsive cell
CL:0000393.def: A cell whose function is determined by its response to an electric signal.

CL:0000394.name: plasmatocyte
CL:0000394.def: A phagocytic hemocyte, responsible for the engulfment of small particles, microbes, and apoptotic tissue debris. It may also secretes antimicrobial peptides and contribute to the production and secretion of proteins of the hemolymph.

CL:0000395.name: procrystal cell
CL:0000395.def: A precursor of mature crystal cells.

CL:0000396.name: lamellocyte
CL:0000396.def: A hemocyte found in immuno-stimulated larvae.

CL:0000397.name: ganglion interneuron
CL:0000397.def: Any interneuron that has its soma located in some ganglion.

CL:0000399.name: obsolete phloem element
CL:0000399.def: Obsolete. Consult Plant Ontology instead. OBSOLETED, not defined prior to obsoletion.

CL:0000400.name: obsolete pavement cell
CL:0000400.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000332 from Plant Ontology instead. An epidermal cell with a characteristic convoluted anticlinal cell wall that gives a jigsaw like appearance to the lamina.

CL:0000402.name: obsolete CNS interneuron
CL:0000402.def: OBSOLETE. An interneuron that has its cell body in a central nervous system.

CL:0000404.name: electrically signaling cell
CL:0000404.def: A cell that initiates an electrical signal and passes that signal to another cell.

CL:0000407.name: scolopidial ligament cell
CL:0000407.def: A cell that anchors the cell body of a scolopidial neuron to the integument.

CL:0000408.name: male gamete
CL:0000408.def: Any male germ cell that has characteristic some haploid and is capable of some fertilization.

CL:0000411.name: Caenorhabditis hypodermal cell
CL:0000411.def: An epithelial cell of the hypodermis of Caenorhabditis.

CL:0000412.name: polyploid cell
CL:0000412.def: A cell that contains more than two haploid sets of chromosomes.

CL:0000413.name: haploid cell
CL:0000413.def: A cell whose nucleus contains a single haploid genome.

CL:0000414.name: obsolete cell by ploidy
CL:0000414.def: OBSOLETE: A classification of cells by the number of haploid genome equivalents of their nucleus or nuclei.

CL:0000415.name: diploid cell
CL:0000415.def: A cell whose nucleus has two haploid genomes.

CL:0000418.name: arcade cell
CL:0000418.def: An epithelial cell found in C. elegans that firmly hold the outer body wall and the lips to the inner cylinder of the pharynx in a manner that keeps these organs from breaking apart, while still giving each organ freedom of movement during feeding.

CL:0000419.name: seam cell
CL:0000419.def: An epithelial fate stem cell found in flatworms.

CL:0000420.name: syncytial epithelial cell
CL:0000420.def: An epithelial cell that forms a syncytium, which is a multinucleated cell resulting from the fusion of multiple cells.

CL:0000421.name: coelomocyte
CL:0000421.def: A free floating cell, including amebocytes and eleocytes, in the coelom of certain animals, especially annelids.

CL:0000422.name: mitogenic signaling cell
CL:0000422.def: A cell whose primary function is to cause growth by stimulating cell division in its immediate cellular environment.

CL:0000424.name: excretory cell
CL:0000424.def: A cell involved in the elimination of metabolic and foreign toxins, and in maintaining the ionic, acid-base and water balance of biological fluids.

CL:0000425.name: pore cell
CL:0000425.def: Forms the terminal part of the cuticle-lined excretory duct of C. elegans.

CL:0000427.name: GLR cell
CL:0000427.def: A scaffolding cell type found in C. elegans, this cell plays a supportive role to the muscle arms. May also have an endocrine role.

CL:0000429.name: imaginal disc cell
CL:0000429.def: A columnar epithelial cell that is part of an insect imaginal disc.

CL:0000430.name: xanthophore cell
CL:0000430.def: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains cartenoid pigments in structures called pterinosomes or xanthosomes. This gives an appearance ranging from a golden yellow to orange and red.

CL:0000431.name: iridophore
CL:0000431.def: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. The cell contains flat light-reflecting platelets, probably of guanine, in stacks called reflecting platelets or iridisomes. The color-generating components produce a silver, gold, or iridescent color.

CL:0000432.name: reticular cell
CL:0000432.def: A fibroblast that synthesizes collagen and uses it to produce reticular fibers, thus providing structural support. Reticular cells are found in many organs, including the spleen, lymph nodes and kidneys. Subtypes of reticular cells include epithelial, mesenchymal, and fibroblastic reticular cells. Fibroblastic reticular cells are involved in directing B cells and T cells to specific regions within a tissue, whereas epithelial and mesenchymal reticular cells are associated with certain areas of the brain.

CL:0000433.name: obsolete functional megaspore
CL:0000433.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000244 from Plant Ontology instead. In monosporic and bisporic megasporogenesis: the megaspore(s) that will undergo megagametogenesis.

CL:0000434.name: eccrine cell
CL:0000434.def: A secretory cell that discharges its product without loss of cytoplasm.

CL:0000437.name: gonadtroph
CL:0000437.def: A rounded cell that is usually situated next to sinusoids; secretes follicular stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

CL:0000438.name: luteinizing hormone secreting cell
CL:0000438.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell pituitary that produces luteinizing hormone.

CL:0000439.name: prolactin secreting cell
CL:0000439.def: A peptide hormone cell that secretes prolactin.

CL:0000440.name: melanocyte stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000440.def: A cell of the intermediate pituitary that produces melanocyte stimulating hormone.

CL:0000441.name: follicle stem cell (sensu Arthropoda)
CL:0000441.def: A stem cell that gives rise to the follicle cells that surround the oocyte in female arthropods.

CL:0000442.name: follicular dendritic cell
CL:0000442.def: A cell with extensive dendritic processes found in the B cell areas (primary follicles and germinal centers) of lymphoid tissue. They are unrelated to the dendritic cell associated with T cells. Follicular dendritic cells have Fc receptors and C3b receptors, but unlike other dendritic cells, they do not process or present antigen in a way that allows recognition by T cells. Instead, they hold antigen in the form of immune complexes on their surfaces for long periods and can present antigen to B cells during an immune response.

CL:0000443.name: calcitonin secreting cell
CL:0000443.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some calcitonin secretion.

CL:0000444.name: obliquely striated muscle cell
CL:0000444.def: A muscle cell in which the fibers are organised into sarcomeres but in which adjacent myofibrils are offset from each other, producing an oblique banding pattern.

CL:0000446.name: chief cell of parathyroid gland
CL:0000446.def: An epithelial cell of the parathyroid gland that is arranged in wide, irregular interconnecting columns; responsible for the synthesis and secretion of parathyroid hormone.

CL:0000448.name: white adipocyte
CL:0000448.def: An adipocyte with light coloration and few mitochondria. It contains a scant ring of cytoplasm surrounding a single large lipid droplet or vacuole.

CL:0000449.name: brown adipocyte
CL:0000449.def: A cell from the thermogenic form of adipose tissue found in many species,  particularly in newborns and hibernating mammals, but also in lesser amounts in adults of other mammals including humans. Brown fat is capable of rapid liberation of energy and seems to be important in the maintenance of body temperature immediately after birth and upon waking from hibernation.

CL:0000451.name: dendritic cell
CL:0000451.def: A cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation. These cells are lineage negative (CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD34-negative, and CD56-negative).

CL:0000453.name: Langerhans cell
CL:0000453.def: Langerhans cell is a conventional dendritic cell that has plasma membrane part CD207. A Langerhans cell is a stellate dendritic cell of myeloid origin, that appears clear on light microscopy and has a dark-staining, indented nucleus and characteristic inclusions (Birbeck granules) in the cytoplasm; Langerhans cells are found principally in the stratum spinosum of the epidermis, but they also occur in other stratified epithelia and have been identified in the lung, lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus.

CL:0000454.name: epinephrine secreting cell
CL:0000454.def: A cell capable of producing epinephrine. Epiniphrine is synthesized from norepiniphrine by the actions of the phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase enzyme, which is expressed in the adrenal glands, androgenic neurons, and in other cell types.

CL:0000455.name: obsolete starch sheath cell
CL:0000455.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0004531 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell characterized by conspicuous and rather stable accumulation of starch.

CL:0000456.name: mineralocorticoid secreting cell
CL:0000456.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some mineralocorticoid secretion.

CL:0000459.name: noradrenergic cell
CL:0000459.def: A cell capable of producting norepiniphrine. Norepiniphrine is a catecholamine with multiple roles including as a hormone and a neurotransmitter. In addition, epiniphrine is synthesized from norepiniphrine by the actions of the phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase enzyme.

CL:0000460.name: glucocorticoid secreting cell
CL:0000460.def: Any secretory cell that is capable of some glucocorticoid secretion.

CL:0000462.name: adepithelial cell
CL:0000462.def: A cell of mesodermal origin that is closely associated with the epithelium of an imaginal disc. It is a precursor of some of the insect's adult muscles.

CL:0000463.name: epidermal cell (sensu Arthropoda)
CL:0000463.def: An epidermal cell that secretes chitinous cuticle from its apical side.

CL:0000464.name: epidermoblast
CL:0000464.def: An epidermal progenitor cell that arises from neuroectoderm and in turn gives rise to the epidermal sheath of ventral and cephalic regions.

CL:0000465.name: cardioblast (sensu Arthropoda)
CL:0000465.def: A precursor of the cells that form the dorsal vessel of arthropods.

CL:0000467.name: adrenocorticotropic hormone secreting cell
CL:0000467.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that produces adrenocorticotropin, or corticotropin.

CL:0000468.name: neuroglioblast (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
CL:0000468.def: A precursor of the central nervous system that gives rise to both neurons and glial cells.

CL:0000469.name: ganglion mother cell
CL:0000469.def: A neural progenitor cell that is the daughter of a neuroblast (sensu arthopoda).  The progeny of ganglion mother cells develop into neurons, glia and (occasionally) epithelial cells.

CL:0000472.name: obsolete chlorenchyma cell
CL:0000472.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000076 from Plant Ontology instead. OBSOLETE, use term from Plant Ontology. Parenchyma cells containing chloroplasts; a component of leaf mesophyll and other green parenchyma tissue.

CL:0000473.name: OBSOLETE defensive cell
CL:0000473.def: OBSOLETE: A cell whose primary function is to protect the organism.

CL:0000474.name: pericardial nephrocyte
CL:0000474.def: An insect renal cell that filters hemolymph and is found with other pericardial nephrocytes in two rows flanking the dorsal vessel.

CL:0000475.name: obsolete degenerate megaspore
CL:0000475.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000245 from Plant Ontology instead. In monosporic and bisporic megasporogenesis: the megaspore(s) that do not participate in megagametogenesis.

CL:0000476.name: thyrotroph
CL:0000476.def: A basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces thyroid stimulating hormone, thyrotrophin. This cell type is elongated, polygonal and lie in clusters towards the adenohypophyseal center.

CL:0000477.name: follicle cell of egg chamber
CL:0000477.def: A somatic epithelial cell of the insect egg chamber.

CL:0000478.name: oxytocin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000478.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes oxytocin stimulating hormone

CL:0000479.name: vasopressin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000479.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes vasopressin stimulating hormone

CL:0000480.name: secretin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000480.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes secretin stimulating hormone

CL:0000481.name: cholecystokin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000481.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes cholecystokin stimulating hormone.

CL:0000482.name: juvenile hormone secreting cell
CL:0000482.def: An endocrine cell that secretes juvenile hormone.

CL:0000483.name: bombesin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000483.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes bombesin stimulating hormone.

CL:0000484.name: connective tissue type mast cell
CL:0000484.def: Mast cell subtype whose granules contain both the serine proteases tryptase and chymase. These cells are primarily found in connective tissue, such as the peritoneal cavity, skin, and intestinal submucosa. Their development is T-cell independent.

CL:0000485.name: mucosal type mast cell
CL:0000485.def: Mast cell subtype that contains only the serine protease trypase in its granules. These cells are primarily found in mucosal tissue, such as intestinal mucosa and alveoli. They depend upon T-cells for development of phenotype.

CL:0000486.name: garland cell
CL:0000486.def: A large binucleate cell that forms a 'garland' around the anterior end of the proventriculus (cardia) at its junction with the esophagus in both adults and larvae flies. Each cell is surrounded by a basement membrane and there are numerous micro-invaginations (lacunae) extending from the surface into the cytoplasm. At the mouth of each lacuna is a doubled filament forming a specialised filtration system (diaphragm). The filtrate is endocytosed from the lacunae.

CL:0000487.name: oenocyte
CL:0000487.def: A secretory cell of ectodermal origin. This cell may have important functions in fatty acid and hydrocarbon metabolism and is metabolically linked to the fat body and tracheae. This cell is exclusive of arthropods.

CL:0000488.name: visible light photoreceptor cell
CL:0000488.def: A photoreceptor cell that detects visible light.

CL:0000491.name: obsolete cytotoxic T cell
CL:0000491.def: OBSOLETE: A cell responsible for spontaneous cytotoxicity of a variety of tumor cells without prior immunization. These natural killer cells are found in non-immune humans and experimental animals and are thought by some to be the same as killer cells (killing by antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity), but they can also kill in the absence of antibody.

CL:0000492.name: CD4-positive helper T cell
CL:0000492.def: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that cooperates with other lymphocytes via direct contact or cytokine release to initiate a variety of immune functions.

CL:0000493.name: obsolete regulatory T cell
CL:0000493.def: OBSOLETE: Subpopulation of CD4+ cells which induce CD8+ suppressor T cells to suppress antibody production by B cells. They also stimulate other cellular immune responses.

CL:0000494.name: UV sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000494.def: A photoreceptor cell that detects ultraviolet light.

CL:0000495.name: blue sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000495.def: A photoreceptor cell that is sensitive to blue light.

CL:0000496.name: green sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000496.def: A photoreceptor cell that is sensitive to green light.

CL:0000497.name: red sensitive photoreceptor cell
CL:0000497.def: A photoreceptor cell that is sensitive to red light.

CL:0000498.name: inhibitory interneuron
CL:0000498.def: An interneuron (also called relay neuron, association neuron or local circuit neuron) is a multipolar neuron which connects afferent neurons and efferent neurons in neural pathways. Like motor neurons, interneuron cell bodies are always located in the central nervous system (CNS).

CL:0000499.name: stromal cell
CL:0000499.def: A connective tissue cell of an organ found in the loose connective tissue.

CL:0000500.name: follicular epithelial cell
CL:0000500.def: An epithelial somatic cell associated with a maturing oocyte.

CL:0000501.name: granulosa cell
CL:0000501.def: A supporting cell for the developing female gamete in the ovary of mammals. They develop from the coelomic epithelial cells of the gonadal ridge. Granulosa cells form a single layer around the mammalian oocyte in the primordial ovarian follicle and advance to form a multilayered cumulus oophorus surrounding the ovum in the Graafian follicle. The major functions of granulosa cells include the production of steroids and LH receptors.

CL:0000502.name: type D enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000502.def: A cell found throughout the gastrointestinal tract and in the pancreas. They secrete somatostatin in both an endocrine and paracrine manner. Somatostatin inhibits gastrin, cholecystokinin, insulin, glucagon, pancreatic enzymes, and gastric hydrochloric acid. A variety of substances which inhibit gastric acid secretion (vasoactive intestinal peptide, calcitonin gene-related peptide, cholecystokinin, beta-adrenergic agonists, and gastric inhibitory peptide) are thought to act by releasing somatostatin.

CL:0000503.name: theca cell
CL:0000503.def: A specialized stromal cell that forms the theca layer outside the basal lamina lining the ovarian follicle, appearing during the secondary follicle stage.

CL:0000504.name: enterochromaffin-like cell
CL:0000504.def: A enteroendocrine cell part of the glands of the gastric mucosa. They produce histamine and peptides such as chromogranins. This cell type respond to gastrin by releasing histamine which acts as a paracrine stimulator of the release of hydrochloric acid from the gastric parietal cells.

CL:0000505.name: substance P secreting cell
CL:0000505.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes substance P.

CL:0000506.name: enkephalin secreting cell
CL:0000506.def: An endorphine cell that secretes enkephalin.

CL:0000507.name: endorphin secreting cell
CL:0000507.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes endorphin.

CL:0000508.name: type G enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000508.def: An endocrine cell found in the stomach and duodenum and is responsible for the secretion of gastrin and enkephalin. Most abundant in pyloric antrum, pyramidal in form with a narrow apex bearing long microvilli.

CL:0000509.name: gastrin secreting cell
CL:0000509.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes gastrin.

CL:0000510.name: paneth cell
CL:0000510.def: An epithelial cell found in the basal part of the intestinal glands (crypts of Lieberkuhn) including the appendix. Paneth cells synthesize and secrete lysozyme and cryptdins. Numerous in the deeper parts of the intestinal crypts, particularly in the duodenum, rich in zinc, contain large acidophilic granules, with irregular apical microvilli and prominent membrane-bound vacuoles containing matrix.

CL:0000511.name: androgen binding protein secreting cell
CL:0000511.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes androgen binding protein.

CL:0000513.name: cardiac muscle myoblast
CL:0000513.def: A precursor cell destined to differentiate into cardiac muscle cell.

CL:0000514.name: smooth muscle myoblast
CL:0000514.def: A precursor cell destined to differentiate into smooth muscle myocytes.

CL:0000515.name: skeletal muscle myoblast
CL:0000515.def: A myoblast that differentiates into skeletal muscle fibers.

CL:0000516.name: perineuronal satellite cell
CL:0000516.def: A non-neuronal cell that surrounds the neuronal cell bodies of the ganglia.

CL:0000517.name: macrophage derived foam cell
CL:0000517.def: A type of foam cell derived from a macrophage containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherolosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

CL:0000518.name: phagocyte (sensu Vertebrata)
CL:0000518.def: A phagocyte in vertebrates that is able to phagocytosis.

CL:0000519.name: phagocyte (sensu Nematoda and Protostomia)
CL:0000519.def: A phagocyte from organisms in the Nematoda or Protostomia clades.

CL:0000521.name: fungal cell
CL:0000521.def: Any cell that in taxon some Fungi.

CL:0000522.name: obsolete spore
CL:0000522.def: OBSOLETE: The reproductive structure of bacteria, fungi and cryptograms.

CL:0000523.name: mononuclear cytotrophoblast cell
CL:0000523.def: A cell from the inner layer of the trophoblast of the early mammalian embryo that gives rise to the outer surface and villi of the chorion. Mononuclear crytoblasts fuse to give rise to a multinuclear cytotrophoblast.

CL:0000524.name: spheroplast
CL:0000524.def: A cell, usually of bacteria or yeast, which has partially lost its cell wall.

CL:0000525.name: syncytiotrophoblast cell
CL:0000525.def: A cell from the outer syncytial layer of the trophoblast of an early mammalian embryo, directly associated with the maternal blood supply. It secretes hCG in order to maintain progesterone secretion and sustain a pregnancy.

CL:0000526.name: afferent neuron
CL:0000526.def: A neuron which conveys sensory information centrally from the periphery.

CL:0000527.name: efferent neuron
CL:0000527.def: A neuron which sends impulses peripherally to activate muscles or secretory cells.

CL:0000528.name: nitrergic neuron
CL:0000528.def: A nerve cell where transmission is mediated by nitric oxide.

CL:0000530.name: primary neuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000530.def: A neuron that develops during the early segmentation stages in teleosts, before the neural tube is formed.

CL:0000531.name: primary sensory neuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000531.def: A primary neuron (sensu Teleostei) that has a sensory function.

CL:0000532.name: CAP motoneuron
CL:0000532.def: A primary motor neuron with its soma in the caudal region of a spinal cord. The axon of this motoneuron exit the spinal cord from one single point and innervates the lateral surface of ventral axial muscles

CL:0000533.name: primary motor neuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000533.def: A primary neuron (sensu Teleostei) that has a motor function.

CL:0000534.name: primary interneuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000534.def: A primary neuron (sensu Teleostei) that is neither a sensory neuron or a motor neuron.

CL:0000535.name: secondary neuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000535.def: A neuron of teleosts that develops later than a primary neuron, typically during the larval stages.

CL:0000536.name: secondary motor neuron (sensu Teleostei)
CL:0000536.def: A secondary neuron (sensu Teleostei) that has a motor function.

CL:0000537.name: obsolete antipodal cell
CL:0000537.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0020093 from Plant Ontology instead. OBSOLETE, use term from plant ontology. A cell located at the chalazal end of the mature embryo sac in angiosperms.

CL:0000538.name: obsolete epidermal initial
CL:0000538.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000349 from Plant Ontology instead. A relatively unspecialized cell that will give rise to specialized cell types of the epidermis.

CL:0000539.name: obsolete idioblast
CL:0000539.def: OBSOLETE: A cell in a tissue that markedly differs in form, size, or contents from other cells in the same tissue.

CL:0000540.name: neuron
CL:0000540.def: The basic cellular unit of nervous tissue. Each neuron consists of a body, an axon, and dendrites. Their purpose is to receive, conduct, and transmit impulses in the nervous system.

CL:0000541.name: melanoblast
CL:0000541.def: A cell that originates from the neural crest and differentiates into a pigment cell.

CL:0000542.name: lymphocyte
CL:0000542.def: A lymphocyte is a leukocyte commonly found in the blood and lymph that has the characteristics of a large nucleus, a neutral staining cytoplasm, and prominent heterochromatin.

CL:0000543.name: obsolete sieve tube member
CL:0000543.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000289 from Plant Ontology instead. One of the series of cellular components of a sieve tube. It shows a more or less pronounced differentiation between sieve plates (wide pores) and lateral sieve areas (narrow pores). Also sieve tube element and the obsolete sieve tube segment.

CL:0000545.name: T-helper 1 cell
CL:0000545.def: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has the phenotype T-bet-positive, CXCR3-positive, CCR6-negative, and is capable of producing interferon-gamma.

CL:0000546.name: T-helper 2 cell
CL:0000546.def: A CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has the phenotype GATA-3-positive, CXCR3-negative, CCR6-negative, and is capable of producing interleukin-4.

CL:0000547.name: proerythroblast
CL:0000547.def: An immature, nucleated erythrocyte occupying the stage of erythropoeisis that follows formation of erythroid progenitor cells. This cell is CD71-positive, has both a nucleus and a nucleolus, and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

CL:0000548.name: obsolete animal cell
CL:0000548.def: OBSOLETE. A native cell that is part of some Metazoa.

CL:0000549.name: basophilic erythroblast
CL:0000549.def: A nucleated immature erythrocyte, having cytoplasm generally similar to that of the earlier proerythroblast but sometimes even more basophilic, and usually regular in outline. The nucleus is still relatively large, but the chromatin strands are thicker and more deeply staining, giving a coarser appearance; the nucleoli have disappeared. This cell is CD71-positive and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

CL:0000550.name: polychromatophilic erythroblast
CL:0000550.def: A nucleated, immature erythrocyte in which the nucleus occupies a relatively smaller part of the cell than in its precursor, the basophilic erythroblast. The cytoplasm is beginning to acquire hemoglobin and thus is no longer a purely basophilic, but takes on acidophilic aspects, which becomes progressively more marked as the cell matures. The chromatin of the nucleus is arranged in coarse, deeply staining clumps. This cell is CD71-positive and lacks hematopoeitic lineage markers.

CL:0000552.name: orthochromatic erythroblast
CL:0000552.def: The final stage of the nucleated, immature erythrocyte, before nuclear loss. Typically the cytoplasm is described as acidophilic, but it still shows a faint polychromatic tint. The nucleus is small and initially may still have coarse, clumped chromatin, as in its precursor, the polychromatophilic erythroblast, but ultimately it becomes pyknotic, and appears as a deeply staining, blue-black, homogeneous structureless mass. The nucleus is often eccentric and sometimes lobulated.

CL:0000553.name: megakaryocyte progenitor cell
CL:0000553.def: The earliest cytologically identifiable precursor in the thrombocytic series. This cell is capable of endomitosis and lacks expression of hematopoieitic lineage markers (lin-negative).

CL:0000554.name: gastrin stimulating hormone secreting cell
CL:0000554.def: A peptide hormone secreting cell that secretes gastrin stimulating hormone.

CL:0000556.name: megakaryocyte
CL:0000556.def: A large hematopoietic cell (50 to 100 micron) with a lobated nucleus. Once mature, this cell undergoes multiple rounds of endomitosis and cytoplasmic restructuring to allow platelet formation and release.

CL:0000557.name: granulocyte monocyte progenitor cell
CL:0000557.def: A hematopoietic progenitor cell that is committed to the granulocyte and monocyte lineages. These cells are CD123-positive, and do not express Gata1 or Gata2 but do express C/EBPa, and Pu.1.
synonym: CFU-C , Colony forming unit in culture

CL:0000558.name: reticulocyte
CL:0000558.def: An immature erythrocyte that changes the protein composition of its plasma membrane by exosome formation and extrusion. The types of protein removed differ between species though removal of the transferrin receptor is apparent in mammals and birds.

CL:0000559.name: promonocyte
CL:0000559.def: A precursor in the monocytic series, being a cell intermediate in development between the monoblast and monocyte. This cell is CD11b-positive and has fine azurophil granules.

CL:0000560.name: band form neutrophil
CL:0000560.def: A late neutrophilic metamyelocyte in which the nucleus is indented to more than half the distance to the farthest nuclear margin but in no area being condensed to a single filament. The nucleus is in the form of a curved or coiled band, not having acquired the typical multilobar shape of the mature neutrophil. These cells are fMLP receptor-positive, CD11b-positive, CD35-negative, and CD49d-negative.

CL:0000561.name: amacrine cell
CL:0000561.def: Interneuron of the vertebrate retina. They integrate, modulate, and interpose a temporal domain in the visual message presented to the retinal ganglion cells, with which they synapse in the inner plexiform layer. They lack large axons.

CL:0000563.name: endospore
CL:0000563.def: A rounded, inactive form that certain bacteria assume under conditions of extreme temperature, dryness, or lack of food. The bacterium develops a waterproof cell wall that protects it from being dried out or damaged.

CL:0000564.name: neutrophilic promyelocyte
CL:0000564.def: A promyelocyte committed to the neutrophil lineage. This cell type is GATA-1-positive, C/EBPa-positive, AML-1-positive, MPO-positive, has low expression of PU.1 transcription factor and lacks lactotransferrin expression.

CL:0000565.name: fat body cell
CL:0000565.def: A cell found in fat bodies whose primary function is intermediary metabolism.

CL:0000566.name: angioblastic mesenchymal cell
CL:0000566.def: A mesenchymal stem cell capable of developing into blood vessel endothelium.

CL:0000568.name: amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation cell
CL:0000568.def: A cell that originates in the neural crest, that has certain cytochemical and ultrastructural characteristics and is found scattered throughout the body; types include melanocytes, the cells of the chromaffin system, and cells in the hypothalamus, hypophysis, thyroid, parathyroids, lungs, gastrointestinal tract, and pancreas. This cell type concentrates the amino acid precursors of certain amines and decarboxylate them, forming amines that function as regulators and neurotransmitters. This cell type produces substances such as epinephrine, norepinephrine, dopamine, serotonin, enkephalin, somatostatin, neurotensin, and substance P, the actions of which may affect contiguous cells, nearby groups of cells, or distant cells, thus functioning as local or systemic hormones. The name is an acronym for amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation cell.

CL:0000569.name: cardiac mesenchymal cell
CL:0000569.def: A mesenchymal cell found in the developing heart and that develops into some part of the heart.  These cells derive from intra- and extra-cardiac sources, including the endocardium, epicardium, neural crest, and second heart field.

CL:0000570.name: parafollicular cell
CL:0000570.def: A neuroepithelial cells that occurs singly or in small groups, close to the outer follicular borders but within the follicular basement membrane of the thyroid. Expresses a form of the neural cell adhesion molecule (N-CAM) on their surface. Secretes calcitonin, 5-hydroxytryptamine and dopamine.

CL:0000571.name: leucophore
CL:0000571.def: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains uric acid or other purine crystals deposited in stacks called leucosomes. The crystals reflect light and this gives a white appearance under white light.

CL:0000573.name: retinal cone cell
CL:0000573.def: One of the two photoreceptor cell types in the vertebrate retina. In cones the photopigment is in invaginations of the cell membrane of the outer segment. Cones are less sensitive to light than rods, but they provide vision with higher spatial and temporal acuity, and the combination of signals from cones with different pigments allows color vision.

CL:0000574.name: erythrophore
CL:0000574.def: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains pteridine and/or carotenoid pigments in structures called pterinosomes or erythrosomes. This gives an orange to red appearance.

CL:0000575.name: corneal epithelial cell
CL:0000575.def: An epithelial cell of the cornea.

CL:0000576.name: monocyte
CL:0000576.def: Myeloid mononuclear recirculating leukocyte that can act as a precursor of tissue macrophages, osteoclasts and some populations of tissue dendritic cells.

CL:0000577.name: type EC enteroendocrine cell
CL:0000577.def: A subtype of enteroendocrine cells found in the gastrointestinal mucosa, particularly in the glands of pyloric antrum; duodenum; and ileum. These cell type secretes serotonin and some neurotransmitters including enkephalins and substance P. Their secretory granules stain readily with silver (argentaffin stain).

CL:0000578.name: experimentally modified cell in vitro
CL:0000578.def: A cell in vitro that has undergone physical changes as a consequence of a deliberate and specific experimental procedure.

CL:0000579.name: border follicle cell
CL:0000579.def: A follicle cell that migrates from the anterior pole of the insect egg chamber to the anterior of the oocyte where they participate in the formation of the micropyle.

CL:0000580.name: neutrophilic myelocyte
CL:0000580.def: A neutrophil precursor in the granulocytic series, being a cell intermediate in development between a promyelocyte and a metamyelocyte; in this stage, production of primary granules is complete and neutrophil-specific granules has started. No nucleolus is present. This cell type is CD13-positive, CD16-negative, integrin alpha-M-positive, CD15-positive, CD33-positive, CD24-positive, C/EBP-a-positive, C/EBPe-positive, PU.1-positive, lactotransferrin-positive, myeloperoxidase-positive and NGAL-positive.

CL:0000581.name: peritoneal macrophage
CL:0000581.def: A macrophage resident in the peritoneum under non-inflammatory conditions. Markers include F4/80-high, CD11b-high, CD68-positive, SIGNR1-positive, CD115-high, MHC-II-negative, and Dectin-1-positive.

CL:0000582.name: neutrophilic metamyelocyte
CL:0000582.def: A neutrophil precursor in the granulocytic series, being a cell intermediate in development between a myelocyte and the band form neutrophil. The protein synthesis seen in earlier stages decreases or stops; the nucleus becomes indented where the indentation is smaller than half the distance to the farthest nuclear margin; chromatin becomes coarse and clumped; specific granules predominate while primary granules are rare; and the cytoplasm becomes amphophilic like that of a mature granulocyte. This cell type is integrin alpha-M-positive, CD13-negative, CD15-positive, CD16-positive, CD33-positive, CD24-positive, fMLP receptor-negative and has expression of C/EBP-a, C/EBP-e, PU.1 transcription factor, lactotransferrin, myeloperoxidase and neutrophil gelatinase associated lipocalin.

CL:0000583.name: alveolar macrophage
CL:0000583.def: A tissue-resident macrophage found in the alveoli of the lungs. Ingests small inhaled particles resulting in degradation and presentation of the antigen to immunocompetent cells. Markers include F4/80-positive, CD11b-/low, CD11c-positive, CD68-positive, sialoadhesin-positive, dectin-1-positive, MR-positive, CX3CR1-negative.

CL:0000584.name: enterocyte
CL:0000584.def: An epithelial cell that has its apical plasma membrane folded into microvilli to provide ample surface for the absorption of nutrients from the intestinal lumen.

CL:0000585.name: obsolete null cell
CL:0000585.def: OBSOLETE: A class of lymphocytes characterized by the lack of surface markers specific for either T or B cells.

CL:0000586.name: germ cell
CL:0000586.def: The reproductive cell in multicellular organisms.

CL:0000587.name: cold sensing thermoreceptor cell
CL:0000587.def: A thermoreceptor cell that detects reduced temperatures.

CL:0000588.name: odontoclast
CL:0000588.def: A specialized osteoclast associated with the absorption and removal of cementum.

CL:0000589.name: cochlear inner hair cell
CL:0000589.def: A bulbous cell that is medially placed in one row in the organ of Corti. In contrast to the outer hair cells, the inner hair cells are fewer in number, have fewer sensory hairs, and are less differentiated.

CL:0000590.name: small luteal cell
CL:0000590.def: A progesterone secreting cell in the corpus luteum that develops from theca cells.

CL:0000591.name: warmth sensing thermoreceptor cell
CL:0000591.def: A thermoreceptor cell that detects increased temperatures.

CL:0000592.name: large luteal cell
CL:0000592.def: A large, progesterone secreting cell in the corpus luteum that develops from the granulosa cells.

CL:0000593.name: androgen secreting cell
CL:0000593.def: A steroid hormone secreting cell that secretes androgen.

CL:0000594.name: skeletal muscle satellite cell
CL:0000594.def: An elongated, spindle-shaped, cell that is located between the basal lamina and the plasmalemma of a muscle fiber. These cells are mostly quiescent, but upon activation they divide to produce cells that generate new muscle fibers.

CL:0000596.name: sexual spore
CL:0000596.def: A spore formed following meiosis. Sometimes following meiosis, prospores may undergo one or more rounds of mitosis before they are fully mature.

CL:0000597.name: microconidium
CL:0000597.def: The smaller of two types of asexual spores formed by some fungi. An ovoid to pear-shaped asexual spore that contains very little cytoplasm and organelles, is uninucleate, and forms in vegetative hypae within a mycelium. Micronidia are extruded from the hyphal cell wall.

CL:0000598.name: pyramidal neuron
CL:0000598.def: Pyramidal neurons have a pyramid-shaped soma with a single axon, a large apical dendrite and multiple basal dendrites. The apex and an apical dendrite typically point toward the pial surface and other dendrites and an axon emerging from the base. The axons may have local collaterals but also project outside their region. Pyramidal neurons are found in the cerebral cortex, the hippocampus, and the amygdala.

CL:0000599.name: conidium
CL:0000599.def: An asexual, nonmotile spore formed by higher fungi; conidia are usually made from the side or tip of specialized sporogenous cells and do not form by progressive cleavage of the cytoplasm.

CL:0000600.name: heterokaryon
CL:0000600.def: A fungal cell with two or more genetically distinct nuclei.

CL:0000601.name: cochlear outer hair cell
CL:0000601.def: A mechanoreceptor in the organ of Corti. In mammals the outer hair cells are arranged in three rows which are further from the modiolus than the single row of inner hair cells. The motile properties of the outer hair cells may contribute actively to tuning the sensitivity and frequency selectivity of the cochlea.

CL:0000602.name: pressoreceptor cell
CL:0000602.def: A receptor in the vascular system, particularly the aorta and carotid sinus, which is sensitive to stretch of the vessel walls.

CL:0000603.name: dikaryon
CL:0000603.def: A fungal cell with two genetically distinct haploid nuclei.

CL:0000604.name: retinal rod cell
CL:0000604.def: One of the two photoreceptor cell types of the vertebrate retina. In rods the photopigment is in stacks of membranous disks separate from the outer cell membrane. Rods are more sensitive to light than cones, but rod mediated vision has less spatial and temporal resolution than cone vision.

CL:0000605.name: fungal asexual spore
CL:0000605.def: A spore formed following mitosis or mitoses.

CL:0000606.name: macroconidium
CL:0000606.def: The larger of two types of asexual spores formed by some fungi; usually round or oblong.

CL:0000607.name: ascospore
CL:0000607.def: A thick walled spore that stores and protects one or more nuclei following sexual reproduction in an Ascomycete.

CL:0000608.name: zygospore
CL:0000608.def: A thick walled, sexual, resting spore formed by Zygomycetes; sometimes refers to the spore and the multi-layered cell wall that encloses the spore, the zygosporangium.

CL:0000609.name: vestibular hair cell
CL:0000609.def: A mechanoreceptor located in the acoustic maculae and the semicircular canals that mediates the sense of balance, movement, and head position. The vestibular hair cells are connected to accessory structures in such a way that movements of the head displace their stereocilia. This influences the membrane potential of the cells which relay information about movements via the vestibular part of the vestibulocochlear nerve to the brain stem.

CL:0000611.name: eosinophil progenitor cell
CL:0000611.def: Any granulocytopoietic cell that has part some transcription factor PU.1 and has part some CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein alpha and has part some erythroid transcription factor and lacks plasma membrane part some CD19 molecule and lacks plasma membrane part some CD4 molecule and lacks plasma membrane part some integrin alpha-M and lacks plasma membrane part some CD3 epsilon and lacks plasma membrane part some neural cell adhesion molecule 1 and lacks plasma membrane part some CD2 molecule and lacks plasma membrane part some T-cell surface glycoprotein CD8 alpha chain and lacks plasma membrane part some membrane-spanning 4-domains subfamily A member 1 and lacks plasma membrane part some T-cell surface glycoprotein CD5 and lacks plasma membrane part some CD14 molecule and lacks plasma membrane part some lymphocyte antigen 6G and lacks plasma membrane part some lymphocyte antigen 76 (mouse) and has plasma membrane part some CD34 molecule and has plasma membrane part some ADP-ribosyl cyclase/cyclic ADP-ribose hydrolase 1 and has plasma membrane part some interleukin-3 receptor class 2 alpha chain and has plasma membrane part some interleukin-5 receptor subunit alpha and has plasma membrane part some mast/stem cell growth factor receptor and is capable of some eosinophil differentiation.

CL:0000612.name: eosinophilic myelocyte
CL:0000612.def: A eosinophil precursor in the granulocytic series, being a cell intermediate in development between a promyelocyte and a metamyelocyte;in this stage, production of primary granules is complete and eosinophil-specific granules has started. No nucleolus is present. These cells are integrin alpha-M-positive, CD13-positive, CD15-positive, CD16-negative, CD24-positive, and CD33-positive.

CL:0000613.name: basophil progenitor cell
CL:0000613.def: A progenitor cell committed to the basophil lineage. This cell lacks hematopoietic lineage markers (lin-negative) and is CD34-positive, T1/ST2-low, CD117-negative, and FceRIa-high. This cell also expresses Gata-1, Gata-2 and C/EBPa.

CL:0000614.name: basophilic myelocyte
CL:0000614.def: A basophil precursor in the granulocytic series, being a cell intermediate in development between a promyelocyte and a metamyelocyte; in this stage, production of primary granules is complete and basophil-specific granules has started. No nucleolus is present. Markers are being integrin alpha-M-positive, fucosyltransferase FUT4-positive, CD33-positive, CD24-positive, aminopeptidase N-positive.

CL:0000615.name: basidiospore
CL:0000615.def: A thick walled spore containing one or more haploid nuclei produced by sexual reproduction in an Basidiomycete; formed externally on extrusions of the basidium.

CL:0000616.name: obsolete sporangiospore
CL:0000616.def: OBSOLETE: A walled spore produced in a sporangium.

CL:0000617.name: GABAergic neuron
CL:0000617.def: A neuron that uses GABA as a vesicular neurotransmitter

CL:0000620.name: obsolete zoospore
CL:0000620.def: OBSOLETE: A sporangiospore that is motile, having flagella.

CL:0000621.name: fusion competent myoblast
CL:0000621.def: A myoblast that is committed to a myotube-specific program of differentiation but not yet fused. It undergoes very limited additional proliferation. After fusion, it will take on a muscle identity specified by a `muscle founder cell` (CL:0008006).

CL:0000622.name: acinar cell
CL:0000622.def: A secretory cell that is grouped together with other cells of the same type to form grape shaped clusters known as acini (singular acinus).

CL:0000623.name: natural killer cell
CL:0000623.def: A lymphocyte that can spontaneously kill a variety of target cells without prior antigenic activation via germline encoded activation receptors and also regulate immune responses via cytokine release and direct contact with other cells.

CL:0000624.name: CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell
CL:0000624.def: A mature alpha-beta T cell that expresses an alpha-beta T cell receptor and the CD4 coreceptor.

CL:0000625.name: CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
CL:0000625.def: A T cell expressing an alpha-beta T cell receptor and the CD8 coreceptor.

CL:0000626.name: olfactory granule cell
CL:0000626.def: A granule cell that has a soma located in an olfactory bulb granule cell layer. An olfactory granule cell is an interneuron that lacks an axon, makes reciprocal dendro-dendritic synapses with mitral cells and tufted cells and is involved in the fine spatio-temporal tuning of the responses of these principal olfactory bulb neurons to odors.

CL:0000627.name: transporting cell
CL:0000627.def: A cell involved in transporting nutrients, minerals, water, gases and other chemicals between cells for a variety of purposes including conveying nutrition to other tissues, removing waste products from the tissues, conveying gases for respiration, distributing heat and repelling invasion of foreign substances.

CL:0000628.name: photosynthetic cell
CL:0000628.def: A cell that can perform photosynthesis, in which carbohydrates are synthesized from carbon dioxide and water, using light as the energy source.

CL:0000629.name: storage cell
CL:0000629.def: A cell that is specialized to store a particular substance(s), which is(are) later released from the store for a particular purpose.

CL:0000630.name: supporting cell
CL:0000630.def: A cell whose primary function is to support other cell types.

CL:0000631.name: labyrinth supporting cell
CL:0000631.def: Cells forming a framework supporting the organ of Corti. Specific cells are those of Claudius, Deiters and Hensen.

CL:0000632.name: hepatic stellate cell
CL:0000632.def: A cell that is found in the perisinusoidal space of the liver that is capable of multiple roles including storage of retinol, presentation of antigen to T cells (including CD1d-restricted NKT cells), and upon activation, production of extracellular matrix components that can contribute to liver fibrosis. This activated state has a myofibroblast-like phenotype, though it's not clear in the literature if this is terminally differentiated. This cell type comprises approximately 8-15% of total cells in the liver.

CL:0000633.name: Hensen cell
CL:0000633.def: A tall supporting cell that is arranged in rows adjacent to the last row of outer phalangeal cells. This cell type constitutes the outer border of the organ of Corti.
synonym: external limiting cell of organ of Corti

CL:0000634.name: Claudius cell
CL:0000634.def: A cuboidal cell which along with Boettcher's cells form the floor of the external spiral sulcus, external to the organ of Corti.

CL:0000635.name: Deiter's cell
CL:0000635.def: The outer phalangeal cells of the organ of Corti. This cell holds the base of the hair cell in a cup-shaped depression.

CL:0000636.name: Mueller cell
CL:0000636.def: Astrocyte-like radial glial cell that extends vertically throughout the retina, with the nucleus are usually in the middle of the inner nuclear layer.

CL:0000637.name: chromophil cell of anterior pituitary gland
CL:0000637.def: A cell that stains readily in the anterior pituitary gland.

CL:0000638.name: acidophil cell of pars distalis of adenohypophysis
CL:0000638.def: An acidophilic chromophil cell that of the anterior pituitary gland.
synonym: acidophil cell of pars anterior of adenohypophysis
acidophil of pars anterior of adenohypophysis
acidophil of pars distalis of adenohypophysis

CL:0000639.name: basophil cell of pars distalis of adenohypophysis
CL:0000639.def: A basophilic chromophil cell that of the anterior pituitary gland.
synonym: basophil cell of anterior lobe of hypophysis

CL:0000641.name: chromophobe cell
CL:0000641.def: A cell that is resistant to stains.

CL:0000642.name: folliculostellate cell
CL:0000642.def: An agranular supporting cell of the anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) that is characterized by a star-like morphology and ability to form follicles. Folliculostellate cells communicate with each other and with endocrine cells via gap junctions.

CL:0000644.name: Bergmann glial cell
CL:0000644.def: Type of radial astrocyte in the cerebellar cortex that have their cell bodies in the Purkinje cell layer and processes that extend into the molecular layer, terminating with bulbous endfeet at the pial surface. Bergmann glia express high densities of glutamate transporters that limit diffusion of the neurotransmitter glutamate during its release from synaptic terminals. Besides their role in early development of the cerebellum, Bergmann glia are also required for the pruning or addition of synapses.

CL:0000645.name: pituicyte
CL:0000645.def: A glial cell of astrocytic lineage with long processes running parallel to adjacent axons in the proximal infundibulum of the neurohypophysis. These processes form a three-dimensional network among the axons of the hypothalamic neurosecretory cells and are connected by gap junctions which provide for their metabolic coupling. This cell type constitutes most of the nonexcitable tissue in the neurohypophsis; function may include possibly acting as an intermediate in the modulation of oxytocin and vasopressin release. This cell type is highly variable in size and shape and commonly contain lipid droplets and deposits of lipochrome pigment.

CL:0000646.name: basal cell
CL:0000646.def: Undifferentiated; mitotic stem cell for other epithelial cell types; rounded or elliptical with little cytoplasm and few organelles; contain cytokeratin intermediate filament.

CL:0000647.name: multinucleated giant cell
CL:0000647.def: A phagocytic syncytial cell formed by the fusion of macrophages, occurs in chronic inflammatory responses to persistent microorganism such as M.tuberculosis, component of granulomas. Sometimes used to refer to megakaryocytes.

CL:0000648.name: kidney granular cell
CL:0000648.def: A smooth muscle cell that synthesizes, stores, and secretes the enzyme renin. This cell type are located in the wall of the afferent arteriole at the entrance to the glomerulus. While having a different origin than other kidney smooth muscle cells, this cell type expresses smooth muscle actin upon maturation.

CL:0000649.name: prickle cell
CL:0000649.def: A cell with delicate radiating processes known as desmosomes that form intercellular bridges between other cells of this type. This cell type forms the stratum spinosum (prickle cell layer). A function of this cell is to generate keratin.

CL:0000650.name: mesangial cell
CL:0000650.def: A cell type that encapsulates the capillaries and venules in the kidney. This cell secretes mesangial matrix that provides the structural support for the capillaries.

CL:0000651.name: obsolete mucous neck cell
CL:0000651.def: OBSOLETE. A mucus-secreting cell, with numerous apical secretory vesicles containing mucins; nucleus are basally displaced; numerous at the neck of mucus secreting glands

CL:0000652.name: pinealocyte
CL:0000652.def: This cell type produces and secretes melatonin and forms the pineal parenchyma. Extending from each cell body, which has a spherical, oval or lobulated mucleus, are one or more tortuous basophilic processes, containing parallel microtubules known as synaptic ribbons. These processes end in expanded terminal buds near capillaries or less, frequently, ependymal cells of the pineal recess. The terminal buds contain granular endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and electron-dense cored vesicles, which store monoamines and polypeptide hormones, release of which appears to require sympathetic innervation.

CL:0000653.name: podocyte
CL:0000653.def: A specialized kidney epithelial cell, contained within a glomerulus, that contains foot processes that interdigitate with the foot processes of other podocytes.
synonym: epithelial cell of visceral layer of glomerular capsule

CL:0000654.name: primary oocyte
CL:0000654.def: A primary oocyte is an oocyte that has not completed female meosis I.

CL:0000655.name: secondary oocyte
CL:0000655.def: A secondary oocyte is an oocyte that has not completed meiosis II.

CL:0000656.name: primary spermatocyte
CL:0000656.def: A diploid cell that has derived from a spermatogonium and can subsequently begin meiosis and divide into two haploid secondary spermatocytes.

CL:0000657.name: secondary spermatocyte
CL:0000657.def: One of the two haploid cells into which a primary spermatocyte divides, and which in turn gives origin to spermatids.

CL:0000658.name: cuticle secreting cell
CL:0000658.def: An epithelial cell that secretes cuticle.

CL:0000659.name: eggshell secreting cell
CL:0000659.def: An extracellular matrix secreting cell that secretes eggshell.

CL:0000660.name: glycocalyx secreting cell
CL:0000660.def: An extracellular matrix secreting cell that secretes glycocalyx.

CL:0000666.name: fenestrated endothelial cell
CL:0000666.def: An endothelial cell that has small pores, or fenestrations, which allow for the efficient exchange of substances between the blood and surrounding tissues.

CL:0000667.name: collagen secreting cell
CL:0000667.def: An extracellular matrix secreting cell that secretes collagen.

CL:0000668.name: obsolete parenchymal cell
CL:0000668.def: OBSOLETE: The cell characteristic of an organ, as distinguished from associated connective or supporting tissues.

CL:0000669.name: pericyte
CL:0000669.def: An elongated, contractile cell found wrapped about precapillary arterioles outside the basement membrane. Pericytes are present in capillaries where proper adventitia and muscle layer are missing (thus distingushing this cell type from adventitial cells). They are relatively undifferentiated and may become fibroblasts, macrophages, or smooth muscle cells.

CL:0000670.name: primordial germ cell
CL:0000670.def: A primordial germ cell is a diploid germ cell precursors that transiently exist in the embryo before they enter into close association with the somatic cells of the gonad and become irreversibly committed as germ cells.

CL:0000671.name: centripetally migrating follicle cell
CL:0000671.def: A follicle cell that migrates from the dorso-anterior part of the oocyte associated follicular epithelium, in between the nurse cells and the oocyte, and participates in the formation of the operculum.

CL:0000672.name: obsolete tracheary element
CL:0000672.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0000290 from Plant Ontology instead. A water conducting cell, tracheid or vessel member.

CL:0000673.name: Kenyon cell
CL:0000673.def: An intrinsic neuron of the mushroom body of arthropods and annelids. They have tightly packed, cytoplasm-poor cell bodies.

CL:0000674.name: interfollicle cell
CL:0000674.def: A follicle cell that is part of the stalk connecting adjacent egg chambers.

CL:0000675.name: female gamete
CL:0000675.def: A mature sexual reproductive cell of the female germline.

CL:0000677.name: gut absorptive cell
CL:0000677.def: Cell of the intestinal epithelium with a brush border made up of many parallel packed microvilli; associated with absorption, particularly of macromolecules.

CL:0000678.name: commissural neuron
CL:0000678.def: A neuron with soma location in the central nervous system that project its axon to the contralateral side of a central nervous system. This neuron can have its soma in the spinal cord, in the hemisphere of the brain, in the retina or in the ventral nerve cord of invertebrates.

CL:0000679.name: glutamatergic neuron
CL:0000679.def: A neuron that is capable of some neurotansmission by glutamate secretion.

CL:0000680.name: muscle precursor cell
CL:0000680.def: A non-terminally differentiated cell that is capable of developing into a muscle cell.

CL:0000681.name: radial glial cell
CL:0000681.def: A cell present in the developing CNS. Functions as both a precursor cell and as a scaffold to support neuronal migration.

CL:0000682.name: M cell of gut
CL:0000682.def: An absorptive cell of the gut epithelium that endocytoses microorganisms and intact macromolecules from the gut lumen and transports them to the subepithelial space where they are presented to antigen-presenting cells and lymphocytes.

CL:0000683.name: ependymoglial cell
CL:0000683.def: A cell that transports hormones from neurosecretory cells. This nerve cell is characterized by bipolar shape and endfeet that contact a basal lamina around blood vessels, and/or the pia mater or vitreous body of the eye and additionally contact the ventricular surface or sub-retinal space.

CL:0000685.name: obsolete meristematic cell
CL:0000685.def: Obsolete. Use PO:0004010 from Plant Ontology instead. A cell synthesizing protoplasm and producing new cells by division and with only a primary cell wall.

CL:0000686.name: cerebrospinal fluid secreting cell
CL:0000686.def: A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell that secretes cerebrospinal fluid.

CL:0000688.name: perijunctional fibroblast
CL:0000688.def: A fibroblast-like cell that provides support at neuromuscular junctions in vertebrates and are localized outside the synaptic basal lamina.

CL:0000689.name: myoendocrine cell
CL:0000689.def: A cell with both myofibrils and secretory granules.

CL:0000691.name: stellate interneuron
CL:0000691.def: Any interneuron that has characteristic some stellate morphology.

CL:0000692.name: terminal Schwann cell
CL:0000692.def: A neuroglial cell of the peripheral nervous system inside the basal lamina of the neuromuscular junction providing chemical and physical support to the synapse.

CL:0000693.name: neurogliaform cell
CL:0000693.def: An interneuron that has spider-like appearance with a small round soma, a large number (7-10) of short, smooth, or slightly beaded primary dendrites that give rise to only a few secondary branches, and a branched axon that establishes a dense axonal mesh with thin shafts.

CL:0000695.name: Cajal-Retzius cell
CL:0000695.def: A neuron of the human embryonic marginal zone which display, as a salient feature, radial ascending processes that contact the pial surface, and a horizontal axon plexus located in the deep marginal zone. One feature of these cells in mammals is that they express the Reelin gene.

CL:0000696.name: PP cell
CL:0000696.def: A cell that stores and secretes pancreatic polypeptide hormone.

CL:0000699.name: paraganglial type 1 cell
CL:0000699.def: A type of glomus or chief cell, is sensitive to hypoxia and produce catecholamines.

CL:0000700.name: dopaminergic neuron
CL:0000700.def: A neuron that releases dopamine as a neurotransmitter.

CL:0000703.name: sustentacular cell
CL:0000703.def: Cell that provides some or all mechanical, nutritional and phagocytic support to their neighbors.

CL:0000704.name: endothelial tip cell
CL:0000704.def: A specialized endothelial cell that senses extracellular signals and guides the directed growth of blood vessels.

CL:0000706.name: choroid plexus epithelial cell
CL:0000706.def: A specialized ependymal cell that is part of the choroid plexus epithelium, responsible for producing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by selectively filtering and modifying blood plasma components before secreting it into the brain and spinal cord. This cell is characterized by a brush border on its apical surface, which enhances the secretion of CSF.

CL:0000708.name: leptomeningeal cell
CL:0000708.def: Stromal cell that forms the internal covering of the vertebrate brain and produces ECM for this and the choroid plexus.

CL:0000710.name: neurecto-epithelial cell
CL:0000710.def: Epithelial cells derived from neural plate and neural crest.

CL:0000711.name: cumulus granulosa cell
CL:0000711.def: Cumulus cell is a specialized granulosa cell that surrounds and nourishes the oocyte. This cell-type surrounds the fully-grown oocyte to form a cumulus-oocyte complex (abbr. COC). The terms cumulus oophorus cells, cumulus granulosa cells, cumulus oophorous granulosa cells, granulosa-cumulus cells are used to make a distinction between this cell and the other functionally different subpopulation of granulosa cells at the wall of the Graafian follicle.

CL:0000712.name: stratum granulosum cell
CL:0000712.def: Any epidermal cell that is part of some stratum granulosum of epidermis.

CL:0000715.name: embryonic crystal cell
CL:0000715.def: A crystal cell that derives from the embryonic head mesoderm.

CL:0000716.name: lymph gland crystal cell
CL:0000716.def: A crystal cell that derives from the larval lymph gland.

CL:0000717.name: obsolete fusimotor neuron
CL:0000717.def: OBSOLETE. A subset of motor neurons that innervates intrafusal muscle fibers and has small diameter axons.

CL:0000718.name: compound eye cone cell
CL:0000718.def: A cell of an ommatidium that secretes lens materials.

CL:0000723.name: somatic stem cell
CL:0000723.def: A stem cell that can give rise to cell types of the body other than those of the germ-line.

CL:0000724.name: heterocyst
CL:0000724.def: A differentiated cell that functions as a site of nitrogen fixation under aerobic conditions.

CL:0000725.name: nitrogen fixing cell
CL:0000725.def: Any cell that is capable of some nitrogen fixation.

CL:0000726.name: chlamydospore
CL:0000726.def: An asexual 1-celled spore (primarily for perennation, not dissemination). Originates endogenously and singly within part of a pre-existing cell by the contraction of the protoplast. Possesses an inner secondary and often thickened hyaline or brown wall, usually impregnated with hydrophobic material.

CL:0000730.name: leading edge cell
CL:0000730.def: A cell at the front of a migrating epithelial sheet.

CL:0000731.name: urothelial cell
CL:0000731.def: A cell of a layer of transitional epithelium in the wall of the proximal urethra, bladder, ureter or renal pelvis, external to the lamina propria.

CL:0000733.name: lymph gland plasmatocyte
CL:0000733.def: A plasmatocyte that derives from the larval lymph gland.

CL:0000735.name: lymph gland hemocyte
CL:0000735.def: A hemocyte that derives from the larval lymph gland.

CL:0000737.name: striated muscle cell
CL:0000737.def: Muscle cell which has as its direct parts myofilaments organized into sarcomeres.

CL:0000738.name: leukocyte
CL:0000738.def: An achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages capable of ameboid movement, found in blood or other tissue.

CL:0000740.name: retinal ganglion cell
CL:0000740.def: The set of neurons that receives neural inputs via bipolar, horizontal and amacrine cells. The axons of these cells make up the optic nerve.

CL:0000741.name: spinal accessory motor neuron
CL:0000741.def: A motor neuron that is located in the cervical region of the spinal cord and selectively innervates the sternocleidmastoid or trapezius muscle. Unlike other motor neurons, they extend axons dorsally along lateral margins of the spinal cord.

CL:0000742.name: periarticular chondrocyte
CL:0000742.def: A round chondrocyte that first differentiates in the late embryonic growth plate of bone.

CL:0000743.name: hypertrophic chondrocyte
CL:0000743.def: Chondrocyte that is terminally differentiated, produces type X collagen, is large in size, and often associated with the replacement of cartilage by bone (endochondral ossification).

CL:0000744.name: columnar chondrocyte
CL:0000744.def: A columnar chondrocyte that differentiates in the late embryonic growth plate of bone. Columnar chondrocytes vigorously proliferate and form columns in the growth plate.

CL:0000745.name: retina horizontal cell
CL:0000745.def: A neuron that laterally connects other neurons in the inner nuclear layer of the retina.

CL:0000746.name: cardiac muscle cell
CL:0000746.def: Cardiac muscle cells are striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction. In mammals, the contractile fiber resembles those of skeletal muscle but are only one third as large in diameter, are richer in sarcoplasm, and contain centrally located instead of peripheral nuclei.

CL:0000747.name: cyanophore
CL:0000747.def: A pigment cell derived from the neural crest. Contains blue pigment of unknown chemical composition in fibrous organelles termed cyanosomes. This gives a blue appearance.

CL:0000748.name: retinal bipolar neuron
CL:0000748.def: A bipolar neuron found in the retina and having connections with photoreceptors cells and neurons in the inner plexiform layer.

CL:0000749.name: ON-bipolar cell
