GO:0000011.name: vacuole inheritance
GO:0000011.def: The distribution of vacuoles into daughter cells after mitosis or meiosis, mediated by interactions between vacuoles and the cytoskeleton.

GO:0000018.name: regulation of DNA recombination
GO:0000018.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of DNA recombination, a DNA metabolic process in which a new genotype is formed by reassortment of genes resulting in gene combinations different from those that were present in the parents.

GO:0000041.name: transition metal ion transport
GO:0000041.def: The directed movement of transition metal ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. A transition metal is an element whose atom has an incomplete d-subshell of extranuclear electrons, or which gives rise to a cation or cations with an incomplete d-subshell. Transition metals often have more than one valency state. Biologically relevant transition metals include vanadium, manganese, iron, copper, cobalt, nickel, molybdenum and silver.

GO:0000070.name: mitotic sister chromatid segregation
GO:0000070.def: The cell cycle process in which replicated homologous chromosomes are organized and then physically separated and apportioned to two sets during the mitotic cell cycle. Each replicated chromosome, composed of two sister chromatids, aligns at the cell equator, paired with its homologous partner. One homolog of each morphologic type goes into each of the resulting chromosome sets.

GO:0000105.name: L-histidine biosynthetic process
GO:0000105.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of L-histidine, 2-amino-3-(1H-imidazol-4-yl)propanoic acid.

GO:0000139.name: Golgi membrane
GO:0000139.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments of the Golgi apparatus.

GO:0000146.name: microfilament motor activity
GO:0000146.def: A motor activity that generates movement along a microfilament, driven by ATP hydrolysis.

GO:0000166.name: nucleotide binding
GO:0000166.def: Binding to a nucleotide, any compound consisting of a nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the ribose or deoxyribose.

GO:0000226.name: microtubule cytoskeleton organization
GO:0000226.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising microtubules and their associated proteins.

GO:0000228.name: nuclear chromosome
GO:0000228.def: A chromosome that encodes the nuclear genome and is found in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell during the cell cycle phases when the nucleus is intact.

GO:0000271.name: polysaccharide biosynthetic process
GO:0000271.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a polysaccharide, a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically.

GO:0000272.name: polysaccharide catabolic process
GO:0000272.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a polysaccharide, a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically.

GO:0000278.name: mitotic cell cycle
GO:0000278.def: Progression through the phases of the mitotic cell cycle, the most common eukaryotic cell cycle, which canonically comprises four successive phases called G1, S, G2, and M and includes replication of the genome and the subsequent segregation of chromosomes into daughter cells. In some variant cell cycles nuclear replication or nuclear division may not be followed by cell division, or G1 and G2 phases may be absent.

GO:0000279.name: M phase
GO:0000279.def: A cell cycle phase during which nuclear division occurs, and which is comprises the phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.

GO:0000280.name: nuclear division
GO:0000280.def: The division of a cell nucleus into two nuclei, with DNA and other nuclear contents distributed between the daughter nuclei.

GO:0000295.name: adenine nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0000295.def: Enables the transfer of adenine nucleotides (AMP, ADP, and ATP) from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0000302.name: response to reactive oxygen species
GO:0000302.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a reactive oxygen species stimulus. Reactive oxygen species include singlet oxygen, superoxide, and oxygen free radicals.

GO:0000303.name: response to superoxide
GO:0000303.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a superoxide stimulus. Superoxide is the anion, oxygen-, formed by addition of one electron to dioxygen (O2) or any compound containing the superoxide anion.

GO:0000305.name: response to oxygen radical
GO:0000305.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an oxygen radical stimulus. An oxygen radical is any oxygen species that carries a free electron; examples include hydroxyl radicals and the superoxide anion.

GO:0000313.name: organellar ribosome
GO:0000313.def: A ribosome contained within a subcellular membrane-bounded organelle.

GO:0000323.name: lytic vacuole
GO:0000323.def: A vacuole that is maintained at an acidic pH and which contains degradative enzymes, including a wide variety of acid hydrolases.

GO:0000578.name: embryonic axis specification
GO:0000578.def: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of a pattern along a line or a point in an embryo.

GO:0000740.name: nuclear membrane fusion
GO:0000740.def: The joining of 2 or more lipid bilayer membranes that surround the nucleus.

GO:0000741.name: karyogamy
GO:0000741.def: The creation of a single nucleus from multiple nuclei as a result of fusing the lipid bilayers that surround each nuclei.

GO:0000768.name: syncytium formation by plasma membrane fusion
GO:0000768.def: The formation of a syncytium, a mass of cytoplasm containing several nuclei enclosed within a single plasma membrane, by the fusion of the plasma membranes of two or more individual cells.

GO:0000785.name: chromatin
GO:0000785.def: The ordered and organized complex of DNA, protein, and sometimes RNA, that forms the chromosome.

GO:0000791.name: euchromatin
GO:0000791.def: A dispersed and relatively uncompacted form of chromatin that is in a transcription-competent conformation.

GO:0000792.name: heterochromatin
GO:0000792.def: A compact and highly condensed form of chromatin that is refractory to transcription.

GO:0000819.name: sister chromatid segregation
GO:0000819.def: The cell cycle process in which sister chromatids are organized and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets.

GO:0000820.name: regulation of glutamine family amino acid metabolic process
GO:0000820.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.
GO:0000820.synonym: regulation of glutamine family amino acid metabolism

GO:0000902.name: cell morphogenesis
GO:0000902.def: The developmental process in which the size or shape of a cell is generated and organized.

GO:0001101.name: response to acid chemical
GO:0001101.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus by the chemical structure of the anion portion of a dissociated acid (rather than the acid acting as a proton donor). The acid chemical may be in gaseous, liquid or solid form.

GO:0001501.name: skeletal system development
GO:0001501.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skeleton over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The skeleton is the bony framework of the body in vertebrates (endoskeleton) or the hard outer envelope of insects (exoskeleton or dermoskeleton).

GO:0001503.name: ossification
GO:0001503.def: The formation of bone or of a bony substance, or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.

GO:0001504.name: neurotransmitter uptake
GO:0001504.def: The directed movement of neurotransmitters into neurons or glial cells. This process leads to inactivation and recycling of neurotransmitters.

GO:0001507.name: acetylcholine catabolic process in synaptic cleft
GO:0001507.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of acetylcholine that occurs in the synaptic cleft during synaptic transmission.

GO:0001508.name: action potential
GO:0001508.def: A process in which membrane potential cycles through a depolarizing spike, triggered in response to depolarization above some threshold, followed by repolarization. This cycle is driven by the flow of ions through various voltage gated channels with different thresholds and ion specificities.

GO:0001525.name: angiogenesis
GO:0001525.def: Blood vessel formation when new vessels emerge from the proliferation of pre-existing blood vessels.
GO:0001525.synonym: blood vessel formation from pre-existing blood vessels

GO:0001534.name: radial spoke
GO:0001534.def: Protein complex that links the outer microtubule doublet of a 9+2 type ciliary or flagellar axoneme with the sheath that surrounds the central pair of microtubules. Composed of a stalk that attaches to each doublet microtubule and a globular structure (spoke head) that projects toward the central pair of microtubules.

GO:0001539.name: cilium or flagellum-dependent cell motility
GO:0001539.def: Cell motility due to movement of eukaryotic cilia or bacterial-type flagella or archaeal-type flagella.

GO:0001541.name: ovarian follicle development
GO:0001541.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ovarian follicle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0001545.name: primary ovarian follicle growth
GO:0001545.def: Increase in size of primary follicles including oocyte growth and granulosa and/or theca cell proliferation until more than one layer of granulosa cells is present (preantral follicle).

GO:0001546.name: preantral ovarian follicle growth
GO:0001546.def: Increase in size of follicles surrounded by two or more layers of granulosa cells up to the onset of antrum formation.

GO:0001547.name: antral ovarian follicle growth
GO:0001547.def: Increase in size of antral follicles due to cell proliferation and/or growth of the antral cavity.

GO:0001549.name: cumulus cell differentiation
GO:0001549.def: The process in which a subpopulation of granulosa cells surrounding the oocyte acquires the specialized features of an ovarian cumulus cell.

GO:0001552.name: ovarian follicle atresia
GO:0001552.def: A periodic process in which immature ovarian follicles degenerate and are subsequently re-absorbed.

GO:0001553.name: luteinization
GO:0001553.def: The set of processes resulting in differentiation of theca and granulosa cells into luteal cells and in the formation of a corpus luteum after ovulation.

GO:0001555.name: oocyte growth
GO:0001555.def: The developmental growth process in which an oocyte irreversibly increases in size over time by accretion and biosynthetic production of matter similar to that already present.

GO:0001556.name: oocyte maturation
GO:0001556.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for an oocyte to attain its fully functional state. Oocyte maturation commences after reinitiation of meiosis commonly starting with germinal vesicle breakdown, and continues up to the second meiotic arrest prior to fertilization.

GO:0001558.name: regulation of cell growth
GO:0001558.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, extent or direction of cell growth.

GO:0001560.name: regulation of cell growth by extracellular stimulus
GO:0001560.def: Any process in which external signals modulate the frequency, rate or extent of cell growth, the irreversible increase in size of a cell over time.
synonym: interpretation of external signals that regulate cell growth
regulation of cell growth by detection of exogenous stimulus
regulation of cell growth by sensing of exogenous stimulus
regulation of growth by exogenous signal
regulation of growth by exogenous stimuli
regulation of growth by exogenous stimulus
regulation of growth by external signal
regulation of growth by external stimuli
regulation of growth by external stimulus

GO:0001568.name: blood vessel development
GO:0001568.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a blood vessel over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The blood vessel is the vasculature carrying blood.

GO:0001569.name: branching involved in blood vessel morphogenesis
GO:0001569.def: The process of coordinated growth and sprouting of blood vessels giving rise to the organized vascular system.

GO:0001570.name: vasculogenesis
GO:0001570.def: The differentiation of endothelial cells from progenitor cells during blood vessel development, and the de novo formation of blood vessels and tubes.

GO:0001578.name: microtubule bundle formation
GO:0001578.def: A process that results in a parallel arrangement of microtubules.

GO:0001614.name: purinergic nucleotide receptor activity
GO:0001614.def: Combining with a purine nucleotide and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0001621.name: G protein-coupled ADP receptor activity
GO:0001621.def: Combining with ADP and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.

GO:0001649.name: osteoblast differentiation
GO:0001649.def: The process whereby a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of an osteoblast, a mesodermal or neural crest cell that gives rise to bone.

GO:0001653.name: peptide receptor activity
GO:0001653.def: Combining with an extracellular or intracellular peptide to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0001654.name: eye development
GO:0001654.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the eye over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The eye is the organ of sight.

GO:0001655.name: urogenital system development
GO:0001655.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the urogenital system over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0001656.name: metanephros development
GO:0001656.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the metanephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In mammals, the metanephros is the excretory organ of the fetus, which develops into the mature kidney and is formed from the rear portion of the nephrogenic cord. The metanephros is an endocrine and metabolic organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0001657.name: ureteric bud development
GO:0001657.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ureteric bud over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0001658.name: branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis
GO:0001658.def: The process in which the branching structure of the ureteric bud is generated and organized. The ureteric bud is an epithelial tube that grows out from the metanephric duct. The bud elongates and branches to give rise to the ureter and kidney collecting tubules.

GO:0001659.name: temperature homeostasis
GO:0001659.def: A homeostatic process in which an organism modulates its internal body temperature.

GO:0001664.name: G protein-coupled receptor binding
GO:0001664.def: Binding to a G protein-coupled receptor.

GO:0001666.name: response to hypoxia
GO:0001666.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating lowered oxygen tension. Hypoxia, defined as a decline in O2 levels below normoxic levels of 20.8 - 20.95%, results in metabolic adaptation at both the cellular and organismal level.

GO:0001667.name: ameboidal-type cell migration
GO:0001667.def: Cell migration that is accomplished by extension and retraction of a pseudopodium.

GO:0001669.name: acrosomal vesicle
GO:0001669.def: A structure in the head of a spermatozoon that contains acid hydrolases, and is concerned with the breakdown of the outer membrane of the ovum during fertilization. It lies just beneath the plasma membrane and is derived from the lysosome.

GO:0001673.name: male germ cell nucleus
GO:0001673.def: The nucleus of a male germ cell, a reproductive cell in males.

GO:0001674.name: female germ cell nucleus
GO:0001674.def: The nucleus of the female germ cell, a reproductive cell in females.

GO:0001675.name: acrosome assembly
GO:0001675.def: The formation of the acrosome from the spermatid Golgi.

GO:0001677.name: formation of translation initiation ternary complex
GO:0001677.def: Formation of a complex between aminoacylated initiator methionine tRNA, GTP, and initiation factor 2 (either eIF2 in eukaryotes, or IF2 in prokaryotes). In prokaryotes, fMet-tRNA (initiator) is used rather than Met-tRNA (initiator).

GO:0001678.name: intracellular glucose homeostasis
GO:0001678.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of glucose within a cell.

GO:0001692.name: histamine metabolic process
GO:0001692.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving histamine, a physiologically active amine, found in plant and animal tissue and released from mast cells as part of an allergic reaction in humans.

GO:0001694.name: histamine biosynthetic process
GO:0001694.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of histamine, a physiologically active amine, found in plant and animal tissue and released from mast cells as part of an allergic reaction in humans.

GO:0001695.name: histamine catabolic process
GO:0001695.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of histamine, a physiologically active amine, found in plant and animal tissue and released from mast cells as part of an allergic reaction in humans.

GO:0001696.name: gastric acid secretion
GO:0001696.def: The regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

GO:0001700.name: embryonic development via the syncytial blastoderm
GO:0001700.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the embryo over time, from zygote formation through syncytial blastoderm to the hatching of the first instar larva. An example of this process is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0001701.name: in utero embryonic development
GO:0001701.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the embryo in the uterus over time, from formation of the zygote in the oviduct, to birth. An example of this process is found in Mus musculus.

GO:0001702.name: gastrulation with mouth forming second
GO:0001702.def: A gastrulation process in which the initial invagination becomes the anus and the mouth forms second.

GO:0001703.name: gastrulation with mouth forming first
GO:0001703.def: A gastrulation process in which the initial invagination becomes the mouth and the anus forms second.

GO:0001704.name: formation of primary germ layer
GO:0001704.def: The formation of the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm during gastrulation.

GO:0001705.name: ectoderm formation
GO:0001705.def: The formation of ectoderm during gastrulation.

GO:0001706.name: endoderm formation
GO:0001706.def: The formation of the endoderm during gastrulation.

GO:0001707.name: mesoderm formation
GO:0001707.def: The process that gives rise to the mesoderm. This process pertains to the initial formation of the structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0001742.name: oenocyte differentiation
GO:0001742.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of an oenocyte. Oenocytes are large secretory cells found in clusters underlying the epidermis of larval abdominal segments.

GO:0001743.name: lens placode formation
GO:0001743.def: The initial developmental process that will lead to the formation of an eye.

GO:0001745.name: compound eye morphogenesis
GO:0001745.def: The morphogenetic process in which the anatomical structures of the compound eye are generated and organized. The adult compound eye is a precise assembly of 700-800 ommatidia. Each ommatidium is composed of 20 cells, identified by cell type and position. An example of compound eye morphogenesis is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0001751.name: compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
GO:0001751.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of an eye photoreceptor cell.

GO:0001754.name: eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
GO:0001754.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a photoreceptor cell, as found in the eye, the primary visual organ of most organisms.

GO:0001755.name: neural crest cell migration
GO:0001755.def: The characteristic movement of cells from the dorsal ridge of the neural tube to a variety of locations in a vertebrate embryo.

GO:0001756.name: somitogenesis
GO:0001756.def: The formation of mesodermal clusters that are arranged segmentally along the anterior posterior axis of an embryo.

GO:0001763.name: morphogenesis of a branching structure
GO:0001763.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of branches are generated and organized. A branch is a division or offshoot from a main stem. Examples in animals would include blood vessels, nerves, lymphatics and other endothelial or epithelial tubes.

GO:0001764.name: neuron migration
GO:0001764.def: The characteristic movement of an immature neuron from germinal zones to specific positions where they will reside as they mature.

GO:0001767.name: establishment of lymphocyte polarity
GO:0001767.def: The directed orientation of lymphocyte signaling molecules and associated membrane rafts towards a chemokine gradient or a contact point with an appropriate activating cell.

GO:0001768.name: establishment of T cell polarity
GO:0001768.def: The directed orientation of T cell signaling molecules and associated membrane rafts towards a chemokine gradient or a contact point with antigen presenting cell.

GO:0001769.name: establishment of B cell polarity
GO:0001769.def: The directed orientation of B cell signaling molecules and associated membrane rafts towards a chemokine gradient of a contact point with an antigen displaying cell.

GO:0001770.name: establishment of natural killer cell polarity
GO:0001770.def: The directed orientation of natural killer cell signaling molecules and associated membrane rafts towards a chemokine gradient or a contact point with a cell displaying natural killer cell activating ligands.

GO:0001773.name: myeloid dendritic cell activation
GO:0001773.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a dendritic cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

GO:0001774.name: microglial cell activation
GO:0001774.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a microglial cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

GO:0001775.name: cell activation
GO:0001775.def: A multicellular organismal process by which exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand results in a change in the morphology or behavior of a cell.

GO:0001776.name: leukocyte homeostasis
GO:0001776.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of cells of the immune system such that the total number of cells of a particular cell type within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0001777.name: T cell homeostatic proliferation
GO:0001777.def: The non-specific expansion of T cell populations within a whole or part of an organism to reach to a total number of T cells which will then remain stable over time in the absence of an external stimulus.

GO:0001779.name: natural killer cell differentiation
GO:0001779.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a natural killer cell.

GO:0001780.name: neutrophil homeostasis
GO:0001780.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of neutrophils such that the total number of neutrophils within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0001781.name: neutrophil apoptotic process
GO:0001781.def: Any apoptotic process in a neutrophil, any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte that in its mature form has a nucleus with three to five lobes connected by slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing fine inconspicuous granules and stainable by neutral dyes.
synonym: neutrophil programmed cell death by apoptosis
programmed cell death of neutrophils by apoptosis

GO:0001782.name: B cell homeostasis
GO:0001782.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of B cells such that the total number of B cells within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0001783.name: B cell apoptotic process
GO:0001783.def: Any apoptotic process in a B cell, a lymphocyte of B lineage with the phenotype CD19-positive and capable of B cell mediated immunity.
synonym: B cell programmed cell death by apoptosis
B lymphocyte programmed cell death by apoptosis
B-cell programmed cell death by apoptosis
B-lymphocyte programmed cell death by apoptosis
programmed cell death of B cells by apoptosis
programmed cell death of B lymphocytes by apoptosis
programmed cell death of B-cells by apoptosis
programmed cell death of B-lymphocytes by apoptosis

GO:0001787.name: natural killer cell proliferation
GO:0001787.def: The expansion of a natural killer cell population by cell division.

GO:0001816.name: cytokine production
GO:0001816.def: The appearance of a cytokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0001817.name: regulation of cytokine production
GO:0001817.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of production of a cytokine.

GO:0001818.name: negative regulation of cytokine production
GO:0001818.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the rate of production of a cytokine.
synonym: down regulation of cytokine biosynthetic process
negative regulation of cytokine biosynthetic process

GO:0001819.name: positive regulation of cytokine production
GO:0001819.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of production of a cytokine.
synonym: positive regulation of cytokine biosynthetic process

GO:0001820.name: serotonin secretion
GO:0001820.def: The regulated release of serotonin by a cell. Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, or 5-HT) is a monoamine synthesized in serotonergic neurons in the central nervous system, enterochromaffin cells in the gastrointestinal tract and some immune system cells.

GO:0001821.name: histamine secretion
GO:0001821.def: The regulated release of histamine by a cell or tissue. It is formed by decarboxylation of histidine and it acts through receptors in smooth muscle and in secretory systems.

GO:0001822.name: kidney development
GO:0001822.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the kidney over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The kidney is an organ that filters the blood and/or excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0001823.name: mesonephros development
GO:0001823.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In mammals, the mesonephros is the second of the three embryonic kidneys to be established and exists only transiently. In lower vertebrates such as fish and amphibia, the mesonephros will form the mature kidney.

GO:0001824.name: blastocyst development
GO:0001824.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the blastocyst over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mammalian blastocyst is a hollow ball of cells containing two cell types, the inner cell mass and the trophectoderm. The blastula follows the morula and precedes the gastrula in the developmental sequence.

GO:0001825.name: blastocyst formation
GO:0001825.def: The initial formation of a blastocyst from a solid ball of cells known as a morula.

GO:0001826.name: inner cell mass cell differentiation
GO:0001826.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an inner cell mass cell.

GO:0001829.name: trophectodermal cell differentiation
GO:0001829.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a trophectoderm cell.

GO:0001832.name: blastocyst growth
GO:0001832.def: An increase in size of a blastocyst due to expansion of the blastocoelic cavity cell shape changes and cell proliferation.

GO:0001833.name: inner cell mass cell proliferation
GO:0001833.def: The proliferation of cells in the inner cell mass.

GO:0001834.name: trophectodermal cell proliferation
GO:0001834.def: The proliferation of cells in the trophectoderm.

GO:0001837.name: epithelial to mesenchymal transition
GO:0001837.def: A transition where an epithelial cell loses apical/basolateral polarity, severs intercellular adhesive junctions, degrades basement membrane components and becomes a migratory mesenchymal cell.
synonym: mesenchymal cell differentiation from epithelial cell

GO:0001838.name: embryonic epithelial tube formation
GO:0001838.def: The morphogenesis of an embryonic epithelium into a tube-shaped structure.

GO:0001839.name: neural plate morphogenesis
GO:0001839.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the neural plate are generated and organized. The neural plate is a specialized region of columnar epithelial cells in the dorsal ectoderm that will give rise to nervous system tissue.

GO:0001840.name: neural plate development
GO:0001840.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the neural plate over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The neural plate is a flat, thickened layer of ectodermal cells. The underlying dorsal mesoderm signals the ectodermal cells above it to elongate into columnar neural plate cells. The neural plate subsequently develops into the neural tube, which gives rise to the central nervous system.

GO:0001841.name: neural tube formation
GO:0001841.def: The formation of a tube from the flat layer of ectodermal cells known as the neural plate. This will give rise to the central nervous system.

GO:0001842.name: neural fold formation
GO:0001842.def: The process in which the neural fold is formed. The edges of the neural plate thicken and move up to form a U-shaped structure called the neural groove.

GO:0001865.name: NK T cell differentiation
GO:0001865.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a NK T cell.

GO:0001866.name: NK T cell proliferation
GO:0001866.def: The expansion of a NK T cell population by cell division.

GO:0001873.name: polysaccharide immune receptor activity
GO:0001873.def: Combining with a polysaccharide and transmitting the signal to initiate an innate immune response. A polysaccharide is a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically.

GO:0001885.name: endothelial cell development
GO:0001885.def: The progression of an endothelial cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0001886.name: endothelial cell morphogenesis
GO:0001886.def: The change in form (cell shape and size) that occurs during the differentiation of an endothelial cell.

GO:0001889.name: liver development
GO:0001889.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the liver over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The liver is an exocrine gland which secretes bile and functions in metabolism of protein and carbohydrate and fat, synthesizes substances involved in the clotting of the blood, synthesizes vitamin A, detoxifies poisonous substances, stores glycogen, and breaks down worn-out erythrocytes.

GO:0001890.name: placenta development
GO:0001890.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the placenta over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The placenta is an organ of metabolic interchange between fetus and mother, partly of embryonic origin and partly of maternal origin.

GO:0001892.name: embryonic placenta development
GO:0001892.def: The embryonically driven process whose specific outcome is the progression of the placenta over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The placenta is an organ of metabolic interchange between fetus and mother, partly of embryonic origin and partly of maternal origin.

GO:0001893.name: maternal placenta development
GO:0001893.def: Maternally driven process whose specific outcome is the progression of the placenta over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The placenta is an organ of metabolic interchange between fetus and mother, partly of embryonic origin and partly of maternal origin.

GO:0001894.name: tissue homeostasis
GO:0001894.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state within a defined tissue of an organism, including control of cellular proliferation and death and control of metabolic function.

GO:0001906.name: cell killing
GO:0001906.def: Any process in an organism that results in the killing of its own cells or those of another organism, including in some cases the death of the other organism. Killing here refers to the induction of death in one cell by another cell, not cell-autonomous death due to internal or other environmental conditions.

GO:0001909.name: leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0001909.def: The directed killing of a target cell by a leukocyte.

GO:0001910.name: regulation of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0001910.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity.
synonym: regulation of immune cell mediated cell death
regulation of immune cell mediated cell killing
regulation of immune cell mediated cytotoxicity

GO:0001911.name: negative regulation of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0001911.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the rate of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity.
synonym: down regulation of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity
negative regulation of immune cell mediated cytotoxicity
negative regulation of leucocyte mediated cytotoxicity

GO:0001912.name: positive regulation of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0001912.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity.
synonym: positive regulation of immune cell mediated cytotoxicity
positive regulation of leucocyte mediated cytotoxicity
up regulation of leukocyte mediated cytotoxicity

GO:0001913.name: T cell mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0001913.def: The directed killing of a target cell by a T cell through the release of granules containing cytotoxic mediators or through the engagement of death receptors.

GO:0001914.name: regulation of T cell mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0001914.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of T cell mediated cytotoxicity.
synonym: regulation of T cell mediated apoptosis

GO:0001922.name: B-1 B cell homeostasis
GO:0001922.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of B cells of the B-1 subset such that the total number of B-1 B cells within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus. B-1 B cells are a distinct subset of B cells characterized as being CD5 positive, found predominantly in the peritoneum, pleural cavities, and spleen, and enriched for self-reactivity.

GO:0001923.name: B-1 B cell differentiation
GO:0001923.def: The process in which a hemopoietic stem cell acquires the specialized features of a B-1 B cell. B-1 B cells are a distinct subset of B cells characterized as being CD5 positive, found predominantly in the peritoneum, pleural cavities, and spleen, and enriched for self-reactivity.

GO:0001924.name: regulation of B-1 B cell differentiation
GO:0001924.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of B-1 B cell differentiation. B-1 B cells are a distinct subset of B cells characterized as being CD5 positive, found predominantly in the peritoneum, pleural cavities, and spleen, and enriched for self-reactivity.
synonym: regulation of B-1 B cell development
regulation of B-1 B lymphocyte differentiation

GO:0001925.name: negative regulation of B-1 B cell differentiation
GO:0001925.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the rate of B-1 B cell differentiation.

GO:0001926.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of B-1 B cell differentiation.

GO:0001932.name: regulation of protein phosphorylation
GO:0001932.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of addition of phosphate groups into an amino acid in a protein.
GO:0001932.synonym: regulation of protein amino acid phosphorylation

GO:0001933.name: negative regulation of protein phosphorylation
GO:0001933.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate of addition of phosphate groups to amino acids within a protein.

GO:0001935.name: endothelial cell proliferation
GO:0001935.def: The multiplication or reproduction of endothelial cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. Endothelial cells are thin flattened cells which line the inside surfaces of body cavities, blood vessels, and lymph vessels, making up the endothelium.

GO:0001936.name: regulation of endothelial cell proliferation
GO:0001936.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of endothelial cell proliferation.

GO:0001937.name: negative regulation of endothelial cell proliferation
GO:0001937.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the rate or extent of endothelial cell proliferation.
synonym: down regulation of endothelial cell proliferation

GO:0001938.name: positive regulation of endothelial cell proliferation
GO:0001938.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of endothelial cell proliferation.
synonym: up regulation of endothelial cell proliferation

GO:0001940.name: male pronucleus
GO:0001940.def: The pronucleus originating from the spermatozoa that was involved in fertilization.

GO:0001941.name: postsynaptic membrane organization
GO:0001941.def: A process which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a postsynaptic membrane, the specialized area of membrane facing the presynaptic membrane on the tip of the nerve ending and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft).

GO:0001942.name: hair follicle development
GO:0001942.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hair follicle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A hair follicle is a tube-like opening in the epidermis where the hair shaft develops and into which the sebaceous glands open.

GO:0001944.name: vasculature development
GO:0001944.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vasculature over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The vasculature is an interconnected tubular multi-tissue structure that contains fluid that is actively transported around the organism.

GO:0001945.name: lymph vessel development
GO:0001945.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lymph vessel over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0001946.name: lymphangiogenesis
GO:0001946.def: Lymph vessel formation when new vessels emerge from the proliferation of pre-existing vessels.

GO:0001949.name: sebaceous gland cell differentiation
GO:0001949.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized epidermal cell acquires the specialized features of a sebaceous gland cell.

GO:0001955.name: blood vessel maturation
GO:0001955.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a blood vessel to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0001956.name: positive regulation of neurotransmitter secretion
GO:0001956.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of a neurotransmitter.

GO:0001957.name: intramembranous ossification
GO:0001957.def: Direct ossification that occurs within mesenchyme or an accumulation of relatively unspecialized cells.

GO:0001958.name: endochondral ossification
GO:0001958.def: Replacement ossification wherein bone tissue replaces cartilage.

GO:0001959.name: regulation of cytokine-mediated signaling pathway
GO:0001959.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the cytokine mediated signaling pathway.
synonym: regulation of cytokine and chemokine mediated signaling pathway
regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
regulation of cytokine mediated signalling pathway

GO:0001960.name: negative regulation of cytokine-mediated signaling pathway
GO:0001960.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the cytokine mediated signaling pathway.
synonym: down regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
down-regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
downregulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
inhibition of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
negative regulation of cytokine and chemokine mediated signaling pathway
negative regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
negative regulation of cytokine mediated signalling pathway

GO:0001961.name: positive regulation of cytokine-mediated signaling pathway
GO:0001961.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a cytokine mediated signaling pathway.
synonym: activation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
positive regulation of cytokine and chemokine mediated signaling pathway
positive regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
positive regulation of cytokine mediated signalling pathway
stimulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
up regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
up-regulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway
upregulation of cytokine mediated signaling pathway

GO:0001963.name: synaptic transmission, dopaminergic
GO:0001963.def: The vesicular release of dopamine. from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of dopamine receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

GO:0001974.name: blood vessel remodeling
GO:0001974.def: The reorganization or renovation of existing blood vessels.

GO:0001976.name: nervous system process involved in regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
GO:0001976.def: The regulation of blood pressure mediated by detection of stimuli and a neurological response.
synonym: blood pressure regulation by neurological process
neurological process involved in regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
neurological system process involved in regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure

GO:0001977.name: renal system process involved in regulation of blood volume
GO:0001977.def: A slow mechanism of blood pressure regulation that responds to changes in pressure resulting from fluid and salt intake by modulating the quantity of blood in the circulatory system.
synonym: renal blood volume control of blood pressure

GO:0001990.name: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure by hormone
GO:0001990.def: The process in which hormones modulate the force with which blood passes through the circulatory system. A hormone is one of a group of substances formed in very small amounts in one specialized organ or group of cells and carried (sometimes in the bloodstream) to another organ or group of cells, in the same organism, upon which they have a specific regulatory action.

GO:0001991.name: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure by circulatory renin-angiotensin
GO:0001991.def: The process in which angiotensinogen metabolites in the bloodstream modulate the force with which blood passes through the circulatory system. The process begins when renin is released and cleaves angiotensinogen.
synonym: circulatory renin-angiotensin control of blood pressure
circulatory renin-angiotensin regulation of blood pressure
control of blood pressure by circulatory renin-angiotensin

GO:0001992.name: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure by vasopressin
GO:0001992.def: The regulation of blood pressure mediated by the signaling molecule vasopressin. Vasopressin is produced in the hypothalamus, and affects vasoconstriction, and renal water transport.

GO:0001999.name: renal response to blood flow involved in circulatory renin-angiotensin regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
GO:0001999.def: The physiological response of the kidneys to a decrease in blood flow.
GO:0001999.synonym: renal response to blood flow during renin-angiotensin control of blood pressure

GO:0002001.name: renin secretion into blood stream
GO:0002001.def: The regulated release of renin into the blood stream by juxtoglomerular cells.

GO:0002009.name: morphogenesis of an epithelium
GO:0002009.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of epithelia are generated and organized. An epithelium consists of closely packed cells arranged in one or more layers, that covers the outer surfaces of the body or lines any internal cavity or tube.

GO:0002011.name: morphogenesis of an epithelial sheet
GO:0002011.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of an epithelial sheet are generated and organized. An epithelial sheet is a flat surface consisting of closely packed epithelial cells.

GO:0002027.name: regulation of heart rate
GO:0002027.def: Any process that modulates the frequency or rate of heart contraction.
synonym: regulation of rate of heart contraction

GO:0002028.name: regulation of sodium ion transport
GO:0002028.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of sodium ions (Na+) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0002036.name: regulation of L-glutamate import across plasma membrane
GO:0002036.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of L-glutamate import into a cell.

GO:0002037.name: negative regulation of L-glutamate import across plasma membrane
GO:0002037.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of L-glutamate import into a cell.

GO:0002038.name: positive regulation of L-glutamate import across plasma membrane
GO:0002038.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of L-glutamate import into a cell.

GO:0002052.name: positive regulation of neuroblast proliferation
GO:0002052.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate of neuroblast proliferation.

GO:0002053.name: positive regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation
GO:0002053.def: The process of activating or increasing the rate or extent of mesenchymal cell proliferation. Mesenchymal cells are loosely organized embryonic cells.
synonym: up regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation

GO:0002062.name: chondrocyte differentiation
GO:0002062.def: The process in which a chondroblast acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a chondrocyte. A chondrocyte is a polymorphic cell that forms cartilage.

GO:0002063.name: chondrocyte development
GO:0002063.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a chondrocyte over time, from its commitment to its mature state. Chondrocyte development does not include the steps involved in committing a chondroblast to a chondrocyte fate.

GO:0002064.name: epithelial cell development
GO:0002064.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an epithelial cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface.

GO:0002065.name: columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0002065.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell. A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface. Columnar/cuboidal epithelial cells take on the shape of a column or cube.

GO:0002066.name: columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell development
GO:0002066.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface. Columnar/cuboidal epithelial cells take on the shape of a column or cube.

GO:0002067.name: glandular epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0002067.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a glandular epithelial cell. A glandular epithelial cell is a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface exposed to the lumen of a gland.

GO:0002068.name: glandular epithelial cell development
GO:0002068.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a glandular epithelial cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A glandular epithelial cell is a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface exposed to the lumen of a gland.

GO:0002069.name: columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell maturation
GO:0002069.def: The developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a columna/cuboidal epithelial cell to attain its fully functional state. A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface. Columnar/cuboidal epithelial cells take on the shape of a column or cube.

GO:0002070.name: epithelial cell maturation
GO:0002070.def: The developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for an epithelial cell to attain its fully functional state. An epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface.

GO:0002071.name: glandular epithelial cell maturation
GO:0002071.def: The developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a glandular epithelial cell to attain its fully functional state. A glandular epithelial cell is a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell is a cell found in a two dimensional sheet with a free surface exposed to the lumen of a gland.

GO:0002072.name: optic cup morphogenesis involved in camera-type eye development
GO:0002072.def: The invagination of the optic vesicle to form two-walled indentations, the optic cups, that will go on to form the retina. This process begins with the optic vesicle becoming a two-walled structure and its subsequent shape changes. It does not include the fate commitment of cells to become the pigmented retina and the neural retina. An example of this process is found in Mus musculus.
GO:0002072.synonym: optic cup morphogenesis involved in camera-style eye development

GO:0002076.name: osteoblast development
GO:0002076.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an osteoblast over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Osteoblast development does not include the steps involved in committing a cranial neural crest cell or an osteoprogenitor cell to an osteoblast fate. An osteoblast is a cell that gives rise to bone.

GO:0002080.name: acrosomal membrane
GO:0002080.def: The membrane that surrounds the acrosomal lumen. The acrosome is a special type of lysosome in the head of a spermatozoon that contains acid hydrolases and is concerned with the breakdown of the outer membrane of the ovum during fertilization.

GO:0002085.name: inhibition of neuroepithelial cell differentiation
GO:0002085.def: Any process that prevents the activation of neuroepithelial cell differentiation. Neuroepithelial cell differentiation is the process in which epiblast cells acquire specialized features of neuroepithelial cells.
synonym: negative regulation of neural plate formation
repression of premature neural plate formation

GO:0002087.name: regulation of respiratory gaseous exchange by nervous system process
GO:0002087.def: A process carried out by the nervous system that is required for the proper control of respiratory gaseous exchange. This process occurs in the respiratory center of the brain in vertebrates.
synonym: regulation of respiratory gaseous exchange by neurological system process

GO:0002088.name: lens development in camera-type eye
GO:0002088.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lens over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The lens is a transparent structure in the eye through which light is focused onto the retina. An example of this process is found in Mus musculus.

GO:0002089.name: lens morphogenesis in camera-type eye
GO:0002089.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the lens are generated and organized. The lens is a transparent structure in the eye through which light is focused onto the retina. An example of this process is found in Mus musculus.

GO:0002093.name: auditory receptor cell morphogenesis
GO:0002093.def: Any process that alters the size or shape of an auditory receptor cell.

GO:0002158.name: osteoclast proliferation
GO:0002158.def: The multiplication or reproduction of osteoclasts, resulting in the expansion of an osteoclast cell population. An osteoclast is a specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue, which typically differentiates from monocytes.

GO:0002164.name: larval development
GO:0002164.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the larva over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The larva is the early, immature form of an that at birth or hatching is fundamentally unlike its parent and must metamorphose before assuming the adult characters.

GO:0002165.name: instar larval or pupal development
GO:0002165.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the instar larva or pupa over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An example of this process is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0002176.name: male germ cell proliferation
GO:0002176.def: The multiplication or reproduction of male germ cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0002181.name: cytoplasmic translation
GO:0002181.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a protein in the cytoplasm. This is a ribosome-mediated process in which the information in messenger RNA (mRNA) is used to specify the sequence of amino acids in the protein.

GO:0002182.name: cytoplasmic translational elongation
GO:0002182.def: The successive addition of amino acid residues to a nascent polypeptide chain during protein biosynthesis in the cytoplasm.

GO:0002183.name: cytoplasmic translational initiation
GO:0002183.def: The process preceding formation of the peptide bond between the first two amino acids of a protein in the cytoplasm. This includes the formation of a complex of the ribosome, mRNA or circRNA, and an initiation complex that contains the first aminoacyl-tRNA.

GO:0002184.name: cytoplasmic translational termination
GO:0002184.def: The process resulting in the release of a polypeptide chain from the ribosome in the cytoplasm, usually in response to a termination codon.

GO:0002200.name: somatic diversification of immune receptors
GO:0002200.def: The somatic process allowing for the production of immune receptors whose specificity is not encoded in the germline genomic sequences.

GO:0002204.name: somatic recombination of immunoglobulin genes involved in immune response
GO:0002204.def: The process in which immunoglobulin genes are formed through recombination of the germline genetic elements, also known as immunoglobulin gene segments, within a single locus following the induction of and contributing to an immune response.
synonym: somatic recombination of antibody genes during immune response
somatic recombination of immunoglobulin genes during immune response

GO:0002208.name: somatic diversification of immunoglobulins involved in immune response
GO:0002208.def: The somatic process that results in the generation of sequence diversity of immunoglobulins after induction, and contributes to an immune response.
synonym: somatic diversification of antibodies during immune response
somatic diversification of immunoglobulins during immune response

GO:0002213.name: defense response to insect
GO:0002213.def: A response to protect an organism from a directly detected or perceived external threat from an insect or insects to that organism.

GO:0002215.name: defense response to nematode
GO:0002215.def: A response to protect an organism from a directly detected or perceived external threat from a nematode or nematodes, which results in restriction of damage to the organism attacked or prevention/recovery from the infection caused by the attack.

GO:0002225.name: positive regulation of antimicrobial peptide production
GO:0002225.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of antimicrobial peptide production.
synonym: up regulation of antimicrobial peptide production

GO:0002227.name: innate immune response in mucosa
GO:0002227.def: Any process of the innate immune response that takes place in the mucosal tissues.

GO:0002228.name: natural killer cell mediated immunity
GO:0002228.def: The promotion of an immune response by natural killer cells through direct recognition of target cells or through the release of cytokines.

GO:0002232.name: leukocyte chemotaxis involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002232.def: The movement of an immune cell in response to an external stimulus contributing to an inflammatory response.
synonym: immune cell chemotaxis during inflammatory response

GO:0002233.name: leukocyte chemotaxis involved in immune response
GO:0002233.def: The movement of an immune cell in response to an external stimulus a part of an immune response.
synonym: immune cell chemotaxis during immune response

GO:0002244.name: hematopoietic progenitor cell differentiation
GO:0002244.def: The process in which precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a hematopoietic progenitor cell, a class of cell types including myeloid progenitor cells and lymphoid progenitor cells.

GO:0002246.name: wound healing involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002246.def: The series of events that restore integrity to damaged tissue that contribute to an inflammatory response.

GO:0002249.name: lymphocyte anergy
GO:0002249.def: Any process contributing to lymphocyte anergy, a state of functional inactivation.

GO:0002250.name: adaptive immune response
GO:0002250.def: An immune response mediated by cells expressing specific receptors for antigens produced through a somatic diversification process, and allowing for an enhanced secondary response to subsequent exposures to the same antigen (immunological memory).

GO:0002251.name: organ or tissue specific immune response
GO:0002251.def: An immune response taking place in an organ or tissues such as the liver, brain, mucosa, or nervous system tissues.
GO:0002251.synonym: immune response in organ or tissue

GO:0002252.name: immune effector process
GO:0002252.def: Any process of the immune system that executes a component of an immune response. An effector immune process takes place after its activation.

GO:0002260.name: lymphocyte homeostasis
GO:0002260.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of lymphocytes such that the total number of lymphocytes within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0002262.name: myeloid cell homeostasis
GO:0002262.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of myeloid cells such that the total number of myeloid cells within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0002263.name: cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002263.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002264.name: endothelial cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002264.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of an endothelial cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002264.synonym: endothelial cell activation during immune response

GO:0002265.name: astrocyte activation involved in immune response
GO:0002265.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of an astrocyte resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002266.name: follicular dendritic cell activation
GO:0002266.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a follicular dendritic cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand.

GO:0002267.name: follicular dendritic cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002267.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a follicular dendritic cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002267.synonym: follicular dendritic cell activation during immune response

GO:0002268.name: follicular dendritic cell differentiation
GO:0002268.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a follicular dendritic cell.

GO:0002269.name: leukocyte activation involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002269.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a leukocyte resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an inflammatory response.
synonym: immune cell activation during inflammatory response

GO:0002270.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell activation
GO:0002270.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a plasmacytoid dendritic cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand.

GO:0002271.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002271.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a plasmacytoid dendritic cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002271.synonym: plasmacytoid dendritic cell activation during immune response

GO:0002272.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002272.def: The process in which an immature plasmacytoid dendritic cell acquires the specialized features of a mature plasmacytoid dendritic cell contributing to an immune response.
GO:0002272.synonym: plasmacytoid dendritic cell differentiation during immune response

GO:0002273.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell differentiation
GO:0002273.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized hemopoietic precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a plasmacytoid dendritic cell.

GO:0002274.name: myeloid leukocyte activation
GO:0002274.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a myeloid leukocyte resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand.

GO:0002275.name: myeloid cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002275.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a myeloid cell resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002275.synonym: myeloid cell activation during immune response

GO:0002276.name: basophil activation involved in immune response
GO:0002276.def: A change in morphology and behavior of a basophil resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, soluble factor, or to (at least in mammals) an antigen which the basophil has specifically bound via IgE bound to Fc-epsilonRI receptors, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002277.name: myeloid dendritic cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002277.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a myeloid dendritic cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002277.synonym: myeloid dendritic cell activation during immune response

GO:0002278.name: eosinophil activation involved in immune response
GO:0002278.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a eosinophil resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002279.name: mast cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002279.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a mast cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, soluble factor, or to (at least in mammals) an antigen which the mast cell has specifically bound via IgE bound to Fc-epsilonRI receptors, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002279.synonym: mast cell activation during immune response

GO:0002280.name: monocyte activation involved in immune response
GO:0002280.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a monocyte resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002281.name: macrophage activation involved in immune response
GO:0002281.def: A change in morphology and behavior of a macrophage resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
synonym: macrophage polarization involved in immune response

GO:0002282.name: microglial cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002282.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a microglial cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
GO:0002282.synonym: microglial cell activation during immune response

GO:0002283.name: neutrophil activation involved in immune response
GO:0002283.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a neutrophil resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002284.name: myeloid dendritic cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002284.def: The process in which an immature myeloid dendritic cell acquires the specialized features of a mature myeloid dendritic cell as part of an immune response.
GO:0002284.synonym: myeloid dendritic cell differentiation during immune response

GO:0002285.name: lymphocyte activation involved in immune response
GO:0002285.def: A change in morphology and behavior of a lymphocyte resulting from exposure to a specific antigen, mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002286.name: T cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002286.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a mature or immature T cell resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002287.def: The change in morphology and behavior of an alpha-beta T cell resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002290.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a gamma-delta T cell resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.

GO:0002292.name: T cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002292.def: The process in which an antigenically naive T cell acquires the specialized features of an effector, regulatory, or memory T cell as part of an immune response. Effector T cells include cells which provide T cell help or exhibit cytotoxicity towards other cells.
synonym: T cell development involved in immune response
T cell differentiation during immune response
T lymphocyte differentiation during immune response

GO:0002293.name: alpha-beta T cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002293.def: The process in which an antigenically naive alpha-beta T cell acquires the specialized features of an effector, regulatory, or memory T cell during an immune response. Effector T cells include cells which provide T cell help or exhibit cytotoxicity towards other cells.
synonym: alpha-beta T cell development involved in immune response

alpha-beta T lymphocyte differentiation during immune response

GO:0002294.def: The process in which an antigenically naive CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell acquires the specialized features of an effector, regulatory, or memory T cell as part of an immune response. synonym: CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell development involved in immune response

GO:0002298.name: CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002298.def: The process in which an antigenically naive CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell acquires the specialized features of a CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell as part of an immune response.
synonym: CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell differentiation during immune response
CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T lymphocyte differentiation during immune response
CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T-cell differentiation during immune response
CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T-lymphocyte differentiation during immune response
CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta T cell development involved in immune response

GO:0002299.name: alpha-beta intraepithelial T cell differentiation
GO:0002299.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of an alpha-beta intraepithelial T cell. Intraepithelial T cells are found among epithelial cells in mucosal areas and have distinct phenotypes and developmental pathways.

GO:0002300.name: CD8-positive, alpha-beta intraepithelial T cell differentiation
GO:0002300.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a CD8-positive, alpha-beta intraepithelial T cell. Intraepithelial T cells are found among epithelial cells in mucosal areas and have distinct phenotypes and developmental pathways.
synonym: CD8-positive, alpha-beta intraepithelial T cell development
CD8-positive, alpha-beta intraepithelial T lymphocyte differentiation
