GO:0002312.name: B cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002312.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a mature or immature B cell during an immune response, resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.
synonym: B cell activation during immune response
B lymphocyte activation during immune response

GO:0002313.name: mature B cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002313.def: The process in which a naive B cell acquires the specialized features of a mature or memory B cell during an immune response.
synonym: mature B cell development involved in immune response
mature B cell differentiation during immune response
mature B lymphocyte differentiation during immune response
mature B-cell differentiation during immune response
mature B-lymphocyte differentiation during immune response

GO:0002314.name: germinal center B cell differentiation
GO:0002314.def: The process in which a B cell in the spleen acquires the specialized features of a germinal center B cell. Germinal center B cells are rapidly cycling B cells which have downregulated IgD expression and exhibit high levels of binding by peanut agglutinin (PNA).

GO:0002315.name: marginal zone B cell differentiation
GO:0002315.def: The process in which a B cell in the spleen acquires the specialized features of a marginal zone B cell. Marginal zone B cells are localized in a distinct anatomical region of the spleen that represents the major antigen-filtering and scavenging area (by specialized macrophages resident there). It appears that they are preselected to express a BCR repertoire similar to B-1 B cells, biased toward bacterial cell wall constituents and senescent self-components (such as oxidized LDL).

GO:0002316.name: follicular B cell differentiation
GO:0002316.def: The process in which a B cell in the spleen acquires the specialized features of a follicular B cell. Follicular B cells are major population of mature recirculating B cells in the spleen and are located in the B-cell follicle region.

GO:0002317.name: plasma cell differentiation
GO:0002317.def: The process in which a B cell acquires the specialized features of a plasma cell. A plasma cell is a lymphocyte which develops from a B cell and produces high amounts of antibody.

GO:0002318.name: myeloid progenitor cell differentiation
GO:0002318.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a myeloid progenitor cell. Myeloid progenitor cells include progenitor cells for any of the myeloid lineages.

GO:0002319.name: memory B cell differentiation
GO:0002319.def: The process in which a B cell acquires the specialized features of a memory B cell. Memory B cells are cells that can respond rapidly to antigen re-exposure by production of high-affinity antibody.

GO:0002320.name: lymphoid progenitor cell differentiation
GO:0002320.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a lymphoid progenitor cell. Lymphoid progenitor cells include progenitor cells for any of the lymphoid lineages.

GO:0002321.name: natural killer cell progenitor differentiation
GO:0002321.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a natural killer cell progenitor.

GO:0002322.name: B cell proliferation involved in immune response
GO:0002322.def: The expansion of a B cell population by cell division following B cell activation during an immune response.
synonym: B cell proliferation during immune response
B lymphocyte proliferation during immune response

GO:0002323.name: natural killer cell activation involved in immune response
GO:0002323.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a natural killer cell resulting from exposure a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
synonym: natural killer cell activation during immune response
NK cell activation during immune response

GO:0002324.name: natural killer cell proliferation involved in immune response
GO:0002324.def: The expansion of a natural killer cell population by cell division as part of an immune response.
synonym: natural killer cell proliferation during immune response
NK cell proliferation during immune response

GO:0002325.name: natural killer cell differentiation involved in immune response
GO:0002325.def: The process in which a naive natural killer cell acquires the specialized features of an effector natural killer T cell as part of an immune response.
synonym: natural killer cell development involved in immune response
natural killer cell differentiation during immune response
NK cell differentiation during immune response

GO:0002327.name: immature B cell differentiation
GO:0002327.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of an immature B cell.

GO:0002328.name: pro-B cell differentiation
GO:0002328.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a pro-B cell. Pro-B cells are the earliest stage of the B cell lineage and undergo heavy chain D and J gene rearrangements, although they are not fully committed.

GO:0002329.name: pre-B cell differentiation
GO:0002329.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a pre-B cell. Pre-B cells follow the pro-B cell stage of immature B cell differentiation and undergo rearrangement of heavy chain V, D, and J gene segments.

GO:0002332.name: transitional stage B cell differentiation
GO:0002332.def: The process in which immature B cells from the bone marrow become mature B cells in the spleen. Transitional stage B cells are subdivided into transitional one (T1) and transitional two (T2) stages and are short-lived and functionally incompetent.

GO:0002335.name: mature B cell differentiation
GO:0002335.def: The process in which transitional stage B cells acquire the specialized features of mature B cells in the spleen.

GO:0002337.name: B-1a B cell differentiation
GO:0002337.def: The process in which B cells acquire the specialized features of B-1a B cells. B-1a B cells are B-1 cells that express CD5 and arise from fetal liver precursors.

GO:0002338.name: B-1b B cell differentiation
GO:0002338.def: The process in which B cells acquire the specialized features of B-1b B cells. B-1b B cells are B-1 cells that do not express CD5.

GO:0002339.name: B cell selection
GO:0002339.def: The process dependent upon B cell antigen receptor signaling in response to self or foreign antigen through which B cells are selected for survival.

GO:0002343.name: peripheral B cell selection
GO:0002343.def: Any B cell selection process that occurs in the periphery.

GO:0002344.name: B cell affinity maturation
GO:0002344.def: The process in which B cells produce antibodies with increased antigen affinity. This is accomplished by somatic hypermutation and selection for B cells which produce higher affinity antibodies to antigen.

GO:0002349.name: histamine production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002349.def: The synthesis or release of histamine following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
GO:0002349.synonym: histamine production involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002351.name: serotonin production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002351.def: The synthesis or release of serotonin following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
GO:0002351.synonym: serotonin production involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002358.name: B cell homeostatic proliferation
GO:0002358.def: The non-specific expansion of B cell populations within a whole or part of an organism to reach to a total number of B cells which will then remain stable over time in the absence of an external stimulus.

GO:0002359.name: B-1 B cell proliferation
GO:0002359.def: The expansion of a B-1 B cell by cell division. Follows B cell activation.

GO:0002361.name: CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell differentiation
GO:0002361.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell.
synonym: CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T cell development

CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T-cell differentiation
CD4-positive, CD25-positive, alpha-beta regulatory T-lymphocyte differentiation

GO:0002366.name: leukocyte activation involved in immune response
GO:0002366.def: A change in morphology and behavior of a leukocyte resulting from exposure to a specific antigen, mitogen, cytokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor, leading to the initiation or perpetuation of an immune response.
synonym: immune cell activation during immune response

GO:0002367.name: cytokine production involved in immune response
GO:0002367.def: The appearance of a cytokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus contributing to an immune response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
synonym: cytokine biosynthetic process involved in immune response
cytokine secretion involved in immune response

GO:0002368.name: B cell cytokine production
GO:0002368.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a B cell.

GO:0002369.name: T cell cytokine production
GO:0002369.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a T cell.

GO:0002370.name: natural killer cell cytokine production
GO:0002370.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a natural killer cell.

GO:0002371.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a dendritic cell.

GO:0002372.name: myeloid dendritic cell cytokine production
GO:0002372.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a myeloid dendritic cell.

GO:0002373.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell cytokine production
GO:0002373.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a plasmacytoid dendritic cell.

GO:0002376.name: immune system process
GO:0002376.def: Any process involved in the development or functioning of the immune system, an organismal system for calibrated responses to potential internal or invasive threats.

GO:0002377.name: immunoglobulin production
GO:0002377.def: The appearance of immunoglobulin due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0002381.name: immunoglobulin production involved in immunoglobulin-mediated immune response
GO:0002381.def: The appearance of immunoglobulin due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus during an immune response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
synonym: immunoglobulin biosynthetic process involved in immune response

GO:0002384.name: hepatic immune response
GO:0002384.def: An immune response taking place in the liver.

GO:0002385.name: mucosal immune response
GO:0002385.def: An immune response taking place in mucosal tissues, including those of the intestinal tract, nasal and upper respiratory tract, and genital tract.
synonym: immune response in mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue

GO:0002387.name: immune response in gut-associated lymphoid tissue
GO:0002387.def: Immune response taking place in the gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT). GALT includes Peyer's patches, appendix, and solitary lymph nodules.

GO:0002388.name: immune response in Peyer's patch
GO:0002388.def: Immune response taking place in the Peyer's patch, nodular lymphoid structures on the serosal surface of the small intestine.

GO:0002389.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the Peyer's patches.

GO:0002394.name: tolerance induction in gut-associated lymphoid tissue
GO:0002394.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT).

GO:0002395.name: immune response in nasopharyngeal-associated lymphoid tissue
GO:0002395.def: An immune response taking place in the nasopharyngeal-associated lymphoid tissue (NALT). NALT includes the tonsils and adenoids.

GO:0002396.name: MHC protein complex assembly
GO:0002396.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form an MHC protein complex.

GO:0002399.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form an MHC class II protein complex.

GO:0002400.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the nasopharyngeal-associated lymphoid tissue (NALT).

GO:0002401.name: tolerance induction in mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue
GO:0002401.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT).

GO:0002402.name: B cell tolerance induction in mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue
GO:0002402.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) mediated by B cells.
GO:0002402.synonym: B cell tolerance induction in MALT

GO:0002403.name: T cell tolerance induction in mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue
GO:0002403.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) mediated by T cells.
GO:0002403.synonym: T cell tolerance induction in MALT

GO:0002407.name: dendritic cell chemotaxis
GO:0002407.def: The movement of a dendritic cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0002408.name: myeloid dendritic cell chemotaxis
GO:0002408.def: The movement of a myeloid dendritic cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0002409.name: Langerhans cell chemotaxis
GO:0002409.def: The movement of a Langerhans cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0002410.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell chemotaxis
GO:0002410.def: The movement of a plasmacytoid dendritic cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0002427.name: mucosal tolerance induction
GO:0002427.def: Tolerance induction taking place in the mucosal tissues.

GO:0002432.name: granuloma formation
GO:0002432.def: The formation of nodular inflammatory lesions, usually small or granular, firm, persistent, well-structured, and containing compactly grouped T lymphocytes and modified phagocytes such as epithelioid cells, giant cells, and other macrophages. Granuloma formation represents a chronic inflammatory response initiated by various infectious and noninfectious agents. The center of a granuloma consists of fused macrophages, which can become necrotic.

GO:0002440.name: production of molecular mediator of immune response
GO:0002440.def: The synthesis or release of any molecular mediator of the immune response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
GO:0002440.synonym: production of cellular mediator of immune response

GO:0002441.name: histamine secretion involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002441.def: The regulated release of histamine by a cell as part of an inflammatory response.

GO:0002444.def: Any process involved in the carrying out of an immune response by a myeloid leukocyte.

GO:0002446.name: neutrophil mediated immunity

GO:0002447.name: eosinophil mediated immunity
GO:0002447.def: Any process involved in the carrying out of an immune response by an eosinophil.

GO:0002448.def: Any process involved in the carrying out of an immune response by a mast cell.

GO:0002449.name: lymphocyte mediated immunity
GO:0002449.def: Any process involved in the carrying out of an immune response by a lymphocyte.

GO:0002450.name: B cell antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002450.def: The process in which a B cell expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.
synonym: B lymphocyte antigen processing and presentation

GO:0002451.name: peripheral B cell tolerance induction
GO:0002451.def: Tolerance induction of mature B cells in the peripheral lymphoid tissues: the blood, lymph nodes, spleen, and mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue.

GO:0002456.name: T cell mediated immunity
GO:0002456.def: Any process involved in the carrying out of an immune response by a T cell.

GO:0002457.name: T cell antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002457.def: The process in which a T cell expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.
synonym: T lymphocyte antigen processing and presentation

GO:0002458.name: peripheral T cell tolerance induction
GO:0002458.def: Tolerance induction of T cells in the periphery, in this case, any location in the body other than the thymus.

GO:0002460.name: adaptive immune response based on somatic recombination of immune receptors built from immunoglobulin superfamily domains
GO:0002460.def: An immune response mediated by lymphocytes expressing specific receptors for antigen produced through a somatic diversification process that includes somatic recombination of germline gene segments encoding immunoglobulin superfamily domains. Recombined receptors for antigen encoded by immunoglobulin superfamily domains include T cell receptors and immunoglobulins (antibodies) produced by B cells. The first encounter with antigen elicits a primary immune response that is slow and not of great magnitude. T and B cells selected by antigen become activated and undergo clonal expansion. A fraction of antigen-reactive T and B cells become memory cells, whereas others differentiate into effector cells. The memory cells generated during the primary response enable a much faster and stronger secondary immune response upon subsequent exposures to the same antigen (immunological memory). An example of this is the adaptive immune response found in Mus musculus.

GO:0002461.name: tolerance induction dependent upon immune response
GO:0002461.def: Tolerance induction dependent upon an immune response, typically a response by a mature T or B cell in the periphery resulting tolerance towards an antigen via induction of anergy, cellular deletion, or regulatory T cell activation.

GO:0002462.name: tolerance induction to nonself antigen
GO:0002462.def: Tolerance induction in response to nonself antigens.

GO:0002465.name: peripheral tolerance induction
GO:0002465.def: Tolerance induction in the peripheral lymphoid tissues: blood, lymph nodes, spleen, and mucosal-associated lymphoid tissues.

GO:0002467.name: germinal center formation
GO:0002467.def: The process in which germinal centers form. A germinal center is a specialized microenvironment formed when activated B cells enter lymphoid follicles. Germinal centers are the foci for B cell proliferation and somatic hypermutation.

GO:0002468.name: dendritic cell antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002468.def: The process in which a dendritic cell expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.

GO:0002469.name: myeloid dendritic cell antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002469.def: The process in which a myeloid dendritic cell expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.

GO:0002470.name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002470.def: The process in which a plasmacytoid dendritic cell expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.

GO:0002471.name: monocyte antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002471.def: The process in which a monocyte expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.

GO:0002472.name: macrophage antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002472.def: The process in which a macrophage expresses antigen (peptide or lipid) on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex.

GO:0002474.name: antigen processing and presentation of peptide antigen via MHC class I
GO:0002474.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses a peptide antigen on its cell surface in association with an MHC class I protein complex. Class I here refers to classical class I molecules.
GO:0002474.synonym: peptide antigen processing and presentation via MHC class I

GO:0002478.name: antigen processing and presentation of exogenous peptide antigen
GO:0002478.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses a peptide antigen of exogenous origin on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex. The peptide is typically a fragment of a larger exogenous protein which has been degraded within the cell.
GO:0002478.synonym: exogenous peptide antigen processing and presentation

GO:0002483.name: antigen processing and presentation of endogenous peptide antigen
GO:0002483.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses a peptide antigen of endogenous origin on its cell surface in association with an MHC protein complex. The peptide is typically a fragment of a larger endogenous protein which has been degraded within the cell.
GO:0002483.synonym: endogenous peptide antigen processing and presentation

GO:0002491.name: antigen processing and presentation of endogenous peptide antigen via MHC class II
GO:0002491.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses a peptide antigen of endogenous origin on its cell surface in association with an MHC class II protein complex. The peptide antigen is typically, but not always, processed from a whole protein.
GO:0002491.synonym: endogenous peptide antigen processing and presentation via MHC class II

GO:0002495.name: antigen processing and presentation of peptide antigen via MHC class II
GO:0002495.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses a peptide antigen on its cell surface in association with an MHC class II protein complex. The peptide antigen is typically, but not always, processed from a whole protein.
GO:0002495.synonym: peptide antigen processing and presentation via MHC class II

GO:0002496.name: proteolysis associated with antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002496.def: The hydrolysis of a peptide bond or bonds within a protein contributing to antigen processing and presentation.

GO:0002500.name: proteolysis within lysosome associated with antigen processing and presentation
GO:0002500.def: The hydrolysis of a peptide bond or bonds within a protein by lysosomal resident proteases contributing to antigen processing and presentation.
GO:0002500.synonym: lysosomal proteolysis associated with antigen processing and presentation

GO:0002504.name: antigen processing and presentation of peptide or polysaccharide antigen via MHC class II
GO:0002504.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses antigen (peptide or polysaccharide) on its cell surface in association with an MHC class II protein complex.
GO:0002504.synonym: peptide or polysaccharide antigen processing and presentation of via MHC class II

GO:0002507.name: tolerance induction
GO:0002507.def: A process that directly activates any of the steps required for tolerance, a physiologic state in which the immune system does not react destructively against the components of an organism that harbors it or against antigens that are introduced to it.

GO:0002514.name: B cell tolerance induction
GO:0002514.def: A process involving any mechanism for tolerance induction in B cells.

GO:0002515.name: B cell anergy
GO:0002515.def: Any process contributing to anergy in B cells, a state of functional inactivation which is part of B cell tolerance induction.

GO:0002516.name: B cell deletion
GO:0002516.def: The apoptotic death of B cells which is part of B cell tolerance induction.

GO:0002517.name: T cell tolerance induction
GO:0002517.def: A process involving any mechanism for tolerance induction in T cells.

GO:0002519.name: natural killer cell tolerance induction
GO:0002519.def: Tolerance induction of natural killer cells.

GO:0002520.name: immune system development
GO:0002520.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an organismal system whose objective is to provide calibrated responses by an organism to a potential internal or invasive threat, over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A system is a regularly interacting or interdependent group of organs or tissues that work together to carry out a given biological process.

GO:0002521.name: leukocyte differentiation
GO:0002521.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized hemopoietic precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a leukocyte. A leukocyte is an achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages capable of ameboid movement, found in blood or other tissue.

GO:0002522.name: leukocyte migration involved in immune response
GO:0002522.def: The movement of a leukocyte within or between different tissues and organs of the body as part of an immune response.
synonym: immune cell migration during immune response
immune cell trafficking during immune response

GO:0002523.name: leukocyte migration involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002523.def: The movement of a leukocyte within or between different tissues and organs of the body contributing to an inflammatory response.
synonym: immune cell migration during inflammatory response
immune cell trafficking during inflammatory response

GO:0002526.name: acute inflammatory response
GO:0002526.def: Inflammation which comprises a rapid, short-lived, relatively uniform response to acute injury or antigenic challenge and is characterized by accumulations of fluid, plasma proteins, and granulocytic leukocytes. An acute inflammatory response occurs within a matter of minutes or hours, and either resolves within a few days or becomes a chronic inflammatory response.

GO:0002528.name: regulation of vascular permeability involved in acute inflammatory response
GO:0002528.def: Any process that modulates the extent to which blood vessels can be pervaded by fluid contributing to an acute inflammatory response.
GO:0002528.synonym: regulation of vascular permeability during acute inflammatory response

GO:0002532.name: production of molecular mediator involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002532.def: The synthesis or release of any molecular mediator of the inflammatory response following an inflammatory stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
synonym: production of cellular mediator of acute inflammation
production of molecular mediator involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002534.name: cytokine production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002534.def: The synthesis or release of a cytokine following a inflammatory stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
GO:0002534.synonym: cytokine production involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002536.name: respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002536.def: A phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals, resulting in an increase in their intracellular or extracellular levels.
synonym: oxidative burst during acute inflammatory response
production of reactive oxygen species during acute inflammatory response
respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002537.name: nitric oxide production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002537.def: The synthesis or release of nitric oxide following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
synonym: nitric oxide production involved in acute inflammatory response
production of nitric oxide involved in acute inflammatory response
production of nitric oxide involved in inflammatory response

GO:0002538.name: arachidonate metabolite production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002538.def: The synthesis or release of products of arachidonic acid metabolism following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in their intracellular or extracellular levels.
synonym: arachidonic acid metabolite production involved in acute inflammatory response
arachidonic acid metabolite production involved in inflammatory response
production of arachidonic acid metabolites involved in acute inflammatory response
production of arachidonic acid metabolites involved in inflammatory response

GO:0002539.name: prostaglandin production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002539.def: The synthesis or release of any prostaglandin following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
GO:0002539.synonym: prostaglandin production involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002540.name: leukotriene production involved in inflammatory response
GO:0002540.def: The synthesis or release of any leukotriene following a stimulus as part of an inflammatory response, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.
GO:0002540.synonym: leukotriene production involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0002544.name: chronic inflammatory response
GO:0002544.def: Inflammation of prolonged duration (weeks or months) in which active inflammation, tissue destruction, and attempts at repair are proceeding simultaneously. Although it may follow acute inflammation, chronic inflammation frequently begins insidiously, as a low-grade, smoldering, often asymptomatic response.

GO:0002574.name: thrombocyte differentiation

GO:0002932.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a tendon sheath over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A tendon sheath is a layer of membrane around a tendon. It permits the tendon to move.

GO:0003002.name: regionalization

GO:0003006.name: developmental process involved in reproduction
GO:0003006.def: A developmental process in which a progressive change in the state of some part of an organism, germline or somatic, specifically contributes to its ability to form offspring.

GO:0003007.name: heart morphogenesis
GO:0003007.def: The developmental process in which the heart is generated and organized. The heart is a hollow, muscular organ, which, by contracting rhythmically, keeps up the circulation of the blood.

GO:0003008.name: system process
GO:0003008.def: A multicellular organismal process carried out by any of the organs or tissues in an organ system. An organ system is a regularly interacting or interdependent group of organs or tissues that work together to carry out a biological objective.

GO:0003009.name: skeletal muscle contraction
GO:0003009.def: A process in which force is generated within skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. In the skeletal muscle, the muscle contraction takes advantage of an ordered sarcomeric structure and in most cases it is under voluntary control.

GO:0003012.name: muscle system process
GO:0003012.def: An organ system process carried out at the level of a muscle. Muscle tissue is composed of contractile cells or fibers.

GO:0003013.name: circulatory system process
GO:0003013.def: An organ system process carried out by any of the organs or tissues of the circulatory system. The circulatory system is an organ system that moves extracellular fluids to and from tissue within a multicellular organism.

GO:0003014.name: renal system process
GO:0003014.def: An organ system process carried out by any of the organs or tissues of the renal system. The renal system maintains fluid balance, and contributes to electrolyte balance, acid/base balance, and disposal of nitrogenous waste products. In humans, the renal system comprises a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, urinary bladder, urethra, sphincter muscle and associated blood vessels; in other species, the renal system may comprise related structures (e.g., nephrocytes and malpighian tubules in Drosophila).

GO:0003015.name: heart process
GO:0003015.def: A circulatory system process carried out by the heart. The heart is a hollow, muscular organ, which, by contracting rhythmically, keeps up the circulation of the blood. The heart is a hollow, muscular organ, which, by contracting rhythmically, keeps up the circulation of the blood.

GO:0003016.name: respiratory system process
GO:0003016.def: A process carried out by the organs or tissues of the respiratory system. The respiratory system is an organ system responsible for respiratory gaseous exchange.

GO:0003018.name: vascular process in circulatory system
GO:0003018.def: A circulatory process that occurs at the level of the vasculature.

GO:0003032.name: detection of oxygen
GO:0003032.def: The series of events in which an oxygen stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0003044.name: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure mediated by a chemical signal
GO:0003044.def: The regulation of blood pressure mediated by biochemical signaling: hormonal, autocrine or paracrine.
GO:0003044.synonym: blood pressure regulation mediated by a chemical signal

GO:0003071.name: renal system process involved in regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
GO:0003071.def: Renal process that modulates the force with which blood travels through the circulatory system. The process is controlled by a balance of processes that increase pressure and decrease pressure.
synonym: renal regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure

GO:0003073.name: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure
GO:0003073.def: The process that modulates the force with which blood travels through the systemic arterial circulatory system. The process is controlled by a balance of processes that increase pressure and decrease pressure.

GO:0003081.name: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure by renin-angiotensin
GO:0003081.def: The process in which renin-angiotensin modulates the force with which blood passes through the circulatory system.

GO:0003091.name: renal water homeostasis
GO:0003091.def: Renal process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of water in the body.
GO:0003091.synonym: water homeostasis by the renal system

GO:0003093.name: regulation of glomerular filtration
GO:0003093.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glomerular filtration. Glomerular filtration is the process in which blood is filtered by the glomerulus into the renal tubule.

GO:0003094.name: glomerular filtration
GO:0003094.def: The process in which plasma is filtered through the glomerular membrane which consists of capillary endothelial cells, the basement membrane, and epithelial cells. The glomerular filtrate is the same as plasma except it has no significant amount of protein.

GO:0003096.name: renal sodium ion transport
GO:0003096.def: The directed movement of sodium ions (Na+) by the renal system.

GO:0003097.name: renal water transport
GO:0003097.def: The directed movement of water (H2O) by the renal system.

GO:0003104.name: positive regulation of glomerular filtration
GO:0003104.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of glomerular filtration. Glomerular filtration is the process whereby blood is filtered by the glomerulus into the renal tubule.

GO:0003105.name: negative regulation of glomerular filtration
GO:0003105.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of glomerular filtration. Glomerular filtration is the process whereby blood is filtered by the glomerulus into the renal tubule.

GO:0003131.name: mesodermal-endodermal cell signaling
GO:0003131.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from mesodermal cells to endodermal cells.

GO:0003133.name: endodermal-mesodermal cell signaling
GO:0003133.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from endodermal cells to mesodermal cells.

GO:0003142.name: cardiogenic plate morphogenesis
GO:0003142.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the cardiogenic plate are generated and organized. The cardiogenic plate is the first recognizable structure derived from the heart field.

GO:0003143.name: embryonic heart tube morphogenesis
GO:0003143.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the embryonic heart tube are generated and organized. The embryonic heart tube is an epithelial tube that will give rise to the mature heart.

GO:0003144.name: embryonic heart tube formation
GO:0003144.def: The process that gives rise to the embryonic heart tube. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts. The embryonic heart tube is an epithelial tube that will give rise to the mature heart.

GO:0003145.name: embryonic heart tube formation via epithelial folding
GO:0003145.def: The process that gives rise to the embryonic heart tube by the cells of the heart field along a linear axis.

GO:0003147.name: neural crest cell migration involved in heart formation
GO:0003147.def: The characteristic movement of a cell from the dorsal ridge of the neural tube towards the heart and that contributes to heart formation.

GO:0003148.name: outflow tract septum morphogenesis
GO:0003148.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the outflow tract septum are generated and organized. The outflow tract septum is a partition in the outflow tract.

GO:0003149.name: membranous septum morphogenesis
GO:0003149.def: The process in which the membranous septum is generated and organized. The membranous septum is the upper part of ventricular septum.

GO:0003150.name: muscular septum morphogenesis
GO:0003150.def: The process in which the muscular septum is generated and organized. The muscular septum is the lower part of the ventricular septum.

GO:0003151.name: outflow tract morphogenesis
GO:0003151.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the outflow tract are generated and organized. The outflow tract is the portion of the heart through which blood flows into the arteries.

GO:0003152.name: morphogenesis of an epithelial fold involved in embryonic heart tube formation
GO:0003152.def: The morphogenetic process in which an epithelial sheet bends along a linear axis, contributing to embryonic heart tube formation.

GO:0003156.name: regulation of animal organ formation
GO:0003156.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of animal organ formation. Organ formation is the process pertaining to the initial formation of an organ from unspecified parts. The process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the discrete structure, such as inductive events, and ends when the structural rudiment of the organ is recognizable, such as a condensation of mesenchymal cells into the organ rudiment.

GO:0003157.name: endocardium development
GO:0003157.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the endocardium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The endocardium is an anatomical structure comprised of an endothelium and an extracellular matrix that forms the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.

GO:0003158.name: endothelium development
GO:0003158.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an endothelium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Endothelium refers to the layer of cells lining blood vessels, lymphatics, the heart, and serous cavities, and is derived from bone marrow or mesoderm. Corneal endothelium is a special case, derived from neural crest cells.

GO:0003159.name: morphogenesis of an endothelium
GO:0003159.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of an endothelium is generated and organized. Endothelium refers to the layer of cells lining blood vessels, lymphatics, the heart, and serous cavities, and is derived from bone marrow or mesoderm. Corneal endothelium is a special case, derived from neural crest cells.

GO:0003160.name: endocardium morphogenesis
GO:0003160.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of the endocardium is generated and organized. The endocardium is an anatomical structure comprised of an endothelium and an extracellular matrix that forms the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.

GO:0003161.name: cardiac conduction system development
GO:0003161.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cardiac conduction system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The cardiac conduction system consists of specialized cardiomyocytes that regulate the frequency of heart beat.

GO:0003162.name: atrioventricular node development
GO:0003162.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the atrioventricular (AV) node over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The AV node is part of the cardiac conduction system that controls the timing of ventricle contraction by receiving electrical signals from the sinoatrial (SA) node and relaying them to the His-Purkinje system.

GO:0003163.name: sinoatrial node development
GO:0003163.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the sinoatrial (SA) node over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The SA node is part of the cardiac conduction system that controls the timing of heart muscle contraction. It relays electrical signals to the AV node.

GO:0003164.name: His-Purkinje system development
GO:0003164.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the His-Purkinje system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The His-Purkinje system receives signals from the AV node and is composed of the fibers that regulate cardiac muscle contraction in the ventricles.

GO:0003165.name: Purkinje myocyte development
GO:0003165.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a Purkinje myocyte over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The Purkinje myocyte (also known as cardiac Purkinje fiber) is part of the cardiac conduction system that receives signals from the bundle of His and innervates the ventricular cardiac muscle.

GO:0003166.name: bundle of His development
GO:0003166.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the bundle of His over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The bundle of His is part of the His-Purkinje system that transmits signals from the AV node to the cardiac Purkinje fibers.

GO:0003167.name: atrioventricular bundle cell differentiation
GO:0003167.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cell of the atrioventricular bundle. These cells are specialized cardiomyocytes that transmit signals from the AV node to the cardiac Purkinje fibers.

GO:0003168.name: Purkinje myocyte differentiation
GO:0003168.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a Purkinje myocyte (also known as cardiac Purkinje fiber cell). These cells are specialized cardiomyocytes that receive signals from the bundle of His and innervate the ventricular cardiac muscle.

GO:0003169.name: coronary vein morphogenesis
GO:0003169.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of veins of the heart are generated and organized.

GO:0003170.name: heart valve development
GO:0003170.def: The progression of a heart valve over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A heart valve is a structure that restricts the flow of blood to different regions of the heart and forms from an endocardial cushion.

GO:0003179.name: heart valve morphogenesis
GO:0003179.def: The process in which the structure of a heart valve is generated and organized.

GO:0003188.name: heart valve formation
GO:0003188.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a heart valve from unspecified parts. This process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the discrete structure and ends when the structural rudiment is recognizable.

GO:0003197.name: endocardial cushion development
GO:0003197.def: The progression of a cardiac cushion over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The endocardial cushion is a specialized region of mesenchymal cells that will give rise to the heart septa and valves.

GO:0003203.name: endocardial cushion morphogenesis
GO:0003203.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of the endocardial cushion is generated and organized. The endocardial cushion is a specialized region of mesenchymal cells that will give rise to the heart septa and valves.

GO:0003204.name: cardiac skeleton development
GO:0003204.def: The progression of the cardiac skeleton over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The cardiac skeleton is a specialized extracellular matrix that separates the atria from the ventricles and provides physical support for the heart.

GO:0003205.name: cardiac chamber development
GO:0003205.def: The progression of a cardiac chamber over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A cardiac chamber is an enclosed cavity within the heart.

GO:0003206.name: cardiac chamber morphogenesis
GO:0003206.def: The process in which a cardiac chamber is generated and organized. A cardiac chamber is an enclosed cavity within the heart.

GO:0003207.name: cardiac chamber formation
GO:0003207.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a cardiac chamber from unspecified parts. A cardiac chamber is an enclosed cavity within the heart.

GO:0003208.name: cardiac ventricle morphogenesis
GO:0003208.def: The process in which the cardiac ventricle is generated and organized. A cardiac ventricle receives blood from a cardiac atrium and pumps it out of the heart.

GO:0003209.name: cardiac atrium morphogenesis
GO:0003209.def: The process in which the cardiac atrium is generated and organized. A cardiac atrium receives blood from a vein and pumps it to a cardiac ventricle.

GO:0003210.name: cardiac atrium formation
GO:0003210.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a cardiac atrium from unspecified parts. A cardiac atrium receives blood from a vein and pumps it to a cardiac ventricle.

GO:0003211.name: cardiac ventricle formation
GO:0003211.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a cardiac ventricle from unspecified parts. A cardiac ventricle receives blood from a cardiac atrium and pumps it out of the heart.

GO:0003212.name: cardiac left atrium morphogenesis
GO:0003212.def: The process in which the left cardiac atrium is generated and organized.

GO:0003213.name: cardiac right atrium morphogenesis
GO:0003213.def: The process in which the right cardiac atrium is generated and organized.

GO:0003214.name: cardiac left ventricle morphogenesis
GO:0003214.def: The process in which the left cardiac ventricle is generated and organized.

GO:0003215.name: cardiac right ventricle morphogenesis
GO:0003215.def: The process in which the right cardiac ventricle is generated and organized.

GO:0003216.name: cardiac left atrium formation
GO:0003216.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a left cardiac atrium from unspecified parts.

GO:0003217.name: cardiac right atrium formation
GO:0003217.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a cardiac right atrium from unspecified parts.

GO:0003218.name: cardiac left ventricle formation
GO:0003218.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a left cardiac ventricle from unspecified parts.

GO:0003219.name: cardiac right ventricle formation
GO:0003219.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a right cardiac ventricle from unspecified parts.

GO:0003220.name: left ventricular cardiac muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0003220.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of left cardiac ventricle muscle are generated and organized.

GO:0003221.name: right ventricular cardiac muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0003221.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the right cardiac ventricle muscle are generated and organized.

GO:0003222.name: ventricular trabecula myocardium morphogenesis
GO:0003222.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the trabecular cardiac ventricle muscle are generated and organized.

GO:0003225.name: left ventricular trabecular myocardium morphogenesis
GO:0003225.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of cardiac left ventricular trabecular myocardium are generated and organized.

GO:0003227.name: right ventricular trabecular myocardium morphogenesis
GO:0003227.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the right ventricular myocardium are generated and organized.

GO:0003228.name: atrial cardiac muscle tissue development
GO:0003228.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of cardiac muscle of the atrium over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0003229.name: ventricular cardiac muscle tissue development
GO:0003229.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of ventricular cardiac muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0003230.name: cardiac atrium development
GO:0003230.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cardiac atrium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A cardiac atrium receives blood from a vein and pumps it to a cardiac ventricle.

GO:0003231.name: cardiac ventricle development
GO:0003231.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cardiac ventricle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A cardiac ventricle receives blood from a cardiac atrium and pumps it out of the heart.

GO:0003235.name: sinus venosus development
GO:0003235.def: The progression of the sinus venosus over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The sinus venosus is a heart chamber attached to the atrium on the venous side of the embryonic heart.

GO:0003236.name: sinus venosus morphogenesis
GO:0003236.def: The process in which the sinus venosus is generated and organized. The sinus venosus is a heart chamber attached to the atrium on the venous side of the embryonic heart.

GO:0003237.name: sinus venosus formation
GO:0003237.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the sinus venosus from unspecified parts. The sinus venosus is a heart chamber attached to the atrium on the venous side of the embryonic heart.

GO:0003238.name: conus arteriosus development
GO:0003238.def: The progression of the conus arteriosus over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The conus arteriosus is a valved chamber with thick muscular walls stemming from the ventricle and connecting to the pulmonary trunk.

GO:0003239.name: conus arteriosus morphogenesis
GO:0003239.def: The process in which the conus arteriosus is generated and organized. The conus arteriosus is a valved chamber with thick muscular walls stemming from the ventricle and connecting to the pulmonary trunk.

GO:0003240.name: conus arteriosus formation
GO:0003240.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the conus arteriosus from unspecified parts. The conus arteriosus is a valved chamber with thick muscular walls stemming from the ventricle and connecting to the pulmonary trunk.

GO:0003241.name: growth involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0003241.def: Developmental growth that contributes to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0003245.name: cardiac muscle tissue growth involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0003245.def: The developmental growth of cardiac muscle tissue that contributes to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0003248.name: heart capillary growth
GO:0003248.def: The increase in heart capillaries that accompanies physiological hypertrophy of cardiac muscle.

GO:0003249.name: cell proliferation involved in heart valve morphogenesis
GO:0003249.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells that contributes to the shaping of a heart valve.

GO:0003250.name: regulation of cell proliferation involved in heart valve morphogenesis
GO:0003250.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of cell proliferation that contributes to the shaping of a heart valve.

GO:0003251.name: positive regulation of cell proliferation involved in heart valve morphogenesis
GO:0003251.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of cell proliferation that contributes to the shaping of a heart valve.

GO:0003252.name: negative regulation of cell proliferation involved in heart valve morphogenesis
GO:0003252.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of cell proliferation that contributes to the shaping of a heart valve.

GO:0003253.name: cardiac neural crest cell migration involved in outflow tract morphogenesis
GO:0003253.def: The orderly movement of a neural crest cell from one site to another that will contribute to the morphogenesis of the outflow tract.

GO:0003260.name: cardioblast migration
GO:0003260.def: The orderly movement of a cardiac progenitor cell to form the heart field. Cardiac progenitor cells are non-terminally differentiated, mesoderm-derived cells that are committed to differentiate into cells of the heart. A cardioblast is a cardiac precursor cell. It is a cell that has been committed to a cardiac fate, but will undergo more cell division rather than terminally differentiating.

GO:0003272.name: endocardial cushion formation
GO:0003272.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of an endocardial cushion. The endocardial cushion is a specialized region of mesenchymal cells that will give rise to the heart septa and valves.

GO:0003273.name: cell migration involved in endocardial cushion formation
GO:0003273.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another that will contribute to the formation of an endocardial cushion. The endocardial cushion is a specialized region of mesenchymal cells that will give rise to the heart septa and valves.

GO:0003275.name: apoptotic process involved in outflow tract morphogenesis
GO:0003275.def: Any apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of the outflow tract. The outflow tract is the portion of the heart through which blood flows into the arteries.
GO:0003275.synonym: apoptosis involved in outflow tract morphogenesis

GO:0003276.name: apoptotic process involved in heart valve morphogenesis
GO:0003276.def: Any apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of a heart valve.
GO:0003276.synonym: apoptosis involved in heart valve morphogenesis

GO:0003277.name: apoptotic process involved in endocardial cushion morphogenesis
GO:0003277.def: Any apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of an endocardial cushion. The endocardial cushion is a specialized region of mesenchymal cells that will give rise to the heart septa and valves.
GO:0003277.synonym: apoptosis involved in endocardial cushion morphogenesis

GO:0003278.name: apoptotic process involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0003278.def: Any apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0003279.name: cardiac septum development
GO:0003279.def: The progression of a cardiac septum over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure.

GO:0003281.name: ventricular septum development
GO:0003281.def: The progression of the ventricular septum over time from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0003283.name: atrial septum development
GO:0003283.def: The progression of the atrial septum over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure.

GO:0003292.name: cardiac septum cell differentiation
GO:0003292.def: The process in which an endocardial cushion cell becomes a cell of a cardiac septum.

GO:0003293.name: heart valve cell differentiation
GO:0003293.def: The process in which an endocardial cushion cell give rise to a cell that is part of a heart valve.

GO:0003298.name: physiological muscle hypertrophy
GO:0003298.def: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of a muscle organ or tissue due to an increase in the size of its muscle cells. Physiological hypertrophy is a normal process during development.

GO:0003300.name: cardiac muscle hypertrophy
GO:0003300.def: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of the heart muscle due to an increase in size of cardiac muscle cells without cell division.

GO:0003301.name: physiological cardiac muscle hypertrophy
GO:0003301.def: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of the heart muscle due to an increase in size of cardiac muscle cells without cell division. This process contributes to the developmental growth of the heart.

GO:0003309.name: type B pancreatic cell differentiation
GO:0003309.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of a type B pancreatic cell. A type B pancreatic cell is a cell located towards center of the islets of Langerhans that secretes insulin.

GO:0003310.name: pancreatic A cell differentiation
GO:0003310.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and functional features of a pancreatic A cell. A pancreatic A cell is a cell in the pancreas that secretes glucagon.

GO:0003311.name: pancreatic D cell differentiation
GO:0003311.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and functional features that characterize a pancreatic delta cell. A delta cell is a cell of the pancreas that produces somatostatin.

GO:0003312.name: pancreatic PP cell differentiation
GO:0003312.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and functional features of a pancreatic polypeptide-producing cell. A pancreatic polypeptide-producing cell is a cell in the pancreas that produces pancreatic polypeptide.

GO:0003313.name: heart rudiment development
GO:0003313.def: The progression of the heart rudiment over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The heart rudiment is a cone-like structure that is formed when myocardial progenitor cells of the heart field fuse at the midline. The heart rudiment is the first structure of the heart tube.

GO:0003314.name: heart rudiment morphogenesis
GO:0003314.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the heart rudiment are generated and organized.

GO:0003315.name: heart rudiment formation
GO:0003315.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the heart rudiment.

GO:0003322.name: pancreatic A cell development
GO:0003322.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pancreatic A cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A pancreatic A cell is a cell in the pancreas that secretes glucagon.

GO:0003323.name: type B pancreatic cell development
GO:0003323.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a type B pancreatic cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A type B pancreatic cell is a cell located towards center of the islets of Langerhans that secretes insulin.

GO:0003324.name: pancreatic D cell development
GO:0003324.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pancreatic delta cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A delta cell is a cell of the pancreas that produces somatostatin.

GO:0003325.name: pancreatic PP cell development
GO:0003325.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pancreatic PP cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A pancreatic polypeptide-producing cell is a cell in the pancreas that produces pancreatic polypeptide.

GO:0003330.name: regulation of extracellular matrix constituent secretion
GO:0003330.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the controlled release of molecules that form the extracellular matrix, including carbohydrates and glycoproteins by a cell or a group of cells.

GO:0003331.name: positive regulation of extracellular matrix constituent secretion
GO:0003331.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the controlled release of molecules that form the extracellular matrix, including carbohydrates and glycoproteins by a cell or a group of cells.

GO:0003332.name: negative regulation of extracellular matrix constituent secretion
GO:0003332.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent the controlled release of molecules that form the extracellular matrix, including carbohydrates and glycoproteins by a cell or a group of cells.

GO:0003333.name: amino acid transmembrane transport
GO:0003333.def: The process in which an amino acid is transported across a membrane.

GO:0003334.name: keratinocyte development
GO:0003334.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a keratinocyte over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0003335.name: corneocyte development
GO:0003335.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the corneocyte over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A corneocyte is the last stage of development of a keratinocyte where the keratinocyte flattens, loses its nucleus and eventually delaminates from the epidermis.

GO:0003337.name: mesenchymal to epithelial transition involved in metanephros morphogenesis
GO:0003337.def: A transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity,forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell that will contribute to the shaping of the metanephros.

GO:0003338.name: metanephros morphogenesis
GO:0003338.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the metanephros are generated and organized.

GO:0003339.name: regulation of mesenchymal to epithelial transition involved in metanephros morphogenesis
GO:0003339.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity,forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell that will contribute to the shaping of the metanephros.

GO:0003340.name: negative regulation of mesenchymal to epithelial transition involved in metanephros morphogenesis
GO:0003340.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity,forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell that will contribute to the shaping of the metanephros.

GO:0003341.name: cilium movement
GO:0003341.def: The directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium.

GO:0003342.name: proepicardium development
GO:0003342.def: The progression of the proepicardium from its formation to the mature structure. The proepicardium is an outpouching of the septum transversum.

GO:0003343.name: septum transversum development
GO:0003343.def: The progression of the septum transversum from its initial formation to the mature structure. The septum transversum is a portion of the trunk mesenchyme.

GO:0003344.name: pericardium morphogenesis
GO:0003344.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of the pericardium is generated and organized.

GO:0003348.name: cardiac endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0003348.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardiac endothelial cell.

GO:0003352.name: regulation of cilium movement
GO:0003352.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of cilium movement, the directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium.

GO:0003353.name: positive regulation of cilium movement
GO:0003353.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of cilium movement, the directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium.
synonym: positive regulation of microtubule-based flagellum movement

GO:0003354.name: negative regulation of cilium movement
GO:0003354.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of cilium movement, the directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium.
synonym: negative regulation of microtubule-based flagellum movement

GO:0003357.name: noradrenergic neuron differentiation
GO:0003357.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an noradrenergic neuron, a neuron that secretes noradrenaline.

GO:0003358.name: noradrenergic neuron development
GO:0003358.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a noradrenergic neuron over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0003360.name: brainstem development
GO:0003360.def: The progression of the brainstem from its formation to the mature structure. The brainstem is the part of the brain that connects the brain with the spinal cord.

GO:0003361.name: noradrenergic neuron differentiation involved in brainstem development
GO:0003361.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an noradrenergic neuron that is part of the brainstem.

GO:0003365.name: establishment of cell polarity involved in ameboidal cell migration
GO:0003365.def: The specification and formation of anisotropic intracellular organization that contributes to the self-propelled directed movement of an ameboid cell.

GO:0003371.name: establishment or maintenance of cytoskeleton polarity involved in ameboidal cell migration
GO:0003371.def: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of polarized cytoskeletal structures that contribute to the cell polarity of a migrating ameboid cell.

GO:0003379.name: establishment of cell polarity involved in gastrulation cell migration
GO:0003379.def: The specification and formation of anisotropic intracellular organization that contributes to the self-propelled directed movement of an ameboid cell taking part in gastrulation.

GO:0003380.name: establishment or maintenance of cytoskeleton polarity involved in gastrulation
GO:0003380.def: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of polarized cytoskeletal structures that contribute to the cell polarity of a migrating ameboid cell taking part in gastrulation.

GO:0003381.name: epithelial cell morphogenesis involved in gastrulation
GO:0003381.def: The change in form that occurs when an epithelial cell progresses from it initial formation to its mature state, contributing to the process of gastrulation.

GO:0003382.name: epithelial cell morphogenesis
GO:0003382.def: The change in form that occurs when an epithelial cell progresses from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0003403.name: optic vesicle formation
GO:0003403.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the optic vesicle from the lateral wall of the forebrain. This process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the vesicle and ends when the vesicle has evaginated. The optic vesicle is the evagination of neurectoderm that precedes formation of the optic cup.

GO:0003404.name: optic vesicle morphogenesis
GO:0003404.def: The developmental process pertaining to the formation and shaping of the optic vesicle. This process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the vesicle and ends when the vesicle has evaginated. The optic vesicle is the evagination of neurectoderm that precedes formation of the optic cup.

GO:0003406.name: retinal pigment epithelium development
GO:0003406.def: The progression of the retinal pigment epithelium over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The retinal pigment epithelium is the melanin-containing layer of cells between the retina and the choroid that absorbs scattered and reflected light and removes waste products produced by the photoreceptor cells.

GO:0003407.name: neural retina development
GO:0003407.def: The progression of the neural retina over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The neural retina is the part of the retina that contains neurons and photoreceptor cells.

GO:0003411.name: cell motility involved in camera-type eye morphogenesis
GO:0003411.def: Any process involved in the controlled self-propelled movement of a cell that results in translocation of the cell from one place to another and contributes to the physical shaping or formation of the camera-type eye.

GO:0003413.name: chondrocyte differentiation involved in endochondral bone morphogenesis
GO:0003413.def: The process in which a chondroblast acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a chondrocyte that will contribute to the development of a bone. A chondrocyte is a polymorphic cell that forms cartilage.

GO:0003414.name: chondrocyte morphogenesis involved in endochondral bone morphogenesis
GO:0003414.def: The process in which the structures of a chondrocyte that will contribute to bone development are generated and organized.

GO:0003415.name: chondrocyte hypertrophy
GO:0003415.def: The growth of a chondrocyte, where growth contributes to the progression of the chondrocyte over time.

GO:0003416.name: endochondral bone growth
GO:0003416.def: The increase in size or mass of an endochondral bone that contributes to the shaping of the bone.

GO:0003417.name: growth plate cartilage development
GO:0003417.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cartilage that will provide a scaffold for mineralization of endochondral bones as they elongate or grow.

GO:0003418.name: growth plate cartilage chondrocyte differentiation
GO:0003418.def: The process in which a chondroblast acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a chondrocyte that will contribute to the growth of a bone. A chondrocyte is a polymorphic cell that forms cartilage.

GO:0003422.name: growth plate cartilage morphogenesis
GO:0003422.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of growth plate cartilage are generated and organized.

GO:0003429.name: growth plate cartilage chondrocyte morphogenesis
GO:0003429.def: The process in which the structures of a chondrocyte in the growth plate cartilage are generated and organized.

GO:0003430.name: growth plate cartilage chondrocyte growth
GO:0003430.def: The growth of a growth plate cartilage chondrocyte, where growth contributes to the progression of the chondrocyte over time from one condition to another.

GO:0003431.name: growth plate cartilage chondrocyte development
GO:0003431.def: The progression of a growth plate cartilage chondrocyte over time from after its fate commitment to the mature cell.

GO:0003432.name: cell growth involved in growth plate cartilage chondrocyte morphogenesis
GO:0003432.def: The growth of a growth plate cartilage chondrocyte, where growth contributes to the shaping of the chondrocyte over time.

GO:0003433.name: chondrocyte development involved in endochondral bone morphogenesis
GO:0003433.def: The progression of a chondrocyte over time from after its commitment to its mature state where the chondrocyte will contribute to the shaping of an endochondral bone.

GO:0003436.name: regulation of cell adhesion involved in growth plate cartilage morphogenesis
GO:0003436.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of attachment of a cell to another cell or to the extracellular matrix and contributes to the shaping of the growth plate cartilage of an endochondral bone.

GO:0003437.name: regulation of cell communication involved in growth plate cartilage morphogenesis
GO:0003437.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell communication that contributes to the shaping of the growth plate cartilage.

GO:0003674.name: molecular_function
GO:0003674.def: A molecular process that can be carried out by the action of a single macromolecular machine, usually via direct physical interactions with other molecular entities. Function in this sense denotes an action, or activity, that a gene product (or a complex) performs.

GO:0003677.name: DNA binding
GO:0003677.def: Any molecular function by which a gene product interacts selectively and non-covalently with DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).

GO:0003682.name: chromatin binding
GO:0003682.def: Binding to chromatin, the network of fibers of DNA, protein, and sometimes RNA, that make up the chromosomes of the eukaryotic nucleus during interphase.
synonym: nuclear membrane vesicle binding to chromatin

GO:0003723.name: RNA binding
GO:0003723.def: Binding to an RNA molecule or a portion thereof.

GO:0003774.name: cytoskeletal motor activity
GO:0003774.def: Generation of force resulting in movement, for example along a microfilament or microtubule, or in torque resulting in membrane scission or rotation of a flagellum. The energy required is obtained either from the hydrolysis of a nucleoside triphosphate or by an electrochemical proton gradient (proton-motive force).

GO:0003777.name: microtubule motor activity
GO:0003777.def: A motor activity that generates movement along a microtubule, driven by ATP hydrolysis.

GO:0003824.name: catalytic activity
GO:0003824.def: Catalysis of a biochemical reaction at physiological temperatures. In biologically catalyzed reactions, the reactants are known as substrates, and the catalysts are naturally occurring macromolecular substances known as enzymes. Enzymes possess specific binding sites for substrates, and are usually composed wholly or largely of protein, but RNA that has catalytic activity (ribozyme) is often also regarded as enzymatic.

GO:0004518.name: nuclease activity
GO:0004518.def: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of ester linkages within nucleic acids.

GO:0004536.name: DNA nuclease activity
GO:0004536.def: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of ester linkages within deoxyribonucleic acid.

GO:0004672.name: protein kinase activity
GO:0004672.def: Catalysis of the phosphorylation of an amino acid residue in a protein, usually according to the reaction: a protein + ATP = a phosphoprotein + ADP.

GO:0004713.name: protein tyrosine kinase activity
GO:0004713.def: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + a protein tyrosine = ADP + protein tyrosine phosphate.

GO:0004714.name: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase activity
GO:0004714.def: Combining with a signal and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity by catalysis of the reaction: ATP + a protein-L-tyrosine = ADP + a protein-L-tyrosine phosphate.

GO:0004888.name: transmembrane signaling receptor activity
GO:0004888.def: Combining with an extracellular or intracellular signal and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity or state as part of signal transduction.

GO:0004896.name: cytokine receptor activity
GO:0004896.def: Combining with a cytokine and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0004925.name: prolactin receptor activity
GO:0004925.def: Combining with prolactin and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0004930.name: G protein-coupled receptor activity
GO:0004930.def: Combining with an extracellular signal and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.
synonym: G-protein coupled receptor activity, unknown ligand
orphan G protein coupled receptor activity
super conserved receptor expressed in brain receptor activity

GO:0004948.name: calcitonin receptor activity
GO:0004948.def: Combining with calcitonin and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.

GO:0004951.name: cholecystokinin receptor activity
GO:0004951.def: Combining with cholecystokinin and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein to initiate a change in cell activity. Cholecystokinin can act as a neuropeptide or as a gastrointestinal hormone.

GO:0004967.name: glucagon receptor activity
GO:0004967.def: Combining with glucagon and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.

GO:0004969.name: histamine receptor activity
GO:0004969.def: Combining with histamine to initiate a change in cell activity. Histamine is a physiologically active amine, found in plant and animal tissue and released from mast cells as part of an allergic reaction in humans.

GO:0004970.name: glutamate-gated receptor activity
GO:0004970.def: Catalysis of the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when glutamate has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0004977.name: melanocortin receptor activity
GO:0004977.def: Combining with melanocortin to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0004978.name: corticotropin receptor activity
GO:0004978.def: Combining with corticotropin to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0004990.name: oxytocin receptor activity
GO:0004990.def: Combining with oxytocin to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0004993.name: G protein-coupled serotonin receptor activity
GO:0004993.def: Combining with the biogenic amine serotonin and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein. Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) is a neurotransmitter and hormone found in vertebrates and invertebrates.
synonym: G protein coupled serotonin receptor activity

GO:0004994.name: somatostatin receptor activity
GO:0004994.def: Combining with somatostatin to initiate a change in cell activity. Somatostatin is a peptide hormone that regulates the endocrine system by signaling via G protein-coupled somatostatin receptors. Somatostatin has two active forms produced by proteolytic cleavage: a 14 amino acid peptide (SST-14) and a 28 amino acid peptide (SST-28).
synonym: somatotrophin release inhibiting factor receptor activity

GO:0005000.name: vasopressin receptor activity
GO:0005000.def: Combining with vasopressin to initiate a change in cell activity.
GO:0005000.synonym: vasopressin activated calcium mobilizing receptor activity

GO:0005009.name: insulin receptor activity
GO:0005009.def: Combining with insulin receptor ligand and transmitting the signal across the plasma membrane to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0005044.name: scavenger receptor activity
GO:0005044.def: Combining with any modified low-density lipoprotein (LDL) or other polyanionic ligand and delivering the ligand into the cell via endocytosis. Ligands include acetylated and oxidized LDL, Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, apoptotic cells, amyloid-beta fibrils, and advanced glycation end products (AGEs).

GO:0005102.name: signaling receptor binding
GO:0005102.def: Binding to one or more specific sites on a receptor molecule, a macromolecule that undergoes combination with a hormone, neurotransmitter, drug or intracellular messenger to initiate a change in cell function.

GO:0005122.name: torso binding
GO:0005122.def: Binding to a torso (tor) protein, a receptor tyrosine kinase.

GO:0005172.name: vascular endothelial growth factor receptor binding
GO:0005172.def: Binding to a vascular endothelial growth factor receptor.
