GO:0007283.def: The developmental process by which male germ line stem cells self renew or give rise to successive cell types resulting in the development of a spermatozoa.

GO:0007284.name: spermatogonial cell division
GO:0007284.def: The mitotic divisions of the primary spermatogonial cell (a primordial male germ cell) to form secondary spermatogonia (primary spermatocytes).

GO:0007285.name: primary spermatocyte growth
GO:0007285.def: The phase of growth and gene expression that male germ cells undergo as they enter the spermatocyte stage. The cells grow in volume and transcribe most of the gene products needed for the morphological events that follow meiosis.

GO:0007286.name: spermatid development
GO:0007286.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spermatid over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0007288.name: sperm axoneme assembly
GO:0007288.def: The assembly and organization of the sperm flagellar axoneme, the bundle of microtubules and associated proteins that forms the core of the eukaryotic sperm flagellum, and is responsible for movement.

GO:0007289.name: spermatid nucleus differentiation
GO:0007289.def: The specialization of the spermatid nucleus during the development of a spermatid into a mature male gamete competent for fertilization.

GO:0007292.name: female gamete generation
GO:0007292.def: Generation of the female gamete; specialised haploid cells produced by meiosis and along with a male gamete takes part in sexual reproduction.

GO:0007293.name: germarium-derived egg chamber formation
GO:0007293.def: Construction of a stage-1 egg chamber in the anterior part of the germarium, from the progeny of germ-line and somatic stem cells. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007297.name: follicle cell of egg chamber migration
GO:0007297.def: The directed movement of an ovarian follicle cell that takes place during oogenesis. During egg chamber formation, follicle cells migrate to envelop the germ-line cysts and move in between cysts. At stage 10B, follicle cells migrate centripetally between the nurse cells and the oocyte, enclosing the anterior of the egg. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007298.name: border follicle cell migration
GO:0007298.def: The directed movement of a border cell through the nurse cells to reach the oocyte. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007308.name: oocyte construction
GO:0007308.def: The synthesis, deposition, and organization of the materials in a cell of an ovary; where the cell can then undergo meiosis and form an ovum. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007309.name: oocyte axis specification
GO:0007309.def: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of an axis in the oocyte. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007314.name: oocyte anterior/posterior axis specification
GO:0007314.def: Polarization of the oocyte along its anterior-posterior axis. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007320.name: insemination
GO:0007320.def: The introduction of semen or sperm into the genital tract of a female.

GO:0007338.name: single fertilization
GO:0007338.def: The union of male and female gametes to form a zygote.

GO:0007343.name: egg activation
GO:0007343.def: The process in which the egg becomes metabolically active, initiates protein and DNA synthesis and undergoes structural changes to its cortex and/or cytoplasm.

GO:0007346.name: regulation of mitotic cell cycle
GO:0007346.def: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of progress through the mitotic cell cycle.
synonym: modulation of mitotic cell cycle progression
regulation of mitotic cell cycle progression
regulation of progression through mitotic cell cycle

GO:0007349.name: cellularization
GO:0007349.def: The separation of a multi-nucleate cell or syncytium into individual cells. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster embryo development.

GO:0007350.name: blastoderm segmentation
GO:0007350.def: The hierarchical steps resulting in the progressive subdivision of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo.

GO:0007351.name: tripartite regional subdivision
GO:0007351.def: Subdivision of the embryo along the anterior/posterior axis into anterior, posterior and terminal regions.

GO:0007354.name: zygotic determination of anterior/posterior axis, embryo
GO:0007354.def: The specification of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo by products of genes expressed in the zygote; exemplified in insects by the gap genes, pair rule genes and segment polarity gene cascade.

GO:0007369.name: gastrulation
GO:0007369.def: A complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals. The details of gastrulation vary from species to species, but usually result in the formation of the three primary germ layers, ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.

GO:0007378.name: amnioserosa formation
GO:0007378.def: Formation of the amnioserosa, an epithelium that occupies a hole in the embryonic dorsal epidermis. This occurs by the transformation of a narrow strip of cells at the dorsal midline of the blastoderm from columnar to squamous cells, accompanied by a lateral shift.

GO:0007389.name: pattern specification process
GO:0007389.def: Any developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within an organism to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate.

GO:0007398.name: ectoderm development
GO:0007398.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ectoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In animal embryos, the ectoderm is the outer germ layer of the embryo, formed during gastrulation.

GO:0007399.name: nervous system development
GO:0007399.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of nervous tissue over time, from its formation to its mature state.

GO:0007405.name: neuroblast proliferation
GO:0007405.def: The expansion of a neuroblast population by cell division. A neuroblast is any cell that will divide and give rise to a neuron.

GO:0007406.name: negative regulation of neuroblast proliferation
GO:0007406.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the proliferation of neuroblasts.

GO:0007407.name: neuroblast activation
GO:0007407.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a neuroblast resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand.

GO:0007409.name: axonogenesis
GO:0007409.def: De novo generation of a long process of a neuron, including the terminal branched region. Refers to the morphogenesis or creation of shape or form of the developing axon, which carries efferent (outgoing) action potentials from the cell body towards target cells.

GO:0007416.name: synapse assembly
GO:0007416.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a synapse. This process ends when the synapse is mature (functional).

GO:0007417.name: central nervous system development
GO:0007417.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the central nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The central nervous system is the core nervous system that serves an integrating and coordinating function. In vertebrates it consists of the brain and spinal cord. In those invertebrates with a central nervous system it typically consists of a brain, cerebral ganglia and a nerve cord.

GO:0007418.name: ventral midline development
GO:0007418.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ventral midline over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In protostomes (such as insects, snails and worms) as well as deuterostomes (vertebrates), the midline is an embryonic region that functions in patterning of the adjacent nervous tissue. The ventral midline in insects is a cell population extending along the ventral surface of the embryo and is the region from which cells detach to form the ventrally located nerve cords. In vertebrates, the midline is originally located dorsally. During development, it folds inwards and becomes the ventral part of the dorsally located neural tube and is then called the ventral midline, or floor plate.

GO:0007420.name: brain development
GO:0007420.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the brain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Brain development begins with patterning events in the neural tube and ends with the mature structure that is the center of thought and emotion. The brain is responsible for the coordination and control of bodily activities and the interpretation of information from the senses (sight, hearing, smell, etc.).

GO:0007422.name: peripheral nervous system development
GO:0007422.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the peripheral nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The peripheral nervous system is one of the two major divisions of the nervous system. Nerves in the PNS connect the central nervous system (CNS) with sensory organs, other organs, muscles, blood vessels and glands.

GO:0007423.name: sensory organ development
GO:0007423.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of sensory organs over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0007424.name: open tracheal system development
GO:0007424.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an open tracheal system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An open tracheal system is a respiratory system, a branched network of epithelial tubes that supplies oxygen to target tissues via spiracles. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007431.name: salivary gland development
GO:0007431.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the salivary gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Salivary glands include any of the saliva-secreting exocrine glands of the oral cavity.

GO:0007435.name: salivary gland morphogenesis
GO:0007435.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the salivary gland are generated and organized.

GO:0007438.name: oenocyte development
GO:0007438.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the oenocyte over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The oenocytes are large secretory cells found in clusters underlying the epidermis of larval abdominal segments.

GO:0007439.name: ectodermal digestive tract development
GO:0007439.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ectodermal digestive tract over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The ectodermal digestive tract includes those portions that are derived from ectoderm.

GO:0007440.name: foregut morphogenesis
GO:0007440.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the foregut are generated and organized.

GO:0007442.name: hindgut morphogenesis
GO:0007442.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the hindgut are generated and organized.

GO:0007443.name: Malpighian tubule morphogenesis
GO:0007443.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the Malpighian tubule are generated and organized. This process takes place entirely during the embryonic phase. A Malpighian tubule is a fine, thin-walled excretory tubule in insects which leads into the posterior part of the gut.

GO:0007444.name: imaginal disc development
GO:0007444.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the imaginal disc over time, from its formation to the metamorphosis to form adult structures. Imaginal discs are epithelial infoldings in the larvae of holometabolous insects that develop into adult structures (legs, antennae, wings, etc.).

GO:0007446.name: imaginal disc growth
GO:0007446.def: The increase in mass of imaginal discs by cell proliferation prior to metamorphosis. Imaginal discs are epithelial infoldings in the larvae of holometabolous insects that develop into adult structures (legs, antennae, wings, etc.) during metamorphosis from larval to adult form.

GO:0007488.name: histoblast morphogenesis
GO:0007488.def: The process in which the anatomical structures derived from the histoblast disc are generated and organized. This includes the transformation of histoblast cells into adult structures during pupal metamorphosis. Histoblast cells are cells founded in the embryo that are the progenitors to the adult abdomen.

GO:0007492.name: endoderm development
GO:0007492.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the endoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The endoderm is the innermost germ layer that develops into the gastrointestinal tract, the lungs and associated tissues.

GO:0007494.name: midgut development
GO:0007494.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the midgut over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The midgut is the middle part of the alimentary canal from the stomach, or entrance of the bile duct, to, or including, the large intestine.

GO:0007498.name: mesoderm development
GO:0007498.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesoderm is the middle germ layer that develops into muscle, bone, cartilage, blood and connective tissue.

GO:0007506.name: gonadal mesoderm development
GO:0007506.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the gonadal mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The gonadal mesoderm is the middle layer of the three primary germ layers of the embryo which will go on to form the gonads of the organism.

GO:0007507.name: heart development
GO:0007507.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the heart over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The heart is a hollow, muscular organ, which, by contracting rhythmically, keeps up the circulation of the blood.

GO:0007516.name: hemocyte development
GO:0007516.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hemocyte over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Hemocytes are blood cells associated with a hemocoel (the cavity containing most of the major organs of the arthropod body) which are involved in defense and clotting of hemolymph, but not involved in transport of oxygen.

GO:0007517.name: muscle organ development
GO:0007517.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The muscle is an organ consisting of a tissue made up of various elongated cells that are specialized to contract and thus to produce movement and mechanical work.

GO:0007519.name: skeletal muscle tissue development
GO:0007519.def: The developmental sequence of events leading to the formation of adult skeletal muscle tissue. The main events are: the fusion of myoblasts to form myotubes that increase in size by further fusion to them of myoblasts, the formation of myofibrils within their cytoplasm and the establishment of functional neuromuscular junctions with motor neurons. At this stage they can be regarded as mature muscle fibers.

GO:0007528.name: neuromuscular junction development
GO:0007528.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a neuromuscular junction.

GO:0007548.name: sex differentiation
GO:0007548.def: The establishment of the sex of an organism by physical differentiation.

GO:0007552.name: metamorphosis
GO:0007552.def: A biological process in which an animal physically develops after birth or hatching, involving a conspicuous and relatively abrupt change in the animal's form or structure. Examples include the change from tadpole to frog, and the change from larva to adult. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0007553.name: regulation of ecdysteroid metabolic process
GO:0007553.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving ecdysteroids, a group of polyhydroxylated ketosteroids which initiate post-embryonic development, including the metamorphosis of immature forms and the development of the reproductive system and the maturation of oocytes in adult females.

GO:0007554.name: regulation of ecdysteroid biosynthetic process
GO:0007554.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of ecdysteroids.

GO:0007555.name: regulation of ecdysteroid secretion
GO:0007555.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of ecdysteroid from a cell.

GO:0007556.name: regulation of juvenile hormone metabolic process
GO:0007556.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving juvenile hormone.

GO:0007557.name: regulation of juvenile hormone biosynthetic process
GO:0007557.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of juvenile hormone.

GO:0007558.name: regulation of juvenile hormone secretion
GO:0007558.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of juvenile hormone secretion.

GO:0007560.name: imaginal disc morphogenesis
GO:0007560.def: The process in which the anatomical structures derived from an imaginal disc are generated and organized. The imaginal discs are epithelial infoldings in the larvae of holometabolous insects that develop into adult appendages (legs, antennae, wings, etc.) during metamorphosis from larval to adult form.

GO:0007565.name: female pregnancy
GO:0007565.def: The set of physiological processes that allow an embryo or foetus to develop within the body of a female animal. It covers the time from fertilization of a female ovum by a male spermatozoon until birth.

GO:0007566.name: embryo implantation
GO:0007566.def: Attachment of the blastocyst to the uterine lining.

GO:0007585.name: respiratory gaseous exchange by respiratory system
GO:0007585.def: The process of gaseous exchange between an organism and its environment. In plants, microorganisms, and many small animals, air or water makes direct contact with the organism's cells or tissue fluids, and the processes of diffusion supply the organism with dioxygen (O2) and remove carbon dioxide (CO2). In larger animals the efficiency of gaseous exchange is improved by specialized respiratory organs, such as lungs and gills, which are ventilated by breathing mechanisms.

GO:0007586.name: digestion
GO:0007586.def: The whole of the physical, chemical, and biochemical processes carried out by multicellular organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

GO:0007588.name: excretion
GO:0007588.def: The elimination by an organism of the waste products that arise as a result of metabolic activity. These products include water, carbon dioxide (CO2), and nitrogenous compounds.

GO:0007589.name: body fluid secretion
GO:0007589.def: The controlled release of a fluid by a cell or tissue in an animal.

GO:0007595.name: lactation
GO:0007595.def: The regulated release of milk from the mammary glands and the period of time that a mother lactates to feed her young.

GO:0007596.name: blood coagulation
GO:0007596.def: The sequential process in which the multiple coagulation factors of the blood interact, ultimately resulting in the formation of an insoluble fibrin clot; it may be divided into three stages: stage 1, the formation of intrinsic and extrinsic prothrombin converting principle; stage 2, the formation of thrombin; stage 3, the formation of stable fibrin polymers.

GO:0007599.name: hemostasis
GO:0007599.def: The stopping of bleeding (loss of body fluid) or the arrest of the circulation to an organ or part.

GO:0007600.name: sensory perception
GO:0007600.def: The series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

GO:0007601.name: visual perception
GO:0007601.def: The series of events required for an organism to receive a visual stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Visual stimuli are detected in the form of photons and are processed to form an image.

GO:0007605.name: sensory perception of sound
GO:0007605.def: The series of events required for an organism to receive an auditory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Sonic stimuli are detected in the form of vibrations and are processed to form a sound.

GO:0007606.name: sensory perception of chemical stimulus
GO:0007606.def: The series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory chemical stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

GO:0007608.name: sensory perception of smell
GO:0007608.def: The series of events required for an organism to receive an olfactory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Olfaction involves the detection of chemical composition of an organism's ambient medium by chemoreceptors. This is a neurological process.

GO:0007610.name: behavior
GO:0007610.def: The internally coordinated responses (actions or inactions) of animals (individuals or groups) to internal or external stimuli, via a mechanism that involves nervous system activity.

GO:0007611.name: learning or memory
GO:0007611.def: The acquisition and processing of information and/or the storage and retrieval of this information over time.

GO:0007612.name: learning
GO:0007612.def: Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs as the result of experience.

GO:0007613.name: memory
GO:0007613.def: The activities involved in the mental information processing system that receives (registers), modifies, stores, and retrieves informational stimuli. The main stages involved in the formation and retrieval of memory are encoding (processing of received information by acquisition), storage (building a permanent record of received information as a result of consolidation) and retrieval (calling back the stored information and use it in a suitable way to execute a given task).

GO:0007617.name: mating behavior
GO:0007617.def: The behavioral interactions between organisms for the purpose of mating, or sexual reproduction resulting in the formation of zygotes.

GO:0007620.name: copulation
GO:0007620.def: The act of sexual union between male and female, involving the transfer of sperm.

GO:0007626.name: locomotory behavior
GO:0007626.def: The specific movement from place to place of an organism in response to external or internal stimuli. Locomotion of a whole organism in a manner dependent upon some combination of that organism's internal state and external conditions.

GO:0007635.name: chemosensory behavior
GO:0007635.def: Behavior that is dependent upon the sensation of chemicals.

GO:0008015.name: blood circulation
GO:0008015.def: The flow of blood through the body of an animal, enabling the transport of nutrients to the tissues and the removal of waste products.

GO:0008016.name: regulation of heart contraction
GO:0008016.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of heart contraction. Heart contraction is the process in which the heart decreases in volume in a characteristic way to propel blood through the body.

GO:0008017.name: microtubule binding
GO:0008017.def: Binding to a microtubule, a filament composed of tubulin monomers.

GO:0008028.name: monocarboxylic acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0008028.def: Enables the transfer of monocarboxylic acids from one side of a membrane to the other. A monocarboxylic acid is an organic acid with one COOH group.

GO:0008066.name: glutamate receptor activity
GO:0008066.def: Combining with glutamate and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0008078.name: mesodermal cell migration
GO:0008078.def: The orderly movement of mesodermal cells from one site to another.

GO:0008088.name: axo-dendritic transport
GO:0008088.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in neuron projections.

GO:0008089.name: anterograde axonal transport
GO:0008089.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules from the cell body toward the cell periphery in nerve cell axons.

GO:0008090.name: retrograde axonal transport
GO:0008090.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules from the cell periphery toward the cell body in nerve cell axons.

GO:0008092.name: cytoskeletal protein binding
GO:0008092.def: Binding to a protein component of a cytoskeleton (actin, microtubule, or intermediate filament cytoskeleton).

GO:0008094.name: ATP-dependent activity, acting on DNA
GO:0008094.def: Catalytic activity that acts to modify DNA, driven by ATP hydrolysis.

GO:0008104.name: protein localization
GO:0008104.def: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.
synonym: establishment and maintenance of asymmetric protein localization
establishment and maintenance of protein localization

GO:0008134.name: transcription factor binding
GO:0008134.def: Binding to a transcription factor, a protein required to initiate or regulate transcription.

GO:0008150.name: biological_process
GO:0008150.def: A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.

GO:0008152.name: metabolic process
GO:0008152.def: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism transforms chemical substances. This includes including anabolism (biosynthetic process) and catabolism (catabolic process). Metabolic processes includes the transformation of small molecules, as well  macromolecular processes such as DNA repair and replication, protein synthesis and degradation.

GO:0008186.name: ATP-dependent activity, acting on RNA
GO:0008186.def: Catalysis of the reaction: ATP + H2O = ADP + phosphate; this reaction requires the presence of RNA, and it drives another reaction.

GO:0008188.name: neuropeptide receptor activity
GO:0008188.def: Combining with a neuropeptide to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0008202.name: steroid metabolic process
GO:0008202.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving steroids, compounds with a 1,2,cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus.

GO:0008206.name: bile acid metabolic process
GO:0008206.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving bile acids, a group of steroid carboxylic acids occurring in bile, where they are present as the sodium salts of their amides with glycine or taurine.

GO:0008207.name: C21-steroid hormone metabolic process
GO:0008207.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving C21-steroid hormones, steroid compounds containing 21 carbons which function as hormones.

GO:0008208.name: C21-steroid hormone catabolic process
GO:0008208.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of C21-steroid hormones, steroid compounds containing 21 carbons which function as hormones.

GO:0008211.name: glucocorticoid metabolic process
GO:0008211.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glucocorticoids, hormonal C21 corticosteroids synthesized from cholesterol. Glucocorticoids act primarily on carbohydrate and protein metabolism, and have anti-inflammatory effects.

GO:0008212.name: mineralocorticoid metabolic process
GO:0008212.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving mineralocorticoids, hormonal C21 corticosteroids synthesized from cholesterol. Mineralocorticoids act primarily on water and electrolyte balance.

GO:0008217.name: regulation of blood pressure
GO:0008217.def: Any process that modulates the force with which blood travels through the circulatory system. The process is controlled by a balance of processes that increase pressure and decrease pressure.

GO:0008219.name: cell death
GO:0008219.def: Any biological process that results in permanent cessation of all vital functions of a cell. A cell should be considered dead when any one of the following molecular or morphological criteria is met: (1) the cell has lost the integrity of its plasma membrane; (2) the cell, including its nucleus, has undergone complete fragmentation into discrete bodies (frequently referred to as apoptotic bodies). The cell corpse (or its fragments) may be engulfed by an adjacent cell in vivo, but engulfment of whole cells should not be considered a strict criteria to define cell death as, under some circumstances, live engulfed cells can be released from phagosomes (see PMID:18045538).

GO:0008227.name: G protein-coupled amine receptor activity
GO:0008227.def: Combining with an extracellular amine and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.

GO:0008277.name: regulation of G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway
GO:0008277.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway.
synonym: regulation of G protein coupled receptor protein signaling pathway
regulation of G protein coupled receptor protein signalling pathway
regulation of G-protein coupled receptor protein signaling pathway
regulation of G-protein coupled receptor protein signalling pathway
regulation of G-protein-coupled receptor protein signalling pathway
regulation of GPCR protein signaling pathway
regulation of GPCR protein signalling pathway

GO:0008283.name: cell population proliferation
GO:0008283.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0008284.name: positive regulation of cell population proliferation
GO:0008284.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of cell proliferation.

GO:0008285.name: negative regulation of cell population proliferation
GO:0008285.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate or extent of cell proliferation.

GO:0008286.name: insulin receptor signaling pathway
GO:0008286.def: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of the insulin receptor binding to insulin.

GO:0008291.name: acetylcholine metabolic process
GO:0008291.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving acetylcholine, the acetic acid ester of the organic base choline. Acetylcholine is a major neurotransmitter and neuromodulator both in the central and peripheral nervous systems. It also acts as a paracrine signal in various non-neural tissues.

GO:0008292.name: acetylcholine biosynthetic process
GO:0008292.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of acetylcholine, the acetic acid ester of the organic base choline.

GO:0008299.name: isoprenoid biosynthetic process
GO:0008299.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of an isoprenoid compound, isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) or compounds containing or derived from linked isoprene (3-methyl-2-butenylene) residues.

GO:0008300.name: isoprenoid catabolic process
GO:0008300.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of an isoprenoid compound, isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) or compounds containing or derived from linked isoprene (3-methyl-2-butenylene) residues.

GO:0008306.name: associative learning
GO:0008306.def: Learning by associating a stimulus (the cause) with a particular outcome (the effect).

GO:0008320.name: protein transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0008320.def: Enables the transfer of a protein from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0008324.name: monoatomic cation transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0008324.def: Enables the transfer of cation from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0008328.name: ionotropic glutamate receptor complex
GO:0008328.def: A multimeric assembly of four or five subunits which form a structure with an extracellular N-terminus and a large loop that together form the ligand binding domain. The C-terminus is intracellular. The ionotropic glutamate receptor complex itself acts as a ligand-gated ion channel; on binding glutamate, charged ions pass through a channel in the center of the receptor complex.

GO:0008347.name: glial cell migration
GO:0008347.def: The orderly movement of a glial cell, non-neuronal cells that provide support and nutrition, maintain homeostasis, form myelin, and participate in signal transmission in the nervous system.

GO:0008348.name: negative regulation of antimicrobial humoral response
GO:0008348.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of an antimicrobial humoral response.
synonym: down regulation of antimicrobial humoral response

GO:0008354.name: germ cell migration
GO:0008354.def: The orderly movement of a cell specialized to produce haploid gametes through the embryo from its site of production to the place where the gonads will form.

GO:0008355.name: olfactory learning
GO:0008355.def: Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs in response to (repeated) exposure to an olfactory cue.

GO:0008356.name: asymmetric cell division
GO:0008356.def: The asymmetric division of cells to produce two daughter cells with different developmental potentials. It is of fundamental significance for the generation of cell diversity.

GO:0008358.name: maternal determination of anterior/posterior axis, embryo
GO:0008358.def: The specification of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo by gradients of maternally-transcribed gene products; exemplified in insects by the morphogens, bicoid and nanos.

GO:0008361.name: regulation of cell size
GO:0008361.def: Any process that modulates the size of a cell.

GO:0008366.name: axon ensheathment
GO:0008366.def: Any process in which the axon of a neuron is insulated, and that insulation maintained, thereby preventing dispersion of the electrical signal.

GO:0008406.name: gonad development
GO:0008406.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the gonad over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The gonad is an animal organ that produces gametes; in some species it also produces hormones.

GO:0008502.name: melatonin receptor activity
GO:0008502.def: Combining with melatonin, N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine, to initiate a change in cell activity. Melatonin is a neuroendocrine substance that stimulates the aggregation of melanosomes in melanophores, thus lightening the skin.

GO:0008504.name: monoamine transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0008504.def: Enables the transfer of monoamines, organic compounds that contain one amino group that is connected to an aromatic ring by an ethylene group (-CH2-CH2-), from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0008514.name: organic anion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0008514.def: Enables the transfer of organic anions from one side of a membrane to the other. Organic anions are atoms or small molecules with a negative charge which contain carbon in covalent linkage.

GO:0008519.name: ammonium channel activity
GO:0008519.def: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of ammonium through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

GO:0008528.name: G protein-coupled peptide receptor activity
GO:0008528.def: Combining with a peptide and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.
synonym: G protein coupled peptide receptor activity
peptide receptor activity, G protein coupled

GO:0008544.name: epidermis development
GO:0008544.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the epidermis over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The epidermis is the outer epithelial layer of an animal, it may be a single layer that produces an extracellular material (e.g. the cuticle of arthropods) or a complex stratified squamous epithelium, as in the case of many vertebrate species.

GO:0008584.name: male gonad development
GO:0008584.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the male gonad over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0008585.name: female gonad development
GO:0008585.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the female gonad over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0008594.name: photoreceptor cell morphogenesis
GO:0008594.def: The process in which the structures of a photoreceptor cell are generated and organized. This process occurs while the initially relatively unspecialized cell is acquiring the specialized features of a photoreceptor cell, a sensory cell that reacts to the presence of light. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0008595.name: anterior/posterior axis specification, embryo
GO:0008595.def: The specification of the anterior/posterior axis of the embryo by the products of genes expressed maternally and genes expressed in the zygote.

GO:0008610.name: lipid biosynthetic process
GO:0008610.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipids, compounds soluble in an organic solvent but not, or sparingly, in an aqueous solvent.

GO:0008643.name: carbohydrate transport
GO:0008643.def: The directed movement of carbohydrate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carbohydrates are a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

GO:0008645.name: hexose transmembrane transport
GO:0008645.def: The process in which hexose is transported across a membrane. Hexoses are aldoses with a chain of six carbon atoms in the molecule.

GO:0008652.name: amino acid biosynthetic process
GO:0008652.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids, organic acids containing one or more amino substituents.

GO:0009056.name: catabolic process
GO:0009056.def: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism breaks down substances. This includes the breakdown of carbon compounds with the liberation of energy for use by the cell or organism.

GO:0009057.name: macromolecule catabolic process
GO:0009057.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

GO:0009058.name: biosynthetic process
GO:0009058.def: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism synthesizes chemical substances. This typically represents the energy-requiring part of metabolism in which simpler substances are transformed into more complex ones.

GO:0009059.name: macromolecule biosynthetic process
GO:0009059.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

GO:0009062.name: fatty acid catabolic process
GO:0009062.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a fatty acid, any of the aliphatic monocarboxylic acids that can be liberated by hydrolysis from naturally occurring fats and oils. Fatty acids are predominantly straight-chain acids of 4 to 24 carbon atoms, which may be saturated or unsaturated; branched fatty acids and hydroxy fatty acids also occur, and very long chain acids of over 30 carbons are found in waxes.

GO:0009063.name: amino acid catabolic process
GO:0009063.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids, organic acids containing one or more amino substituents.

GO:0009064.name: glutamine family amino acid metabolic process
GO:0009064.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.

GO:0009065.name: glutamine family amino acid catabolic process
GO:0009065.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.

GO:0009069.name: serine family amino acid metabolic process
GO:0009069.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

GO:0009070.name: serine family amino acid biosynthetic process
GO:0009070.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

GO:0009071.name: serine family amino acid catabolic process
GO:0009071.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of amino acids of the serine family, comprising cysteine, glycine, homoserine, selenocysteine and serine.

GO:0009072.name: aromatic amino acid metabolic process
GO:0009072.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).
synonym: aromatic amino acid family metabolic process

GO:0009073.name: aromatic amino acid family biosynthetic process
GO:0009073.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).
synonym: aromatic amino acid family biosynthetic process, shikimate pathway

GO:0009074.name: aromatic amino acid family catabolic process
GO:0009074.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of aromatic amino acid family, amino acids with aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).

GO:0009084.name: glutamine family amino acid biosynthetic process
GO:0009084.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of amino acids of the glutamine family, comprising arginine, glutamate, glutamine and proline.

GO:0009100.name: glycoprotein metabolic process
GO:0009100.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

GO:0009101.name: glycoprotein biosynthetic process
GO:0009101.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycoproteins, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

GO:0009117.name: nucleotide metabolic process
GO:0009117.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleotide, a nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the glycose moiety; may be mono-, di- or triphosphate; this definition includes cyclic nucleotides (nucleoside cyclic phosphates).

GO:0009132.name: nucleoside diphosphate metabolic process
GO:0009132.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009133.name: nucleoside diphosphate biosynthetic process
GO:0009133.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a nucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a deoxyribose or ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009134.name: nucleoside diphosphate catabolic process

GO:0009135.name: purine nucleoside diphosphate metabolic process

GO:0009145.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine nucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009146.name: purine nucleoside triphosphate catabolic process
GO:0009146.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of purine nucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose or deoxyribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009150.name: purine ribonucleotide metabolic process
GO:0009150.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a purine ribonucleotide, a compound consisting of ribonucleoside (a purine base linked to a ribose sugar) esterified with a phosphate group at either the 3' or 5'-hydroxyl group of the sugar.

GO:0009152.name: purine ribonucleotide biosynthetic process
GO:0009152.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a purine ribonucleotide, a compound consisting of ribonucleoside (a purine base linked to a ribose sugar) esterified with a phosphate group at either the 3' or 5'-hydroxyl group of the sugar.

GO:0009154.name: purine ribonucleotide catabolic process
GO:0009154.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a purine ribonucleotide, a compound consisting of ribonucleoside (a purine base linked to a ribose sugar) esterified with a phosphate group at either the 3' or 5'-hydroxyl group of the sugar.

GO:0009165.name: nucleotide biosynthetic process
GO:0009165.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of nucleotides, any nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the glycose moiety; may be mono-, di- or triphosphate; this definition includes cyclic-nucleotides (nucleoside cyclic phosphates).

GO:0009166.name: nucleotide catabolic process
GO:0009166.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of nucleotides, any nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the glycose moiety; may be mono-, di- or triphosphate; this definition includes cyclic-nucleotides (nucleoside cyclic phosphates).

GO:0009179.name: purine ribonucleoside diphosphate metabolic process
GO:0009179.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving purine ribonucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009180.name: purine ribonucleoside diphosphate biosynthetic process
GO:0009180.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine ribonucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009185.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a ribonucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009188.name: ribonucleoside diphosphate biosynthetic process
GO:0009188.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a ribonucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009191.name: ribonucleoside diphosphate catabolic process
GO:0009191.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a ribonucleoside diphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a ribose sugar esterified with diphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009199.name: ribonucleoside triphosphate metabolic process
GO:0009199.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a ribonucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009201.name: ribonucleoside triphosphate biosynthetic process
GO:0009201.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a ribonucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009203.name: ribonucleoside triphosphate catabolic process
GO:0009203.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a ribonucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a nucleobase linked to a ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009205.name: purine ribonucleoside triphosphate metabolic process
GO:0009205.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving purine ribonucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009206.name: purine ribonucleoside triphosphate biosynthetic process
GO:0009206.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of purine ribonucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009207.name: purine ribonucleoside triphosphate catabolic process
GO:0009207.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of purine ribonucleoside triphosphate, a compound consisting of a purine base linked to a ribose sugar esterified with triphosphate on the sugar.

GO:0009247.name: glycolipid biosynthetic process
GO:0009247.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glycolipid, a class of 1,2-di-O-acylglycerols joined at oxygen 3 by a glycosidic linkage to a carbohydrate part (usually a mono-, di- or tri-saccharide).

GO:0009250.name: glucan biosynthetic process
GO:0009250.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glucans, polysaccharides consisting only of glucose residues.

GO:0009251.name: glucan catabolic process
GO:0009251.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of glucans, polysaccharides consisting only of glucose residues.

GO:0009259.name: ribonucleotide metabolic process
GO:0009259.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a ribonucleotide, a compound consisting of ribonucleoside (a base linked to a ribose sugar) esterified with a phosphate group at either the 3' or 5'-hydroxyl group of the sugar.

GO:0009260.name: ribonucleotide biosynthetic process
GO:0009260.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a ribonucleotide, a compound consisting of ribonucleoside (a base linked to a ribose sugar) esterified with a phosphate group at either the 3' or 5'-hydroxyl group of the sugar.

GO:0009261.name: ribonucleotide catabolic process
GO:0009261.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a ribonucleotide, a compound consisting of ribonucleoside (a base linked to a ribose sugar) esterified with a phosphate group at either the 3' or 5'-hydroxyl group of the sugar.

GO:0009266.name: response to temperature stimulus
GO:0009266.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a temperature stimulus.

GO:0009306.name: protein secretion
GO:0009306.def: The controlled release of proteins from a cell.
synonym: protein secretion during cell fate commitment
protein secretion resulting in cell fate commitment

GO:0009308.name: amine metabolic process
GO:0009308.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any organic compound that is weakly basic in character and contains an amino or a substituted amino group. Amines are called primary, secondary, or tertiary according to whether one, two, or three carbon atoms are attached to the nitrogen atom.

GO:0009309.name: amine biosynthetic process
GO:0009309.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of any organic compound that is weakly basic in character and contains an amino or a substituted amino group. Amines are called primary, secondary, or tertiary according to whether one, two, or three carbon atoms are attached to the nitrogen atom.

GO:0009310.name: amine catabolic process
GO:0009310.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of any organic compound that is weakly basic in character and contains an amino or a substituted amino group. Amines are called primary, secondary, or tertiary according to whether one, two, or three carbon atoms are attached to the nitrogen atom.

GO:0009314.name: response to radiation
GO:0009314.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an electromagnetic radiation stimulus. Electromagnetic radiation is a propagating wave in space with electric and magnetic components. These components oscillate at right angles to each other and to the direction of propagation.

GO:0009399.name: nitrogen fixation
GO:0009399.def: The process in which nitrogen is taken from its relatively inert molecular form (N2) in the atmosphere and converted into ammonium, which is more biologically available.

GO:0009411.name: response to UV
GO:0009411.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an ultraviolet radiation (UV light) stimulus. Ultraviolet radiation is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 to 380 nanometers.

GO:0009414.name: response to water deprivation
GO:0009414.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a water deprivation stimulus, prolonged deprivation of water.

GO:0009415.name: response to water
GO:0009415.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of water.

GO:0009416.name: response to light stimulus
GO:0009416.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a light stimulus, electromagnetic radiation of wavelengths classified as infrared, visible or ultraviolet light.

GO:0009448.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid metabolic process
GO:0009448.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate), an amino acid which acts as a neurotransmitter in some organisms.

GO:0009449.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid biosynthetic process
GO:0009449.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate), an amino acid which acts as a neurotransmitter in some organisms.

GO:0009450.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid catabolic process
GO:0009450.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate), an amino acid which acts as a neurotransmitter in some organisms.

GO:0009566.name: fertilization
GO:0009566.def: The union of gametes of opposite sexes during the process of sexual reproduction to form a zygote. It involves the fusion of the gametic nuclei (karyogamy) and cytoplasm (plasmogamy).

GO:0009581.name: detection of external stimulus
GO:0009581.def: The series of events in which an external stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0009582.name: detection of abiotic stimulus
GO:0009582.def: The series of events in which an (non-living) abiotic stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0009583.name: detection of light stimulus
GO:0009583.def: The series of events in which a light stimulus (in the form of photons) is received and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0009584.name: detection of visible light
GO:0009584.def: The series of events in which a visible light stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. A visible light stimulus is electromagnetic radiation that can be perceived visually by an organism; for organisms lacking a visual system, this can be defined as light with a wavelength within the range 380 to 780 nm.

GO:0009589.name: detection of UV
GO:0009589.def: The series of events in which an ultraviolet radiation (UV light) stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal. Ultraviolet radiation is electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength in the range of 10 to 380 nanometers.

GO:0009590.name: detection of gravity
GO:0009590.def: The series of events in which a gravitational stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0009593.name: detection of chemical stimulus
GO:0009593.def: The series of events in which a chemical stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0009605.name: response to external stimulus
GO:0009605.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an external stimulus.

GO:0009607.name: response to biotic stimulus
GO:0009607.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a biotic stimulus, a stimulus caused or produced by a living organism.

GO:0009611.name: response to wounding
GO:0009611.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating damage to the organism.

GO:0009612.name: response to mechanical stimulus
GO:0009612.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a mechanical stimulus.

GO:0009617.name: response to bacterium
GO:0009617.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a bacterium.

GO:0009620.name: response to fungus
GO:0009620.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus from a fungus.

GO:0009628.name: response to abiotic stimulus
GO:0009628.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an abiotic (not derived from living organisms) stimulus.

GO:0009629.name: response to gravity
GO:0009629.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a gravitational stimulus.

GO:0009636.name: response to toxic substance
GO:0009636.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a toxic stimulus.

GO:0009653.name: anatomical structure morphogenesis
GO:0009653.def: The process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Morphogenesis pertains to the creation of form.

GO:0009712.name: catechol-containing compound metabolic process
GO:0009712.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a compound containing a pyrocatechol (1,2-benzenediol) nucleus or substituent.

GO:0009713.name: catechol-containing compound biosynthetic process
GO:0009713.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of catechol-containing compounds. Catechol is a compound containing a pyrocatechol nucleus or substituent.

GO:0009719.name: response to endogenous stimulus
GO:0009719.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus arising within the organism.

GO:0009725.name: response to hormone
GO:0009725.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a hormone stimulus.

GO:0009743.name: response to carbohydrate
GO:0009743.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a carbohydrate stimulus.

GO:0009746.name: response to hexose
GO:0009746.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a hexose stimulus.

GO:0009749.name: response to glucose
GO:0009749.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a glucose stimulus.

GO:0009755.name: hormone-mediated signaling pathway
GO:0009755.def: The series of molecular signals mediated by the detection of a hormone.

GO:0009786.name: regulation of asymmetric cell division
GO:0009786.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of asymmetric cell division.

GO:0009790.name: embryo development
GO:0009790.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an embryo from its formation until the end of its embryonic life stage. The end of the embryonic stage is organism-specific. For example, for mammals, the process would begin with zygote formation and end with birth. For insects, the process would begin at zygote formation and end with larval hatching. For plant zygotic embryos, this would be from zygote formation to the end of seed dormancy. For plant vegetative embryos, this would be from the initial determination of the cell or group of cells to form an embryo until the point when the embryo becomes independent of the parent plant.

GO:0009791.name: post-embryonic development
GO:0009791.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the organism over time, from the completion of embryonic development to the mature structure. See embryonic development.

GO:0009792.name: embryo development ending in birth or egg hatching
GO:0009792.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an embryo over time, from zygote formation until the end of the embryonic life stage. The end of the embryonic life stage is organism-specific and may be somewhat arbitrary; for mammals it is usually considered to be birth, for insects the hatching of the first instar larva from the eggshell.

GO:0009798.name: axis specification
GO:0009798.def: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of a pattern along a line or around a point.

GO:0009880.name: embryonic pattern specification
GO:0009880.def: The process that results in the patterns of cell differentiation that will arise in an embryo.

GO:0009886.name: post-embryonic animal morphogenesis
GO:0009886.def: The process, occurring after animal embryonic development, by which anatomical structures are generated and organized.
GO:0009886.synonym: post-embryonic morphogenesis of an anatomical structure

GO:0009887.name: animal organ morphogenesis
GO:0009887.def: Morphogenesis of an animal organ. An organ is defined as a tissue or set of tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Morphogenesis is the process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

GO:0009888.name: tissue development
GO:0009888.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a tissue over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0009889.name: regulation of biosynthetic process
GO:0009889.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of substances.

GO:0009890.name: negative regulation of biosynthetic process
GO:0009890.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the rate of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of substances.

GO:0009891.name: positive regulation of biosynthetic process
GO:0009891.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of substances.

GO:0009892.name: negative regulation of metabolic process
GO:0009892.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways within a cell or an organism.
synonym: negative regulation of multicellular organismal metabolic process

GO:0009893.name: positive regulation of metabolic process
GO:0009893.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways within a cell or an organism.
synonym: positive regulation of multicellular organismal metabolic process

GO:0009894.name: regulation of catabolic process
GO:0009894.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances.

GO:0009895.name: negative regulation of catabolic process
GO:0009895.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances.

GO:0009896.name: positive regulation of catabolic process
GO:0009896.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of substances.

GO:0009913.name: epidermal cell differentiation
GO:0009913.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an epidermal cell, any of the cells making up the epidermis.

GO:0009914.name: hormone transport
GO:0009914.def: The directed movement of hormones into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0009948.name: anterior/posterior axis specification
GO:0009948.def: The establishment, maintenance and elaboration of the anterior/posterior axis. The anterior-posterior axis is defined by a line that runs from the head or mouth of an organism to the tail or opposite end of the organism.

GO:0009952.name: anterior/posterior pattern specification
GO:0009952.def: The regionalization process in which specific areas of cell differentiation are determined along the anterior-posterior axis. The anterior-posterior axis is defined by a line that runs from the head or mouth of an organism to the tail or opposite end of the organism.

GO:0009966.name: regulation of signal transduction
GO:0009966.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

GO:0009967.name: positive regulation of signal transduction
GO:0009967.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

GO:0009968.name: negative regulation of signal transduction
GO:0009968.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction.

GO:0009977.name: proton motive force dependent protein transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0009977.def: Catalysis of the transfer of proteins from one side of a membrane to the other. Transportation is dependent on pH gradient across the membrane.

GO:0009987.name: cellular process
GO:0009987.def: Any process that is carried out at the cellular level, but not necessarily restricted to a single cell. For example, cell communication occurs among more than one cell, but occurs at the cellular level.

GO:0009992.name: intracellular water homeostasis
GO:0009992.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of water within a cell.

GO:0009994.name: oocyte differentiation
GO:0009994.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized immature germ cell acquires the specialized features of a mature female gamete.

GO:0010001.name: glial cell differentiation
GO:0010001.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a glial cell.

GO:0010002.name: cardioblast differentiation
GO:0010002.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized mesodermal cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardioblast. A cardioblast is a cardiac precursor cell. It is a cell that has been committed to a cardiac fate, but will undergo more cell division rather than terminally differentiating.

GO:0010004.name: gastrulation involving germ band extension
GO:0010004.def: A complex and coordinated series of cellular movements, including germ band extension, that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development. An example of this process is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0010032.name: meiotic chromosome condensation
GO:0010032.def: Compaction of chromatin structure prior to meiosis in eukaryotic cells.
GO:0010032.synonym: chromosome condensation involved in meiotic cell cycle

GO:0010038.name: response to metal ion
GO:0010038.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a metal ion stimulus.

GO:0010039.name: response to iron ion
GO:0010039.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an iron ion stimulus.

GO:0010070.name: zygote asymmetric cell division
GO:0010070.def: The division of the zygote into two daughter cells that will adopt developmentally distinct potentials.

GO:0010109.name: regulation of photosynthesis
GO:0010109.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of photosynthesis.

GO:0010155.name: regulation of proton transport
GO:0010155.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of proton transport into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010160.name: formation of animal organ boundary
GO:0010160.def: The regionalization process that specifies animal organ primordium boundaries resulting in a restriction of organogenesis to a limited spatial domain and keeping the organ separate from surrounding tissues.

GO:0010171.name: body morphogenesis
GO:0010171.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the soma are generated and organized.

GO:0010232.name: vascular transport
GO:0010232.def: The directed movement of substances, into, out of or within a cell, either in a vascular tissue or in the vascular membrane.

GO:0010256.name: endomembrane system organization
GO:0010256.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the endomembrane system.

GO:0010453.name: regulation of cell fate commitment
GO:0010453.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field.

GO:0010454.name: negative regulation of cell fate commitment
GO:0010454.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency or rate of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field.

GO:0010455.name: positive regulation of cell fate commitment
GO:0010455.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency or rate of cell fate commitment. Cell fate commitment is the commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a cell (the initial one-cell zygote) or within a developmental field.

GO:0010456.name: cell proliferation in dorsal spinal cord
GO:0010456.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of the dorsal spinal cord cell population.

GO:0010463.name: mesenchymal cell proliferation
GO:0010463.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a mesenchymal cell population. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets.

GO:0010464.name: regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation
GO:0010464.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of mesenchymal cell proliferation. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets.

GO:0010467.name: gene expression
GO:0010467.def: The process in which a gene's sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA). This includes the production of an RNA transcript and its processing, as well as translation and maturation for protein-coding genes.

GO:0010468.name: regulation of gene expression
GO:0010468.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression. Gene expression is the process in which a gene's coding sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA).

GO:0010469.name: regulation of signaling receptor activity
GO:0010469.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a signaling receptor activity. Receptor activity is when a molecule combines with an extracellular or intracellular messenger to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0010470.name: regulation of gastrulation
GO:0010470.def: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of gastrulation. Gastrulation is the complex and coordinated series of cellular movements that occurs at the end of cleavage during embryonic development of most animals.

GO:0010481.name: epidermal cell division
GO:0010481.def: Any process resulting in the physical partitioning and separation of an epidermal cell, any of the cells making up the epidermis, into daughter cells.

GO:0010482.name: regulation of epidermal cell division
GO:0010482.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the physical partitioning and separation of an epidermal cell into daughter cells. An epidermal cell is any of the cells that make up the epidermis.

GO:0010496.name: intercellular transport
GO:0010496.def: The movement of substances between cells.

GO:0010543.name: regulation of platelet activation
GO:0010543.def: Any process that modulates the rate or frequency of platelet activation. Platelet activation is a series of progressive, overlapping events triggered by exposure of the platelets to subendothelial tissue.

GO:0010544.name: negative regulation of platelet activation
GO:0010544.def: Any process that decreases the rate or frequency of platelet activation. Platelet activation is a series of progressive, overlapping events triggered by exposure of the platelets to subendothelial tissue.

GO:0010549.name: regulation of membrane disassembly
GO:0010549.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of membrane disassembly.

GO:0010556.name: regulation of macromolecule biosynthetic process
GO:0010556.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

GO:0010557.name: positive regulation of macromolecule biosynthetic process
GO:0010557.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

GO:0010558.name: negative regulation of macromolecule biosynthetic process
