GO:0010559.name: regulation of glycoprotein biosynthetic process
GO:0010559.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a glycoprotein, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

GO:0010560.name: positive regulation of glycoprotein biosynthetic process
GO:0010560.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a glycoprotein, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

GO:0010561.name: negative regulation of glycoprotein biosynthetic process
GO:0010561.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a glycoprotein, a protein that contains covalently bound glycose (i.e. monosaccharide) residues; the glycose occurs most commonly as oligosaccharide or fairly small polysaccharide but occasionally as monosaccharide.

GO:0010562.name: positive regulation of phosphorus metabolic process
GO:0010562.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving phosphorus or compounds containing phosphorus.

GO:0010563.name: negative regulation of phosphorus metabolic process
GO:0010563.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving phosphorus or compounds containing phosphorus.

GO:0010564.name: regulation of cell cycle process
GO:0010564.def: Any process that modulates a cellular process that is involved in the progression of biochemical and morphological phases and events that occur in a cell during successive cell replication or nuclear replication events.

GO:0010565.name: regulation of ketone metabolic process
GO:0010565.def: Any process that modulates the chemical reactions and pathways involving any of a class of organic compounds that contain the carbonyl group, CO, and in which the carbonyl group is bonded only to carbon atoms. GO:0010566.name: regulation of ketone biosynthetic process
GO:0010566.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a ketone, carried out by individual cells.

GO:0010567.name: regulation of ketone catabolic process
GO:0010567.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a ketone, carried out by individual cells.

GO:0010572.name: positive regulation of platelet activation
GO:0010572.def: Any process that increases the rate or frequency of platelet activation. Platelet activation is a series of progressive, overlapping events triggered by exposure of the platelets to subendothelial tissue.

GO:0010594.name: regulation of endothelial cell migration
GO:0010594.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the orderly movement of an endothelial cell into the extracellular matrix to form an endothelium.

GO:0010595.name: positive regulation of endothelial cell migration
GO:0010595.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the orderly movement of an endothelial cell into the extracellular matrix to form an endothelium.

GO:0010596.name: negative regulation of endothelial cell migration
GO:0010596.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the orderly movement of an endothelial cell into the extracellular matrix to form an endothelium.

GO:0010604.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving macromolecules, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

GO:0010608.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression after the production of an RNA transcript.

GO:0010611.name: regulation of cardiac muscle hypertrophy
GO:0010611.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of the heart due to an increase in size (not length) of individual cardiac muscle fibers, without cell division.

GO:0010612.name: regulation of cardiac muscle adaptation
GO:0010612.def: Any process that modulates the rate, extent or frequency of the process in which cardiac muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors.

GO:0010613.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle hypertrophy

GO:0010614.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle hypertrophy
GO:0010614.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of the heart due to an increase in size (not length) of individual cardiac muscle fibers, without cell division.

GO:0010615.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle adaptation

GO:0010623.name: programmed cell death involved in cell development
GO:0010623.def: The activation of endogenous cellular processes that result in the death of a cell as part of its development.

GO:0010624.name: regulation of Schwann cell proliferation
GO:0010624.def: Any process that modulates the frequency or rate of multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells, resulting in the expansion of their population. Schwann cells are a type of glial cell in the peripheral nervous system.

GO:0010625.name: positive regulation of Schwann cell proliferation
GO:0010625.def: Any process that increases the frequency or rate of the multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells, resulting in the expansion of their population. Schwann cells are a type of glial cell in the peripheral nervous system.

GO:0010626.name: negative regulation of Schwann cell proliferation
GO:0010626.def: Any process that decreases the frequency or extent of the multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells, resulting in the expansion of their population. Schwann cells are a type of glial cell in the peripheral nervous system.

GO:0010628.name: positive regulation of gene expression
GO:0010628.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression. Gene expression is the process in which a gene's coding sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA).

GO:0010629.name: negative regulation of gene expression
GO:0010629.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression. Gene expression is the process in which a gene's coding sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA).

GO:0010631.name: epithelial cell migration
GO:0010631.def: The orderly movement of an epithelial cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0010632.name: regulation of epithelial cell migration
GO:0010632.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell migration.

GO:0010633.name: negative regulation of epithelial cell migration
GO:0010633.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell migration.

GO:0010634.name: positive regulation of epithelial cell migration
GO:0010634.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell migration.

GO:0010638.name: positive regulation of organelle organization
GO:0010638.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of a process involved in the formation, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an organelle.
synonym: positive regulation of organelle organization and biogenesis

GO:0010639.name: negative regulation of organelle organization
GO:0010639.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of a process involved in the formation, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an organelle.
synonym: negative regulation of organelle organization and biogenesis

GO:0010646.name: regulation of cell communication
GO:0010646.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell communication. Cell communication is the process that mediates interactions between a cell and its surroundings. Encompasses interactions such as signaling or attachment between one cell and another cell, between a cell and an extracellular matrix, or between a cell and any other aspect of its environment.

GO:0010647.name: positive regulation of cell communication
GO:0010647.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell communication. Cell communication is the process that mediates interactions between a cell and its surroundings. Encompasses interactions such as signaling or attachment between one cell and another cell, between a cell and an extracellular matrix, or between a cell and any other aspect of its environment.

GO:0010648.name: negative regulation of cell communication
GO:0010648.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of cell communication. Cell communication is the process that mediates interactions between a cell and its surroundings. Encompasses interactions such as signaling or attachment between one cell and another cell, between a cell and an extracellular matrix, or between a cell and any other aspect of its environment.

GO:0010656.name: negative regulation of muscle cell apoptotic process
GO:0010656.def: Any process that decreases the rate or frequency of muscle cell apoptotic process, a form of programmed cell death induced by external or internal signals that trigger the activity of proteolytic caspases whose actions dismantle a muscle cell and result in its death.
GO:0010656.synonym: negative regulation of muscle cell apoptosis

GO:0010657.name: muscle cell apoptotic process
GO:0010657.def: A form of programmed cell death induced by external or internal signals that trigger the activity of proteolytic caspases, whose actions dismantle a muscle cell and result in its death. A muscle cell is a mature contractile cell, commonly known as a myocyte, that forms one of three kinds of muscle.

GO:0010658.name: striated muscle cell apoptotic process
GO:0010658.def: A form of programmed cell death induced by external or internal signals that trigger the activity of proteolytic caspases, whose actions dismantle a striated muscle cell and result in its death. Striated muscle cells make up striated muscle fibers which are divided by transverse bands into striations.

GO:0010659.name: cardiac muscle cell apoptotic process
GO:0010659.def: A form of programmed cell death induced by external or internal signals that trigger the activity of proteolytic caspases, whose actions dismantle a cardiac muscle cell and result in its death. Cardiac muscle cells are striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction.

GO:0010660.name: regulation of muscle cell apoptotic process
GO:0010660.def: Any process that modulates the rate or frequency of muscle cell apoptotic process, a form of programmed cell death induced by external or internal signals that trigger the activity of proteolytic caspases whose actions dismantle a muscle cell and result in its death.

GO:0010668.name: ectodermal cell differentiation
GO:0010668.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an ectodermal cell. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0010700.name: negative regulation of norepinephrine secretion
GO:0010700.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of norepinephrine.

GO:0010701.name: positive regulation of norepinephrine secretion
GO:0010701.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of norepinephrine.

GO:0010710.name: regulation of collagen catabolic process
GO:0010710.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of collagen catabolism. Collagen catabolism is the proteolytic chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of collagen in the extracellular matrix.

GO:0010711.name: negative regulation of collagen catabolic process
GO:0010711.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of collagen catabolism. Collagen catabolism is the proteolytic chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of collagen in the extracellular matrix.
synonym: down regulation of collagen catabolic process

GO:0010712.name: regulation of collagen metabolic process
GO:0010712.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the metabolism of collagen, any of a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals.

GO:0010713.name: negative regulation of collagen metabolic process
GO:0010713.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the metabolism of collagen, any of a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals.

GO:0010714.name: positive regulation of collagen metabolic process
GO:0010714.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the metabolism of collagen, any of a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals.

GO:0010715.name: regulation of extracellular matrix disassembly
GO:0010715.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of extracellular matrix disassembly. Extracellular matrix disassembly is a process that results in the breakdown of the extracellular matrix.

GO:0010716.name: negative regulation of extracellular matrix disassembly
GO:0010716.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of extracellular matrix disassembly. Extracellular matrix disassembly is a process that results in the breakdown of the extracellular matrix.
synonym: down regulation of extracellular matrix disassembly
negative regulation of extracellular matrix breakdown
negative regulation of extracellular matrix degradation

GO:0010717.name: regulation of epithelial to mesenchymal transition
GO:0010717.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of epithelial to mesenchymal transition. Epithelial to mesenchymal transition where an epithelial cell loses apical/basolateral polarity, severs intercellular adhesive junctions, degrades basement membrane components and becomes a migratory mesenchymal cell.

GO:0010718.name: positive regulation of epithelial to mesenchymal transition
GO:0010718.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of epithelial to mesenchymal transition. Epithelial to mesenchymal transition is where an epithelial cell loses apical/basolateral polarity, severs intercellular adhesive junctions, degrades basement membrane components and becomes a migratory mesenchymal cell.

GO:0010719.name: negative regulation of epithelial to mesenchymal transition
GO:0010719.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of epithelial to mesenchymal transition. Epithelial to mesenchymal transition where an epithelial cell loses apical/basolateral polarity, severs intercellular adhesive junctions, degrades basement membrane components and becomes a migratory mesenchymal cell.

GO:0010720.name: positive regulation of cell development
GO:0010720.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of the progression of the cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0010721.name: negative regulation of cell development
GO:0010721.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the progression of the cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0010725.name: regulation of primitive erythrocyte differentiation
GO:0010725.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of primitive erythrocyte differentiation. Primitive erythrocyte differentiation occurs as part of the process of primitive hemopoiesis.
synonym: regulation of primitive red blood cell differentiation

GO:0010742.name: macrophage derived foam cell differentiation
GO:0010742.def: The process in which a monocyte acquires the specialized features of a foam cell. A foam cell is a type of cell containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

GO:0010743.name: regulation of macrophage derived foam cell differentiation
GO:0010743.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage derived foam cell differentiation. Macrophage derived foam cell differentiation is the process in which a macrophage acquires the specialized features of a foam cell. A foam cell is a type of cell containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

Macrophage derived foam cell differentiation is the process in which a macrophage acquires the specialized features of a foam cell. A foam cell is a type of cell containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

GO:0010758.name: regulation of macrophage chemotaxis
GO:0010758.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage chemotaxis. Macrophage chemotaxis is the movement of a macrophage in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0010759.name: positive regulation of macrophage chemotaxis
GO:0010759.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage chemotaxis. Macrophage chemotaxis is the movement of a macrophage in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0010760.name: negative regulation of macrophage chemotaxis
GO:0010760.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage chemotaxis. Macrophage chemotaxis is the movement of a macrophage in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0010761.name: fibroblast migration
GO:0010761.def: Cell migration that is accomplished by extension and retraction of a fibroblast pseudopodium. A fibroblast is a connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules.

GO:0010762.name: regulation of fibroblast migration
GO:0010762.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of fibroblast cell migration. Fibroblast cell migration is accomplished by extension and retraction of a pseudopodium.

GO:0010763.name: positive regulation of fibroblast migration
GO:0010763.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of fibroblast cell migration. Fibroblast cell migration is accomplished by extension and retraction of a pseudopodium.
GO:0010763.synonym: positive regulation of fibroblast cell migration

GO:0010764.name: negative regulation of fibroblast migration
GO:0010764.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of fibroblast cell migration. Fibroblast cell migration is accomplished by extension and retraction of a pseudopodium.
GO:0010764.synonym: negative regulation of fibroblast cell migration

GO:0010765.name: positive regulation of sodium ion transport
GO:0010765.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of sodium ions (Na+) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010766.name: negative regulation of sodium ion transport
GO:0010766.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of sodium ions (Na+) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010770.name: positive regulation of cell morphogenesis
GO:0010770.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell morphogenesis contributing to cell differentiation. Cell morphogenesis involved in differentiation is the change in form (cell shape and size) that occurs when relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the cells, tissues, or organs of the mature organism or some other relatively stable phase of the organism's life history.

GO:0010771.name: negative regulation of cell morphogenesis
GO:0010771.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of cell morphogenesis contributing to cell differentiation. Cell morphogenesis involved in differentiation is the change in form (cell shape and size) that occurs when relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the cells, tissues, or organs of the mature organism or some other relatively stable phase of the organism's life history.

GO:0010816.name: calcitonin catabolic process
GO:0010816.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of the peptide calcitonin.

GO:0010817.name: regulation of hormone levels
GO:0010817.def: Any process that modulates the levels of hormone within an organism or a tissue. A hormone is any substance formed in very small amounts in one specialized organ or group of cells and carried (sometimes in the bloodstream) to another organ or group of cells in the same organism, upon which it has a specific regulatory action.

GO:0010818.name: T cell chemotaxis
GO:0010818.def: The directed movement of a T cell in response to an external stimulus. A T cell is a type of lymphocyte whose defining characteristic is the expression of a T cell receptor complex.

GO:0010819.name: regulation of T cell chemotaxis
GO:0010819.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of T cell chemotaxis. T cell chemotaxis is the directed movement of a T cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0010820.name: positive regulation of T cell chemotaxis
GO:0010820.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of T cell chemotaxis. T cell chemotaxis is the directed movement of a T cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0010827.name: regulation of D-glucose transmembrane transport
GO:0010827.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glucose transport across a membrane. Glucose transport is the directed movement of the hexose monosaccharide glucose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010828.name: positive regulation of D-glucose transmembrane transport
GO:0010828.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of glucose transport across a membrane. Glucose transport is the directed movement of the hexose monosaccharide glucose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010829.name: negative regulation of D-glucose transmembrane transport

GO:0010830.name: regulation of myotube differentiation
GO:0010830.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of myotube differentiation. Myotube differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0010831.name: positive regulation of myotube differentiation
GO:0010831.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of myotube differentiation. Myotube differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0010832.name: negative regulation of myotube differentiation
GO:0010832.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of myotube differentiation. Myotube differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0010837.name: regulation of keratinocyte proliferation
GO:0010837.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of keratinocyte proliferation. Keratinocyte proliferation is the multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0010838.name: positive regulation of keratinocyte proliferation
GO:0010838.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of keratinocyte proliferation. Keratinocyte proliferation is the multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0010839.name: negative regulation of keratinocyte proliferation
GO:0010839.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of keratinocyte proliferation. Keratinocyte proliferation is the multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0010842.name: retina layer formation
GO:0010842.def: The process in which the vertebrate retina is organized into three laminae: the outer nuclear layer (ONL), which contains photoreceptor nuclei; the inner nuclear layer (INL), which contains amacrine, bipolar and horizontal cells; and the retinal ganglion cell (RGC) layer. Between the inner and outer nuclear layers, the outer plexiform layer (OPL) contains connections between the photoreceptors and bipolar and horizontal cells. The inner plexiform layer (IPL) is positioned between the INL and the ganglion cell layer and contains the dendrites of RGCs and processes of bipolar and amacrine cells. Spanning all layers of the retina are the radially oriented Mueller glia.

GO:0010876.name: lipid localization
GO:0010876.def: Any process in which a lipid is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

GO:0010882.name: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling
GO:0010882.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction by changing the calcium ion signals that trigger contraction.
GO:0010882.synonym: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction by calcium ion signalling

GO:0010893.name: positive regulation of steroid biosynthetic process
GO:0010893.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroids, compounds with a 1,2,cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus.

GO:0010894.name: negative regulation of steroid biosynthetic process
GO:0010894.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroids, compounds with a 1,2,cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus.

GO:0010906.name: regulation of glucose metabolic process
GO:0010906.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of glucose metabolism. Glucose metabolic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways involving glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose.

GO:0010907.name: positive regulation of glucose metabolic process
GO:0010907.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of glucose metabolism. Glucose metabolic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways involving glucose, the aldohexose gluco-hexose.

GO:0010927.name: cellular component assembly involved in morphogenesis
GO:0010927.def: The cellular component assembly that is part of the initial shaping of the component during its developmental progression.

GO:0010931.name: macrophage tolerance induction
GO:0010931.def: A process involving any mechanism for tolerance induction in macrophages.

GO:0010932.name: regulation of macrophage tolerance induction
GO:0010932.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of macrophage tolerance induction.

GO:0010933.name: positive regulation of macrophage tolerance induction
GO:0010933.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of B cell tolerance induction.

GO:0010934.name: macrophage cytokine production
GO:0010934.def: The appearance of a macrophage cytokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0010935.name: regulation of macrophage cytokine production
GO:0010935.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage cytokine production. Macrophage cytokine production is the appearance of a chemokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0010936.name: negative regulation of macrophage cytokine production
GO:0010936.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage cytokine production. Macrophage cytokine production is the appearance of a chemokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0010937.name: regulation of cytoplasmic microtubule depolymerization
GO:0010937.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cytoplasmic microtubule depolymerization.

GO:0010938.name: cytoplasmic microtubule depolymerization
GO:0010938.def: The removal of tubulin heterodimers from one or both ends of a cytoplasmic microtubule.

GO:0010948.name: negative regulation of cell cycle process
GO:0010948.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of a cellular process that is involved in the progression of biochemical and morphological phases and events that occur in a cell during successive cell replication or nuclear replication events.

GO:0010954.name: positive regulation of protein processing
GO:0010954.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage.
GO:0010954.synonym: positive regulation of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage

GO:0010955.name: negative regulation of protein processing
GO:0010955.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage.
GO:0010955.synonym: negative regulation of protein maturation by peptide bond cleavage

GO:0010958.name: regulation of amino acid import across plasma membrane
GO:0010958.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of amino acid import into a cell.

GO:0010959.name: regulation of metal ion transport
GO:0010959.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of metal ion transport. Metal ion transport is the directed movement of metal ions, any metal ion with an electric charge, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010962.name: regulation of glucan biosynthetic process
GO:0010962.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of glucan biosynthesis. Glucan biosynthetic processes are the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of glucans, polysaccharides consisting only of glucose residues.

GO:0010966.name: regulation of phosphate transport
GO:0010966.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of phosphate transport. Phosphate transport is the directed movement of phosphate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0010968.name: regulation of microtubule nucleation
GO:0010968.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of microtubule nucleation. Microtubule nucleation is the 'de novo' formation of a microtubule, in which tubulin heterodimers form metastable oligomeric aggregates, some of which go on to support formation of a complete microtubule. Microtubule nucleation usually occurs from a specific site within a cell.

GO:0010970.name: transport along microtubule
GO:0010970.def: The movement of organelles or other particles from one location in the cell to another along microtubules, driven by motor activity.
synonym: establishment of localization by movement along microtubule

GO:0010975.name: regulation of neuron projection development
GO:0010975.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of neuron projection development. Neuron projection development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

GO:0010976.name: positive regulation of neuron projection development
GO:0010976.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of neuron projection development. Neuron projection development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

GO:0010977.name: negative regulation of neuron projection development
GO:0010977.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of neuron projection development. Neuron projection development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

GO:0012501.name: programmed cell death
GO:0012501.def: A process which begins when a cell receives an internal or external signal and activates a series of biochemical events (signaling pathway). The process ends with the death of the cell.

GO:0012505.name: endomembrane system
GO:0012505.def: A collection of membranous structures involved in transport within the cell. The main components of the endomembrane system are endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, vesicles, cell membrane and nuclear envelope. Members of the endomembrane system pass materials through each other or though the use of vesicles.

GO:0012506.name: vesicle membrane
GO:0012506.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding any membrane-bounded vesicle in the cell.

GO:0014000.name: morula development
GO:0014000.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the morula over time. The morula is a spherical embryonic mass of blastomeres formed before the blastula and resulting from cleavage of the fertilized ovum.

GO:0014002.name: astrocyte development
GO:0014002.def: The process aimed at the progression of an astrocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An astrocyte is the most abundant type of glial cell. Astrocytes provide support for neurons and regulate the environment in which they function.

GO:0014003.name: oligodendrocyte development
GO:0014003.def: The process aimed at the progression of an oligodendrocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An oligodendrocyte is a type of glial cell involved in myelinating the axons in the central nervous system.

GO:0014004.name: microglia differentiation
GO:0014004.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell. Microglia are glial cells that act as the immune cells of the central nervous system. They form part of the supporting structure of this system.

GO:0014005.name: microglia development
GO:0014005.def: The process aimed at the progression of a microglial cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0014006.name: regulation of microglia differentiation
GO:0014006.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.

GO:0014007.name: negative regulation of microglia differentiation
GO:0014007.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.
synonym: negative regulation of microglial cell differentiation

GO:0014008.name: positive regulation of microglia differentiation
GO:0014008.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.
synonym: positive regulation of microglial cell differentiation

GO:0014009.name: glial cell proliferation
GO:0014009.def: The multiplication or reproduction of glial cells by cell division, resulting in the expansion of their population. Glial cells exist throughout the nervous system, and include Schwann cells, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes among others.

GO:0014010.name: Schwann cell proliferation
GO:0014010.def: The multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells, resulting in the expansion of their population. Schwann cells are a type of glial cell in the peripheral nervous system.

GO:0014013.name: regulation of gliogenesis
GO:0014013.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.

GO:0014014.name: negative regulation of gliogenesis
GO:0014014.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.

GO:0014015.name: positive regulation of gliogenesis
GO:0014015.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.

GO:0014016.name: neuroblast differentiation
GO:0014016.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuroblast. There are at least four stages through which the pluripotent cells of epiblast or blastula become neuroblasts.

GO:0014019.name: neuroblast development
GO:0014019.def: The process aimed at the progression of a neuroblast over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific state, to the mature neuroblast. It does not include processes where the neuroblast turns into a glial cell or a neuron.

GO:0014020.name: primary neural tube formation
GO:0014020.def: The formation of the neural tube from an epithelial cell sheet (the neuroepithelium or neural plate). In primary neurulation, the cells surrounding the neural plate direct the neural plate cells to proliferate, invaginate, and pinch off from the surface to form a hollow epithelial tube. Primary neurulation is the typical mechanism of formation of the anterior neural tube.

GO:0014023.name: neural rod formation
GO:0014023.def: The formation of a solid rod of neurectoderm derived from the neural keel. The neural rod is roughly circular in cross section. Neural rod formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts.

GO:0014025.name: neural keel formation
GO:0014025.def: The formation of a thickened region of the neurectoderm that is roughly triangular in cross section. The neural keel develops from the neural plate and develops into the neural rod. Neural keel formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts.

GO:0014028.name: notochord formation
GO:0014028.def: The formation of the notochord from the chordamesoderm. The notochord is composed of large cells packed within a firm connective tissue sheath and is found in all chordates at the ventral surface of the neural tube. In vertebrates, the notochord contributes to the vertebral column.

GO:0014029.name: neural crest formation
GO:0014029.def: The formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds.

GO:0014031.name: mesenchymal cell development
GO:0014031.def: The process aimed at the progression of a mesenchymal cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0014032.name: neural crest cell development
GO:0014032.def: The process aimed at the progression of a neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0014033.name: neural crest cell differentiation
GO:0014033.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neural crest cell.

GO:0014037.name: Schwann cell differentiation
GO:0014037.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a Schwann cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function.

GO:0014038.name: regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
GO:0014038.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.

GO:0014039.name: negative regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
GO:0014039.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.
synonym: down regulation of Schwann cell differentiation

GO:0014040.name: positive regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
GO:0014040.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.
synonym: up regulation of Schwann cell differentiation

GO:0014041.name: regulation of neuron maturation
GO:0014041.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation, the process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of a neuron. This process is independent of morphogenetic change.

GO:0014042.name: positive regulation of neuron maturation
GO:0014042.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation.

GO:0014043.name: negative regulation of neuron maturation
GO:0014043.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation.

GO:0014044.name: Schwann cell development
GO:0014044.def: The process aimed at the progression of a Schwann cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function.

GO:0014046.name: dopamine secretion
GO:0014046.def: The regulated release of dopamine by a cell. Dopamine is a catecholamine and a precursor of adrenaline and noradrenaline. It acts as a neurotransmitter in the central nervous system but it is also produced peripherally and acts as a hormone.

GO:0014047.name: glutamate secretion
GO:0014047.def: The controlled release of glutamate by a cell. The glutamate is the most abundant excitatory neurotransmitter in the nervous system.

GO:0014048.name: regulation of glutamate secretion
GO:0014048.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.

GO:0014049.name: positive regulation of glutamate secretion
GO:0014049.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.

GO:0014050.name: negative regulation of glutamate secretion
GO:0014050.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.

GO:0014051.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
GO:0014051.def: The regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid by a cell or a tissue. The gamma-aminobutyric acid is the principal inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain but is also found in several extraneural tissues.

GO:0014052.name: regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
GO:0014052.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.

GO:0014053.name: negative regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
GO:0014053.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.
synonym: down regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

GO:0014054.name: positive regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
GO:0014054.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.
synonym: up regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

GO:0014055.name: acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0014055.def: The regulated release of acetylcholine by a cell. The acetylcholine acts as a neurotransmitter that acts in both the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and central nervous system (CNS).

GO:0014056.name: regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0014056.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.

GO:0014057.name: positive regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0014057.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.

GO:0014058.name: negative regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0014058.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.

GO:0014059.name: regulation of dopamine secretion
GO:0014059.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of dopamine.

GO:0014060.name: regulation of epinephrine secretion
GO:0014060.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of epinephrine.

GO:0014061.name: regulation of norepinephrine secretion
GO:0014061.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of norepinephrine.

GO:0014062.name: regulation of serotonin secretion
GO:0014062.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.

GO:0014063.name: negative regulation of serotonin secretion
GO:0014063.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.

GO:0014064.name: positive regulation of serotonin secretion
GO:0014064.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.

GO:0014074.name: response to purine-containing compound
GO:0014074.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a purine-containing compound stimulus.

GO:0014075.name: response to amine
GO:0014075.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amine stimulus. An amine is a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

GO:0014706.name: striated muscle tissue development
GO:0014706.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a striated muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Striated muscle contain fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations, and cardiac and skeletal muscle are types of striated muscle. Skeletal muscle myoblasts fuse to form myotubes and eventually multinucleated muscle fibers. The fusion of cardiac cells is very rare and can only form binucleate cells.

GO:0014707.name: branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
GO:0014707.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The branchiomeric muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls facial expression, pharyngeal and laryngeal function, operating the jaw. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. Branchiomeric muscles of mammals correspond to the gill musculature of fish.

GO:0014711.name: regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
GO:0014711.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0014712.name: positive regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
GO:0014712.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0014713.name: negative regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
GO:0014713.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0014716.name: skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014716.def: Skeletal muscle satellite cell asymmetric division that occurs during a process in which damaged muscle tissue is being rebuilt.
GO:0014716.synonym: satellite cell asymmetric division involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

GO:0014717.name: regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014717.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of satellite cell activation. The satellite cell activation is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate.

GO:0014718.name: positive regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014718.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of activation of satellite cell involved in skeletal muscle regeneration. The activation of satellite cell is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate.

GO:0014719.name: skeletal muscle satellite cell activation
GO:0014719.def: The change of a skeletal muscle satellite cell from a mitotically quiescent to a mitotically active state following exposure to some activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage.

GO:0014722.name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling
GO:0014722.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing the calcium ion signals that trigger contraction.
GO:0014722.synonym: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signalling

GO:0014733.name: regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation
GO:0014733.def: Any process in which skeletal muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.

GO:0014734.name: skeletal muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014734.def: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of an organ due to an increase in size (not length) of individual muscle fibers without cell division. In the case of skeletal muscle cells this happens due to the additional synthesis of sarcomeric proteins and assembly of myofibrils.

GO:0014741.name: negative regulation of muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014741.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of muscle hypertrophy.

GO:0014742.name: positive regulation of muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014742.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of muscle hypertrophy.

GO:0014743.name: regulation of muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014743.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of muscle hypertrophy.

GO:0014744.name: positive regulation of muscle adaptation
GO:0014744.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of muscle adaptation.

GO:0014745.name: negative regulation of muscle adaptation
GO:0014745.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of muscle adaptation.

GO:0014805.name: smooth muscle adaptation
GO:0014805.def: Any process in which smooth muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.

GO:0014807.name: regulation of somitogenesis
GO:0014807.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of somitogenesis.

GO:0014812.name: muscle cell migration
GO:0014812.def: The orderly movement of a muscle cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0014816.name: skeletal muscle satellite cell differentiation
GO:0014816.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a satellite cell.

GO:0014819.name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction
GO:0014819.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction.

GO:0014821.name: phasic smooth muscle contraction
GO:0014821.def: A process in which force is generated within phasic smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. In the phasic smooth muscle, the muscle contraction occurs without an ordered sarcomeric structure. Phasic smooth muscle contraction occurs in a series of discrete contractions and relaxations.

GO:0014827.name: intestine smooth muscle contraction
GO:0014827.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the intestine. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The intestine is the section of the alimentary canal from the stomach to the anal canal. It includes the large intestine and small intestine.

GO:0014831.name: gastro-intestinal system smooth muscle contraction
GO:0014831.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the gastro-intestinal system. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The gastro-intestinal system generally refers to the digestive structures stretching from the mouth to anus, but does not include the accessory glandular organs (liver, pancreas and biliary tract).

GO:0014832.name: urinary bladder smooth muscle contraction
GO:0014832.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the urinary bladder. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The urinary bladder is a musculomembranous sac along the urinary tract.

GO:0014833.name: skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division
GO:0014833.def: The asymmetric division of a skeletal muscle satellite stem cell to produce two daughter cells, one of which is destined to differentiate and the other to be a quiescent cell that restocks the satellite cell pool.

GO:0014834.name: skeletal muscle satellite cell maintenance involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014834.def: Any process by which the number of skeletal muscle satellite cells in a skeletal muscle is maintained during muscle regeneration. There are at least three mechanisms by which this is achieved. Skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division ensures satellite stem cell numbers are kept constant. Symmetric division of these cells amplifies the number of skeletal muscle satellite stem cells. Some adult skeletal muscle myoblasts (descendants of activated satellite cells) can develop back into quiescent satellite cells, replenishing the overall pool of satellite cells.
synonym: satellite cell compartment self-renewal involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

GO:0014835.name: myoblast differentiation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014835.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized satellite cell acquires specialized features of a myoblast. This occurs as part of skeletal muscle regeneration. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

GO:0014839.name: myoblast migration involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014839.def: The process in which a myoblast migrates along an entire fiber to the site of injury. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.
GO:0014839.synonym: mononucleate cell migration involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

GO:0014841.name: skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation
GO:0014841.def: The multiplication or reproduction of satellite cells, resulting in the expansion of the cell population. Satellite cells are quiescent cells that are located between the basal lamina and the plasmalemma of the muscle fiber, which are the main contributors to postnatal muscle growth. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage.

GO:0014842.name: regulation of skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation
GO:0014842.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle satellite cell proliferation.

GO:0014848.name: urinary tract smooth muscle contraction
GO:0014848.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the urinary tract. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The urinary tract consists of organs of the body that produce and discharge urine. These include the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra.

GO:0014849.name: ureter smooth muscle contraction
GO:0014849.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. This process occurs in the ureter. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The ureter is one of a pair of thick-walled tubes that transports urine from the kidney pelvis to the urinary bladder.

GO:0014852.name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by neural stimulation via neuromuscular junction
GO:0014852.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by variation of the pattern of stimulation by nervous system.

GO:0014853.name: regulation of excitatory postsynaptic membrane potential involved in skeletal muscle contraction
GO:0014853.def: Any process, involved in skeletal muscle contraction, that modulates the establishment or extent of the excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP). Excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP) is a temporary increase in postsynaptic potential due to the flow of positively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an EPSP is an excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) and makes it easier for the neuron to fire an action potential.
GO:0014853.synonym: regulation of excitatory post-synaptic membrane potential involved in skeletal muscle contraction

GO:0014855.name: striated muscle cell proliferation
GO:0014855.def: The multiplication or reproduction of striated muscle cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. Striated muscles contain fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations, and cardiac and skeletal muscle are types of striated muscle.

GO:0014856.name: skeletal muscle cell proliferation
GO:0014856.def: The multiplication or reproduction of skeletal muscle cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0014857.name: regulation of skeletal muscle cell proliferation
GO:0014857.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle cell proliferation.

GO:0014858.name: positive regulation of skeletal muscle cell proliferation
GO:0014858.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle cell proliferation.

GO:0014859.name: negative regulation of skeletal muscle cell proliferation
GO:0014859.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle cell proliferation.

GO:0014860.name: neurotransmitter secretion involved in regulation of skeletal muscle contraction
GO:0014860.def: The regulated release of neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft involved in skeletal muscle contraction. A neurotransmitter is any of a group of substances that are released on excitation from the axon terminal of a presynaptic neuron of the central or peripheral nervous system and travel across the synaptic cleft to either excite or inhibit the target cell. Among the many substances that have the properties of a neurotransmitter are acetylcholine, noradrenaline, adrenaline, dopamine, glycine, gamma aminobutyrate, glutamic acid, substance P, enkephalins, endorphins and serotonin.
GO:0014860.synonym: neurotransmitter secretion involved in control of skeletal muscle contraction

GO:0014861.name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction via regulation of action potential
GO:0014861.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by depolarization of muscle membrane and ionic fluxes.
GO:0014861.synonym: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction via membrane action potential

GO:0014866.name: skeletal myofibril assembly
GO:0014866.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skeletal myofibril over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A skeletal myofibril is a myofibril specific to skeletal muscle cells.

GO:0014872.name: myoblast division
GO:0014872.def: The process resulting in the physical partitioning and separation of a myoblast into daughter cells. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

GO:0014874.name: response to stimulus involved in regulation of muscle adaptation
GO:0014874.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus. This occurs as part of the regulation of muscle adaptation.
GO:0014874.synonym: response to stimulus involved in regulation of muscle plasticity

GO:0014878.name: response to electrical stimulus involved in regulation of muscle adaptation
GO:0014878.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an electrical stimulus. This process occurs as part of the regulation of muscle adaptation.
GO:0014878.synonym: response to electrical stimulus involved in regulation of muscle plasticity

GO:0014879.name: detection of electrical stimulus involved in regulation of muscle adaptation
GO:0014879.def: The series of events by which an electrical stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal. This occurs as part of the regulation of muscle adaptation.

GO:0014887.name: cardiac muscle adaptation
GO:0014887.def: The process in which cardiac muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors.

GO:0014888.name: striated muscle adaptation
GO:0014888.def: Any process in which striated muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.

GO:0014895.name: smooth muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014895.def: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of an organ due to an increase in size of its smooth muscle cells without cell division. Physiological hypertrophy is a normal process during development, and can also occur in mature structures on demand. In the uterus, smooth muscle cells undergo hypertrophy during pregnancy.

GO:0014896.name: muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014896.def: The muscle system process that results in enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of a muscle organ due to an increase in the size of its muscle cells. Physiological hypertrophy is a normal process during development (it stops in cardiac muscle after adolescence) and can also be brought on in response to demand. In athletes cardiac and skeletal muscles undergo hypertrophy stimulated by increasing muscle activity on exercise. Smooth muscle cells in the uterus undergo hypertrophy during pregnancy.

GO:0014897.name: striated muscle hypertrophy
GO:0014897.def: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of an organ due to an increase in size of muscle cells without cell division. In the case of striated muscle, this happens due to the additional synthesis of sarcomeric proteins and assembly of myofibrils.

GO:0014901.name: satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014901.def: The process that initiates skeletal muscle satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage.

GO:0014902.name: myotube differentiation
GO:0014902.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotube differentiation starts with myoblast fusion and the appearance of specific cell markers (this is the cell development step). Then individual myotubes can fuse to form bigger myotubes and start to contract. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0014904.name: myotube cell development
GO:0014904.def: The process aimed at the progression of a myotube cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0014906.name: myotube cell development involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014906.def: The process aimed at the progression of a myotube cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. This occurs as part of the process of skeletal muscle regeneration. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0014908.name: myotube differentiation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0014908.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a myotube cell. Myotube differentiation starts with myoblast fusion and the appearance of specific cell markers (this is the cell development step). Then individual myotubes can fuse to form bigger myotubes and start to contract. This process occurs as part of the process of skeletal muscle regeneration. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate and fuse.

GO:0014909.name: smooth muscle cell migration
GO:0014909.def: The orderly movement of a smooth muscle cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0014910.name: regulation of smooth muscle cell migration
GO:0014910.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of smooth muscle cell migration.

GO:0014911.name: positive regulation of smooth muscle cell migration
GO:0014911.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of smooth muscle cell migration.

GO:0014912.name: negative regulation of smooth muscle cell migration
GO:0014912.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of smooth muscle cell migration.

GO:0015031.name: protein transport
GO:0015031.def: The directed movement of proteins into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0015075.name: monoatomic ion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015075.def: Enables the transfer of an ion from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015078.name: proton transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015078.def: Enables the transfer of a proton from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015079.name: potassium ion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015079.def: Enables the transfer of potassium ions (K+) from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015081.name: sodium ion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015081.def: Enables the transfer of sodium ions (Na+) from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015085.name: calcium ion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015085.def: Enables the transfer of calcium (Ca) ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015101.name: organic cation transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015101.def: Enables the transfer of organic cations from one side of a membrane to the other. Organic cations are atoms or small molecules with a positive charge that contain carbon in covalent linkage.

GO:0015103.name: inorganic anion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015103.def: Enables the transfer of inorganic anions from one side of a membrane to the other. Inorganic anions are atoms or small molecules with a negative charge which do not contain carbon in covalent linkage.

GO:0015106.name: bicarbonate transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015106.def: Enables the transfer of bicarbonate from one side of a membrane to the other. Bicarbonate is the hydrogencarbonate ion, HCO3-.

GO:0015125.name: bile acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015125.def: Enables the transfer of bile acid from one side of a membrane to the other. Bile acids are any of a group of steroid carboxylic acids occurring in bile, where they are present as the sodium salts of their amides with glycine or taurine.

GO:0015144.name: carbohydrate transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015144.def: Enables the transfer of carbohydrate from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015145.name: monosaccharide transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015145.def: Enables the transfer of a monosaccharide from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015149.name: hexose transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015149.def: Enables the transfer of a hexose sugar, a monosaccharide with 6 carbon atoms, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015159.name: polysaccharide transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015159.def: Enables the transfer of polysaccharides from one side of a membrane to the other. A polysaccharide is a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically.

GO:0015171.name: amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015171.def: Enables the transfer of amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Amino acids are organic molecules that contain an amino group and a carboxyl group.

GO:0015172.name: acidic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015172.def: Enables the transfer of acidic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Acidic amino acids have side chains with a negative charge at pH 7.3.

GO:0015173.name: aromatic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015173.def: Enables the transfer of aromatic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Aromatic amino acids have an aromatic ring.

GO:0015174.name: basic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015174.def: Enables the transfer of basic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Basic amino acids have side chains with a positive charge at pH 7.3.
synonym: cationic amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

GO:0015175.name: neutral L-amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015175.def: Enables the transfer of neutral L-amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Neutral amino acids have side chains with no charge at pH 7.3.
synonym: neutral amino acid transmembrane transporter activity

GO:0015179.name: L-amino acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015179.def: Enables the transfer of an L-amino acid from one side of a membrane to the other. L-amino acids are the L-enantiomers of amino acids.

GO:0015185.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015185.def: Enables the transfer of gamma-aminobutyric acid from one side of a membrane to the other. Gamma-aminobutyric acid is 4-aminobutyrate (GABA).

GO:0015187.name: glycine transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015187.def: Enables the transfer of glycine from one side of a membrane to the other. Glycine is aminoethanoic acid.

GO:0015215.name: nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015215.def: Enables the transfer of a nucleotide, any compound consisting of a nucleoside that is esterified with (ortho)phosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015216.name: purine nucleotide transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015216.def: Enables the transfer of a purine nucleotide, any compound consisting of a purine nucleoside esterified with (ortho)phosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015217.name: ADP transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015217.def: Enables the transfer of ADP, adenosine diphosphate, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0015245.name: fatty acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015245.def: Enables the transfer of fatty acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Fatty acids are aliphatic monocarboxylic acids liberated from naturally occurring fats and oils by hydrolysis.

GO:0015250.name: water channel activity
GO:0015250.def: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of water through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

GO:0015252.name: proton channel activity
GO:0015252.def: Enables the facilitated diffusion of a hydrogen ion (by an energy-independent process) involving passage through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel without evidence for a carrier-mediated mechanism.

GO:0015267.name: channel activity
GO:0015267.def: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of a solute through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. Stereospecificity is not exhibited but this transport may be specific for a particular molecular species or class of molecules.

GO:0015269.name: calcium-activated potassium channel activity
GO:0015269.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a potassium cation by a channel that opens when a calcium cation has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0015276.name: ligand-gated monoatomic ion channel activity
GO:0015276.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0015277.name: kainate selective glutamate receptor activity
GO:0015277.def: An ionotropic glutamate receptor activity that exhibits fast gating by glutamate, acts by opening a cation channel permeable to sodium and potassium, and for which kainate is an agonist.

GO:0015280.name: ligand-gated sodium channel activity
GO:0015280.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a sodium ion by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0015291.name: secondary active transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015291.def: Enables the transfer of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other, up its concentration gradient. The transporter binds the solute and undergoes a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction and is driven by a chemiosmotic source of energy, not direct ATP coupling. Secondary active transporters include symporters and antiporters.
synonym: energizer of outer membrane receptor-mediated transport activity

GO:0015318.name: inorganic molecular entity transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0015318.def: Enables the transfer of an inorganic molecular entity from the outside of a cell to the inside of the cell across a membrane. An inorganic molecular entity is a molecular entity that contains no carbon.
synonym: inorganic solute uptake transmembrane transporter activity

GO:0015355.name: secondary active monocarboxylate transmembrane transporter activity
