GO:0021732.name: midbrain-hindbrain boundary maturation
GO:0021732.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for the midbrain-hindbrain boundary to attain its fully functional state. The midbrain-hindbrain domain of the embryonic brain is comprised of the mesencephalic vesicle and the first rhombencephalic vesicle at early somitogenesis stages. An organizing center at the boundary patterns the midbrain and hindbrain primordia of the neural plate.

GO:0021743.name: hypoglossal nucleus development
GO:0021743.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hypoglossal nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021747.name: cochlear nucleus development
GO:0021747.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cochlear nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021748.name: dorsal cochlear nucleus development
GO:0021748.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the dorsal cochlear nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021749.name: ventral cochlear nucleus development
GO:0021749.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ventral cochlear nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021751.name: salivary nucleus development
GO:0021751.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a salivary nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021753.name: superior salivary nucleus development
GO:0021753.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the superior salivary nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021754.name: facial nucleus development
GO:0021754.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the facial nucleus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0021755.name: eurydendroid cell differentiation
GO:0021755.def: The process in which neuroblasts acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the mature eurydendroid cell. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a neuroblast to a eurydendroid cell fate. A eurydendroid cell is an efferent neuron found in the cerebellar cortex of teleosts.

GO:0021756.name: striatum development
GO:0021756.def: The progression of the striatum over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The striatum is a region of the forebrain consisting of the caudate nucleus, putamen and fundus striati.

GO:0021757.name: caudate nucleus development
GO:0021757.def: The progression of the caudate nucleus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The caudate nucleus is the C-shaped structures of the striatum containing input neurons involved with control of voluntary movement in the brain.

GO:0021758.name: putamen development
GO:0021758.def: The progression of the putamen over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The putamen is the lens-shaped basal ganglion involved with control of voluntary movement in the brain.

GO:0021761.name: limbic system development
GO:0021761.def: The progression of the limbic system over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The limbic system is a collection of structures in the brain involved in emotion, motivation and emotional aspects of memory.

GO:0021762.name: substantia nigra development
GO:0021762.def: The progression of the substantia nigra over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The substantia nigra is the layer of gray substance that separates the posterior parts of the cerebral peduncles (tegmentum mesencephali) from the anterior parts; it normally includes a posterior compact part with many pigmented cells (pars compacta) and an anterior reticular part whose cells contain little pigment (pars reticularis).

GO:0021764.name: amygdala development
GO:0021764.def: The progression of the amygdala over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The amygdala is an almond-shaped set of neurons in the medial temporal lobe of the brain that play a key role in processing emotions such as fear and pleasure.

GO:0021766.name: hippocampus development
GO:0021766.def: The progression of the hippocampus over time from its initial formation until its mature state.

GO:0021767.name: mammillary body development
GO:0021767.def: The progression of the mammillary body over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The mammillary body is a protrusion at the posterior end of the hypothalamus that contains hypothalamic nuclei.

GO:0021768.name: nucleus accumbens development
GO:0021768.def: The progression of the nucleus accumbens over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The nucleus accumbens is a collection of pleomorphic cells in the caudal part of the anterior horn of the lateral ventricle, in the region of the olfactory tubercle, lying between the head of the caudate nucleus and the anterior perforated substance. It is part of the ventral striatum, a composite structure considered part of the basal ganglia.

GO:0021771.name: lateral geniculate nucleus development
GO:0021771.def: The progression of the lateral geniculate nucleus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The lateral geniculate nucleus is the primary processor of visual information received from the retina.

GO:0021772.name: olfactory bulb development
GO:0021772.def: The progression of the olfactory bulb over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The olfactory bulb coordinates neuronal signaling involved in the perception of smell. It receives input from the sensory neurons and outputs to the olfactory cortex.

GO:0021773.name: striatal medium spiny neuron differentiation
GO:0021773.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a medium spiny neuron residing in the striatum.

GO:0021782.name: glial cell development
GO:0021782.def: The process aimed at the progression of a glial cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0021783.name: preganglionic parasympathetic fiber development
GO:0021783.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a preganglionic parasympathetic fiber over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A preganglionic parasympathetic fiber is a cholinergic axonal fiber projecting from the CNS to a parasympathetic ganglion.

GO:0021794.name: thalamus development
GO:0021794.def: The process in which the thalamus changes over time, from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0021795.name: cerebral cortex cell migration
GO:0021795.def: The orderly movement of cells from one site to another in the cerebral cortex.

GO:0021799.name: cerebral cortex radially oriented cell migration
GO:0021799.def: The migration of cells in the developing cerebral cortex in which cells move from the ventricular and/or subventricular zone toward the surface of the brain.

GO:0021801.name: cerebral cortex radial glia-guided migration
GO:0021801.def: The radial migration of neuronal or glial precursor cells along radial glial cells during the development of the cerebral cortex.
synonym: cerebral cortex radial glia guided migration
cerebral cortex radial glia-dependent cell migration

GO:0021814.name: cell motility involved in cerebral cortex radial glia guided migration
GO:0021814.def: The movement of a cell along the process of a radial glial cell involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial migration.
synonym: cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial migration
cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex radial glia guided migration

GO:0021815.name: modulation of microtubule cytoskeleton involved in cerebral cortex radial glia guided migration
GO:0021815.def: Rearrangements of the microtubule cytoskeleton that contribute to the movement of cells along radial glial cells as a component of the process of cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial migration.
GO:0021815.synonym: modulation of microtubule cytoskeleton involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial migration

GO:0021819.name: layer formation in cerebral cortex
GO:0021819.def: The detachment of cells from radial glial fibers at the appropriate time when they cease to migrate and form distinct layer in the cerebral cortex.

GO:0021822.name: negative regulation of cell motility involved in cerebral cortex radial glia guided migration
GO:0021822.def: The intracellular signaling pathway that results in the cessation of cell movement involved in lamination of the cerebral cortex.
synonym: down regulation of cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial cell migration
down-regulation of cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial cell migration
downregulation of cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial cell migration
inhibition of cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial cell migration
negative regulation of cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex glial-mediated radial migration
negative regulation of cell locomotion involved in cerebral cortex radial glia guided migration

GO:0021826.name: substrate-independent telencephalic tangential migration
GO:0021826.def: The process where neuronal precursors migrate tangentially in the telencephalon, primarily guided by interactions that do not require cell-cell contact.

GO:0021830.name: interneuron migration from the subpallium to the cortex
GO:0021830.def: The directed movement of interneurons from the subpallium to the cortex during forebrain development.

GO:0021843.name: substrate-independent telencephalic tangential interneuron migration
GO:0021843.def: The directional movement of tangentially migrating interneurons that are not guided by attaching to extracellular substrates.

GO:0021846.name: cell proliferation in forebrain
GO:0021846.def: The creation of greater cell numbers in the forebrain due to cell division of progenitor cells.

GO:0021848.name: neuroblast division in subpallium
GO:0021848.def: The division of neuroblasts in the subpallium area of the forebrain. The interneuron precursors that these cells give rise to include GABAergic interneurons and will migrate tangentially.
GO:0021848.synonym: neuroblast division in the ventral telencephalon

GO:0021852.name: pyramidal neuron migration to cerebral cortex
GO:0021852.def: The migration of a pyramidal neuron precursor from the ventricular zone to the correct layer of the cerebral cortex.

GO:0021853.name: cerebral cortex GABAergic interneuron migration
GO:0021853.def: The migration of GABAergic interneuron precursors from the subpallium to the cerebral cortex.

GO:0021854.name: hypothalamus development
GO:0021854.def: The progression of the hypothalamus region of the forebrain, from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0021859.name: pyramidal neuron differentiation
GO:0021859.def: The process in which a neuroblast or one of its progeny commits to a pyramidal neuron fate, migrates from the ventricular zone to the appropriate layer in the cortex and develops into a mature neuron.

GO:0021860.name: pyramidal neuron development
GO:0021860.def: The progression of a pyramidal neuron from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0021861.name: forebrain radial glial cell differentiation
GO:0021861.def: The process in which neuroepithelial cells of the neural tube give rise to radial glial cells, specialized bipotential progenitors cells of the forebrain. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.
GO:0021861.synonym: radial glial cell differentiation in forebrain

GO:0021863.name: forebrain neuroblast differentiation
GO:0021863.def: The process in which neuroepithelial cells in the neural tube acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of basal progenitor cells, neuroblasts that lose their contacts with the ventricular surface. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0021870.name: Cajal-Retzius cell differentiation
GO:0021870.def: The process in which a neuroblast acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a Cajal-Retzius cell, one of a transient population of pioneering neurons in the cerebral cortex. These cells are slender bipolar cells of the developing marginal zone. One feature of these cells in mammals is that they express the Reelin gene.

GO:0021872.name: forebrain generation of neurons
GO:0021872.def: The process in which nerve cells are generated in the forebrain. This includes the production of neuroblasts from and their differentiation into neurons.

GO:0021879.name: forebrain neuron differentiation
GO:0021879.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuron that will reside in the forebrain.

GO:0021884.name: forebrain neuron development
GO:0021884.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron that resides in the forebrain, from its initial commitment to its fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0021885.name: forebrain cell migration
GO:0021885.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another at least one of which is located in the forebrain.

GO:0021889.name: olfactory bulb interneuron differentiation
GO:0021889.def: The process in which a neuroblast acquires specialized features of an interneuron residing in the olfactory bulb.

GO:0021891.name: olfactory bulb interneuron development
GO:0021891.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an interneuron residing in the olfactory bulb, from its initial commitment, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0021892.name: cerebral cortex GABAergic interneuron differentiation
GO:0021892.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a GABAergic interneuron residing in the cerebral cortex.

GO:0021894.name: cerebral cortex GABAergic interneuron development
GO:0021894.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cerebral cortex GABAergic interneuron over time, from initial commitment to its fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0021895.name: cerebral cortex neuron differentiation
GO:0021895.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuron residing in the cerebral cortex.

GO:0021896.name: forebrain astrocyte differentiation
GO:0021896.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of an astrocyte residing in the forebrain. An astrocyte is the most abundant type of glial cell. Astrocytes provide support for neurons and regulate the environment in which they function.

GO:0021897.name: forebrain astrocyte development
GO:0021897.def: The process aimed at the progression of an astrocyte that resides in the forebrain, from initial commitment of the cell to its fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An astrocyte is the most abundant type of glial cell. Astrocytes provide support for neurons and regulate the environment in which they function.

GO:0021903.name: rostrocaudal neural tube patterning
GO:0021903.def: The process in which the neural tube is divided into specific regions along the rostrocaudal axis.

GO:0021905.name: forebrain-midbrain boundary formation
GO:0021905.def: The process whose specific outcome is the creation of the forebrain-midbrain boundary.

GO:0021906.name: hindbrain-spinal cord boundary formation
GO:0021906.def: The process whose specific outcome is the formation of the hindbrain-spinal cord boundary.

GO:0021915.name: neural tube development
GO:0021915.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the neural tube over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mature structure of the neural tube exists when the tube has been segmented into the forebrain, midbrain, hindbrain and spinal cord regions. In addition neural crest has budded away from the epithelium.

GO:0021921.name: regulation of cell proliferation in dorsal spinal cord
GO:0021921.def: The process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell proliferation in the dorsal spinal cord.

GO:0021952.name: central nervous system projection neuron axonogenesis
GO:0021952.def: Generation of a long process of a CNS neuron, that carries efferent (outgoing) action potentials from the cell body towards target cells in a different central nervous system region.
GO:0021952.synonym: central nervous system axon tract development

GO:0021953.name: central nervous system neuron differentiation
GO:0021953.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuron whose cell body resides in the central nervous system.

GO:0021954.name: central nervous system neuron development
GO:0021954.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron whose cell body is located in the central nervous system, from initial commitment of the cell to a neuronal fate, to the fully functional differentiated neuron.

GO:0021955.name: central nervous system neuron axonogenesis
GO:0021955.def: Generation of a long process from a neuron whose cell body resides in the central nervous system. The process carries efferent (outgoing) action potentials from the cell body towards target cells.

GO:0021957.name: corticospinal tract morphogenesis
GO:0021957.def: Generation of a long process of a pyramidal cell, that carries efferent (outgoing) action potentials from the cell body in cerebral cortex layer V towards target cells in the gray matter of the spinal cord. This axonal process is a member of those that make up the corticospinal tract.

GO:0021982.name: pineal gland development
GO:0021982.def: The progression of the pineal gland over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The pineal gland is an endocrine gland that secretes melatonin and is involved in circadian rhythms.

GO:0021983.name: pituitary gland development
GO:0021983.def: The progression of the pituitary gland over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The pituitary gland is an endocrine gland that secretes hormones that regulate many other glands.

GO:0021984.name: adenohypophysis development
GO:0021984.def: The progression of the adenohypophysis over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The adenohypophysis is the anterior part of the pituitary. It secretes a variety of hormones and its function is regulated by the hypothalamus.

GO:0021985.name: neurohypophysis development
GO:0021985.def: The progression of the neurohypophysis over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The neurohypophysis is the part of the pituitary gland that secretes hormones involved in blood pressure regulation.

GO:0021987.name: cerebral cortex development
GO:0021987.def: The progression of the cerebral cortex over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The cerebral cortex is the outer layered region of the telencephalon.

GO:0021988.name: olfactory lobe development
GO:0021988.def: The progression of the olfactory lobe over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The olfactory lobe is the area of the brain that process the neural inputs for the sense of smell.

GO:0021989.name: olfactory cortex development
GO:0021989.def: The progression of the olfactory cortex over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The olfactory cortex is involved in the perception of smell. It receives input from the olfactory bulb and is responsible for the identification of odors.

GO:0021990.name: neural plate formation
GO:0021990.def: The formation of the flat, thickened layer of ectodermal cells known as the neural plate. The underlying dorsal mesoderm signals the ectodermal cells above it to elongate into columnar neural plate cells. The neural plate subsequently develops into the neural tube, which gives rise to the central nervous system.

GO:0021999.name: neural plate anterior/posterior regionalization
GO:0021999.def: The process that regulates the coordinated growth and differentiation that establishes the non-random anterior-posterior spatial arrangement of the neural plate.

GO:0022008.name: neurogenesis
GO:0022008.def: Generation of cells within the nervous system.

GO:0022009.name: central nervous system vasculogenesis
GO:0022009.def: The differentiation of endothelial cells from progenitor cells during blood vessel development, and the de novo formation of blood vessels and tubes in the central nervous system. The capillary endothelial cells in the brain are specialized to form the blood-brain barrier.

GO:0022010.name: central nervous system myelination
GO:0022010.def: The process in which neuronal axons and dendrites become coated with a segmented lipid-rich sheath (myelin) to enable faster and more energetically efficient conduction of electrical impulses. The sheath is formed by the cell membranes of oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system. Adjacent myelin segments are separated by a non-myelinated stretch of axon called a node of Ranvier.

GO:0022011.name: myelination in peripheral nervous system
GO:0022011.def: The process in which neuronal axons and dendrites become coated with a segmented lipid-rich sheath (myelin) to enable faster and more energetically efficient conduction of electrical impulses. The sheath is formed by the cell membranes of Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system. Adjacent myelin segments are separated by a non-myelinated stretch of axon called a node of Ranvier.

GO:0022012.name: subpallium cell proliferation in forebrain
GO:0022012.def: The multiplication or reproduction of subpallium cells in the forebrain, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0022029.name: telencephalon cell migration
GO:0022029.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another at least one of which is located in the telencephalon.

GO:0022030.name: telencephalon glial cell migration
GO:0022030.def: The orderly movement of glial cells through the telencephalon.

GO:0022031.name: telencephalon astrocyte cell migration
GO:0022031.def: The orderly movement of an astrocyte cell through the telencephalon.

GO:0022032.name: telencephalon oligodendrocyte cell migration
GO:0022032.def: The multiplication or reproduction of telencephalon oligodendrocyte cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0022033.name: telencephalon microglial cell migration
GO:0022033.def: The orderly movement of microglial cells through the telencephalon.

GO:0022035.name: rhombomere cell migration
GO:0022035.def: The movement of a cell within a rhombomere. This process is known to occur as an early step in the generation of anatomical structure from a rhombomere.

GO:0022037.name: metencephalon development
GO:0022037.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the metencephalon over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0022402.name: cell cycle process
GO:0022402.def: The cellular process that ensures successive accurate and complete genome replication and chromosome segregation.

GO:0022403.name: cell cycle phase
GO:0022403.def: One of the distinct periods or stages into which the cell cycle is divided. Each phase is characterized by the occurrence of specific biochemical and morphological events.

GO:0022404.name: molting cycle process
GO:0022404.def: A multicellular organismal process involved in the periodic casting off and regeneration of an outer covering of cuticle, feathers, hair, horns, skin.

GO:0022405.name: hair cycle process
GO:0022405.def: A multicellular organismal process involved in the cyclical phases of growth (anagen), regression (catagen), quiescence (telogen), and shedding (exogen) in the life of a hair; one of the collection or mass of filaments growing from the skin of an animal, and forming a covering for a part of the head or for any part or the whole of the body.

GO:0022406.name: membrane docking
GO:0022406.def: The initial attachment of a membrane or protein to a target membrane. Docking requires only that the proteins come close enough to interact and adhere.

GO:0022407.name: regulation of cell-cell adhesion
GO:0022407.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of attachment of a cell to another cell.

GO:0022408.name: negative regulation of cell-cell adhesion
GO:0022408.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate or extent of cell adhesion to another cell.

GO:0022409.name: positive regulation of cell-cell adhesion
GO:0022409.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of cell adhesion to another cell.

GO:0022411.name: cellular component disassembly
GO:0022411.def: A cellular process that results in the breakdown of a cellular component.
synonym: cellular component disassembly at cellular level

GO:0022412.name: cellular process involved in reproduction in multicellular organism
GO:0022412.def: A process, occurring at the cellular level, that is involved in the reproductive function of a multicellular organism.
GO:0022412.synonym: reproductive cellular process in multicellular organism

GO:0022413.name: reproductive process in single-celled organism
GO:0022413.def: A process, occurring at the cellular level, that is involved in the reproductive function of a single-celled organism.

GO:0022414.name: reproductive process
GO:0022414.def: A biological process that directly contributes to the process of producing new individuals by one or two organisms. The new individuals inherit some proportion of their genetic material from the parent or parents.

GO:0022600.name: digestive system process
GO:0022600.def: A physical, chemical, or biochemical process carried out by living organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

GO:0022602.name: ovulation cycle process
GO:0022602.def: A process involved in the sexual cycle seen in females, often with physiologic changes in the endometrium that recur at regular intervals during the reproductive years.

GO:0022603.name: regulation of anatomical structure morphogenesis
GO:0022603.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of anatomical structure morphogenesis.

GO:0022604.name: regulation of cell morphogenesis
GO:0022604.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell morphogenesis. Cell morphogenesis is the developmental process in which the shape of a cell is generated and organized.
synonym: negative regulation of cell shape and cell size
positive regulation of cell shape and cell size
regulation of cell shape and cell size

GO:0022605.name: mammalian oogenesis stage
GO:0022605.def: A reproductive process that is a step in the formation and maturation of an ovum or female gamete from a primordial female germ cell.

GO:0022607.name: cellular component assembly
GO:0022607.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a cellular component.
synonym: cellular component assembly at cellular level

GO:0022612.name: gland morphogenesis
GO:0022612.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a gland are generated and organized.

GO:0022613.name: ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis
GO:0022613.def: A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a complex containing RNA and proteins. Includes the biosynthesis of the constituent RNA and protein molecules, and those macromolecular modifications that are involved in synthesis or assembly of the ribonucleoprotein complex.

GO:0022617.name: extracellular matrix disassembly
GO:0022617.def: A process that results in the breakdown of the extracellular matrix.

GO:0022618.name: protein-RNA complex assembly
GO:0022618.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins and RNA molecules to form a ribonucleoprotein complex.

GO:0022626.name: cytosolic ribosome
GO:0022626.def: A ribosome located in the cytosol.

GO:0022803.name: passive transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0022803.def: Enables the transfer of a single solute from one side of a membrane to the other by a mechanism involving conformational change, either by facilitated diffusion or in a membrane potential dependent process if the solute is charged.

GO:0022804.name: active transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0022804.def: Enables the transfer of a specific substance or related group of substances from one side of a membrane to the other, up the solute's concentration gradient. The transporter binds the solute and undergoes a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction.

GO:0022824.name: transmitter-gated monoatomic ion channel activity
GO:0022824.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when a specific neurotransmitter has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0022834.name: ligand-gated channel activity
GO:0022834.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a solute by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0022835.name: transmitter-gated channel activity
GO:0022835.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a solute by a channel that opens when a specific neurotransmitter has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0022836.name: gated channel activity
GO:0022836.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a solute by a channel that opens in response to a specific stimulus.

GO:0022839.name: monoatomic ion-gated channel activity
GO:0022839.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a solute by a channel that opens in response to a specific ion stimulus.

GO:0022848.name: acetylcholine-gated monoatomic cation-selective channel activity
GO:0022848.def: Selectively enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens upon binding acetylcholine.

GO:0022849.name: glutamate-gated calcium ion channel activity
GO:0022849.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a calcium ion by a channel that opens when glutamate has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0022850.name: serotonin-gated monoatomic cation channel activity
GO:0022850.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens when serotonin has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0022857.name: transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0022857.def: Enables the transfer of a substance, usually a specific substance or a group of related substances, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0022884.name: macromolecule transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0022884.def: Enables the transfer of a macromolecule from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0022890.name: inorganic cation transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0022890.def: Enables the transfer of inorganic cations from one side of a membrane to the other. Inorganic cations are atoms or small molecules with a positive charge that do not contain carbon in covalent linkage.
synonym: di-, tri-valent inorganic cation transmembrane transporter activity
divalent inorganic cation transmembrane transporter activity
monovalent inorganic cation transmembrane transporter activity
trivalent inorganic cation transmembrane transporter activity

GO:0022898.name: regulation of transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0022898.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of transmembrane transporter activity.

GO:0023019.name: signal transduction involved in regulation of gene expression
GO:0023019.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gene expression as a consequence of a process in which a signal is released and/or conveyed from one location to another.
GO:0023019.synonym: regulation of gene expression as a consequence of signal transmission

GO:0023023.name: MHC protein complex binding
GO:0023023.def: Binding to a major histocompatibility complex.

GO:0023026.name: MHC class II protein complex binding
GO:0023026.def: Binding to a class II major histocompatibility complex.

GO:0023029.name: MHC class Ib protein binding
GO:0023029.def: Binding to a major histocompatibility complex class Ib molecules.

GO:0023051.name: regulation of signaling
GO:0023051.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a signaling process.

GO:0023052.name: signaling
GO:0023052.def: The entirety of a process in which information is transmitted within a biological system. This process begins with an active signal and ends when a cellular response has been triggered.

GO:0023056.name: positive regulation of signaling
GO:0023056.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a signaling process.

GO:0023057.name: negative regulation of signaling
GO:0023057.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a signaling process.

GO:0023061.name: signal release
GO:0023061.def: The process in which a signal is secreted or discharged into the extracellular medium from a cellular source.

GO:0030001.name: metal ion transport
GO:0030001.def: The directed movement of metal ions, any metal ion with an electric charge, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0030003.name: intracellular monoatomic cation homeostasis
GO:0030003.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of monoatomic cations within a cell. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are cations consisting of exactly one atom.

GO:0030007.name: intracellular potassium ion homeostasis
GO:0030007.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of potassium ions within a cell.

GO:0030010.name: establishment of cell polarity
GO:0030010.def: The specification and formation of anisotropic intracellular organization or cell growth patterns.
synonym: bud site selection/establishment of cell polarity

GO:0030016.name: myofibril
GO:0030016.def: The contractile element of skeletal and cardiac muscle; a long, highly organized bundle of actin, myosin, and other proteins that contracts by a sliding filament mechanism.

GO:0030017.name: sarcomere
GO:0030017.def: The repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

GO:0030029.name: actin filament-based process
GO:0030029.def: Any cellular process that depends upon or alters the actin cytoskeleton, that part of the cytoskeleton comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins.

GO:0030030.name: cell projection organization
GO:0030030.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a prolongation or process extending from a cell, e.g. a flagellum or axon.
synonym: cell surface structure organization and biogenesis

GO:0030031.name: cell projection assembly
GO:0030031.def: Formation of a prolongation or process extending from a cell, e.g. a flagellum or axon.
synonym: formation of a cell surface projection

GO:0030033.name: microvillus assembly
GO:0030033.def: Formation of a microvillus, a thin cylindrical membrane-covered projection on the surface of a cell.

GO:0030036.name: actin cytoskeleton organization
GO:0030036.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins.

GO:0030048.name: actin filament-based movement
GO:0030048.def: Movement of organelles or other particles along actin filaments, or sliding of actin filaments past each other, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0030050.name: vesicle transport along actin filament
GO:0030050.def: Movement of a vesicle along an actin filament, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0030054.name: cell junction
GO:0030054.def: A cellular component that forms a specialized region of connection between two or more cells, or between a cell and the extracellular matrix, or between two membrane-bound components of a cell, such as flagella.

GO:0030055.name: cell-substrate junction
GO:0030055.def: A cell junction that forms a connection between a cell and the extracellular matrix.

GO:0030070.name: insulin processing
GO:0030070.def: The formation of mature insulin by proteolysis of the precursor preproinsulin. The signal sequence is first cleaved from preproinsulin to form proinsulin; proinsulin is then cleaved to release the C peptide, leaving the A and B chains of mature insulin linked by disulfide bridges.

GO:0030072.name: peptide hormone secretion
GO:0030072.def: The regulated release of a peptide hormone from a cell.

GO:0030073.name: insulin secretion
GO:0030073.def: The regulated release of proinsulin from secretory granules accompanied by cleavage of proinsulin to form mature insulin. In vertebrates, insulin is secreted from B granules in the B cells of the vertebrate pancreas and from insulin-producing cells in insects.

GO:0030097.name: hemopoiesis
GO:0030097.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the myeloid and lymphoid derived organ/tissue systems of the blood and other parts of the body over time, from formation to the mature structure. The site of hemopoiesis is variable during development, but occurs primarily in bone marrow or kidney in many adult vertebrates.

GO:0030098.name: lymphocyte differentiation
GO:0030098.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized precursor cell acquires specialized features of a lymphocyte. A lymphocyte is a leukocyte commonly found in the blood and lymph that has the characteristics of a large nucleus, a neutral staining cytoplasm, and prominent heterochromatin.

GO:0030099.name: myeloid cell differentiation
GO:0030099.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of any cell of the myeloid leukocyte, megakaryocyte, thrombocyte, or erythrocyte lineages.

GO:0030100.name: regulation of endocytosis
GO:0030100.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of endocytosis.

GO:0030101.name: natural killer cell activation
GO:0030101.def: The change in morphology and behavior of a natural killer cell in response to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

GO:0030103.name: vasopressin secretion
GO:0030103.def: The regulated release of vasopressin from secretory granules into the blood.

GO:0030133.name: transport vesicle
GO:0030133.def: Any of the vesicles of the constitutive secretory pathway, which carry cargo from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, between Golgi cisternae, from the Golgi to the ER (retrograde transport) or to destinations within or outside the cell.

GO:0030141.name: secretory granule
GO:0030141.def: A small subcellular vesicle, surrounded by a membrane, that is formed from the Golgi apparatus and contains a highly concentrated protein destined for secretion. Secretory granules move towards the periphery of the cell and upon stimulation, their membranes fuse with the cell membrane, and their protein load is exteriorized. Processing of the contained protein may take place in secretory granules.

GO:0030148.name: sphingolipid biosynthetic process
GO:0030148.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sphingolipids, any of a class of lipids containing the long-chain amine diol sphingosine or a closely related base (a sphingoid).

GO:0030149.name: sphingolipid catabolic process
GO:0030149.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of sphingolipids, any of a class of lipids containing the long-chain amine diol sphingosine or a closely related base (a sphingoid).

GO:0030154.name: cell differentiation
GO:0030154.def: The cellular developmental process in which a relatively unspecialized cell, e.g. embryonic or regenerative cell, acquires specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize a specific cell. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate and its subsequent development to the mature state.

GO:0030155.name: regulation of cell adhesion
GO:0030155.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of attachment of a cell to another cell or to the extracellular matrix.

GO:0030162.name: regulation of proteolysis
GO:0030162.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the hydrolysis of a peptide bond or bonds within a protein.

GO:0030163.name: protein catabolic process
GO:0030163.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein by the destruction of the native, active configuration, with or without the hydrolysis of peptide bonds.

GO:0030166.name: proteoglycan biosynthetic process
GO:0030166.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of proteoglycans, any glycoprotein in which the carbohydrate units are glycosaminoglycans.

GO:0030167.name: proteoglycan catabolic process
GO:0030167.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of proteoglycans, any glycoprotein in which the carbohydrate units are glycosaminoglycans.

GO:0030168.name: platelet activation
GO:0030168.def: A series of progressive, overlapping events triggered by exposure of the platelets to subendothelial tissue. These events include shape change, adhesiveness, aggregation, and release reactions. When carried through to completion, these events lead to the formation of a stable hemostatic plug.

GO:0030182.name: neuron differentiation
GO:0030182.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuron.

GO:0030183.name: B cell differentiation
GO:0030183.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a B cell. A B cell is a lymphocyte of B lineage with the phenotype CD19-positive and capable of B cell mediated immunity.

GO:0030184.name: nitric oxide transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0030184.def: Enables the transfer of nitric oxide, nitrogen monoxide, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0030185.name: nitric oxide transport
GO:0030185.def: The directed movement of nitric oxide, nitrogen monoxide, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0030186.name: melatonin metabolic process
GO:0030186.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine).

GO:0030187.name: melatonin biosynthetic process
GO:0030187.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine).

GO:0030193.name: regulation of blood coagulation
GO:0030193.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of blood coagulation.

GO:0030194.name: positive regulation of blood coagulation
GO:0030194.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of blood coagulation.

GO:0030195.name: negative regulation of blood coagulation
GO:0030195.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of blood coagulation.

GO:0030198.name: extracellular matrix organization
GO:0030198.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an extracellular matrix.

GO:0030199.name: collagen fibril organization
GO:0030199.def: Any process that determines the size and arrangement of collagen fibrils within an extracellular matrix.

GO:0030202.name: heparin proteoglycan metabolic process
GO:0030202.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving heparin proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparin glycosaminoglycan. The heparin chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups, and the latter being e a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids. Heparin is similar to heparan sulfate but it contains more N-sulfate and O-sulfate groups. Heparin proteoglycans are stored selectively in the secretory granules of mammalian mast cells.

GO:0030203.name: glycosaminoglycan metabolic process
GO:0030203.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glycosaminoglycans, any of a group of linear polysaccharides composed of repeating disaccharide units.

GO:0030210.name: heparin proteoglycan biosynthetic process
GO:0030210.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of heparin proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a heparin glycosaminoglycan. The heparin chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-alpha-(1,4)-hexuronic acid, the former being either sulfated or deacetylated on its amino group as well as sulfated on one of its hydroxyl groups, and the latter being a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids. Heparin is similar to heparan sulfate but it contains more N-sulfate and O-sulfate groups. Heparin chains are covalently linked to serine/threonine residues (O-linked) of the core protein via a tetrasaccharide linker sequence (xylose-galactose-galactose-glucuronate).

GO:0030212.name: hyaluronan metabolic process
GO:0030212.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving hyaluronan, the naturally occurring anionic form of hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronan is a type of non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

GO:0030213.name: hyaluronan biosynthetic process
GO:0030213.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of hyaluronan, the naturally occurring anionic form of hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronan is a type of non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

GO:0030214.name: hyaluronan catabolic process
GO:0030214.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of hyaluronan, the naturally occurring anionic form of hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronan is a type of non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta(1,4)-D-glucuronic acid-beta(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine.

GO:0030216.name: keratinocyte differentiation
GO:0030216.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a keratinocyte.

GO:0030217.name: T cell differentiation
GO:0030217.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires characteristics of a more mature T-cell. A T cell is a type of lymphocyte whose definin characteristic is the expression of a T cell receptor complex.

GO:0030218.name: erythrocyte differentiation
GO:0030218.def: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires specializes features of an erythrocyte.

GO:0030219.name: megakaryocyte differentiation
GO:0030219.def: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires specializes features of a megakaryocyte.

GO:0030220.name: platelet formation
GO:0030220.def: The process in which platelets bud from long processes extended by megakaryocytes.

GO:0030221.name: basophil differentiation
GO:0030221.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires specialized features of a basophil cell.

GO:0030222.name: eosinophil differentiation
GO:0030222.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specializes features of an eosinophil.

GO:0030223.name: neutrophil differentiation
GO:0030223.def: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a neutrophil.

GO:0030224.name: monocyte differentiation
GO:0030224.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a monocyte.

GO:0030225.name: macrophage differentiation
GO:0030225.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized monocyte acquires the specialized features of a macrophage.

GO:0030228.name: lipoprotein particle receptor activity
GO:0030228.def: Combining with a lipoprotein particle and delivering the lipoprotein particle into the cell via endocytosis. A lipoprotein particle, also known as a lipoprotein, is a clathrate complex consisting of a lipid enwrapped in a protein host without covalent binding in such a way that the complex has a hydrophilic outer surface consisting of all the protein and the polar ends of any phospholipids.

GO:0030239.name: myofibril assembly
GO:0030239.def: Formation of myofibrils, the repeating units of striated muscle.

GO:0030246.name: carbohydrate binding
GO:0030246.def: Binding to a carbohydrate, which includes monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides as well as substances derived from monosaccharides by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more hydroxy groups to afford the corresponding aldehydes, ketones, or carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by a hydrogen atom. Cyclitols are generally not regarded as carbohydrates.

GO:0030247.name: polysaccharide binding
GO:0030247.def: Binding to a polysaccharide, a polymer of many (typically more than 10) monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically.
GO:0030247.synonym: polysaccharide assembly with MHC class II protein complex

GO:0030252.name: growth hormone secretion
GO:0030252.def: The regulated release of growth hormone from secretory granules into the blood.

GO:0030261.name: chromosome condensation
GO:0030261.def: The progressive compaction of dispersed interphase chromatin into threadlike chromosomes prior to mitotic or meiotic nuclear division, or during apoptosis, in eukaryotic cells.

GO:0030262.name: apoptotic nuclear changes
GO:0030262.def: Alterations undergone by nuclei at the molecular and morphological level as part of the execution phase of apoptosis.

GO:0030263.name: apoptotic chromosome condensation
GO:0030263.def: The compaction of chromatin during apoptosis.

GO:0030264.name: nuclear fragmentation involved in apoptotic nuclear change
GO:0030264.def: The breakdown of the nucleus into small membrane-bounded compartments, or blebs, each of which contain compacted DNA.

GO:0030278.name: regulation of ossification
GO:0030278.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of ossification, the formation of bone or of a bony substance or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.

GO:0030279.name: negative regulation of ossification
GO:0030279.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of ossification, the formation of bone or of a bony substance or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone or a bony substance.

GO:0030282.name: bone mineralization
GO:0030282.def: The deposition of hydroxyapatite, a form of calcium phosphate with the formula Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2, in bone tissue.

GO:0030286.name: dynein complex
GO:0030286.def: Any of several large complexes that contain two or three dynein heavy chains and several light chains, and have microtubule motor activity.

GO:0030307.name: positive regulation of cell growth
GO:0030307.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, extent or direction of cell growth.

GO:0030308.name: negative regulation of cell growth
GO:0030308.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, extent or direction of cell growth.

GO:0030312.name: external encapsulating structure
GO:0030312.def: A structure that lies outside the plasma membrane and surrounds the entire cell or cells. This does not include the periplasmic space.

GO:0030316.name: osteoclast differentiation
GO:0030316.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized monocyte acquires the specialized features of an osteoclast. An osteoclast is a specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue.

GO:0030317.name: flagellated sperm motility
GO:0030317.def: The directed, self-propelled movement of a cilium (aka flagellum) that contributes to the movement of a flagellated sperm.
synonym: sperm flagellum movement involved in flagellated sperm motility
sperm flagellum movement involved in flagellated sperm movement

GO:0030318.name: melanocyte differentiation
GO:0030318.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a melanocyte.

GO:0030323.name: respiratory tube development
GO:0030323.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the respiratory tube over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The respiratory tube is assumed to mean any tube in the respiratory tract.

GO:0030324.name: lung development
GO:0030324.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lung over time, from its formation to the mature structure. In all air-breathing vertebrates the lungs are developed from the ventral wall of the oesophagus as a pouch which divides into two sacs. In amphibians and many reptiles the lungs retain very nearly this primitive sac-like character, but in the higher forms the connection with the esophagus becomes elongated into the windpipe and the inner walls of the sacs become more and more divided, until, in the mammals, the air spaces become minutely divided into tubes ending in small air cells, in the walls of which the blood circulates in a fine network of capillaries. In mammals the lungs are more or less divided into lobes, and each lung occupies a separate cavity in the thorax.

GO:0030325.name: adrenal gland development
GO:0030325.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the adrenal gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. This gland can either be a discrete structure located bilaterally above each kidney, or a cluster of cells in the head kidney that perform the functions of the adrenal gland. In either case, this organ consists of two cells types, aminergic chromaffin cells and steroidogenic cortical cells.

GO:0030331.name: nuclear estrogen receptor binding
GO:0030331.def: Binding to a nuclear estrogen receptor.

GO:0030334.name: regulation of cell migration
GO:0030334.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell migration.

GO:0030335.name: positive regulation of cell migration
GO:0030335.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell migration.

GO:0030336.name: negative regulation of cell migration
GO:0030336.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cell migration.

GO:0030397.name: membrane disassembly
GO:0030397.def: The controlled breakdown of any cell membrane in the context of a normal process such as autophagy.

GO:0030421.name: defecation
GO:0030421.def: The expulsion of feces from the rectum.

GO:0030424.name: axon
GO:0030424.def: The long process of a neuron that conducts nerve impulses, usually away from the cell body to the terminals and varicosities, which are sites of storage and release of neurotransmitter.

GO:0030425.name: dendrite
GO:0030425.def: A neuron projection that has a short, tapering, morphology. Dendrites receive and integrate signals from other neurons or from sensory stimuli, and conduct nerve impulses towards the axon or the cell body. In most neurons, the impulse is conveyed from dendrites to axon via the cell body, but in some types of unipolar neuron, the impulse does not travel via the cell body.

GO:0030432.name: peristalsis
GO:0030432.def: A wavelike sequence of involuntary muscular contraction and relaxation that passes along a tubelike structure, such as the intestine, impelling the contents onwards.

GO:0030435.name: sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore
GO:0030435.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a cellular spore, a cell form that can be used for dissemination, for survival of adverse conditions because of its heat and desiccation resistance, and/or for reproduction.

GO:0030437.name: ascospore formation
GO:0030437.def: The process in which cells that are products of meiosis acquire the specialized features of ascospores. Ascospores are generally found in clusters of four or eight spores within a single mother cell, the ascus, and are characteristic of the ascomycete fungi (phylum Ascomycota).

GO:0030473.name: nuclear migration along microtubule
GO:0030473.def: The directed movement of the nucleus along microtubules within the cell, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0030485.name: smooth muscle contractile fiber
GO:0030485.def: The contractile fiber of smooth muscle cells.

GO:0030500.name: regulation of bone mineralization
GO:0030500.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of bone mineralization.

GO:0030501.name: positive regulation of bone mineralization
GO:0030501.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of bone mineralization.

GO:0030502.name: negative regulation of bone mineralization
GO:0030502.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of bone mineralization.

GO:0030539.name: male genitalia development
GO:0030539.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the male genitalia over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0030540.name: female genitalia development
GO:0030540.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the female genitalia over time, from formation to the mature structure.

GO:0030554.name: adenyl nucleotide binding
GO:0030554.def: Binding to an adenyl nucleotide, an adenosine esterified with (ortho)phosphate.

GO:0030573.name: bile acid catabolic process
GO:0030573.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of bile acids, any of a group of steroid carboxylic acids occurring in bile.

GO:0030574.name: collagen catabolic process
GO:0030574.def: The proteolytic chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of collagen in the extracellular matrix, usually carried out by proteases secreted by nearby cells.

GO:0030593.name: neutrophil chemotaxis
GO:0030593.def: The directed movement of a neutrophil cell, the most numerous polymorphonuclear leukocyte found in the blood, in response to an external stimulus, usually an infection or wounding.

GO:0030594.name: neurotransmitter receptor activity
GO:0030594.def: Combining with a neurotransmitter and transmitting the signal to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0030595.name: leukocyte chemotaxis
GO:0030595.def: The movement of a leukocyte in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0030643.name: intracellular phosphate ion homeostasis
GO:0030643.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of phosphate ions within a cell.

GO:0030658.name: transport vesicle membrane
GO:0030658.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a transport vesicle.
synonym: constitutive secretory pathway transport vesicle membrane

GO:0030659.name: cytoplasmic vesicle membrane
GO:0030659.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a cytoplasmic vesicle.

GO:0030660.name: Golgi-associated vesicle membrane
GO:0030660.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a vesicle associated with the Golgi apparatus.

GO:0030661.name: chitosome membrane
GO:0030661.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a chitosome.

GO:0030667.name: secretory granule membrane
GO:0030667.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a secretory granule.

GO:0030705.name: cytoskeleton-dependent intracellular transport
GO:0030705.def: The directed movement of substances along cytoskeletal fibers such as microfilaments or microtubules within a cell.

GO:0030707.name: follicle cell of egg chamber development
GO:0030707.def: The process that occurs during oogenesis involving the ovarian follicle cells, somatic cells which surround the germ cells of an ovary. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0030718.name: germ-line stem cell population maintenance
GO:0030718.def: Any process by which an organism or tissue maintains a population of germ-line stem cells.

GO:0030720.name: oocyte localization involved in germarium-derived egg chamber formation
GO:0030720.def: Directed movement of the oocyte, following its specification, from its original central position in the cyst to a posterior position relative to the nurse cells of the egg chamber, and its maintenance in this posterior location. This is the first sign of anterior-posterior asymmetry in the developing egg chamber.
synonym: establishment and maintenance of oocyte localization in egg chamber
establishment and maintenance of oocyte position during oogenesis
oocyte localisation involved in germarium-derived egg chamber formation
oocyte localization during germarium-derived egg chamber formation
oogenesis, establishment and maintenance of oocyte localization

GO:0030808.name: regulation of nucleotide biosynthetic process
GO:0030808.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of nucleotides.

GO:0030809.name: negative regulation of nucleotide biosynthetic process
GO:0030809.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of nucleotides.

GO:0030810.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of nucleotides.

GO:0030850.name: prostate gland development
GO:0030850.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the prostate gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The prostate gland is a partly muscular, partly glandular body that is situated near the base of the mammalian male urethra and secretes an alkaline viscid fluid which is a major constituent of the ejaculatory fluid.

GO:0030851.name: granulocyte differentiation
GO:0030851.def: The process in which a myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a granulocyte. Granulocytes are a class of leukocytes characterized by the presence of granules in their cytoplasm. These cells are active in allergic immune reactions such as arthritic inflammation and rashes. This class includes basophils, eosinophils and neutrophils.

GO:0030852.name: regulation of granulocyte differentiation
GO:0030852.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of granulocyte differentiation.

GO:0030853.name: negative regulation of granulocyte differentiation
GO:0030853.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of granulocyte differentiation.

GO:0030854.name: positive regulation of granulocyte differentiation
GO:0030854.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of granulocyte differentiation.

GO:0030855.name: epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0030855.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an epithelial cell, any of the cells making up an epithelium.

GO:0030856.name: regulation of epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0030856.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell differentiation.

GO:0030857.name: negative regulation of epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0030857.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell differentiation.
synonym: down regulation of epithelial cell differentiation

GO:0030858.name: positive regulation of epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0030858.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of epithelial cell differentiation.
synonym: up regulation of epithelial cell differentiation

GO:0030878.name: thyroid gland development
GO:0030878.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the thyroid gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The thyroid gland is an endoderm-derived gland that produces thyroid hormone.

GO:0030879.name: mammary gland development
GO:0030879.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mammary gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mammary gland is a large compound sebaceous gland that in female mammals is modified to secrete milk. Its development starts with the formation of the mammary line and ends as the mature gland cycles between nursing and weaning stages.

GO:0030885.name: regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation
GO:0030885.def: Any process that modulates the frequency or rate of myeloid dendritic cell activation.

GO:0030886.name: negative regulation of myeloid dendritic cell activation
GO:0030886.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of myeloid dendritic cell activation.

GO:0030900.name: forebrain development
GO:0030900.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the forebrain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The forebrain is the anterior of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes especially the cerebral hemispheres, the thalamus, and the hypothalamus and especially in higher vertebrates is the main control center for sensory and associative information processing, visceral functions, and voluntary motor functions).

GO:0030901.name: midbrain development
GO:0030901.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the midbrain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The midbrain is the middle division of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes a ventral part containing the cerebral peduncles and a dorsal tectum containing the corpora quadrigemina and that surrounds the aqueduct of Sylvius connecting the third and fourth ventricles).

GO:0030902.name: hindbrain development
GO:0030902.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hindbrain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The hindbrain is the posterior of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain, or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes the cerebellum, pons, and medulla oblongata and controls the autonomic functions and equilibrium).

GO:0030903.name: notochord development
GO:0030903.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the notochord over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The notochord is a mesoderm-derived structure located ventral of the developing nerve cord. In vertebrates, the notochord serves as a core around which other mesodermal cells form the vertebrae. In the most primitive chordates, which lack vertebrae, the notochord persists as a substitute for a vertebral column.

GO:0030910.name: olfactory placode formation
GO:0030910.def: The formation of a thickening of the neural ectoderm in the head region of the vertebrate embryo which develops into the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

GO:0030916.name: otic vesicle formation
GO:0030916.def: The process resulting in the transition of the otic placode into the otic vesicle, a transient embryonic structure formed during development of the vertebrate inner ear.

GO:0030917.name: midbrain-hindbrain boundary development
GO:0030917.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the midbrain-hindbrain boundary over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The midbrain-hindbrain domain of the embryonic brain is comprised of the mesencephalic vesicle and the first rhombencephalic vesicle at early somitogenesis stages.

GO:0030936.name: transmembrane collagen trimer
GO:0030936.def: Any collagen trimer that passes through a lipid bilayer membrane.

GO:0030951.name: establishment or maintenance of microtubule cytoskeleton polarity
GO:0030951.def: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of polarized microtubule-based cytoskeletal structures.

GO:0030952.name: establishment or maintenance of cytoskeleton polarity
GO:0030952.def: Any cellular process that results in the specification, formation or maintenance of polarized cytoskeletal structures.

GO:0030990.name: intraciliary transport particle
GO:0030990.def: A nonmembrane-bound oligomeric protein complex that participates in bidirectional transport of molecules (cargo) along axonemal microtubules.

GO:0031012.name: extracellular matrix
GO:0031012.def: A structure lying external to one or more cells, which provides structural support, biochemical or biomechanical cues for cells or tissues.

GO:0031016.name: pancreas development
GO:0031016.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pancreas over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pancreas is an endoderm derived structure that produces precursors of digestive enzymes and blood glucose regulating hormones.

GO:0031017.name: exocrine pancreas development
GO:0031017.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the exocrine pancreas over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The exocrine pancreas produces and store zymogens of digestive enzymes, such as chymotrypsinogen and trypsinogen in the acinar cells.

GO:0031018.name: endocrine pancreas development
GO:0031018.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the endocrine pancreas over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The endocrine pancreas is made up of islet cells that produce insulin, glucagon and somatostatin.

GO:0031022.name: nuclear migration along microfilament
GO:0031022.def: The directed movement of the nucleus along microfilaments within the cell, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0031023.name: microtubule organizing center organization
GO:0031023.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a microtubule organizing center, a structure from which microtubules grow.
synonym: microtubule organizing center organization and biogenesis

GO:0031032.name: actomyosin structure organization
GO:0031032.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures containing both actin and myosin or paramyosin. The myosin may be organized into filaments.

GO:0031045.name: dense core granule
GO:0031045.def: Electron-dense organelle with a granular internal matrix; contains proteins destined to be secreted.

GO:0031069.name: hair follicle morphogenesis
GO:0031069.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the hair follicle are generated and organized.

GO:0031076.name: embryonic camera-type eye development
GO:0031076.def: The process occurring during the embryonic phase whose specific outcome is the progression of the eye over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0031090.name: organelle membrane
GO:0031090.def: A membrane that is one of the two lipid bilayers of an organelle envelope or the outermost membrane of single membrane bound organelle.

GO:0031099.name: regeneration
GO:0031099.def: The regrowth of a lost or destroyed body part, such as an organ or tissue. This process may occur via renewal, repair, and/or growth alone (i.e. increase in size or mass).

GO:0031100.name: animal organ regeneration
GO:0031100.def: The regrowth of a lost or destroyed animal organ.

GO:0031109.name: microtubule polymerization or depolymerization
GO:0031109.def: Assembly or disassembly of microtubules by the addition or removal of tubulin heterodimers from a microtubule.

GO:0031110.name: regulation of microtubule polymerization or depolymerization
GO:0031110.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of microtubule polymerization or depolymerization by the addition or removal of tubulin heterodimers from a microtubule.

GO:0031111.name: negative regulation of microtubule polymerization or depolymerization
GO:0031111.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of microtubule polymerization or depolymerization.

GO:0031122.name: cytoplasmic microtubule organization
GO:0031122.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of structures formed of microtubules and associated proteins in the cytoplasm of a cell.

GO:0031128.name: developmental induction
GO:0031128.def: A developmental process involving two tissues in which one tissue (the inducer) produces a signal that directs cell fate commitment of cells in the second tissue (the responder).

GO:0031143.name: pseudopodium
GO:0031143.def: A temporary protrusion or retractile process of a cell, associated with flowing movements of the protoplasm, and serving for locomotion and feeding.

GO:0031175.name: neuron projection development
GO:0031175.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a neuron projection over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A neuron projection is any process extending from a neural cell, such as axons or dendrites (collectively called neurites).

GO:0031214.name: biomineral tissue development
GO:0031214.def: Formation of hard tissues that consist mainly of inorganic compounds, and also contain a small amounts of organic matrices that are believed to play important roles in their formation.

GO:0031252.name: cell leading edge
GO:0031252.def: The area of a motile cell closest to the direction of movement.

GO:0031253.name: cell projection membrane
GO:0031253.def: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding a plasma membrane bounded cell surface projection.

GO:0031256.name: leading edge membrane
GO:0031256.def: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding the leading edge of a motile cell.

GO:0031268.name: pseudopodium organization
GO:0031268.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a pseudopodium, a temporary protrusion or retractile process of a cell, associated with cellular movement.

GO:0031269.name: pseudopodium assembly
GO:0031269.def: The assembly of a pseudopodium by rearrangement of the actin cytoskeleton and overlying membrane.

GO:0031270.name: pseudopodium retraction
GO:0031270.def: The myosin-based contraction and retraction of a pseudopodium.

GO:0031272.name: regulation of pseudopodium assembly
GO:0031272.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the assembly of pseudopodia.

GO:0031273.name: negative regulation of pseudopodium assembly

GO:0031274.name: positive regulation of pseudopodium assembly

GO:0031294.name: lymphocyte costimulation
GO:0031294.def: The process of providing, via surface-bound receptor-ligand pairs, a second, antigen-independent, signal in addition to that provided by the B- or T cell receptor to augment B- or T cell activation.

GO:0031295.name: T cell costimulation
GO:0031295.def: The process of providing, via surface-bound receptor-ligand pairs, a second, antigen-independent, signal in addition to that provided by the T cell receptor to augment T cell activation.

GO:0031296.name: B cell costimulation
GO:0031296.def: The process of providing, via surface-bound receptor-ligand pairs, a second, antigen-independent, signal in addition to that provided by the B cell receptor to augment B cell activation.

GO:0031406.name: carboxylic acid binding
GO:0031406.def: Binding to a carboxylic acid, an organic acid containing one or more carboxyl (COOH) groups or anions (COO-).

GO:0031409.name: pigment binding
GO:0031409.def: Binding to a pigment, a general or particular coloring matter in living organisms, e.g. melanin.

GO:0031410.name: cytoplasmic vesicle
GO:0031410.def: A vesicle found in the cytoplasm of a cell.

GO:0031420.name: alkali metal ion binding
GO:0031420.def: Binding to an alkali metal ion; alkali metals are those elements in group Ia of the periodic table, with the exception of hydrogen.

GO:0031424.name: keratinization
GO:0031424.def: The process in which the cytoplasm of the outermost cells of the vertebrate epidermis is replaced by keratin. Keratinization occurs in the stratum corneum, feathers, hair, claws, nails, hooves, and horns.

GO:0031503.name: protein-containing complex localization
GO:0031503.def: A localization process that acts on a protein complex; the complex is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.
synonym: establishment and maintenance of cellular protein complex localization
establishment and maintenance of protein complex localization

GO:0031514.name: motile cilium
GO:0031514.def: A cilium which may have a variable arrangement of axonemal microtubules and also contains molecular motors. It may beat with a whip-like pattern that promotes cell motility or transport of fluids and other cells across a cell surface, such as on epithelial cells that line the lumenal ducts of various tissues; or they may display a distinct twirling motion that directs fluid flow asymmetrically across the cellular surface to affect asymmetric body plan organization. Motile cilia can be found in single as well as multiple copies per cell.

GO:0031594.name: neuromuscular junction
GO:0031594.def: The junction between the axon of a motor neuron and a muscle fiber. In response to the arrival of action potentials, the presynaptic button releases molecules of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These diffuse across the cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to a change in post-synaptic potential.

GO:0031641.name: regulation of myelination
GO:0031641.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of a myelin sheath around nerve axons.

GO:0031642.name: negative regulation of myelination

GO:0032835.name: glomerulus development
GO:0032835.def: The progression of the glomerulus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The glomerulus is a capillary tuft which forms a close network with the visceral epithelium (podocytes) and the mesangium to form the filtration barrier and is surrounded by Bowman's capsule in nephrons of the vertebrate kidney. The glomerulus is part of the nephron and is restricted to one body segment.

Kainate receptors are multimeric assemblies of GluK1-3 (also called GluR5-7), GluK4 (KA1) and GluK5 (KA2) subunits.

GO:0034242.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of a syncytium, a mass of cytoplasm containing several nuclei enclosed within a single plasma membrane, by the fusion of the plasma membranes of two or more individual cells.
