GO:0043436.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any oxoacid; an oxoacid is a compound which contains oxygen, at least one other element, and at least one hydrogen bound to oxygen, and which produces a conjugate base by loss of positive hydrogen ion(s) (hydrons).

GO:0043455.name: regulation of secondary metabolic process
GO:0043455.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of secondary metabolism, the chemical reactions and pathways involving compounds that are not necessarily required for growth and maintenance of cells, and are often unique to a taxon.

GO:0043462.name: regulation of ATP-dependent activity
GO:0043462.def: Any process that modulates the rate of an ATP-dependent activity.

GO:0043467.name: regulation of generation of precursor metabolites and energy
GO:0043467.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of precursor metabolites, substances from which energy is derived, and the processes involved in the liberation of energy from these substances.

GO:0043470.name: regulation of carbohydrate catabolic process
GO:0043470.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of carbohydrates.

GO:0043473.name: pigmentation
GO:0043473.def: The accumulation of pigment in an organism, tissue or cell, either by increased deposition or by increased number of cells.

GO:0043474.name: pigment metabolic process involved in pigmentation
GO:0043474.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a pigment, any general or particular coloring matter in living organisms, resulting in the deposition or aggregation of pigment in an organism, tissue or cell.

GO:0043500.name: muscle adaptation
GO:0043500.def: A process in which muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.

GO:0043501.name: skeletal muscle adaptation
GO:0043501.def: Any process in which skeletal muscles change their phenotypic profiles in response to altered functional demands and a variety of signals.

GO:0043502.name: regulation of muscle adaptation
GO:0043502.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of muscle adaptation.

GO:0043523.name: regulation of neuron apoptotic process
GO:0043523.def: Any process that modulates the occurrence or rate of cell death by apoptotic process in neurons.
synonym: regulation of apoptosis of neuronal cells
regulation of neuron programmed cell death
regulation of neuronal cell programmed cell death
regulation of programmed cell death of neuronal cells
regulation of programmed cell death, neurons

GO:0043524.name: negative regulation of neuron apoptotic process
GO:0043524.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cell death by apoptotic process in neurons.
synonym: negative regulation of programmed cell death, neurons

GO:0043525.name: positive regulation of neuron apoptotic process
GO:0043525.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell death of neurons by apoptotic process.
synonym: positive regulation of programmed cell death, neurons

GO:0043534.name: blood vessel endothelial cell migration
GO:0043534.def: The orderly movement of an endothelial cell into the extracellular matrix in order to form new blood vessels during angiogenesis.

GO:0043535.name: regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
GO:0043535.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the migration of the endothelial cells of blood vessels.

GO:0043536.name: positive regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
GO:0043536.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the migration of the endothelial cells of blood vessels.
synonym: activation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
stimulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
up regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
up-regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
upregulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration

GO:0043537.name: negative regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
GO:0043537.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the migration of the endothelial cells of blood vessels.
synonym: down regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
down-regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
downregulation of blood vessel endothelial cell migration
inhibition of blood vessel endothelial cell migration

GO:0043542.name: endothelial cell migration
GO:0043542.def: The orderly movement of an endothelial cell into the extracellular matrix to form an endothelium.

GO:0043549.name: regulation of kinase activity
GO:0043549.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of kinase activity, the catalysis of the transfer of a phosphate group, usually from ATP, to a substrate molecule.

GO:0043555.name: regulation of translation in response to stress
GO:0043555.def: Modulation of the frequency, rate or extent of translation as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress. The stress is usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

GO:0043556.name: regulation of translation in response to oxidative stress
GO:0043556.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of translation as a result of oxidative stress, a state often resulting from exposure to high levels of reactive oxygen species, e.g. superoxide anions, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and hydroxyl radicals.

GO:0043558.name: regulation of translational initiation in response to stress
GO:0043558.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of translation initiation, as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress.
GO:0043558.synonym: regulation of translation initiation in response to stress

GO:0043559.name: insulin binding
GO:0043559.def: Binding to insulin, a polypeptide hormone produced by the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas in mammals, and by the homologous organs of other organisms.

GO:0043576.name: regulation of respiratory gaseous exchange
GO:0043576.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the process of gaseous exchange between an organism and its environment.

GO:0043583.name: ear development
GO:0043583.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the ear over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The ear is the sense organ in vertebrates that is specialized for the detection of sound, and the maintenance of balance. Includes the outer ear and middle ear, which collect and transmit sound waves; and the inner ear, which contains the organs of balance and (except in fish) hearing. Also includes the pinna, the visible part of the outer ear, present in some mammals.

GO:0043584.name: nose development
GO:0043584.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the nose over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The nose is the specialized structure of the face that serves as the organ of the sense of smell and as part of the respiratory system. Includes the nasi externus (external nose) and cavitas nasi (nasal cavity).

GO:0043585.name: nose morphogenesis
GO:0043585.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the nose are generated and organized. The nose is the specialized structure of the face that serves as the organ of the sense of smell and as part of the respiratory system. Includes the nasi externus (external nose) and cavitas nasi (nasal cavity).

GO:0043586.name: tongue development
GO:0043586.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the tongue over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The tongue is the movable, muscular organ on the floor of the mouth of most vertebrates, in many other mammals is the principal organ of taste, aids in the prehension of food, in swallowing, and in modifying the voice as in speech.

GO:0043587.name: tongue morphogenesis
GO:0043587.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the tongue are generated and organized. The tongue is the movable, muscular organ on the floor of the mouth of most vertebrates, in man other mammals is the principal organ of taste, aids in the prehension of food, in swallowing, and in modifying the voice as in speech.

GO:0043588.name: skin development
GO:0043588.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skin over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The skin is the external membranous integument of an animal. In vertebrates the skin generally consists of two layers, an outer nonsensitive and nonvascular epidermis (cuticle or skarfskin) composed of cells which are constantly growing and multiplying in the deeper, and being thrown off in the superficial layers, as well as an inner vascular dermis (cutis, corium or true skin) composed mostly of connective tissue.

GO:0043589.name: skin morphogenesis
GO:0043589.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the skin are generated and organized. The skin is the external membranous integument of an animal. In vertebrates the skin generally consists of two layers, an outer nonsensitive and nonvascular epidermis (cuticle or skarfskin) composed of cells which are constantly growing and multiplying in the deeper, and being thrown off in the superficial layers, as well as an inner, sensitive and vascular dermis (cutis, corium or true skin) composed mostly of connective tissue.

GO:0043603.name: amide metabolic process
GO:0043603.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving an amide, any derivative of an oxoacid in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group, as carried out by individual cells.

GO:0043604.name: amide biosynthetic process
GO:0043604.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of an amide, any derivative of an oxoacid in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

GO:0043605.name: amide catabolic process
GO:0043605.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of an amide, any derivative of an oxoacid in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

GO:0043615.name: astrocyte cell migration
GO:0043615.def: The orderly movement of an astrocyte, a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system, the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord.

GO:0043616.name: keratinocyte proliferation
GO:0043616.def: The multiplication or reproduction of keratinocytes, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. Keratinocytes are epidermal cells which synthesize keratin and undergo a characteristic change as they move upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin.

GO:0043648.name: dicarboxylic acid metabolic process
GO:0043648.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving dicarboxylic acids, any organic acid containing two carboxyl (COOH) groups or anions (COO-).

GO:0043649.name: dicarboxylic acid catabolic process
GO:0043649.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of dicarboxylic acids, any organic acid containing two carboxyl (-COOH) groups.

GO:0043650.name: dicarboxylic acid biosynthetic process
GO:0043650.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of dicarboxylic acids, any organic acid containing two carboxyl (-COOH) groups.

GO:0043679.name: axon terminus
GO:0043679.def: Terminal inflated portion of the axon, containing the specialized apparatus necessary to release neurotransmitters. The axon terminus is considered to be the whole region of thickening and the terminal button is a specialized region of it.

GO:0043695.name: detection of pheromone
GO:0043695.def: The series of events in which a pheromone stimulus is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0043931.name: ossification involved in bone maturation
GO:0043931.def: The formation of bone or of a bony substance, or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone, involved in the progression of the skeleton from its formation to its mature state.

GO:0043932.name: ossification involved in bone remodeling
GO:0043932.def: The formation or growth of bone or of a bony substance, or the conversion of fibrous tissue or of cartilage into bone, involved in response to injury or other physical, physiological or environmental stress stimuli.

GO:0043933.name: protein-containing complex organization
GO:0043933.def: Any process in which macromolecules aggregate, disaggregate, or are modified, resulting in the formation, disassembly, or alteration of a protein complex.

GO:0043934.name: sporulation
GO:0043934.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spore over time, from its initiation to the mature structure. A spore is a structure that can be used for dissemination, for survival of adverse conditions because of its heat and desiccation resistance, and/or for reproduction.

GO:0043935.name: sexual sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore
GO:0043935.def: The formation of spores derived from the products of meiosis. A cellular spore is a cell form that can be used for dissemination, for survival of adverse conditions because of its heat and desiccation resistance, and/or for reproduction.

GO:0043937.name: regulation of sporulation
GO:0043937.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of sporulation, the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spore over time, from its initiation to the mature structure.

GO:0043938.name: positive regulation of sporulation
GO:0043938.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of sporulation, the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spore over time, from its initiation to the mature structure.

GO:0043939.name: negative regulation of sporulation
GO:0043939.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of sporulation, the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spore over time, from its initiation to the mature structure.

GO:0043940.name: regulation of sexual sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore
GO:0043940.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of cellular spores derived from the products of meiosis.

GO:0043941.name: positive regulation of sexual sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore
GO:0043941.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of cellular spores derived from the products of meiosis.

GO:0043942.name: negative regulation of sexual sporulation resulting in formation of a cellular spore
GO:0043942.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of cellular spores derived from the products of meiosis.

GO:0044042.name: glucan metabolic process
GO:0044042.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving glucans, polysaccharides consisting only of glucose residues.

GO:0044057.name: regulation of system process
GO:0044057.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a system process, a multicellular organismal process carried out by any of the organs or tissues in an organ system.

GO:0044058.name: regulation of digestive system process
GO:0044058.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a digestive system process, a physical, chemical, or biochemical process carried out by living organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

GO:0044060.name: regulation of endocrine process
GO:0044060.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of an endocrine process, a process involving the secretion of or response to endocrine hormones. An endocrine hormone is a hormone released into the circulatory system.

GO:0044062.name: regulation of excretion
GO:0044062.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of excretion, the elimination by an organism of the waste products that arise as a result of metabolic activity.

GO:0044065.name: regulation of respiratory system process
GO:0044065.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a respiratory system process, an organ system process carried out by any of the organs or tissues of the respiratory system.

GO:0044085.name: cellular component biogenesis
GO:0044085.def: A process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a cellular component. Includes biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, and those macromolecular modifications that are involved in synthesis or assembly of the cellular component.
GO:0044085.synonym: cellular component biogenesis at cellular level

GO:0044087.name: regulation of cellular component biogenesis
GO:0044087.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cellular component biogenesis, a process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a cellular component.

GO:0044088.name: regulation of vacuole organization
GO:0044088.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a process involved in the formation, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a vacuole.

GO:0044089.name: positive regulation of cellular component biogenesis
GO:0044089.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cellular component biogenesis, a process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a cellular component.

GO:0044090.name: positive regulation of vacuole organization
GO:0044090.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a process involved in the formation, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a vacuole.

GO:0044091.name: membrane biogenesis
GO:0044091.def: A cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of a membrane.

GO:0044092.name: negative regulation of molecular function
GO:0044092.def: Any process that stops or reduces the rate or extent of a molecular function, an elemental biological activity occurring at the molecular level, such as catalysis or binding.

GO:0044093.name: positive regulation of molecular function
GO:0044093.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of a molecular function, an elemental biological activity occurring at the molecular level, such as catalysis or binding.

GO:0044207.name: translation initiation ternary complex
GO:0044207.def: A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains aminoacylated initiator methionine tRNA, GTP, and initiation factor 2 (either eIF2 in eukaryotes, or IF2 in prokaryotes). In prokaryotes, fMet-tRNA (initiator) is used rather than Met-tRNA (initiator).

GO:0044237.name: obsolete cellular metabolic process
GO:0044237.def: OBSOLETE. The chemical reactions and pathways by which individual cells transform chemical substances.

GO:0044238.name: primary metabolic process
GO:0044238.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving those compounds which are formed as a part of the normal anabolic and catabolic processes. These processes take place in most, if not all, cells of the organism.

GO:0044258.name: intestinal lipid catabolic process
GO:0044258.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown into fatty acids and monoglycerides of lipids in the small intestine. Lipids are broken down by lipases released by the pancreas.

GO:0044272.name: sulfur compound biosynthetic process
GO:0044272.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of compounds that contain sulfur, such as the amino acids methionine and cysteine or the tripeptide glutathione.

GO:0044273.name: sulfur compound catabolic process
GO:0044273.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of compounds that contain sulfur, such as the amino acids methionine and cysteine or the tripeptide glutathione.

GO:0044281.name: small molecule metabolic process
GO:0044281.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving small molecules, any low molecular weight, monomeric, non-encoded molecule.

GO:0044282.name: small molecule catabolic process
GO:0044282.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of small molecules, any low molecular weight, monomeric, non-encoded molecule.

GO:0044283.name: small molecule biosynthetic process
GO:0044283.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of small molecules, any low molecular weight, monomeric, non-encoded molecule.

GO:0044292.name: dendrite terminus
GO:0044292.def: A structure at the distal end of a dendrite adapted to carry out a specific function, e.g. dendriole.

GO:0044293.name: dendriole
GO:0044293.def: Small dendrites that makes up a brush structure found as the terminal specialization of a dendrite of a unipolar brush cell (UBC).

GO:0044297.name: cell body
GO:0044297.def: The portion of a cell bearing surface projections such as axons, dendrites, cilia, or flagella that includes the nucleus, but excludes all cell projections.

GO:0044306.name: neuron projection terminus
GO:0044306.def: The specialized, terminal region of a neuron projection such as an axon or a dendrite.

GO:0044316.name: cone cell pedicle
GO:0044316.def: A specialized axon terminus which is produced by retinal cone cells. Pedicles are large, conical, flat end-feet (8-10 micrometers diameter) of the retinal cone axon that lie more or less side by side on the same plane at the outer edge of the outer plexiform layer (OPL).

GO:0044342.name: type B pancreatic cell proliferation
GO:0044342.def: The multiplication or reproduction of pancreatic B cells, resulting in the expansion of an pancreatic B cell population. Pancreatic B cell are cells of the pancreas that secrete insulin.

GO:0044346.name: fibroblast apoptotic process
GO:0044346.def: Any apoptotic process in a fibroblast, a connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules.

GO:0044380.name: protein localization to cytoskeleton
GO:0044380.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within the cytoskeleton.

GO:0044419.name: biological process involved in interspecies interaction between organisms
GO:0044419.def: Any process evolved to enable an interaction with an organism of a different species.

GO:0044458.name: motile cilium assembly
GO:0044458.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a motile cilium.

GO:0044565.name: dendritic cell proliferation
GO:0044565.def: The expansion of a dendritic cell population by cell division. A dendritic cell is a cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation.

GO:0044566.name: chondrocyte activation
GO:0044566.def: A change in the morphology or behavior of a chondrocyte resulting from exposure to an activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand. A chondrocyte is a polymorphic cell that forms cartilage.

GO:0044703.name: multi-organism reproductive process
GO:0044703.def: A biological process that directly contributes to the process of producing new individuals, involving another organism.

GO:0044706.name: multi-multicellular organism process
GO:0044706.def: A multicellular organism process which involves another multicellular organism of the same or different species.

GO:0044743.name: protein transmembrane import into intracellular organelle
GO:0044743.def: The directed movement of proteins into an intracellular organelle, across a membrane.

GO:0044782.name: cilium organization
GO:0044782.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a cilium, a specialized eukaryotic organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface. Each cilium is bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored basally in a centriole.

GO:0044848.name: biological phase
GO:0044848.def: A distinct period or stage in a biological process or cycle.

GO:0044872.name: lipoprotein localization
GO:0044872.def: Any process in which a lipoprotein is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

GO:0044873.name: lipoprotein localization to membrane
GO:0044873.def: A process in which a lipoprotein is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location in a membrane.

GO:0044874.name: lipoprotein localization to outer membrane
GO:0044874.def: A process in which a lipoprotein is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location in an outer membrane.

GO:0045009.name: chitosome
GO:0045009.def: An intracellular membrane-bounded particle found in fungi and containing chitin synthase; it synthesizes chitin microfibrils. Chitin synthase activity exists in chitosomes and they are proposed to act as a reservoir for regulated transport of chitin synthase enzymes to the division septum.

GO:0045019.name: negative regulation of nitric oxide biosynthetic process
GO:0045019.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of nitric oxide.
synonym: down regulation of nitric oxide biosynthetic process
down-regulation of nitric oxide biosynthetic process
downregulation of nitric oxide biosynthetic process
inhibition of nitric oxide biosynthetic process
negative regulation of nitric oxide anabolism
negative regulation of nitric oxide biosynthesis
negative regulation of nitric oxide formation
negative regulation of nitric oxide synthesis

GO:0045026.name: plasma membrane fusion
GO:0045026.def: The joining of the lipid bilayer membrane that surround a cell with that of another cell, producing a single cell.

GO:0045028.name: G protein-coupled purinergic nucleotide receptor activity
GO:0045028.def: Combining with a purine nucleotide and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.
synonym: G protein coupled purinergic nucleotide receptor activity
G-protein coupled purinergic nucleotide receptor activity
purinergic nucleotide receptor activity, G protein coupled
purinergic nucleotide receptor activity, G-protein coupled

GO:0045031.name: G protein-coupled ATP receptor activity
GO:0045031.def: Combining with ATP and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.

GO:0045055.name: regulated exocytosis
GO:0045055.def: A process of exocytosis in which soluble proteins and other substances are initially stored in secretory vesicles for later release. It is found mainly in cells that are specialized for secreting products such as hormones, neurotransmitters, or digestive enzymes rapidly on demand.

GO:0045058.name: T cell selection
GO:0045058.def: The process in which T cells that express T cell receptors that are restricted by self MHC protein complexes and tolerant to self antigens are selected for further maturation.

GO:0045063.name: T-helper 1 cell differentiation
GO:0045063.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized T cell acquires the specialized features of a T-helper 1 (Th1) cell. A Th1 cell is a CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has the phenotype T-bet-positive and produces interferon-gamma.

GO:0045064.name: T-helper 2 cell differentiation
GO:0045064.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized T cell acquires specialized features of a T-helper 2 (Th2) cell. A Th2 cell is a CD4-positive, alpha-beta T cell that has the phenotype GATA-3-positive and produces interleukin-4.

GO:0045065.name: cytotoxic T cell differentiation
GO:0045065.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized T cell acquires specialized features of a cytotoxic T cell.

GO:0045066.name: regulatory T cell differentiation
GO:0045066.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized T cell acquires specialized features of a regulatory T cell. Regulatory T cells control or suppress immune responses through a variety of mechanisms and subsets include the CD4+CD25+ cell type as well as certain CD8+ cell types.

GO:0045087.name: innate immune response
GO:0045087.def: Innate immune responses are defense responses mediated by germline encoded components that directly recognize components of potential pathogens.

GO:0045088.name: regulation of innate immune response
GO:0045088.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the innate immune response, the organism's first line of defense against infection.

GO:0045089.name: positive regulation of innate immune response
GO:0045089.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the innate immune response, the organism's first line of defense against infection.
synonym: up regulation of innate immune response

GO:0045095.name: keratin filament
GO:0045095.def: A filament composed of acidic and basic keratins (types I and II), typically expressed in epithelial cells. The keratins are the most diverse classes of IF proteins, with a large number of keratin isoforms being expressed. Each type of epithelium always expresses a characteristic combination of type I and type II keratins.

GO:0045103.name: intermediate filament-based process
GO:0045103.def: Any cellular process that depends upon or alters the intermediate filament cytoskeleton, that part of the cytoskeleton comprising intermediate filaments and their associated proteins.

GO:0045104.name: intermediate filament cytoskeleton organization
GO:0045104.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising intermediate filaments and their associated proteins.
synonym: intermediate filament cytoskeleton organization and biogenesis

GO:0045109.name: intermediate filament organization
GO:0045109.def: Control of the spatial distribution of intermediate filaments; includes organizing filaments into meshworks, bundles, or other structures, as by cross-linking.

GO:0045110.name: intermediate filament bundle assembly
GO:0045110.def: The formation of the bundles of intermediate filaments. Intermediate filament-associated proteins (IFAPs) cross-link intermediate filaments with one another, forming a bundle or a network, and with other cell structures, including the plasma membrane. The organization of intermediate filaments and their supportive function in various cells types depends in large part on their linkage to other cell structures via IFAPs.

GO:0045111.name: intermediate filament cytoskeleton
GO:0045111.def: Cytoskeletal structure made from intermediate filaments, typically organized in the cytosol as an extended system that stretches from the nuclear envelope to the plasma membrane. Some intermediate filaments run parallel to the cell surface, while others traverse the cytosol; together they form an internal framework that helps support the shape and resilience of the cell.

GO:0045117.name: azole transmembrane transport
GO:0045117.def: The directed movement of azoles, heterocyclic compounds found in many biologically important substances, across a lipid bilayer, across a membrane.

GO:0045120.name: pronucleus
GO:0045120.def: The nucleus of either the ovum or the spermatozoon following fertilization. Thus, in the fertilized ovum, there are two pronuclei, one originating from the ovum, the other from the spermatozoon that brought about fertilization; they approach each other, but do not fuse until just before the first cleavage, when each pronucleus loses its membrane to release its contents.

GO:0045124.name: regulation of bone resorption
GO:0045124.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of bone tissue loss (resorption).

GO:0045132.name: meiotic chromosome segregation
GO:0045132.def: The process in which genetic material, in the form of chromosomes, is organized into specific structures and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets during M phase of the meiotic cell cycle.

GO:0045137.name: development of primary sexual characteristics
GO:0045137.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the primary sexual characteristics over time, from their formation to the mature structures. The primary sexual characteristics are the testes in males and the ovaries in females and they develop in response to sex hormone secretion.

GO:0045144.name: meiotic sister chromatid segregation
GO:0045144.def: The cell cycle process in which sister chromatids are organized and then physically separated and randomly apportioned to two sets during the second division of the meiotic cell cycle.

GO:0045165.name: cell fate commitment
GO:0045165.def: The cellular developmental process by which a cell establishes the intrinsic character of a cell or tissue region irreversibly committing it to a particular fate.

GO:0045168.name: cell-cell signaling involved in cell fate commitment
GO:0045168.def: Signaling at long or short range between cells that results in the commitment of a cell to a certain fate.
synonym: cell-cell signaling during in cell fate commitment
cell-cell signaling resulting in cell fate commitment
cell-cell signalling during cell fate commitment
cell-cell signalling involved in cell fate specification
cell-cell signalling resulting in cell fate commitment

GO:0045184.name: establishment of protein localization
GO:0045184.def: The directed movement of a protein to a specific location.

GO:0045185.name: maintenance of protein location
GO:0045185.def: Any process in which a protein is maintained in a location and prevented from moving elsewhere. These include sequestration, stabilization to prevent transport elsewhere and the active retrieval of proteins that do move away.

GO:0045190.name: isotype switching
GO:0045190.def: The switching of activated B cells from IgM biosynthesis to biosynthesis of other isotypes of immunoglobulin, accomplished through a recombination process involving an intrachromosomal deletion involving switch regions that reside 5' of each constant region gene segment in the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus.

GO:0045191.name: regulation of isotype switching
GO:0045191.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of isotype switching.

GO:0045196.name: establishment or maintenance of neuroblast polarity

GO:0045202.name: synapse
GO:0045202.def: The junction between an axon of one neuron and a dendrite of another neuron, a muscle fiber or a glial cell. As the axon approaches the synapse it enlarges into a specialized structure, the presynaptic terminal bouton, which contains mitochondria and synaptic vesicles. At the tip of the terminal bouton is the presynaptic membrane; facing it, and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft) is a specialized area of membrane on the receiving cell, known as the postsynaptic membrane. In response to the arrival of nerve impulses, the presynaptic terminal bouton secretes molecules of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These diffuse across the cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane.

GO:0045211.name: postsynaptic membrane
GO:0045211.def: A specialized area of membrane facing the presynaptic membrane on the tip of the nerve ending and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft). Neurotransmitters cross the synaptic cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane.

GO:0045214.name: sarcomere organization

GO:0045216.name: cell-cell junction organization

GO:0046530.def: The specialization of organization of a photoreceptor, a cell that responds to incident electromagnetic radiation, particularly visible light. An example of this process is found in Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0046541.name: saliva secretion
GO:0046541.def: The regulated release of saliva from the salivary glands. In man, the saliva is a turbid and slightly viscous fluid, generally of an alkaline reaction, and is secreted by the parotid, submaxillary, and sublingual glands. In the mouth the saliva is mixed with the secretion from the buccal glands. In man and many animals, saliva is an important digestive fluid on account of the presence of the peculiar enzyme, ptyalin.

GO:0046545.name: development of primary female sexual characteristics
GO:0046545.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the primary female sexual characteristics over time, from their formation to the mature structure. The primary female sexual characteristics are the ovaries, and they develop in response to sex hormone secretion.

GO:0046546.name: development of primary male sexual characteristics

GO:0046548.name: retinal rod cell development
GO:0046548.def: Development of a rod cell, one of the sensory cells in the eye that reacts to the presence of light. Rod cells contain the photopigment rhodopsin or porphyropsin and are responsible for vision in dim light.

GO:0046549.name: retinal cone cell development
GO:0046549.def: Development of a cone cell, one of the sensory cells in the eye that reacts to the presence of light. Cone cells contain the photopigment iodopsin or cyanopsin and are responsible for photopic (daylight) vision.

GO:0046683.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an organophosphorus stimulus. GO:0046697.name: decidualization
GO:0046697.def: The cellular and vascular changes occurring in the endometrium of the pregnant uterus just after the onset of blastocyst implantation. This process involves the proliferation and differentiation of the fibroblast-like endometrial stromal cells into large, polyploid decidual cells that eventually form the maternal component of the placenta.

GO:0046716.name: muscle cell cellular homeostasis

GO:0046848.name: hydroxyapatite binding
GO:0046848.def: Binding to hydroxyapatite, the calcium phosphate mineral of formula Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2 found both in rocks of nonorganic origin and as a component of bone and dentin.

GO:0046849.name: bone remodeling
GO:0046849.def: The continuous turnover of bone matrix and mineral that involves first, an increase in resorption (osteoclastic activity) and later, reactive bone formation (osteoblastic activity). The process of bone remodeling takes place in the adult skeleton at discrete foci. The process ensures the mechanical integrity of the skeleton throughout life and plays an important role in calcium homeostasis. An imbalance in the regulation of bone resorption and bone formation results in many of the metabolic bone diseases, such as osteoporosis.

GO:0046850.name: regulation of bone remodeling
GO:0046850.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of bone remodeling, the processes of bone formation and resorption that combine to maintain skeletal integrity.

GO:0046864.name: isoprenoid transport
GO:0046864.def: The directed movement of isoprenoids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Isoprenoids comprise a group of compounds containing or derived from linked isoprene (3-methyl-2-butenylene) residues.

GO:0046865.name: terpenoid transport
GO:0046865.def: The directed movement of terpenoids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Terpenoids are a class of compounds characterized by an isoprenoid chemical structure and include derivatives with various functional groups.

GO:0046866.name: tetraterpenoid transport
GO:0046866.def: The directed movement of tetraterpenoids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Tetraterpenoids are terpenoids with eight isoprene units.

GO:0046867.name: carotenoid transport
GO:0046867.def: The directed movement of carotenoids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carotenoids are tetraterpenoid compounds in which two units of 4 isoprenoid residues joined head-to-tail are themselves joined tail-to-tail.

GO:0046873.def: Enables the transfer of metal ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0046888.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of a hormone from a cell.

GO:0046889.name: positive regulation of lipid biosynthetic process
GO:0046889.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipids.
synonym: up regulation of lipid biosynthetic process

GO:0046890.name: regulation of lipid biosynthetic process
GO:0046890.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lipids.

GO:0046903.name: secretion
GO:0046903.def: The controlled release of a substance by a cell or a tissue.

GO:0046907.name: intracellular transport
GO:0046907.def: The directed movement of substances within a cell.

GO:0046914.name: transition metal ion binding
GO:0046914.def: Binding to a transition metal ions; a transition metal is an element whose atom has an incomplete d-subshell of extranuclear electrons, or which gives rise to a cation or cations with an incomplete d-subshell. Transition metals often have more than one valency state. Biologically relevant transition metals include vanadium, manganese, iron, copper, cobalt, nickel, molybdenum and silver.

GO:0046915.name: transition metal ion transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0046915.def: Enables the transfer of transition metal ions from one side of a membrane to the other. A transition metal is an element whose atom has an incomplete d-subshell of extranuclear electrons, or which gives rise to a cation or cations with an incomplete d-subshell. Transition metals often have more than one valency state. Biologically relevant transition metals include vanadium, manganese, iron, copper, cobalt, nickel, molybdenum and silver.

GO:0046928.name: regulation of neurotransmitter secretion
GO:0046928.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of a neurotransmitter from a cell.

GO:0046929.name: negative regulation of neurotransmitter secretion
GO:0046929.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of a neurotransmitter.

GO:0046930.name: pore complex
GO:0046930.def: A protein complex providing a discrete opening in a membrane that allows the passage of gases and/or liquids.

GO:0046931.name: pore complex assembly
GO:0046931.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a pore complex. A pore complex is a small opening in a membrane that allows the passage of liquids and/or gases.

GO:0046942.name: carboxylic acid transport
GO:0046942.def: The directed movement of carboxylic acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carboxylic acids are organic acids containing one or more carboxyl (COOH) groups or anions (COO-).

GO:0046943.name: carboxylic acid transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0046943.def: Enables the transfer of carboxylic acids from one side of a membrane to the other. Carboxylic acids are organic acids containing one or more carboxyl (COOH) groups or anions (COO-).

GO:0047496.name: vesicle transport along microtubule
GO:0047496.def: The directed movement of a vesicle along a microtubule, mediated by motor proteins. This process begins with the attachment of a vesicle to a microtubule, and ends when the vesicle reaches its final destination.

GO:0048002.name: antigen processing and presentation of peptide antigen
GO:0048002.def: The process in which an antigen-presenting cell expresses peptide antigen in association with an MHC protein complex on its cell surface, including proteolysis and transport steps for the peptide antigen both prior to and following assembly with the MHC protein complex. The peptide antigen is typically, but not always, processed from an endogenous or exogenous protein.

GO:0048020.name: CCR chemokine receptor binding
GO:0048020.def: Binding to a CCR chemokine receptor.

GO:0048029.name: monosaccharide binding
GO:0048029.def: Binding to a monosaccharide. Monosaccharides are the simplest carbohydrates; they are polyhydroxy aldehydes H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)H or polyhydroxy ketones H[CHOH]nC(=O)[CHOH]mH with three or more carbon atoms. They form the constitutional repeating units of oligo- and polysaccharides.

GO:0048048.name: embryonic eye morphogenesis
GO:0048048.def: The process occurring in the embryo by which the anatomical structures of the post-embryonic eye are generated and organized.

GO:0048066.name: developmental pigmentation
GO:0048066.def: The developmental process that results in the deposition of coloring matter in an organism, tissue or cell.

GO:0048070.name: regulation of developmental pigmentation
GO:0048070.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the developmental process that results in the deposition of coloring matter in an organism.

GO:0048086.name: negative regulation of developmental pigmentation
GO:0048086.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the developmental process that results in the deposition of coloring matter in an organism.

GO:0048087.name: positive regulation of developmental pigmentation
GO:0048087.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the developmental process that results in the deposition of coloring matter in an organism.

GO:0048103.name: somatic stem cell division
GO:0048103.def: The self-renewing division of a somatic stem cell, a stem cell that can give rise to cell types of the body other than those of the germ-line.

GO:0048132.name: female germ-line stem cell asymmetric division
GO:0048132.def: The self-renewing division of a germline stem cell in the female gonad, to produce a daughter stem cell and a daughter germ cell, which will divide to form the female gametes.

GO:0048133.name: male germ-line stem cell asymmetric division
GO:0048133.def: The self-renewing division of a germline stem cell in the male gonad, to produce a daughter stem cell and a daughter germ cell, which will divide to form the male gametes.

GO:0048137.name: spermatocyte division
GO:0048137.def: The meiotic divisions undergone by the primary and secondary spermatocytes to produce haploid spermatids.

GO:0048143.name: astrocyte activation
GO:0048143.def: A change in morphology and behavior of an astrocyte resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

GO:0048144.name: fibroblast proliferation
GO:0048144.def: The multiplication or reproduction of fibroblast cells, resulting in the expansion of the fibroblast population.

GO:0048145.name: regulation of fibroblast proliferation
GO:0048145.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of multiplication or reproduction of fibroblast cells.

GO:0048146.name: positive regulation of fibroblast proliferation
GO:0048146.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of multiplication or reproduction of fibroblast cells.

GO:0048147.name: negative regulation of fibroblast proliferation
GO:0048147.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of multiplication or reproduction of fibroblast cells.

GO:0048162.name: multi-layer follicle stage
GO:0048162.def: The stage in oogenesis when many layers of follicle cells surround the oocyte. There is a yolk nucleus (Balbiani's Body) near the germinal vesicle.

GO:0048165.name: fused antrum stage
GO:0048165.def: The stage in oogenesis when the antral spaces fuse to form a single antral space. The oocyte is suspended in the cumulus oophorous and the first polar body in the perivitelline space.

GO:0048193.name: Golgi vesicle transport
GO:0048193.def: The directed movement of substances into, out of or within the Golgi apparatus, mediated by vesicles.

GO:0048194.name: Golgi vesicle budding
GO:0048194.def: The evagination of the Golgi membrane, resulting in formation of a vesicle.

GO:0048199.name: vesicle targeting, to, from or within Golgi
GO:0048199.def: The process in which vesicles are directed to specific destination membranes during transport to, from or within the Golgi apparatus; mediated by the addition of specific coat proteins, including COPI and COPII proteins and clathrin, to the membrane during vesicle formation.
synonym: vesicle targeting, to, from or within dictyosome

GO:0048209.name: regulation of vesicle targeting, to, from or within Golgi
GO:0048209.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or destination of vesicle-mediated transport to, from or within the Golgi apparatus.

GO:0048232.name: male gamete generation
GO:0048232.def: Generation of the male gamete; specialised haploid cells produced by meiosis and along with a female gamete takes part in sexual reproduction.

GO:0048240.name: sperm capacitation
GO:0048240.def: A process required for sperm to reach fertilization competence. Sperm undergo an incompletely understood series of morphological and molecular maturational processes, termed capacitation, involving, among other processes, protein tyrosine phosphorylation and increased intracellular calcium.

GO:0048241.name: epinephrine transport
GO:0048241.def: The directed movement of epinephrine into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0048242.name: epinephrine secretion
GO:0048242.def: The regulated release of epinephrine by a cell. Epinephrine is a catecholamine hormone secreted by the adrenal medulla and a neurotransmitter, released by certain neurons and active in the central nervous system.

GO:0048243.name: norepinephrine secretion
GO:0048243.def: The regulated release of norepinephrine by a cell. Norepinephrine is a catecholamine and it acts as a hormone and as a neurotransmitter of most of the sympathetic nervous system.

GO:0048245.name: eosinophil chemotaxis
GO:0048245.def: The movement of an eosinophil in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0048246.name: macrophage chemotaxis
GO:0048246.def: The movement of a macrophage in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0048247.name: lymphocyte chemotaxis
GO:0048247.def: The directed movement of a lymphocyte in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0048251.name: elastic fiber assembly
GO:0048251.def: Assembly of the extracellular matrix fibers that enables the matrix to recoil after transient stretching.

GO:0048280.name: vesicle fusion with Golgi apparatus
GO:0048280.def: The joining of the lipid bilayer membrane around a vesicle to the lipid bilayer membrane around the Golgi.

GO:0048284.name: organelle fusion
GO:0048284.def: The creation of a single organelle from two or more organelles.

GO:0048285.name: organelle fission
GO:0048285.def: The creation of two or more organelles by division of one organelle.

GO:0048286.name: lung alveolus development
GO:0048286.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the alveolus over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The alveolus is a sac for holding air in the lungs; formed by the terminal dilation of air passageways.

GO:0048288.name: nuclear membrane fusion involved in karyogamy
GO:0048288.def: The joining of 2 or more lipid bilayer membranes that surround the nucleus during the creation of a single nucleus from multiple nuclei.

GO:0048289.name: isotype switching to IgE isotypes
GO:0048289.def: The switching of activated B cells from IgM biosynthesis to IgE biosynthesis, accomplished through a recombination process involving an intrachromosomal deletion between switch regions that reside 5' of the IgM and IgE constant region gene segments in the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus.
synonym: class switch recombination to IgE isotypes
isotype switch recombination to IgE isotypes

GO:0048293.name: regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
GO:0048293.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of isotype switching to IgE isotypes.
synonym: regulation of class switch recombination to IgE isotypes
regulation of class switching to IgE isotypes
regulation of isotype switch recombination to IgE isotypes

GO:0048294.name: negative regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
GO:0048294.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of isotype switching to IgE isotypes.
synonym: down regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
down-regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
downregulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
inhibition of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
negative regulation of class switch recombination to IgE isotypes
negative regulation of class switching to IgE isotypes
negative regulation of isotype switch recombination to IgE isotypes

GO:0048295.name: positive regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
GO:0048295.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of isotype switching to IgE isotypes.
synonym: activation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
positive regulation of class switch recombination to IgE isotypes
positive regulation of class switching to IgE isotypes
positive regulation of isotype switch recombination to IgE isotypes
stimulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
up regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
up-regulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes
upregulation of isotype switching to IgE isotypes

GO:0048306.name: calcium-dependent protein binding
GO:0048306.def: Binding to a protein or protein complex in the presence of calcium.

GO:0048308.name: organelle inheritance
GO:0048308.def: The partitioning of organelles between daughter cells at cell division.

GO:0048313.name: Golgi inheritance
GO:0048313.def: The partitioning of Golgi apparatus between daughter cells at cell division.

GO:0048318.name: axial mesoderm development
GO:0048318.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the axial mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The axial mesoderm includes the prechordal mesoderm and the chordamesoderm. It gives rise to the prechordal plate and to the notochord.

GO:0048319.name: axial mesoderm morphogenesis
GO:0048319.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the axial mesoderm are generated and organized.

GO:0048320.name: axial mesoderm formation
GO:0048320.def: The process that gives rise to the axial mesoderm. This process pertains to the initial formation of the structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0048332.name: mesoderm morphogenesis
GO:0048332.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesoderm are generated and organized.

GO:0048333.name: mesodermal cell differentiation
GO:0048333.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a mesoderm cell.

GO:0048339.name: paraxial mesoderm development
GO:0048339.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the paraxial mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The paraxial mesoderm is the mesoderm located bilaterally adjacent to the notochord and neural tube.

GO:0048340.name: paraxial mesoderm morphogenesis
GO:0048340.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the paraxial mesoderm are generated and organized.

GO:0048341.name: paraxial mesoderm formation
GO:0048341.def: The process that gives rise to the paraxial mesoderm. This process pertains to the initial formation of the structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0048368.name: lateral mesoderm development
GO:0048368.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lateral mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0048369.name: lateral mesoderm morphogenesis
GO:0048369.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the lateral mesoderm are generated and organized.

GO:0048370.name: lateral mesoderm formation
GO:0048370.def: The process that gives rise to the lateral mesoderm. This process pertains to the initial formation of the structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0048389.name: intermediate mesoderm development
GO:0048389.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the intermediate mesoderm over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The intermediate mesoderm is located between the lateral mesoderm and the paraxial mesoderm. It develops into the kidney and gonads.

GO:0048390.name: intermediate mesoderm morphogenesis
GO:0048390.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the intermediate mesoderm are generated and organized.

GO:0048391.name: intermediate mesoderm formation
GO:0048391.def: The process that gives rise to the intermediate mesoderm. This process pertains to the initial formation of the structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0048468.name: cell development
GO:0048468.def: The cellular developmental process in which a specific cell progresses from an immature to a mature state. Cell development start once cell commitment has taken place.

GO:0048469.name: cell maturation
GO:0048469.def: The cellular developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a specific cell to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0048477.name: oogenesis
GO:0048477.def: The complete process of formation and maturation of an ovum or female gamete from a primordial female germ cell. Examples of this process are found in Mus musculus and Drosophila melanogaster.

GO:0048483.name: autonomic nervous system development
GO:0048483.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the autonomic nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The autonomic nervous system is composed of neurons that are not under conscious control, and is comprised of two antagonistic components, the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. The autonomic nervous system regulates key functions including the activity of the cardiac (heart) muscle, smooth muscles (e.g. of the gut), and glands.

GO:0048484.name: enteric nervous system development
GO:0048484.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the enteric nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The enteric nervous system is composed of two ganglionated neural plexuses in the gut wall which form one of the three major divisions of the autonomic nervous system. The enteric nervous system innervates the gastrointestinal tract, the pancreas, and the gallbladder. It contains sensory neurons, interneurons, and motor neurons. Thus the circuitry can autonomously sense the tension and the chemical environment in the gut and regulate blood vessel tone, motility, secretions, and fluid transport. The system is itself governed by the central nervous system and receives both parasympathetic and sympathetic innervation.

GO:0048485.name: sympathetic nervous system development
GO:0048485.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the sympathetic nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The sympathetic nervous system is one of the two divisions of the vertebrate autonomic nervous system (the other being the parasympathetic nervous system). The sympathetic preganglionic neurons have their cell bodies in the thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord and connect to the paravertebral chain of sympathetic ganglia. Innervate heart and blood vessels, sweat glands, viscera and the adrenal medulla. Most sympathetic neurons, but not all, use noradrenaline as a post-ganglionic neurotransmitter.

GO:0048486.name: parasympathetic nervous system development
GO:0048486.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the parasympathetic nervous system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The parasympathetic nervous system is one of the two divisions of the vertebrate autonomic nervous system. Parasympathetic nerves emerge cranially as pre ganglionic fibers from oculomotor, facial, glossopharyngeal and vagus and from the sacral region of the spinal cord. Most neurons are cholinergic and responses are mediated by muscarinic receptors. The parasympathetic system innervates, for example: salivary glands, thoracic and abdominal viscera, bladder and genitalia.

GO:0048505.name: regulation of timing of cell differentiation
GO:0048505.def: The process controlling the activation and/or rate at which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized features. Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the XXX at a consistent predetermined time point during its development.

GO:0048511.name: rhythmic process
GO:0048511.def: Any process pertinent to the generation and maintenance of rhythms in the physiology of an organism.

GO:0048513.name: animal organ development
GO:0048513.def: Development of a tissue or tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Development pertains to the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a structure over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

GO:0048514.name: blood vessel morphogenesis
GO:0048514.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of blood vessels are generated and organized. The blood vessel is the vasculature carrying blood.

GO:0048515.name: spermatid differentiation
GO:0048515.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spermatid over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0048518.name: positive regulation of biological process
GO:0048518.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a biological process. Biological processes are regulated by many means; examples include the control of gene expression, protein modification or interaction with a protein or substrate molecule.

GO:0048519.name: negative regulation of biological process
GO:0048519.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a biological process. Biological processes are regulated by many means; examples include the control of gene expression, protein modification or interaction with a protein or substrate molecule.

GO:0048520.name: positive regulation of behavior
GO:0048520.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of behavior, the internally coordinated responses (actions or inactions) of whole living organisms (individuals or groups) to internal or external stimuli.

GO:0048521.name: negative regulation of behavior
GO:0048521.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of behavior, the internally coordinated responses (actions or inactions) of whole living organisms (individuals or groups) to internal or external stimuli.

GO:0048522.name: positive regulation of cellular process
GO:0048522.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a cellular process, any of those that are carried out at the cellular level, but are not necessarily restricted to a single cell. For example, cell communication occurs among more than one cell, but occurs at the cellular level.
synonym: positive regulation of cellular physiological process

GO:0048523.name: negative regulation of cellular process
GO:0048523.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a cellular process, any of those that are carried out at the cellular level, but are not necessarily restricted to a single cell. For example, cell communication occurs among more than one cell, but occurs at the cellular level.
synonym: negative regulation of cellular physiological process

GO:0048534.name: hematopoietic or lymphoid organ development
GO:0048534.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of any organ involved in hematopoiesis (also known as hemopoiesis) or lymphoid cell activation over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Such development includes differentiation of resident cell types (stromal cells) and of migratory cell types dependent on the unique microenvironment afforded by the organ for their proper differentiation.

GO:0048535.name: lymph node development
GO:0048535.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of lymph nodes over time, from their formation to the mature structure. A lymph node is a round, oval, or bean shaped structure localized in clusters along the lymphatic vessels, with a distinct internal structure including specialized vasculature and B- and T-zones for the activation of lymphocytes.

GO:0048536.name: spleen development
GO:0048536.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the spleen over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The spleen is a large vascular lymphatic organ composed of white and red pulp, involved both in hemopoietic and immune system functions.

GO:0048537.name: mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue development
GO:0048537.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Mucosal-associated lymphoid tissue is typically found as nodules associated with mucosal epithelia with distinct internal structures including B- and T-zones for the activation of lymphocytes.

GO:0048538.name: thymus development
GO:0048538.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the thymus over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The thymus is a symmetric bi-lobed organ involved primarily in the differentiation of immature to mature T cells, with unique vascular, nervous, epithelial, and lymphoid cell components.

GO:0048539.name: bone marrow development
GO:0048539.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the bone marrow over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0048541.name: Peyer's patch development
GO:0048541.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of Peyer's patches over time, from their formation to the mature structure. Peyer's patches are typically found as nodules associated with gut epithelium with distinct internal structures including B- and T-zones for the activation of lymphocytes.

GO:0048542.name: lymph gland development
GO:0048542.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lymph gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The lymph gland is one of the sites of hemocyte differentiation. It consists of three to six bilaterally paired lobes that are attached to the cardioblasts during larval stages, and it degenerates during pupal stages.

GO:0048545.name: response to steroid hormone
GO:0048545.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a steroid hormone stimulus.

GO:0048546.name: digestive tract morphogenesis
GO:0048546.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the digestive tract are generated and organized. The digestive tract is the anatomical structure through which food passes and is processed.

GO:0048562.name: embryonic organ morphogenesis
GO:0048562.def: Morphogenesis, during the embryonic phase, of a tissue or tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Morphogenesis is the process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

GO:0048565.name: digestive tract development
GO:0048565.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the digestive tract over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The digestive tract is the anatomical structure through which food passes and is processed.

GO:0048568.name: embryonic organ development
GO:0048568.def: Development, taking place during the embryonic phase, of a tissue or tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Development pertains to the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a structure over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

GO:0048570.name: notochord morphogenesis
GO:0048570.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the notochord are generated and organized. The notochord is a mesoderm-derived structure located ventral of the developing nerve cord. In vertebrates, the notochord serves as a core around which other mesodermal cells form the vertebrae. In the most primitive chordates, which lack vertebrae, the notochord persists as a substitute for a vertebral column.

GO:0048580.name: regulation of post-embryonic development
GO:0048580.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of post-embryonic development. Post-embryonic development is defined as the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the organism over time, from the completion of embryonic development to the mature structure.

GO:0048581.name: negative regulation of post-embryonic development
GO:0048581.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of post-embryonic development. Post-embryonic development is defined as the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the organism over time, from the completion of embryonic development to the mature structure.

GO:0048582.name: positive regulation of post-embryonic development
GO:0048582.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of post-embryonic development. Post-embryonic development is defined as the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the organism over time, from the completion of embryonic development to the mature structure.

GO:0048583.name: regulation of response to stimulus
GO:0048583.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a response to a stimulus. Response to stimulus is a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus.

GO:0048584.name: positive regulation of response to stimulus
GO:0048584.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the rate of a response to a stimulus. Response to stimulus is a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus.
synonym: up regulation of response to stimulus

GO:0048585.name: negative regulation of response to stimulus
GO:0048585.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a response to a stimulus. Response to stimulus is a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus.
synonym: down regulation of response to stimulus

GO:0048588.name: developmental cell growth
GO:0048588.def: The growth of a cell, where growth contributes to the progression of the cell over time from one condition to another.
GO:0048588.synonym: developmental growth of a unicellular organism

GO:0048589.name: developmental growth
GO:0048589.def: The increase in size or mass of an entire organism, a part of an organism or a cell, where the increase in size or mass has the specific outcome of the progression of the organism over time from one condition to another.

GO:0048592.name: eye morphogenesis
GO:0048592.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the eye are generated and organized.

GO:0048593.name: camera-type eye morphogenesis
GO:0048593.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the eye are generated and organized. The camera-type eye is an organ of sight that receives light through an aperture and focuses it through a lens, projecting it on a photoreceptor field.

GO:0048596.name: embryonic camera-type eye morphogenesis
GO:0048596.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the eye are generated and organized during embryonic development.

GO:0048598.name: embryonic morphogenesis
GO:0048598.def: The process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized during the embryonic phase. The embryonic phase begins with zygote formation. The end of the embryonic phase is organism-specific. For example, it would be at birth for mammals, larval hatching for insects and seed dormancy in plants.

GO:0048599.name: oocyte development
GO:0048599.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0048601.name: oocyte morphogenesis
GO:0048601.def: The process in which the structures of an oocyte are generated and organized. This process occurs while the initially relatively unspecialized cell is acquiring the specialized features of an oocyte.

GO:0048608.name: reproductive structure development
GO:0048608.def: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of somatic structures that will be used in the process of creating new individuals from one or more parents, from their formation to the mature structures.

GO:0048609.name: multicellular organismal reproductive process
GO:0048609.def: The process, occurring above the cellular level, that is pertinent to the reproductive function of a multicellular organism. This includes the integrated processes at the level of tissues and organs.
synonym: reproductive process in a multicellular organism

GO:0048619.name: embryonic hindgut morphogenesis
GO:0048619.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the hindgut are generated and organized, during the embryonic phase.

GO:0048627.name: myoblast development
GO:0048627.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the myoblast over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

GO:0048628.name: myoblast maturation
GO:0048628.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a myoblast to attain its fully functional state. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.

GO:0048630.name: skeletal muscle tissue growth
GO:0048630.def: The increase in size or mass of a skeletal muscle. This may be due to a change in the fiber number or size.

GO:0048631.name: regulation of skeletal muscle tissue growth
GO:0048631.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle growth.

GO:0048632.name: negative regulation of skeletal muscle tissue growth
GO:0048632.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle growth.
synonym: down regulation of skeletal muscle growth

GO:0048633.name: positive regulation of skeletal muscle tissue growth
GO:0048633.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the rate of skeletal muscle growth.
synonym: up regulation of skeletal muscle growth

GO:0048634.name: regulation of muscle organ development
GO:0048634.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of muscle development.

GO:0048635.name: negative regulation of muscle organ development
GO:0048635.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of muscle development.

GO:0048636.name: positive regulation of muscle organ development
GO:0048636.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the rate of muscle development.

GO:0048638.name: regulation of developmental growth
GO:0048638.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of developmental growth.

GO:0048639.name: positive regulation of developmental growth
GO:0048639.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the rate of developmental growth.

GO:0048640.name: negative regulation of developmental growth
GO:0048640.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of developmental growth.

GO:0048641.name: regulation of skeletal muscle tissue development
GO:0048641.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle tissue development.

GO:0048642.name: negative regulation of skeletal muscle tissue development
GO:0048642.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle tissue development.
synonym: down regulation of skeletal muscle development

GO:0048643.name: positive regulation of skeletal muscle tissue development
GO:0048643.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the rate of skeletal muscle tissue development.
synonym: up regulation of skeletal muscle development

GO:0048644.name: muscle organ morphogenesis
GO:0048644.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of muscle are generated and organized.

GO:0048645.name: animal organ formation
GO:0048645.def: The process pertaining to the initial formation of an animal organ from unspecified parts. The process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the discrete structure, such as inductive events, and ends when the structural rudiment of the organ is recognizable, such as a condensation of mesenchymal cells into the organ rudiment. Organs are a natural part or structure in an animal or a plant, capable of performing some special action (termed its function), which is essential to the life or well-being of the whole. The heart and lungs are organs of animals, and the petal and leaf are organs of plants. In animals the organs are generally made up of several tissues, one of which usually predominates, and determines the principal function of the organ.
synonym: initiation of an animal organ primordium

GO:0048646.name: anatomical structure formation involved in morphogenesis
