GO:0051799.name: negative regulation of hair follicle development
GO:0051799.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of hair follicle development.
synonym: down regulation of hair follicle development

GO:0051861.name: glycolipid binding
GO:0051861.def: Binding to a glycolipid, any compound containing one or more monosaccharide residues bound by a glycosidic linkage to a hydrophobic group such as an acylglycerol, a sphingoid, a ceramide (N-acylsphingoid) or a prenyl phosphate.

GO:0051875.name: pigment granule localization
GO:0051875.def: Any process in which a pigment granule is transported to, and/or maintained in, a specific location within the cell.

GO:0051890.name: regulation of cardioblast differentiation
GO:0051890.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardioblast differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized mesodermal cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardioblast. A cardioblast is a cardiac precursor cell. It is a cell that has been committed to a cardiac fate, but will undergo more cell division rather than terminally differentiating.

GO:0051891.name: positive regulation of cardioblast differentiation
GO:0051891.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardioblast differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized mesodermal cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardioblast. A cardioblast is a cardiac precursor cell. It is a cell that has been committed to a cardiac fate, but will undergo more cell division rather than terminally differentiating.

GO:0051892.name: negative regulation of cardioblast differentiation
GO:0051892.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardioblast differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized mesodermal cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardioblast. A cardioblast is a cardiac precursor cell. It is a cell that has been committed to a cardiac fate, but will undergo more cell division rather than terminally differentiating.

GO:0051904.name: pigment granule transport
GO:0051904.def: The directed movement of pigment granules into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0051905.name: establishment of pigment granule localization
GO:0051905.def: The directed movement of a pigment granule to a specific location.

GO:0051924.name: regulation of calcium ion transport
GO:0051924.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of calcium ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0051926.name: negative regulation of calcium ion transport
GO:0051926.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of calcium ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
synonym: down regulation of calcium ion transport

GO:0051928.name: positive regulation of calcium ion transport
GO:0051928.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of calcium ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
synonym: up regulation of calcium ion transport

GO:0051930.name: regulation of sensory perception of pain
GO:0051930.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the sensory perception of pain, the series of events required for an organism to receive a painful stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal.

GO:0051931.name: regulation of sensory perception
GO:0051931.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of sensory perception, the series of events required for an organism to receive a sensory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal.

GO:0051932.name: synaptic transmission, GABAergic
GO:0051932.def: The vesicular release of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA). from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of GABA receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

GO:0051937.name: catecholamine transport
GO:0051937.def: The directed movement of catecholamines, a group of physiologically important biogenic amines that possess a catechol (3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) nucleus and are derivatives of 3,4-dihydroxyphenylethylamine.

GO:0051938.name: L-glutamate import
GO:0051938.def: The directed movement of L-glutamate, the L-enantiomer of the anion of 2-aminopentanedioic acid, into a cell or organelle.

GO:0051939.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid import
GO:0051939.def: The directed movement of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA, 4-aminobutyrate) into a cell or organelle.

GO:0051952.name: regulation of amine transport
GO:0051952.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of amines into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0051953.name: negative regulation of amine transport
GO:0051953.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of amines into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0051954.name: positive regulation of amine transport
GO:0051954.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of amines into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0051955.name: regulation of amino acid transport
GO:0051955.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of amino acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0051956.name: negative regulation of amino acid transport
GO:0051956.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of amino acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
synonym: down regulation of amino acid transport
negative regulation of amino acid transmembrane transport

GO:0051957.name: positive regulation of amino acid transport
GO:0051957.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of amino acids into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
synonym: positive regulation of amino acid transmembrane transport
up regulation of amino acid transport

GO:0051960.name: regulation of nervous system development
GO:0051960.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of nervous system development, the origin and formation of nervous tissue.

GO:0051961.name: negative regulation of nervous system development
GO:0051961.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of nervous system development, the origin and formation of nervous tissue.
synonym: down regulation of nervous system development

GO:0051962.name: positive regulation of nervous system development
GO:0051962.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of nervous system development, the origin and formation of nervous tissue.
synonym: up regulation of nervous system development

GO:0051963.name: regulation of synapse assembly
GO:0051963.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of synapse assembly, the aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a synapse.

GO:0051964.name: negative regulation of synapse assembly
GO:0051964.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of synapse assembly, the aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a synapse.

GO:0051965.name: positive regulation of synapse assembly
GO:0051965.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of synapse assembly, the aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a synapse.

GO:0051966.name: regulation of synaptic transmission, glutamatergic
GO:0051966.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glutamatergic synaptic transmission, the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glutamate.

GO:0051967.name: negative regulation of synaptic transmission, glutamatergic
GO:0051967.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of glutamatergic synaptic transmission, the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glutamate.
synonym: down regulation of synaptic transmission, glutamatergic

GO:0051968.name: positive regulation of synaptic transmission, glutamatergic
GO:0051968.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of glutamatergic synaptic transmission, the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glutamate.
synonym: up regulation of synaptic transmission, glutamatergic

GO:0051969.name: regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
GO:0051969.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of transmission of a nerve impulse, the sequential electrochemical polarization and depolarization that travels across the membrane of a neuron in response to stimulation.
GO:0051969.synonym: regulation of conduction of nerve impulse

GO:0051970.name: negative regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
GO:0051970.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of transmission of a nerve impulse, the sequential electrochemical polarization and depolarization that travels across the membrane of a neuron in response to stimulation.
synonym: down regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
down-regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
downregulation of transmission of nerve impulse
inhibition of transmission of nerve impulse
negative regulation of conduction of nerve impulse

GO:0051971.name: positive regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
GO:0051971.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of transmission of a nerve impulse, the sequential electrochemical polarization and depolarization that travels across the membrane of a neuron in response to stimulation.
synonym: activation of transmission of nerve impulse
positive regulation of conduction of nerve impulse
stimulation of transmission of nerve impulse
up regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
up-regulation of transmission of nerve impulse
upregulation of transmission of nerve impulse

GO:0051983.name: regulation of chromosome segregation
GO:0051983.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of chromosome segregation, the process in which genetic material, in the form of chromosomes, is organized and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets.

GO:0051984.name: positive regulation of chromosome segregation
GO:0051984.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of chromosome segregation, the process in which genetic material, in the form of chromosomes, is organized and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets.

GO:0051985.name: negative regulation of chromosome segregation
GO:0051985.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of chromosome segregation, the process in which genetic material, in the form of chromosomes, is organized and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets.

GO:0052803.name: imidazole-containing compound metabolic process
GO:0052803.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving imidazoles, five-membered organic heterocycle containing two nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3, or any of its derivatives; compounds containing an imidazole skeleton.

GO:0052805.name: imidazole-containing compound catabolic process
GO:0052805.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of imidazoles, five-membered organic heterocycle containing two nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3, or any of its derivatives; compounds containing an imidazole skeleton.

GO:0055001.name: muscle cell development
GO:0055001.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a muscle cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Muscle cell development does not include the steps involved in committing an unspecified cell to the muscle cell fate.

GO:0055002.name: striated muscle cell development
GO:0055002.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a striated muscle cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Striated muscle cells contain fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations, and cardiac and skeletal muscle are types of striated muscle.

GO:0055003.name: cardiac myofibril assembly
GO:0055003.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cardiac myofibril over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A cardiac myofibril is a myofibril specific to cardiac muscle cells.

GO:0055006.name: cardiac cell development
GO:0055006.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cardiac cell over time, from its formation to the mature state. A cardiac cell is a cell that will form part of the cardiac organ of an individual.

GO:0055007.name: cardiac muscle cell differentiation
GO:0055007.def: The process in which a cardiac muscle precursor cell acquires specialized features of a cardiac muscle cell. Cardiac muscle cells are striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction.

GO:0055008.name: cardiac muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0055008.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of cardiac muscle tissue are generated and organized.

GO:0055009.name: atrial cardiac muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0055009.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of cardiac atrium muscle is generated and organized.

GO:0055010.name: ventricular cardiac muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0055010.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of cardiac ventricle muscle is generated and organized.

GO:0055011.name: atrial cardiac muscle cell differentiation
GO:0055011.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a cardiac muscle cell in the atrium. Cardiac muscle cells are striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction. The atrium is the part of the heart that receives blood into the organ.

GO:0055013.name: cardiac muscle cell development
GO:0055013.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cardiac muscle cell over time, from its formation to the mature state.

GO:0055014.name: atrial cardiac muscle cell development
GO:0055014.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an atrial cardiac muscle cell over time, from its formation to the mature state. Cardiac muscle cells are striated muscle cells that are responsible for heart contraction. The atrium is the part of the heart that receives blood into the organ.

GO:0055017.name: cardiac muscle tissue growth
GO:0055017.def: The increase in size or mass of a cardiac muscle, where the increase in size or mass has the specific outcome of the progression of the organism over time from one condition to another.

GO:0055018.name: regulation of cardiac muscle fiber development
GO:0055018.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle fiber development.
synonym: regulation of cardiac muscle fibre development
regulation of heart muscle fiber development

GO:0055019.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle fiber development
GO:0055019.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle fiber development.
synonym: down regulation of cardiac muscle fiber development
down-regulation of cardiac muscle fiber development
downregulation of cardiac muscle fiber development
inhibition of cardiac muscle fiber development
negative regulation of cardiac muscle fibre development
negative regulation of heart muscle fiber development

GO:0055020.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle fiber development.
synonym: activation of cardiac muscle fiber development

positive regulation of heart muscle fiber development
stimulation of cardiac muscle fiber development

GO:0055021.name: regulation of cardiac muscle tissue growth
GO:0055021.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle growth.

GO:0055022.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle tissue growth
GO:0055022.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle growth.
synonym: down regulation of cardiac muscle growth
negative regulation of heart muscle growth

GO:0055023.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle tissue growth
GO:0055023.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle growth.
synonym: positive regulation of heart muscle growth
up regulation of cardiac muscle growth

GO:0055024.name: regulation of cardiac muscle tissue development
GO:0055024.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle tissue development.

GO:0055025.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle tissue development
GO:0055025.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle tissue development.
synonym: positive regulation of heart muscle development
up regulation of cardiac muscle development

GO:0055026.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle tissue development
GO:0055026.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle tissue development.
synonym: down regulation of cardiac muscle development
negative regulation of heart muscle development

GO:0055056.name: D-glucose transmembrane transporter activity
GO:0055056.def: Enables the transfer of the D-enantiomer of the hexose monosaccharide glucose from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0055057.name: neuroblast division
GO:0055057.def: The process resulting in the physical partitioning and separation of a neuroblast into daughter cells. A neuroblast is any cell that will divide and give rise to a neuron.

GO:0055059.name: asymmetric neuroblast division
GO:0055059.def: The process resulting in the physical partitioning and separation of a neuroblast into two daughter cells with different developmental potentials.

GO:0055062.name: phosphate ion homeostasis
GO:0055062.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of phosphate ions within an organism or cell.

GO:0055074.name: calcium ion homeostasis
GO:0055074.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of calcium ions within an organism or cell.

GO:0055075.name: potassium ion homeostasis
GO:0055075.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of potassium ions within an organism or cell.

GO:0055078.name: sodium ion homeostasis
GO:0055078.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of sodium ions within an organism or cell.

GO:0055080.name: monoatomic cation homeostasis
GO:0055080.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of monoatomic cations within an organism or cell. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are cations consisting of exactly one atom.

GO:0055082.name: intracellular chemical homeostasis
GO:0055082.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of a chemical within a cell.

GO:0055085.name: transmembrane transport
GO:0055085.def: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0055086.name: nucleobase-containing small molecule metabolic process
GO:0055086.def: The cellular chemical reactions and pathways involving a nucleobase-containing small molecule: a nucleobase, a nucleoside, or a nucleotide.
synonym: nucleobase, nucleoside and nucleotide metabolic process

GO:0055088.name: lipid homeostasis
GO:0055088.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of lipid within an organism or cell.

GO:0055089.name: fatty acid homeostasis
GO:0055089.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of fatty acid within an organism or cell.

GO:0055094.name: response to lipoprotein particle
GO:0055094.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lipoprotein particle stimulus.

GO:0055107.name: Golgi to secretory granule transport
GO:0055107.def: The directed movement of proteins from the Golgi to a secretory granule. The secretory granule is a membrane-bounded particle, usually protein, formed in the granular endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi complex.

GO:0055108.name: Golgi to transport vesicle transport
GO:0055108.def: The directed movement of proteins from the Golgi to a transport vesicle. Continuously secreted proteins are sorted into transport vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane, releasing their contents by exocytosis.

GO:0055111.name: ingression involved in gastrulation with mouth forming second
GO:0055111.def: The migration of individual cells into the embryo involved in deuterostomic gastrulation.

GO:0055117.name: regulation of cardiac muscle contraction
GO:0055117.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction.

GO:0055118.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle contraction
GO:0055118.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction.

GO:0055123.name: digestive system development
GO:0055123.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the digestive system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The digestive system is the entire structure in which digestion takes place. Digestion is all of the physical, chemical, and biochemical processes carried out by multicellular organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

GO:0055127.name: vibrational conductance of sound to the inner ear
GO:0055127.def: The transmission of vibrations via ossicles to the inner ear.

GO:0060004.name: reflex
GO:0060004.def: An automatic response to a stimulus beginning with a nerve impulse from a receptor and ending with the action of an effector such as a gland or a muscle. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

GO:0060005.name: vestibular reflex
GO:0060005.def: A reflex process in which a response to an angular or linear acceleration stimulus begins with an afferent nerve impulse from a receptor in the inner ear and ends with the compensatory action of eye muscles. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

GO:0060007.name: linear vestibuloocular reflex
GO:0060007.def: A vestibular reflex by which a response to a linear acceleration stimulus begins with an afferent nerve impulse from a receptor in the otolith and ends with the compensatory action of eye muscles. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

GO:0060008.name: Sertoli cell differentiation
GO:0060008.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a Sertoli cell. A Sertoli cell is a supporting cell projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules.

GO:0060009.name: Sertoli cell development
GO:0060009.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a Sertoli cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a Sertoli cell fate.

GO:0060011.name: Sertoli cell proliferation
GO:0060011.def: The multiplication or reproduction of Sertoli cells, resulting in the expansion of the Sertoli cell population. A Sertoli cell is a supporting cell projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules.

GO:0060012.name: synaptic transmission, glycinergic
GO:0060012.def: The vesicular release of glycine from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of glycine receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

GO:0060014.name: granulosa cell differentiation
GO:0060014.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a granulosa cell, a supporting cell for the developing female gamete in the ovary of mammals.

GO:0060016.name: granulosa cell development
GO:0060016.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a granulosa cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a granulosa cell fate.

GO:0060017.name: parathyroid gland development
GO:0060017.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the parathyroid gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The parathyroid gland is an organ specialised for secretion of parathyroid hormone.

GO:0060019.name: radial glial cell differentiation
GO:0060019.def: The process in which neuroepithelial cells of the neural tube give rise to radial glial cells, specialized bipotential progenitors cells of the brain. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060020.name: Bergmann glial cell differentiation
GO:0060020.def: The process in which neuroepithelial cells of the neural tube give rise to Brgmann glial cells, specialized bipotential progenitors cells of the cerebellum. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060021.name: roof of mouth development
GO:0060021.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of the roof of the mouth from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the structure and ends with the mature structure. The roof of the mouth is the partition that separates the nasal and oral cavities.

GO:0060034.name: notochord cell differentiation
GO:0060034.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features cells that make up the notochord. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a notochord cell fate.

GO:0060037.name: pharyngeal system development
GO:0060037.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pharyngeal system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pharyngeal system is a transient embryonic complex that is specific to vertebrates. It comprises the pharyngeal arches, bulges of tissues of mesoderm and neural crest derivation through which pass nerves and pharyngeal arch arteries. The arches are separated internally by pharyngeal pouches, evaginations of foregut endoderm, and externally by pharyngeal clefts, invaginations of surface ectoderm. The development of the system ends when the structure it contributes to are forming: the thymus, thyroid, parathyroids, maxilla, mandible, aortic arch, cardiac outflow tract, external and middle ear.

GO:0060038.name: cardiac muscle cell proliferation
GO:0060038.def: The expansion of a cardiac muscle cell population by cell division.

GO:0060039.name: pericardium development
GO:0060039.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the pericardium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The pericardium is a double-walled sac that contains the heart and the roots of the aorta, vena cava and the pulmonary artery.

GO:0060040.name: retinal bipolar neuron differentiation
GO:0060040.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a bipolar cell, the last neuron to be generated in the retina.

GO:0060041.name: retina development in camera-type eye
GO:0060041.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the retina over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The retina is the innermost layer or coating at the back of the eyeball, which is sensitive to light and in which the optic nerve terminates.

GO:0060042.name: retina morphogenesis in camera-type eye
GO:0060042.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of the retina is generated and organized.

GO:0060043.name: regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation
GO:0060043.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell proliferation.
synonym: regulation of heart muscle cell proliferation

GO:0060044.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation
GO:0060044.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell proliferation.
GO:0060044.synonym: negative regulation of heart muscle cell proliferation

GO:0060045.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle cell proliferation
GO:0060045.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell proliferation.
GO:0060045.synonym: positive regulation of heart muscle cell proliferation

GO:0060047.name: heart contraction
GO:0060047.def: The multicellular organismal process in which the heart decreases in volume in a characteristic way to propel blood through the body.

GO:0060048.name: cardiac muscle contraction
GO:0060048.def: Muscle contraction of cardiac muscle tissue.

GO:0060054.name: positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation involved in wound healing
GO:0060054.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of epithelial cell proliferation, contributing to the restoration of integrity to a damaged tissue following an injury.

GO:0060055.name: angiogenesis involved in wound healing
GO:0060055.def: Blood vessel formation when new vessels emerge from the proliferation of pre-existing blood vessels and contribute to the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

GO:0060065.name: uterus development
GO:0060065.def: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the uterus over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060066.name: oviduct development
GO:0060066.def: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oviduct over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An oviduct is a tube through which an ova passes from the ovary to the uterus, or from the ovary to the outside of the organism.

GO:0060067.name: cervix development
GO:0060067.def: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cervix over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060068.name: vagina development
GO:0060068.def: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vagina over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060073.name: micturition
GO:0060073.def: The regulation of body fluids process in which parasympathetic nerves stimulate the bladder wall muscle to contract and expel urine from the body.

GO:0060076.name: excitatory synapse
GO:0060076.def: A synapse in which an action potential in the presynaptic cell increases the probability of an action potential occurring in the postsynaptic cell.

GO:0060078.name: regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential
GO:0060078.def: Any process that modulates the potential difference across a post-synaptic membrane.

GO:0060079.name: excitatory postsynaptic potential
GO:0060079.def: A process that leads to a temporary increase in postsynaptic potential due to the flow of positively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an EPSP is an excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) and makes it easier for the neuron to fire an action potential.
synonym: regulation of excitatory post-synaptic membrane potential

GO:0060082.name: eye blink reflex
GO:0060082.def: The reflex process in which a mechanical stimulus applied to the eye elicits a response of the eyelid closing.

GO:0060083.name: smooth muscle contraction involved in micturition
GO:0060083.def: The process leading to shortening and/or development of tension in the urinary bladder smooth muscle tissue involved in the expulsion urine from the body.
synonym: smooth muscle contraction involved in urination
urinary bladder smooth muscle contraction involved in micturition

GO:0060084.name: synaptic transmission involved in micturition
GO:0060084.def: The process of communication from a neuron to a smooth muscle in the bladder that contributes to the expulsion of urine from the body.

GO:0060089.name: molecular transducer activity
GO:0060089.def: A compound molecular function in which an effector function is controlled by one or more regulatory components.

GO:0060090.name: molecular adaptor activity
GO:0060090.def: The binding activity of a molecule that brings together two or more molecules through a selective, non-covalent, often stoichiometric interaction, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way.

GO:0060092.name: regulation of synaptic transmission, glycinergic
GO:0060092.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glycinergic synaptic transmission. Glycinergic synaptic transmission is the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glycine.

GO:0060093.name: negative regulation of synaptic transmission, glycinergic
GO:0060093.def: Any process that stops or decreases the frequency, rate or extent of glycinergic synaptic transmission. Glycinergic synaptic transmission is the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glycine.
GO:0060093.synonym: negative regulation of glycinergic synaptic transmission

GO:0060094.name: positive regulation of synaptic transmission, glycinergic
GO:0060094.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of glycinergic synaptic transmission. Glycinergic synaptic transmission is the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter glycine.
GO:0060094.synonym: positive regulation of glycinergic synaptic transmission

GO:0060096.name: serotonin secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0060096.def: The regulated release of serotonin by a cell, in which released serotonin acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0060113.name: inner ear receptor cell differentiation
GO:0060113.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells, acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of inner ear receptor cells. Inner ear receptor cells are mechanorecptors found in the inner ear responsible for transducing signals involved in balance and sensory perception of sound.

GO:0060114.name: vestibular receptor cell differentiation
GO:0060114.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a vestibular hair cell.

GO:0060116.name: vestibular receptor cell morphogenesis
GO:0060116.def: Any process that alters the size or shape of a vestibular receptor cell.

GO:0060117.name: auditory receptor cell development
GO:0060117.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an auditory receptor cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060118.name: vestibular receptor cell development
GO:0060118.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a vestibular receptor cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060119.name: inner ear receptor cell development
GO:0060119.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an inner ear receptor cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060123.name: regulation of growth hormone secretion
GO:0060123.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of growth hormone from a cell.

GO:0060124.name: positive regulation of growth hormone secretion
GO:0060124.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of growth hormone from a cell.

GO:0060125.name: negative regulation of growth hormone secretion
GO:0060125.def: Any process that decreases or stops the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of growth hormone from a cell.

GO:0060126.name: somatotropin secreting cell differentiation
GO:0060126.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a somatotropin secreting cell. A somatotropin secreting cell is an acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces growth hormone, somatotropin.

GO:0060127.name: prolactin secreting cell differentiation
GO:0060127.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a prolactin secreting cell. A prolactin secreting cell is an acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces prolactin.

GO:0060128.name: corticotropin hormone secreting cell differentiation
GO:0060128.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a corticotropic hormone secreting cell. An corticotropic hormone secreting cell is a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces corticotropin.

GO:0060129.name: thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell differentiation
GO:0060129.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell. A thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell is a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces thyroid-stimulating hormone, thyrotrophin.
synonym: thyroid stimulating hormone secreting cell differentiation

GO:0060130.name: thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell development
GO:0060130.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting cell is a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces thyroid stimulating hormone, thyrotrophin.
synonym: thyroid stimulating hormone secreting cell development

GO:0060131.name: corticotropin hormone secreting cell development
GO:0060131.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a corticotropic hormone secreting cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An corticotropic hormone secreting cell is a basophil cell of the anterior pituitary that produces corticotropin.

GO:0060132.name: prolactin secreting cell development
GO:0060132.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a prolactin secreting cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A prolactin secreting cell is an acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces prolactin.

GO:0060133.name: somatotropin secreting cell development
GO:0060133.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a somatotropin secreting cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A somatotropin secreting cell is an acidophilic cell of the anterior pituitary that produces growth hormone, somatotropin.

GO:0060135.name: maternal process involved in female pregnancy
GO:0060135.def: A reproductive process occurring in the mother that allows an embryo or fetus to develop within it.

GO:0060136.name: embryonic process involved in female pregnancy
GO:0060136.def: A reproductive process occurring in the embryo or fetus that allows the embryo or fetus to develop within the mother.

GO:0060142.name: regulation of syncytium formation by plasma membrane fusion
GO:0060142.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of a syncytium, a mass of cytoplasm containing several nuclei enclosed within a single plasma membrane, by the fusion of the plasma membranes of two or more individual cells.

GO:0060143.name: positive regulation of syncytium formation by plasma membrane fusion
GO:0060143.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the formation of a syncytium, a mass of cytoplasm containing several nuclei enclosed within a single plasma membrane, by the fusion of the plasma membranes of two or more individual cells.

GO:0060156.name: milk ejection reflex
GO:0060156.def: A reflex that occurs in response to suckling, beginning with a nerve impulse from a receptor in the mammary gland and ending with the ejection of milk from the gland. Signaling never reaches a level of consciousness.

GO:0060157.name: urinary bladder development
GO:0060157.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the urinary bladder over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The urinary bladder is an elastic, muscular sac situated in the anterior part of the pelvic cavity in which urine collects before excretion.

GO:0060166.name: olfactory pit development
GO:0060166.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of the olfactory pit from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the olfactory pit, which is an indentation of the olfactory placode, and ends when the pits hollows out to form the nasopharynx.

GO:0060170.name: ciliary membrane
GO:0060170.def: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding a cilium.

GO:0060173.name: limb development
GO:0060173.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a limb over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A limb is an appendage of an animal used for locomotion or grasping. Examples include legs, arms or some types of fin.

GO:0060174.name: limb bud formation
GO:0060174.def: The process pertaining to the initial formation of a limb bud from unspecified parts. This process begins with the formation of a local condensation of mesenchyme cells within the prospective limb field, and ends when a limb bud is recognizable.

GO:0060214.name: endocardium formation
GO:0060214.def: Formation of the endocardium of the heart. The endocardium is an anatomical structure comprised of an endothelium and an extracellular matrix that forms the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.

GO:0060215.name: primitive hemopoiesis
GO:0060215.def: A first transient wave of blood cell production that, in vertebrates, gives rise to erythrocytes (red blood cells) and myeloid cells.

GO:0060217.name: hemangioblast cell differentiation
GO:0060217.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the characteristics of a mature hemangioblast. Hemangioblasts are the proposed common precursor of blood and endothelial lineages.

GO:0060218.name: hematopoietic stem cell differentiation
GO:0060218.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a hematopoietic stem cell. A stem cell is a cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

GO:0060219.name: camera-type eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
GO:0060219.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a photoreceptor cell in a camera-type eye.

GO:0060221.name: retinal rod cell differentiation
GO:0060221.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a retinal rod cell.

GO:0060231.name: mesenchymal to epithelial transition
GO:0060231.def: A transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity, forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell.
synonym: epithelial cell differentiation from mesenchymal cell

GO:0060249.name: anatomical structure homeostasis
GO:0060249.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state within a defined anatomical structure of an organism, including control of cellular proliferation and death and control of metabolic function. An anatomical structure is any biological entity that occupies space and is distinguished from its surroundings. Anatomical structures can be macroscopic such as a carpel, or microscopic such as an acrosome.

GO:0060251.name: regulation of glial cell proliferation
GO:0060251.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glial cell proliferation.

GO:0060252.name: positive regulation of glial cell proliferation
GO:0060252.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of glial cell proliferation.

GO:0060253.name: negative regulation of glial cell proliferation
GO:0060253.def: Any process that stops or decreases the rate or extent of glial cell proliferation.

GO:0060255.name: regulation of macromolecule metabolic process
GO:0060255.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving macromolecules, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

GO:0060263.name: regulation of respiratory burst
GO:0060263.def: Any process that modulates the rate frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

GO:0060264.name: regulation of respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
GO:0060264.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases made as a defense response ; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.
GO:0060264.synonym: regulation of respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0060265.name: positive regulation of respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
GO:0060265.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases made as a defense response ; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.
GO:0060265.synonym: positive regulation of respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0060266.name: negative regulation of respiratory burst involved in inflammatory response
GO:0060266.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases made as a defense response ; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.
GO:0060266.synonym: negative regulation of respiratory burst involved in acute inflammatory response

GO:0060267.name: positive regulation of respiratory burst
GO:0060267.def: Any process that increases the rate frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

GO:0060268.name: negative regulation of respiratory burst
GO:0060268.def: Any process that decreases the rate frequency or extent of a phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases; this leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals.

GO:0060269.name: centripetally migrating follicle cell migration
GO:0060269.def: The cell migration process in which a follicle cell migrates as part of an epithelial sheet between the nurse cells and the oocyte. At the end of migration, they cover the anterior of the oocyte.

GO:0060271.name: cilium assembly
GO:0060271.def: The assembly of a cilium, a specialized eukaryotic organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface. Each cilium is bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored basally in a centriole.

GO:0060281.name: regulation of oocyte development
GO:0060281.def: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of the process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0060282.name: positive regulation of oocyte development
GO:0060282.def: Any process that increases the rate or extent of the process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0060283.name: negative regulation of oocyte development
GO:0060283.def: Any process that decreases the rate or extent of the process whose specific outcome is the progression of an oocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0060284.name: regulation of cell development
GO:0060284.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the progression of the cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060285.name: cilium-dependent cell motility
GO:0060285.def: Cell motility due to the motion of one or more eukaryotic cilia. A eukaryotic cilium is a specialized organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface. Each cilium is bounded by an extrusion of the cytoplasmic (plasma) membrane, and contains a regular longitudinal array of microtubules, anchored basally in a centriole.

GO:0060294.name: cilium movement involved in cell motility
GO:0060294.def: Movement of cilia mediated by motor proteins that contributes to the movement of a cell.

GO:0060295.name: regulation of cilium movement involved in cell motility
GO:0060295.def: Any process that modulates the rate frequency or extent of cilium movement involved in ciliary motility.

GO:0060297.name: regulation of sarcomere organization
GO:0060297.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of myofibril assembly by organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres. The sarcomere is the repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

GO:0060298.name: positive regulation of sarcomere organization
GO:0060298.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of myofibril assembly by organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres. The sarcomere is the repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

GO:0060299.name: negative regulation of sarcomere organization
GO:0060299.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of myofibril assembly by organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres. The sarcomere is the repeating unit of a myofibril in a muscle cell, composed of an array of overlapping thick and thin filaments between two adjacent Z discs.

GO:0060312.name: regulation of blood vessel remodeling
GO:0060312.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of blood vessel remodeling, the reorganization or renovation of existing blood vessels.

GO:0060313.name: negative regulation of blood vessel remodeling
GO:0060313.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of blood vessel remodeling, the reorganization or renovation of existing blood vessels.
synonym: negative regulation of blood vessel remodelling

GO:0060319.name: primitive erythrocyte differentiation
GO:0060319.def: Erythrocyte differentiation which occurs as part of the process of primitive hemopoiesis.

GO:0060322.name: head development
GO:0060322.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a head from an initial condition to its mature state. The head is the anterior-most division of the body.

GO:0060323.name: head morphogenesis
GO:0060323.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the head are generated and organized. The head is the anterior-most division of the body.

GO:0060324.name: face development
GO:0060324.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a face from an initial condition to its mature state. The face is the ventral division of the head.

GO:0060325.name: face morphogenesis
GO:0060325.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the face are generated and organized. The face is the ventral division of the head.

GO:0060326.name: cell chemotaxis
GO:0060326.def: The directed movement of a motile cell guided by a specific chemical concentration gradient. Movement may be towards a higher concentration (positive chemotaxis) or towards a lower concentration (negative chemotaxis).

GO:0060327.name: cytoplasmic actin-based contraction involved in cell motility
GO:0060327.def: The actin filament-based movement by which cytoplasmic actin filaments slide past one another resulting in a contraction that propels the cell from one place to another.

GO:0060341.name: regulation of cellular localization
GO:0060341.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a process in which a cell, a substance, or a cellular entity is transported to, or maintained in a specific location within or in the membrane of a cell.

GO:0060343.name: trabecula formation
GO:0060343.def: The process of creating a trabecula in an organ. A trabecula is a small, often microscopic, tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod, which generally has a mechanical function. Trabecula are usually but not necessarily, composed of dense collagenous tissue.

GO:0060344.name: liver trabecula formation
GO:0060344.def: The process of creating a trabecula in the liver. A trabecula is a tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod.

GO:0060345.name: spleen trabecula formation
GO:0060345.def: The process of creating a trabecula in the spleen. A trabecula is a tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod.

GO:0060347.name: heart trabecula formation
GO:0060347.def: The process of creating a trabecula in the heart. A trabecula is a tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod.

GO:0060348.name: bone development
GO:0060348.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of bone over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Bone is the hard skeletal connective tissue consisting of both mineral and cellular components.

GO:0060349.name: bone morphogenesis
GO:0060349.def: The process in which bones are generated and organized.

GO:0060350.name: endochondral bone morphogenesis
GO:0060350.def: The process in which bones are generated and organized as a result of the conversion of initial cartilaginous anlage into bone.

GO:0060351.name: cartilage development involved in endochondral bone morphogenesis
GO:0060351.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cartilage that will provide a scaffold for mineralization of endochondral bones.

GO:0060359.name: response to ammonium ion
GO:0060359.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an ammonium stimulus.

GO:0060363.name: cranial suture morphogenesis
GO:0060363.def: The process in which any suture between cranial bones is generated and organized.

GO:0060364.name: frontal suture morphogenesis
GO:0060364.def: The process in which the frontal suture is generated and organized.

GO:0060374.name: mast cell differentiation
GO:0060374.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a mast cell. A mast cell is a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.

GO:0060375.name: regulation of mast cell differentiation
GO:0060375.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a mast cell. A mast cell is a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.

GO:0060376.name: positive regulation of mast cell differentiation
GO:0060376.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a mast cell. A mast cell is a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.

GO:0060377.name: negative regulation of mast cell differentiation
GO:0060377.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized myeloid precursor cell acquires the specialized features of a mast cell. A mast cell is a cell that is found in almost all tissues containing numerous basophilic granules and capable of releasing large amounts of histamine and heparin upon activation.

GO:0060379.name: cardiac muscle cell myoblast differentiation
GO:0060379.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a cardiac myoblast. A cardiac myoblast is a precursor cell that has been committed to a cardiac muscle cell fate but retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life.

GO:0060404.name: axonemal microtubule depolymerization
GO:0060404.def: The removal of tubulin heterodimers from one or both ends of an axonemal microtubule. An axonemal microtubule is a microtubule in the axoneme of a cilium or flagellum; an axoneme contains nine modified doublet microtubules surrounding a pair of single microtubules.

GO:0060408.name: regulation of acetylcholine metabolic process
GO:0060408.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving acetylcholine, the acetic acid ester of the organic base choline. Acetylcholine is a major neurotransmitter and neuromodulator both in the central and peripheral nervous systems. It also acts as a paracrine signal in various non-neural tissues.

GO:0060409.name: positive regulation of acetylcholine metabolic process
GO:0060409.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving acetylcholine, the acetic acid ester of the organic base choline. Acetylcholine is a major neurotransmitter and neuromodulator both in the central and peripheral nervous systems. It also acts as a paracrine signal in various non-neural tissues.

GO:0060410.name: negative regulation of acetylcholine metabolic process
GO:0060410.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving acetylcholine, the acetic acid ester of the organic base choline. Acetylcholine is a major neurotransmitter and neuromodulator both in the central and peripheral nervous systems. It also acts as a paracrine signal in various non-neural tissues.

GO:0060411.name: cardiac septum morphogenesis
GO:0060411.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of a cardiac septum is generated and organized. A cardiac septum is a partition that separates parts of the heart.

GO:0060412.name: ventricular septum morphogenesis
GO:0060412.def: The developmental process in which a ventricular septum is generated and organized. A ventricular septum is an anatomical structure that separates the lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart from one another.

GO:0060413.name: atrial septum morphogenesis
GO:0060413.def: The developmental process in which atrial septum is generated and organized. The atrial septum separates the upper chambers (the atria) of the heart from one another.

GO:0060414.name: aorta smooth muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0060414.def: The process in which the structure of the smooth muscle tissue surrounding the aorta is generated and organized. An aorta is an artery that carries blood from the heart to other parts of the body.

GO:0060415.name: muscle tissue morphogenesis
GO:0060415.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of muscle tissue are generated and organized. Muscle tissue consists of a set of cells that are part of an organ and carry out a contractive function.

GO:0060419.name: heart growth
GO:0060419.def: The increase in size or mass of the heart.

GO:0060420.name: regulation of heart growth
GO:0060420.def: Any process that modulates the rate or extent of heart growth. Heart growth is the increase in size or mass of the heart.

GO:0060421.name: positive regulation of heart growth
GO:0060421.def: Any process that increases the rate or extent of heart growth. Heart growth is the increase in size or mass of the heart.

GO:0060425.name: lung morphogenesis
GO:0060425.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the lung are generated and organized.

GO:0060426.name: lung vasculature development
GO:0060426.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lung vasculature from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the lung vasculature and ends with the mature structure. The lung vasculature is composed of the tubule structures that carry blood or lymph in the lungs.

GO:0060427.name: lung connective tissue development
GO:0060427.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of lung connective tissue from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of lung connective tissue and ends with the mature structure. The lung connective tissue is a material made up of fibers forming a framework and support structure for the lungs.

GO:0060428.name: lung epithelium development
GO:0060428.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lung epithelium from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of lung epithelium and ends with the mature structure. The lung epithelium is the specialized epithelium that lines the inside of the lung.

GO:0060429.name: epithelium development
GO:0060429.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an epithelium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An epithelium is a tissue that covers the internal or external surfaces of an anatomical structure.

GO:0060431.name: primary lung bud formation
GO:0060431.def: The morphogenetic process in which the foregut region specified to become the lung forms the initial left and right buds.

GO:0060433.name: bronchus development
GO:0060433.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a bronchus from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the bronchus and ends with the mature structure. The bronchus is the portion of the airway that connects to the lungs.

GO:0060434.name: bronchus morphogenesis
GO:0060434.def: The process in which the bronchus is generated and organized. The bronchus is the portion of the airway that connects to the lungs.

GO:0060435.name: bronchiole development
GO:0060435.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a bronchiole from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the bronchiole and ends with the mature structure. A bronchiole is the first airway branch that no longer contains cartilage; it is a branch of the bronchi.

GO:0060436.name: bronchiole morphogenesis
GO:0060436.def: The process in which a bronchiole is generated and organized. A bronchiole is the first airway branch that no longer contains cartilage; it is a branch of the bronchi.

GO:0060437.name: lung growth
GO:0060437.def: The increase in size or mass of a lung. In all air-breathing vertebrates the lungs are developed from the ventral wall of the oesophagus as a pouch which divides into two sacs. In amphibians and many reptiles the lungs retain very nearly this primitive sac-like character, but in the higher forms the connection with the esophagus becomes elongated into the windpipe and the inner walls of the sacs become more and more divided, until, in the mammals, the air spaces become minutely divided into tubes ending in small air cells, in the walls of which the blood circulates in a fine network of capillaries. In mammals the lungs are more or less divided into lobes, and each lung occupies a separate cavity in the thorax.

GO:0060438.name: trachea development
GO:0060438.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a trachea over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The trachea is the portion of the airway that attaches to the bronchi as it branches.

GO:0060439.name: trachea morphogenesis
GO:0060439.def: The process in which a trachea is generated and organized. The trachea is the portion of the airway that attaches to the bronchi as it branches.

GO:0060440.name: trachea formation
GO:0060440.def: The process pertaining to the initial formation of a trachea from unspecified parts. The process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the discrete structure and ends when the trachea is recognizable. The trachea is the portion of the airway that attaches to the bronchi as it branches.

GO:0060441.name: epithelial tube branching involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0060441.def: The process in which a highly ordered sequence of patterning events generates the branched epithelial tubes of the lung, consisting of reiterated combinations of bud outgrowth, elongation, and dichotomous subdivision of terminal units.

GO:0060442.name: branching involved in prostate gland morphogenesis
GO:0060442.def: The process in which the branching structure of the prostate gland is generated and organized. A branch is a division or offshoot from a main stem.

GO:0060443.name: mammary gland morphogenesis
GO:0060443.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the mammary gland are generated and organized. Morphogenesis refers to the creation of shape. The mammary gland is a large compound sebaceous gland that in female mammals is modified to secrete milk.

GO:0060444.name: branching involved in mammary gland duct morphogenesis
GO:0060444.def: The process in which the branching structure of the mammary gland duct is generated and organized. The mammary gland is a large compound sebaceous gland that in female mammals is modified to secrete milk.

GO:0060445.name: branching involved in salivary gland morphogenesis
GO:0060445.def: The process in which the branching structure of the salivary gland is generated and organized.

GO:0060446.name: branching involved in open tracheal system development
GO:0060446.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of branches in the open tracheal system are generated and organized.

GO:0060450.name: positive regulation of hindgut contraction
GO:0060450.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of muscle contraction of the hindgut, the posterior part of the alimentary canal, including the rectum, and the large intestine.

GO:0060451.name: negative regulation of hindgut contraction
GO:0060451.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of muscle contraction of the hindgut, the posterior part of the alimentary canal, including the rectum, and the large intestine.

GO:0060452.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle contraction
GO:0060452.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle contraction.

GO:0060453.name: regulation of gastric acid secretion
GO:0060453.def: Any process that modulates the rate frequency or extent of gastric secretion. Gastric secretion is the regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

GO:0060454.name: positive regulation of gastric acid secretion
GO:0060454.def: Any process that increases the rate frequency or extent of gastric secretion. Gastric secretion is the regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

GO:0060455.name: negative regulation of gastric acid secretion
GO:0060455.def: Any process that decreases the rate frequency or extent of gastric secretion. Gastric secretion is the regulated release of gastric acid (hydrochloric acid) by parietal or oxyntic cells during digestion.

GO:0060456.name: positive regulation of digestive system process
GO:0060456.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of a digestive system process, a physical, chemical, or biochemical process carried out by living organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

GO:0060457.name: negative regulation of digestive system process
GO:0060457.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of a digestive system process, a physical, chemical, or biochemical process carried out by living organisms to break down ingested nutrients into components that may be easily absorbed and directed into metabolism.

GO:0060458.name: right lung development
GO:0060458.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a right lung from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the right lung and ends with the mature structure. The right lung is the lung which is on the right side of the anterior posterior axis looking from a dorsal to ventral aspect.

GO:0060459.name: left lung development
GO:0060459.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a left lung from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the left lung and ends with the mature structure. The left lung is the lung which is on the left side of the anterior posterior axis looking from a dorsal to ventral aspect.

GO:0060460.name: left lung morphogenesis
GO:0060460.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the left lung are generated and organized.

GO:0060461.name: right lung morphogenesis
GO:0060461.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the right lung are generated and organized.

GO:0060462.name: lung lobe development
GO:0060462.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lung lobe from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of a lung lobe by branching morphogenesis and ends with the mature structure. A lung lobe is one of the rounded projections that compose the lung.

GO:0060463.name: lung lobe morphogenesis
GO:0060463.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a lung lobe are generated and organized. A lung lobe is a projection that extends from the lung.

GO:0060464.name: lung lobe formation
GO:0060464.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a lung lobe from unspecified parts. This process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the lobe and ends when the structural rudiment is recognizable. A lung lobe is a projection that extends from the lung.

GO:0060465.name: pharynx development
GO:0060465.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pharynx from an initial condition to its mature state. The pharynx is the part of the digestive system immediately posterior to the mouth.

GO:0060467.name: negative regulation of fertilization
GO:0060467.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of fertilization. Fertilization is the union of gametes of opposite sexes during the process of sexual reproduction to form a zygote. It involves the fusion of the gametic nuclei (karyogamy) and cytoplasm (plasmogamy).

GO:0060468.name: prevention of polyspermy
GO:0060468.def: The negative regulation of fertilization process that takes place as part of egg activation, ensuring that only a single sperm fertilizes the egg.
synonym: negative regulation of fertilization involved in egg activation

GO:0060474.name: positive regulation of flagellated sperm motility involved in capacitation
GO:0060474.def: The process in which the controlled movement of a flagellated sperm cell is initiated as part of the process required for flagellated sperm to reach fertilization competence.
GO:0060474.synonym: positive regulation of sperm motility involved in capacitation

GO:0060479.name: lung cell differentiation
GO:0060479.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells, e.g. embryonic or regenerative cells, acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of a mature cell found in the lung. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060480.name: lung goblet cell differentiation
GO:0060480.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a lung goblet cell. A goblet cell is a cell of the epithelial lining that produces and secretes mucins.

GO:0060481.name: lobar bronchus epithelium development
GO:0060481.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lobar bronchus epithelium from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the lobar bronchus epithelium and ends with the mature structure. The lobar bronchus epithelium is the tissue made up of epithelial cells that lines the inside of the lobar bronchus.

GO:0060482.name: lobar bronchus development
GO:0060482.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lobar bronchus from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the lobar bronchus and ends with the mature structure. The lobar bronchus is the major airway within the respiratory tree that starts by division of the principal bronchi on both sides and ends at the point of its own subdivision into tertiary or segmental bronchi.

GO:0060483.name: lobar bronchus mesenchyme development
GO:0060483.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lobar bronchus mesenchyme from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the lobar bronchus mesenchyme and ends with the mature structure. The lobar bronchus mesenchyme is the mass of tissue composed of mesenchymal cells in the lobar bronchus.

GO:0060484.name: lung-associated mesenchyme development
GO:0060484.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lung-associated mesenchyme from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of lung-associated mesenchyme and ends with the mature structure. Lung-associated mesenchyme is the tissue made up of loosely connected mesenchymal cells in the lung.

GO:0060485.name: mesenchyme development
GO:0060485.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a mesenchymal tissue over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A mesenchymal tissue is made up of loosely packed stellate cells.

GO:0060486.name: club cell differentiation
GO:0060486.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a club cell. A club cell is an unciliated epithelial cell found in the respiratory and terminal bronchioles.

GO:0060487.name: lung epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0060487.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an epithelial cell that contributes to the epithelium of the lung.

GO:0060490.name: lateral sprouting involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0060490.def: The process in which a branch forms along the side of the lung epithelial tube.

GO:0060491.name: regulation of cell projection assembly
GO:0060491.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of cell projection assembly.

GO:0060495.name: cell-cell signaling involved in lung development
GO:0060495.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another and contributes to the progression of the lung, from its initial state to the mature structure.
GO:0060495.synonym: cell-cell signalling involved in lung development

GO:0060496.name: mesenchymal-epithelial cell signaling involved in lung development
GO:0060496.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from a mesenchymal cell to an epithelial cell and contributes to the development of the lung.
GO:0060496.synonym: mesenchymal-epithelial cell signalling involved in lung development

GO:0060497.name: mesenchymal-endodermal cell signaling
GO:0060497.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information between a mesenchymal cell and an endodermal cell.

GO:0060501.name: positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0060501.def: Any process that increases the rate or frequency of epithelial cell proliferation that results in the lung attaining its shape.

GO:0060502.name: epithelial cell proliferation involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0060502.def: The multiplication or reproduction of epithelial cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population that contributes to the shaping of the lung.

GO:0060509.name: type I pneumocyte differentiation
GO:0060509.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a type I pneumocyte. A type I pneumocyte is a flattened cell with greatly attenuated cytoplasm and a paucity of organelles.
