GO:0060510.name: type II pneumocyte differentiation
GO:0060510.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a type II pneumocyte. A type II pneumocyte is a surfactant secreting cell that contains abundant cytoplasm containing numerous lipid-rich multilamellar bodies.

GO:0060512.name: prostate gland morphogenesis
GO:0060512.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a prostate gland are generated and organized.

GO:0060513.name: prostatic bud formation
GO:0060513.def: The morphogenetic process in which a region of the fetal urogenital sinus epithelium is specified to become the prostate, resulting in prostate bud outgrowth.

GO:0060525.name: prostate glandular acinus development
GO:0060525.def: The progression of a glandular acinus of the prostate gland over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The glandular acini are the saclike structures of the gland.

GO:0060526.name: prostate glandular acinus morphogenesis
GO:0060526.def: The process in which the prostate glandular acini are generated and organized. The glandular acini are the saclike structures of the gland.

GO:0060530.name: smooth muscle cell differentiation involved in prostate glandular acinus development
GO:0060530.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a smooth muscle cell of the prostate glandular acinus.

GO:0060531.name: neuroendocrine cell differentiation involved in prostate gland acinus development
GO:0060531.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquires specialized structural and functions of a neuroendocrine cell of the prostate gland acinus.

GO:0060532.name: bronchus cartilage development
GO:0060532.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of lung cartilage over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cartilage is a connective tissue dominated by extracellular matrix containing collagen type II and large amounts of proteoglycan, particularly chondroitin sulfate.

GO:0060533.name: bronchus cartilage morphogenesis
GO:0060533.def: The process in which the bronchus cartilage is generated and organized. The bronchus cartilage is the connective tissue of the portion of the airway that connects to the lungs.

GO:0060534.name: trachea cartilage development
GO:0060534.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the tracheal cartilage over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cartilage is a connective tissue dominated by extracellular matrix containing collagen type II and large amounts of proteoglycan, particularly chondroitin sulfate.

GO:0060535.name: trachea cartilage morphogenesis
GO:0060535.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of cartilage in the trachea are generated and organized.

GO:0060536.name: cartilage morphogenesis
GO:0060536.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of cartilage are generated and organized.

GO:0060537.name: muscle tissue development
GO:0060537.def: The progression of muscle tissue over time, from its initial formation to its mature state. Muscle tissue is a contractile tissue made up of actin and myosin fibers.

GO:0060538.name: skeletal muscle organ development
GO:0060538.def: The progression of a skeletal muscle organ over time from its initial formation to its mature state. A skeletal muscle organ includes the skeletal muscle tissue and its associated connective tissue.

GO:0060539.name: diaphragm development
GO:0060539.def: The progression of the diaphragm over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The diaphragm is a skeletal muscle that is responsible for contraction and expansion of the lungs.

GO:0060540.name: diaphragm morphogenesis
GO:0060540.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the diaphragm are generated and organized.

GO:0060541.name: respiratory system development
GO:0060541.def: The progression of the respiratory system over time from its formation to its mature structure. The respiratory system carries out respiratory gaseous exchange.

GO:0060560.name: developmental growth involved in morphogenesis
GO:0060560.def: The increase in size or mass of an anatomical structure that contributes to the structure attaining its shape.

GO:0060561.name: apoptotic process involved in morphogenesis
GO:0060561.def: Any apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of an anatomical structure.

GO:0060562.name: epithelial tube morphogenesis
GO:0060562.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a tube are generated and organized from an epithelium. Epithelial tubes transport gases, liquids and cells from one site to another and form the basic structure of many organs and tissues, with tube shape and organization varying from the single-celled excretory organ in Caenorhabditis elegans to the branching trees of the mammalian kidney and insect tracheal system.

GO:0060563.name: neuroepithelial cell differentiation
GO:0060563.def: The process in which epiblast cells acquire specialized features of neuroepithelial cells.

GO:0060568.name: regulation of peptide hormone processing
GO:0060568.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of peptide hormone processing. Peptide hormone processing is the generation of a mature peptide hormone by posttranslational processing of a prohormone.

GO:0060569.name: positive regulation of peptide hormone processing
GO:0060569.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of peptide hormone processing. Peptide hormone processing is the generation of a mature peptide hormone by posttranslational processing of a prohormone.

GO:0060570.name: negative regulation of peptide hormone processing
GO:0060570.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of peptide hormone processing. Peptide hormone processing is the generation of a mature peptide hormone by posttranslational processing of a prohormone.

GO:0060571.name: morphogenesis of an epithelial fold
GO:0060571.def: The morphogenetic process in which an epithelial sheet bends along a linear axis.

GO:0060572.name: morphogenesis of an epithelial bud
GO:0060572.def: The morphogenetic process in which a bud forms from an epithelial sheet. A bud is a protrusion that forms form the sheet by localized folding.

GO:0060574.name: intestinal epithelial cell maturation
GO:0060574.def: The developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a columna/cuboidal epithelial cell of the intestine to attain its fully functional state. A columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell of the intestine mature as they migrate from the intestinal crypt to the villus.

GO:0060575.name: intestinal epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0060575.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell of the intestine.

GO:0060576.name: intestinal epithelial cell development
GO:0060576.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell of the intestine over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060577.name: pulmonary vein morphogenesis
GO:0060577.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of the pulmonary venous blood vessels are generated and organized. Pulmonary veins are blood vessels that transport blood from the lungs to the heart.

GO:0060578.name: superior vena cava morphogenesis
GO:0060578.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of superior vena cava generated and organized. The superior vena cava is a blood vessel that transports blood from the upper body to the heart.

GO:0060581.name: cell fate commitment involved in pattern specification
GO:0060581.def: The commitment of cells to specific cell fates and their capacity to differentiate into particular kinds of cells within a field of cells that will exhibit a certain pattern of differentiation. Positional information is established through protein signals that emanate from a localized source within a developmental field resulting in specification of a cell type. Those signals are then interpreted in a cell-autonomous manner resulting in the determination of the cell type.

GO:0060586.name: multicellular organismal-level iron ion homeostasis
GO:0060586.def: A chemical homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of iron within extracellular body fluids, such as blood, xylem or phloem, of a multicellular organism. This is distinct from maintenance of cellular homeostasis, which occurs within a cell.

GO:0060591.name: chondroblast differentiation
GO:0060591.def: The process in which a mesenchymal cell, acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a chondroblast. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a chondroblast fate. A chondroblast is a precursor cell to chondrocytes.

GO:0060592.name: mammary gland formation
GO:0060592.def: The process pertaining to the initial formation of the mammary gland from unspecified parts. The process begins with formation of the mammary line and ends when the solid mammary bud invades the primary mammary mesenchyme.

GO:0060596.name: mammary placode formation
GO:0060596.def: The developmental process in which the mammary placode forms. The mammary placode is a transient lens shaped structure that will give rise to the mammary bud proper.

GO:0060599.name: lateral sprouting involved in mammary gland duct morphogenesis
GO:0060599.def: The process in which a branch forms along the side of a mammary duct.

GO:0060601.name: lateral sprouting from an epithelium
GO:0060601.def: The process in which a branch forms along the side of an epithelium.

GO:0060603.name: mammary gland duct morphogenesis
GO:0060603.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the mammary ducts are generated and organized. Mammary ducts are epithelial tubes that transport milk.

GO:0060610.name: mesenchymal cell differentiation involved in mammary gland development
GO:0060610.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a mammary gland mesenchymal cell. Mammary gland mesenchymal cells form a loosely connected network of cells that surround the mammary ducts.

GO:0060611.name: mammary gland fat development
GO:0060611.def: The progression of the mammary gland fat over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mammary fat is an adipose structure in the gland that is invaded by the mammary ducts.

GO:0060612.name: adipose tissue development
GO:0060612.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of adipose tissue over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Adipose tissue is specialized tissue that is used to store fat.

GO:0060615.name: mammary gland bud formation
GO:0060615.def: The morphogenetic process in which a bud forms from the mammary placode. A mammary bud is bulb of epithelial cells that is distinct from the surrounding epidermis.

GO:0060616.name: mammary gland cord formation
GO:0060616.def: The process in which the mammary gland cord forms by elongation of the mammary bud. The cord is formed once the elongating bud breaks through the mesenchyme and reaches the fat pad.

GO:0060618.name: nipple development
GO:0060618.def: The progression of the nipple over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The nipple is a part of the mammary gland that protrudes from the surface ectoderm.

GO:0060619.name: cell migration involved in mammary placode formation
GO:0060619.def: The orderly movement of epithelial cells within the mammary line that contributes to the formation of the mammary placode.

GO:0060623.name: regulation of chromosome condensation
GO:0060623.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of chromosome condensation, the progressive compaction of dispersed interphase chromatin into threadlike chromosomes prior to mitotic or meiotic nuclear division, or during apoptosis, in eukaryotic cells.

GO:0060627.name: regulation of vesicle-mediated transport
GO:0060627.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of vesicle-mediated transport, the directed movement of substances, either within a vesicle or in the vesicle membrane, into, out of or within a cell.

GO:0060632.name: regulation of microtubule-based movement
GO:0060632.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of microtubule-based movement, the movement of organelles, other microtubules and other particles along microtubules, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0060638.name: mesenchymal-epithelial cell signaling
GO:0060638.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from a mesenchymal cell to an epithelial cell where it is received and interpreted.

GO:0060642.name: white fat cell differentiation involved in mammary gland fat development
GO:0060642.def: The process in which a preadipocyte acquires specialized features of a white adipocyte of the mammary gland. White adipocytes have cytoplasmic lipids arranged in a unique vacuole.

GO:0060643.name: epithelial cell differentiation involved in mammary gland bud morphogenesis
GO:0060643.def: The process in which a cell of the mammary placode becomes a cell of the mammary gland bud.

GO:0060644.name: mammary gland epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0060644.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized epithelial cell becomes a more specialized epithelial cell of the mammary gland.

GO:0060647.name: mesenchymal cell condensation involved in mammary fat development
GO:0060647.def: The cell adhesion process in which mammary mesenchyme cells adhere to one another in the initial stages of the formation of mammary fat development.

GO:0060648.name: mammary gland bud morphogenesis
GO:0060648.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the mammary gland buds are generated and organized. Mammary gland buds form by an outpocketing of the mammary placodes and grow to invade the mammary fat, when they form the mammary cord.

GO:0060652.name: mammary gland cord morphogenesis
GO:0060652.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the mammary gland cord are generated and organized. Mammary gland cords form when the mammary gland bud invades the mammary fat.

GO:0060653.name: epithelial cell differentiation involved in mammary gland cord morphogenesis
GO:0060653.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized epithelial cell becomes a more specialized epithelial cell of the mammary gland cord. Epithelial cells of the mammary cord give it its funnel-like shape and some are cornified.
GO:0060653.synonym: epithelial cell differentiation involved in mammary gland sprout morphogenesis

GO:0060655.name: branching involved in mammary gland cord morphogenesis
GO:0060655.def: The process in which the branching structure of the mammary gland cord is generated and organized. The mammary gland cord is a solid epithelial structure that will hollow out, forming the mammary duct.

GO:0060658.name: nipple morphogenesis
GO:0060658.def: The process in which the nipple is generated and organized.

GO:0060660.name: epidermis morphogenesis involved in nipple formation
GO:0060660.def: The process in which the epidermis of the nipple sheath is uplifted to form an umbrella-like projection.

GO:0060661.name: submandibular salivary gland formation
GO:0060661.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a submandibular salivary gland. This process begins with a thickening of the epithelium next to the tongue and ends when a bud linked to the oral surface is formed.

GO:0060664.name: epithelial cell proliferation involved in salivary gland morphogenesis
GO:0060664.def: The multiplication or reproduction of epithelial cells of the submandibular salivary gland, resulting in the expansion of a cell population and the shaping of the gland.

GO:0060669.name: embryonic placenta morphogenesis
GO:0060669.def: The process in which the embryonic placenta is generated and organized.

GO:0060670.name: branching involved in labyrinthine layer morphogenesis
GO:0060670.def: The process in which the branches of the fetal placental villi are generated and organized. The villous part of the placenta is called the labyrinth layer.

GO:0060671.name: epithelial cell differentiation involved in embryonic placenta development
GO:0060671.def: The process in which a trophoblast cell acquires specialized features of an epithelial cell of the placental labyrinthine layer.

GO:0060673.name: cell-cell signaling involved in placenta development
GO:0060673.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another.
GO:0060673.synonym: cell-cell signalling involved in placenta development

GO:0060674.name: placenta blood vessel development
GO:0060674.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a blood vessel of the placenta over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060675.name: ureteric bud morphogenesis
GO:0060675.def: The process in which the ureteric bud is generated and organized.

GO:0060676.name: ureteric bud formation
GO:0060676.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the ureteric bud from the Wolffian duct. This process begins when the bud protrudes from the duct and ends when it is a recognizable bud.

GO:0060680.name: lateral sprouting involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis
GO:0060680.def: The process in which a branch forms along the side of a ureteric bud.

GO:0060684.name: epithelial-mesenchymal cell signaling
GO:0060684.def: Any process that results in the transfer of information from an epithelial cell to a mesenchymal cell where it is interpreted.

GO:0060685.name: regulation of prostatic bud formation
GO:0060685.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of prostatic bud formation, the morphogenetic process in which a region of the fetal urogenital sinus epithelium is specified to become the prostate, resulting in prostate bud outgrowth.

GO:0060686.name: negative regulation of prostatic bud formation
GO:0060686.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of prostatic bud formation, the morphogenetic process in which a region of the fetal urogenital sinus epithelium is specified to become the prostate, resulting in prostate bud outgrowth.

GO:0060687.name: regulation of branching involved in prostate gland morphogenesis
GO:0060687.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of prostate gland branching, the process in which the branching structure of the prostate gland is generated and organized. A branch is a division or offshoot from a main stem.

GO:0060688.name: regulation of morphogenesis of a branching structure
GO:0060688.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of branching morphogenesis, the process in which the anatomical structures of branches are generated and organized.

GO:0060689.name: cell differentiation involved in salivary gland development
GO:0060689.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the cells of the salivary gland.

GO:0060690.name: epithelial cell differentiation involved in salivary gland development
GO:0060690.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquire specialized structural and/or functional features of an epithelial cell of the salivary gland.

GO:0060691.name: epithelial cell maturation involved in salivary gland development
GO:0060691.def: The developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for an epithelial cell of the salivary gland to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0060692.name: mesenchymal cell differentiation involved in salivary gland development
GO:0060692.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a mesenchymal cell of the salivary gland. A mesenchymal cell is a loosely associated cell that is part of the connective tissue in an organism. Mesenchymal cells give rise to more mature connective tissue cell types.

GO:0060693.name: regulation of branching involved in salivary gland morphogenesis
GO:0060693.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of branching morphogenesis in the salivary gland epithelium.

GO:0060704.name: acinar cell differentiation involved in salivary gland development
GO:0060704.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize an acinar cell of the salivary gland. Acinar cells are protein-secreting cells in the gland.

GO:0060705.name: neuron differentiation involved in salivary gland development
GO:0060705.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the neurons of the salivary gland.

GO:0060706.name: cell differentiation involved in embryonic placenta development
GO:0060706.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of the embryonic placenta.

GO:0060707.name: trophoblast giant cell differentiation
GO:0060707.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a trophoblast giant cell of the placenta. Trophoblast giant cells are the cell of the placenta that line the maternal decidua.

GO:0060708.name: spongiotrophoblast differentiation
GO:0060708.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell of the ectoplacental cone acquires specialized features of a spongiotrophoblast of the placenta. A spongiotrophoblast cell is a basophilic cell.

GO:0060711.name: labyrinthine layer development
GO:0060711.def: The process in which the labyrinthine layer of the placenta progresses, from its formation to its mature state.

GO:0060712.name: spongiotrophoblast layer development
GO:0060712.def: The process in which the spongiotrophoblast layer of the placenta progresses from its formation to its mature state.

GO:0060713.name: labyrinthine layer morphogenesis
GO:0060713.def: The process in which the labyrinthine layer of the placenta is generated and organized.

GO:0060714.name: labyrinthine layer formation
GO:0060714.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the labyrinthine layer of the placenta.

GO:0060716.name: labyrinthine layer blood vessel development
GO:0060716.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a blood vessel of the labyrinthine layer of the placenta over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The embryonic vessels grow through the layer to come in close contact with the maternal blood supply.

GO:0060717.name: chorion development
GO:0060717.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a chorion from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the structure and ends with the mature structure. The chorion is an extraembryonic membrane.

GO:0060718.name: chorionic trophoblast cell differentiation
GO:0060718.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells of the ectoplacental cone acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize chorionic trophoblasts. These cells will migrate towards the spongiotrophoblast layer and give rise to syncytiotrophoblasts of the labyrinthine layer.

GO:0060719.name: chorionic trophoblast cell development
GO:0060719.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the chorionic trophoblast over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a specific fate.

GO:0060722.name: cell proliferation involved in embryonic placenta development
GO:0060722.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of the population in the embryonic placenta.

GO:0060723.name: regulation of cell proliferation involved in embryonic placenta development
GO:0060723.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of cell proliferation involved in embryonic placenta development.

GO:0060736.name: prostate gland growth
GO:0060736.def: The increase in size or mass of the prostate gland where the increase in size or mass has the specific outcome of the progression of the gland, from its formation to its mature state.

GO:0060737.name: prostate gland morphogenetic growth
GO:0060737.def: The differential increase in size or mass of the prostate gland that contributes to the gland attaining its form.
GO:0060737.synonym: prostate gland growth involved in morphogenesis

GO:0060738.name: epithelial-mesenchymal signaling involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060738.def: Any process that results in the transfer of information from an epithelial cell to a mesenchymal cell where it is interpreted and contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time.
GO:0060738.synonym: epithelial-mesenchymal signalling involved in prostate gland development

GO:0060739.name: mesenchymal-epithelial cell signaling involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060739.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from a mesenchymal cell to an epithelial cell where it is received and interpreted contributing to the progression of the prostate gland over time.
GO:0060739.synonym: mesenchymal-epithelial cell signalling involved in prostate gland development

GO:0060740.name: prostate gland epithelium morphogenesis
GO:0060740.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of epithelia of the prostate gland are generated and organized. An epithelium consists of closely packed cells arranged in one or more layers, that covers the outer surfaces of the body or lines any internal cavity or tube.

GO:0060741.name: prostate gland stromal morphogenesis
GO:0060741.def: The process in which the prostate gland stroma is generated and organized. The prostate gland stroma is made up of the mesenchymal or fibroblast cells of the prostate gland.

GO:0060742.name: epithelial cell differentiation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060742.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an epithelial cell of the prostate gland.

GO:0060743.name: epithelial cell maturation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060743.def: The developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for an epithelial cell of the prostate gland to attain its fully functional state. An epithelial cell is a cell usually found in a two-dimensional sheet with a free surface.

GO:0060749.name: mammary gland alveolus development
GO:0060749.def: The progression of the mammary gland alveolus over time, from its formation to its mature state. The mammary gland alveolus is a sac-like structure that is found in the mature gland.

GO:0060753.name: regulation of mast cell chemotaxis
GO:0060753.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell chemotaxis. Mast cell chemotaxis is the movement of a mast cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0060754.name: positive regulation of mast cell chemotaxis
GO:0060754.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell chemotaxis. Mast cell chemotaxis is the movement of a mast cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0060755.name: negative regulation of mast cell chemotaxis
GO:0060755.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of mast cell chemotaxis. Mast cell chemotaxis is the movement of a mast cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0060759.name: regulation of response to cytokine stimulus
GO:0060759.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of a response to cytokine stimulus.

GO:0060760.name: positive regulation of response to cytokine stimulus
GO:0060760.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of a response to cytokine stimulus.

GO:0060761.name: negative regulation of response to cytokine stimulus
GO:0060761.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of a response to cytokine stimulus.

GO:0060762.name: regulation of branching involved in mammary gland duct morphogenesis
GO:0060762.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of branching involved in mammary gland duct morphogenesis.

GO:0060764.name: cell-cell signaling involved in mammary gland development
GO:0060764.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another and contributes to the progression of the mammary gland, from its initial state to the mature structure.
GO:0060764.synonym: cell-cell signalling involved in mammary gland development

GO:0060767.name: epithelial cell proliferation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060767.def: The multiplication or reproduction of epithelial cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population that contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time.

GO:0060768.name: regulation of epithelial cell proliferation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060768.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of epithelial cell proliferation that contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time.

GO:0060769.name: positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060769.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of epithelial cell proliferation that contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time.

GO:0060770.name: negative regulation of epithelial cell proliferation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060770.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of epithelial cell proliferation that contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time.

GO:0060781.name: mesenchymal cell proliferation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060781.def: The multiplication or reproduction of mesenchymal cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population that contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time.

GO:0060782.name: regulation of mesenchymal cell proliferation involved in prostate gland development
GO:0060782.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of mesenchymal cell proliferation that contributes to the progression of the prostate gland over time. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets.

GO:0060784.name: regulation of cell proliferation involved in tissue homeostasis
GO:0060784.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell proliferation resulting in the maintenance of a steady-state number of cells within a tissue.

GO:0060785.name: regulation of apoptosis involved in tissue homeostasis
GO:0060785.def: Any process that modulates the occurrence or rate of cell death by apoptosis that results in the maintenance of the steady-state number of cells within a tissue.

GO:0060786.name: regulation of cell differentiation involved in tissue homeostasis
GO:0060786.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell differentiation that contributes to the maintenance of a steady state of a cell type within a tissue.

GO:0060788.name: ectodermal placode formation
GO:0060788.def: The developmental process in which an ectodermal placode forms. An ectodermal placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that is the primordium of many structures derived from the ectoderm.

GO:0060789.name: hair follicle placode formation
GO:0060789.def: The developmental process in which a hair placode forms. An hair follicle placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the hair follicle bud.

GO:0060790.name: tooth placode formation
GO:0060790.def: The developmental process in which the tooth placode forms. A tooth placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the tooth bud.

GO:0060791.name: sebaceous gland placode formation
GO:0060791.def: The developmental process in which a sebaceous gland placode forms. A sebaceous gland placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the sebaceous gland bud.

GO:0060792.name: sweat gland development
GO:0060792.def: The progression of the sweat gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Sweat glands secrete an aqueous solution that is used in thermoregulation.

GO:0060793.name: sweat gland placode formation
GO:0060793.def: The developmental process in which the sweat gland placode forms. An sweat gland placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the sweat gland bud.

GO:0060795.name: cell fate commitment involved in formation of primary germ layer
GO:0060795.def: The commitment of cells to specific cell fates of the endoderm, ectoderm, or mesoderm as a part of gastrulation.

GO:0060800.name: regulation of cell differentiation involved in embryonic placenta development
GO:0060800.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of cell differentiation that contributes to the progression of the placenta over time, from its initial condition to its mature state.

GO:0060806.name: negative regulation of cell differentiation involved in embryonic placenta development
GO:0060806.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of cell differentiation that contributes to the progression of the placenta over time, from its initial condition to its mature state.

GO:0060815.name: regulation of translation involved in anterior/posterior axis specification
GO:0060815.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of translation of mRNAs that contribute to the specification of the anterior/posterior axis.

GO:0060836.name: lymphatic endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0060836.def: The process in which a venous blood vessel endothelial cell acquires specialized features of a lymphatic vessel endothelial cell, a thin flattened cell that lines the inside surfaces of lymph vessels.

GO:0060837.name: blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0060837.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a blood vessel endothelial cell, a thin flattened cell that lines the inside surfaces of blood vessels.

GO:0060840.name: artery development
GO:0060840.def: The progression of the artery over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. An artery is a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart to a capillary bed.

GO:0060841.name: venous blood vessel development
GO:0060841.def: The progression of the venous blood vessel over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. Venous blood vessels carry blood back to the heart after the capillary bed.

GO:0060842.name: arterial endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0060842.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized endothelial cell acquires specialized features of an arterial endothelial cell, a thin flattened cell that lines the inside surfaces of arteries.

GO:0060843.name: venous endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0060843.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized endothelial cell acquires specialized features of a venous endothelial cell, a thin flattened cell that lines the inside surfaces of veins.

GO:0060854.name: branching involved in lymph vessel morphogenesis
GO:0060854.def: The process of the coordinated growth and sprouting of lymph vessels giving rise to the organized lymphatic system.

GO:0060872.name: semicircular canal development
GO:0060872.def: The progression of the semicircular canal from its initial formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060876.name: semicircular canal formation
GO:0060876.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the semicircular canal from the otic vesicle. This process begins with the regionalization of the vesicle that specifies the area where the vesicles will form and continues through the process of fusion which forms the initial tubes.

GO:0060877.name: regionalization involved in semicircular canal formation
GO:0060877.def: The pattern specification process that results in the subdivision of the otic epithelium in space to define an area or volume in which cells will differentiate to give rise to the semicircular canals.

GO:0060878.name: pouch outgrowth involved in semicircular canal formation
GO:0060878.def: The morphogenetic process in which an epithelial sheet bends along a linear axis and gives rise to a pouch that will form a semicircular canal.

GO:0060887.name: limb epidermis development
GO:0060887.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the epidermis of the limb over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The limb epidermis is the outer epithelial layer of the limb, it is a complex stratified squamous epithelium.

GO:0060896.name: neural plate pattern specification
GO:0060896.def: The developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within the neural plate to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate.

GO:0060897.name: neural plate regionalization
GO:0060897.def: The pattern specification process that results in the subdivision of an axis or axes of the neural plate in space to define an area or volume in which specific patterns of cell differentiation will take place or in which cells interpret a specific environment.

GO:0060900.name: embryonic camera-type eye formation
GO:0060900.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a camera-type eye from unspecified neurectoderm. This process begins with the differentiation of cells that form the optic field and ends when the optic cup has attained its shape.

GO:0060907.name: positive regulation of macrophage cytokine production
GO:0060907.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of macrophage cytokine production. Macrophage cytokine production is the appearance of a chemokine due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0060914.name: heart formation
GO:0060914.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the heart from unspecified parts. This process begins with the specific processes that contribute to the appearance of the heart field and the arrival of cardiac neural crest to the heart region. The process ends when the structural rudiment is recognizable.

GO:0060915.name: mesenchymal cell differentiation involved in lung development
GO:0060915.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a mesenchymal cell of the lung. A mesenchymal cell is a loosely associated cell that is part of the connective tissue in an organism. Mesenchymal cells give rise to more mature connective tissue cell types.

GO:0060916.name: mesenchymal cell proliferation involved in lung development
GO:0060916.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a mesenchymal cell population that contributes to the progression of the lung over time. A mesenchymal cell is a cell that normally gives rise to other cells that are organized as three-dimensional masses, rather than sheets.

GO:0060920.name: cardiac pacemaker cell differentiation
GO:0060920.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a pacemaker cell. Pacemaker cells are specialized cardiomyocytes that are responsible for regulating the timing of heart contractions.

GO:0060921.name: sinoatrial node cell differentiation
GO:0060921.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a sinoatrial (SA) node cell. SA node cells are pacemaker cells that are found in the sinoatrial node.

GO:0060922.name: atrioventricular node cell differentiation
GO:0060922.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an atrioventricular (AV) node cell. AV node cells are pacemaker cells that are found in the atrioventricular node.

GO:0060926.name: cardiac pacemaker cell development
GO:0060926.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pacemaker cell over time, from its formation to the mature state. Pacemaker cells are specialized cardiomyocytes that are responsible for regulating the timing of heart contractions.

GO:0060928.name: atrioventricular node cell development
GO:0060928.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an atrioventricular (AV) node cell over time, from its formation to the mature state.

GO:0060931.name: sinoatrial node cell development
GO:0060931.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a sinoatrial (SA) node cell over time, from its formation to the mature state. SA node cells are pacemaker cells that are found in the sinoatrial node.

GO:0060932.name: His-Purkinje system cell differentiation
GO:0060932.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cell of the His-Purkinje system. These cells form the fibers regulate cardiac muscle contraction in the ventricles.

GO:0060933.name: His-Purkinje system cell development
GO:0060933.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a His-Purkinje cell over time, from its formation to the mature state. These cells form the fibers that regulate cardiac muscle contraction in the ventricles.

GO:0060935.name: cardiac fibroblast cell differentiation
GO:0060935.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a cardiac fibroblast. A cardiac fibroblast is a connective tissue cell in the heart which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules.

GO:0060936.name: cardiac fibroblast cell development
GO:0060936.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cardiac fibroblast over time, from its formation to the mature state. A cardiac fibroblast is a connective tissue cell of the heart which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules.

GO:0060945.name: cardiac neuron differentiation
GO:0060945.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuron of the heart.

GO:0060946.name: cardiac blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0060946.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a blood vessel endothelial cell of the heart. Blood vessel endothelial cells are thin flattened cells that line the inside surfaces of blood vessels.

GO:0060950.name: cardiac glial cell differentiation
GO:0060950.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a glial cell of the heart.

GO:0060952.name: cardiac glial cell development
GO:0060952.def: The process aimed at the progression of a cardiac glial cell over time, from its formation to the fully functional mature cell.

GO:0060956.name: endocardial cell differentiation
GO:0060956.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of an endocardial cell. An endocardial cell is a specialized endothelial cell that makes up the endocardium portion of the heart. The endocardium is the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.

GO:0060958.name: endocardial cell development
GO:0060958.def: The progression of an endocardial cell over time, from its formation to the mature cell. An endocardial cell is a specialized endothelial cell that makes up the endocardium portion of the heart.

GO:0060959.name: cardiac neuron development
GO:0060959.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cardiac neuron over time, from its formation to the mature state.

GO:0060973.name: cell migration involved in heart development
GO:0060973.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another that will contribute to the progression of the heart over time, from its initial formation, to the mature organ.

GO:0060974.name: cell migration involved in heart formation
GO:0060974.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another that contribute to the formation of the heart. The initial heart structure is made up of mesoderm-derived heart progenitor cells and neural crest-derived cells.

GO:0060976.name: coronary vasculature development
GO:0060976.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the blood vessels of the heart over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0060977.name: coronary vasculature morphogenesis
GO:0060977.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of blood vessels of the heart are generated and organized. The blood vessel is the vasculature carrying blood.

GO:0060978.name: angiogenesis involved in coronary vascular morphogenesis
GO:0060978.def: Blood vessel formation in the heart when new vessels emerge from the proliferation of pre-existing blood vessels.
synonym: angiogenesis involved in cardiac vascular morphogenesis
angiogenesis involved in heart vascular morphogenesis

GO:0060979.name: vasculogenesis involved in coronary vascular morphogenesis
GO:0060979.def: The differentiation of endothelial cells from progenitor cells that contributes to blood vessel development in the heart, and the de novo formation of blood vessels and tubes.
synonym: vasculogenesis involved in coronary blood vessel morphogenesis

GO:0060980.name: cell migration involved in coronary vasculogenesis
GO:0060980.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another that will contribute to the differentiation of an endothelial cell that will form the blood vessels of the heart.

GO:0060981.name: cell migration involved in coronary angiogenesis
GO:0060981.def: The orderly movement of a cell from one site to another that will contribute to the formation of new blood vessels in the heart from pre-existing blood vessels.

GO:0060982.name: coronary artery morphogenesis
GO:0060982.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of coronary arteries are generated and organized. Coronary arteries are blood vessels that transport blood to the heart muscle.

GO:0060986.name: endocrine hormone secretion
GO:0060986.def: The regulated release of a hormone into the circulatory system.

GO:0060993.name: kidney morphogenesis
GO:0060993.def: Morphogenesis of a kidney. A kidney is an organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0060995.name: cell-cell signaling involved in kidney development
GO:0060995.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another and contributes to the progression of the kidney over time, from its formation to the mature organ.
GO:0060995.synonym: cell-cell signalling involved in kidney development

GO:0061004.name: pattern specification involved in kidney development
GO:0061004.def: Any developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within the kidney to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate.
synonym: pattern formation involved in kidney development

GO:0061005.name: cell differentiation involved in kidney development
GO:0061005.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the cells of the kidney as it progresses from its formation to the mature state.

GO:0061006.name: regulation of cell proliferation involved in kidney morphogenesis
GO:0061006.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cell proliferation that contributes to the shaping of the kidney.

GO:0061007.name: hepaticobiliary system process
GO:0061007.def: A system process carried out by any of the organs or tissues of the hepaticobiliary system. The hepaticobiliary system is responsible for metabolic and catabolic processing of small molecules absorbed from the blood or gut, hormones and serum proteins, detoxification, storage of glycogen, triglycerides, metals and lipid soluble vitamins and excretion of bile. Included are the synthesis of albumin, blood coagulation factors, complement, and specific binding proteins.

GO:0061008.name: hepaticobiliary system development
GO:0061008.def: The progression of the hepaticobiliary system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The hepaticobiliary system is responsible for metabolic and catabolic processing of small molecules absorbed from the blood or gut, hormones and serum proteins, detoxification, storage of glycogen, triglycerides, metals and lipid soluble vitamins and excretion of bile. Included are the synthesis of albumin, blood coagulation factors, complement, and specific binding proteins.

GO:0061009.name: common bile duct development
GO:0061009.def: The progression of the common bile duct over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The common bile duct is formed from the joining of the common hepatic duct running from the liver, and the cystic duct running from the gallbladder. The common bile duct transports bile from the liver and gallbladder to the intestine.

GO:0061010.name: gallbladder development
GO:0061010.def: The progression of the gallbladder over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The gallbladder is a cavitated organ that stores bile.

GO:0061011.name: hepatic duct development
GO:0061011.def: The progression of the hepatic duct over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The hepatic duct is the duct that leads from the liver to the common bile duct.

GO:0061017.name: hepatoblast differentiation
GO:0061017.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a hepatoblast. A hepatoblast is a cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into hepatocytes and cholangiocytes.

GO:0061024.name: membrane organization
GO:0061024.def: A process which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a membrane. A membrane is a double layer of lipid molecules that encloses all cells, and, in eukaryotes, many organelles; may be a single or double lipid bilayer; also includes associated proteins.

GO:0061025.name: membrane fusion
GO:0061025.def: The membrane organization process that joins two lipid bilayers to form a single membrane.

GO:0061027.name: umbilical cord development
GO:0061027.def: The process whose specific outcome is the development of the umbilical cord, from its formation to the mature structure. The umbilical cord is an organ or embryonic origin consisting of the 2 umbilical arteries and the one umbilical vein. The umbilical cord connects the cardiovascular system of the fetus to the mother via the placenta.

GO:0061029.name: eyelid development in camera-type eye
GO:0061029.def: The progression of the eyelid in a camera-type eye from its formation to the mature state. The eyelid is a membranous cover that helps protect and lubricate the eye.

GO:0061030.name: epithelial cell differentiation involved in mammary gland alveolus development
GO:0061030.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized epithelial cell becomes a more specialized epithelial cell of the mammary gland alveolus.

GO:0061032.name: visceral serous pericardium development
GO:0061032.def: The progression of the visceral serous pericardium from its formation to the mature structure. The visceral serous pericardium is the inner layer of the pericardium.

GO:0061034.name: olfactory bulb mitral cell layer development
GO:0061034.def: The progression of the olfactory bulb mitral cell layer over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The mitral cell layer is composed of pyramidal neurons whose cell bodies are located between the granule cell layer and the plexiform layer.

GO:0061035.name: regulation of cartilage development
GO:0061035.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of cartilage development, the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cartilage over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cartilage is a connective tissue dominated by extracellular matrix containing collagen type II and large amounts of proteoglycan, particularly chondroitin sulfate.

GO:0061036.name: positive regulation of cartilage development
GO:0061036.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of cartilage development, the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cartilage over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cartilage is a connective tissue dominated by extracellular matrix containing collagen type II and large amounts of proteoglycan, particularly chondroitin sulfate.

GO:0061037.name: negative regulation of cartilage development
GO:0061037.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of cartilage development, the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the cartilage over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cartilage is a connective tissue dominated by extracellular matrix containing collagen type II and large amounts of proteoglycan, particularly chondroitin sulfate.

GO:0061038.name: uterus morphogenesis
GO:0061038.def: The process in which anatomical structures of the uterus are generated and organized.

GO:0061040.name: female gonad morphogenesis
GO:0061040.def: The process in which a female gonad is generated and organized.

GO:0061041.name: regulation of wound healing
GO:0061041.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

GO:0061045.name: negative regulation of wound healing
GO:0061045.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the series of events that restore integrity to a damaged tissue, following an injury.

GO:0061046.name: regulation of branching involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0061046.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the process in which a highly ordered sequence of patterning events generates the branched structures of the lung, consisting of reiterated combinations of bud outgrowth, elongation, and dichotomous subdivision of terminal units.

GO:0061047.name: positive regulation of branching involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0061047.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the process in which a highly ordered sequence of patterning events generates the branched structures of the lung, consisting of reiterated combinations of bud outgrowth, elongation, and dichotomous subdivision of terminal units.

GO:0061048.name: negative regulation of branching involved in lung morphogenesis
GO:0061048.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the process in which a highly ordered sequence of patterning events generates the branched structures of the lung, consisting of reiterated combinations of bud outgrowth, elongation, and dichotomous subdivision of terminal units.

GO:0061049.name: cell growth involved in cardiac muscle cell development
GO:0061049.def: The growth of a cardiac muscle cell, where growth contributes to the progression of the cell over time from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0061050.name: regulation of cell growth involved in cardiac muscle cell development
GO:0061050.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the growth of a cardiac muscle cell, where growth contributes to the progression of the cell over time from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0061051.name: positive regulation of cell growth involved in cardiac muscle cell development
GO:0061051.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the growth of a cardiac muscle cell, where growth contributes to the progression of the cell over time from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0061052.name: negative regulation of cell growth involved in cardiac muscle cell development
GO:0061052.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the growth of a cardiac muscle cell, where growth contributes to the progression of the cell over time from its initial formation to its mature state.

GO:0061053.name: somite development
GO:0061053.def: The progression of a somite from its initial formation to the mature structure. Somites are mesodermal clusters that are arranged segmentally along the anterior posterior axis of an embryo.

GO:0061054.name: dermatome development
GO:0061054.def: The progression of the dermatome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The dermatome is the portion of a somite that will form skin.

GO:0061055.name: myotome development
GO:0061055.def: The progression of the myotome over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The myotome is the portion of the somite that will give rise to muscle.

GO:0061056.name: sclerotome development
GO:0061056.def: The progression of the sclerotome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The sclerotome is the portion of the somite that will give rise to a vertebra.

GO:0061061.name: muscle structure development
GO:0061061.def: The progression of a muscle structure over time, from its formation to its mature state. Muscle structures are contractile cells, tissues or organs that are found in multicellular organisms.

GO:0061068.name: urethra development
GO:0061068.def: The progression of the urethra over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The urethra is a renal system organ that carries urine from the bladder to outside the body.

GO:0061069.name: male urethra development
GO:0061069.def: The progression of the male urethra over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The male urethra is a renal system organ that carries urine from the bladder through the penis to outside the body.

GO:0061070.name: female urethra development
GO:0061070.def: The progression of the female urethra over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The female urethra is a renal system organ that carries urine from the bladder to outside the body, exiting above the vaginal opening.

GO:0061071.name: urethra epithelium development
GO:0061071.def: The progression of the urethra epithelium over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The urethra is a renal system organ that carries urine from the bladder to outside the body. The epithelium is the tubular, planar layer of cells through which the urine passes.

GO:0061072.name: iris morphogenesis
GO:0061072.def: The process in which the iris is generated and organized. The iris is an anatomical structure in the eye whose opening forms the pupil. The iris is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil and the amount of light reaching the retina.

GO:0061073.name: ciliary body morphogenesis
GO:0061073.def: The process in which the ciliary body generated and organized. The ciliary body is the circumferential tissue inside the eye composed of the ciliary muscle and ciliary processes.

GO:0061074.name: regulation of neural retina development
GO:0061074.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of neural retina development, the progression of the neural retina over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The neural retina is the part of the retina that contains neurons and photoreceptor cells.

GO:0061075.name: positive regulation of neural retina development
GO:0061075.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of neural retina development, the progression of the neural retina over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The neural retina is the part of the retina that contains neurons and photoreceptor cells.

GO:0061076.name: negative regulation of neural retina development
GO:0061076.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of neural retina development, the progression of the neural retina over time from its initial formation to the mature structure. The neural retina is the part of the retina that contains neurons and photoreceptor cells.

GO:0061080.name: right horn of sinus venosus development
GO:0061080.def: The progression of the right horn of the sinus venosus from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061081.name: positive regulation of myeloid leukocyte cytokine production involved in immune response
GO:0061081.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the production of a cytokine that contributes to the immune response.
GO:0061081.synonym: positive regulation of myeloid cell cytokine production involved in immune response

GO:0061082.name: myeloid leukocyte cytokine production
GO:0061082.def: Any process that contributes to cytokine production by a myeloid cell.

GO:0061097.name: regulation of protein tyrosine kinase activity
GO:0061097.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of protein tyrosine kinase activity.

GO:0061098.name: positive regulation of protein tyrosine kinase activity
GO:0061098.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of protein tyrosine kinase activity.

GO:0061099.name: negative regulation of protein tyrosine kinase activity
GO:0061099.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of protein tyrosine kinase activity.

GO:0061100.name: lung neuroendocrine cell differentiation
GO:0061100.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuroendocrine cell of the lung epithelium.

GO:0061101.name: neuroendocrine cell differentiation
GO:0061101.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a neuroendocrine cell. A neuroendocrine cell is a cell that receives input form a neuron which controls the secretion of an endocrine substance.

GO:0061102.name: stomach neuroendocrine cell differentiation
GO:0061102.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuroendocrine cell of the stomach epithelium.

GO:0061104.name: adrenal chromaffin cell differentiation
GO:0061104.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of an adrenal chromaffin cell. An adrenal chromaffin cell is a neuroendocrine cell that stores epinephrine secretory vesicles.

GO:0061105.name: regulation of stomach neuroendocrine cell differentiation
GO:0061105.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of the differentiation of a neuroendocrine cell in the stomach.

GO:0061106.name: negative regulation of stomach neuroendocrine cell differentiation
GO:0061106.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of the differentiation of a neuroendocrine cell in the stomach.

GO:0061107.name: seminal vesicle development
GO:0061107.def: The progression of the seminal vesicle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The seminal vesicle is a gland that contributes to the production of semen.

GO:0061108.name: seminal vesicle epithelium development
GO:0061108.def: The progression of the seminal vesicle epithelium over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061109.name: dense core granule organization
GO:0061109.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a dense core granule. A dense core granule is a secretory organelle found in endocrine cells.

GO:0061111.name: epithelial-mesenchymal cell signaling involved in lung development
GO:0061111.def: Any process that results in the transfer of information from an epithelial cell to a mesenchymal cell and contributes to the progression of the lung over time from its initial formation to the mature organ.
GO:0061111.synonym: epithelial-mesenchymal cell signalling involved in lung development

GO:0061113.name: pancreas morphogenesis
GO:0061113.def: Morphogenesis of the pancreas. Morphogenesis is the process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized.

GO:0061114.name: branching involved in pancreas morphogenesis
GO:0061114.def: The process in which the branches of the pancreas are generated and organized.

GO:0061117.name: negative regulation of heart growth
GO:0061117.def: Any process that decreases the rate or extent of heart growth. Heart growth is the increase in size or mass of the heart.

GO:0061130.name: pancreatic bud formation
GO:0061130.def: The morphogenetic process in which the foregut region specified to become the pancreas forms a bud.

GO:0061138.name: morphogenesis of a branching epithelium
GO:0061138.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a branched epithelium are generated and organized.

GO:0061140.name: lung secretory cell differentiation
GO:0061140.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a lung secretory cell. A lung secretory cell is a specialized epithelial cell of the lung that contains large secretory granules in its apical part.

GO:0061141.name: lung ciliated cell differentiation
GO:0061141.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a lung ciliated cell. A lung ciliated cell is a specialized lung epithelial cell that contains cilia for moving substances released from lung secretory cells.

GO:0061146.name: Peyer's patch morphogenesis
GO:0061146.def: The process in which a Peyer's patch is generated and organized. Peyer's patches are typically found as nodules associated with gut epithelium with distinct internal structures including B- and T-zones for the activation of lymphocytes.

GO:0061147.name: endocardial endothelium development
GO:0061147.def: The progression of the endocardial endothelium over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The endocardium is an anatomical structure comprised of an endothelium and an extracellular matrix that forms the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.

GO:0061148.name: extracellular matrix organization involved in endocardium development
GO:0061148.def: A process which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an extracellular matrix of the endocardium. The endocardium is an anatomical structure comprised of an endothelium and an extracellular matrix that forms the innermost layer of tissue of the heart, and lines the heart chambers.
GO:0061148.synonym: extracellular matrix organisation involved in endocardium development

GO:0061152.name: trachea submucosa development
GO:0061152.def: The progression of the trachea submucosa over time from its formation to the mature structure. The trachea submucosa is made up of the glands and elastic tissue that lie under the mucosa in the trachea.

GO:0061153.name: trachea gland development
GO:0061153.def: The progression of a trachea gland over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Trachea glands are found under the mucus of the trachea and secrete mucus, and agents that help protect the lung from injury and infection.

GO:0061154.name: endothelial tube morphogenesis
GO:0061154.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a tube are generated and organized from an endothelium. Endothelium refers to the layer of cells lining blood vessels, lymphatics, the heart, and serous cavities, and is derived from bone marrow or mesoderm. Corneal endothelium is a special case, derived from neural crest cells.

GO:0061155.name: pulmonary artery endothelial tube morphogenesis
GO:0061155.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a tube are generated and organized from the pulmonary artery endothelium. An pulmonary artery endothelium is an epithelium that lines the pulmonary artery.

GO:0061156.name: pulmonary artery morphogenesis
GO:0061156.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the pulmonary artery are generated and organized. The pulmonary artery is the artery that carries blood from the heart to the lungs.

GO:0061168.name: regulation of hair follicle placode formation
GO:0061168.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of hair follicle placode formation, the developmental process in which a hair placode forms. An hair follicle placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the hair follicle bud.

GO:0061169.name: positive regulation of hair placode formation
GO:0061169.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of hair follicle placode formation, the developmental process in which a hair placode forms. An hair follicle placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the hair follicle bud.

GO:0061170.name: negative regulation of hair follicle placode formation
GO:0061170.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of hair follicle placode formation, the developmental process in which a hair placode forms. An hair follicle placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that will give rise to the hair follicle bud.

GO:0061178.name: regulation of insulin secretion involved in cellular response to glucose stimulus
GO:0061178.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of insulin that contributes to the response of a cell to glucose.
GO:0061178.synonym: regulation of insulin secretion in response to glucose

GO:0061179.name: negative regulation of insulin secretion involved in cellular response to glucose stimulus
GO:0061179.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of insulin that contributes to the response of a cell to glucose.
synonym: negative regulation of insulin secretion in response to glucose
negative regulation of insulin secretion involved in cellular response to glucose

GO:0061180.name: mammary gland epithelium development
GO:0061180.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mammary gland epithelium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mammary gland is a large compound sebaceous gland that in female mammals is modified to secrete milk.

GO:0061181.name: regulation of chondrocyte development
GO:0061181.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a chondrocyte over time, from its commitment to its mature state. Chondrocyte development does not include the steps involved in committing a chondroblast to a chondrocyte fate.

GO:0061182.name: negative regulation of chondrocyte development
GO:0061182.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a chondrocyte over time, from its commitment to its mature state. Chondrocyte development does not include the steps involved in committing a chondroblast to a chondrocyte fate.

GO:0061183.name: regulation of dermatome development
GO:0061183.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the progression of the dermatome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The dermatome is the portion of a somite that will form skin.

GO:0061184.name: positive regulation of dermatome development
GO:0061184.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the progression of the dermatome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The dermatome is the portion of a somite that will form skin.

GO:0061185.name: negative regulation of dermatome development
GO:0061185.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of the progression of the dermatome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The dermatome is the portion of a somite that will form skin.

GO:0061189.name: positive regulation of sclerotome development
GO:0061189.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the progression of the sclerotome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The sclerotome is the portion of the somite that will give rise to a vertebra.

GO:0061190.name: regulation of sclerotome development
GO:0061190.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the progression of the sclerotome over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. The sclerotome is the portion of the somite that will give rise to a vertebra.

GO:0061193.name: taste bud development
GO:0061193.def: The progression of the taste bud over time, from its formation to the mature state. The taste bud is a specialized area of the tongue that contains taste receptors.

GO:0061194.name: taste bud morphogenesis
GO:0061194.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the taste bud are generated and organized. The taste bud is a specialized area of the tongue that contains taste receptors.

GO:0061195.name: taste bud formation
GO:0061195.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the taste bud from unspecified parts. The taste bud is a specialized area of the tongue that contains taste receptors.

GO:0061205.name: paramesonephric duct development
GO:0061205.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the paramesonephric duct over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Mullerian ducts (or paramesonephric ducts) are paired ducts of the embryo that run down the lateral sides of the urogenital ridge and terminate at the mullerian eminence in the primitive urogenital sinus. In the female, they will develop to form the fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, and the upper portion of the vagina; in the male, they are lost. These ducts are made of tissue of mesodermal origin.

GO:0061206.name: mesonephros morphogenesis
GO:0061206.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesonephros are generated and organized.

GO:0061208.name: cell differentiation involved in mesonephros development
GO:0061208.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the cells of the mesonephros as it progresses from its formation to the mature state.

GO:0061209.name: cell proliferation involved in mesonephros development
GO:0061209.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of the population in the mesonephros.

GO:0061210.name: cell-cell signaling involved in mesonephros development
GO:0061210.def: Any process that mediates the transfer of information from one cell to another and contributes to the progression of the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature organ.
GO:0061210.synonym: cell-cell signalling involved in mesonephros development

GO:0061211.name: mesonephric collecting duct development
GO:0061211.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a collecting duct in the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The collecting duct regulates water, electrolyte and acid-base balance. The collecting duct is the final common path through which urine flows before entering the ureter and then emptying into the bladder.

GO:0061212.name: mesonephric juxtaglomerular apparatus development
GO:0061212.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the juxtaglomerular apparatus in the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The juxtaglomerular apparatus is an anatomical structure which consists of juxtaglomerular cells, extraglomerular mesangial cells and the macula densa. The juxtaglomerular apparatus lies adjacent to the glomerulus and regulates kidney function by maintaining the blood flow to the kidney and the filtration rate.

GO:0061213.name: positive regulation of mesonephros development
GO:0061213.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of mesonephros development. Mesonephros development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephros is an organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0061214.name: mesonephric smooth muscle tissue development
GO:0061214.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of smooth muscle in the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061215.name: mesonephric nephron development
GO:0061215.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a nephron in the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A nephron is the functional unit of the kidney.

GO:0061217.name: regulation of mesonephros development
GO:0061217.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of mesonephros development. Mesonephros development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephros is an endocrine and metabolic organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0061218.name: negative regulation of mesonephros development
GO:0061218.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of mesonephros development. Mesonephros development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephros over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephros is an organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0061219.name: mesonephric mesenchyme development
GO:0061219.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a mesonephric mesenchyme from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of mesonephric mesenchyme and ends with the mature structure. Mesonephric mesenchyme is the tissue made up of loosely connected mesenchymal cells in the mesonephros.

GO:0061220.name: mesonephric macula densa development
GO:0061220.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephric macula densa over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric macula densa is an area of specialized cells in the distal tubule of the mesonephros that makes contact with the vascular pole of the glomerulus.

GO:0061221.name: mesonephric mesenchyme morphogenesis
GO:0061221.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a mesonephric mesenchymal tissue are generated and organized. Mesonephric mesenchyme is the tissue made up of loosely connected mesenchymal cells in the mesonephros.

GO:0061224.name: mesonephric glomerulus development
GO:0061224.def: The progression of the mesonephric glomerulus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The mesonephric glomerulus is a capillary tuft which forms a close network with the visceral epithelium (podocytes) and the mesangium to form the filtration barrier and is surrounded by Bowman's capsule in nephrons of the mature vertebrate kidney, or mesonephros.

GO:0061227.name: pattern specification involved in mesonephros development
GO:0061227.def: Any developmental process that results in the creation of defined areas or spaces within the mesonephros to which cells respond and eventually are instructed to differentiate.

GO:0061228.name: mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
GO:0061228.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesonephric nephron are generated and organized. A mesonephric nephron is the functional unit of the mesonephros.

GO:0061231.name: mesonephric glomerulus vasculature development
