GO:0061231.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a mesonephric glomerulus vasculature from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the mesonephric glomerulus vasculature and ends with the mature structure. The mesonephric glomerulus vasculature is composed of the tubule structures that carry blood or lymph in the mesonephric glomerulus.

GO:0061232.name: mesonephric glomerular epithelium development
GO:0061232.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephric glomerular epithelium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric glomerular epithelium is an epithelial tissue that covers the outer surfaces of the glomerulus in the mesonephros. The mesonephric glomerular epithelium consists of both parietal and visceral epithelium. Mesonephric glomerular parietal epithelial cells are specialized epithelial cells that form tight junctions as a barrier to protein transport. A mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell is a specialized epithelial cell that contains 'feet' that interdigitate with the 'feet' of other glomerular epithelial cells in the mesonephros.

GO:0061234.name: mesonephric glomerulus morphogenesis
GO:0061234.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesonephric glomerulus are generated and organized. The mesonephric glomerulus is a capillary tuft surrounded by Bowman's capsule in nephrons of the vertebrate mesonephros.

GO:0061235.name: mesenchymal stem cell maintenance involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
GO:0061235.def: The process in which an organism retains a population of mesenchymal stem cells that contributes to the shaping of a nephron in the mesonephros. A mesenchymal stem cell is a cell that retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized mesenchymal cells.

GO:0061236.name: mesonephric comma-shaped body morphogenesis
GO:0061236.def: The process in which the mesonephric comma-shaped body is generated and organized. The mesonephric comma-shaped body is the precursor structure to the mesonephric S-shaped body that contributes to the morphogenesis of a nephron in the mesonephros.

GO:0061240.name: mesonephric nephron tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061240.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a mesonephric nephron tubule are generated and organized. A mesonephric nephron tubule is an epithelial tube that is part of the mesonephric nephron, the functional part of the mesonephros.

GO:0061241.name: mesonephric nephron epithelium development
GO:0061241.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephric nephron epithelium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. An epithelium is a tissue that covers the internal or external surfaces of an anatomical structure. The mesonephric nephron epithelium is a tissue that covers the surface of a nephron in the mesonephros.

GO:0061242.name: mesonephric nephron tubule development
GO:0061242.def: The progression of a mesonephric nephron tubule over time, from its initial formation to the mature structure. A mesonephric nephron tubule is an epithelial tube that is part of the mesonephric nephron, the functional part of the mesonephros.

GO:0061243.name: mesonephric renal vesicle morphogenesis
GO:0061243.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesonephric renal vesicle are generated and organized. The renal vesicle is the primordial structure of the mesonephric nephron epithelium, and is formed by the condensation of mesenchymal cells.

GO:0061244.name: mesonephric S-shaped body morphogenesis
GO:0061244.def: The process in which the mesonephric S-shaped body is generated and organized. The mesonephric S-shaped body is the successor of the mesonephric comma-shaped body that contributes to the morphogenesis of a nephron in the mesonephros.

GO:0061247.name: mesonephric glomerular mesangium development
GO:0061247.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephric glomerular mesangium over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric glomerular mesangium is the thin membrane connective tissue composed of mesangial cells in the mesonephros, which helps to support the capillary loops in a renal glomerulus.

GO:0061248.name: mesonephric glomerulus vasculature morphogenesis
GO:0061248.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesonephric glomerulus vasculature are generated and organized. The mesonephric glomerulus vasculature is composed of the tubule structures that carry blood or lymph in the mesonephric glomerulus.

GO:0061249.name: mesonephric glomerular capillary formation
GO:0061249.def: The process that gives rise to a mesonephric glomerular capillary. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0061250.name: mesonephric glomerular epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0061250.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a mesonephric glomerular epithelial cell. Mesonephric glomerular epithelial cells are specialized epithelial cells that form part of the mesonephric glomerulus; there are two types, mesonephric glomerular parietal epithelial cells and mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cells.

GO:0061251.name: mesonephric glomerular epithelial cell development
GO:0061251.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a mesonephric glomerular epithelial cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Mesonephric glomerular epithelial cells are specialized epithelial cells that form part of the mesonephric glomerulus; there are two types, mesonephric glomerular parietal epithelial cells and mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cells.

GO:0061256.name: mesonephric podocyte differentiation
GO:0061256.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell. A mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell is a specialized epithelial cell that contains 'feet' that interdigitate with the 'feet' of other glomerular epithelial cells in the mesonephros.
GO:0061256.synonym: mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell differentiation

GO:0061257.name: mesonephric podocyte development
GO:0061257.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell is a specialized epithelial cell that contains 'feet' that interdigitate with the 'feet' of other glomerular epithelial cells in the mesonephros.
GO:0061257.synonym: mesonephric glomerular visceral epithelial cell development

GO:0061261.name: mesenchymal to epithelial transition involved in mesonephros morphogenesis
GO:0061261.def: A transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity, forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell that will contribute to the shaping of the mesonephros.

GO:0061262.name: mesonephric renal vesicle formation
GO:0061262.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the mesonephros.

GO:0061265.name: mesonephric nephron tubule epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0061265.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and/or functional features that characterize the cells of the mesonephric nephron tubule as it progresses from its formation to the mature state.

GO:0061271.name: mesenchymal to epithelial transition involved in mesonephric renal vesicle formation
GO:0061271.def: A transition where a mesenchymal cell establishes apical/basolateral polarity,forms intercellular adhesive junctions, synthesizes basement membrane components and becomes an epithelial cell that will contribute to the shaping of the mesonephric renal vesicle.

GO:0061272.name: mesonephric connecting tubule development
GO:0061272.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephric connecting tubule over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric connecting tubule is a tubular segment of the mesonephric nephron; it connects the distal tubule to the collecting duct in the mesonephros.

GO:0061273.name: mesonephric distal tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061273.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a mesonephric distal tubule are generated and organized. The mesonephric distal tubule is a mesonephric nephron tubule that begins at the macula densa and extends to the mesonephric connecting tubule.

GO:0061274.name: mesonephric distal tubule development
GO:0061274.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the mesonephric distal tubule over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric distal tubule is a mesonephric nephron tubule that begins at the terminal segment of the proximal tubule and ends at the mesonephric connecting tubule.

GO:0061275.name: mesonephric proximal tubule development
GO:0061275.def: The progression of the mesonephric proximal tubule over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric proximal tubule extends from the capsule to the distal tubule.

GO:0061276.name: mesonephric proximal tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061276.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a mesonephric proximal tubule are generated and organized. The mesonephric proximal tubule extends from the capsule to the distal tubule.

GO:0061277.name: mesonephric nephron tubule formation
GO:0061277.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a mesonephric nephron tubule from unspecified parts. A mesonephric nephron tubule is an epithelial tube that is part of a nephron in the mesonephros.

GO:0061278.name: epithelial cell migration involved in mesonephric nephron tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061278.def: The orderly movement of epithelial cells within a renal tubule that contributes to mesonephric nephron tubule morphogenesis.

GO:0061279.name: epithelial cell migration involved in mesonephric distal tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061279.def: The orderly movement of epithelial cells within a renal tubule that contributes to mesonephric distal tubule morphogenesis.

GO:0061280.name: epithelial cell migration involved in mesonephric proximal tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061280.def: The orderly movement of epithelial cells within a renal tubule that contributes to mesonephric proximal tubule morphogenesis.

GO:0061285.name: mesonephric capsule development
GO:0061285.def: The progression of the mesonephric capsule over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The mesonephric capsule is the tough fibrous layer surrounding the mesonephros, covered in a thick layer of perinephric adipose tissue.

GO:0061286.name: mesonephric capsule morphogenesis
GO:0061286.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the mesonephric capsule are generated and organized. The mesonephric capsule is the tough fibrous layer surrounding the mesonephros, covered in a thick layer of perinephric adipose tissue. It provides some protection from trauma and damage.

GO:0061287.name: mesonephric capsule formation
GO:0061287.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of a mesonephric capsule from unspecified parts. The mesonephric capsule is the tough fibrous layer surrounding the mesonephros, covered in a thick layer of perinephric adipose tissue. It provides some protection from trauma and damage.

GO:0061295.name: regulation of mesenchymal cell apoptotic process involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
GO:0061295.def: Any process that modulates the occurrence or rate of mesenchymal stem cell death by apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of the nephron in the mesonephros.
synonym: regulation of mesenchymal stem cell apoptosis involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
regulation of mesenchymal stem cell apoptotic process involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis

GO:0061296.name: negative regulation of mesenchymal cell apoptotic process involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
GO:0061296.def: Any process that reduces the occurrence or rate of mesenchymal stem cell death by apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of the nephron in the mesonephros.
synonym: negative regulation of mesenchymal stem cell apoptosis involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
negative regulation of mesenchymal stem cell apoptotic process involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis

GO:0061297.name: positive regulation of mesenchymal cell apoptotic process involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
GO:0061297.def: Any process that increases the occurrence or rate of mesenchymal stem cell death by apoptotic process that contributes to the shaping of the nephron in the mesonephros.
synonym: positive regulation of mesenchymal stem cell apoptosis involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis
positive regulation of mesenchymal stem cell apoptotic process involved in mesonephric nephron morphogenesis

GO:0061298.name: retina vasculature development in camera-type eye
GO:0061298.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vasculature of the retina over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061299.name: retina vasculature morphogenesis in camera-type eye
GO:0061299.def: The process in which the vasculature of the retina is generated and organized.

GO:0061300.name: cerebellum vasculature development
GO:0061300.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vasculature of the cerebellum over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061301.name: cerebellum vasculature morphogenesis
GO:0061301.def: The process in which the vasculature of the cerebellum is generated and organized.

GO:0061303.name: cornea development in camera-type eye
GO:0061303.def: The progression of the cornea over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The cornea is the transparent structure that covers the anterior of the eye.

GO:0061304.name: retinal blood vessel morphogenesis
GO:0061304.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a blood vessel of the retina over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061307.name: cardiac neural crest cell differentiation involved in heart development
GO:0061307.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a cardiac neural crest cell that will migrate to the heart and contribute to its development. Cardiac neural crest cells are specialized cells that migrate toward the heart from the third, fourth and sixth pharyngeal arches.

GO:0061308.name: cardiac neural crest cell development involved in heart development
GO:0061308.def: The process aimed at the progression of a cardiac neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell that contributes to the development of the heart.

GO:0061309.name: cardiac neural crest cell development involved in outflow tract morphogenesis
GO:0061309.def: The process aimed at the progression of a cardiac neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell that contributes to the shaping of the outflow tract.

GO:0061311.name: cell surface receptor signaling pathway involved in heart development
GO:0061311.def: The series of molecular signals initiated by a ligand the binding to its receptor on the surface of a cell, which contributes to the progression of the heart over time.
synonym: cell surface receptor linked signaling pathway involved in heart development
cell surface receptor linked signalling pathway involved in heart development

GO:0061318.name: renal filtration cell differentiation
GO:0061318.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of a renal filtration cell. Renal filtration cells are specialized cells of the renal system that filter fluids by charge, size or both. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate and its subsequent development to the mature state.

GO:0061319.name: nephrocyte differentiation
GO:0061319.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a nephrocyte. A nephrocyte is an insect renal cell that filters hemolymph. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate and its subsequent development to the mature state.

GO:0061320.name: pericardial nephrocyte differentiation
GO:0061320.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a pericardial nephrocyte. A pericardial nephrocyte is an insect renal cell that filters hemolymph and is found with other pericardial nephrocytes in two rows flanking the dorsal vessel. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate and its subsequent development to the mature state.

GO:0061321.name: garland nephrocyte differentiation
GO:0061321.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a garland nephrocyte. A garland nephrocyte is an insect renal cell that filters hemolymph and forms a ring with other garland nephrocytes around the esophagus. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate and its subsequent development to the mature state.

GO:0061322.name: disseminated nephrocyte differentiation
GO:0061322.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a disseminated nephrocyte. A disseminated nephrocyte is an insect renal cell that filters hemolymph and is found at scattered locations in the fat body or other tissues. Differentiation includes the processes involved in commitment of a cell to a specific fate and its subsequent development to the mature state.

GO:0061323.name: cell proliferation involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0061323.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population that contributes to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0061325.name: cell proliferation involved in outflow tract morphogenesis
GO:0061325.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population that contributes to the shaping of the outflow tract.

GO:0061326.name: renal tubule development
GO:0061326.def: The progression of the renal tubule over time from its formation to the mature form. A renal tubule is a tube that filters, re-absorbs and secretes substances to rid an organism of waste and to play a role in fluid homeostasis.

GO:0061330.name: Malpighian tubule stellate cell differentiation
GO:0061330.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a Malpighian tubule stellate cell. A Malpighian tubule stellate cell is a specialized epithelial secretory cell that moves chloride ions and water across the tubule epithelium.

GO:0061331.name: epithelial cell proliferation involved in Malpighian tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061331.def: The multiplication or reproduction of epithelial cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population and contributing to the shaping of a Malpighian tubule.

GO:0061332.name: Malpighian tubule bud morphogenesis
GO:0061332.def: The morphogenetic process in which a bud forms from the embryonic hindgut tube to form the Malpighian tubule. A bud is a protrusion that forms from the tube by localized changes in cell shape and position.

GO:0061333.name: renal tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061333.def: The process in which the renal tubule is generated by specification of cell fate, through the maintenance of cell polarity, regulated cell proliferation and morphogenetic cell rearrangements, shape changes and growth. A renal tubule is a tube that filters, re-absorbs and secretes substances to rid an organism of waste and to play a role in fluid homeostasis.

GO:0061334.name: cell rearrangement involved in Malpighian tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061334.def: The movement of an epithelial cell with respect to other epithelial cells that contributes to the shaping of the Malpighian tubule.
GO:0061334.synonym: cell migration involved in Malpighian tubule morphogenesis

GO:0061335.name: cell growth involved in Malpighian tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061335.def: The growth of an epithelial cell dependent on cycles of endoreplication, where growth contributes to the shaping of the Malpighian tubule.

GO:0061336.name: cell morphogenesis involved in Malpighian tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061336.def: The shape change of an epithelial cell from a columnar to squamous cell morphology that contributes to the shaping of the Malpighian tubule.

GO:0061337.name: cardiac conduction
GO:0061337.def: Transfer of an organized electrical impulse across the heart to coordinate the contraction of cardiac muscles. The process begins with generation of an action potential (in the sinoatrial node (SA) in humans) and ends with a change in the rate, frequency, or extent of the contraction of the heart muscles.

GO:0061343.name: cell adhesion involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0061343.def: The attachment of a cell, either to another cell or to an underlying substrate such as the extracellular matrix, via cell adhesion molecules that contributes to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0061344.name: regulation of cell adhesion involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0061344.def: Any process that modulates the extent of cell adhesion contributing to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0061351.name: neural precursor cell proliferation
GO:0061351.def: The multiplication or reproduction of neural precursor cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. A neural precursor cell is either a nervous system stem cell or a nervous system progenitor cell.

GO:0061352.name: cell chemotaxis involved in Malpighian tubule morphogenesis
GO:0061352.def: The directed movement of the outgrowing Malpighian tubule guided by specific chemical cues/signals. Movement may be towards a guidance cue (positive chemotaxis) or away from it (negative chemotaxis). Guidance contributes to the final positioning of the tubule.

GO:0061360.name: optic chiasma development
GO:0061360.def: The developmental process pertaining to the progression of the optic chiasm from its initial formation to the mature structure. The process begins when the pathfinding of the axons of the developing optic nerve cause some axons to cross at the midline of the brain and ends when the axons are mature.

GO:0061370.name: testosterone biosynthetic process
GO:0061370.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of testosterone, an androgen having 17beta-hydroxy and 3-oxo groups, together with unsaturation at C-4 C-5.

GO:0061377.name: mammary gland lobule development
GO:0061377.def: The progression of the mammary gland lobule over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A mammary gland lobule is a small rounded projection of the mammary gland.

GO:0061382.name: Malpighian tubule tip cell differentiation
GO:0061382.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a Malpighian tubule tip cell. A Malpighian tubule tip cell is a mitogenic signaling cell that controls the proliferation of its neighboring cells.

GO:0061383.name: trabecula morphogenesis
GO:0061383.def: The process of shaping a trabecula in an organ. A trabecula is a small, often microscopic, tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod, which generally has a mechanical function. Trabecula are usually but not necessarily, composed of dense collagenous tissue.

GO:0061384.name: heart trabecula morphogenesis
GO:0061384.def: The process of shaping a trabecula in the heart. A trabecula is a small, often microscopic, tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod, which generally has a mechanical function. Trabecula are usually but not necessarily, composed of dense collagenous tissue.

GO:0061385.name: fibroblast proliferation involved in heart morphogenesis
GO:0061385.def: The multiplication or reproduction of fibroblasts, resulting in the expansion of a fibroblast population that contributes to the shaping of the heart.

GO:0061437.name: renal system vasculature development
GO:0061437.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of vasculature of the renal system over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061438.name: renal system vasculature morphogenesis
GO:0061438.def: The process in which the renal system vasculature is generated and organized. Morphogenesis pertains to the creation of form.

GO:0061439.name: kidney vasculature morphogenesis
GO:0061439.def: The process in which the kidney vasculature is generated and organized. Morphogenesis pertains to the creation of form.

GO:0061440.name: kidney vasculature development
GO:0061440.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vasculature of the kidney over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061441.name: renal artery morphogenesis
GO:0061441.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of a renal artery is generated and organized. Renal arteries supply the kidneys with blood.

GO:0061448.name: connective tissue development
GO:0061448.def: The progression of a connective tissue over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061449.name: olfactory bulb tufted cell development
GO:0061449.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an olfactory bulb tufted cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0061450.name: trophoblast cell migration
GO:0061450.def: Trophoblast cell migration that is accomplished by extension and retraction of a pseudopodium. Trophoblast cells line the outside of the blastocyst.

GO:0061451.name: retrotrapezoid nucleus development
GO:0061451.def: The progression of the retrotrapezoid nucleus (RTN) over time from it's initial formation to its mature state. The retrotrapezoid nucleus is a group of neurons in the rostral medulla, which are responsible regulating respiration.

GO:0061452.name: retrotrapezoid nucleus neuron differentiation
GO:0061452.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuron whose cell body resides in the retrotrapezoid nucleus.

GO:0061453.name: interstitial cell of Cajal differentiation
GO:0061453.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an interstitial cell of Cajal. An interstitial cell of Cajal is an intestinal neuroepithelial cell that serves as a pacemaker to trigger gut contraction.

GO:0061454.name: release of sequestered calcium ion into cytosol by Golgi
GO:0061454.def: The directed movement of calcium ions (Ca2+) out of the Golgi apparatus into the cytosol.

GO:0061458.name: reproductive system development
GO:0061458.def: The progression of the reproductive system over time from its formation to the mature structure. The reproductive system consists of the organs that function in reproduction.

GO:0061462.name: protein localization to lysosome
GO:0061462.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within a lysosome.

GO:0061469.name: regulation of type B pancreatic cell proliferation
GO:0061469.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of type B pancreatic cell proliferation.

GO:0061470.name: T follicular helper cell differentiation
GO:0061470.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized T cell acquires specialized features of a mature T follicular helper cell.

GO:0061484.name: hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis
GO:0061484.def: Any biological process involved in the maintenance of the steady-state number of hematopoietic stem cells within a population of cells.

GO:0061485.name: memory T cell proliferation
GO:0061485.def: The expansion of a memory T cell population by cell division.

GO:0061512.name: protein localization to cilium
GO:0061512.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within a cilium.

GO:0061515.name: myeloid cell development
GO:0061515.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a myeloid cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061519.name: macrophage homeostasis
GO:0061519.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of macrophage cells such that the total number of myeloid cells within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0061520.name: Langerhans cell differentiation
GO:0061520.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a Langerhans cell.

GO:0061521.name: hepatic stellate cell differentiation
GO:0061521.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized structural and/or functional features of a hepatic stellate cell.

GO:0061523.name: cilium disassembly
GO:0061523.def: A cellular process that results in the breakdown of a cilium.

GO:0061524.name: central canal development
GO:0061524.def: The process whose specific outcome is the formation of the central canal of the spinal cord from its formation to the mature structure. The central canal is a spinal cord structure that is part of the ventricular system and is filled with cerebral-spinal fluid and runs the length of the spinal cord.

GO:0061525.name: hindgut development
GO:0061525.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the hindgut over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The hindgut is part of the alimentary canal that lies posterior to the midgut.

GO:0061526.name: acetylcholine secretion
GO:0061526.def: The regulated release of acetylcholine by a cell.

GO:0061527.name: dopamine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061527.def: The regulated release of dopamine by a cell in which the dopamine acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061533.name: norepinephrine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061533.def: The regulated release of norepinephrine by a cell, in which the norepinephrine acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061534.name: gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061534.def: The regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid by a cell, in which the gamma-aminobutyric acid acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061535.name: glutamate secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061535.def: The controlled release of glutamate by a cell, in which the glutamate acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061536.name: glycine secretion
GO:0061536.def: The controlled release of glycine by a cell.

GO:0061537.name: glycine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061537.def: The controlled release of glycine by a cell, in which glycine acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061538.name: histamine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061538.def: The controlled release of histamine by a cell, in which the histamine acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061544.name: peptide secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061544.def: The controlled release of a peptide from a cell in which the peptide acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061548.name: ganglion development
GO:0061548.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a ganglion over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061549.name: sympathetic ganglion development
GO:0061549.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a sympathetic ganglion over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061550.name: cranial ganglion development
GO:0061550.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cranial ganglion over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061551.name: trigeminal ganglion development
GO:0061551.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a trigeminal ganglion over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0061552.name: ganglion morphogenesis
GO:0061552.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of ganglion are generated and organized.

GO:0061553.name: ganglion maturation
GO:0061553.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for ganglion to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0061554.name: ganglion formation
GO:0061554.def: The process that gives rise to ganglion. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0061556.name: trigeminal ganglion morphogenesis
GO:0061556.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of a trigeminal ganglion is generated and organized.

GO:0061557.name: trigeminal ganglion maturation
GO:0061557.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a trigeminal ganglion to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0061558.name: cranial ganglion maturation
GO:0061558.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a cranial ganglion to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0061559.name: cranial ganglion morphogenesis
GO:0061559.def: The process in which the anatomical structure of a cranial ganglion is generated and organized.

GO:0061560.name: cranial ganglion formation
GO:0061560.def: The process that gives rise to a cranial ganglion. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0061561.name: trigeminal ganglion formation
GO:0061561.def: The process that gives rise to the trigeminal ganglion. This process pertains to the initial formation of a structure from unspecified parts.

GO:0061564.name: axon development
GO:0061564.def: The progression of an axon over time. Covers axonogenesis (de novo generation of an axon) and axon regeneration (regrowth), as well as processes pertaining to the progression of the axon over time (fasciculation and defasciculation).

GO:0061572.name: actin filament bundle organization
GO:0061572.def: A process that results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of an actin filament bundle.

GO:0061580.name: colon epithelial cell migration
GO:0061580.def: The orderly movement of a colonic epithelial cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0061581.name: corneal epithelial cell migration
GO:0061581.def: The orderly movement of a corneal epithelial cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0061582.name: intestinal epithelial cell migration
GO:0061582.def: The orderly movement of an intestinal epithelial cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0061584.name: orexin secretion
GO:0061584.def: The controlled release of orexin from a cell or a tissue.

GO:0061585.name: orexin secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0061585.def: The controlled release of orexin from a cell in which orexin acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0061626.name: pharyngeal arch artery morphogenesis
GO:0061626.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a pharyngeal arch artery is generated and organized. The pharyngeal arch arteries are a series of six paired embryological vascular structures, the development of which give rise to several major arteries, such as the stapedial artery, the middle meningeal artery, the internal carotid artery and the pulmonary artery.

GO:0061629.name: RNA polymerase II-specific DNA-binding transcription factor binding
GO:0061629.def: Binding to a sequence-specific DNA binding RNA polymerase II transcription factor, any of the factors that interact selectively and non-covalently with a specific DNA sequence in order to modulate transcription.
synonym: RNA polymerase II activating transcription factor binding
RNA polymerase II repressing transcription factor binding
RNA polymerase II sequence-specific DNA binding transcription factor binding
RNA polymerase II sequence-specific DNA-binding transcription factor binding
RNA polymerase II transcription factor binding

GO:0061682.name: seminal vesicle morphogenesis
GO:0061682.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a seminal vesicle are generated and organized.

GO:0061683.name: branching involved in seminal vesicle morphogenesis
GO:0061683.def: The process in which the branching structure of the seminal vesicle is generated and organized. A branch is a division or offshoot from a main stem.

GO:0061687.name: detoxification of inorganic compound
GO:0061687.def: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of inorganic compounds. These include transport of such compounds away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of inorganic compounds.

GO:0061695.name: transferase complex, transferring phosphorus-containing groups
GO:0061695.def: A transferase complex capable of catalysis of the transfer of a phosphorus-containing group from one compound (donor) to another (acceptor).

GO:0061725.name: cytosolic lipolysis
GO:0061725.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lipid droplets and hydrolysis of stored triglycerides occurring through the orchestrated activation of cytosolic lipases.

GO:0061792.name: secretory granule maturation
GO:0061792.def: Steps required to transform an immature secretory vesicle into a mature secretory vesicle. Typically proceeds through homotypic membrane fusion and membrane remodeling.

GO:0061842.name: microtubule organizing center localization
GO:0061842.def: Any process in which the microtubule organizing center is transported to, and/or maintained in, a specific location within the cell.

GO:0061844.name: antimicrobial humoral immune response mediated by antimicrobial peptide
GO:0061844.def: An immune response against microbes mediated by anti-microbial peptides in body fluid.

GO:0061847.name: response to cholecystokinin
GO:0061847.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cholecystokinin stimulus.

GO:0061848.name: cellular response to cholecystokinin
GO:0061848.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cholecystokinin stimulus.

GO:0061853.name: regulation of neuroblast migration
GO:0061853.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neuroblast migration.

GO:0061854.name: positive regulation of neuroblast migration
GO:0061854.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of neuroblast migration.

GO:0061855.name: negative regulation of neuroblast migration
GO:0061855.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of neuroblast migration.

GO:0061856.name: Golgi calcium ion transmembrane transport
GO:0061856.def: A process in which a calcium ion is transported from one side of a Golgi membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0061868.name: hepatic stellate cell migration
GO:0061868.def: The orderly movement of a hepatic stellate cell from one site to another.

GO:0061869.name: regulation of hepatic stellate cell migration
GO:0061869.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of hepatic stellate cell migration.

GO:0061870.name: positive regulation of hepatic stellate cell migration
GO:0061870.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of hepatic stellate cell migration.

GO:0061871.name: negative regulation of hepatic stellate cell migration
GO:0061871.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of hepatic stellate cell migration.

GO:0061888.name: regulation of astrocyte activation
GO:0061888.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of astrocyte activation.

GO:0061889.name: negative regulation of astrocyte activation
GO:0061889.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of astrocyte activation.

GO:0061890.name: positive regulation of astrocyte activation
GO:0061890.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of astrocyte activation.

GO:0061900.name: glial cell activation
GO:0061900.def: A change in morphology and behavior of a glial cell resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

GO:0061938.name: protein localization to somatodendritic compartment
GO:0061938.def: A process in which a protein is transported to or maintained in a location within the somatodendritic compartment.

GO:0061951.name: establishment of protein localization to plasma membrane
GO:0061951.def: The directed movement of a protein to a specific location in a plasma membrane.

GO:0061971.name: replacement bone morphogenesis
GO:0061971.def: The process in which bones are generated and organized as a result of the conversion of another structural tissue into bone.

GO:0061972.name: dermal bone morphogenesis
GO:0061972.def: The process in which bone which forms superficially in the organism are generated and organized.

GO:0061973.name: membrane bone morphogenesis
GO:0061973.def: The process in which bone which forms deep in the organism are generated and organized.

GO:0061983.name: meiosis II cell cycle process
GO:0061983.def: A process that coontributes to the second meiotic division. The second meiotic division separates chromatids resulting in a haploid number of chromosomes.

GO:0062012.name: regulation of small molecule metabolic process
GO:0062012.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of a small molecule metabolic process.

GO:0062013.name: positive regulation of small molecule metabolic process
GO:0062013.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of a small molecule metabolic process.
GO:0062013.synonym: positive regulation of small molecule metabolism

GO:0062014.name: negative regulation of small molecule metabolic process
GO:0062014.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of a small molecule metabolic process.
GO:0062014.synonym: negative regulation of small molecule metabolism

GO:0062023.name: collagen-containing extracellular matrix
GO:0062023.def: An extracellular matrix consisting mainly of proteins (especially collagen) and glycosaminoglycans (mostly as proteoglycans) that provides not only essential physical scaffolding for the cellular constituents but can also initiate crucial biochemical and biomechanical cues required for tissue morphogenesis, differentiation and homeostasis. The components are secreted by cells in the vicinity and form a sheet underlying or overlying cells such as endothelial and epithelial cells.

GO:0062033.name: positive regulation of mitotic sister chromatid segregation
GO:0062033.def: Any process that starts or increases the frequency, rate or extent of sister chromatid segregation during mitosis.

GO:0062056.name: compound eye pigment cell differentiation
GO:0062056.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a compound eye pigment cell, a cell of the retina containing screening pigments that functions to screen photoreceptors from light leaking from adjacent ommatidia.

GO:0062094.name: stomach development
GO:0062094.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the stomach over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The stomach is an expanded region of the vertebrate alimentary tract that serves as a food storage compartment and digestive organ.

GO:0062137.name: cargo receptor complex
GO:0062137.def: Any protein complex that is part of a membrane and which functions as a cargo receptor.

GO:0062149.name: detection of stimulus involved in sensory perception of pain
GO:0062149.def: The series of events involved in the perception of pain in which a stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0062170.name: lutein metabolic process
GO:0062170.def: The chemical reactions and pathways, including anabolism and catabolism, by which living organisms transform lutein.

GO:0062171.name: lutein biosynthetic process
GO:0062171.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of lutein.

GO:0062172.name: lutein catabolic process
GO:0062172.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lutein.

GO:0062177.name: radial spoke assembly
GO:0062177.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form the radial spoke, a protein complex that links the outer microtubule doublet of the ciliary or flagellum axoneme with the sheath that surrounds the central pair of microtubules.

GO:0062197.name: cellular response to chemical stress
GO:0062197.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a chemical stimulus indicating the organism is under stress.

GO:0062236.name: ionocyte differentiation
GO:0062236.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized structural and/or functional features of an ionocyte. Ionocytes are specialized epithelial cells that contribute to osmotic homeostasis.

GO:0062237.name: protein localization to postsynapse
GO:0062237.def: Any process in which a protein is transported to, and/or maintained at the postsynapse, the part of a synapse that is part of the post-synaptic cell.

GO:0065002.name: intracellular protein transmembrane transport
GO:0065002.def: The directed movement of proteins in a cell, from one side of a membrane to another by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
synonym: intracellular membrane translocation of a protein
intracellular protein transport across a membrane

GO:0065003.name: protein-containing complex assembly
GO:0065003.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of macromolecules to form a protein-containing complex.

GO:0065005.name: protein-lipid complex assembly
GO:0065005.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of proteins and lipids to form a protein-lipid complex.

GO:0065007.name: biological regulation
GO:0065007.def: Any process that modulates a measurable attribute of any biological process, quality or function.

GO:0065008.name: regulation of biological quality
GO:0065008.def: Any process that modulates a qualitative or quantitative trait of a biological quality. A biological quality is a measurable attribute of an organism or part of an organism, such as size, mass, shape, color, etc.

GO:0065009.name: regulation of molecular function
GO:0065009.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a molecular function, an elemental biological activity occurring at the molecular level, such as catalysis or binding.

GO:0065010.name: extracellular membrane-bounded organelle
GO:0065010.def: Organized structure of distinctive morphology and function, bounded by a lipid bilayer membrane and occurring outside the cell.

GO:0070013.name: intracellular organelle lumen
GO:0070013.def: An organelle lumen that is part of an intracellular organelle.

GO:0070050.name: neuron cellular homeostasis
GO:0070050.def: The cellular homeostatic process that preserves a neuron in a stable, differentiated functional and structural state.

GO:0070051.name: fibrinogen binding
GO:0070051.def: Binding to fibrinogen, a highly soluble hexameric glycoprotein complex that is found in blood plasma and is converted to fibrin by thrombin in the coagulation cascade.

GO:0070062.name: extracellular exosome
GO:0070062.def: A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.

GO:0070091.name: glucagon secretion
GO:0070091.def: The regulated release of glucagon from secretory granules in the A (alpha) cells of the pancreas (islets of Langerhans).

GO:0070092.name: regulation of glucagon secretion
GO:0070092.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of glucagon.

GO:0070093.name: negative regulation of glucagon secretion
GO:0070093.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of glucagon.

GO:0070094.name: positive regulation of glucagon secretion

GO:0070254.name: mucus secretion
GO:0070254.def: The regulated release of mucus by the mucosa. Mucus is a viscous slimy secretion consisting of mucins and various inorganic salts dissolved in water, with suspended epithelial cells and leukocytes. The mucosa, or mucous membrane, is the membrane covered with epithelium that lines the tubular organs of the body. Mucins are carbohydrate-rich glycoproteins that have a lubricating and protective function.

GO:0070278.name: extracellular matrix constituent secretion
GO:0070278.def: The controlled release of molecules that form the extracellular matrix, including carbohydrates and glycoproteins by a cell.

GO:0070285.name: pigment cell development
GO:0070285.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pigment cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a pigment cell fate.

GO:0070286.name: axonemal dynein complex assembly
GO:0070286.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form an axonemal dynein complex, a dynein complex found in eukaryotic cilia and flagella, in which the motor domain heads interact with adjacent microtubules to generate a sliding force which is converted to a bending motion.

GO:0070293.name: renal absorption
GO:0070293.def: A renal system process in which water, ions, glucose and proteins are taken up from the collecting ducts, glomerulus and proximal and distal loops of the nephron. GO:0070295.name: renal water absorption
GO:0070295.def: A renal system process in which water is taken up from the collecting ducts and proximal and distal loops of the nephron. In non-mammalian species, absorption may occur in related structures.

GO:0070306.name: lens fiber cell differentiation
GO:0070306.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a lens fiber cell, any of the elongated, tightly packed cells that make up the bulk of the mature lens in the camera-type eye. The cytoplasm of a lens fiber cell is devoid of most intracellular organelles including the cell nucleus, and contains primarily crystallins, a group of water-soluble proteins expressed in vary large quantities.

GO:0070307.name: lens fiber cell development
GO:0070307.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a lens fiber cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Cell development does not include the steps involved in committing a cell to a lens fiber cell fate. A lens fiber cell is any of the elongated, tightly packed cells that make up the bulk of the mature lens in a camera-type eye.

GO:0070444.name: oligodendrocyte progenitor proliferation
GO:0070444.def: The multiplication or reproduction of oligodendrocyte progenitor cells by cell division, resulting in the expansion of their population. Oligodendrocyte progenitors give rise to oligodendrocytes, which form the insulating myelin sheath of axons in the central nervous system.

GO:0070459.def: The regulated release of prolactin, a peptide hormone that stimulates lactation, from secretory granules in the anterior pituitary.

GO:0070460.name: thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion
GO:0070460.def: The regulated release of thyroid-stimulating hormone, a peptide hormone that stimulates the activity of the thyroid gland, from secretory granules in the anterior pituitary.

GO:0070482.name: response to oxygen levels
GO:0070482.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of oxygen.

GO:0070483.name: detection of hypoxia
GO:0070483.def: The series of events in which a stimulus indicating lowered oxygen tension is received by a cell and converted into a molecular signal. Hypoxia, defined as a decline in O2 levels below normoxic levels of 20.8 - 20.95%, results in metabolic adaptation at both the cellular and organismal level.

GO:0070507.name: regulation of microtubule cytoskeleton organization

GO:0070509.name: calcium ion import

GO:0070998.def: The series of events required for an organism to receive a gravitational stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. This is a neurological process.

GO:0070999.name: detection of mechanical stimulus involved in sensory perception of gravity
GO:0070999.def: The series of events involved in the perception of gravity in which a sensory mechanical stimulus is received and converted into a molecular signal.

GO:0071168.def: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, a part of a chromosome that is organized into chromatin.

GO:0071169.name: establishment of protein localization to chromatin

GO:0071169.synonym: establishment of protein localisation to chromatin

GO:0071214.name: cellular response to abiotic stimulus
GO:0071214.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an abiotic (non-living) stimulus.

GO:0071229.name: cellular response to acid chemical
GO:0071229.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus by the chemical structure of the anion portion of the dissociated acid (rather than the acid acting as a proton donor). The acid chemical may be in gaseous, liquid or solid form.

GO:0071230.name: cellular response to amino acid stimulus
GO:0071230.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amino acid stimulus. An amino acid is a carboxylic acids containing one or more amino groups.

GO:0071242.name: cellular response to ammonium ion

GO:0071345.name: cellular response to cytokine stimulus

GO:0071384.name: cellular response to corticosteroid stimulus
GO:0071384.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a corticosteroid hormone stimulus. A corticosteroid is a steroid hormone that is produced in the adrenal cortex. Corticosteroids are involved in a wide range of physiologic systems such as stress response, immune response and regulation of inflammation, carbohydrate metabolism, protein catabolism, blood electrolyte levels, and behavior. They include glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids.

GO:0071385.name: cellular response to glucocorticoid stimulus
GO:0071385.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a glucocorticoid stimulus. Glucocorticoids are hormonal C21 corticosteroids synthesized from cholesterol with the ability to bind with the cortisol receptor and trigger similar effects. Glucocorticoids act primarily on carbohydrate and protein metabolism, and have anti-inflammatory effects.

GO:0071389.name: cellular response to mineralocorticoid stimulus
GO:0071389.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a mineralocorticoid stimulus. Mineralocorticoids are hormonal C21 corticosteroids synthesized from cholesterol and characterized by their similarity to aldosterone. Mineralocorticoids act primarily on water and electrolyte balance.

GO:0071392.name: cellular response to estradiol stimulus
GO:0071392.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of stimulus by estradiol, a C18 steroid hormone hydroxylated at C3 and C17 that acts as a potent estrogen.

GO:0071393.name: cellular response to progesterone stimulus
GO:0071393.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a progesterone stimulus.

GO:0071394.name: cellular response to testosterone stimulus
GO:0071394.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a testosterone stimulus.

GO:0071396.name: cellular response to lipid
GO:0071396.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lipid stimulus.

GO:0071398.name: cellular response to fatty acid
GO:0071398.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a fatty acid stimulus.

GO:0071402.name: cellular response to lipoprotein particle stimulus
GO:0071402.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a lipoprotein particle stimulus.

GO:0071418.name: cellular response to amine stimulus
GO:0071418.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amine stimulus. An amine is a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.

GO:0071420.name: cellular response to histamine
GO:0071420.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a histamine stimulus. Histamine, the biogenic amine 2-(1H-imidazol-4-yl)ethanamine, is involved in local immune responses as well as regulating physiological function in the gut and acting as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0071425.name: hematopoietic stem cell proliferation
GO:0071425.def: The expansion of a hematopoietic stem cell population by cell division. A hematopoietic stem cell is a stem cell from which all cells of the lymphoid and myeloid lineages develop.

GO:0071450.name: cellular response to oxygen radical
GO:0071450.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an oxygen radical stimulus. An oxygen radical is any oxygen species that carries a free electron; examples include hydroxyl radicals and the superoxide anion.

GO:0071451.name: cellular response to superoxide
GO:0071451.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a superoxide stimulus. Superoxide is the anion, oxygen-, formed by addition of one electron to dioxygen (O2) or any compound containing the superoxide anion.

GO:0071462.name: cellular response to water stimulus
GO:0071462.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of water.

GO:0071495.name: cellular response to endogenous stimulus
GO:0071495.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus arising within the organism.

GO:0071542.name: dopaminergic neuron differentiation
GO:0071542.def: The process in which a neuroblast acquires the specialized structural and functional features of a dopaminergic neuron, a neuron that secretes dopamine.

GO:0071599.name: otic vesicle development
GO:0071599.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the otic vesicle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The otic vesicle is a transient embryonic structure formed during development of the vertebrate inner ear.

GO:0071600.name: otic vesicle morphogenesis
GO:0071600.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the otic vesicle are generated and organized. The otic vesicle is a transient embryonic structure formed during development of the vertebrate inner ear.

GO:0071621.name: granulocyte chemotaxis
GO:0071621.def: The movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0071622.name: regulation of granulocyte chemotaxis
GO:0071622.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of granulocyte chemotaxis. Granulocyte chemotaxis is the movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0071623.name: negative regulation of granulocyte chemotaxis
GO:0071623.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of granulocyte chemotaxis. Granulocyte chemotaxis is the movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0071624.name: positive regulation of granulocyte chemotaxis
GO:0071624.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of granulocyte chemotaxis. Granulocyte chemotaxis is the movement of a granulocyte in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0071626.name: mastication
GO:0071626.def: The process of biting and mashing food with the teeth prior to swallowing.

GO:0071670.name: smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
GO:0071670.def: The directed movement of a smooth muscle cell in response to an external stimulus.

GO:0071671.name: regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
GO:0071671.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis.

GO:0071672.name: negative regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
GO:0071672.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate, or extent of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis.
synonym: down regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
down-regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
downregulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
inhibition of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis

GO:0071673.name: positive regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
GO:0071673.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate, or extent of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis.
synonym: activation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
stimulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
up regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
up-regulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis
upregulation of smooth muscle cell chemotaxis

GO:0071674.name: mononuclear cell migration
GO:0071674.def: The movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0071675.name: regulation of mononuclear cell migration
GO:0071675.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of mononuclear cell migration. Mononuclear cell migration is the movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0071676.name: negative regulation of mononuclear cell migration
GO:0071676.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of mononuclear cell migration. Mononuclear cell migration is the movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.
synonym: down regulation of mononuclear cell migration

GO:0071677.name: positive regulation of mononuclear cell migration
GO:0071677.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of mononuclear cell migration. Mononuclear cell migration is the movement of a mononuclear cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.
synonym: up regulation of mononuclear cell migration

GO:0071692.name: protein localization to extracellular region
GO:0071692.def: Any process in which a protein is transported from one specific location in the extracellular region to another, or maintained in a specific extracellular location.

GO:0071695.name: anatomical structure maturation
GO:0071695.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for an anatomical structure to attain its fully functional state.

GO:0071696.name: ectodermal placode development
GO:0071696.def: The progression of an ectodermal placode over time from its initial formation until its mature state. An ectodermal placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that is the primordium of many structures derived from the ectoderm.

GO:0071697.name: ectodermal placode morphogenesis
GO:0071697.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of an ectodermal placode are generated and organized. An ectodermal placode is a thickening of the ectoderm that is the primordium of many structures derived from the ectoderm.

GO:0071698.name: olfactory placode development
GO:0071698.def: The progression of the olfactory placode over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The olfactory placode is a thickening of the neural ectoderm in the head region of the vertebrate embryo which develops into the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

GO:0071699.name: olfactory placode morphogenesis
GO:0071699.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of the olfactory placode are generated and organized. The olfactory placode is a thickening of the neural ectoderm in the head region of the vertebrate embryo which develops into the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

GO:0071700.name: olfactory placode maturation
GO:0071700.def: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for the olfactory placode to attain its fully functional state. The olfactory placode is a thickening of the neural ectoderm in the head region of the vertebrate embryo which develops into the olfactory region of the nasal cavity.

GO:0071705.name: nitrogen compound transport
GO:0071705.def: The directed movement of nitrogen-containing compounds into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0071706.name: tumor necrosis factor superfamily cytokine production
GO:0071706.def: The appearance of any member of the TNF superfamily due to biosynthesis or secretion following a cellular stimulus, resulting in an increase in its intracellular or extracellular levels.

GO:0071707.name: immunoglobulin heavy chain V-D-J recombination
GO:0071707.def: The process in which immunoglobulin heavy chain V, D, and J gene segments are recombined within a single locus utilizing the conserved heptamer and nonomer recombination signal sequences (RSS).

GO:0071708.name: immunoglobulin light chain V-J recombination
GO:0071708.def: The process in which immunoglobulin light chain V and J gene segments are recombined within a single locus utilizing the conserved heptamer and nonomer recombination signal sequences (RSS).

GO:0071709.name: membrane assembly
GO:0071709.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a membrane.

GO:0071711.name: basement membrane organization
GO:0071711.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the basement membrane.

GO:0071731.name: response to nitric oxide
GO:0071731.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitric oxide stimulus.

GO:0071732.name: cellular response to nitric oxide
GO:0071732.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitric oxide stimulus.

GO:0071735.name: IgG immunoglobulin complex
GO:0071735.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of an IgG isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds. An IgG immunoglobulin complex may be embedded in the plasma membrane or present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071736.name: IgG immunoglobulin complex, circulating
GO:0071736.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of an IgG isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds, and present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071738.name: IgD immunoglobulin complex
GO:0071738.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgD isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds. An IgD immunoglobulin complex may be embedded in the plasma membrane or present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071739.name: IgD immunoglobulin complex, circulating
GO:0071739.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgD isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds, and present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071742.name: IgE immunoglobulin complex
GO:0071742.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgE isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds. An IgE immunoglobulin complex may be embedded in the plasma membrane or present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071743.name: IgE immunoglobulin complex, circulating
GO:0071743.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgE isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds, and present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071745.name: IgA immunoglobulin complex
GO:0071745.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgA isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds, and sometimes complexed with J chain or J chain and secretory component. An IgA immunoglobulin complex may be embedded in the plasma membrane or present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071746.name: IgA immunoglobulin complex, circulating
GO:0071746.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of an IgA isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds, sometimes complexed with J chain or J chain and secretory component, and present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071753.name: IgM immunoglobulin complex
GO:0071753.def: A protein complex composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgM isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds, and in its circulating form complexed with J chain in polymeric forms. An IgM immunoglobulin complex may be embedded in the plasma membrane or present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or circulating in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071754.name: IgM immunoglobulin complex, circulating
GO:0071754.def: A polymer of five or six IgM core units each composed of two identical immunoglobulin heavy chains of the IgM isotype and two identical immunoglobulin light chains, held together by disulfide bonds; the individual IgM core units are held together via disulfide bonds with a single J chain polypeptide acting as a bridge between two of the polymeric units. Circulating IgM is present in the extracellular space, in mucosal areas or other tissues, or in the blood or lymph.

GO:0071763.name: nuclear membrane organization
GO:0071763.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the nuclear inner or outer membrane.

GO:0071764.name: nuclear outer membrane organization
GO:0071764.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the nuclear outer membrane.
synonym: nuclear outer membrane organization and biogenesis

GO:0071805.name: potassium ion transmembrane transport
GO:0071805.def: A process in which a potassium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0071806.name: protein transmembrane transport
GO:0071806.def: The process in which a protein is transported across a membrane.

GO:0071813.name: lipoprotein particle binding
GO:0071813.def: Binding to a lipoprotein particle. A lipoprotein particle, also known as a lipoprotein, is a clathrate complex consisting of a lipid enwrapped in a protein host without covalent binding in such a way that the complex has a hydrophilic outer surface consisting of all the protein and the polar ends of any phospholipids.

GO:0071814.name: protein-lipid complex binding
GO:0071814.def: Binding to a protein-lipid complex, any macromolecular complex that contains both protein and lipid molecules.

GO:0071825.name: protein-lipid complex organization
GO:0071825.def: Any process in which macromolecules aggregate, disaggregate, or are modified, resulting in the formation, disassembly, or alteration of a protein-lipid complex.

GO:0071826.name: protein-RNA complex organization
GO:0071826.def: Any process in which macromolecules aggregate, disaggregate, or are modified, resulting in the formation, disassembly, or alteration of a ribonucleoprotein complex.

GO:0071840.name: cellular component organization or biogenesis
GO:0071840.def: A process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a cellular component.
synonym: cellular component organisation or biogenesis at cellular level
cellular component organization or biogenesis at cellular level

GO:0071867.name: response to monoamine
GO:0071867.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a monoamine stimulus. A monoamine is any of a group of molecular messengers that contain one amino group that is connected to an aromatic ring by ethylene group (-CH2-CH2-). Monoamines are derived from the aromatic amino acids phenylalanine, tyrosine, histidine and tryptophan.

GO:0071868.name: cellular response to monoamine stimulus
GO:0071868.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a monoamine stimulus. A monoamine is any of a group of molecular messengers that contain one amino group that is connected to an aromatic ring by ethylene group (-CH2-CH2-). Monoamines are derived from the aromatic amino acids phenylalanine, tyrosine, histidine and tryptophan.

GO:0071869.name: response to catecholamine
GO:0071869.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a catecholamine stimulus. A catecholamine is any of a group of biogenic amines that includes 4-(2-aminoethyl)pyrocatechol [4-(2-aminoethyl)benzene-1,2-diol] and derivatives formed by substitution.

GO:0071870.name: cellular response to catecholamine stimulus
GO:0071870.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a catecholamine stimulus. A catecholamine is any of a group of biogenic amines that includes 4-(2-aminoethyl)pyrocatechol [4-(2-aminoethyl)benzene-1,2-diol] and derivatives formed by substitution.

GO:0071873.name: response to norepinephrine
GO:0071873.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a norepinephrine stimulus. Norepinephrine is a catecholamine that has the formula C8H11NO3; it acts as a hormone, and as a neurotransmitter in most of the sympathetic nervous system.

GO:0071874.name: cellular response to norepinephrine stimulus
GO:0071874.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a norepinephrine stimulus. Norepinephrine is a catecholamine that has the formula C8H11NO3; it acts as a hormone, and as a neurotransmitter in most of the sympathetic nervous system.

GO:0071887.name: leukocyte apoptotic process
GO:0071887.def: Any apoptotic process in a leukocyte, an achromatic cell of the myeloid or lymphoid lineages capable of ameboid movement, found in blood or other tissue.

GO:0071888.name: macrophage apoptotic process
GO:0071888.def: Any apoptotic process in a macrophage, a mononuclear phagocyte present in a variety of tissues.

GO:0071895.name: odontoblast differentiation
GO:0071895.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell of neural crest origin acquires the specialized features of an odontoblast, a cell on the outer surface of the dental pulp whose biological function is the creation of dentin.

GO:0071897.name: DNA biosynthetic process
GO:0071897.def: The biosynthetic process resulting in the formation of DNA.

GO:0071941.name: nitrogen cycle metabolic process
GO:0071941.def: A nitrogen compound metabolic process that contributes to the nitrogen cycle. The nitrogen cycle is a series of metabolic pathways by which nitrogen is converted between various forms and redox states; it encompasses pathways in which nitrogen is acted upon directly, such as nitrification, denitrification, nitrogen fixation, and mineralization.

GO:0071944.name: cell periphery
GO:0071944.def: The broad region around and including the plasma membrane of a cell, encompassing the cell cortex (inside the cell), the plasma membrane, and any external encapsulating structures.

GO:0071953.name: elastic fiber
GO:0071953.def: An supramolecular fiber that consists of an insoluble core of polymerized tropoelastin monomers and a surrounding mantle of microfibrils. Elastic fibers provide elasticity and recoiling to tissues and organs, and maintain structural integrity against mechanical strain.

GO:0071971.name: extracellular exosome assembly
