GO:0072674.name: multinuclear osteoclast differentiation
GO:0072674.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized monocyte acquires the specialized features of a multinuclear osteoclast. An osteoclast is a specialized phagocytic cell associated with the absorption and removal of the mineralized matrix of bone tissue.

GO:0072676.name: lymphocyte migration
GO:0072676.def: The movement of a lymphocyte within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0072677.name: eosinophil migration
GO:0072677.def: The movement of an eosinophil within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0072678.name: T cell migration
GO:0072678.def: The movement of a T cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0072679.name: thymocyte migration
GO:0072679.def: The movement of a thymocyte through distinct intrathymic niches (e.g. medulla, cortex), where it receives a unique set of developmental cues required for T-cell development.

GO:0072697.name: protein localization to cell cortex
GO:0072697.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, the cell cortex.

GO:0072698.name: protein localization to microtubule cytoskeleton
GO:0072698.def: A cellular protein localization process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, a location within the microtubule cytoskeleton.

GO:0075296.name: positive regulation of ascospore formation
GO:0075296.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of ascospore formation, a process in which a sexual spore, named ascospore, from Ascomycete fungi was produced inside an ascus.

GO:0075297.name: negative regulation of ascospore formation
GO:0075297.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of ascospore formation, a process in which a sexual spore, named ascospore, from Ascomycete fungi was produced inside an ascus.

GO:0075298.name: regulation of zygospore formation
GO:0075298.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of zygospore formation, a process in which a thick-walled spore of some algae and fungi is formed by union of two similar sexual cells, usually serves as a resting spore, and produces the sporophytic phase.

GO:0075299.name: positive regulation of zygospore formation
GO:0075299.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of frequency, rate or extent of zygospore formation, a process in which a thick-walled spore of some algae and fungi is formed by union of two similar sexual cells, usually serves as a resting spore, and produces the sporophytic phase.

GO:0075300.name: negative regulation of zygospore formation
GO:0075300.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of zygospore formation, a process in which a thick-walled spore of some algae and fungi is formed by union of two similar sexual cells, usually serves as a resting spore, and produces the sporophytic phase.

GO:0075302.name: regulation of basidiospore formation
GO:0075302.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of basidiospore formation, a process in which a sexually produced fungal spore is formed on a basidium in the fungi Basidiomycetes.

GO:0075303.name: positive regulation of basidiospore formation
GO:0075303.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of frequency, rate or extent of basidiospore formation, a process in which a sexually produced fungal spore is formed on a basidium in the fungi basidiomycetes.

GO:0075304.name: negative regulation of basidiospore formation
GO:0075304.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of basidiospore formation, a process in which a sexually produced fungal spore is formed on a basidium in the fungi basidiomycetes.

GO:0080090.name: regulation of primary metabolic process
GO:0080090.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways within a cell or an organism involving those compounds formed as a part of the normal anabolic and catabolic processes. These processes take place in most, if not all, cells of the organism.

GO:0080134.name: regulation of response to stress
GO:0080134.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a response to stress. Response to stress is a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in organismal or cellular homeostasis, usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

GO:0080135.name: regulation of cellular response to stress
GO:0080135.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a cellular response to stress. Cellular response to stress is a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress. The stress is usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

GO:0080144.name: intracellular amino acid homeostasis
GO:0080144.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of amino acids within a cell.

GO:0080154.name: regulation of fertilization
GO:0080154.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of fertilization. Fertilization is the union of gametes of opposite sexes during the process of sexual reproduction to form a zygote. It involves the fusion of the gametic nuclei (karyogamy) and cytoplasm (plasmogamy).

GO:0080164.name: regulation of nitric oxide metabolic process
GO:0080164.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways involving nitric oxide, nitrogen monoxide (NO), a colorless gas only slightly soluble in water.

GO:0080171.name: lytic vacuole organization
GO:0080171.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a lytic vacuole.

GO:0085029.name: extracellular matrix assembly
GO:0085029.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of the extracellular matrix.

GO:0086068.def: The process that mediates interactions between a Purkinje myocyte and its surroundings that contributes to the process of the Purkinje myocyte communicating with a ventricular cardiac muscle cell in cardiac conduction. GO:0086069.def: The process that mediates interactions between a bundle of His cell and its surroundings that contributes to the process of the bundle of His cell communicating with a Purkinje myocyte in cardiac conduction. GO:0089718.def: The directed movement of an amino acid from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0090009.name: primitive streak formation
GO:0090009.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of the primitive streak from unspecified parts. The primitive streak is a ridge of cells running along the midline of the embryo where the mesoderm ingresses. It defines the anterior-posterior axis.

GO:0090022.name: regulation of neutrophil chemotaxis
GO:0090022.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of neutrophil chemotaxis. Neutrophil chemotaxis is the directed movement of a neutrophil cell, the most numerous polymorphonuclear leukocyte found in the blood, in response to an external stimulus, usually an infection or wounding.

GO:0090023.name: positive regulation of neutrophil chemotaxis
GO:0090023.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of neutrophil chemotaxis. Neutrophil chemotaxis is the directed movement of a neutrophil cell, the most numerous polymorphonuclear leukocyte found in the blood, in response to an external stimulus, usually an infection or wounding.

GO:0090024.name: negative regulation of neutrophil chemotaxis
GO:0090024.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate, or extent of neutrophil chemotaxis. Neutrophil chemotaxis is the directed movement of a neutrophil cell, the most numerous polymorphonuclear leukocyte found in the blood, in response to an external stimulus, usually an infection or wounding.

GO:0090025.name: regulation of monocyte chemotaxis
GO:0090025.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of monocyte chemotaxis.

GO:0090026.name: positive regulation of monocyte chemotaxis
GO:0090026.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of monocyte chemotaxis.

GO:0090027.name: negative regulation of monocyte chemotaxis
GO:0090027.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate, or extent of monocyte chemotaxis.

GO:0090030.name: regulation of steroid hormone biosynthetic process
GO:0090030.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroid hormones,compounds with a 1, 2, cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus that act as hormones.

GO:0090031.name: positive regulation of steroid hormone biosynthetic process
GO:0090031.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroid hormones,compounds with a 1, 2, cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus that act as hormones.

GO:0090032.name: negative regulation of steroid hormone biosynthetic process
GO:0090032.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of steroid hormones,compounds with a 1, 2, cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene nucleus that act as hormones.

GO:0090063.name: positive regulation of microtubule nucleation
GO:0090063.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of microtubule nucleation. Microtubule nucleation is the 'de novo' formation of a microtubule, in which tubulin heterodimers form metastable oligomeric aggregates, some of which go on to support formation of a complete microtubule. Microtubule nucleation usually occurs from a specific site within a cell.

GO:0090066.name: regulation of anatomical structure size
GO:0090066.def: Any process that modulates the size of an anatomical structure.

GO:0090068.name: positive regulation of cell cycle process
GO:0090068.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of a cellular process that is involved in the progression of biochemical and morphological phases and events that occur in a cell during successive cell replication or nuclear replication events.

GO:0090069.name: regulation of ribosome biogenesis
GO:0090069.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of ribosome biogenesis. Ribosome biogenesis is the cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of ribosome subunits.

GO:0090070.name: positive regulation of ribosome biogenesis
GO:0090070.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of ribosome biogenesis. Ribosome biogenesis is the cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of ribosome subunits.

GO:0090071.name: negative regulation of ribosome biogenesis
GO:0090071.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of ribosome biogenesis. Ribosome biogenesis is the cellular process that results in the biosynthesis of constituent macromolecules, assembly, and arrangement of constituent parts of ribosome subunits.

GO:0090077.name: foam cell differentiation
GO:0090077.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a foam cell. A foam cell is a type of cell containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

GO:0090078.name: smooth muscle derived foam cell differentiation
GO:0090078.def: The process in which a smooth muscle cell acquires the specialized features of a foam cell. A foam cell is a type of cell containing lipids in small vacuoles and typically seen in atherosclerotic lesions, as well as other conditions.

GO:0090087.name: regulation of peptide transport
GO:0090087.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of peptides, compounds of two or more amino acids where the alpha carboxyl group of one is bound to the alpha amino group of another, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0090091.name: positive regulation of extracellular matrix disassembly
GO:0090091.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of extracellular matrix disassembly. Extracellular matrix disassembly is a process that results in the breakdown of the extracellular matrix.

GO:0090102.name: cochlea development
GO:0090102.def: The progression of the cochlea over time from its formation to the mature structure. The cochlea is the snail-shaped portion of the inner ear that is responsible for the detection of sound.

GO:0090103.name: cochlea morphogenesis
GO:0090103.def: The process in which the cochlea is generated and organized.

GO:0090104.name: pancreatic epsilon cell differentiation
GO:0090104.def: The process in which relatively unspecialized cells acquire specialized structural and functional features of a pancreatic epsilon cell. A pancreatic epsilon cell is a cell in the pancreas that secretes ghrelin.

GO:0090105.name: pancreatic E cell development
GO:0090105.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a pancreatic E cell over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0090109.name: regulation of cell-substrate junction assembly
GO:0090109.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of cell-substrate junction assembly. Cell-substrate junction assembly is the aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a junction between a cell and its substrate.

GO:0090130.name: tissue migration
GO:0090130.def: The process in which the population of cells that make up a tissue undergo directed movement.

GO:0090131.name: mesenchyme migration
GO:0090131.def: The process in which the population of cells that make up a mesenchyme undergo directed movement.

GO:0090132.name: epithelium migration
GO:0090132.def: The process in which the population of cells that make up an epithelium undergo directed movement.

GO:0090138.name: regulation of actin cytoskeleton organization by cell-cell adhesion
GO:0090138.def: Any cell-cell adhesion process that modulates the formation, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins.

GO:0090153.name: regulation of sphingolipid biosynthetic process
GO:0090153.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of sphingolipid biosynthesis. Sphingolipid biosynthesis is the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sphingolipids, any of a class of lipids containing the long-chain amine diol sphingosine or a closely related base (a sphingoid).

GO:0090154.name: positive regulation of sphingolipid biosynthetic process
GO:0090154.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of sphingolipid biosynthesis. Sphingolipid biosynthesis is the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of sphingolipids, any of a class of lipids containing the long-chain amine diol sphingosine or a closely related base (a sphingoid).

GO:0090155.name: negative regulation of sphingolipid biosynthetic process
GO:0090155.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of sphingolipid biosynthesis. GO:0090156.name: intracellular sphingolipid homeostasis

GO:0090160.name: Golgi to lysosome transport

GO:0090162.name: establishment of epithelial cell polarity

GO:0090170.name: regulation of Golgi inheritance
GO:0090170.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of Golgi inheritance. Golgi inheritance is the partitioning of Golgi apparatus between daughter cells at cell division.

GO:0090171.name: chondrocyte morphogenesis
GO:0090171.def: The process in which the structures of a chondrocyte are generated and organized. This process occurs while the initially relatively unspecialized cell is acquiring the specialized features of a chondrocyte.

GO:0090174.name: organelle membrane fusion
GO:0090174.def: The joining of two lipid bilayers to form a single organelle membrane.

GO:0090183.name: regulation of kidney development
GO:0090183.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of kidney development. Kidney development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the kidney over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The kidney is an organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0090184.name: positive regulation of kidney development
GO:0090184.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of kidney development. Kidney development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the kidney over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The kidney is an organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0090185.name: negative regulation of kidney development
GO:0090185.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of kidney development. Kidney development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the kidney over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The kidney is an organ that filters the blood and excretes the end products of body metabolism in the form of urine.

GO:0090189.name: regulation of branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis
GO:0090189.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis, the process in which the branching structure of the ureteric bud is generated and organized. The ureteric bud is an epithelial tube that grows out from the metanephric duct. The bud elongates and branches to give rise to the ureter and kidney collecting tubules.

GO:0090190.name: positive regulation of branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis
GO:0090190.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis, the process in which the branching structure of the ureteric bud is generated and organized. The ureteric bud is an epithelial tube that grows out from the metanephric duct. The bud elongates and branches to give rise to the ureter and kidney collecting tubules.

GO:0090191.name: negative regulation of branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis
GO:0090191.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency or extent of branching involved in ureteric bud morphogenesis, the process in which the branching structure of the ureteric bud is generated and organized. The ureteric bud is an epithelial tube that grows out from the metanephric duct. The bud elongates and branches to give rise to the ureter and kidney collecting tubules.

GO:0090192.name: regulation of glomerulus development
GO:0090192.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency or extent of glomerulus development, the progression of the glomerulus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The glomerulus is a capillary tuft surrounded by Bowman's capsule in nephrons of the vertebrate kidney.

GO:0090193.name: positive regulation of glomerulus development
GO:0090193.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency or extent of glomerulus development, the progression of the glomerulus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The glomerulus is a capillary tuft surrounded by Bowman's capsule in nephrons of the vertebrate kidney.

GO:0090194.name: negative regulation of glomerulus development

GO:0090214.def: The increase in size or mass of the spongiotrophoblast layer of the placenta where the increase in size or mass contributes to the progression of that layer over time from its formation to its mature state.

GO:0090279.name: regulation of calcium ion import
GO:0090279.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of the directed movement of calcium ions into a cell or organelle.

GO:0090280.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the directed movement of calcium ions into a cell or organelle.

GO:0090290.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of the multiplication or reproduction of osteoclasts, resulting in the expansion of an osteoclast cell population.

GO:0090299.name: regulation of neural crest formation
GO:0090299.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of neural crest formation. Neural crest formation is the formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds.

GO:0090300.name: positive regulation of neural crest formation
GO:0090300.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of neural crest formation. Neural crest formation is the formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds.

GO:0090301.name: negative regulation of neural crest formation
GO:0090301.def: Any process that decreases the rate, frequency, or extent of neural crest formation. Neural crest formation is the formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds.

GO:0090303.name: positive regulation of wound healing

GO:0090304.name: nucleic acid metabolic process
GO:0090304.def: Any cellular metabolic process involving nucleic acids.

GO:0090316.name: positive regulation of intracellular protein transport
GO:0090316.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of proteins within cells.

GO:0090317.name: negative regulation of intracellular protein transport
GO:0090317.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of proteins within cells.

GO:0090322.name: regulation of superoxide metabolic process
GO:0090322.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of superoxide metabolism, the chemical reactions and pathways involving superoxide, the superoxide anion O2- (superoxide free radical), or any compound containing this species.

GO:0090325.name: regulation of locomotion involved in locomotory behavior
GO:0090325.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of the self-propelled movement of a cell or organism from one location to another in a behavioral context; the aspect of locomotory behavior having to do with movement.

GO:0090326.name: positive regulation of locomotion involved in locomotory behavior
GO:0090326.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of the self-propelled movement of a cell or organism from one location to another in a behavioral context; the aspect of locomotory behavior having to do with movement.

GO:0090327.name: negative regulation of locomotion involved in locomotory behavior
GO:0090327.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate, or extent of the self-propelled movement of a cell or organism from one location to another in a behavioral context; the aspect of locomotory behavior having to do with movement.

GO:0090328.name: regulation of olfactory learning
GO:0090328.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of olfactory learning. Olfactory learning is any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs in response to (repeated) exposure to an olfactory cue.

GO:0090335.name: regulation of brown fat cell differentiation
GO:0090335.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of brown fat cell differentiation. Brown fat cell differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a brown adipocyte, an animal connective tissue cell involved in adaptive thermogenesis. Brown adipocytes contain multiple small droplets of triglycerides and a high number of mitochondria.

GO:0090336.name: positive regulation of brown fat cell differentiation
GO:0090336.def: Any process that increases the rate, frequency, or extent of brown fat cell differentiation. Brown fat cell differentiation is the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a brown adipocyte, an animal connective tissue cell involved in adaptive thermogenesis. Brown adipocytes contain multiple small droplets of triglycerides and a high number of mitochondria.

GO:0090394.name: negative regulation of excitatory postsynaptic potential
GO:0090394.def: Any process that prevents the establishment or decreases the extent of the excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP) which is a temporary increase in postsynaptic potential due to the flow of positively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an EPSP is an excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) and makes it easier for the neuron to fire an action potential.
synonym: negative regulation of excitatory post-synaptic membrane potential
reduction of excitatory postsynaptic membrane potential

GO:0090407.name: organophosphate biosynthetic process
GO:0090407.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the biosynthesis of deoxyribose phosphate, the phosphorylated sugar 2-deoxy-erythro-pentose.

GO:0090425.name: acinar cell differentiation
GO:0090425.def: The epithelial cell differentiation process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an acinar cell, a secretory cell that is grouped together with other cells of the same type to form grape-shaped clusters known as acini.

GO:0090435.name: protein localization to nuclear envelope
GO:0090435.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, a location within a nuclear envelope.

GO:0090454.name: glutamate transmembrane import into vacuole
GO:0090454.def: The directed movement of glutamate into the vacuole across the vacuolar membrane.

GO:0090461.name: intracellular glutamate homeostasis
GO:0090461.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of glutamate within a cell.

GO:0090493.name: catecholamine uptake
GO:0090493.def: The directed movement of catecholamine into a cell.

GO:0090494.name: dopamine uptake
GO:0090494.def: The directed movement of dopamine into a cell.

GO:0090496.name: mesenchyme migration involved in limb bud formation
GO:0090496.def: The migration of mesenchymal tissue that contributes to the formation of a limb bud.

GO:0090497.name: mesenchymal cell migration
GO:0090497.def: The orderly movement of a mesenchymal cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism.

GO:0090513.name: L-histidine transmembrane import into vacuole
GO:0090513.def: The directed movement of L-histidine into the vacuole across the vacuolar membrane.

GO:0090515.name: L-glutamate transmembrane import into vacuole
GO:0090515.def: The directed movement of L-glutamate into the vacuole across the vacuolar membrane.

GO:0090521.name: podocyte cell migration
GO:0090521.def: The orderly movement of a podocyte from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism or multicellular structure. A podocyte is a specialized kidney epithelial cell.

GO:0090594.name: inflammatory response to wounding
GO:0090594.def: The immediate defensive reaction by vertebrate tissue to injury caused by chemical or physical agents.

GO:0090596.name: sensory organ morphogenesis
GO:0090596.def: Morphogenesis of a sensory organ. A sensory organ is defined as a tissue or set of tissues that work together to receive and transmit signals from external or internal stimuli. Morphogenesis is the process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

GO:0090598.name: male anatomical structure morphogenesis
GO:0090598.def: The processes by which anatomical structures that are only present in the male organism are generated and organized.

GO:0090634.name: microglial cell mediated cytotoxicity
GO:0090634.def: The directed killing of a target cell by a microglial cell.

GO:0090685.name: RNA localization to nucleus
GO:0090685.def: A macromolecular localization process in which RNA is transported to and maintained in a location within the nucleus.

GO:0090713.name: immunological memory process
GO:0090713.def: Any process of the immune system that can contribute to the formation of immunological memory or an immune response based upon activation of immunological memory.

GO:0090715.name: immunological memory formation process
GO:0090715.def: Any immunological memory process that can contribute to the formation of immunological memory.

GO:0090741.name: pigment granule membrane
GO:0090741.def: Any membrane that is part of a pigment granule.

GO:0095500.name: acetylcholine receptor signaling pathway
GO:0095500.def: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of an acetylcholine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.

GO:0097014.name: ciliary plasm
GO:0097014.def: All of the contents of a cilium, excluding the plasma membrane surrounding the cilium.

GO:0097026.name: dendritic cell dendrite assembly
GO:0097026.def: Formation of dendrites, branched cellular projections (or cytoplasmic extension) that are extended from the surface of a dendritic immune cell, and which enable the cell to sample luminal pathogens and increase the surface area for antigen presentation to T cells.

GO:0097028.name: dendritic cell differentiation
GO:0097028.def: The process in which a precursor cell type acquires the specialized features of a dendritic cell. A dendritic cell is a leukocyte of dendritic lineage specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation.

GO:0097029.name: mature conventional dendritic cell differentiation
GO:0097029.def: The process in which antigen-activated dendritic cells acquire the specialized features of a mature conventional dendritic cell. Mature conventional dendritic cells upregulate the surface expression of MHC molecules, chemokine receptors and adhesion molecules, and increase the number of dendrites (cytoplasmic protrusions) in preparation for migration to lymphoid organs where they present antigen to T cells.

GO:0097048.name: dendritic cell apoptotic process
GO:0097048.def: Any apoptotic process in a dendritic cell, a cell of hematopoietic origin, typically resident in particular tissues, specialized in the uptake, processing, and transport of antigens to lymph nodes for the purpose of stimulating an immune response via T cell activation.

GO:0097049.name: motor neuron apoptotic process
GO:0097049.def: Any apoptotic process in a motor neuron, an efferent neuron that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes movement.

GO:0097050.name: type B pancreatic cell apoptotic process
GO:0097050.def: Any apoptotic process in a type B pancreatic cell, a cell located towards center of the islets of Langerhans that secretes insulin.

GO:0097054.name: L-glutamate biosynthetic process
GO:0097054.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of L-glutamate, the L enantiomer anion of 2-aminopentanedioic acid.

GO:0097060.name: synaptic membrane
GO:0097060.def: A specialized area of membrane on either the presynaptic or the postsynaptic side of a synapse, the junction between a nerve fiber of one neuron and another neuron or muscle fiber or glial cell.

GO:0097084.name: vascular associated smooth muscle cell development
GO:0097084.def: The process aimed at the progression of a vascular smooth muscle cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. A vascular smooth muscle cell is a non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the blood vessels.

GO:0097086.name: amniotic stem cell differentiation
GO:0097086.def: The process whereby a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of an amniotic stem cell. An amniotic stem cell is a mesenchymal stem cell extracted from amniotic fluid. Amniotic stem cells are able to differentiate into various tissue types such as skin, cartilage, cardiac tissue, nerves, muscle, and bone.

GO:0097094.name: craniofacial suture morphogenesis
GO:0097094.def: The process in which any suture between cranial and/or facial bones is generated and organized.

GO:0097096.name: facial suture morphogenesis
GO:0097096.def: The process in which any suture between facial bones is generated and organized.

GO:0097104.name: postsynaptic membrane assembly
GO:0097104.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a postsynaptic membrane, a specialized area of membrane facing the presynaptic membrane on the tip of the nerve ending and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft).

GO:0097120.name: receptor localization to synapse
GO:0097120.def: Any process in which a receptor is transported to, and/or maintained at the synapse, the junction between a nerve fiber of one neuron and another neuron or muscle fiber or glial cell.

GO:0097152.name: mesenchymal cell apoptotic process
GO:0097152.def: Any apoptotic process in a mesenchymal cell. A mesenchymal cell is a loosely associated cell that is part of the connective tissue in an organism. Mesenchymal cells give rise to more mature connective tissue cell types.

GO:0097154.name: GABAergic neuron differentiation
GO:0097154.def: The process in which a neuroblast acquires the specialized structural and functional features of a GABAergic neuron.

GO:0097164.name: ammonium ion metabolic process
GO:0097164.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving the ammonium ion.

GO:0097186.name: amelogenesis
GO:0097186.def: The process whose specific outcome is the formation of tooth enamel, occurring in two stages: secretory stage and maturation stage.

GO:0097187.name: dentinogenesis
GO:0097187.def: The process whose specific outcome is the formation of dentin, the mineralized tissue that constitutes the major bulk of teeth. Dentin may be one of three types: primary dentin, secondary dentin, and tertiary dentin.

GO:0097190.name: apoptotic signaling pathway
GO:0097190.def: The series of molecular signals which triggers the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with reception of a signal, and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.
synonym: induction of apoptosis by extracellular signals

GO:0097191.name: extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway
GO:0097191.def: The series of molecular signals in which a signal is conveyed from the cell surface to trigger the apoptotic death of a cell. The pathway starts with either a ligand binding to a cell surface receptor, or a ligand being withdrawn from a cell surface receptor (e.g. in the case of signaling by dependence receptors), and ends when the execution phase of apoptosis is triggered.
synonym: extrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway in presence of ligand

GO:0097194.name: execution phase of apoptosis
GO:0097194.def: A stage of the apoptotic process that starts with the controlled breakdown of the cell through the action of effector caspases or other effector molecules (e.g. cathepsins, calpains etc.). Key steps of the execution phase are rounding-up of the cell, retraction of pseudopodes, reduction of cellular volume (pyknosis), chromatin condensation, nuclear fragmentation (karyorrhexis), plasma membrane blebbing and fragmentation of the cell into apoptotic bodies. When the execution phase is completed, the cell has died.

GO:0097205.name: renal filtration
GO:0097205.def: A renal system process in which fluid circulating through the body is filtered through a barrier system.

GO:0097212.name: lysosomal membrane organization
GO:0097212.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a lysosomal membrane. A lysosomal membrane is the lipid bilayer surrounding the lysosome and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm.

GO:0097232.name: lamellar body membrane
GO:0097232.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a lamellar body. A lamellar body is a membrane-bounded organelle, specialized for the storage and secretion of various substances (surfactant phospholipids, glycoproteins and acid phosphates) which are arranged in the form of tightly packed, concentric, membrane sheets or lamellae. Has some similar properties to, but is distinct from, a lysosome.

GO:0097237.name: cellular response to toxic substance
GO:0097237.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a toxic stimulus.

GO:0097252.name: oligodendrocyte apoptotic process
GO:0097252.def: Any apoptotic process in an oligodendrocyte. Oligodendrocytes belong to a class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system, where they form the insulating myelin sheath of axons.

GO:0097254.name: renal tubular secretion
GO:0097254.def: The elimination of substances from peritubular capillaries (or surrounding hemolymph in invertebrates) into the renal tubules to be incorporated subsequently into the urine. Substances that are secreted include organic anions, ammonia, potassium and drugs.

GO:0097272.name: ammonium homeostasis
GO:0097272.def: Any biological process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of ammonium.

GO:0097275.name: intracellular ammonium homeostasis
GO:0097275.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of ammonium within a cell.

GO:0097283.name: keratinocyte apoptotic process
GO:0097283.def: Any apoptotic process in a keratinocyte. A keratinocyte is an epidermal cell which synthesizes keratin and undergoes a characteristic change as it moves upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin.

GO:0097284.name: hepatocyte apoptotic process
GO:0097284.def: Any apoptotic process in a hepatocyte, the main structural component of the liver.

GO:0097305.name: response to alcohol
GO:0097305.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an alcohol stimulus.
GO:0097305.synonym: process resulting in tolerance to alcohol

GO:0097306.name: cellular response to alcohol
GO:0097306.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an alcohol stimulus.

GO:0097324.name: melanocyte migration
GO:0097324.def: The orderly movement of melanocytes from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism. A melanocyte is a pigment cell derived from the neural crest. It contains melanin-filled pigment granules, which give a brown to black appearance.

GO:0097355.name: protein localization to heterochromatin
GO:0097355.def: Any process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained at, a part of a chromosome that is organized into heterochromatin.

GO:0097360.name: chorionic trophoblast cell proliferation
GO:0097360.def: The multiplication or reproduction of chorionic trophoblast cells, resulting in the expansion of their population.

GO:0097386.name: glial cell projection
GO:0097386.def: A prolongation or process extending from a glial cell.

GO:0097402.name: neuroblast migration
GO:0097402.def: The orderly movement of a neuroblast from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism or multicellular structure. A neuroblast is any cell that will divide and give rise to a neuron.

GO:0097410.name: hippocampal interneuron differentiation
GO:0097410.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a hippocampal interneuron.

GO:0097427.name: microtubule bundle
GO:0097427.def: An arrangement of closely apposed microtubules running parallel to each other.

GO:0097432.name: hippocampal pyramidal neuron differentiation
GO:0097432.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a hippocampal pyramidal neuron, a pyramidal cell of the hippocampus.

GO:0097435.name: supramolecular fiber organization
GO:0097435.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a supramolecular fiber, a polymer consisting of an indefinite number of protein or protein complex subunits that have polymerised to form a fiber-shaped structure.

GO:0097447.name: dendritic tree
GO:0097447.def: The entire complement of dendrites for a neuron, consisting of each primary dendrite and all its branches.

GO:0097449.name: astrocyte projection
GO:0097449.def: A prolongation or process extending from the soma of an astrocyte and wrapping around neurons.

GO:0097454.name: Schwann cell microvillus
GO:0097454.def: Small finger-like extension of a Schwann cell that contacts the nodal membrane.

GO:0097457.name: hippocampal mossy fiber
GO:0097457.def: An axon of a hippocampal granule cell, including dentate gyrus granule cell and CA3 granule cell, characterized by expansions (mossy fiber expansions) giving the fibers a mossy appearance. These unmyelinated axons were first described by Ramon y Cajal.

GO:0097473.name: retinal rod cell apoptotic process
GO:0097473.def: Any apoptotic process in a retinal rod cell, one of the two photoreceptor cell types of the vertebrate retina.

GO:0097474.name: retinal cone cell apoptotic process
GO:0097474.def: Any apoptotic process in a retinal cone cell, one of the two photoreceptor cell types of the vertebrate retina.

GO:0097475.name: motor neuron migration
GO:0097475.def: The orderly movement of a motor neuron from one site to another. A motor neuron is an efferent neuron that passes from the central nervous system or a ganglion toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes movement.

GO:0097476.name: spinal cord motor neuron migration
GO:0097476.def: The orderly movement of a spinal cord motor neuron from one site to another. A spinal cord motor neuron is a motor neuron that passes from the spinal cord toward or to a muscle and conducts an impulse that causes movement.

GO:0097477.name: lateral motor column neuron migration
GO:0097477.def: The orderly movement of a lateral motor column neuron from one site to another. A lateral motor column neuron is a motor neuron that is generated only on limb levels and send axons into the limb mesenchyme.

GO:0097499.name: protein localization to non-motile cilium
GO:0097499.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within a non-motile cilium.
GO:0097499.synonym: protein localization to nonmotile primary cilium

GO:0097511.name: dendritic cell dendrite
GO:0097511.def: A branched cellular projection (or cytoplasmic extension) that is extended from the surface of a dendritic immune cell, and which enables the cell to sample luminal pathogens and increase the surface area for antigen presentation to T cells.

GO:0097512.name: cardiac myofibril
GO:0097512.def: A cardiac myofibril is a myofibril specific to cardiac muscle cells.

GO:0097524.name: sperm plasma membrane
GO:0097524.def: A plasma membrane that is part of a sperm cell.

GO:0097529.name: myeloid leukocyte migration
GO:0097529.def: The movement of a myeloid leukocyte within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0097530.name: granulocyte migration
GO:0097530.def: The movement of a granulocyte within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0097531.name: mast cell migration
GO:0097531.def: The movement of a mast cell within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:0097534.name: lymphoid lineage cell migration
GO:0097534.def: The orderly movement of a lymphoid lineage cell from one site to another. A lymphoid lineage cell, also called a lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell, is a progenitor cell restricted to the lymphoid lineage.
GO:0097534.synonym: lymphoid lineage restricted progenitor cell migration

GO:0097536.name: thymus epithelium morphogenesis
GO:0097536.def: The process in which the thymus epithelium is generated and organized.

GO:0097540.name: axonemal central pair
GO:0097540.def: Part of the axoneme consisting of the inner two microtubule doublets of the 9+2 axoneme occurring in most motile cilia.

GO:0097545.name: axonemal doublet microtubule
GO:0097545.def: A cellular anatomical entity that is part of an axoneme consisting of a doublet microtubule.

GO:0097553.name: calcium ion transmembrane import into cytosol
GO:0097553.def: A process in which a calcium ion is transported from one side of a membrane to the other into the cytosol by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0097576.name: vacuole fusion
GO:0097576.def: Merging of two or more vacuoles, or of vacuoles and vesicles within a cell to form a single larger vacuole.

GO:0097623.name: potassium ion export across plasma membrane
GO:0097623.def: The directed movement of potassium ions from inside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the extracellular region.

GO:0097628.name: distal tip cell migration
GO:0097628.def: The orderly movement of a distal tip cell.

GO:0097642.name: calcitonin family receptor activity
GO:0097642.def: Combining with any member of the calcitonin family (e.g. adrenomedullin, adrenomedullin 2 (intermedin), amylin, calcitonin and calcitonin gene-related peptides (CGRPs)) to initiate a change in cell activity.

GO:0097644.name: calcitonin family binding
GO:0097644.def: Binding to a member of the calcitonin family (e.g. adrenomedullin, adrenomedullin 2 (intermedin), amylin, calcitonin and calcitonin gene-related peptides (CGRPs)).

GO:0097648.name: G protein-coupled receptor complex
GO:0097648.def: A protein complex that contains G protein-coupled receptors.

GO:0097649.name: A axonemal microtubule
GO:0097649.def: A complete microtubule with 13 protofilaments that fuses with an incomplete microtubule called B tubule (containing 10 protofilaments only) to form an axonemal outer doublet. Inner and outer dynein arms, as well as the radial spoke, are attached to the A tubule.

GO:0097650.name: B axonemal microtubule
GO:0097650.def: An incomplete microtubule containing 10 protofilaments that fuses with a complete microtubule called A tubule (containing 13 protofilaments) to form an axonemal outer doublet.

GO:0097708.name: intracellular vesicle
GO:0097708.def: Any vesicle that is part of the intracellular region.

GO:0097711.name: ciliary basal body-plasma membrane docking
GO:0097711.def: The docking of a cytosolic centriole/basal body to the plasma membrane via the ciliary transition fibers. In some species this may happen via an intermediate step, by first docking to the ciliary vesicle via the ciliary transition fibers. The basal body-ciliary vesicle then relocates to the plasma membrane, followed by the ciliary vesicle fusing with the plasma membrane, effectively attaching the basal body to the plasma membrane.
synonym: anchoring of the basal body to the plasma membrane

GO:0097712.name: vesicle targeting, trans-Golgi to periciliary membrane compartment
GO:0097712.def: The process in which vesicles formed at the trans-Golgi network are directed to the plasma membrane surrounding the base of the cilium, including the ciliary pocket, mediated by molecules at the vesicle membrane and target membrane surfaces.

GO:0097719.name: neural tissue regeneration
GO:0097719.def: The regrowth of neural tissue following its loss or destruction.

GO:0097722.name: sperm motility
GO:0097722.def: Any process involved in the controlled movement of a sperm cell.

GO:0097729.name: 9+2 motile cilium
GO:0097729.def: A motile cilium where the axoneme has a ring of nine outer microtubule doublets plus two central microtubules (and is therefore called a 9+2 axoneme).

GO:0097730.name: non-motile cilium
GO:0097730.def: A cilium which may have a variable array of axonemal microtubules but does not contain molecular motors.

GO:0097734.name: extracellular exosome biogenesis
GO:0097734.def: The assembly and secretion of an extracellular exosome, a membrane-bounded vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane.

GO:0097742.name: de novo centriole assembly
GO:0097742.def: Centriole assembly in which a centriole arises de novo, rather than by replication from an existing centriole. This process may occur via different mechanisms. Examples include the deuterosome pathway in multicilated epithelial animal cells and formation of centrioles during parthenogenesis in some insects.
synonym: de novo ciliary basal body assembly

GO:0098520.name: excitatory neuromuscular junction
GO:0098520.def: The junction between the axon of a motor neuron and a muscle fiber. In response to the arrival of action potentials, the presynaptic button releases molecules of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These diffuse across the cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to a post-synaptic potential responsible for muscle contraction.

GO:0098522.name: neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscle fiber
GO:0098522.def: A neuromuscular junction in which the target muscle cell is a skeletal muscle fiber.

GO:0098523.name: neuromuscular junction of myotube
GO:0098523.def: A neuromuscular junction in which the target muscle cell is a myotube.

GO:0098524.name: neuromuscular junction of somatic muscle myotube
GO:0098524.def: A neuromuscular junction in which the target muscle cell is a somatic muscle myotube, such as an arthropod somatic muscle cell.

GO:0098525.name: excitatory neuromuscular junction of somatic myotube
GO:0098525.def: A neuromuscular junction that functions in the excitation of somatic muscle myotubes, such as an arthropod somatic muscle cells.

GO:0098527.name: neuromuscular junction of somatic muscle
GO:0098527.def: A neuromuscular junction in which the target muscle cell is a somatic muscle cell, such as those found in nematodes and arthropods.

GO:0098528.name: skeletal muscle fiber differentiation
GO:0098528.def: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a skeletal muscle fiber cell. Skeletal muscle fiber differentiation starts with myoblast fusion and the appearance of specific cell markers (this is the cell development step). Then individual skeletal muscle fibers fuse to form bigger myotubes and start to contract.

GO:0098529.name: neuromuscular junction development, skeletal muscle fiber
GO:0098529.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a neuromuscular junction that targets a skeletal muscle fiber.

GO:0098534.name: centriole assembly
GO:0098534.def: A cellular process that results in the assembly of one or more centrioles.

GO:0098535.name: de novo centriole assembly involved in multi-ciliated epithelial cell differentiation
GO:0098535.def: Centriole assembly in which a centriole arises de novo by a process involving an electron-dense structure known as a deuterosome, rather than by duplication of an existing centriole, and occurring as part of multi-ciliated epithelial cell differentiation.
synonym: de novo centriole assembly via deuterosome

GO:0098536.name: deuterosome
GO:0098536.def: A spherical, electron dense, cytoplasmic structure that is involved in de novo assembly of centrioles.

GO:0098537.name: obsolete lobed nucleus
GO:0098537.def: OBSOLETE. Nucleus with two or more lobes connected by a thin filament that contains no internal chromatin. Examples include the nuclei of mature basophils, eosinophils and neutrophils in mice and humans.

GO:0098542.name: defense response to other organism
GO:0098542.def: Reactions triggered in response to the presence of another organism that act to protect the cell or organism from damage caused by that organism.
synonym: defence response to pathogen, incompatible interaction

GO:0098544.name: maintenance of protein complex location
GO:0098544.def: Any process in which a protein complex is maintained in a location and prevented from moving elsewhere. These include sequestration, stabilization to prevent transport elsewhere and the active retrieval of protein complexes that move away.

GO:0098545.name: maintenance of protein complex location in cytoplasm
GO:0098545.def: Any process in which a protein complex is maintained in a specific location within the cytoplasm and is prevented from moving elsewhere.

GO:0098588.name: bounding membrane of organelle
GO:0098588.def: The lipid bilayer that forms the outer-most layer of an organelle.

GO:0098590.name: plasma membrane region
GO:0098590.def: A membrane that is a (regional) part of the plasma membrane.

GO:0098594.name: mucin granule
GO:0098594.def: A secretory granule that contains mucin.

GO:0098609.name: cell-cell adhesion
GO:0098609.def: The attachment of one cell to another cell via adhesion molecules.

GO:0098631.name: cell adhesion mediator activity
GO:0098631.def: The binding by a cell-adhesion protein on a cell surface to an adhesion molecule on another cell surface or an external substrate, to mediate adhesion of the cell to the external substrate or to another cell.
synonym: protein binding involved in cell adhesion

GO:0098632.name: cell-cell adhesion mediator activity
GO:0098632.def: The binding by a cell-adhesion protein on the cell surface to an extracellular matrix component, to mediate adhesion of the cell to another cell.
synonym: protein binding involved in cell-cell adhesion

GO:0098635.name: protein complex involved in cell-cell adhesion
GO:0098635.def: Any protein complex that is capable of carrying out some part of the process of cell-cell adhesion.

GO:0098636.name: protein complex involved in cell adhesion
GO:0098636.def: Any protein complex that is capable of carrying out some part of the process of cell adhesion to the cell matrix or to another cell.

GO:0098641.name: cadherin binding involved in cell-cell adhesion
GO:0098641.def: Any cadherin binding that occurs as part of the process of cell-cell adhesion.

GO:0098642.name: network-forming collagen trimer
GO:0098642.def: A collagen trimer that forms networks.

GO:0098643.name: banded collagen fibril
GO:0098643.def: A supramolecular assembly of fibrillar collagen complexes in the form of a long fiber (fibril) with transverse striations (bands).

GO:0098644.name: complex of collagen trimers
GO:0098644.def: A complex of collagen trimers such as a fibril or collagen network.

GO:0098645.name: collagen network
GO:0098645.def: A supramolecular complex that consists of collagen triple helices associated to form a network.

GO:0098655.name: monoatomic cation transmembrane transport
GO:0098655.def: The process in which a monoatomic cation is transported across a membrane. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are positively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.
synonym: ATP hydrolysis coupled cation transmembrane transport

GO:0098657.name: import into cell
GO:0098657.def: The directed movement of some substance from outside of a cell into a cell. This may occur via transport across the plasma membrane or via endocytosis.

GO:0098658.name: inorganic anion import across plasma membrane
GO:0098658.def: The directed movement of inorganic anions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098659.name: inorganic cation import across plasma membrane
GO:0098659.def: The directed movement of inorganic cations from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098660.name: inorganic ion transmembrane transport
GO:0098660.def: The process in which an inorganic ion is transported across a membrane.

GO:0098661.name: inorganic anion transmembrane transport
GO:0098661.def: The process in which an inorganic anion is transported across a membrane.

GO:0098662.name: inorganic cation transmembrane transport
GO:0098662.def: A process in which an inorganic cation is transported from one side of a membrane to the other by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

GO:0098664.name: G protein-coupled serotonin receptor signaling pathway
GO:0098664.def: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of a G protein-coupled serotonin receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.
GO:0098664.synonym: G-protein coupled serotonin receptor signaling pathway

GO:0098665.name: serotonin receptor complex
GO:0098665.def: A protein complex that is capable of serotonin receptor activity.

GO:0098666.name: G protein-coupled serotonin receptor complex
GO:0098666.def: A protein complex that is capable of G protein-coupled serotonin receptor activity.

GO:0098690.name: glycinergic synapse
GO:0098690.def: A synapse that uses glycine as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0098691.name: dopaminergic synapse
GO:0098691.def: A synapse that uses dopamine as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0098693.name: regulation of synaptic vesicle cycle
GO:0098693.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the synaptic vesicle cycle.

GO:0098703.name: calcium ion import across plasma membrane
GO:0098703.def: The directed movement of calcium ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098704.name: carbohydrate import across plasma membrane
GO:0098704.def: The directed movement of a carbohydrate from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098708.name: D-glucose import across plasma membrane
GO:0098708.def: The directed movement of D-glucose from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098711.name: iron ion import across plasma membrane
GO:0098711.def: The directed movement of iron ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.
synonym: ferrous iron import across plasma membrane

GO:0098712.name: L-glutamate import across plasma membrane
GO:0098712.def: The directed movement of L-glutamate from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098719.name: sodium ion import across plasma membrane
GO:0098719.def: The directed movement of sodium ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098722.name: asymmetric stem cell division
GO:0098722.def: Division of a stem cell during which it retains its identity and buds off a daughter cell with a new identity.

GO:0098723.name: skeletal muscle myofibril
GO:0098723.def: A myofibril of a skeletal muscle fiber.

GO:0098727.name: maintenance of cell number
GO:0098727.def: Any process by which the numbers of cells of a particular type or in a tissue are maintained.

GO:0098728.name: germline stem cell asymmetric division
GO:0098728.def: The self-renewing division of a germline stem cell, to produce a daughter stem cell and a daughter germ cell which will divide to form one or more gametes.

GO:0098731.name: skeletal muscle satellite stem cell maintenance involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
GO:0098731.def: Any process by which the number of skeletal muscle satellite stem cells in a skeletal muscle is maintained during skeletal muscle regeneration. There are at least two mechanisms by which this is achieved. Skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division ensures satellite stem cell numbers are kept constant. Symmetric division of these cells amplifies the number of skeletal muscle satellite stem cells.

GO:0098739.name: import across plasma membrane
GO:0098739.def: The directed movement of some substance from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0098749.name: cerebellar neuron development
GO:0098749.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a cerebellar neuron over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0098751.name: bone cell development
GO:0098751.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a bone cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.

GO:0098754.name: detoxification
GO:0098754.def: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of a toxic substance. These may include transport of the toxic substance away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of the toxic substance.

GO:0098771.name: inorganic ion homeostasis
GO:0098771.def: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of inorganic ions within an organism or cell.

GO:0098773.name: skin epidermis development
GO:0098773.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the skin epidermis over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0098793.name: presynapse
GO:0098793.def: The part of a synapse that is part of the presynaptic cell.

GO:0098794.name: postsynapse
GO:0098794.def: The part of a synapse that is part of the post-synaptic cell.

GO:0098796.name: membrane protein complex
GO:0098796.def: Any protein complex that is part of a membrane.

GO:0098797.name: plasma membrane protein complex
GO:0098797.def: Any protein complex that is part of the plasma membrane.

GO:0098801.name: regulation of renal system process
GO:0098801.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a system process, a multicellular organismal process carried out by the renal system.

GO:0098802.name: plasma membrane signaling receptor complex
GO:0098802.def: Any protein complex that is part of the plasma membrane and which functions as a signaling receptor.

GO:0098804.name: non-motile cilium membrane
GO:0098804.def: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding a non-motile cilium.

GO:0098813.name: nuclear chromosome segregation
GO:0098813.def: The process in which genetic material, in the form of nuclear chromosomes, is organized into specific structures and then physically separated and apportioned to two or more sets. Nuclear chromosome segregation begins with the condensation of chromosomes, includes chromosome separation, and ends when chromosomes have completed movement to the spindle poles.

GO:0098815.name: modulation of excitatory postsynaptic potential
GO:0098815.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of excitatory postsynaptic potential (EPSP). EPSP is a process that leads to a temporary increase in postsynaptic potential due to the flow of positively charged ions into the postsynaptic cell. The flow of ions that causes an EPSP is an excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) and makes it easier for the neuron to fire an action potential.

GO:0098840.name: protein transport along microtubule
GO:0098840.def: The directed movement of a protein along a microtubule, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0098852.name: lytic vacuole membrane
GO:0098852.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a lytic vacuole and separating its contents from the cytoplasm of the cell.

GO:0098858.name: actin-based cell projection
GO:0098858.def: A cell projection supported by an assembly of actin filaments, and which lacks microtubules.

GO:0098862.name: cluster of actin-based cell projections
GO:0098862.def: A cell part consisting of multiple, closely packed actin-based cell projections.

GO:0098867.name: intramembranous bone growth
GO:0098867.def: The increase in size or mass of an intramembranous bone that contributes to the shaping of the bone.

GO:0098868.name: bone growth
GO:0098868.def: The increase in size or mass of a bone that contributes to the shaping of that bone.

GO:0098871.name: postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton
GO:0098871.def: The actin cytoskeleton that is part of a postsynapse.

GO:0098876.name: vesicle-mediated transport to the plasma membrane
GO:0098876.def: The directed movement of substances to the plasma membrane in transport vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane by exocytosis.

GO:0098877.name: neurotransmitter receptor transport to plasma membrane
GO:0098877.def: The directed movement of neurotransmitter receptor to the plasma membrane in transport vesicles.

GO:0098878.name: neurotransmitter receptor complex
GO:0098878.def: Any protein complex that is capable of functioning as a neurotransmitter receptor.

GO:0098883.name: synapse pruning
GO:0098883.def: A cellular process that results in the controlled breakdown of synapse. After it starts the process is continuous until the synapse has disappeared.

GO:0098900.name: regulation of action potential
GO:0098900.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

GO:0098901.name: regulation of cardiac muscle cell action potential
GO:0098901.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a cardiac muscle cell. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

GO:0098904.name: regulation of AV node cell action potential
GO:0098904.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in an atrioventricular node myocyte. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.
synonym: regulation of atrioventricular node cardiac muscle cell action potential
regulation of AV node cardiac muscle cell action potential

GO:0098905.name: regulation of bundle of His cell action potential
GO:0098905.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a cardiac muscle cell of the bundle of His. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.
GO:0098905.synonym: regulation of bundle of His cardiac muscle cell action potential

GO:0098906.name: regulation of Purkinje myocyte action potential
GO:0098906.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a Purkinje myocyte. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

GO:0098907.name: regulation of SA node cell action potential
GO:0098907.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in an SA node cardiac myocyte. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.
synonym: regulation of SA node cardiac muscle cell action potential
regulation of SAN cardiac muscle cell action potential
regulation of sinoatrial node cardiac muscle cell action potential
regulation of sinus node cardiac muscle cell action potential

GO:0098908.name: regulation of neuronal action potential
GO:0098908.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a neuron. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

GO:0098909.name: regulation of cardiac muscle cell action potential involved in regulation of contraction
GO:0098909.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a cardiac muscle cell contributing to the regulation of its contraction.

GO:0098910.name: regulation of atrial cardiac muscle cell action potential
GO:0098910.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in an atrial cardiac muscle cell contributing to the regulation of its contraction. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

GO:0098911.name: regulation of ventricular cardiac muscle cell action potential
GO:0098911.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination in a ventricular cardiac muscle cell contributing to the regulation of its contraction. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

GO:0098916.name: anterograde trans-synaptic signaling
GO:0098916.def: Cell-cell signaling from pre to post-synapse, across the synaptic cleft.

GO:0098917.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling
GO:0098917.def: Cell-cell signaling from post to pre-synapse, across the synaptic cleft.

GO:0098920.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by lipid
GO:0098920.def: Cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by a lipid ligand.

GO:0098923.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by soluble gas
GO:0098923.def: Cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by an soluble gas ligand.

GO:0098924.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by nitric oxide
GO:0098924.def: Cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by nitric oxide.

GO:0098925.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by nitric oxide, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0098925.def: Modulation of synaptic transmission by cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by nitric oxide.

GO:0098926.name: postsynaptic signal transduction
GO:0098926.def: Signal transduction in which the initial step occurs in a postsynapse.

GO:0098928.name: presynaptic signal transduction
GO:0098928.def: Signal transduction in which the initial step occurs in a presynapse.

GO:0098930.name: axonal transport
GO:0098930.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in axons.

GO:0098934.name: retrograde dendritic transport
GO:0098934.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in a dendrite from the postsynapse towards the cell body.

GO:0098935.name: dendritic transport
GO:0098935.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules in dendrites.

GO:0098937.name: anterograde dendritic transport
GO:0098937.def: The directed movement of organelles or molecules along microtubules from the cell body toward the postsynapse in dendrites.

GO:0098940.name: anterograde trans-synaptic signaling by nitric oxide
GO:0098940.def: Cell-cell signaling from presynapse to postynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by nitric oxide.

GO:0098960.name: postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptor activity
GO:0098960.def: Neurotransmitter receptor activity occurring in the postsynaptic membrane during synaptic transmission.
GO:0098960.synonym: neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in chemical synaptic transmission

GO:0098961.name: dendritic transport of ribonucleoprotein complex
GO:0098961.def: The directed movement of a ribonucleoprotein complex along microtubules in nerve cell dendrites.

GO:0098962.name: regulation of postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptor activity
GO:0098962.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in synaptic transmission. Modulation may be via an effect on ligand affinity, or effector function such as ion selectivity or pore opening/closing in ionotropic receptors.

GO:0098967.name: exocytic insertion of neurotransmitter receptor to postsynaptic membrane
GO:0098967.def: The exocytic fusion of neurotransmitter receptor containing vesicles with the postsynaptic membrane resulting in the integration of NT receptors, enabling them to participate in neurotransmitter reception. This process includes tethering and docking steps that prepare vesicles for fusion.

GO:0098969.name: neurotransmitter receptor transport to postsynaptic membrane
GO:0098969.def: The directed movement of neurotransmitter receptor to the postsynaptic membrane in transport vesicles.

GO:0098971.name: anterograde dendritic transport of neurotransmitter receptor complex
GO:0098971.def: The directed movement of a neurotransmitter receptor complex along microtubules in nerve cell dendrites towards the postsynapse.

GO:0098974.name: postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton organization
GO:0098974.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins in the postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton.

GO:0098975.name: postsynapse of neuromuscular junction
GO:0098975.def: The postsynapse of a neuromuscular junction. In vertebrate muscles this includes the motor end-plate, consisting of postjunctional folds of the sarcolemma.

GO:0098976.name: excitatory chemical synaptic transmission
GO:0098976.def: Synaptic transmission that results in an excitatory postsynaptic potential.

GO:0098978.name: glutamatergic synapse
GO:0098978.def: A synapse that uses glutamate as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0098981.name: cholinergic synapse
GO:0098981.def: A synapse that uses acetylcholine as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0098982.name: GABA-ergic synapse
GO:0098982.def: A synapse that uses GABA as a neurotransmitter. These synapses are typically inhibitory.

GO:0098988.name: G protein-coupled glutamate receptor activity
GO:0098988.def: Combining with glutamate and transmitting a signal from one side of the membrane to the other by activating an associated G-protein, initiating a change in cell activity.

GO:0098991.name: kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
GO:0098991.def: The series of molecular signals initiated by glutamate binding to an kainate-selective glutamate receptor on the surface of the target cell, followed by the movement of ions through a channel in the receptor complex, ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

GO:0098992.name: neuronal dense core vesicle
GO:0098992.def: A dense core vesicle (granule) that is part of a neuron. These vesicles typically contain neuropeptides. They can be found in all parts of neurons, including the soma, dendrites, axonal swellings (varicosities) and synaptic terminals.

GO:0099003.name: vesicle-mediated transport in synapse
GO:0099003.def: Any vesicle-mediated transport that occurs in a synapse.

GO:0099012.name: neuronal dense core vesicle membrane
GO:0099012.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding a neuronal dense core vesicle.

GO:0099014.name: neuronal dense core vesicle organization
GO:0099014.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a neuronal dense core vesicle.

GO:0099054.name: presynapse assembly
GO:0099054.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a presynapse.

GO:0099068.name: postsynapse assembly
GO:0099068.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a postsynapse.

GO:0099072.name: regulation of postsynaptic membrane neurotransmitter receptor levels
GO:0099072.def: Any process that regulates the the local concentration of neurotransmitter receptor at the postsynaptic membrane.

GO:0099080.name: supramolecular complex
GO:0099080.def: A cellular component that consists of an indeterminate number of proteins or macromolecular complexes, organized into a regular, higher-order structure such as a polymer, sheet, network or a fiber.

GO:0099082.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by neuropeptide
GO:0099082.def: Cell-cell signaling from postsynapse to presynapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by a neuropeptide.

GO:0099083.name: retrograde trans-synaptic signaling by neuropeptide, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099083.def: Modulation of synaptic transmission by cell-cell signaling across the synaptic cleft from postsynapse to presynapse, mediated by a neuropeptide.

GO:0099094.name: ligand-gated monoatomic cation channel activity
GO:0099094.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of an inorganic cation by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0099096.name: vestibular calyx terminal
GO:0099096.def: The giant, cup-shaped axon terminal of a vestibular afferent neuron, serving as a post-synaptic contact to a type I hair cell.

GO:0099098.name: microtubule polymerization based movement
GO:0099098.def: The movement of a cellular component as a result of microtubule polymerization.

GO:0099111.name: microtubule-based transport
GO:0099111.def: A microtubule-based process that results in the transport of organelles, other microtubules, or other cellular components. Examples include motor-driven movement along microtubules and movement driven by polymerization or depolymerization of microtubules.

GO:0099112.name: microtubule polymerization based protein transport
GO:0099112.def: The transport of a protein driven by polymerization of a microtubule to which it is attached.

GO:0099118.name: microtubule-based protein transport
GO:0099118.def: A microtubule-based process that results in the transport of proteins.

GO:0099123.name: somato-dendritic dopamine secretion
GO:0099123.def: The regulated release of dopamine from the somatodendritic compartment (cell body or dendrites) of a neuron.

GO:0099124.name: axonal dopamine secretion
GO:0099124.def: The regulated release of dopamine from an axon.

GO:0099140.name: presynaptic actin cytoskeleton organization
GO:0099140.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising actin filaments and their associated proteins in the presynaptic actin cytoskeleton.

GO:0099143.name: presynaptic actin cytoskeleton
GO:0099143.def: The actin cytoskeleton that is part of a presynapse.

GO:0099145.name: regulation of exocytic insertion of neurotransmitter receptor to postsynaptic membrane
GO:0099145.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of exocytic fusion of neurotransmitter receptor containing vesicles into the postsynaptic membrane.

GO:0099156.name: cell-cell signaling via exosome
GO:0099156.def: Cell-cell signaling in which the ligand is carried between cells by an exosome.

GO:0099157.name: trans-synaptic signaling via exosome
GO:0099157.def: Transynaptic signaling in which the ligand is carried across the synapse by an exosome.

GO:0099160.name: postsynaptic intermediate filament cytoskeleton
