GO:0099160.def: The intermediate filament cytoskeleton that is part of a postsynapse.

GO:0099163.name: synaptic signaling by nitric oxide
GO:0099163.def: Cell-cell signaling to or from a synapse, mediated by nitric oxide.

GO:0099170.name: postsynaptic modulation of chemical synaptic transmission
GO:0099170.def: Any process, acting in the postsynapse that results in modulation of chemical synaptic transmission.

GO:0099171.name: presynaptic modulation of chemical synaptic transmission
GO:0099171.def: Any process, acting in the presynapse that results in modulation of chemical synaptic transmission.

GO:0099172.name: presynapse organization
GO:0099172.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a presynapse.

GO:0099173.name: postsynapse organization
GO:0099173.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a postsynapse.

GO:0099174.name: regulation of presynapse organization
GO:0099174.def: Any process that modulates the physical form of a presynapse.
synonym: regulation of presynapse organization and biogenesis

GO:0099175.name: regulation of postsynapse organization
GO:0099175.def: Any process that modulates the physical form of a postsynapse.
synonym: regulation of postsynapse organization and biogenesis

GO:0099177.name: regulation of trans-synaptic signaling
GO:0099177.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of trans-synaptic signaling.

GO:0099182.name: presynaptic intermediate filament cytoskeleton
GO:0099182.def: The intermediate filament cytoskeleton that is part of a presynapse.

GO:0099185.name: postsynaptic intermediate filament cytoskeleton organization
GO:0099185.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprised of intermediate filament and their associated proteins in the postsynaptic cytoskeleton.

GO:0099187.name: presynaptic cytoskeleton organization
GO:0099187.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures and their associated proteins in the presynaptic cytoskeleton.

GO:0099188.name: postsynaptic cytoskeleton organization
GO:0099188.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures comprising cytoskeletal filaments and their associated proteins in the postsynaptic cytoskeleton.

GO:0099500.name: vesicle fusion to plasma membrane
GO:0099500.def: Fusion of the membrane of a vesicle with the plasma membrane, thereby releasing its contents into the extracellular space.

GO:0099501.name: exocytic vesicle membrane
GO:0099501.def: The lipid bilayer surrounding an exocytic vesicle.

GO:0099503.name: secretory vesicle
GO:0099503.def: A cytoplasmic, membrane bound vesicle that is capable of fusing to the plasma membrane to release its contents into the extracellular space.

GO:0099504.name: synaptic vesicle cycle
GO:0099504.def: A biological process in which synaptic vesicles are loaded with neurotransmitters, move to the active zone, exocytose and are then recycled via endocytosis, ultimately leading to reloading with neurotransmitters.

GO:0099512.name: supramolecular fiber
GO:0099512.def: A polymer consisting of an indefinite number of protein or protein complex subunits that have polymerised to form a fiber-shaped structure.

GO:0099513.name: polymeric cytoskeletal fiber
GO:0099513.def: A component of the cytoskeleton consisting of a homo or heteropolymeric fiber constructed from an indeterminate number of protein subunits.

GO:0099515.name: actin filament-based transport
GO:0099515.def: The transport of organelles or other particles from one location in the cell to another along actin filaments.

GO:0099518.name: vesicle cytoskeletal trafficking
GO:0099518.def: The directed movement of a vesicle along a cytoskeletal fiber such as a microtubule or and actin filament, mediated by motor proteins.

GO:0099519.name: dense core granule cytoskeletal transport
GO:0099519.def: The directed movement of dense core granules along cytoskeletal fibers, such as microtubules or actin filaments.

GO:0099522.name: cytosolic region
GO:0099522.def: Any (proper) part of the cytosol of a single cell of sufficient size to still be considered cytosol.

GO:0099523.name: presynaptic cytosol
GO:0099523.def: The region of the cytosol consisting of all cytosol that is part of the presynapse.

GO:0099524.name: postsynaptic cytosol
GO:0099524.def: The region of the cytosol consisting of all cytosol that is part of the postsynapse.

GO:0099528.name: G protein-coupled neurotransmitter receptor activity
GO:0099528.def: Combining with a neurotransmitter and transmitting the signal across the membrane by activating an associated G-protein; promotes the exchange of GDP for GTP on the alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein complex.

GO:0099529.name: neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential
GO:0099529.def: Neurotransmitter receptor activity occurring in the postsynaptic membrane that is involved in regulating postsynaptic membrane potential, either directly (ionotropic receptors) or indirectly (e.g. via GPCR activation of an ion channel).

GO:0099530.name: G protein-coupled receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential
GO:0099530.def: A G protein-coupled receptor activity occurring in the postsynaptic membrane that is part of a GPCR signaling pathway that positively regulates ion channel activity in the postsynaptic membrane.
GO:0099530.synonym: G-protein coupled receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential

GO:0099531.name: presynaptic process involved in chemical synaptic transmission
GO:0099531.def: The pathway leading to secretion of a neurotransmitter from the presynapse as part of synaptic transmission.

GO:0099536.name: synaptic signaling
GO:0099536.def: Cell-cell signaling to, from or within a synapse.

GO:0099537.name: trans-synaptic signaling
GO:0099537.def: Cell-cell signaling in either direction across the synaptic cleft.

GO:0099538.name: synaptic signaling via neuropeptide
GO:0099538.def: Cell-cell signaling to or from a synapse, mediated by a peptide.

GO:0099540.name: trans-synaptic signaling by neuropeptide
GO:0099540.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse mediated by a peptide ligand crossing the synaptic cleft.

GO:0099541.name: trans-synaptic signaling by lipid
GO:0099541.def: Cell-cell signaling from post to pre-synapse, across the synaptic cleft, mediated by a lipid.

GO:0099543.name: trans-synaptic signaling by soluble gas
GO:0099543.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse mediated by a soluble gas ligand crossing the synaptic cleft.

GO:0099546.name: protein catabolic process, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099546.def: Any protein degradation process, occurring at a presynapse, that regulates synaptic transmission.

GO:0099547.name: regulation of translation at synapse, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099547.def: Any process that modulates synaptic transmission by regulating translation occurring at the synapse.

GO:0099548.name: trans-synaptic signaling by nitric oxide
GO:0099548.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse mediated by nitric oxide.

GO:0099550.name: trans-synaptic signaling, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099550.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse, across the synaptic cleft, that modulates the synaptic transmission properties of the synapse.

GO:0099551.name: trans-synaptic signaling by neuropeptide, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099551.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse, via the vesicular release and reception of neuropeptide molecules, that modulates the synaptic transmission properties of the synapse.

GO:0099552.name: trans-synaptic signaling by lipid, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099552.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse, via the release and reception of lipid molecules, that modulates the synaptic transmission properties of the synapse.

GO:0099554.name: trans-synaptic signaling by soluble gas, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099554.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse, via the release and reception of gaseous molecules, that modulates the synaptic transmission properties of the synapse.

GO:0099555.name: trans-synaptic signaling by nitric oxide, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099555.def: Cell-cell signaling between presynapse and postsynapse, via the release and reception of nitric oxide molecules, that modulates the synaptic transmission properties of the synapse.

GO:0099565.name: chemical synaptic transmission, postsynaptic
GO:0099565.def: The part of synaptic transmission occurring in the post-synapse: a signal transduction pathway consisting of neurotransmitter receptor activation and its effects on postsynaptic membrane potential and the ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol.
GO:0099565.synonym: postsynaptic process involved in chemical synaptic transmission

GO:0099568.name: cytoplasmic region
GO:0099568.def: Any (proper) part of the cytoplasm of a single cell of sufficient size to still be considered cytoplasm.

GO:0099569.name: presynaptic cytoskeleton
GO:0099569.def: The portion of the cytoskeleton contained within the presynapse.

GO:0099571.name: postsynaptic cytoskeleton
GO:0099571.def: The portion of the cytoskeleton contained within the postsynapse.

GO:0099574.name: regulation of protein catabolic process at synapse, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099574.def: Any process that modulates synaptic transmission by regulating protein degradation at the synapse.

GO:0099575.name: regulation of protein catabolic process at presynapse, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099575.def: Any process that modulates synaptic transmission by regulating a catabolic process occurring at a presynapse.

GO:0099576.name: regulation of protein catabolic process at postsynapse, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099576.def: Any process that modulates synaptic transmission by regulating a catabolic process occurring at a postsynapse.

GO:0099577.name: regulation of translation at presynapse, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099577.def: Any process that modulates synaptic transmission by regulating translation occurring at the presynapse.

GO:0099578.name: regulation of translation at postsynapse, modulating synaptic transmission
GO:0099578.def: Any process that modulates synaptic transmission by regulating translation occurring at the postsynapse.

GO:0099579.name: G protein-coupled neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential
GO:0099579.def: A G protein-coupled neurotransmitter receptor activity, occurring in the postsynaptic membrane, involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential.
GO:0099579.synonym: G-protein coupled neurotransmitter receptor activity involved in regulation of postsynaptic membrane potential

GO:0099585.name: release of sequestered calcium ion into presynaptic cytosol
GO:0099585.def: The process in which calcium ions sequestered in the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus or mitochondria are released into the presynaptic cytosol.

GO:0099586.name: release of sequestered calcium ion into postsynaptic cytosol
GO:0099586.def: The process in which calcium ions sequestered in the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus or mitochondria are released into the postsynaptic cytosol.

GO:0099587.name: inorganic ion import across plasma membrane
GO:0099587.def: The directed movement of inorganic ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0099589.name: serotonin receptor activity
GO:0099589.def: Combining with the biogenic amine serotonin and transmitting a signal across a membrane by activating some effector activity. Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) is a neurotransmitter and hormone found in vertebrates and invertebrates.

GO:0099601.name: regulation of neurotransmitter receptor activity
GO:0099601.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neurotransmitter receptor activity. Modulation may be via an effect on ligand affinity, or effector function such as ion selectivity or pore opening/closing in ionotropic receptors.

GO:0099604.name: ligand-gated calcium channel activity
GO:0099604.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a calcium ions by a channel that opens when a specific ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

GO:0099612.name: protein localization to axon
GO:0099612.def: A process in which a protein is transported to or maintained in a location within an axon.

GO:0099632.name: protein transport within plasma membrane
GO:0099632.def: A process in which protein is transported from one region of the plasma membrane to another.

GO:0099637.name: neurotransmitter receptor transport
GO:0099637.def: The directed movement of neurotransmitter receptors.

GO:0099640.name: axo-dendritic protein transport
GO:0099640.def: The directed movement of proteins along microtubules in neuron projections.

GO:0099641.name: anterograde axonal protein transport
GO:0099641.def: The directed movement of proteins along microtubules from the cell body toward the cell periphery in nerve cell axons.

GO:0099642.name: retrograde axonal protein transport
GO:0099642.def: The directed movement of proteins along microtubules from the cell periphery toward the cell body in nerve cell axons.

GO:0099643.name: signal release from synapse
GO:0099643.def: Any signal release from a synapse.

GO:0099738.name: cell cortex region
GO:0099738.def: The complete extent of cell cortex that underlies some some region of the plasma membrane.

GO:0100001.name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by action potential
GO:0100001.def: Any action potential process that regulates skeletal muscle contraction.

GO:0101010.name: pulmonary blood vessel remodeling
GO:0101010.def: The reorganization or renovation of existing pulmonary blood vessels.

GO:0101023.name: vascular endothelial cell proliferation
GO:0101023.def: The multiplication or reproduction of blood vessel endothelial cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population.

GO:0101024.name: mitotic nuclear membrane organization
GO:0101024.def: A mitotic cell cycle process which results in the assembly, arrangement, or disassembly of the nuclear inner or outer membrane during mitosis.
GO:0101024.synonym: nuclear membrane organization involved in mitotic nuclear division

GO:0101025.name: nuclear membrane biogenesis
GO:0101025.def: The process in which a nuclear membrane is synthesized, aggregates, and bonds together.

GO:0104004.name: cellular response to environmental stimulus
GO:0104004.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an environmental stimulus.

GO:0106014.name: regulation of inflammatory response to wounding
GO:0106014.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the inflammatory response to wounding.

GO:0106015.name: negative regulation of inflammatory response to wounding
GO:0106015.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the inflammatory response to wounding.

GO:0106016.name: positive regulation of inflammatory response to wounding
GO:0106016.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the inflammatory response to wounding.

GO:0106027.name: neuron projection organization
GO:0106027.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a prolongation or process extending from a neuron, e.g. an axon, or a dendrite.

GO:0106134.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle cell contraction
GO:0106134.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell contraction.

GO:0106135.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle cell contraction
GO:0106135.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle cell contraction.

GO:0106214.name: regulation of vesicle fusion with Golgi apparatus
GO:0106214.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of vesicle fusion with Golgi apparatus.

GO:0106215.name: negative regulation of vesicle fusion with Golgi apparatus
GO:0106215.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of vesicle fustion with Golgi apparatus.

GO:0106216.name: positive regulation of vesicle fusion with Golgi apparatus
GO:0106216.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of vesicle fusion with Golgi apparatus.

GO:0106426.name: regulation of kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
GO:0106426.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway.

GO:0106427.name: negative regulation of kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
GO:0106427.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway.

GO:0106428.name: positive regulation of kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway
GO:0106428.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the kainate selective glutamate receptor signaling pathway.

GO:0110011.name: regulation of basement membrane organization
GO:0110011.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the assembly, disassembly or arrangement of constituent parts of the basement membrane.

GO:0110020.name: regulation of actomyosin structure organization
GO:0110020.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of cytoskeletal structures containing both actin and myosin or paramyosin.

GO:0110021.name: cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation
GO:0110021.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cardiac muscle myoblasts, resulting in the expansion of a cardiac muscle myoblast cell population. A cardiac myoblast is a precursor cell that has been committed to a cardiac muscle cell fate but retains the ability to divide and proliferate throughout life.

GO:0110022.name: regulation of cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation
GO:0110022.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation.

GO:0110023.name: negative regulation of cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation
GO:0110023.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation.

GO:0110024.name: positive regulation of cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation
GO:0110024.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cardiac muscle myoblast proliferation.

GO:0110053.name: regulation of actin filament organization
GO:0110053.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of actin filament organization.

GO:0110057.name: regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0110057.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation.

GO:0110058.name: positive regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0110058.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation.

GO:0110059.name: negative regulation of blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation
GO:0110059.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of blood vessel endothelial cell differentiation.

GO:0110067.name: ammonium transmembrane transporter complex
GO:0110067.def: High affinity ammonium transporter complex that enables the transfer of ammonium from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:0110077.name: vesicle-mediated intercellular transport
GO:0110077.def: A cellular transport process in which transported substances are moved in extracellular vesicles between cells; transported substances are enclosed in the vesicle lumen or located in the extracellular vesicle membrane.

GO:0110079.name: regulation of placenta blood vessel development
GO:0110079.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of placenta blood vessel development.

GO:0110080.name: positive regulation of placenta blood vessel development
GO:0110080.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of placenta blood vessel development.

GO:0110081.name: negative regulation of placenta blood vessel development
GO:0110081.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of placenta blood vessel development.

GO:0110088.name: hippocampal neuron apoptotic process
GO:0110088.def: Any apoptotic process that occurs in a hippocampal neuron.

GO:0110089.name: regulation of hippocampal neuron apoptotic process
GO:0110089.def: Any process that modulates the occurrence or rate of cell death by apoptotic process in hippocampal neurons.

GO:0110090.name: positive regulation of hippocampal neuron apoptotic process
GO:0110090.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cell death by apoptotic process in hippocampal neurons.

GO:0110091.name: negative regulation of hippocampal neuron apoptotic process
GO:0110091.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cell death by apoptotic process in hippocampal neurons.

GO:0110095.name: cellular detoxification of aldehyde
GO:0110095.def: Any process carried out at the cellular level that reduces or removes the toxicity of an aldehyde. These may include transport of aldehydes away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of the toxic substance.

GO:0110096.name: cellular response to aldehyde
GO:0110096.def: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an aldehyde stimulus.

GO:0110110.name: positive regulation of animal organ morphogenesis
GO:0110110.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of animal organ morphogenesis.

GO:0110111.name: negative regulation of animal organ morphogenesis
GO:0110111.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of animal organ morphogenesis.

GO:0110113.name: positive regulation of lipid transporter activity
GO:0110113.def: Any process that increases the frequency, rate, or extent of lipid transporter activity.

GO:0110114.name: negative regulation of lipid transporter activity
GO:0110114.def: Any process that decreases the frequency, rate, or extent of lipid transporter activity.

GO:0110116.name: regulation of compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
GO:0110116.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation.

GO:0110117.name: positive regulation of compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
GO:0110117.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation.

GO:0110118.name: negative regulation of compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation
GO:0110118.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of compound eye photoreceptor cell differentiation.

GO:0110122.name: myotube cell migration
GO:0110122.def: The orderly movement of a myotube cell from one site to another, often during the development of a multicellular organism. Myotubes are multinucleated cells that are formed when proliferating myoblasts exit the cell cycle, differentiate, and fuse.

GO:0110123.name: regulation of myotube cell migration
GO:0110123.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of myotube cell migration.

GO:0110124.name: positive regulation of myotube cell migration
GO:0110124.def: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of myotube cell migration.

GO:0110125.name: negative regulation of myotube cell migration
GO:0110125.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of myotube cell migration.

GO:0110165.name: cellular anatomical structure
GO:0110165.def: A part of a cellular organism consisting of a material entity with granularity above the level of a protein complex but below that of an anatomical system. Note that cellular organisms exclude viruses.

GO:0120006.name: regulation of glutamatergic neuron differentiation
GO:0120006.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of glutamatergic neuron differentiation.

GO:0120007.name: negative regulation of glutamatergic neuron differentiation
GO:0120007.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of glutamatergic neuron differentiation.

GO:0120008.name: positive regulation of glutamatergic neuron differentiation
GO:0120008.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of glutamatergic neuron differentiation.

GO:0120023.name: somatostatin binding
GO:0120023.def: Binding to somatostatin, a polypeptide hormone involved in regulating pancreatic alpha and pancreatic beta cells and controlling growth hormone secretion as well as many other functions. Somatostatin is produced by several cell types including pancreatic delta cells. There are several different mature forms of somatostatin.

GO:0120025.name: plasma membrane bounded cell projection
GO:0120025.def: A prolongation or process extending from a cell and that is bounded by plasma membrane, e.g. a cilium, lamellipodium, or axon.

GO:0120029.name: proton export across plasma membrane
GO:0120029.def: The directed movement of hydrogen ions (protons) from inside a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the extracellular region.
synonym: hydrogen ion export across plasma membrane

GO:0120031.name: plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly
GO:0120031.def: Formation of a prolongation or process extending and that is bounded by plasma membrane, e.g. a cilium, lamellipodium, or axon.

GO:0120032.name: regulation of plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly
GO:0120032.def: Any process that modulates the rate, frequency, or extent of plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly.

GO:0120033.name: negative regulation of plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly
GO:0120033.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly.

GO:0120034.name: positive regulation of plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly
GO:0120034.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of plasma membrane bounded cell projection assembly.

GO:0120035.name: regulation of plasma membrane bounded cell projection organization
GO:0120035.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of a process involved in the formation, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of plasma membrane bounded cell projections.

GO:0120036.name: plasma membrane bounded cell projection organization
GO:0120036.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a plasma membrane bounded prolongation or process extending from a cell, e.g. a cilium or axon.

GO:0120039.name: plasma membrane bounded cell projection morphogenesis
GO:0120039.def: The process in which the anatomical structures of a plasma membrane bounded cell projection are generated and organized.

GO:0120111.name: neuron projection cytoplasm
GO:0120111.def: All of the contents of a plasma membrane bounded neuron projection, excluding the plasma membrane surrounding the projection.

GO:0120116.name: glucagon processing
GO:0120116.def: The formation of mature glucagon by proteolysis of the precursor proglucagon.

GO:0120158.name: positive regulation of collagen catabolic process
GO:0120158.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of collagen catabolism. Collagen catabolism is the proteolytic chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of collagen in the extracellular matrix.
synonym: up regulation of collagen catabolic process

GO:0120178.name: steroid hormone biosynthetic process
GO:0120178.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of any steroid hormone, naturally occurring substances secreted by specialized cells that affects the metabolism or behavior of other cells possessing functional receptors for the hormone.

GO:0120180.name: cell-substrate junction disassembly
GO:0120180.def: The disaggregation of a cell-substrate junction into its constituent components.

GO:0120186.name: negative regulation of protein localization to chromatin
GO:0120186.def: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of protein localization to chromatin.
GO:0120186.synonym: negative regulation of protein localisation to chromatin

GO:0120187.name: positive regulation of protein localization to chromatin
GO:0120187.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of protein localization to chromatin.
GO:0120187.synonym: positive regulation of protein localisation to chromatin

GO:0120188.name: regulation of bile acid secretion
GO:0120188.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of bile acid from a cell or a tissue.

GO:0120189.name: positive regulation of bile acid secretion
GO:0120189.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of bile acid from a cell or a tissue.

GO:0120190.name: negative regulation of bile acid secretion
GO:0120190.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of bile acid from a cell or a tissue.

GO:0120192.name: tight junction assembly
GO:0120192.def: A cellular process that results in the aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a tight junction. A tight junction seals cells together in an epithelium in a way that prevents even small molecules from leaking from one side of the sheet to the other.

GO:0120193.name: tight junction organization
GO:0120193.def: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a tight junction. A tight junction seals cells together in an epithelium in a way that prevents even small molecules from leaking from one side of the sheet to the other.

GO:0120213.name: regulation of histidine biosynthetic process
GO:0120213.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of histidine biosynthetic process.

GO:0120214.name: negative regulation of histidine biosynthetic process
GO:0120214.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of histidine biosynthetic process.
synonym: down regulation of histidine biosynthetic process

GO:0120215.name: positive regulation of histidine biosynthetic process
GO:0120215.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of histidine biosynthetic process.
synonym: up regulation of histidine biosynthetic process

GO:0120222.name: regulation of blastocyst development
GO:0120222.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of blastocyst development.

GO:0120223.name: larynx morphogenesis
GO:0120223.def: The process in which the larynx is generated and organized. The larynx is a continuation of the pharynx that is involved in breathing, sound production, and protecting the trachea against food aspiration.

GO:0120224.name: larynx development
GO:0120224.def: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of a larynx from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the larynx and ends with the mature structure. A larynx is a continuation of the pharynx that is involved in breathing, sound production, and protecting the trachea against food aspiration.

GO:0120229.name: protein localization to motile cilium
GO:0120229.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, a location within a motile cilium.
GO:0120229.synonym: protein localization to nonmotile primary cilium

GO:0120254.name: olefinic compound metabolic process
GO:0120254.def: The chemical reactions and pathways involving an olefinic compound, any compound which contains a carbon-carbon double bond (aka C=C).

GO:0120255.name: olefinic compound biosynthetic process
GO:0120255.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of an olefinic compound, any compound which contains a carbon-carbon double bond (aka C=C).

GO:0120256.name: olefinic compound catabolic process
GO:0120256.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of an olefinic compound, any compound which contains a carbon-carbon double bond (aka C=C).

GO:0120275.name: cerebral blood circulation
GO:0120275.def: The flow of blood through the network of arteries and veins supplying the cerebrum, enabling the transport of nutrients to the tissues and the removal of waste products.

GO:0120276.name: regulation of cerebral blood circulation
GO:0120276.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cerebral blood circulation.

GO:0120277.name: positive regulation of cerebral blood circulation
GO:0120277.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of cerebral blood circulation.
synonym: positive regulation of cerebrum blood circulation
positive regulation of telencephalon blood circulation
up regulation of cerebral blood circulation

GO:0120278.name: negative regulation of cerebral blood circulation
GO:0120278.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cerebral blood circulation.
synonym: down regulation of cerebral blood circulation
negative regulation of cerebrum blood circulation
negative regulation of telencephalon blood circulation

GO:0120305.name: regulation of pigmentation
GO:0120305.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the deposition or modulates the distribution of coloring matter in an organism.

GO:0120308.name: axonemal outer doublet assembly
GO:0120308.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form an axonemal outer doublet, a part of an axoneme consisting of a doublet microtubule.

GO:0120316.name: sperm flagellum assembly
GO:0120316.def: The assembly and organization of the sperm flagellum, the microtubule-based axoneme and associated structures that are part of a sperm flagellum (or cilium).

GO:0120327.name: telopode
GO:0120327.def: A telopode is a plasma membrane bounded cell projection that is present on a telocyte and is tens to hundreds of microns long. Telopodes form a labyrinthine system communicating through gap junctions.

GO:0120331.name: endothelial tube formation
GO:0120331.def: The developmental process pertaining to the initial formation of an endothelial tube.

GO:0120543.name: macromolecular conformation isomerase activity
GO:0120543.def: Catalysis of a reaction that alters the macromolecular conformation of a molecule.

GO:0120544.name: polypeptide conformation or assembly isomerase activity
GO:0120544.def: Catalysis of a reaction that alters the conformation or assembly of a polypeptide.

GO:0140001.name: morula formation
GO:0140001.def: The initial formation of a spherical embryonic mass of blastomeres formed before the blastula and resulting from cleavage of the fertilized ovum.

GO:0140013.name: meiotic nuclear division
GO:0140013.def: One of the two nuclear divisions that occur as part of the meiotic cell cycle.

GO:0140014.name: mitotic nuclear division
GO:0140014.def: A mitotic cell cycle process comprising the steps by which the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell divides; the process involves condensation of chromosomal DNA into a highly compacted form. Canonically, mitosis produces two daughter nuclei whose chromosome complement is identical to that of the mother cell.

GO:0140029.name: exocytic process
GO:0140029.def: The cellular processes that contribute to exocytosis.

GO:0140039.name: cell-cell adhesion in response to extracellular stimulus
GO:0140039.def: The attachment of one cell to another cell via adhesion molecules as a result of an extracellular stimulus.

GO:0140056.name: organelle localization by membrane tethering
GO:0140056.def: The process by which an organelle membrane interacts with another membrane via molecular tethers that physically bridge the two membranes and attach them to each other.

GO:0140075.name: regulation of lipoprotein transport
GO:0140075.def: Any process that controls lipoprotein transport.

GO:0140076.name: negative regulation of lipoprotein transport
GO:0140076.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of lipoprotein transport.

GO:0140077.name: positive regulation of lipoprotein transport
GO:0140077.def: Any process that activates or increases the rate or extent of lipoprotein transport.

GO:0140096.name: catalytic activity, acting on a protein
GO:0140096.def: Catalytic activity that acts to modify a protein.

GO:0140097.name: catalytic activity, acting on DNA
GO:0140097.def: Catalytic activity that acts to modify DNA.

GO:0140098.name: catalytic activity, acting on RNA
GO:0140098.def: Catalytic activity that acts to modify RNA.

GO:0140103.name: catalytic activity, acting on a glycoprotein
GO:0140103.def: Catalysis of a biochemical reaction in which one of the substrates is a glycoprotein.

GO:0140112.name: extracellular vesicle biogenesis
GO:0140112.def: The assembly and secretion a set of components to form an extracellular vesicule, a membrane-bounded vesicle that is released into the extracellular region. Extracellular vesicles include exosomes, microvesicles and apoptotic bodies, based on the mechanism by which they are released from cells and differentiated based on their size and content.

GO:0140115.name: export across plasma membrane
GO:0140115.def: The directed movement of some substance from inside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the extracellular region.

GO:0140131.name: positive regulation of lymphocyte chemotaxis
GO:0140131.def: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of lymphocyte chemotaxis.

GO:0140146.name: calcium ion import into vacuole
GO:0140146.def: The directed movement of calcium cations into the vacuole across the vacuolar membrane.

GO:0140157.name: ammonium import across plasma membrane
GO:0140157.def: The directed movement of an ammonium ion from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0140227.name: serotonin-gated cation-selective signaling pathway
GO:0140227.def: The series of molecular signals initiated by serotonin binding to a seratonin receptor on the surface of the target cell, followed by the movement of ions through a channel in the receptor complex. Ends with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

GO:0140231.name: anterograde axonal transport of neurotransmitter receptor complex
GO:0140231.def: The directed movement of a neurotransmitter receptor complex along microtubules from the cell body toward the cell periphery in nerve cell axons.

GO:0140236.name: translation at presynapse
GO:0140236.def: Translation that occurs at the presynapse.

GO:0140237.name: translation at presynapse, modulating chemical synaptic transmission
GO:0140237.def: Translation that occurs at the presynapse, and that modulates chemical synaptic transmission.

GO:0140238.name: presynaptic endocytosis
GO:0140238.def: A vesicle-mediated transport process in which the presynapse take up external materials or membrane constituents by the invagination of a small region of the plasma membrane to form a new membrane-bounded vesicle.

GO:0140239.name: postsynaptic endocytosis
GO:0140239.def: A vesicle-mediated transport process in which the postsynapse take up external materials or membrane constituents by the invagination of a small region of the plasma membrane to form a new membrane-bounded vesicle.

GO:0140241.name: translation at synapse
GO:0140241.def: Translation that occurs at the synapse.

GO:0140242.name: translation at postsynapse
GO:0140242.def: Translation that occurs at the postsynapse.

GO:0140243.name: regulation of translation at synapse
GO:0140243.def: Any process that regulates translation occurring at the synapse.

GO:0140244.name: regulation of translation at presynapse
GO:0140244.def: Any process that regulates translation occurring at the presynapse.

GO:0140245.name: regulation of translation at postsynapse
GO:0140245.def: Any process that regulates translation occurring at the postsynapse.

GO:0140246.name: protein catabolic process at synapse
GO:0140246.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein at a synapse.

GO:0140247.name: protein catabolic process at presynapse
GO:0140247.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein at a presynapse.

GO:0140249.name: protein catabolic process at postsynapse
GO:0140249.def: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein at a postsynapse.

GO:0140250.name: regulation protein catabolic process at synapse
GO:0140250.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein at the synapse.

GO:0140251.name: regulation protein catabolic process at presynapse

GO:0140252.name: regulation protein catabolic process at postsynapse
GO:0140252.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein at the postsynapse.

GO:0140253.name: cell-cell fusion
GO:0140253.def: A cellular process in which two or more cells combine together, their plasma membrane fusing, producing a single cell. In some cases, nuclei fuse, producing a polyploid cell, while in other cases, nuclei remain separate, producing a syncytium.

GO:0140271.name: hexose import across plasma membrane
GO:0140271.def: The directed movement of hexose from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:0140297.name: DNA-binding transcription factor binding
GO:0140297.def: Binding to a DNA-binding transcription factor, a protein that interacts with a specific DNA sequence (sometimes referred to as a motif) within the regulatory region of a gene to modulate transcription.

GO:0140318.name: protein transporter activity
GO:0140318.def: Directly binding to a specific protein and delivering it to a specific cellular location.

GO:0140352.name: export from cell
GO:0140352.def: The directed movement of some substance from a cell, into the extracellular region. This may occur via transport across the plasma membrane or via exocytosis.

GO:0140353.name: lipid export from cell
GO:0140353.def: The directed movement of a lipid from a cell, into the extracellular region.

GO:0140354.name: lipid import into cell
GO:0140354.def: The directed movement of a lipid from outside of a cell into a cell. This may occur via transport across the plasma membrane or via endocytosis.

GO:0140375.name: immune receptor activity
GO:0140375.def: Receiving a signal and transmitting it in a cell to initiate an immune response.

GO:0140448.name: signaling receptor ligand precursor processing
GO:0140448.def: The cleavage of a peptide bond in a precursor form of a signaling receptor ligand, resulting in the mature (active) form of the ligand.

GO:0140513.name: nuclear protein-containing complex
GO:0140513.def: A stable assembly of two or more macromolecules, i.e. proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates or lipids, in which at least one component is a protein and the constituent parts function together in the nucleus.

GO:0140546.name: defense response to symbiont
GO:0140546.def: Reactions triggered in response to the presence of a symbiont that act to protect or prevent damage to the host.

GO:0140572.name: vacuole fission
GO:0140572.def: The division of a vacuole within a cell to form two or more separate vacuoles.

GO:0140640.name: catalytic activity, acting on a nucleic acid
GO:0140640.def: Catalytic activity that acts to modify a nucleic acid.

GO:0140650.name: radial glia-guided pyramidal neuron migration
GO:0140650.def: The radial migration of a pyramidal neuron along radial glial cells.

GO:0140657.name: ATP-dependent activity
GO:0140657.def: A molecular function characterized by the coupling of ATP hydrolysis to other steps of a reaction mechanism to make the reaction energetically favorable, for example to catalyze a reaction or drive transport against a concentration gradient.

GO:0140667.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate, or extent of production of oxytocin.

GO:0140694.name: membraneless organelle assembly
GO:0140694.def: The aggregation, arrangement and bonding together of a set of components to form a non-membrane-bounded organelle.

GO:0140734.name: ammonium excretion
GO:0140734.def: The elimination of ammonium ions from an excretory cell.

GO:0140820.name: cytosol to Golgi apparatus transport
GO:0140820.def: The directed movement of substances from the cytosol into the Golgi apparatus of a cell.

GO:0140961.name: cellular detoxification of metal ion
GO:0140961.def: Any process carried out at the cellular level that reduces or removes the toxicity of a metal ion.

GO:0140962.name: multicellular organismal-level chemical homeostasis
GO:0140962.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of a chemical within extracellular body fluids, such as blood, xylem or phloem, of a multicellular organism. This is distinct from maintenance of cellular homeostasis, which occurs within a cell.

GO:0140979.name: intracellular nucleotide homeostasis
GO:0140979.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of nucleotides within a cell.

GO:0141067.name: intracellular nitrogen homeostasis
GO:0141067.def: A homeostatic process involved in the maintenance of a steady state level of nitrogen within a cell.

GO:0141124.name: intracellular signaling cassette
GO:0141124.def: An intracellular signaling module that is part of larger signaling pathways that can be initiated either intracellularly or by cell surface receptors. Intracellular signaling cassettes are discrete signaling units that are often shared by multiple signaling pathways.

GO:0150063.name: visual system development
GO:0150063.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the visual system over time, from its formation to the mature structure, including the eye, parts of the central nervous system (CNS) involved in processing of visual inputs, and connecting nerve pathways.

GO:0150076.name: neuroinflammatory response
GO:0150076.def: The immediate defensive reaction by neural vertebrate tissue to infection or injury caused by chemical or physical agents.

GO:0150098.name: glial cell-neuron signaling
GO:0150098.def: Cell-cell signaling that mediates the transfer of information from a glial cell to a neuron. This signaling has been shown to be mediated by various molecules, depending on which glial cells release them, and in which tissues the signaling occurs, e.g. microglial cell-derived nerve growth factor (NGF) in the retina, or microglial cell-derived superoxide ions in the cerebellum.

GO:0150099.name: neuron-glial cell signaling
GO:0150099.def: Cell-cell signaling that mediates the transfer of information from a neuron to a glial cell. This signaling has been shown to be mediated by various molecules released by different types of neurons, e.g. glutamate, gamma-amino butyric acid (GABA), noradrenaline, acetylcholine, dopamine and adenosine.

GO:0151001.name: tuft
GO:0151001.def: A dense cluster of elongated, thick microvilli on the apical surface of tuft cells in epithelial tissues, such as the intestine and respiratory tract. The apical tuft extends further into the lumen than typical microvilli, featuring larger, more compact projections with unique actin cores that penetrate deep into the cytoplasm, often reaching the perinuclear region. This distinctive structure, rich in microfilaments and microtubules, supports the chemosensory functions of the cell.

GO:0160024.name: Leydig cell proliferation
GO:0160024.def: The multiplication or reproduction of Leydig cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. Leydig cells are interstitial cells located adjacent to the seminiferous tubules in the testis which produce testosterone.

GO:0160038.name: somatic sensory system development
GO:0160038.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a somatic sensory system over time from its formation to the mature structure. Somatic sensory system is the sensory system for the sense of touch and pain.

GO:0160043.name: catecholamine secretion, neurotransmission
GO:0160043.def: The regulated release of catecholamine by a cell in which the catecholamine acts as a neurotransmitter.

GO:0160048.name: craniofacial suture closure

GO:0160083.name: exhausted T cell differentiation

GO:0160093.name: chordate pharynx development
GO:0160093.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of cordate pharynx over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:0160133.name: bicarbonate channel activity
GO:0160133.def: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of bicarbonate through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

GO:0160165.name: CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell homeostasis
GO:0160165.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of CD8-positive alpha-beta T cells such that the total number of CD8-positive alpha-beta T cells within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:0160173.name: histamine transmembrane transporter activity

GO:0160212.name: glycine-gated cation channel activity
GO:0160212.def: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens when glycine is bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts on the extracellular side of the plasma membrane.

GO:0160231.name: cytospinule
GO:0160231.def: An actin-based cell projection extending laterally from the basolateral membrane of tuft cells in epithelial tissues, including the intestinal epithelium. These thin projections, typically 3-4 per cell and up to 3 micron long, directly contact the nuclei of adjacent epithelial cells, potentially facilitating intercellular communication and molecular exchange.

GO:1990010.def: Any apoptotic process in a compound eye retinal cell.

GO:1990034.name: calcium ion export across plasma membrane
GO:1990034.def: The directed movement of calcium ions from inside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the extracellular region.

GO:1990048.name: anterograde neuronal dense core vesicle transport
GO:1990048.def: The directed movement of substances in neuronal dense core vesicles along axonal microtubules towards the presynapse.

GO:1990049.name: retrograde neuronal dense core vesicle transport
GO:1990049.def: The directed movement of neuronal dense core vesicles along axonal microtubules towards the cell body.

GO:1990086.name: lens fiber cell apoptotic process
GO:1990086.def: Any apoptotic process in a lens fiber cell. Lens fiber cells are elongated, tightly packed cells that make up the bulk of the mature lens in a camera-type eye.

GO:1990182.name: exosomal secretion
GO:1990182.def: The process whereby a membrane-bounded vesicle is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane.
synonym: multi-vesicular body fusion with plasma membrane

GO:1990188.name: euchromatin binding
GO:1990188.def: Binding to euchromatin, a dispersed and relatively uncompacted form of chromatin.

GO:1990234.name: transferase complex
GO:1990234.def: A protein complex capable of catalyzing the transfer of a group, e.g. a methyl group, glycosyl group, acyl group, phosphorus-containing, or other groups, from one compound (generally regarded as the donor) to another compound (generally regarded as the acceptor).

GO:1990254.name: keratin filament binding
GO:1990254.def: Binding to a keratin filament, an intermediate filament composed of acidic and basic keratins (types I and II), typically expressed in epithelial cells.

GO:1990266.name: neutrophil migration
GO:1990266.def: The movement of a neutrophil within or between different tissues and organs of the body.

GO:1990280.name: RNA localization to chromatin
GO:1990280.def: A process in which RNA is transported to and maintained in a part of a chromosome that is organized into chromatin.

GO:1990351.name: transporter complex
GO:1990351.def: A protein complex facilitating transport of molecules (proteins, small molecules, nucleic acids) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells.

GO:1990375.name: baculum development
GO:1990375.def: The reproductive developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of the baculum over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:1990379.name: lipid transport across blood-brain barrier
GO:1990379.def: The directed movement of lipid molecules passing through the blood-brain barrier.
GO:1990379.synonym: lipid transport across blood brain barrier

GO:1990461.name: detoxification of iron ion
GO:1990461.def: Any process that reduces or removes the toxicity of iron ion. These include transport of iron away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of iron ion.

GO:1990497.name: regulation of cytoplasmic translation in response to stress
GO:1990497.def: Modulation of the frequency, rate or extent of cytoplasmic translation as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress. The stress is usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

GO:1990502.name: dense core granule maturation
GO:1990502.def: Steps required to transform a dense core granule generated at the trans-Golgi network into a fully formed and transmissible dense core granule. Dense core granule maturation proceeds through clathrin-mediated membrane remodeling events and is essential for efficient processing of cargo within dense core granules as well as for removing factors that might otherwise interfere with dense core granule trafficking and exocytosis.

GO:1990573.name: potassium ion import across plasma membrane
GO:1990573.def: The directed movement of potassium ions from outside of a cell, across the plasma membrane and into the cytosol.

GO:1990580.name: regulation of cytoplasmic translational termination
GO:1990580.def: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cytoplasmic translational termination.

GO:1990611.name: regulation of cytoplasmic translational initiation in response to stress
GO:1990611.def: Modulation of the frequency, rate or extent of cytoplasmic translational initiation as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress. The stress is usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

GO:1990625.name: negative regulation of cytoplasmic translational initiation in response to stress
GO:1990625.def: Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the rate of cytoplasmic translation initiation as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress.

GO:1990654.name: sebum secreting cell proliferation
GO:1990654.def: The multiplication or reproduction of sebocytes by cell division, resulting in the expansion of their population. A sebocyte is an epithelial cell that makes up the sebaceous glands, and secrete sebum.

GO:1990705.name: cholangiocyte proliferation
GO:1990705.def: The multiplication or reproduction of cholangiocytes, resulting in the expansion of the cholangiocyte population. A cholangiocyte is an epithelial cell that is part of the bile duct. Cholangiocytes contribute to bile secretion via net release of bicarbonate and water.

GO:1990716.name: axonemal central apparatus
GO:1990716.def: Part of the 9+2 axoneme, that occurs in most motile cilia, consisting of the pair of two single central microtubules and their associated structures which include the central pair projections, the central pair bridges linking the two tubules, and the central pair caps which are attached to the distal or plus ends of the microtubules.

GO:1990719.name: C1 axonemal microtubule
GO:1990719.def: One of two microtubules present in the axonemal central pair. It is distinguishable from the C2 axonemal microtubule (also called C2 tubule) by the presence of differing protein components of the projections.

GO:1990720.name: C2 axonemal microtubule
GO:1990720.def: One of two microtubules present in the axonemal central pair. It is distinguishable from the C1 axonemal microtubule (also called C1 tubule) by the presence of differing protein components of the projections.

GO:1990739.name: granulosa cell proliferation
GO:1990739.def: The multiplication or reproduction of granulosa cells, resulting in the expansion of the granulosa cells population. A granulosa cell is a supporting cell for the developing female gamete in the ovary of mammals. They develop from the coelomic epithelial cells of the gonadal ridge.

GO:1990748.name: cellular detoxification
GO:1990748.def: Any process carried out at the cellular level that reduces or removes the toxicity of a toxic substance. These may include transport of the toxic substance away from sensitive areas and to compartments or complexes whose purpose is sequestration of the toxic substance.

GO:1990751.name: Schwann cell chemotaxis
GO:1990751.def: The directed movement of a Schwann cell guided by a specific chemical concentration gradient. Movement may be towards a higher concentration (positive chemotaxis) or towards a lower concentration (negative chemotaxis).

GO:1990765.name: colon smooth muscle contraction
GO:1990765.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry of the large intestine, exclusive of the rectum. The colon is that part of the large intestine that connects the small intestine to the rectum.

GO:1990768.name: gastric mucosal blood circulation
GO:1990768.def: The flow of blood through the gastric mucosa of an animal, enabling the transport of nutrients and the removal of waste products.

GO:1990770.name: small intestine smooth muscle contraction
GO:1990770.def: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry in the intestine between the stomach and the large intestine.

GO:1990777.name: lipoprotein particle
GO:1990777.def: A spherical particle containing non-covalently associated proteins and lipids. Examples are plasma lipoprotein particles which transport lipids in the blood or lymph.

GO:1990778.name: protein localization to cell periphery
GO:1990778.def: A process in which a protein is transported to, or maintained in, the cell periphery.

GO:1990791.name: dorsal root ganglion development
GO:1990791.def: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a dorsal root ganglion over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

GO:1990806.name: ligand-gated ion channel signaling pathway
GO:1990806.def: The series of molecular signals initiated by activation of a ligand-gated ion channel on the surface of a cell. The pathway begins with binding of an extracellular ligand to a ligand-gated ion channel and ends with a molecular function that directly regulates a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription.

GO:1990822.name: basic amino acid transmembrane transport
GO:1990822.def: The directed movement of basic amino acids from one side of a membrane to the other.

GO:1990845.name: adaptive thermogenesis
GO:1990845.def: The regulated production of heat in response to short term environmental changes, such as stress, diet or reduced temperature.

GO:1990849.name: vacuolar localization
GO:1990849.def: Any process in which the vacuole is transported to, and/or maintained in, a specific location within the cell.

GO:1990863.name: acinar cell proliferation
GO:1990863.def: The multiplication or reproduction of acinar cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. An acinar cell is a secretory cell that is grouped together with other cells of the same type to form grape-shaped clusters known as acini (singular acinus).

GO:1990874.name: vascular associated smooth muscle cell proliferation
GO:1990874.def: The multiplication or reproduction of vascular smooth muscle cells, resulting in the expansion of a cell population. A vascular smooth muscle cell is a non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cell found lining the blood vessels.

GO:1990904.name: ribonucleoprotein complex
GO:1990904.def: A macromolecular complex that contains both RNA and protein molecules.

GO:1990922.name: hepatic stellate cell proliferation
GO:1990922.def: The multiplication or reproduction of hepatic stellate cells, resulting in the expansion of a hepatic stellate cell population. Hepatic stellate cells are found in the perisinusoidal space of the liver, and are capable of multiple roles including storage of retinol, presentation of antigen to T cells (including CD1d-restricted NKT cells), and upon activation, production of extracellular matrix components. This cell type comprises approximately 8-15% of total cells in the liver.

GO:1990959.name: eosinophil homeostasis
GO:1990959.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of eosinophils such that the total number of eosinophils within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

GO:1990960.name: basophil homeostasis
GO:1990960.def: The process of regulating the proliferation and elimination of basophils such that the total number of basophils within a whole or part of an organism is stable over time in the absence of an outside stimulus.

IAO:0000078.name: curation status specification
IAO:0000078.def: The curation status of the term. The allowed values come from an enumerated list of predefined terms. See the specification of these instances for more detailed definitions of each enumerated value.

IAO:0000102.name: data about an ontology part
IAO:0000102.def: Data about an ontology part is a data item about a part of an ontology, for example a term

IAO:0000225.name: obsolescence reason specification
IAO:0000225.def: The reason for which a term has been deprecated. The allowed values come from an enumerated list of predefined terms. See the specification of these instances for more detailed definitions of each enumerated value.

IAO:0000409.name: denotator type
IAO:0000409.def: A denotator type indicates how a term should be interpreted from an ontological perspective.

PATO:0000001.name: quality
PATO:0000001.def: A dependent entity that inheres in a bearer by virtue of how the bearer is related to other entities

PATO:0000025.name: composition
PATO:0000025.def: A single physical entity inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's quantities or relative ratios of subparts.

PATO:0000050.name: life span
PATO:0000050.def: A time quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's expected maximum age.

PATO:0000051.name: morphology
PATO:0000051.def: A quality of a single physical entity inhering in the bearer by virtue of the bearer's size or shape or structure.

PATO:0000052.name: shape
PATO:0000052.def: A morphological quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ratios of distances between its features (points, edges, surfaces and also holes etc).

PATO:0000057.name: occurrence
PATO:0000057.def: A quality of a single process inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's occurrence.

PATO:0000068.name: qualitative
PATO:0000068.def: A quality of an entity that is descriptive or observational, typically not represented numerically.

PATO:0000069.name: deviation (from_normal)
PATO:0000069.def: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the whether the bearer differs from normal or average.

PATO:0000117.name: size
PATO:0000117.def: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's physical magnitude.

PATO:0000136.name: closure
PATO:0000136.def: A morphological quality pertaining to the degree to which an object contains an opening, aperture, orifice or vent.

PATO:0000141.name: structure
PATO:0000141.def: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's relative position, shape, arrangements and connectivity of an organism's various parts; the pattern underlying its form.

PATO:0000150.name: texture
PATO:0000150.def: A morphologic quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's relative size, organization and distribution of its surface elements or the representation or invention of the appearance of its surface; visual and tactile surface characteristics.

PATO:0000165.name: time
PATO:0000165.def: A quality in which events occur in sequence.

PATO:0000261.name: maturity
PATO:0000261.def: A quality of a single physical entity which is held by a bearer when the latter exhibits a state of growth, differentiation, or development.

PATO:0000402.name: branched
PATO:0000402.def: A branchiness quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having branches.

PATO:0000404.name: coiled
PATO:0000404.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being curled or wound (especially in concentric rings or spirals).

PATO:0000405.name: curled
PATO:0000405.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having parallel chains in undulate fashion on the border.

PATO:0000407.name: flat
PATO:0000407.def: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a horizontal surface without a slope, tilt, or curvature.

PATO:0000411.name: circular
PATO:0000411.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being such that every part of the surface or the circumference is equidistant from the center.

PATO:0000413.name: square
PATO:0000413.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having an equal-sided rectangular form.

PATO:0000460.name: abnormal
PATO:0000460.def: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's deviation from normal or average.

PATO:0000461.name: normal
PATO:0000461.def: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting no deviation from normal or average.

PATO:0000586.name: increased size
PATO:0000586.def: A size quality which is relatively high.

PATO:0000587.name: decreased size
PATO:0000587.def: A size quality which is relatively low.

PATO:0000588.name: vestigial
PATO:0000588.def: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being a remnant structure from earlier development or evolution.

PATO:0000608.name: closed
PATO:0000608.def: A morphological quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's affording blocked passage or view.

PATO:0000610.name: open
PATO:0000610.def: A morphological quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's affording unobstructed passage or view.

PATO:0000690.name: discontinuous
PATO:0000690.def: A quality of a single process inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked by breaks or interruptions.

PATO:0000947.name: elliptic
PATO:0000947.def: A spheroid quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being oval with two axes of symmetry, as produced by a conical section.

PATO:0000957.name: opacity
PATO:0000957.def: An optical quality which obtains by virtue of the ability of the bearer to absorb visible light.

PATO:0000963.name: opaque
PATO:0000963.def: A optical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's not being clear; not transmitting or reflecting light or radiant energy.

PATO:0000964.name: transparent
PATO:0000964.def: A optical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lacking opacity.

PATO:0000992.name: viscosity
PATO:0000992.def: A physical quality of a fluid inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to internal resistance to flow.

PATO:0000998.name: viscous
PATO:0000998.def: A viscosity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having viscosity.

PATO:0001018.name: physical quality
PATO:0001018.def: A quality of a physical entity that exists through action of continuants at the physical level of organisation in relation to other entities.

PATO:0001031.name: elasticity
PATO:0001031.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to recover its size and shape after deformation in any way.

PATO:0001171.name: elastic
PATO:0001171.def: An elasticity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ability to recover its size and shape after deformation in any way.

PATO:0001185.name: larval
PATO:0001185.def: A maturity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's indirect development, undergoing metamorphosis.

PATO:0001190.name: juvenile
PATO:0001190.def: A maturity quality inhering in a bearer by virtue the bearer's being not fully grown or developed.

PATO:0001236.name: process quality
PATO:0001236.def: A quality which inheres in an process.

PATO:0001241.name: physical object quality
PATO:0001241.def: A quality which inheres in a continuant.
synonym: multiply inhering quality of a physical entity
quality of a single physical entity

PATO:0001292.name: full-spectrum EM radiation quality
PATO:0001292.def: An EM radiation quality that is independent of the EM wavelength range.

PATO:0001294.name: radiation reflective quality
PATO:0001294.def: A scalar EM radiation quality which obtains by the capacity of the bearer to scatter or reflect radiation.

PATO:0001297.name: reflectivity
PATO:0001297.def: A radiation reflective quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the ratio of the energy of a wave reflected from its surface to the energy possessed by the wave striking the bearer's surface.

PATO:0001300.name: optical quality
PATO:0001300.def: An EM radiation quality in which the EM radiation is within the fiat range of the spectrum visible deemed to be light.

PATO:0001374.name: ploidy
PATO:0001374.def: A cellular quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's number of homologous sets of chromosomes in the nucleus or primary chromosome-containing compartment of the cell, each set essentially coding for all the biological traits of the organism.

PATO:0001375.name: haploid
PATO:0001375.def: A ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing a single set of homologous chromosomes.

PATO:0001377.name: polyploid
PATO:0001377.def: A ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing more than two homologous sets of chromosomes.

PATO:0001393.name: euploid
PATO:0001393.def: A ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing an integral multiple of the monoploid number, possibly excluding the sex-determining chromosomes.

PATO:0001394.name: diploid
PATO:0001394.def: A ploidy quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having two copies (homologs) of each chromosome, usually one from the mother and one from the father.

PATO:0001396.name: cellular quality
PATO:0001396.def: A monadic quality of continuant that exists at the cellular level of organisation.

PATO:0001397.name: cellular potency
PATO:0001397.def: A cellular quality that arises by virtue of whether the bearer's disposition to differentiate into one or more mature cell types.

PATO:0001400.name: unipotent
PATO:0001400.def: A cellular potency that is the capacity to produce only one differentiated cell type.

PATO:0001401.name: oligopotent
PATO:0001401.def: A cellular potency that is the capacity to form multiple differentiated cell types of a specific lineage and lack self renewing capacity.

PATO:0001402.name: multipotent
PATO:0001402.def: A cellular potency that is the capacity to form multiple differentiated cell types.

PATO:0001404.name: nucleate quality
PATO:0001404.def: A cellular quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of bearer's number of nuclei.

PATO:0001405.name: anucleate
PATO:0001405.def: A nucleate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having no nucleus.

PATO:0001406.name: binucleate
PATO:0001406.def: A nucleate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having two nuclei.

PATO:0001407.name: mononucleate
PATO:0001407.def: A nucleate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having one nucleus.

PATO:0001408.name: ciliated
PATO:0001408.def: A cellular quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having one or more cilia as a part.

PATO:0001410.name: striated
PATO:0001410.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being marked by narrow lines or grooves, usually parallel.

PATO:0001501.name: immature
PATO:0001501.def: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's lacking complete growth, differentiation, or development.

PATO:0001509.name: functionality
PATO:0001509.def: A quality of a single physical entity that arises by virtue of whether the bearer exhibits the ability to perform a regular function(s).

PATO:0001543.name: flexibility
PATO:0001543.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's disposition to being turned, bowed, or twisted without breaking.

PATO:0001544.name: flexible
PATO:0001544.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ability of being turned, bowed, or twisted without breaking.

PATO:0001546.name: quality of a solid
PATO:0001546.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting the physical characteristics of an entity characterized by particles arranged such that their shape and volume are relatively stable.

PATO:0001547.name: quality of a gas
PATO:0001547.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting the physical characteristics of an entity consisting of particles that have neither a defined volume nor defined shape.

PATO:0001548.name: quality of a liquid
PATO:0001548.def: A physical quality inhering in an entity exhibiting the physical characteristics of an amorphous (non-crystalline) form of matter between a gas and a solid that has a definite volume, but no definite shape.

PATO:0001559.name: having extra function
PATO:0001559.def: A functionality quality which is held by the bearer when the latter is able to perform additional or different function(s).

PATO:0001579.name: contractility
PATO:0001579.def: A physical quality that is the ability to contract or shrink.

PATO:0001580.name: increased contractility
PATO:0001580.def: A contractility which is relatively high.

PATO:0001581.name: decreased contractility
PATO:0001581.def: A contractility which is relatively low.

PATO:0001591.name: curvature
PATO:0001591.def: A surface shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting a degree of bending.

PATO:0001603.name: increased life span
PATO:0001603.def: A life span which is relatively high.

PATO:0001604.name: decreased life span
PATO:0001604.def: A life span which is relatively low.

PATO:0001690.name: contractile
PATO:0001690.def: A contractility quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ability of contracting or being contracted.

PATO:0001735.name: liquid configuration
PATO:0001735.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's parts having the arrangement which exhibits characteristics of liquids.

PATO:0001736.name: solid configuration
PATO:0001736.def: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's parts having the arrangement which exhibits characteristics of solids.

PATO:0001748.name: invaginated
PATO:0001748.def: A shape quality in which a portion of the outermost boundary of an entity folds in space such that a portion that was originally convex is now concave.

PATO:0001776.name: increased flexibility
PATO:0001776.def: A flexibility which is relatively high.

PATO:0001777.name: decreased flexibility
PATO:0001777.def: A flexibility which is relatively low.

PATO:0001794.name: coiling
PATO:0001794.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being wound in a continuous series of loops.

PATO:0001795.name: increased coiling
PATO:0001795.def: A coiling which is relatively high.

PATO:0001796.name: decreased coiling
PATO:0001796.def: A coiling which is relatively low.

PATO:0001857.name: concave
PATO:0001857.def: A shape quality in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's curving inward.

PATO:0001870.name: crescent-shaped
PATO:0001870.def: A shape quality inhering in a circular disk by virtue of the bearer's having a segment of another circle removed from its edge, so that what remains is a shape enclosed by two circular arcs of different diameters which intersect at two points (usually in such a manner that the enclosed shape does not include the center of the original circle).

PATO:0001871.name: reniform
PATO:0001871.def: A concave 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having the shape of a kidney.

PATO:0001872.name: cuboid
PATO:0001872.def: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resemblance to a cube (a 3-D shape with a square cross section).

PATO:0001873.name: cylindrical
PATO:0001873.def: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting a consistently-sized round cross section.

PATO:0001874.name: discoid
PATO:0001874.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cylindrical, in which the height is less than the diameter.

PATO:0001908.name: multinucleate
PATO:0001908.def: A nucleate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having more than one nucleus.

PATO:0001910.name: folded
PATO:0001910.def: A surface feature shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's one part being layered over another connected part.

PATO:0001925.name: surface feature shape
PATO:0001925.def: A surface shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's shape of features present on its surface or outer shell.

PATO:0001979.name: lobed
PATO:0001979.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being partly divided into a determinate number of regions.

PATO:0001987.name: saccular
PATO:0001987.def: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a three dimensional cavity with a narrow or no opening, and often containing an anatomical substance.

PATO:0001988.name: quadrangular
PATO:0001988.def: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having four angles and four sides.

PATO:0001992.name: cellularity
PATO:0001992.def: An organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's consisting cells.

PATO:0001993.name: multicellular
